a17_0000027.text: This is Mission Control. Gene Cernan reporting the launch vehicle maneuvering to the proper attitude, everything looking good at this point.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Wow woozle!

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, babe. Let's check the angles.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Thirty seconds. We're going up. Man, oh, man!

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Thirty seconds, and 17 is Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17. You're Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:00:40 - First stage looks good. Altitude, 1.1 [nautical] miles [2.0 km].
First stage looks good. Altitude, 1.1 [nautical] miles [2.0 km].

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, 1 minute and 68 degrees.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Everything looks great over here, Gene.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay. Okay, stand-by for Max - coming through Max Q. We'll be at 68 degrees.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: ...Okay.
Booster says we look good. We're now at 2.5 [nautical] miles [4.6 km].

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: 17, stand by for Mode I Bravo.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Mark. Mode I Bravo.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger. I Bravo; we're Go at 1 minute.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Gene. You're looking great. Right on the line.
Everybody says 'Looking great - Right on the line.' We're now 1 [nautical] mile [1.85 km] down range. Launch vehicle 4.2 [nautical] miles [7.8 km] high.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we got the RCS command.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: 17, you are feet wet - feet wet.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger. Feet wet.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Man, this thing shakes like a son-of-a-gun.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Yes, that's Max Q. Wait until we get out of Max Q. Stay down there Q-meter.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Man.
Coming up on maximum dynamic pressure at this point. 4 [nautical] miles [7.4 km] down range, 8 [nautical] miles high [14.8 km] and the velocity approaching 3,000 feet per second [1,000 m/s].

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay. 1:30 and about 50 degrees.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: 50 Degrees. Okay, right on.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 01:30, and we are Go, Bob.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Gene. You're looking great.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 2gs. 2½gs. See it quiets out after Max Q.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Yes. Quiets out.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Pushing 3gs.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: I can't - can't hold my hand up there anymore. [Laughter.]

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we're out of Max Q.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay. Cabin's still looking good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Alpha's PC.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, standby for...

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Stand by for Mode I Charlie, 17.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: ...I Charlie.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Mark. Mode I Charlie.
And the Flight Dynamics Officer says we look good on all sources, right on the trajectory.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger, I Charlie. 2 minutes.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: EDS.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: EDS is Off and we are Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17; you're Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 3gs. 3½. Standby for inboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:02:09 - Flight Director Gene Kranz taking a status for staging, we say we look good for staging.
Flight Director Gene Kranz taking a status for staging, we say we look good for staging.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: 17, you are Go for staging.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger. We're Go here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Did you get your Verb 82?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: No.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Standby for inboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay. That's Verb 82.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Inboard cut-off.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. Inboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:02:24 - Inboard engines shutting down on-time as planned.
Inboard engines shutting down on-time as planned.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, now hold on after staging guys.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Standby gang.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay. Here's 20. Where's the safety?

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Okay, it's 19.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Now at 41. It's 41. [Garble] seconds

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 3½ gs.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:02:33 - Crew will experience maximum g forces of about 4gs at shutdown.
Crew will experience maximum g forces of about 4gs at shutdown.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Hold on!

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay. 5 seconds. [Garble] gs. 4gs.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:02:40 - Coming up on first stage shutdown. And we've had shutdown on time on the first stage.
Coming up on first stage shutdown. And we've had shutdown on time on the first stage.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Jesus Christ!

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: I told you to hold on. Look at that son-of-a-bitch. Man!

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Jesus crimany! [Laughter.]

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Bob. I guess we got all five.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. They're looking here - looking good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, standby to ...

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Sure felt like it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Standby. Hold it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: I think we saw them all from here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Jack. And the thrust is Go on all five of them. They're running good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay; 3 minutes and we're Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: See how smooth...

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Geez, this is smooth. Okay, got some tower switches...

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Come on, baby! Go!

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, 13.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we do have skirt sep.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. We confirm skirt sep.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Watch it, Jack!

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: 16, there it goes...

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: There goes the tower.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Wow, there she goes!

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. The tower; you're Mode II.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Mode II.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, [garble] command.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, alpha [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: The steering has converged. The CMC is Go. You're going right down the pike, 17.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Bob. I do confirm guidance.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: And, ELS SEP circuit breakers when you get a chance there, Gene.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:03:43 - That's the automatic guidance system, the inertial guidance system, performing properly.
That's the automatic guidance system, the inertial guidance system, performing properly.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Bob, I got the ELS SEP circuit breakers. And we've seen it all: ignition, staging, and tower.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. Got you.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: By the way, the cabin's sealed. [laughter.].
Apollo 17 now 65 [nautical] miles [120.4 km] high.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay guys, we've got a long way to go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, I'll tell you where in the hell we're going here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay; 4 minutes and we're Go here, Bob.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Gene. We're going round the room. Looks Go here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 21 degrees. We're Mode 2, Ron.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay...

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: You're looking real good, Gene. Right down the line.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, H and H-Dot looks pretty good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: We got a 30 and a 430. I can't really see that, let's see.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay; 04:30 and we're still Go onboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17. You're Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Let me tell you, this night launch is something to behold.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, H and H-Dot are good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, I don't know if you'll be able to pick up any horizon.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:04:47 - Coming up on 5 minutes. Everything still looks very good in the launch of Apollo 17. The launch vehicle/spacecraft now 80 [nautical] miles [148.2 km] high, 230 [nautical] miles [426 km] down range.
Coming up on 5 minutes. Everything still looks very good in the launch of Apollo 17. The launch vehicle/spacecraft now 80 [nautical] miles [148.2 km] high, 230 [nautical] miles [426 km] down range.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: No, it's too dark - too light in here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Yes.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, let's keep - on. One g.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: I got some stars out on the right, but I don't see...

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Five minutes, Geno, and you're Go down here. You're looking great.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: [Garble] Jack, Okay.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Robert. We're Go here at 5.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Coming up on S-IVB to COI.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: You guys believe me about that S-I staging now?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: [Laughter.] I can't...

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: I can't believe how smooth this is.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: I can't - I can't believe how smooth this is.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, let's keep this mother burning. We've got a long way to go. We're only half way there.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: 17, Houston. Your times are nominal. Level sense arm at 8 plus 36; S-II shutdown at 9 plus 20. Nominal times.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 8 plus 36 and 9 plus 20. Roger.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Coming up on gimbal motors, Geno.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay. [Garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:05:38 - CapCom Robert Overmyer advising Gene Cernan and the crew aboard Apollo 17 the second stage shutdown at about 9 minutes, 20 seconds Elapsed Time. That shutdown about 3½ minutes from now.
CapCom Robert Overmyer advising Gene Cernan and the crew aboard Apollo 17 the second stage shutdown at about 9 minutes, 20 seconds Elapsed Time. That shutdown about 3½ minutes from now.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: I forget anything yet, Ron?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Nope.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we're still Mode 2, coming up on...

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Standby for S-IVB to COI capability.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Mark. S-IVB to COI capability.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger. S-IVB to COI. We're Go at 6.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Good. Gimbal motors?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Go ahead.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Geno.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Pitch 1.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Got it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: And Yaw 1.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Got it. Go ahead. ...

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Pitch 2.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Got it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: And Yaw 2.
Apollo 17 still right on the nominal trajectory at an altitude now of about 92 nautical miles [170.4 km].

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Got it. Okay, got a plus 15.8 and a plus 19. [Garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Bob. We're got four good motors and we're Go at 06:20.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. And, 17, we copied the gimbals and watched them and they looked good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: One g? Just like sitting on the pad, isn't it? A [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Okay, our calibration on that tank changed a little bit again, apparently.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Down at 90%.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: 90? On the Tank 2?

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: On the hydrogen.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Hydrogen. Tank 3, I mean.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Stand by for S-IVB to orbit capability.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Bob. [Garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Mark. S-IVB to orbit capability. And we'd like Omni Delta, Jack.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Roger. You've got it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, 7 minutes [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 7, and I'm 6 degrees. How does that sound?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay, that's good. 17, 3. Let's see, 119. We go to [garble] half a mile high.
Now 7 minutes in and we have sufficient velocity to make orbit with the Saturn third stage should we have an unexpected early shutdown of the second stage.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Seven minutes, Bob. We're looking good onboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Am I glad I took my hand off that abort handle!

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: [Laughter.] Man!

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: So am I. [Laughter.] I'll tell ya. [Laughter.]

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we've got to get through this one, and then through staging. Standby for inboard. Okay. [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:07:27 - We're now less than 2 minutes from second stage shutdown and ignition of the Saturn third stage. And the center engine will be shutting down as scheduled in about 10 seconds.
We're now less than 2 minutes from second stage shutdown and ignition of the Saturn third stage. And the center engine will be shutting down as scheduled in about 10 seconds.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Standby for inboard.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Okay. Okay, we're at a g-and-a-half. Standby.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: We have inboard cut-off.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Gene. Inboard on time.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:07:46 - And that inboard shutdown looked to be on time.
And that inboard shutdown looked to be on time.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, she pitches up just like the simulator.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Yep. Sure does. Pitches...

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:07:53 - Apollo 17 now 625 miles downrange, 93 miles in altitude.
Apollo 17 now 625 miles downrange, 93 miles in altitude.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: [Grunting noise.]

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Is that hard to reach, Jack?

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: Yes. Why don't you take it down, I can't quite - g-and-a-half is too much.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Eight minutes, and we are Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17. You're looking great.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, [garble] standby for a PU shift.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Is that what that was?

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Yes, I think it was.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Yes, I think that was it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:08:17 - The spacecraft guidance systems agreeing very closely with the Saturn guidance. It looks good.
The spacecraft guidance systems agreeing very closely with the Saturn guidance. It looks good.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Ron. That level sense arm will be at 36.

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: 36. Okay.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: 17, Houston. You are Go for staging.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Thank you, Bob. We are Go for staging up here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: A little over a g.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: There's a little chug.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:08:32 - Staging now less than 1 minute.
Staging now less than 1 minute.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, we've got to get through this one. Coming in, we're level sense arm now.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: You have level sense arm at this time, Gene.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger, Bob. Level sense arm.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, Ron. Our next thing will be standby for Mode IV, and we'll have staging. I will call it out to you.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:08:48 - Apollo 17 traveling at 21,000 feet per second [6,400 m/s]. It's achieved about 83 per cent of the velocity required for a minimum orbit.
Apollo 17 traveling at 21,000 feet per second [6,400 m/s]. It's achieved about 83 per cent of the velocity required for a minimum orbit.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: And little S-IVB burn, baby burn. Gimbal [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Nine minutes, Bob, and 17 is Go.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger, 17. You're Go here.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Okay, standby.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0000027.text: 000:09:07 - And about 10 seconds to staging.
And about 10 seconds to staging.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: 10 seconds.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Standby for Mode IV capability.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: S-II cut-off.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Mark. Mode IV capability, and we copy cut-off.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Roger. Mode IV. And we do have S-IVB ignition.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger. We see it, and the thrust is looking good on it.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: God, you see that glow [garble].

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Geez!

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: We saw that one, too, Bob.

a17_0000027.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0000027.text: Roger.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Did you see it go past us?

a17_0000027.speaker: Evans
a17_0000027.text: Yes.

a17_0000027.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0000027.text: We're right in the flame.

a17_0000027.speaker: Cernan
a17_0000027.text: Yes, that's what the Titan used to do. Used to fly through the flame of that thing. Let's, let's press on here we've got a lot to do. We're Mode IV.

a17_0000027.speaker: Mission Control

a17_0001347.text: This is Apollo Control; coming up on 14 minutes after lift-off, that lift-off coming about 2 hours, 40 minutes late and we'll be assessing the effects of that late lift-off on subsequent events in the mission timeline, passing those along. One of the effects will be a change in the Acquisition Of Signal/Loss Of Signal time as we move - move along on the ground track.

a17_t-0001342.speaker: Schmitt

a17_t-0001342.speaker: Schmitt

a17_t-0001342.text: And we think it's the EDS Power switch and the fuel cell [garble] switch that are drawing the current that you're seeing there.

a17_t-0001342.speaker: Overmyer
a17_t-0001342.text: Okay, Jack, we're going to lose you in about 1 minute off of Vanguard here and see you at 52:20.

a17_t-0001342.text: Okay, Bob. Everything is looking Go onboard. Everything's stable. We can see the APS firing, and our attitudes look good.

a17_t-0001653.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0001653.text: Okay. Let me get Repress Package valve, Off. Look at those aps - that amplifier.

a17_t-0002006.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0002006.text: Boy, I tell you, I'm sure glad I didn't have to use any SPS stars out there. I never would have seen them. Look at that. Okay, here you go. Your first sight. You're looking to watch the sunrise. Jack, get out here.

a17_t-0002006.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0002006.text: There's some lightning out there. See it?

a17_t-0002006.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0002006.text: Yes, sir. What have you got 16 54 on there for, anything?

a17_t-0002006.speaker: Evans
a17_t-0002006.text: What time is it? Twenty-two. Yes, we're that much early.

a17_t-0002117.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0002117.text: There's some lightning out there. See it?

a17_t-0002117.text: Yes, sir. What have you got 16 54 on there for, anything?

a17_t-0002117.speaker: Evans
a17_t-0002117.text: What time is it? Twenty-two. Yes, we're that much early.

a17_0003533.text: This is Apollo Control. The postlaunch press conference at Cape Kennedy is scheduled to begin at 12:33 Central Standard Time, 1:33 am Eastern Standard Time. Again, that time 12:33 Central Standard Time, 1:33 Eastern Standard for the post-launch press conference at Cape Kennedy.

a17_0003533.speaker: Cernan
a17_0003533.text: The computer is - the computer is with both of our clocks up here.

a17_t-0004521.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0004521.text: Okay. And I'm double checked here on normal - normal and latched.

a17_t-0004521.speaker: Cernan
a17_t-0004521.text: There it went - with that switch.

a17_t-0004521.speaker: Schmitt
a17_t-0004521.text: Okay. You got all the optic stuff; right, Ron?

a17_t-0004521.speaker: Schmitt
a17_t-0004521.text: Okay, you guys. Except for - except for one check over here, which I am going to have to unzip here to do, I think...

a17_t-0004521.speaker: Schmitt
a17_t-0004521.text: Okay, let me tell you what you want.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Okay. We copy that. Okay, while we're filling in some here, you might want to know this, Jack. Your sunset and sunrise times in the Launch Checklist are all off by 8 - approximately 8 minutes and 30 seconds. That every - sunset and sunrise will occur about 8 minutes and 30 seconds sooner than in the - in the Launch Checklist. That's an approximate number.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Okay, we got you.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Okay. And on page 2-17 of the Launch Checklist, you're going to want to delete all reference to Honeysuckle AOS and LOS and delete all reference to Canaries AOS and LOS.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Wilco.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: And we want to add an Ascension pass; AOS at Ascension, 01 plus 54 plus 00, and Ascension LOS will be 02:00:16. [Pause.]

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Okay, Bob; you're going to have to repeat that.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Okay, stand by. Let me give you a page. On 2-17 - let's go Hawaii AOS first of all. On Hawaii AOS, on page 2-17. AOS...

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Go.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: ...is 01 plus 17 plus 24. Hawaii LOS, 01 plus 22 plus 49. [Pause.]

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Gotcha. Now what about the Ascension?

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Okay, here - give you the Ascension again now. AOS, 1 plus 54 plus 00. Ascension LOS will be 02:00:16. Over.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Okay, I got those. Hawaii is 1 plus 17 plus 24, and LOS is 1 plus 22 plus 49. And Ascension is AOS, 1 plus 54:00; and LOS, 2 plus 00:16.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Roger, Jack. Good copy. And booster's looking good down here and you're looking good.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Okay, and I'll do a better job of itemizing those switches. We were pressing pretty hard, and I'll - I'll be able to go back and get most of them, I think. And we'll keep an eye on it - on the Master Alarms.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Roger, Jack. We understand. And I think we copied most of what you said there, and we're working on it.

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: Okay, Bob; other than that Master Alarm, all is well on America, and I understand the booster is looking good to you.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: And, Bob, let me add that not - we did get spurious Master Alarms without switch movement, but many came with switch movements. We've had about seven.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Okay; understand. [Pause.]

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: That was only after insertion. [Pause.]

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Seven times that your heart doesn't need, huh?

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: Oh, we were paying attention to a sunset that was the biggest...

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: Sunrise.

a17_0005356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0005356.text: ...or sunrise or something that we saw. It was the biggest rainbow I'd ever seen.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Beautiful. [Pause.] We can't wait to hear what you had to say about that - the ignition on the S-II. It sounded pretty spectacular.

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: Bob, just let it be said that that was quite a booster ride. When we get a chance a little later...

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Roger.

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: ...maybe we'll be able to tell you something.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: We're about ready to lose comm here. You're looking great, guys, and we'll pick you up in Hawaii here shortly.

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: Okay, we're looking at the deserts of Australia right now and, again, everything's good onboard.

a17_0005356.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0005356.text: Roger. Pick you up at 01:17:24.

a17_0005356.speaker: Cernan
a17_0005356.text: Rog.

This is Apollo Control. We're coming up now one 1 hour after lift-off for Apollo 17. And as you heard, CapCom Robert Overmyer reporting to the crew that everything looks good, including the Saturn third stage. Apparently the indication we had of a possible battery problem in the Instrument Unit, nothing more than a bad bit of telemetry there. When the booster engineer got a good hard look at the telemetry on this pass, reported everything looked good. We're ready at this point to begin the post-launch press conference at Cape Kennedy and we'll switch to Cape Kennedy now, and stand by for that

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: Hello, earthlings. We're back with you.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Roger, Jack. Read you loud and clear; how us?

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: You're loud and clear. And no change systems-wise that I've seen.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Roger, Jack. Any more Master Alarms?

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: We had one when Ron's - looked like his neck ring hit panel 2. [Garble]

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Okay. Sounds like we had something loose in panel 2, huh?

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: Yeah. I don't know - it may be annoying, but so far it doesn't seem to be a problem.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Roger. Just for your information, everything is looking outstanding and no problems. We're taking a good look at the data here at Hawaii, and we'll make a Go/No-Go decision about 60 seconds after acquisition at Goldstone. But there's nothing right now to lead us to believe that zero opportunity will be required.

a17_0011725.speaker: Cernan
a17_0011725.text: Okay, Bob, understand that. We are prepared, however. Spacecraft, other than those Master Alarms, is looking very good. We got the docking probe extended. The SCS reference attitude check is complete.

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: Okay, Bob, I just remembered another switch that I think gave us a Master Alarm was H 2 O Quantity Indicator.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Roger. Copy that, Jack. H 2 O Quantity Indicator.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Roger we're - 17, we're going to lose you in about 30 seconds. But when you get over the stateside here, we're going to take - take the dump on the data, and we'll read it out real carefully so when you get in TLC we ought to be able to see where that Master Alarm glitch is coming in to.

a17_0011725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0011725.text: Okay, Bob. And - yell at me if you want anything done on the comm with this change in AOS/LOS stuff.

a17_0011725.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0011725.text: Negative on that right now. We'll see you at 01:28:59 through Goldstone.

a17_0012500.text: This is Apollo Control; 1 hour, 25 minutes after lift-off. During the post-launch press conference at Cape Kennedy, we had a short acquisition with the crew through the Hawaiian tracking station. During that period of conversation, and during that period of monitoring the systems on the spacecraft and the launch vehicle, we found that the situation was essentially unchanged. That is, both vehicles looking good; the spacecraft and the launch vehicle. And we're progressing toward a normal Translunar Injection 1 hour, 46 minutes, 50 seconds from now. The crew has discussed one unexplained series

a17_0012500.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012500.text: We sam - we saw all three stagings, now, or all three ignitions.

a17_0012500.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012500.text: Yes, 90-degree launch azimuth means we're on our next latitude. We're coming up on our next latitude, which is Cape [garble] latitude - the next latitude will be for the Cape.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: 17, Houston. We're back with you.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay, Bob. We're still same as before and ready when you are for TLI.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: I can see the lights of southern California, Bob.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Right. Your ground track looks like it's taking you right up over the mid part of Baja California.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger, Jack.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Yes, sir; I'll believe that. I'll bet you I can see Ensenada right now.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: We're going to be going a little bit south of that area.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Bob, I expect he'll probably be able to see the lights of Silver City, too.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Well, I'm sure going to be looking for them, I'll tell you. [Long pause.]

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Jack, just for your information, you'll probably - when you come up a little farther in this orbit here and get over Mexico, you should be able to see all that bad weather that was giving us so much worry and had Tindall and New Orleans and everything all messed up this morning when I went through there. They had a pretty bad line of weather along there.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: I was assuming it wasn't too bad. I think you made it, didn't you?

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Oh, yeah, I made it, but I had to - you know, I had to work at it. But it's a - we were - I was worried about it getting down as towards MILA there after - you know if we had to scrub and go tomorrow night. Boy, I'm sure glad we got you off tonight.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Guess who else is.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: No, I can't - I wouldn't believe that.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Parker can't make it back. He's got to come back on the Gulfstream. So you might have to have Young on for a while after we do a TLI.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Hey, you just wouldn't believe, Bob, the lights you can see in the west right now. It must be absolutely clear.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger, Jack. Sounds spectacular. [Pause.] Jack, people in the room here want to know if you've been down your checklist yet?

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Oh, we got that out of the way in about 5 minutes. Have we missed something?

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: There's a different checklist here we're talking about.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: [Laughter.]

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: If you're talking about the Flight Plan, yes.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger.

a17_0012800.speaker: Evans
a17_0012800.text: What a waste.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: If I'm not mistaken, we must be just south of Arizona now. Is that right, Bob?

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: That looks real good. Yes, you're over Mexico there, and looks like you're - oh - maybe a hundred miles south of the border there.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Okay. I was pretty sure I was looking up in the Phoenix-Tucson complex there.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. Understand.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Beautiful...

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Little better than [garble] Florida.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: The west is always that way. [Pause.] I wish it was daylight so we could see Sonora and that country. That's spectacular, I'll bet you.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. [Garble].

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Man's field of stars on the Earth is competing with the heavens, Bob.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Bob, you're coming through with a large squeal right now in the background.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Understand, [garble].

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Okay, I think we got the Gulf Coast showing up now by the band of lights, Bob.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay, Bob. Assume the booster is still looking good, and we'll be Go for a nominal TLI.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Okay.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: And you're still coming up with a loud squeal.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. [Garble].

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: 17, how do you read?

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Would you believe we're just south of Houston now, Bob? [Long pause.]

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: 17, are you receiving Houston now?

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: All right, Bob. You came up unreadable with the squeal that time.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Am I still squealing? This is Houston.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: That's affirm. You're very loud, almost unreadable with the squeal. [Pause.] Bob, why don't you give us the short count?

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Geno, don't change anything. We think it's a ground site situation here, and just stand by.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: I believe it's in the VHF, Bob. [Long pause.]

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay, Bob. I'm not sure exactly where we are, but I'm looking out - to an awful lot of horiz - lights on the horizon out there at 12 o'clock, and an awful lot of lightning in the clouds out there.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. I - we show you just about over the middle of the Gulf. Looking ahead, you're probably seeing the very southern tip of Florida there.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: It looks like almost the entire Florida peninsula has got lights - out by in it somewhere.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. How does my comm sound to you now, Gene?

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay, give us a quick short count.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. Short count follows: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; short count out.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Bob, you're all right now.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Okay.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: And can you give us a feel for what the final weather was at the Cape - at launch?

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Yeah. Let me get that for you. The reason why we had that problem on the comm is we just handed over from Texas to MILA, and we're - and you're going through MILA now. And it's great. So we have a little problem with our Texas site.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: The television coverage had you all the way through staging very well on - and the S-II ignition. Then, you went right behind a cloud for a while, but they were tracking you pretty well.

a17_0012800.speaker: Cernan
a17_0012800.text: Okay.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: They also - cut in for about a half minute or so and showed a view of the crowd in just the available light from the booster, and it stood out pretty well.

a17_0012800.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0012800.text: Okay, Bob. We're going right over Florida now, looking down at Miami. A beautiful view of the Keys all lit up, and I just saw a shooting star right over Miami.

a17_0012800.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0012800.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 17. How do you read?

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Okay. Lost you there for a minute. We had good signal strength all through that, so I figured it was your problem.

a17_0014128.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014128.text: Roger. We're just waiting here - You ready for the PAD?

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: We were calling you, and you missed us. So you might think about that. Ready for the PAD.

a17_0014128.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014128.text: Okay. It's a TLI plus 90, SPS/G&N; 66953; minus 0.59, plus 1.88; ignition time, 004:40:01.48; minus 0351.8, minus 0000.1, plus 3378.2; roll is 180, 073, 003; Noun 94 [means Noun 44] is - H A is not applicable, H P is plus 0020.1; 3396.4, 4:50, 3380.8; sextant star is number 11, that's 11, 342.4, 32.3. Stand by. 17, Houston; are you still reading me? [Long pause.]

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Hey, Houston, if you read, we're reading you. Got you all the way through the trunnion on sextant star.

a17_0014128.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014128.text: Okay, we'll have to wait and pick you up at Ascension. We just had a keyhole pass at Bermuda, and a little bit of a pass at Vanguard.

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Okay, I'll wait for you to finish that, and on the readback. Okay.

a17_0014128.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014128.text: That's affirmative. Stand by. We've got Vanguard, I can continue on with - after trunnion, the boresight star is not applicable, Jack. Noun 61, plus 13.29, minus 032.00; 1099.2, 34904; GET of .05G, 024:38:09. Want to read back that much of the PAD, Jack?

a17_0014128.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014128.text: Roger, Jack. Good readback except burn time is 4:50 and not 4:54. And we'll be losing you here in about a minute, so wait on the rest of that PAD. Just a reminder for Ron, we'll be standing by at Ascension for the next gyro torquing and we, might have a drift update on the IMU there. [Pause.]

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Okay, he copied that. And we'll wait for the rest of the PAD.

a17_0014128.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0014128.text: Burn time was 4:50 - I think that was when you started to cut out.

a17_0014810.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014810.text: 17, this is Houston through ARIA. How do you read? Over.

a17_0014810.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014810.text: 17, Houston. Through ARIA, how do you read? Over.

a17_0014810.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014810.text: 17, Houston. Through ARIA, how do you read?

a17_0014810.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0014810.text: 17, Houston. How do you read through ARIA?

a17_0014810.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0014810.text: 001:50:33 - This is Apollo Control at 1 hour, 51 minutes. We're getting good telemetry data from Apollo 17 through one of the Apollo Range Instrumented Aircraft out over the Atlantic Ocean. Apollo 17 moving across the Atlantic now towards Africa. And on the next revolution, at about this point, the spacecraft will be on its way to the Moon during the Translunar Injection maneuver. Ignition for that burn is scheduled to occur 1 hour, 21 minutes from now. During launch the Flight Surgeon monitoring heart rates on the three crewmen recorded peak heart rates of 130 for the commander, Gene Cernan,

This is Apollo Control at 1 hour, 51 minutes. We're getting good telemetry data from Apollo 17 through one of the Apollo Range Instrumented Aircraft out over the Atlantic Ocean. Apollo 17 moving across the Atlantic now towards Africa. And on the next revolution, at about this point, the spacecraft will be on its way to the Moon during the Translunar Injection maneuver. Ignition for that burn is scheduled to occur 1 hour, 21 minutes from now. During launch the Flight Surgeon monitoring heart rates on the three crewmen recorded peak heart rates of 130 for the commander, Gene Cernan, also 130 for

a17_0015347.text: This is Apollo Control. We should be acquiring the spacecraft through Ascension in about 5 seconds and reestablishing voice communications with the crew.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Go ahead.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. You're back with us. I'll finish up that TLI plus 90 PAD so we can talk a little here if you want.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Go ahead.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay. Set stars are Sirius and Rigel; R-align is 318; 148; 358. There'll be no ullage. Okay. Down at the bottom of the PAD we've got the P37 for Lift-off plus 9. GET is 009:00; Delta-V T , 4897; longitude, minus 175; GET of 400K, 033:49. Over.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Okay, Bob. Zero - Sirius and Rigel; 318; 148; 358; no ullage; 009:00; 4897; minus 175; 033:49. Over.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay, Jack. Good readback.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Okay, Bob. We had - as usual - up here [laughter] a spectacular sunrise, and Gene wants to talk to you.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: I got some numbers on Ron's P52 for you, Bob.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay; standing by to copy. Go ahead.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Okay. Noun 71 were stars 22 and 24; Noun 05 are all balls; Noun 93s are all minus. They're 00.037, 00.007, and 00.021. That's minus 37, minus 07, and minus 21; and they were torqued at 01:51:40.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay. We copy. [Long pause.]

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Bob, we're over - what might be - intermediate to low stratus that have a very strong crenulation pattern - pulling out some geological terms here. I don't think I've ever seen anything like it flying.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Looks like about a north-south lineation with a very strong crinkling, roughly east-west.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. Copy that; that's interesting. You know, you're just directly over that South Atlantic area. Your - you - your path just kind of kept you going right between the - Africa and South America, right dead center all the way. [Long pause.]

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: And, 17, just for your information, we've searched all the data we can, and we cannot find anything wrong with the spacecraft or the booster at all. Everything is looking real fine, and the only problem in the air is that - those Master Alarms which you have reported - we're not able to tie in anything common yet to any of those things either.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Okay, Bob. We have not had any for - quite some time, I think, since the last time we talked to you about them.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. Understand. We'll probably get a good workout on that after TLI and try and track it down a little more.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Okay. But, also, we have not really been doing much switching since the insertion checklist was complete, either.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. Understand. It's got you glued to the windows, I guess, huh?

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: They are interesting; I'll say that.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: Well, I certainly am, Bob, and - again there's a big - a fairly continuous intermediate cloud deck, I think. And it has patterns comparable to what I've seen on pictures of ice floes.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. Understand.

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: And [pause] of pack ice; I should say pictures of pack ice in the Antarctic. [Pause.]

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: 17, Houston. We've got two questions concerning the Master Alarms. One, do you get the Master Alarm on the LEB also; and, two, do you get the tone with the Master Alarm?

a17_0015347.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0015347.text: We did get the tones. The Master Alarms were on both - panel 1 and panel 3. I can't tell you about the LEB right now. Maybe Ron can.

a17_0015347.speaker: Evans
a17_0015347.text: No, I didn't pay that much attention.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Hey, Bob, there was something interesting I wanted to get around to tell you. The - Mission Timer down in the LEB, when Ron went down there to get things squared away, was about 15 seconds or so behind all the other clocks.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Roger. We copy that.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Okay; and we reset it - re synced it - and it's been running okay. I don't know whether that's a clue to anything or not, but apparently it happened either during launch - or somewhere before we got down there right after insertion.

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Okay, we're going to lose you here in about 9 seconds. You are Go is looking great, and we'll work on it, and if you get another MEV, will you check the LEB for us?

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Yes sir, I sure will do, Bob. We'll see you. What's our next AOS?

a17_0015347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0015347.text: Stand by. Carnarvon at 2:25.

a17_0015347.speaker: Cernan
a17_0015347.text: Thank you.

a17_0015347.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0015347.text: 002:00:41 - This is Apollo Control. Apollo 17 now over the horizon from the Ascension site. Will be reacquiring in about 25 minutes through Carnarvon. And as you heard, CapCom Robert Overmyer advising the crew, we've been getting a good look at all the data, and spacecraft, launch vehicles, look fine. No discernable problems. Gene Cernan did mention one anomaly and that was the mission timer. One of the - one of the numerous clocks aboard the spacecraft which was running about 15 minutes [means seconds] slow - and Cernan said it appeared that it happened either during the launch phase or short

This is Apollo Control. Apollo 17 now over the horizon from the Ascension site. Will be reacquiring in about 25 minutes through Carnarvon. And as you heard, CapCom Robert Overmyer advising the crew, we've been getting a good look at all the data, and spacecraft, launch vehicles, look fine. No discernable problems. Gene Cernan did mention one anomaly and that was the mission timer. One of the - one of the numerous clocks aboard the spacecraft which was running about 15 minutes [means seconds] slow - and Cernan said it appeared that it happened either during the launch phase or shortly before th

a17_0022510.text: This is Apollo Control at 2 hours, 25 minutes. Apollo 17 now approaching the west coast of Australia. And we'll be reacquiring the spacecraft in about 35 seconds. During this pass over Carnarvon, we expect to pass up the first set of numbers to the crew that they'll use in the Translunar Injection burn to put them on their trajectory towards the Moon. That maneuver is scheduled to begin at 47 minutes from now. And we have Acquisition Of Signal a little bit early.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: 17, Houston. How are you doing?

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Stand by. It's Carnarvon at 02:25...

a17_0022510.speaker: Cernan
a17_0022510.text: Thank you.

a17_0022510.speaker: Cernan
a17_0022510.text: I see you're trying.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: 17, Houston. How are you doing?

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Well, we're pretty good. You're wavering here a little bit on signal strength.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Okay. We've got a TLI PAD any time you're ready to copy it, Jack.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Goodness; okay, let me get rid of something here. Ron, I'm putting that right underneath you.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: And, guys, we'd like P00 and Accept, please.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Okay.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: You'll get a CSM state vector if you'll give us P00 and Accept.

a17_0022510.speaker: Cernan
a17_0022510.text: Got P00 and Accept.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Okay. Let me have my favorite PAD.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Okay. Here's the TLI PAD. Time base 6 at 3:02:57; 180, 312, 000; 5:51; Delta-V C is 10359.6, 35582; 000, 345, 040; extraction will be at 300, 165, 320; 312.0, 306.0, 57:10, yaw is 0; ejection time, 4 plus 39 plus 00. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Good readback, Jack; and we'd like Omni Charlie, and it's your computer, and you've got your state vector.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Okay. You've got Omni Charlie. [Pause.] And, Bob, we had almost a completely weather-free pass over Africa and Madagascar. And the scenery - both aesthetically and geologically - was something like I've never seen before, for sure.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Roger.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: We got odds and ends on the tape and quite a bit on the film.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Roger; good show. Are you saying that you didn't have any weather over that southern Africa there?

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Not very much. Barely broken clouds in some places. Most of the countryside was clear.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Roger.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: There were - patterns - like I haven't even seen in textbooks. Maybe I haven't been looking enough, but some of the desert and grassland patterns were - had the appearance of ice crystals almost, except on a megascale, if you - have ever looked at ice crystals in sand.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Or, better yet, ice crystals on your car window when you - get out early in the morning up in northern areas.

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: Roger. And just be advised, we'll be standing by for the Go/No-Go for Pyro Arm when we get to Hawaii, and we'll be giving you a Go for TLI about that time.

a17_0022510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0022510.text: Okay; and we'll be ready. [Pause.]

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: And, Ron, in - on the Launch Checklist, on 2-25, on the manual and nominal S-IVB TLI-1, add 34 degrees on the nominal PAD for all the pitch angles; and on the manual PAD, add 34.5 degrees to all the pitch angles, and you'll have it right.

a17_0022510.speaker: Evans
a17_0022510.text: Okay, Bob. You [garble]...

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: And...

a17_0022510.speaker: Evans
a17_0022510.text: ...let me get set. That's - okay, we'll just add 34 to the nominal and 34.5 to all the manual ones [garble]...

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: And you'll want to do that on your cue card also, Ron.

a17_0022510.speaker: Evans
a17_0022510.text: Yeah, that's affirm. [Pause.]

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: And we're about ready to LOS; we'll see you at Hawaii.

a17_0022510.speaker: Cernan
a17_0022510.text: Okay, Bob, we'll see you...

a17_0022510.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0022510.text: 02 plus 50 at Hawaii.

a17_0022510.speaker: Cernan
a17_0022510.text: Okay, 50. And we'll be into our TLI checklist, and - we'll be ready for that Pyro Arm.

a17_0023232.text: This is Apollo Control. We'll be reacqui - reacquiring the spacecraft in about 18 minutes. And during that pass over at Carnarvon, and we've passed up the numbers to the crew they'll use in the Translunar Injection maneuver. The burn is targeted to last 5 minutes, 51 seconds with a change in velocity of some 10,359 feet per second [3,157 m/s], accelerating Apollo 17 to the required speed to get it into an orbit that'll intercept the Moon. And the time of ignition, 300 - 3 hours, 12 minutes, 35 seconds; and we're showing an ejection time of 4 hours, 39 minutes. The Transposition and Docking man

a17_0024900.text: This is Apollo Control at 2 hours, 49 minutes. We're standing by now to acquire radio contact with Apollo 17 through Hawaii. During this Hawaiian pass we're getting another good look at spacecraft and launch vehicle systems. The last look we had through Carnarvon everything looked very good. Flight Director Gene Kranz, going over the status for his flight controllers, observed that there appeared to be no problems that would interfere with TLI and we'd expect to have a normal Translunar Injection about 23 minutes from now as Apollo 17 completes its state-side pass and moves out over the Atlant

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Apollo 17, Houston.

a17_0024900.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0024900.text: Go ahead.

a17_0024900.speaker: Evans
a17_0024900.text: Houston, this is Apollo 17. Go ahead.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Hey, Ron, you're sounding great. Good voice here.

a17_0024900.speaker: Evans
a17_0024900.text: Oh, yeah, we've got things all set up here and we're kind of standing by for a logic check whenever you guys can give us a Go. [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Roger. As soon as we get some TM in here, we'll give you a Go. [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Evans
a17_0024900.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: 17, Houston. We're ready for the logic check.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Okay, Bob. [Pause.] Okay. Wait 1. [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Okay. SECS Arm breakers are closed.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Roger.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Okay; and Logic 1 is On, Mark it...

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: ...and Logic 2 is On...

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: ...Mark it. [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: 17, you're Go for Pyro Arm.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Thank you; understand Go for Pyro Arm.

a17_0024900.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0024900.text: And, Bob, in case you're interested, there - all through the nightside pass here - there's a - quite a strong - well - stronger than I would have ever expected - horizon glow off to the north. I suspect that, I think Gene said a while ago that it's around on his side also.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Roger. Guys, I've got the word you wanted to hear; you are Go for TLI - you're Go for the Moon.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Okay, Robert. Understand. America and Challenger with their S-IVB are Go for TLI.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: You're a sweet talker.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: We try to please here, Gene. [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0024900.text: You know, somehow, Bob, I knew you were going to say that - we were Go - and that you try to please.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: We've been working together too long, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0024900.text: Not long enough, yet. [Long pause.]

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: And, 17; Houston. You're about 1 minute from LOS, and we'll pick you up at Goldstone at about 3 hours and 00 minutes; and that's only a couple of minutes prior to time base 6 start.

a17_0024900.speaker: Cernan
a17_0024900.text: Okay, Bob. We'll be with you.

a17_0024900.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0024900.text: Roger.

a17_0024900.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0024900.text: Bob, that glow is actually above the horizon, just in case you're curious. I can see - stars below the top of the glow - down closer to the Earth.

a17_0030115.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030115.text: 17, Houston. We're with you again, and you're looking good.

a17_0030115.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030115.text: And, Bob, we've got the Pyros Armed now.

a17_0030115.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030115.text: And you can expect some different Omni calls as we go LOS and AOS again.

a17_0030115.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030115.text: Sep light is On, on time.

a17_0030115.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030115.text: And it shows time base 6 right on time, Gene.

a17_0030115.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030115.text: I'll just switch, Bob. I won't give you a call.

a17_0030115.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030115.text: Sep light was Out on time.

a17_0030115.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030115.text: 003:04:21 - This is Apollo Control at 3 hours, 4 minutes. We are now some 8 minutes away from ignition. Everything looking good for the Translunar Injection maneuver. The combined S-IVB, the Saturn third stage and the spacecraft with an orbital weight of 308,298 pounds [139,842 kg] at the start of this maneuver.

This is Apollo Control at 3 hours, 4 minutes. We are now some 8 minutes away from ignition. Everything looking good for the Translunar Injection maneuver. The combined S-IVB, the Saturn third stage and the spacecraft with an orbital weight of 308,298 pounds [139,842 kg] at the start of this maneuver.

a17_0030615.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030615.text: I was just checking with you; you're so quiet down there, we almost forgot you were there.

a17_0030615.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030615.text: Roger. Don't want to forget me. We're just watching everything; we can't find anything wrong, so we're just trying to keep quiet here.

a17_0030615.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030615.text: Okay, Bob. We're watching the S-IVB tanks pressurize.

a17_0030615.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030615.text: You ought to look for the good things rather than the bad.

a17_0030615.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030615.text: Well, that's good when we don't find anything wrong.

a17_0030615.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030615.text: 17, the chilldown is in progress, and the tank pressures are looking good.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: 17, Houston. You are Go at 3 minutes prior to ignition. You're looking good, and you're going to - we're going to have A - ARIA coverage all the way through the burn until Ascension.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Roger; understand, Bob. 57:10, ORDEAL Operate...

And we're coming up now on 2 minutes until ignition. This burn, again, will be a 5 minute, 51 second maneuver. The S-IVB engine delivering about 225,000 pounds [1 MN] of thrust, and it will be increasing the spacecraft velocity in the current state of about 25,000 feet per second up to about 35,585 feet per second.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: We're in average g.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. We confirm it. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: SEP light On at 3:06.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:11:37 - And booster reports the ullage engines are on. This is to settle the propellants in the S-IVB prior to ignition. We're at 53 seconds now from ignition.
And booster reports the ullage engines are on. This is to settle the propellants in the S-IVB prior to ignition. We're at 53 seconds now from ignition.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: 17, you're looking great on the final status check here, and you're Go for TLI. [Long pause.]
20 seconds now to ignition and we're maintaining communications with the spacecraft through one of the ARIA, Apollo Range Instrumented Aircraft.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: [Garble] 42, the SEP lights are Out.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. [Long pause.]
10 seconds.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: The light's on and we have ignition. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:12:46 - And, very faintly we copy the crew reporting S-IVB ignition and that's confirmed by the telemetry and booster reports the thrust looks good on the S-IVB.
And, very faintly we copy the crew reporting S-IVB ignition and that's confirmed by the telemetry and booster reports the thrust looks good on the S-IVB.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: 17, Houston. You're looking good, and the thrust is Go.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Bob, you're down in the mud, but we're Go onboard at 20 seconds.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:13:11 - And telemetry data from the Saturn Instrument Unit shows the velocity increasing up now to 26,000 feet per second [7,900 m/s], beginning to climb ever more rapidly.
And telemetry data from the Saturn Instrument Unit shows the velocity increasing up now to 26,000 feet per second [7,900 m/s], beginning to climb ever more rapidly.

a17_0030937.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030937.text: [Garble] antenna. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:13:24 - This burn was initiated at an altitude of about 97 nautical miles [180 km] above Earth, and when finished, the spacecraft will be at about 150 [nautical] miles [280 km] above Earth, and on its way to the Moon, some 213,000 miles - nautical miles [394,500 km] away.

This burn was initiated at an altitude of about 97 nautical miles [180 km] above Earth, and when finished, the spacecraft will be at about 150 [nautical] miles [280 km] above Earth, and on its way to the Moon, some 213,000 miles - nautical miles [394,500 km] away.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: One minute, Houston in the blind, and we're Go.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger, Gene. We can barely hear you through the ARIA, but you're Go. [Pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030937.text: You have reasonable signal strength, but you are unreadable. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:14:10 - Very weak voice communications and Booster says the data is now static but at last look, everything looked normal.
Very weak voice communications and Booster says the data is now static but at last look, everything looked normal.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Everything's Go at 1:30. [Pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Confirm a PU shift, and Go at 1:45. [Pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: 17, Houston, We can confirm PU shift, and you are Go. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:14:55 - And that was CapCom Robert Overmyer confirming to the crew that our data showed the Saturn shifting its propellant utilization for a most efficient utilization of the propellant.
And that was CapCom Robert Overmyer confirming to the crew that our data showed the Saturn shifting its propellant utilization for a most efficient utilization of the propellant.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Okay, Houston, 2:30 - in the blind - we're still Go.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger, 17. You're Go; looking great.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Okay, Bob. Got that. Understand we're Go from the ground; and it's a good ride, although it's rumbling around a little bit.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:15:31 - Coming up now 3 minutes into the burn and velocity approaching 30,000 feet per second [9,100 m/s].
Coming up now 3 minutes into the burn and velocity approaching 30,000 feet per second [9,100 m/s].

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Three minutes, and we are Go.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger, Gene. [Pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Bob, we're going to TLI right through sunrise.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger; understand.

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:16:01 - Gene Cernan reporting the TLI burn has taken them out of darkness and into sunrise now.
Gene Cernan reporting the TLI burn has taken them out of darkness and into sunrise now.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Okay, 3:30 is Go. We have - 17 is Go at 3:30.

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:16:10 - And, we're showing a velocity of 30,463 feet per second [9285 m/s].
And, we're showing a velocity of 30,463 feet per second [9285 m/s].

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger, 17. [Long pause.]

a17_0030937.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0030937.text: 003:16:31 - Apollo 17 now about 107 nautical miles [198 km] above Earth and continuing to climb ever more rapidly.
Apollo 17 now about 107 nautical miles [198 km] above Earth and continuing to climb ever more rapidly.
4 minutes and 30 seconds now and everything continuing to look good. Apollo 17 at a velocity of 32,000 feet per second [9,754 m/s].

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Okay, Bob, 17 is Go at 4:30. You're still unreadable.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. How do you read me? You are Go, by the way.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Okay, we got you that time. Understand we're Go on the ground, and we're still Go here, and we're TLI-ing right through sunrise.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Understand. [Long pause.]
5 minutes now, less than 1 minute to go, and Booster engineer reports we're very close to the nominal predicted shutdown time.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: 17, Houston. Your burn time is nominal.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: Roger. Understand burn time, nominal. [Long pause.]
Shutdown time now in about 21 seconds. Showing a velocity of 33,000 feet per second [10,058 m/s]. Altitude now approaching 150 [nautical] miles [278 km].

a17_0030937.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0030937.text: Cut-off at 52.

a17_0030937.speaker: Evans
a17_0030937.text: [Laughter.] Did you read the DSKY?

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: We don't have the DSKY. You have to read it to us, Ron.

a17_0030937.speaker: Evans
a17_0030937.text: Okay. V I is - I got a 00 and a 00 and Noun 95 V I is 35573 - is a plus 9.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: And, Bob, the EMS is minus - EMS is minus 19.4, minus 19.4.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Roger. We copy that.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: And it was an auto cut-off - auto cut-off on time.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Understand a guided cut-off on time. Looking great.

a17_0030937.speaker: Cernan
a17_0030937.text: And I am watching tank pressures - are venting, the tanks are venting.

a17_0030937.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0030937.text: Understand. The tanks are venting.

a17_0032004.text: And, we're still getting communications through the Apollo Range Instrumented Aircraft. We'll be picking up through Ascension shortly, at which time we'd expect the communications to improve, the noise to drop off. From Gene Cernan's report, also from the reports from Ron Evans, it appeared that that Translunar Injection was extremely close to nominal. The crew read a cut-off time of 5 minutes, 52 seconds. The premaneuver prediction was 5 minutes, 51 seconds. And the cut-off velocity appeared to be very, very close to the planned normal. Booster engineer Frank Van Rensselaer reports the booste
And Booster engineer now predicting that the maneuver to separation attitude will begin at about 3 hours, 33 minutes, 27 seconds.

a17_0032004.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032004.text: Okay, Houston, how do you read?

a17_0032004.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032004.text: Okay. I picked it up a little bit. How do you read now?

a17_0032004.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032004.text: Okay. I hope you got all that. It was a beautiful burn, right through sunrise. Did you get the numbers?

a17_0032004.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0032004.text: Yeah, we copied your V I and your EMS numbers, and we've got a number for you. Maneuver start time will be at 3 plus 33 plus 27. [Long pause.]

a17_0032004.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032004.text: Okay, we got you. Maneuver at 03:33:27.

a17_0032004.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032004.text: You guys didn't tell us we couldn't see anything going through the sunrise.

a17_0032004.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0032004.text: 17, Houston. We're making plans here for a spacecraft Sep time of 03 plus 43. [Pause.]

a17_0032736.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0032736.text: 17, Houston. We're copying cabin press of 5.9 this time.

a17_0032736.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0032736.text: Roger. We - we just got it, Bob.

a17_0032942.text: This is Apollo Control at 3 hours, 30 minutes. The Flight Dynamics Officer has just reported that initial tracking, following the Translunar Injection burn, shows the spacecraft to be on a very nominal trajectory, and a relatively small midcourse correction indicated at this time. The pre-burn prediction on that first midcourse correction was around 5 feet per second and we expect that that will be updated as we get additional tracking following the burn.

In about 3 minutes the spacecraft should - the launch vehicle should be - begin maneuvering to the proper attitude for separation and we're predicting separation to occur at about 3 hours, 43 minutes - or about 13 minutes from now.

a17_0033204.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033204.text: Frame 65 for the LMPs mag November November.
About 10 seconds now until the Saturn third stage begins maneuvering into the proper separation attitude.
And Booster engineer reports from telemetry data that the booster has begun maneuvering into the proper attitude for spacecraft separation.

a17_0033204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033204.text: Okay. We - we are maneuvering, Houston.

a17_0033204.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033204.text: Now we've got a few very bright particles or fragments or something that go drifting by as we maneuver.

a17_0033204.speaker: Evans
a17_0033204.text: There's a whole bunce of big ones on my window down there - just bright.

a17_0033204.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033204.text: It looks like the Fourth of July out of Ron's window. [Pause.]

a17_0033204.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033204.text: Yeah. Now you can see some of them in shape. They're very jagged, angular fragments that are tumbling.

a17_0033204.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033204.text: Roger. They look like fluid of some sort?

a17_0033204.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033204.text: Not to me. They look like pieces of something.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Bob, for the most part, these fragments are not - or are tumbling at a very slow rate. I tried a couple pictures of them - different settings. You may get an idea of what, at least, the patterns look like.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. I've got you. We're all ears on these fragments if you think you can figure out what they might be.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Well, you know I - I don't know. There are a number of possibilities. If you had some kind of a - I got the impression maybe they were curved a little bit, as if they might be - off the side of the S-IVB. And that's a wild guess...

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. RCS Logic is [garble]...

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: ...ice chunks, possibly. Or maybe there's paint coming off of it.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Rog. I noticed on one trip up the elevator last week near one of the flags. I thought it was on the S-II, but it might have been on the S-IVB. Looked like it was peeling. Maybe that's what you've got.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: And the S-IVB maneuver is complete.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: [Garble] on Main A.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. We'll set the old clock.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. And the - with the maneuver complete, the fragment field is essentially static, except for very slight tumbling within the fragments.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. Copy that.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Every once in a while, a fragment of considerably higher velocity than the others goes across my window. But that's very rare.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Hey, that's that field of view I saw out my window, Jack, do you see it now?

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Yes.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: And, Bob. At least, there - there's no apparent relative motion between fragments.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. Understand.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: I'll take two pictures about a minute apart if I can. And it'll be Frame 70. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Okay. Frame 70.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: And, Bob. This is Geno. My impression is that they are - flat, flake-like particles. Some may be 6 inches across. And, although there's no relative motion between the two, most of them seem to be twinkling. And I think, for the most part, they're all moving away from us.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, Gene. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. We've got 0180 and 0 on the old thumbwheels.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. Trans Control is Armed.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: [Garble] two Armed.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Controller number 2 is Armed.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: [Garble] SECS Logic [garble].

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. SECS Logic is Closed; SECS Arm are Closed; Logic Power is On.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: 17, Houston. You have a Go for T&D.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay. A Go for T&D. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. We'll Arm the Pyros. [Pause.] And we'll hit the GDC Align.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: And maneuver's complete. Okay 0180 and 0, on the GDC. [Pause.] No. It's just [garble] it's kind of diddling.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. Delta-V in Normal. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: S-IVB, okay. [Pause.] Okay, switches are all set.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. Let's start the DET.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Tickity-tick-tickity.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Houston. We're running at 59:30.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. That's Launch Vehicle Sep, push button.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: MC in Auto. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Next?

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Separation, Houston.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, check the covers. Okay. And check the other ones off.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: They're all...

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, I'm going to start the - My god, look at the junk! Okay; there's 15 seconds. Pitch her up. Okay, we'll Proceed on the... [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: [Garble] normal [garble].

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, we've already Proceeded, James. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, we've checked her out. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Houston, we're right in the middle of a snowstorm [laughter].
