a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. And we'd like Omni Delta.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Hey, look at that burst. It's going to be bright as all get out.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: And there goes one of the SLA panels.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Yep. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: We're not there yet. Long ways to go yet. It's on the other side of the Earth, if the simulator's any good. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0033704.text: 003:44:07 - Apollo 17 now in the process of turning around after having separated, blown the pyrotechnic charges that separates the spacecraft from the Saturn third stage.
Apollo 17 now in the process of turning around after having separated, blown the pyrotechnic charges that separates the spacecraft from the Saturn third stage.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Oh, man!

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: There goes another SLA panel, Houston, going the other way.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Yes.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: I've...

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Hey, there's the booster!

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. Bet you never saw the SLA panels on the simulator.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: No, but we've got the booster and is she pretty. Challenger's just sitting in her nest.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. We'd like Omni Bravo, now, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, I'll plus-X it. We'll see the - oh, you can't see [garble]. [Pause.] Okay. Oh, I can't see my COAS.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: And, Houston, some of the particles going by the window...

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, did you change the DAC?

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: ...were obvious enough - fairly obvious to me - paint.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Okay. We'll buy that. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay. There it is. [Pause.] Okay, did you change the DAP? Got Att 1/Rate 2? [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay, Houston, you want the High Gain? [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. We're standing by for it, and the angles as published on L/3-3 should be good.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, it's flying pretty good. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, we're in Reacq here. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Houston, how do you read? We don't have a very good knock - lock on here in Reacq.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, Jack. We're reading you pretty good - voice. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. It looks like it's improving. It dropped off - signal strength dropped off, and now it's picking up again.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: We're getting good signal now, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Jack, the High Gain is looking good. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Oh, okay.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: I'm guessing. I don't know - about a hundred [garble]...

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: That's good news. It seemed to smoo - slew very smoothly, so it looks all right.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, Jack.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Att 1/Rate 2? [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: I can't tell you too much, Bob, from the center seat other than Captain America is very intent on getting Challenger at the moment.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. I can believe that. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Yeah, I'm coming in a little slow, but we've got plenty of time. [Long pause.]
Ron Evans now at the controls of America . Now moving in for the docking with Lunar Module Challenger .

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay, Houston. While we're moving in here, I can see a few chunks of that platy material, possibly paint, down in the SLA sort of bouncing around between the S-IVB and the LM.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: But, so far, LM looks very clean. Can't see anything abnormal from this view yet.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Isn't it, though? That thing is really stable out there.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Yeah. Can you see it at all, Gene? [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Got one little chunk coming out - it just came out of the SLA, and it's spinning along a long axis, and it looks very stable.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Every once in a while, a small particle flies off of it though.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: How big of a chunk are you talking about, Jack?

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Say again?

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: How big an item are you talking about?

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Oh, I - reference to the thrusters, about the same diameter as the thruster on the LM.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Oh, Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: That's how long it was, and about - oh, a fifth that thick or that wide.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: And I don't think - I don't think it's more than a quarter of an inch or maybe even less thick. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: That same particle, Bob, came by and as it was spinning, it was throwing off pieces of itself - radially out.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. We copy.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: There's small ones come floating by and it looked like flakes. [Long pause.] And I think I caught three of the four SLA panels going as we were maneuvering. I've got one out the hatch window now. It's quite a ways out...

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: ...and tumbling in all three axes.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: And I saw the fourth one out my side, so we saw them all. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Area around the two spacecraft is cleaned up pretty well by now. There are just a few fragments moving around. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Now she's coming in. [Long pause.]

The crew of Apollo 17 describing what appear to be paint or possibly ice flaking off the Saturn third stage. But somewhat puzzling at this point is just exactly what the flakes or particles that they're describing might be. And Apollo 17 in the process of docking with the Lunar Module, preparatory to extracting the LM from the Saturn third stage. This occuring at some 5,300 nautical miles [9,800 km] from Earth. And we're watching the spacecraft velocity drop off rapidly as that altitude increases rapidly. The velocity which at the Translunar Injection cut-off was around 35,000 feet per second

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Rover looks in good shape, so far.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, Jack. Can you see down on that quad? Is that what you're looking at?

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Yes, I'm looking right at it. [Pause.] And I got a good view of the MESA top anyway. It's pretty well covered, but it looks all right also.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: All the antennas look good; thruster quads all look great. I could see all four of them a minute ago.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, about 10 feet there, Gene. Stand by for a [garble] on the barber pole. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: All right; in good shape. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: About now. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Capture, Houston.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. We copy.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, we're Free; rates look pretty good. [Pause.] Let's lock it together.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: Okay. You ready?

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Ready. She's lined up not bad.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Prime 1.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Mark it. Stand by.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Here she comes. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Ka-chunk. By gosh!

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay, Houston, ripple fire; but we still have number A barber pole.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. We copy.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: And we have a Master - and a Master Alarm.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: We got - we got the most of the latches, but A is barber pole, and B is gray.

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, check both circuit breakers; they're In. Yeah, Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: We had one clear fire, maybe one or two latches and then a ripple fire on the rest.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: And, by the way, I had a good view into the AOT, and I can still look in there, and it's very clean.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0033704.text: In fact...

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Ron and Gene, we saw your Master Alarm. Did you have any - anything on the matrix light up?

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: No, not a thing. I looked.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger.

a17_0033704.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0033704.text: 003:58:47 - That appeared to be a repeat of the Master Alarm that has been reported several times previously by the crew. They get the alarm light and tone, but when they look for the exact location of precise indication of what's wrong, it's not there, indicating some sort of a spurious response by the Master Alarm to a problem that doesn't exist.

That appeared to be a repeat of the Master Alarm that has been reported several times previously by the crew. They get the alarm light and tone, but when they look for the exact location of precise indication of what's wrong, it's not there, indicating some sort of a spurious response by the Master Alarm to a problem that doesn't exist.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay, Bob, we're going to go ahead and take a look at that docking malfunction before we press on here further and check this barber pole out.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Roger, We're working some words up here. We'll be back with you in a second on that, Gene.

a17_0033704.speaker: Cernan
a17_0033704.text: Okay. We're down on the checklist through the EDS Power breakers, Open.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Understand. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: And, Houston, in case we didn't tell you, it's talkback A that's barber pole.

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Understand. We have it. [Long pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0033704.text: Say - say, Gene, we don't think it's a problem. We'll find out what it is when you get in. We think we should just press right on with the Flight Plan checklist and keep going. [Pause.]

a17_0033704.speaker: Evans
a17_0033704.text: Okay, we concur with that. Okay, we'll press on, Bob. [Long pause.]

a17_0040329.speaker: Evans
a17_0040329.text: Okay, O 2 Heater number 3 went to Auto. [Pause.]

a17_0040808.speaker: Cernan
a17_0040808.text: Okay, Bob. We're reading a Delta-P of greater than 4, and I'm going to open the Pressure Equalization Valve now.

a17_0040808.speaker: Cernan
a17_0040808.text: Okay, the Delta-P is coming down, Bob.

a17_0040808.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0040808.text: Gene, while you're watching that, I just thought you'd be interested. We talked to some of our friends down at the Cape who watched the launch, and they said you were aglow all the way until you faded into - you couldn't tell you from a star. They saw staging, and they could just see you as a star way off in the distance until you faded out. Not a cloud in the way at all.

a17_0040808.speaker: Cernan
a17_0040808.text: Beautiful. Okay, we're at - we're at 2, and we're monitoring it for 3 minutes.

a17_0040808.speaker: Evans
a17_0040808.text: And, Houston. While we're checking the integrity here, on mag Alpha Alpha, there's about 50 per cent.

a17_0040808.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0040808.text: Mag Alpha Alpha, 50 per cent. Roger.

a17_0041159.text: This is Apollo Control at 4 hours, 12 minutes. The crew aboard Apollo 17 at this time pressing ahead with their preparations for separating the Lunar Module and Command Module, now docked together, from the Saturn third stage. You heard some conversation earlier about an indication that all of the docking latches have not locked up. There are 12 of these latches in the docking mechanism, six of which are instrumented, and of the six that are instrumented, there was an indication that one of those may not have latched. However, we are confident that more than enough latches have locked up to as

a17_0041159.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041159.text: Okay, Bob. That's 3 minutes. It's - Delta-P change is less than 0.1.

a17_0041159.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0041159.text: 004:13:11 - That report from Gene Cernan indicating that they have a good seal at the docking interface. Once the hatch is removed between the two vehicles, the crew will get a good look at all of those docking latches and they will be able to tell how many - if any of them didn't latch up. We're pushing ahead now for - for extracting the Lunar Module, separating from the Saturn third stage at Ground Elapsed Time of 4 hours, 39 minutes.

That report from Gene Cernan indicating that they have a good seal at the docking interface. Once the hatch is removed between the two vehicles, the crew will get a good look at all of those docking latches and they will be able to tell how many - if any of them didn't latch up. We're pushing ahead now for - for extracting the Lunar Module, separating from the Saturn third stage at Ground Elapsed Time of 4 hours, 39 minutes.

a17_0041159.speaker: Evans
a17_0041159.text: Okay, you want cabin's at 4.8 now; Repress is about empty. [Pause.] Okay. No, not yet, it's still getting a little bit. [Pause.]

a17_0041159.speaker: Evans
a17_0041159.text: That Repress Package Valve is kind of noisy. [Pause.]

a17_0041159.speaker: Evans
a17_0041159.text: That's all the Repress O 2 . We'll turn that Off.

a17_0041159.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041159.text: Okay, Houston, the Repress Package is empty now, and we're down to a Delta-P of 0.2.

a17_0041159.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041159.text: And, 17. Just be advised, you're going to have an S-IVB non-propulsive vent start 04:18:27- You've got about 3 minutes on that.

a17_0041703.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0041703.text: Can you reach [garble] there?

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Yeah, I'll get them.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Bob. We seem to be holding Delta-P at about 0.2. I suspect that's probably zero.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger. We copy that. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0041703.text: And the cabin pressure's about 4.5. You want us to wait until 5 psi for the Emergency Cabin Pressure Selects?

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Negative on that. Let's just go ahead and just press on.

a17_0041703.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0041703.text: Okay. [Pause.] They should be Both.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Emergency register working. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Coming down though, Gene. Let's wait until it gets down a little ways. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Yeah.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Yeah. Straight up and down as well. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Up point one. Must be the non-propulsive vent that's banging. [Laughter.] Here comes all the - look at all the stuff going again. It's really glowing.

a17_0041703.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0041703.text: Your non-propulsive vent gives quite a glow.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: It looks like a rainbow. Dark one. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay. Repress Package to Fill. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: That ought to take the surge tank down a little bit. About at what? 400? [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: 500 on the surge. [Pause.] No, they ought to be closed off by now, I think. Yeah.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Go ahead.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Rog. Be advised, you don't have to wait until 5 psi cabin to go ahead and open the hatch.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, we're not, Bob. We're pressing on with it now.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay, it looks like we're going to maintain about 400 on the surge. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay? [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Houston. The hatch is coming out.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: [Laughter.] I don't know what you're going to do with it. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Put it up here in the - in the - on the couch. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: There we go.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Hey, that's a lot lighter than it used to be. [Laughter.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: There's going to be a lot of happy people down there, Bob. I haven't checked them all, but visually, they're all locked.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Understand, Gene. All of them are locked.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Let me give them a good check.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Yeah. You'd better check them, because we got a barber pole on that one. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, here's one that didn't come over.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: What is the position of it?

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: 7... [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: 7 and 9? [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Bob. Maybe we aren't all going to be so happy.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Go ahead.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, 7, 9, and 10 - the handle is flush; the bungee is vertical, but the handle is not locked down, and the - and the red button is showing. And I can pull each one of them back slowly. I haven't done anything with them. That's 7, 9, and 10.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger. We copy that. The handle is flush; the bungees are vertical, but the handle is not locked down, and the red button is showing on 7, 9, and 10.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: That's affirm. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Bob. Bob, I just pushed the handle on 10 home a little bit and it did lock. And the red button is flush. So that leaves me 9 and 7.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger; understand. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Geno, go ahead and try the handle on 9 and 7; and, if that doesn't work, cock them and refire them starting with 9, please.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay; the handle doesn't work. I'll have to recock them.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: When you trip it with your - did you cock it twice?

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Yeah.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: And it took two cocks to make it go?

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Yes.

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, 9 cocked twice; it tripped. It is overcenter and locked.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger. How about the barber pole now?

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay. Wait a minute, I've got - Docking Probe Main A circuit breaker's In and gone to Retract, and it's gray.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Okay...

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Aha! That did it.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger. [Pause.] And... [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: Okay, Bob. Cocked 7 twice and tripped it, and it's overcenter and locked.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Roger.

a17_0041703.speaker: Cernan
a17_0041703.text: I think that takes care of them all.

a17_0041703.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0041703.text: Good show. [Long pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Okay, [pause] Docking Probe circuit breakers are Out and Extend/Retract is Off. [Pause.]

a17_0041703.speaker: Evans
a17_0041703.text: Because it belongs on the probe. [Garble] it's painted yellow, it belongs on the probe.

a17_0042834.speaker: Cernan
a17_0042834.text: Okay, Bob. The umbilicals are connected.

a17_0042834.speaker: Cernan
a17_0042834.text: Okay, Houston, 7-Delta on the test meter is now reading 1.0, it jumped up to 2.6, and is now back to 1.0.

a17_0042834.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0042834.text: Roger. We copy. That's good. [Long pause.]

This is Apollo Control at 4 hours, 30 minutes. About nine minutes from now, the crew will be firing the pyrotechnic charges that separate the Lunar Module docked to the Command Module from the Saturn third stage, and springs will push the LM/CSM back away from the launch vehicle at a rate of about 1 foot per second. And at Ground Elapsed Time of 4 hours, 52 minutes; the launch vehicle will yaw to the proper attitude for an evasive manuever of about 10 feet per second to be performed at a Ground Elapsed Time of about 5 hours, 3 minutes. This will increase the separation distance to assure no ch

a17_0042834.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0042834.text: There we go. Okay. There, we're going up in the tunnel.

a17_0042834.speaker: Cernan
a17_0042834.text: Okay, Bob, the hatch is back in. [Pause.]

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: Rog. We've got some new - new angles here for you. [Pause.]

a17_0043424.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043424.text: Stand by a minute, and let me find a place to copy them.

a17_0043424.speaker: Evans
a17_0043424.text: What - what kind of angles are they, Bob?

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: They're your Noun 22 attitude maneuver for APS burn out of the hatch window. They're in the middle of the page L/3-5.

a17_0043424.speaker: Evans
a17_0043424.text: Wait 1. We're not quite with you.

a17_0043424.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043424.text: Okay. I think I'm with you at 3-7; go.

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: It's on 3-5, Jack, middle of the page there. Those Noun 22s.

a17_0043424.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043424.text: Okay, I take it back; 3-5, middle of the page.

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: Okay. You notice there's three angles there - 270, make that 274. [Pause.]

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: And the - no, the next one, the 129-8, change that to 164. [Pause.] And 4.3 on the yaw, change that to zero. It's close enough; zero on the yaw. [Pause.]

a17_0043424.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043424.text: Roger, and the High Gain angles that you've got on the Flight Plan are close enough and should do it. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.text: Telemetry data now shows the crew loading the information into the spacecraft Digital AutoPilot in preparation for separation from the Saturn third stage. That should be occurring in the next minute or so.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay. We're 6 frames a second. [Pause.] Okay, what - what did [garble]. Range [garble]. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, I'll - I'll leave it at 10 feet and about an f - f/8. [Long pause.] Okay, [garble] at set. [Long pause.] Because I had that one to 0180 to 0. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Bob. We're aligning our GDC, and the next thing we'll pick up will be the SECS Arm circuit breakers. And we'll give you a call on the Logic.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Roger, Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Bob. While we're waiting, does the balance on the...

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: I see what you mean [laughter].

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: ...H 2 and O 2 flow in fuel cell 3 - well, actually, in all three fuel cells, look pretty good to you? [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Jack, the flows look just right for the current.

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Okay. Used to seeing them more or less lined up, and I hadn't calculated any farther than that.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Roger.

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: O 2 - O 2 seems a little higher H 2 , relatively speaking. [Laughter.] [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay. That's pretty close. [Pause.] Verified: SECS Arm breakers are Closed.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Houston. We're ready to come up with the Logic. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Houston, Logic 1 is coming on now and Logic 2.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: And, Houston, just to keep track of EMS null bias check that time, was - went from 100 to 100.7 in 100 seconds. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: 17, we'd like to just verify on that top line S-IVB/LM Sep circuit breakers - both of them are Closed?

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, we'll verify them again. We doublechecked them.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Okay, we just didn't hear your call and we want to make sure of that. Didn't want to miss anything here.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay. They are - they are verified Closed, and Jack just checked them again.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Okay. You are Go for Pyro Arm and Go for extraction.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Go for Pyro Arm; Go for Pyro extraction - or LM extraction [laughter].

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Pyro Arm.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, we'll Arm the old Pyros. There's Pyro A; Pyro B.

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Servo Power number 1 [garble].

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: TVC Servo Power, AC 1.

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Trans Control Power, up and On.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Trans Control Power is On.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Rot Controllers are Armed. [Pause.] Okay, I'll wait just a little bit on that - EMS to Normal. Get Delta-V [garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, EMS to Normal? Push right there. Yep.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay; on my mark, the S-IVB/LM Sep will come on.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, and then I'll back it off to... [pause]. Okay?

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, on my mark, S-IVB/LM Sep: 3, 2, 1...

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Mark it. Okay, we got it.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Oh, ho! Man, did we! There she goes. Yeah; LM came with us.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, we're CMC, Auto. All right. We've got six tenths. It's all right. Okay, whoopee-dee-doo! [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Safe the Pyros. [Pause.] Okay, Logic'S Off. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: SECS - SECS Arm breakers are Open. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0043913.text: 004:46:17 - This is Apollo Control. America and Challenger are on their own. LM ejection occurred at 4 hours, 45 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; at an altitude of 13,000 nautical miles [24,000 km] from Earth.
This is Apollo Control. America and Challenger are on their own. LM ejection occurred at 4 hours, 45 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; at an altitude of 13,000 nautical miles [24,000 km] from Earth.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Now I think we ought to go to the maneuver pretty quick. Otherwise, the S-IVB will be so far away you can't see it. [Pause.] Okay, you ready to maneuver?

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay, CMC in Auto, caged. Away we go. [Pause.] That - that [garble] wasn't as bad as the original Sep. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Came right out, though.

a17_0043913.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0043913.text: Mapping Camera and Pan Camera are Off. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Okay. [Pause.] Power's Off. Hey, Jack. Hand me the Hasselblad. I think we're bowing the right direction. [Pause.] Yeah, the Moon is there. The Earth is - that's the Earth. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Servo Power's Off, yes.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: The Earth just fills up window 5. [Pause.] Okay, f, infinity, about a 250th, f/11.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: What - what do you have? A zero in there? Hey, I lost my watch. Turn the AC Off. Yeah, AC's Off. Whoo, what a beauty! What a beauty! Yeah, the Earth. I can't see the S-IVB. It's gone. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Look at that.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah, Madagascar and Africa. Mada... [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: [Garble] see it.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Got to be.

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah, as soon as I find the S-IVB, we'll... [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Hey, there's Antarctica. It's all full of snow. [Pause.] Okay. You want to look? [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah. Oh, there it goes, there. [Pause.] Looks kind of empty down there without the LM...

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay, Bob, we're looking right up the dome of the S-IVB. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Roger. We copy that. We're standing by for your Go for yaw maneuver. [Long pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Yeah. We can give them a Go for - for the yaw, can't we? We can see it now.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Yes, we can see it. You've got the Go for the yaw. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Roger. Thank you, 17. [Pause.]

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Looks like she came out of there clean as a whistle.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: 17, Houston. The yaw maneuver will be starting in about 4 plus 52, a little less than 2 minutes from now.

a17_0043913.speaker: Cernan
a17_0043913.text: Okay.

a17_0043913.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0043913.text: Sounds like you are taking a picture of that old dome out there, huh?

a17_0043913.speaker: Evans
a17_0043913.text: Oh, we're at the end. [Laughter.] We're at the end - you know. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: [Garble.] [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: Hey, there it goes. Look at the aft fire of the thing.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: And we can see it firing now. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger, 17. Yaw maneuver started. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0045221.text: 004:52:54 - The Saturn third stage now maneuvering into attitude for the APS evasive maneuver, a 10-foot-per-second burn using the Auxiliary Propulsion System that will assure...
The Saturn third stage now maneuvering into attitude for the APS evasive maneuver, a 10-foot-per-second burn using the Auxiliary Propulsion System that will assure...

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: The old S-IVB had a flare for the dramatic, but it certainly did its job for us.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Preliminary data indicated that you are about as nominal as you can be.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: That's the way we'd like to keep it, Bob.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: You'd better believe it.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay. She's - as we're looking at it, she's pitching up. She was looking right at us - we were looking right at the dome - and now she's pitching up. The shroud around the IU seems to be totally intact. It - it looked like a super clean separation. I can't really see where there's any paint or anything externally chipped off the - the booster from here. We're beginning to - to pick up the bell. It's really a shame you don't have this - this whole thing on TV; it's really quite a sight.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger. We concur with that. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: The Mylar and the gold coating on the inside of the shroud that's now visible is also intact. [Pause.] It looks like you could use it again if you could get it back.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Well, it's got a job to do when it hits the Moon yet. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay, Bob. We've - we're almost looking at it broadside now.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay. She's spitting a little; looks like the yaw maneuver may be complete. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: We got a - full view of the - entire J-2 from here; and no kidding, Bob, the whole bird, the shroud at the top by the IU, the separation plane down by the S-II, from here all looks as clean as a whistle, all the way.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger, Gene. If you're happy, we'd like a Go from you for the evasive burn.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay. You're going to burn on the booster's plus X-axis, is that right?

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Let's get a picture or two here yet, and we'll give you a Go. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: And, Gene, it'll be about 7 minutes until the evasive burn; 5 plus 03.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay. You have a Go. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: And for your reference, at frame 105 I started a few 250-millimeter pictures of the S-IVB. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: And, Bob, the entire sky, as far as I can make it out through the hatch window, is completely filled with our twinkling flakes. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger. We copy that.

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: I saw a couple particles go by the window awhile back, and it looked a little bit like insulation in this - these particular case - styrofoam insulation, but in flat flakes.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger that.

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: That was right after we separated from the S-IVB.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger.

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: CSM Sep - CSM Sep, Bob.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger. Understand.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Bob, I know - I know we're not the first to discover this, but we'd like to confirm, from the crew of America, that the world is round.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Roger. That's a good data point. Have you gotten a good look at any of that weather down there on the Antarctic?

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Well, on Ron's window number 1 - maybe he can tell you a little about it.

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: You know, it's real funny there in Antarctica the - You can see the snow, but there isn't any weather at all in it. All of the weather's around it in the water.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Rog.

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: That's where the moisture is. [Pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: I don't know what to take a picture of. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: I can't see the U.S. at all.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Go ahead.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: Look's like you've got a superconservative CMP up there. We've run off some numbers - Looks like you used about 40 pounds of RCS on the T&D, and you've used about a total of 42 pounds RCS total; so we're hanging right in there. Beautiful.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Very fine; glad to hear that.

a17_0045221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0045221.text: [Garble] velvet touch.

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: Still a little bit too much, but that's not bad.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: We'll be glad to leave all that extra, I hope, in the Service Module when we get home. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: It's in the Volkswagen pouch down there. [Long pause.]

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: Oh, I'll change the lens now.

a17_0045221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0045221.text: 17, Houston. It's about 30 seconds from the evasive maneuver burn.

a17_0045221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0045221.text: Okay.

a17_0045221.speaker: Evans
a17_0045221.text: Here, Jack, can you see him good? Check the settings there. I took an f/22 stop. [Long pause.]

a17_0050511.text: This is Apollo Control at 5 hours, 5 minutes.

a17_0050511.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0050511.text: 17, Houston. The evasive burn is complete, and the LOX dump will be at 5 plus 24 plus 20.

a17_0050511.speaker: Evans
a17_0050511.text: He's going to be gone, I think, before we can see it. [Long pause.]

a17_0050511.speaker: Cernan
a17_0050511.text: And, Bob, you can tell Frank to forget the - returning that phone call I made to him a couple days ago.

a17_0050511.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0050511.text: Think you've had enough booster briefings, huh?

a17_0050511.speaker: Cernan
a17_0050511.text: Yep. I figure this is probably the best one of all.

a17_0050511.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0050511.text: Frank said he'd guarantee all those S-IVBs would be just as good as this one.

a17_0050511.speaker: Cernan
a17_0050511.text: The S-IC and the S-II didn't put on a bad show either.

a17_0050511.speaker: Evans
a17_0050511.text: Houston, magazine November November's on about 123 right now.

a17_0050511.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0050511.text: Okay, Ron. Magazine November November is on 123.

a17_0050511.speaker: Cernan
a17_0050511.text: And, Bob, we're on page 3-9 of the Flight Plan now. We'll check the LM/CM Delta-P, get the cabin fan filter in. We'll go over the check - the Systems Checklist, get the primary EVAP and a few odds and ends, and start doffing our PGAs. How's that sound?

a17_0051101.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051101.text: I guess you saw that one, Houston. That had no caution or warning with it.

a17_0051101.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051101.text: Gene's got - say again. [Laughter.] You caught me. Forgot to look. Keep after us; we'll get you that data point.

a17_0051101.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051101.text: Gene's got his hands all over panel 2, which probably is what caused it. [Long pause.]

a17_0051101.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051101.text: Jack, we think that might have been a real one due to the accumulator cycle with the O 2 makeup flow going on there. It gave - it held the O 2 flow higher for - greater than the 16 seconds.

a17_0051101.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051101.text: Well, that's certainly a possibility. We didn't notice it - Looked up right at the time. But it - Sure that was the right time?

a17_0051101.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051101.text: Well, EECOM's watching it here, and he feels it is.

a17_0051101.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051101.text: Gee, I can't argue with him.

a17_0051350.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051350.text: Okay, Houston. Ready to deactivate the primary evaporator if you concur. [Pause.]

a17_0051550.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051550.text: Okay, Bob. VHF Simplex Alpha's Off.

a17_0051550.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051550.text: And we're gradually moving into getting out of the suits.

a17_0051550.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051550.text: Yeah. I'll bet you're looking forward to that.

a17_0051550.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051550.text: Well, I'll tell you it's a different world without that old 1-g on you. The old suit's a little bit friendlier.

a17_0051716.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051716.text: And, as you may have noticed, Bob, we've come to the end of the Launch Checklist.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: That's affirmative, and we've put ours away for posterity. [Pause.] We also stored it with our TLI-0 data that we worked so hard to generate.

a17_0051716.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051716.text: Well, I'm just happy didn't use it. That view of the Earth for a rev there was something I was looking forward to and was not disappointed.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: That's great, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Bob, you've got a pretty good size storm over the north - I guess the north-western coast of - of India, where it starts to wrap up and around to the west. It's a - a rounded out on the horizon, so I can't make out exactly where it is too well.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Could we get a read-out on the LM/CM Delta-P? [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051716.text: Plus 0.4.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger. We copy that.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Bob, Antarctica is what I would call effectively just a solid white cap down on the - South Pole. There's a definite contact between the continent and the water. But, as Ron said, most of the clouds seem to be, well very artistic, very picturesque - some in clockwise rotating fashion but appear to be very thin where you can, for the most part, kind of see through those clouds to the blue water below.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: The continent - the continent itself is - is the same color as the clouds; but, of course, more dense - and a striking difference than any of the other white background around because you can definitely see that contact with the water and with the clouds over the water.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Rog. Understand. There'll soon be a comm switch over to Madrid here shortly. We may break lock in a few minutes here. Or a few seconds, rather. [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: And you might watch - your accumulator's going to cycle in about 20 seconds here. Let's see what happens on the Master Alarm. [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: 17, Houston. How do you read through Madrid?

a17_0051716.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0051716.text: You're loud and clear, Bob, and could you give us our distance from the Earth please?

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger. I'm looking up at the board. I'd guess at about 19,000 [nautical] miles [35,000 km], but let me get it exact?

a17_0051716.speaker: Evans
a17_0051716.text: No, just approximate's good enough. [Pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: 18,100 [nautical miles, 33,520 km], FIDO says.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Okay. And I suppose we're seeing as 100 per cent full Earth as we'll ever see; certainly as I've ever seen. It appears to be - it may be a little bit - a little bit of a terminator way out to the - well, to the east - out beyond Australia and beyond India. But beyond that it's about 99 per cent pure. [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Bob, it's these kind of views - these kind of views that stick with you forever.

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger, Gene.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: We've got a - I guess probably the continent of Africa dominates the world right now. It's covering the - oh, the upper third - upper and western third of the - of the world. We can see the Sinai; we can see up into the Mediterranean; we can see across the Mediterranean, although we can't quite make out the countries up there; we can see across into India. I catch a glimpse of Australia out on the far horizon. Got Zanzibar on the southern tip of Africa, the Cape down there just almost directly below us. And, I don't know exactly how big Antarctica is, but I guess we can certainly see more than

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger. We understand.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: And there's one batch of clouds in northern Africa, just a small batch, it looks like it may be up near the - well, no, it's not near the mouth of the Nile; it's quite a bit west of that as a matter of fact, I can see the mouth of the Nile; I can see it running straight down towards us as it parallels the Suez, and then sort of fades out into the central darker brown or darker green portions of Africa. [Pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger, Gene. Sure be nice to have that on TV, wouldn't it?

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Boy, I'd love to give it to you; any way I could. [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: You know - and there's no strings holding it up either. It's out there all by itself. [Pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Roger. I just was going through the 17 status report on CSM systems and, boy, everything is absolutely nominal, with the exception of [garble] glitching Master Alarms that we're trying to still track down; but every other system is just nominal it's - everything's great.

a17_0051716.speaker: Cernan
a17_0051716.text: Okay. Sounds good. That's the way they built it for us. [Long pause.]

a17_0051716.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0051716.text: Gene, looking at our plot board, you're directly over the southern tip of Africa or just slightly out in the Indian Ocean there, according to our plot board, which isn't exactly accurate all the time. But shortly you're going to start going backwards on the Earth here and head back across the Atlantic. That ought to be some sort of a first. You cross the Atlantic twice, going from west to east, and then, now you're going to cross it going from east to west here shortly. All in a very short span of time. [Long pause.]

a17_0053000.text: This is Apollo Control at 5 hours, 30 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The White Team of flight controllers, headed by Gene Kranz, is in the process now of handing over to the team headed by Flight Director Pete Frank. After 12 hours, the team came on about 3 hours prior to the scheduled launch time of 8:53 pm Central Standard Time. Of course, launch occurred 2 hours, 40 minutes late at a Ground Elapsed Time of 11, - of a Central Standard Time rather, 11:33 pm. As a result of the late launch time, the Translunar Injection, that's up through Translunar Injection, also slipped 2 hours, 40 minutes. W

a17_0053000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0053000.text: Bob, I can assume that from what you said there will be - probably not be a midcourse 1?

a17_0053000.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0053000.text: That's exactly what we're working towards, Gene. And I - I'm sorry I didn't convey that feeling to you a little earlier. There's no reason for midcourse 1 right now.

a17_0053000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0053000.text: Okay. Because we prefer to press on and get the suits off and hit the sack rather than make it, unless we have to.

a17_0053000.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0053000.text: That's for sure. Roger. The earlier data showed us midcourse 1 would have been less than 3 feet per second, and we wouldn't have done it. And the data's been fluctuating, but they're smoothing it out, and it's still holding that way; so we won't be doing it, probably.

a17_0053000.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0053000.text: Bob, I'm looking over Gene's shoulder here at the Earth, and it must be an awful clear day for the so-called convergence zone across Africa. Gene, I think, Indicated, as it looked to us as we crossed it earlier, most of Africa is clear. Only some - probably are broken and scattered clouds - cumulus in the east central portion that are running along the line of - north/south lines.

a17_0053000.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0053000.text: Looks like a major circulation system off the southern tip of Africa, as Gene mentioned, plus one west of that, 20 or 30 degrees of longitude. Make that east of that.

a17_0053000.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0053000.text: And, southwest of the - make that south southwest of the tip of Africa at Cape Good Hope, there looks like an incipient circulation system developing about half way between the coast of Antarctica and Africa. If I had to guess, it's going to swing up north towards the Cape and - and then swing west. The whole pattern, [garble] it looks like now, is a fairly equally spaced cyclones that are sort of circling around the Antarctic continent, as we can see it now.

a17_t-0023722.speaker: Schmitt
a17_t-0023722.text: But I would guess that South Africa is going to have good weather for several more days, at least. And if the pattern is - is apparent in the clouds we see is correct, the last disturbance I mentioned probably is going to pass south of the Cape also,

a17_t-0023722.speaker: Schmitt
a17_t-0023722.text: As we were going - over our daylight around the Earth in orbit, it was very clear looking at the various clouds, Bob, what were high clouds and what were low clouds, particularly when you had them together. The high clouds cast very distinct shadow patterns on the lower ones and, very commonly, had entirely different orientations - pattern orientations. The low ones seem to be more associated with arcuate front patterns; whereas, the high clouds were generally transverse to that, roughly north/south directions. That's not completely general observation, but I noticed it several times.

a17_t-0023722.speaker: Overmyer
a17_t-0023722.text: I just noticed on the plot board here, it looks like you're come up on 20,000 [nautical] miles out, right about now.

a17_0053728.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0053728.text: Bob, I have the first hint of contamination on window 5. It's covering, probably, the central - well, I'd say, - roughly around - it's square about - 7 inches in - on a side with a very thin film that's catching the sunlight; and slightly iridescent, but also very finely granular - very finely granular. You can just barely tell what it is, actually.

a17_0053728.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0053728.text: Looks like very uniform in thickness right now.

a17_0054655.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054655.text: Bob, it's Jack. We've got a UCTA dump scheduled, or is possible, at 6 o'clock. There's nothing sacred about that time, is there? [Pause.]

a17_0054655.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054655.text: Nothing at all. Whenever you're ready, just go ahead and dump.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Bob, one of the things that we missed in our training is a good geography lesson, and particularly on Antarctica. I got the monocular out, and apparently the dark band that Gene - Ron mentioned as interface between the continental water is that between the pack ice and the water. And you can, by very subtle changes in the apparent smoothness of the ground, probably make out where the actual continent begins and the pack ice ends. There are a few exposed ranges, I guess it's midsummer down there now, and you can make out the snow-free areas scattered at least in the northern portion of the cont

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. Did you get any pictures of that, Jack?

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Oh, yes. We got some pictures earlier. I'm going to get another one here in a minute. I'll tell you, if there ever was a fragile-appearing piece of blue in space, it's the Earth right now.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: [Laughter.] Roger.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: And we got a Master Alarm.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay. We copy that.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: And there's one in the LEB.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay. Good data point.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: And there are no caution lights.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: It came right at accumulator cycle, along with the high O 2 flow again.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, I just checked the time, and I think you are right on that one. [Pause.] Well, we gave you your LEB data point.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Yes, sir. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: The problem with looking at the Earth [laughter] particularly Antarctica, is it's too bright. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Understand.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: And so I'm using my sunglasses through the monocular, which is not the best [laughter] viewing platform. I think I can see some of the areas of the Dry Valley, but, again, I'm not too sure of my geography Bob. There are clouds over the continent, I believe, but, of course, they're just as white as the snow, and you only see differences in texture brought out by - probably varying photometric return because of fairly low sun angles down there.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: But you can see patterns of what I believe is pack ice - leading off from that sharp interface that was talked about earlier. And those patterns seem to merge directly with the patterns of the clouds as if the - at least near the continent - the oceanic currents are controlling the air currents, up to a point, along with the movement of the pack ice.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: I'm distinguishing the pack ice from clouds mainly by the angularity of the patterns within them. There is no good clear color or albedo distinction. So, I could - I could be looking entirely at clouds, but I suspect there are some pack ice patterns, too. [Pause.] I'm not keeping you awake, am I, Bob?

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: No, sir. Just keep talking; we're listening. And I'm sure not much of the world is listening, but this will all be recorded, and you can read it all when you get back and think it through and tie it up with the pictures. And I'm sure there's going to be people interested in this. And we're interested ourselves; just keep talking.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: All I want to do is read what I say.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. If I had a little more geology training, I'd be asking you some better questions. I'm afraid, right now, I can't think of anything to ask you.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Well, I can't - I really wish I knew that geography. I don't know - I wish I'd thought of bringing a good map of Antarctica. Could somebody do a little researching for me and see if they could tell me if we're - have a Little American view - say on the eastern edge of the continent?

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. We'll see if we can get some Antarctica geographers around.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, I'd like to - and, also, whether or not they think the Dry Valley area is visible to us. Let's see, there's some - some of the people over there in Bill Bennett's group, I think, have a little Antarctic experience, or used to. They might be able to help you out.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay. We'll see what we can track down on it.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Don't use up a lot of people's time on it, but - but I'd be interested.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. It's getting pretty empty around here. It's 5:00 in the morning, so - [laughter] [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Okay. [Pause.] There is a good strong northern hemisphere cyclone up near India, and I think Gene mentioned that. It, I think, was one I saw in some of the forecast sheets as a dissipating hurricane or typhoon. I'm not sure which it is there. I guess it's a typhoon. [Pause.] And I see something here that I noticed in Earth orbit, Bob. That as you approach the terminator - and now I'm looking at the eastern terminator [pause] got to keep all my directions straight here - yeah, eastern terminator. The clouds - those associated with the cyclone over India and one that's - appears to be due south

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. You - you mentioned something in Earth orbit that kind of intrigued me. You mentioned seeing the rainbow, and we were trying to figure out how you saw a rainbow up there. And you were in orbit already at that time. Do you remember that?

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Well, - we're not - we were speaking of the merits of the sunrise. Having a...

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay. Rog.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: ...having a banded color appearance that varied as you approached sunrise. I can't remember what we - I think we put some of that on tape, and we were probably LOS at the time. But the banded character of the sunrise in the atmosphere was very, very marked. There's a - was a gray-blue upper layer followed - that merged or graded into a brilliant blue intermediate zone that was just above the cloud levels. And within the clouds, you got a orange to yellow band, getting more yellow as the Sun rose, that was broken by the dark patterns of the buildups.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. Good show. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: The interesting thing was the continual glow on the horizon we had, even at night, on the darkside pass - and that glow was in the atmosphere because I could see stars rise over the horizon in it and then pass on through it.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. We were talking - the airglow, I guess, is the phenomenon most of the guys had seen before. It's kind of interesting, Yes?

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, that's - that's right. It's interesting - I guess standard airglow, but it is very striking that it's a continuous thing even in the dark pass.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: I think I did see the eastern tip of South America, now. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. You're starting to back up now, coming the other way. So you're still over Africa, according to our chart here, but you're backing up towards the - South America.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, I can see the part of South America that Wegener thought that fitted into the bend in Africa some many decades ago and started people thinking about moving continents around on the crust.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. [Pause.] Jack, how'd - how'd the PGA doffing go? Most of you - are you all out of the PGAs now?

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: That's in work. We're taking it slow and easy up here, Bob.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. Understand. I'll just be curious to see if they all fit in that bag.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: I think you'll find that Ronald Evans will also be curious about that. He's already making comments.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger.

a17_0054848.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0054848.text: 006:00:03 - This is Apollo Control at 6 hours. As Jack Schmitt gives the description of the Earth, Apollo 17 is 22,868 nautical miles [42,352 km] from Earth; velocity, 12,520 feet per second [3,816 m/s].
This is Apollo Control at 6 hours. As Jack Schmitt gives the description of the Earth, Apollo 17 is 22,868 nautical miles [42,352 km] from Earth; velocity, 12,520 feet per second [3,816 m/s].

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Bob, you certainly do have a very clear intuitive impression, although the evidence is hard to pull together, that the - any frontal systems that move off the Antarctic continent do not take on any well-defined character until they get into the moist regions of the ocean. And when they do, they seem to pick up an arcuate circ - circulation that, in the view we have, seem to get fairly regularly spaced cyclone patterns that lie between the - the Cape of Good Hope and northern portion of Antarctica. And these - circulations of the cyclones follows roughly an east/west pattern, and the curve - an

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: All of them - all of them very - very nicely defined as southern hemisphere cyclones. There - about four of those visible swinging around - oh, I guess, that's latitude - I'm having to guess here, but I'd say latitude 50 to 60 south.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay; 50 or 60 south on that, huh?

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, I have to look at the map here in a minute and see if that puts me between Antarctica and the Cape.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Well, the tip - the tip of Africa there is at about 32 south.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Well, that sounds like a pretty good guess, then. It looks like the intertropical convergence zone over Africa is starting to get more and more clouds in it now. I suspect as midday approaches, which is what we're seeing there, we can expect to see more and more moisture indications.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Rog. They're - they're probably about noontime right there right now. It's 11:36 at the zero meridian at Greenwich, so it's just a little bit before noon right in that area you're talking about.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Yeah, some of those masses of what I suspect are cumulus buildups - well, not really. They don't look like they're as concentrated and localized. More like just masses of fairly dense clouds that are developing in that band of green that crosses the lower portion of Africa.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Stay tuned for the next instalment on the Earth. I'll try to get out of this suit.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Okay. Just take it easy, Jack, and we'll be listening.

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Man, I've never taken it so easy in my life. I'll tell you, Bob, I couldn't have believed this would be an experience like it is now.

a17_0054848.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0054848.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0054848.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0054848.text: Every time you turn around, there is something else to see and wonder what's causing it. Whether it's a particle zipping across the window, or one zipping across the cabin, or spring mechanics here in zero g; there's always something going on.

a17_0060705.text: This is Apollo Control at 6 hours, 7 minutes. No midcourse correction number 1 will be performed. The value of the maneuver that would be required is less than 3 feet per second [0.9 m/s] and midcourse correction number 1 will not be performed by Apollo 17. The spacecraft is now at 23,682 nautical miles [43,859 km] from Earth; velocity, 12,301 feet per second [3,749 m/s].

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: Bob, if I'm not waking you up, an observer from another planet certainly - probably could decide that we have such things as clouds and at least large thunderstorms because right at the terminator you get a brightening of the sunlit side and a long, long shadow out to the - out to the east that is reminiscent of what we saw in the early days looking at the Moon at the terminator.

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: However, in the next pass around, I'll bet you wouldn't see them. [Long pause.]

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: I've never been a big - Well, I didn't grow up with the idea of drifting continents and sea-floor spreadings, but I tell you, when you look at the way the pieces of the - of the north-eastern portion of the African continent seem to fit together, separated by a narrow gulf, you could almost make a believer of anybody.

a17_0060955.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0060955.text: Roger. It's beginning to look like the globe that you might buy down at the store, huh?

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: Oh, I don't think so, Bob. [Laughter.]

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: I don't think we'd better put this one up for sale. [Pause.] Somewhere there might be somebody who'd like to buy it. [Long pause.]

a17_0060955.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0060955.text: Say, Jack. We noticed the O 2 flow has dropped down now. We're wondering, did you all close the waste storage vent valve?

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: I don't think so; let me check on that. It might have gotten closed inadvertently in this game we were playing down in the LEB. [Long pause.]

a17_0060955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0060955.text: Ron says it's still on Vent.

a17_0060955.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0060955.text: Okay. We're noticing the flow is coming back up slowly; so something caused it to drop, and it's coming back up.

a17_0061741.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0061741.text: Jack, just to ease those words I said before, we looked at the schematics here a second, and you'd be dumping urine out of that same line as that waste vent, and that would probably cause the pressure to build up enough to slow the O 2 flow. And we noticed that the O 2 flow is climbing back up to where it belongs. [Pause.]

a17_0061741.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0061741.text: Didn't mean to worry you there. Shouldn't have said it, I guess, before we looked at the schematic.

a17_0061741.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0061741.text: Oh, I really hadn't started to worry about it yet, Bob, so no sweat.

a17_0062215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0062215.text: How'd the S-IVB work go Bob? [Pause.]

a17_0062215.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0062215.text: They just finished their second burn, and it's targeted right where they want it. Just working perfectly.

a17_0062215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0062215.text: Where were they going to put that one? I guess I lost track of that. [Long pause.]

a17_0062215.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0062215.text: 7 degrees south and 8 degrees west, Jack.

a17_0062215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0062215.text: Say again, you cut out on the first.

a17_0062215.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0062215.text: Okay; 7 degrees south and 8 degrees west. [Pause.]

a17_0062215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0062215.text: Okay. [Pause.] That ought to be interesting.

a17_0062215.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0062215.text: 006:23:29 - This is Apollo Control at 6 hours, 24 minutes. The S-IVB maneuver that was just being discussed was performed with the Auxiliary Propulsion System; just completed a Delta-V of 13 feet per second [4 m/s] to tune up the trajectory for S-IVB impact at the desired location on the lunar surface of 7 degrees south, 8 degrees west. That's approximately 200 kilometers east of the Apollo 14 ALSEP site where the seismometer is located. That impact is expected to be picked up by the other seismometers on the Moon, the other Apollo lunar surface experiment seismometers. Booster systems enginee
