a17_0351847.text: [Garble] 786, LM weight. [Pause.] Okay, [garble], Off; [garble], Off. That's what I'm doing now. To what? One three, okay. Here we go. [Long pause.] Set my IMU. Okay. Realign the old GDC a little bit. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, GDC is aligned. Stab control breakers. All In and good shape.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Manual ATTs are Rate Command; Deadband, Min; Rate to Low. Yeah.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, TVC's in Rate Command. LM/CSM is in LM/CSM. Gimbal Drive's in Auto. Okay.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Jack, this is Houston. We're ready for the High Gain. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: [Laughter.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: 17, Houston. Do you read? [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: I think there's no trim on this [garble] Flight Plan.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Apollo 17, Houston. How do you copy?

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, so X-axis only trim, to 0.2. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: No trim if it's greater than 2 feet per second. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Yeah, we're down to 6 minutes.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Apollo 17, Houston. How do you read?

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Gordo. We got you.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Okay, we weren't getting through there for a minute or 2. We're ready for the High Gain now. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Minus [pause] minus 21 and 181.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: And 17, You're Go for midcourse 2.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Sounds good. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: And, Jack, you ready for Gimbal Motors? - I mean the Bus Ties? [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Ready for the Bus Ties. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Tape Recorder, High Bit Rate, Record, Forward, and Command Reset. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Check your Helium Valves and check your [garble].

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Servo Power 1 and 2, we got. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, got Servo Power. AC1 and AC2.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: AC, Directs are Off.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: BMAGs, 1/2. Okay.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: No hardovers. Okay. We'll go to SCS. Okay, Pitch 1, Jack...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. Yaw 1...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. Okay. Got a minus - plus 1.1, okay. A minus 0.13; that's almost zero. Okay. Whoo! Man, bounces it around! [Laughter.] little difference.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, we'll give it to the computer. Clockwise. Go TVC TVC. Okay, Pitch 2.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. Got it. Yaw 2.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. Got it? Okay, got the trim, about a plus 12 and a minus 0.1. TVC, TVC, TVC, TVC.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, give it to the computer. Returns to zero. Go TVC TVC. Okay.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: AC/DC. Directs are Main A/Main B.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, zero BMAGs.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, 50 18. Proceed.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Enter it.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Uncage BMAGs. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Let's try a gimbal test. Plus 2, minus 2, 0, plus 2, minus 2, 0. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, she went to trim. 02:38 to go. Okay, we'll reach - Scale was 5 what?

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Rate to High.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, EMS Normal at 1 minute. [Pause.] Yeah, we use bank A. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Two-second burn, we use bank A only. Okay, so in 3 seconds, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, cycle to [garble], Min, Rate to High, Direct, CMC Auto; uncaged, Rate Command, Gimbal Motors, LM/CSM and Gim - Auto.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Houston. 01:30 and we're Go onboard for the burn.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Houston. No ullage.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Houston - Houston, I'm sure you've seen it. We're reading below the green band oxidizer pressure, about 163.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: [Singing] Okay. Let's wait until 30 seconds and...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Control Power is On. [Garble] Delta-V Thrust A switch. Get it and EMS at 30 seconds. Ullage - no ullage. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: We're in average g.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, average g is coming. EMS to Normal. Delta-V Thrust A is On. Okay, no manuals to it. You'll get the 99 - Okay? [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: 10 seconds, Houston.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Uh-hoo! There we go. Lift-off!

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Okay. The burn is on time and - au - auto shutdown

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Let's see what kind of trim we got. Yeah, we trimmed it. Trimmed it to 0.2. Yes. Less than 2. Okay, plus 7 on the EMS.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: I mean on the R-1. [Laughter.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, we'll trim it out to 2. Plus 0.3. [Pause.] One more chance. Okay, there we go.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Houston. You're looking at Noun 85, and the EMS is minus 3.3.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger, Gene.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, gimbal motors check. Two...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. Two...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. One...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it. One...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Mark it.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Servo Power is Off.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Trans Control Power and Directs are Off.

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Delta-V circuit breakers are Open. Hey, we just caught up with all the particles. They're all going with us now. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay, Directs are Off. Pitch and Yaw. Pitch 1, Yaw 1 are Opened. Okay, you got the Delta-V counter? [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. BMAGs are caged. Bus Ties, Jack? [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. Bus Ties are Off. Bit Rate to Low, while you're up there. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: That shouldn't change, I don't think; should it? [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Houston, America.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Okay, the burn was on time. Looked like it was about 2 seconds. Delta-V GX was 0.7. Roll was 132, Pitch was 193, and Yaw was 342. Residuals after trim were zero - plus 0.1, zero, and minus 0.1, and Delta-V C , is minus 3.3. Ox 007. Fuel is 009 and Decrease 50.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: Pan Camera's Off. Map Camera's Off, huh? And SM/AC Power will be coming Off, shortly. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: You know, Houston, we must of caught up with every one of those particles. Because we're right in the middle of them. They're going kind of in a random fashion. Most of them are drifting right along with us. Some of them are going against us and away from us. But before we did the burn - you know, the propulsion they got out of the vent sent them all away from us in what looked like - in more or less the X-direction.

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: How about that.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Say...

a17_0351847.speaker: Evans
a17_0351847.text: We really got a star field out there now [laughter].

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Rog.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Say, Gordy, the LM/CM Delta-P is 1 - That's 1.0. You want me to go to Tunnel Vent?

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0351847.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0351847.text: Yeah, that's affirmative, Geno. You have a Go for Tunnel Vent valve, Vent.

a17_0351847.speaker: Cernan
a17_0351847.text: Okay.

a17_0354109.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0354109.text: Okay, we do want to put Battery A back on Charge as shown in the Flight Plan. And, also, I have a new flyby PAD. No hurry on this one, but it's a flyby PAD post MCC-2. [Pause.]

a17_0354109.speaker: Cernan
a17_0354109.text: Okay, Gordo, how quickly should this tunnel vent?

a17_0354109.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0354109.text: Let me get a reading on that. [Long pause.]

a17_0354109.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0354109.text: Geno, that should take about an hour. We'll try to remember to occasionally remind you to look at it.

a17_0354109.speaker: Cernan
a17_0354109.text: Okay. I'm glad you said that because I don't see any indication of it moving here yet, at all.

a17_0354109.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0354109.text: Never got to give you a 7-Alpha reading on a - after the last charge. It was 0.6 - decimal 6 as before.

a17_0354109.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0354109.text: Okay. Ed Mitchell - Ed Mitchell must be working. I was just about to ask you for that. And for Geno, one reminder, you will have to switch back to LM/CM Delta-P in order to read the Delta-P. Over.

a17_0354109.speaker: Cernan
a17_0354109.text: Yeah, Gordo, I'm - I'm aware of that, and I've done it. But in the about 3 or 4 minutes that I vented, I didn't see any change yet.

a17_0354109.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0354109.text: Okay. It's a pretty slow process.

a17_0354632.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0354632.text: Okay, Gordy, battery A is being charged.

a17_0354632.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0354632.text: And I checked that 7-Alpha in the Vent position, and it's 0.6 also.

a17_0355218.speaker: Evans
a17_0355218.text: Okay, Houston. How's the CMP's "zippen" or ZPN?

a17_0355218.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0355218.text: Let me take a check to my left here.

a17_0355218.speaker: Evans
a17_0355218.text: I'll take a deep breath for you.

a17_0355432.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0355432.text: Okay, Ron. Your ZPN looks good. [Pause.]

a17_0355432.speaker: Evans
a17_0355432.text: Okay, I don't have the other one on yet. But I was a little bit curious because I left the electrodes in this thing, and - you know, the little sponges, I left those inside the electrodes, but they stuck to - to the back of the electrodes and kind of corroded the inside of it there a little bit.

a17_0355432.speaker: Evans
a17_0355432.text: I'll put some new ones in.

a17_0360747.speaker: Evans
a17_0360747.text: Okay, Houston, is my heart beating?

a17_0360747.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0360747.text: I'm sure it is, Ron, but I'll check to my left.

a17_0360747.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0360747.text: We'll wait a couple of minutes. It takes that long to settle down and give you a reading on it.

a17_0360747.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0360747.text: Ron, your EKG looks real good.

a17_0360747.speaker: Evans
a17_0360747.text: That's all new, what you call it - those sponges and stuff, you know. [Pause.] And, Houston, I'm not - I'm not putting - putting any cover tape on it, so if it quits - you know, comes loose or something like that, well, let me know and I'll push it on again.

a17_0361055.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0361055.text: You might make a note that Dr. Evans was assisted in that operation by Dr. Schmitt,

a17_0361055.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0361055.text: Jack, I've still got this flyby PAD standing by.

a17_0361055.speaker: Evans
a17_0361055.text: Can't talk with a mouthful of bread cubes, it all comes out.

a17_0361055.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0361055.text: Okay, what kind of PAD you want to give me? Flyby, right?

a17_0361055.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0361055.text: Okay, and I guess the other one I can cross out, right?

a17_0361055.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0361055.text: That's affirmative. It's obsolete now that you've done midcourse 2. [Long pause.]

a17_0361055.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0361055.text: Okay, it's a flyby. SPS/G&N; 66678; plus 1.21, minus 0.13. Ignition time is 081:14:43.49; plus 0043.3, plus 0211.8, plus 0453.2. Attitude is 128, 146, 317; H A is NA. H P is plus 0021.1. Delta-V T , 0502.1. Burn time, 1:18, 0497.6. Sextant star is 25, 189.3, 27.4. Boresight star is NA. Noun 61 is a plus 15.60, minus 175.00; 1101.6, 36242. GET of 05G is 153:24:03 - GDC stars are Sirius and Rigel; 256; 152; 069. Ullage, none. Remarks: 1, burn docked; and number 2, assumes PTC REFSMMAT. And that's it. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0361055.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0361055.text: Okay, Gordy. Here's your readback. Flyby, SPS/G&N; 66678; plus 1.21, minus 0.13; 081:14:43.49; plus 0043.3, plus 0211.8, plus 0453.2; 128, 146, 317. H A is NA. Plus 0021.1; 0502.1, 1:18, 0497.6; 25, 189.3, 27.4. Boresight, NA. Plus 15.60, minus 175.00; 1101.6, 36242; 153:24:03 - Sirius and Rigel; 256; 152; 069. There's no ullage. Remark 1, burn docked - docked; and 2, PC - PTC REFSMMAT is assumed.

a17_0361755.speaker: Cernan
a17_0361755.text: Gordy, I might mention for future reference that we've established a new list of consumables, or at least add it to the old one. Now includes gray tape and tissues.

a17_0361755.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0361755.text: Okay, you want us to track those?

a17_0361755.speaker: Cernan
a17_0361755.text: It might help. We have a heck of a time finding them in here.

a17_0361755.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0361755.text: Yeah, we'll set up in a special back room. [Pause.]

a17_0361755.speaker: Cernan
a17_0361755.text: Would you call it the T-T room. Tissue and tape, of course.

a17_0361755.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0361755.text: 036:34:41 - This is Apollo Control at 36 hours, 34 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 17, 130,714 nautical miles [242,082 km] out from Earth, velocity now 3,985 feet per second [1,215 m/s], continuing to decelerate as we approach the so-called cross-over between the sphere of influence from Earth to Moon. I can't recall ever seeing two pages of a Flight Plan as blank as these are, from 36 hours to 38 hours. Later on today, the - after the eat-period, the crew will crawl through the hatch into the Lunar Module for some housekeeping chores, checking out of stowage of equipment in the Lunar Modu

a17_0363441.text: This is Apollo Control at 36 hours, 34 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 17, 130,714 nautical miles [242,082 km] out from Earth, velocity now 3,985 feet per second [1,215 m/s], continuing to decelerate as we approach the so-called cross-over between the sphere of influence from Earth to Moon. I can't recall ever seeing two pages of a Flight Plan as blank as these are, from 36 hours to 38 hours. Later on today, the - after the eat-period, the crew will crawl through the hatch into the Lunar Module for some housekeeping chores, checking out of stowage of equipment in the Lunar Module. But the

a17_0364207.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0364207.text: Apollo 17, Houston. It's been about an hour, you might check the LM Command Module Delta-P again.

a17_0364207.speaker: Evans
a17_0364207.text: Okay; thank you. We'll do that. [Long pause.]

a17_0364207.speaker: Cernan
a17_0364207.text: It's 2.2, Gordo; I put it back in Vent.

a17_0370019.speaker: Cernan
a17_0370019.text: Okay, Gordo. We're up to 2.5 on the tunnel and still venting.

a17_0370019.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0370019.text: Okay. Is that music we hear in the background?

a17_0370019.speaker: Cernan
a17_0370019.text: Yes, sir. (Music: Up, Up, and Away by Brazil '66)

a17_0370019.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0370019.text: They've been making fun of some of my music. [Garble].

a17_0370019.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0370019.text: Yes, it's coming down to us in living stereo.

a17_0370019.speaker: Cernan
a17_0370019.text: Reminiscent of yesteryear. (Music: Up, Up, and Away by Brazil '66).

a17_0370019.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0370019.text: Roger. Thank you for the concert. That was very appropriate.

a17_0371007.speaker: Cernan
a17_0371007.text: Gordo, Ron went off the air for a minute, and LM Delta-P is now 2.6.

a17_0371007.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0371007.text: Geno, we'd like for you to let it get up to 2.8 before closing off the Vent.

a17_0372042.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0372042.text: America, Houston. That was a site handover, the reason we lost signal for a second there.

a17_0373247.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0373247.text: Say, are we going to have a pretty good view of the Earth out of any CSM windows at the LM checkout attitude?

a17_0373247.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0373247.text: We're sort of blocked right now.

a17_0374231.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0374231.text: America, Houston. We're predicting that your LM/CM Delta-P ought to be about right now, about 2.8.

a17_0374231.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0374231.text: Gordy, the reason I asked about that view of the Earth, we were sort of thinking maybe we might go early, if it was all right with you, and watch the Earth a little bit more.

a17_0374231.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0374231.text: Okay. We're still trying to get the answer on whether you'll have a window. Stand by. I might have it here.

a17_0375005.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0375005.text: Okay. The LM inspection attitude that you'll go to results in kind of a marginal view of the Earth out of window 1, about 60 degrees away from it, boresight - line of sight. And we're - we can - we've started to work on and if you wanted to do is you can go to kind of intermediate attitude, which will be the LM attitude except for roll which would be off by about 60 degrees, which will - will give you a good view of the Earth out of window 1. And then when we get ready to do the LM entry, you can roll that additional 60 degrees to get to the proper attitude, if you wish. Your choice. Over.

a17_0375005.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0375005.text: Yeah, if that doesn't bother anybody down there, we'd like to do that.

a17_0375005.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0375005.text: Okay. We'll have something for you here in a few minutes.

a17_0375400.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0375400.text: Okay. If you're ready to copy, I've a Verb 49 maneuver for you that will let you look at the Earth.

a17_0375400.speaker: Evans
a17_0375400.text: Wait a minute, Gordo, and I'll just let you load it as we go here.

a17_0375400.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0375400.text: Okay. Roll is 240, pitch is 089, and yaw is 0. And the High Gain for that attitude, we think it'll probably track to this attitude, is plus 29 and 27.

a17_0375918.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0375918.text: America, Houston. Until you get the attitude, Omni Charlie will probably work better. [Long pause.]

a17_0375918.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0375918.text: Okay, Gordy. We got you Omni Charlie now.

a17_0380515.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0380515.text: Gordy, for your information we have our LM transfer items in the jettison bag ready to go over and we're pretty well squared away on the, all the Command Module stowage now with minor exceptions.

a17_0381302.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0381302.text: America, Houston. We'd like you to go ahead and get on the High Gain again since - and stop it just wandering around aimlessly. And how does the Earth look now? [Long pause.]

a17_0381302.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381302.text: Sorry, Gordy, to be so slow. Earth looks great, and we'll get the High Gain up in just a second.

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Okay, Gordy, going from south to north on noontime, at least our noontime weather, it looks like there's a fairly strong mass of polar air moving from the southwest up towards Tierra del Fuego. It's mixed with some cloudiness that extends from that area all the way down to the Antarctic ice shelf. But it looks like some pretty good movement patterns from the southwest, north - northeast. No strong weather waves or cyclone development on that yet, although one may be picking up about halfway between Tierra del Fuego and the coast of Antarctica, the - where the front, or at least the cloud masse

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Except for scattered clouds, Central America and Mexico, for the most part, are clear - as is most of the Caribbean islands - Cuba and the others are - all look like they've pretty good weather. There's a little clouds off - cloud pattern off to the east of those islands, but it doesn't look like any major weather in that area. The eastern half and Midwest of the United States is completely cloud covered right now. There - however, the - extending from Mexico to Sonora and up into Arizona and New Mexico, and possibly as far north as Colorado, is a clear band. But then there's more cloudiness t

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: The Pacific regions west of - the West Coast of the United States is cloudy, at least west of Southern California. I cannot see Baja, so that cloudiness extends down south of - into Baja California. I see no strong new frontal patterns, although I'm looking right across the limb of the Earth now. There may be one that would be lying maybe across northern California and - and into Colorado, with a little clear area ahead of it, possibly in Kansas. But then into this, a solid bank of clouds that stretches from Brownsville, at least, clear up to - well, along the Gulf Coast across the panhandle o

a17_0381931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0381931.text: Roger, Jack. I'm following along on a satellite weather picture here that's taken from about your same vantage point and - although nowhere near the detail that you're describing. [Pause.]

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Have you seen today's analysis charts of the United States or North America?

a17_0381931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0381931.text: No, I haven't. [Long pause.] I was just told, Jack, that the - the weathermen and a lot of other people around here, too, are following your weather reports with great interest.

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Yeah, well, does that mean they're right or wrong? [Laughter.]

a17_0381931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0381931.text: You've got the better view, by far.

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: That doesn't prove much. Okay, Gordy, I'm - I suspect that that's a pretty healthy front. I don't know. Your weather must be cloudy and bad today. Is that right?

a17_0381931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0381931.text: It is. We've got about a half-mile vis and drizzly rain.

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Okay. Well, I suspect comparable weather extends all the way across the eastern United States. That looks like awful dense clouds, although there's no obvious frontal pattern. It just stretches from the Midwest to the East Coast. And, also, there's no good indication of stratification of those clouds, as if they'd be fairly - fairly thick up to - into the cirrus levels. [Pause.]

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: Looks like Arizona, New Mexico, and northern Sonora probably have some - one band of high cirrus. But other than that, probably a beautiful day out in that area. [Long pause.]

a17_0381931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0381931.text: There's some transverse cloud patterns over the Mississippi-Alabama area. It suggests maybe that the jetstream may be just north of that region. But otherwise, there's no good indication of jetstream position right now.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Gordy, there is one minor weather disturbance, possibly just about over Puerto Rico or maybe just - just to the east of that island. No strong circulation patterns, although there's a hint of a cyclone development. There might be just a small depression in that area. I don't know whether your map's carrying anything down there or not.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: I think I see what you're talking about on the satellite picture, but I don't have a surface analysis that goes that far. I do - I just now got a copy of the surface charts for the United States. And there's - there's a front stretching from northern Texas northeastward up through Tennessee and Virginia and another one sort of parallel to it. But, this way southward from Louisiana along the Gulf Coast across northern Florida and on out into the Atlantic. And I guess the two are kind of blending together to make that irregular mass of clouds you mentioned.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay, Gordy. If I'd been a little more observant I could see that there was a little bit, looks like a decrease in at least the thickness of the clouds, vertical thickness, between the two areas you just mentioned. So, there is some indication here of those two fronts, although they are contributing to a general weather pattern in the eastern United States.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Rog.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: I think, with a little experience in this business, you might have picked those two out of that mass. But it's not immediately obvious.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: You got anything on there coming in from the northwest now, say up in Wyoming and Colorado? [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: The way it's drawn on this surface chart shows that - that northern front that I mentioned, just now, sort of curving on up through central Colorado, and then bending westward toward - through Utah. That's about the only other frontal activity. There's one, probably dry front, then a short one through central Arizona and southern Utah.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay. Well, that makes sense. That would match with that - what I was thinking was high cirrus in Arizona. And also I can see how you could bend - that's the northern front up through Colorado and then back westward to - to explain the patterns we're seeing in the clear areas south of that.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Gordy, the zero-phase point now is off the coast of Chile and Ecuador - oh, maybe 10 or 15 degrees of longitude, and it is fairly dull - does not seem to indicate any great amount of choppiness or wave action in that area.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: And about 15 minutes ago, Gordy, I took two more Hasselblad shots of the Earth.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Evans
a17_0382911.text: And also, Houston, frame number, let's see, about 16 and 17 were taken of the Earth about 15 minutes ago too. And it's magazine Sierra-Sierra.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay, Ron. We copy that. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Gordy, with respect to the ice pack off the coast of Antarctica, it's difficult to distinguish pack ice from clouds, in general. However, the clouds seem to pick up reflection patterns with respect to the Sun. And using that as a - and some shadows in below as the criteria, it looks as if the pack ice in the South Atlantic would extend to a latitude almost comparable to that of Tierra del Fuego. I don't know whether that - that's reasonable or not. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. I don't either. But maybe someone who's more of an expert can clear up your question on that. I'll let you know.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Now to the southwest of Tierra del Fuego there's a - looks like a small cyclone developing, clockwise rotation, just off the edge of the pack ice, and - but it does not seem to be closely associated with the frontal activity that I mentioned when I started out speaking at this - this particular time.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Roger.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: There is another - there is another one, maybe a front, a little bit ahead of that cyclone that's now extending north-south. Starts in the pack ice area and extends up - oh, about halfway from there to Buenos Aires - in the direction of Buenos Aires. It doesn't look like a very major mass of air or frontal system. It may develop into something over the next couple days though.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: And centered, Gordy, at about 45 south and say 30 west, there is another cyclone area that's ahead of the last front I talked about, that doesn't look - I think I talked about it yesterday - still does not look too strong, although the cloud, as I recall, the cloud cover is somewhat more well developed, and circulation patterns seem to be better developed. It may be an intensifying storm over what we saw yesterday.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: I cannot see that it's associated with any clear frontal activity, however.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: That, I presume, should be migrating in the direction of the - of the southeast coast of Africa, so we'll keep an eye on it.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: And that reminds me, did you get any information on the - that - what looked like a very strong, concentrated typhoon or hurricane in the South Pacific between Borneo and the Philippines?

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Let me check and see what we got on that. I wasn't here when you first talked about it evidently.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Well, it was one that they didn't seem to be carrying, and it looked extremely well developed from here. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Gordy, yesterday that - the one I'm speaking of was centered at about 15 north and a hundred and - make that about 117 east.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. I've been informed that they are - the satellite people are carrying that one now. I'm not sure whether they had seen it before or didn't see it until after you did. But they are aware of it now and are tracking it.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Oh, we're not competing. They just didn't have any information for me on it yesterday. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: We'll probably be able to see that again late this afternoon.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. The one that you just gave the coordinates on is - does have a name, - that's Therese, Hurricane Therese. And - so the - the other one must be the - must not have a name.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay. Now which one has - is Therese.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: The one you just - the coordinates you gave almost exactly pinpoint Therese.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay. That's near the Philippines.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: That's affirmative. Between there and Vietnam. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay. Well, then that sounds like - if that's an up-to-date position, it has relatively little movement since yesterday.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Rog. [Pause.] They show it moving just very slightly westward.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Are they carrying anything south of Guam now that we talked about yesterday? [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Ah, take a minute to get something on that. They don't have a current map showing anything in Guam right now. [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: And we also had a storm developing south of - or southwest of New Zealand. Might look at that one, too.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Jack, are you making these observations through the monocular? [Pause.]

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Yes, sir.

a17_0382911.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0382911.text: Okay.

a17_0382911.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0382911.text: Although most of them - well, at this distance, Gordy, the circulation - detailed circulation patterns to say what's a cyclone and what isn't are not visible to the naked eye, at least not to mine.

a17_0384649.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0384649.text: Jack, that disturbance you mentioned near Guam isn't being carried on the current charts here as anything significant. They do show some cloudiness north of the tropical convergence zone, but just that.

a17_0384649.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384649.text: Okay. Well, I had a feeling what I was seeing yesterday might have just been the remnants of Theresa, which I think went - out into that area a couple days ago. It was not a very well-developed system, but did seem - seem to be isolated from the other cloudiness that I would have put into the tropical convergence zone. That was between Wake and Kwajalein.

a17_0384904.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384904.text: Gordy, let me try to give you a description of something that is a little bit unusual than what we've been seeing. The - there's an axis that runs from, say, the outer portion of the Ross ice shelf along the - and just off the coast of Antarctica, then bends up so that it would pass just to the east of Tierra del Fuego and - and then continues on that heading so that it would intersect the far east coast of South America, if it continued. Now along that axis, the - what appear to be multiple frontal patterns or at least linear cloud bands, bend very sharply and change from a heading that rough

a17_0384904.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384904.text: And there just, oh, there are probably a dozen, if you tried to pull them out, cloud bands between the Ross Sea and Tierra del Fuego that bend around the same axis. Quite striking.

a17_0384904.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384904.text: Now there's some indications, to me at any rate, that the jetstream in that area may be essentially east-west - oh, maybe 20 degrees of latitude north of the Ross Sea, and then bends down very sharply so that it intersects the - or approaches the coa- Antarctic ice shelf to the east of the Ross Sea, and then maybe it bends up and forms the axis that I just described that's causing that bending of the cloud patterns.

a17_0384904.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0384904.text: Okay. Sounds like a good, theory. [Long pause.]

a17_0384904.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384904.text: There's a linear clear area in that area north of the Ross Sea that - and to the north of that is a sharply defined front that I talked about earlier. And then, both the - that front continues. The clear area is cut off by the axis that I described, a cloud axis.

a17_0384904.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0384904.text: Now that should show up real well on the 250-millimeter pictures we took. [Pause.] Gordy, I'm back looking at zero-phase. And now, apparently, the exact zero-phase was partially obscured by a cloud pattern earlier. Now, when I - There is a very, very small bright spot in the center of the zero-phase area. Nothing comparable to what I described off the coast of Australia yesterday, but an extremely small spot. I suspect that the size of your bright spot in zero-phase has some direct - or indirect, at any rate, relationship to sea state.

a17_0385551.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0385551.text: Gordy, as you might expect, the whole coastline of Chile is - or all of Chile, practically, is clear. Beautifully exposed to us here, and particular the Atacama Desert, which is noted for that particular characteristic, and - at least among geologists it is. And the coast of Peru is also clear with clouds following the Andean Ridge, probably the - certainly the coast side of the Andean Ridge. Lima ought to be enjoying a very nice day today. The - Ecuador, however, looks like it might have a little more cloudy weather, although it doesn't look like any major storm activity.

a17_0390314.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0390314.text: America, Houston. We have a couple of words here on medications. is everyone listening?

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: Yeah; we're all on, Gordo. Go ahead.

a17_0390314.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0390314.text: Okay. Geno, you mentioned taking a nausea pill for some gas yesterday, and we were looking into some of the side effects. You definitely don't want to use that particular pill for gas. One of the side effects is that it's an appetite depressor. And there are some pills loaded in A-7, along with the vitamin pills, specifically for the purpose of eliminating gas. We would appreciate if you'd give us a call in advance prior to taking any medications except the Seconal and aspirin. Over.

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: Okay, Gordy, will do. I was aware that those gas depressors were around. At the time, we couldn't find them in A-7. And so I took one of those other things, whatever it is. And while you're talking about that, as per the preflight food check, gas is very evident on - particularly on me - and I think I'm suppressing it slowly. But is there any problem, or what do you recommend on that Mylinol [sic] or Mylicon or whatever it is?

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: This goes hand-in-hand with the amount of gas that I experienced preflight.

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: And it's the kind of gas - it's the kind of gas that just stays in your stomach.

a17_0390314.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0390314.text: Okay, Geno. The recommended use of those gas pills is to chew one after each meal. And then, if needed, chew up another one before going to sleep at night.

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: Okay; fine. I chewed one after breakfast.

a17_0390314.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0390314.text: Okay. A little water after you chew it up, I guess, helps its effectiveness.

a17_0390314.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390314.text: That's a basic requirement, I believe. The effect of it has not been too obvious yet though.

a17_0390753.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0390753.text: Gordy, you want the O 2 Heaters 1 and 2 to Auto now?

a17_0390753.speaker: Cernan
a17_0390753.text: I don't want to cause any concern on that gas. It's no real great problem. It's just a slight discomfort; that's all.

a17_0390753.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0390753.text: Okay, Gene. I think we understand.

a17_0391033.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0391033.text: Gordy, I have just eaten my first peanut butter sandwich in orbit around the Earth.

a17_0391033.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0391033.text: What's that? [Pause.] Well, it was just as good as it was when I was growing up - which means it was great. I grew up on those things, as I recall. [Pause.]

a17_0391033.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0391033.text: Charlie Duke's here with me and he... [Pause.]

a17_0391033.speaker: Evans
a17_0391033.text: Sure miss the lettuce. Sure missed the lettuce and mayonnaise on mine though.

a17_0391432.speaker: Evans
a17_0391432.text: And, Houston, we'll go ahead and maneuver onto the LM attitude.

a17_0391432.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0391432.text: Okay. We're watching you. Punch it in there.

a17_0392723.speaker: Evans
a17_0392723.text: Okay. Direct O 2 is coming Open now.

a17_0393011.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393011.text: America, before you open the equalization valve, we'd like one final reading on the LM/CM Delta-P.

a17_0393011.speaker: Evans
a17_0393011.text: Okay. With this cabin pressure now, it's up to 3.5, almost 3.6.

a17_0393358.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393358.text: Jack, Houston. We're ready to terminate the charge on battery A. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: CSM/LM pressure equalization, huh? Okay, Cryo Pressure Indicator to Surge/3 and verify cryo. Oh, wait a minute. See if I got the right one here. [Pause.] Recto 2's on. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Cernan
a17_0393528.text: Okay, Gordo, I cycled the Cryo Pressure Indicator from up to down, back to Surge/3. And we got a Master Alarm and there was no O 2 High Flow with it at all.

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Cernan
a17_0393528.text: Okay, I just did it again to verify it. And that picked up - it picked up the Master Alarm, although it might be associated with the fact that the surge tank is down and coming back up.

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: No, I don't think so.

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Roger, Gene. Although, the surge tank shouldn't have caused it.

a17_0393528.speaker: Cernan
a17_0393528.text: Okay, let me give you one more try on it. Well, that time it didn't wait. All I did was go up to 1 slash 2 and the Alarm came on. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Roger.

a17_0393528.speaker: Cernan
a17_0393528.text: Okay, I went back to surge/3; it did not. So maybe it's coming on when I go up to 1 slash 2.

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Cernan
a17_0393528.text: Yes, there it is, Gordy. It's definitely repeatable. I can go up to Pressure Cryo Quantity 1 slash 2 and the Alarm comes on.

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Okay, Geno; understand.

a17_0393528.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0393528.text: You might note that - hey...

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: Okay...

a17_0393528.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0393528.text: Gordo, you might think about the fact that we were getting them when the cabin pressure was high after launch. And there might be some association there, also.

a17_0393528.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0393528.text: Okay, a good observation. [Pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: Emergency Cabin selector to Off. We got to unbolt it down there somewhere. Underneath the commander's couch. Ah, okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: Repress Package valve, Off; should be Off. [Long pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: Okay; verify Direct O 2 is Closed. Okay; Tunnel Vent Valve, LM/Command Module Delta-P. [Pause.] Okay, it's greater than 3.1. It's up around 3.6. [Long pause.]

a17_0393528.speaker: Evans
a17_0393528.text: Okay, we're going to open the Pressure Equalization Valve.

a17_0394109.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0394109.text: And, Gordy, battery A charge has been stopped and the battery compartment pressure is still reading 0.6.

a17_0394109.speaker: Evans
a17_0394109.text: Okay. There's a Delta-P of 2. We'll close the equalization valve. [Pause.] Yeah, we'll monitor for 3 minutes now.

a17_0394401.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0394401.text: Geno, Houston. We just wanted to verify that no - none of the lights in the matrix were - flashed when you operated that switch and got the Master Alarm.

a17_0394401.speaker: Cernan
a17_0394401.text: That's affirmative, Gordo; none of the lights flashed at all.

a17_0394401.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0394401.text: When we get the cabin pressure down, Gordy, here, we might try one more time. [Pause.] Which Gene just did.

a17_0394401.speaker: Evans
a17_0394401.text: Okay, still holding at 2.0 on the Delta-P.

a17_0394401.speaker: Evans
a17_0394401.text: Okay, we'll open the pressure equalization valve and when the cabin pressure gets to 4.0, hit the Repress O 2 , Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0394401.speaker: Evans
a17_0394401.text: Delta-P is about 0.6, we might make it this time.

a17_0394401.speaker: Evans
a17_0394401.text: Delta-P's - Okay, I'm going to open her right up. Delta-P is 0.2 now. [Long pause.]

a17_0394401.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0394401.text: Okay, Houston, the hatch is open.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, the Extend Latch is Engaged. Red is not visible. GN 2 Bleed button. [Singing] Okay; GN 2 Bleed. Not too much in there. [Pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Preload Selector lever - rotate parallel to the orange stripe. Okay. Preload Handle, torque clockwise to unload the old support beams. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: [Clanking noise.] Ah ha! The probe is big. Whoops - Oh, okay.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: The probe's loose in the tunnel. Okay, rotate away from the orange stripe. [Singing] Torque... [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, probe umbilicals. Is the LM Power Off? Proceed - doesn't make any difference. Dock Probe Circuit Breakers undone? [Pause.] [Garble.] [Pause.] That's good and tight.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: [Clanking noise.] Oops. This darn thing. [Pause.] Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Son of a buck. Okay, I'm trying putting those things back on now, just for the heck of it. [Pause.] It's brand new; nice and tight. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Can you smell nitrogen? Smell something up here. [Pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, probe umbilicals disconnected and stow. Electrical connector covers are closed. Yeah, yeah, those are yellow ones. Preload Handle, position against - against the umbilical connector. Okay, that's done.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Selector Lever is in the mid position. Installation Strut. [Pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Installation Strut is unstowed. Capture Latch Release Handle Lock. Okay, the Release Handle is unlocked. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Ratchet Handle unstowed to the full extension; boost to the first detent. [Pause.] That's good and tight going back to the first detent. Okay. Fold probe, looks like. Yes, it's out. [Singing.] [Pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Ooooh! There it comes. [Pause.] That's just like in the simulator. It comes down by itself. It comes - pushes me out of the way, as a matter of fact. Okay. I'll get it a little better. [Pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Ratchet Handle pulled to full extension and then ratchet one stroke. [Pause.] Gets it so it gets it off the thing. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, that's one stroke backwards now. [Pause.] Okay, Ratchet Handle and Installation Strut are restowed. Capture Latch Release Handle. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Capture Latch Release Handle is rotated 180 degrees and it's back in the recess. Okay, let's see if it comes out.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: [Clanking noise.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Ooops. Here it comes. And I couldn't see it awhile ago, Let me look - the Probe Strut's in the way. That's why you can't see it until now. Where do we want to go with this thing down over here at the... [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Houston, it's a nice clean shear pin release there on top of the probe. It's nice and clean down there. The button is depressed. There's play around the little button on the end of the probe there too.

a17_0395039.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0395039.text: Okay, Ron. In about 1 minute, we're going to have a site handover. You'll be talking through Hawaii after that takes place.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Okay. [Pause.] What's the docking angle? Blew it, I guess. 1.2 degrees, huh? [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Yeah, I think I better ver - verify that, just to make sure. COAS looks great. [Long pause.]

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: Hold a minute, Gene - wait a minute. You got - there we go.

a17_0395039.speaker: Evans
a17_0395039.text: [Clanking noise.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: [Garble] even getting - Can't see if there's any scratching on here now. [Pause.] [Garble] I [garble] out there.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Ron, this is Houston. Was that a - We'd like to confirm the tunnel index angle - that's a positive - a plus 1.2, is that right?

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Stand by. I don't believe it yet. I want to check it myself.

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: Well, Gordo, that's what I read, but I figure it's his privilege. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: I was just checking for any scratches on the drogue, but it doesn't look like there is any on there.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger.

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: See [garble]. [Singing. Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Houston. The roll docking index is on a 1.2 - a plus - one point - a plus 1.2.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. Plus 1.2.

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: And - I took a look up there in the docking latch number 4. The bungee is parallel [garble]. Bungee is parallel, but it's not fully extended. You look down in the end of it you know, and it's not fully extended. And the - capture - the docking latch itself or the docking lever is loose on the docking ring. So, it looks like to me that's when I ought to recock and fire it again.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Okay. We copy that, Ron. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Ron, can you estimate in inches how far down the bungee piston is? [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Yeah, it's down about a half an inch.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: And, when I take the - and move the handle back a ways and I can take the hook [pause] no I did [laughter]. I took the hook and I pulled it back off the docking ring and then it caught again, so now it won't go back over the docking ring. Maybe I just lifted the hook off the docking [garble] ring with my finger.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: [Garble].

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Say, Ron, I would like to caution you again, sticking your finger around or under that hook - there may still be some spring energy stored up there that could release.

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Oh, you bet you. Yeah, I know that. No, I was just touching the top of the hook when I pulled it back off the docking ring. [Pause.] I pulled it back onto the docking ring, and it looks like it's back in the cocked position now.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Okay. I think we've got the picture. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Do you want me to open the hatch here, Jack, or do you want to - while they're thinking about that I'll get out of the way and come on and open the hatch. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: [Laughter.] Can't get up and can't get down. [Long pause.] Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: We're having a long conversation here about that latch, Ron. Why don't you all just press on down the checklist and leave it as it is while we think about it?

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Okay. That's what we're doing here Gordo. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Gordo, do you want the O 2 Heaters 1 and 2, Off, and 3, Auto? That's what you've got. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Yeah, that's fine. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Okay. He's going to open the hatch and IVT. Gordo, let me give you a little more on that docking latch. When I looked at it, of course, my handle was flush against the edge and it was also - essentially - locked in position. But since the bungee was down on the thing I took hold of it, and I felt that the hook itself was loose. Okay, so I took the handle and the handle will come back - would come back once you pressed the little button, you know, to release the handle. The handle would come back to about a 45-degree position just like it normally does when you try to cock the latches. Okay, wi

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Gordo, I'm running up through the tunnel from America to Challenger.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Yeah [garble]. Okay [garble].

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: One piece of tape coming up shortly, provided I can find the tape. Here it is. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Piece of tape coming up. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: I'll tell you, Gordo, it's remarkably clean up here. It doesn't look like the snowstorm that I remember coming into last time.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Rog, Geno. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: We tried to leave it all tidied up...

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: [Garble] up here. Hey, you did a good job, friend. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Hey, that's good. Where is it? [Long pause.] Oh, you - straight out there? Let me see; I want to see. I want to take a look at it, too. Hey, there it is; sticking straight out.

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Houston, America has a VHF antenna - looks deployed perfectly.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Hey, you guys are upside down in there [laughter]. [Long pause.] The old latch here. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: The commander's window has a slight amount of condensation on the - along the lower left edge - that's the left-hand edge, really. It seems to be just there when the Sun warms the window.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Houston. 74 on 1-3.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Geez, what was that? [laughter] What was that from? [Garble] cabin repress. [Garble]. What the hell is that? [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Sounds like the cabin repress is working up there.

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: Holy smoley. [Garble].

a17_0400006.speaker: Evans
a17_0400006.text: Man oh man, did the heart beat go up on that?

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Sorry about that [garble].

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: [Laughter.] [Garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Turns out - there's Sun out in the AOT.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Okay. I'm looking out the AOT, and I see a VHF antenna and part of a rendezvous radar antenna in position 1. [Long pause.] Position 2 looks right into the radar antenna, and, as I said yesterday, it looks beautiful.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger.

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Position 3, I can see the other side of America and very, very clean AOT, very clean. [Long pause.] Okay, I got a good view of the side of the Service Module, [pause] and you can see these little blisters in the side of the covering there quite distinctly. I think people were talking about those before.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Yeah, I take that back. That's the side of - that's the side of the Command Module - looking at that has the little blisters on it. Got to get oriented up here. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Got a great view of the hatch through position 6. Watch your eyes there Gene. Look up, rather than into the Sun [garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0400006.text: Okay. Step 1 on 1-4.

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: Okay, Gordy. The LMP OPS is 6100 psi, 6100.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0400006.speaker: Cernan
a17_0400006.text: And the CDR's OPS is 5900, that's five-nine-zero-zero.

a17_0400006.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0400006.text: Okay.

a17_0400006.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0400006.text: 040:21:20 - This is Apollo Control. Cernan and Evans [means Schmitt] at this time have gone into the Lunar Module, and they're going through the housekeeping transfer of items from the Command Module into the Lunar Module and will proceed with the checklist of activating the spacecraft, or Lunar Module, spacecraft communications system, and the communications have been split into two links on Earth, Air-to-Ground 1 for the Command Module, and Air-to-Ground 2 for the Lunar Module. a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: Okay. Zip bag coming up. [Long pause.]

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: You won't scare me any more if I come on up here with you, will you? [Laughter.].

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: I got to go back in there.

a17_0402224.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0402224.text: 040:24:00 - This is Apollo Control, a correction on the earlier statement, it is Cernan and Schmitt in the Lunar Module Challenger at this time. Evans had the detail of removing the probe and drogue earlier, but he's by his lonesome, back in the Command Module.

This is Apollo Control, a correction on the earlier statement, it is Cernan and Schmitt in the Lunar Module Challenger at this time. Evans had the detail of removing the probe and drogue earlier, but he's by his lonesome, back in the Command Module.

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: Yeah. Do you want to stack part of it over there?

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: No, wait a minute. There's strips of the stuff, you know, I'll just give you a strip of it. Take it over there.

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: Okay. Here you go. That's nine of them, isn't it?

a17_0402224.speaker: Evans
a17_0402224.text: Yeah, go ahead, Jack. You're in the tunnel. What do you need.

a17_0402400.text: This is Apollo Control, a correction on the earlier statement, it is Cernan and Schmitt in the Lunar Module Challenger at this time. Evans had the detail of removing the probe and drogue earlier, but he's by his lonesome, back in the Command Module.

a17_0403632.speaker: Evans
a17_0403632.text: Am I not looking in the right place?

a17_0403632.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0403632.text: Let me look. I don't know where one is, right offhand. I'll check here. [Pause.]

a17_0403632.speaker: Evans
a17_0403632.text: Well, just help me with some terms here. I was just looking again at side of - underneath the power bungee.

a17_0403632.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0403632.text: Okay, Gordy; we're at the top of 1-13 and all switches, valves were in proper configuration.

a17_0403632.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0403632.text: Okay, you could have asked me and I could have told you that. [Pause.]

a17_0403632.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0403632.text: We were just trying to give you a plug - Well, if you don't want them - Well, we'll take it back. [Laughter.] [Long pause.] I shouldn't have said anything to the world's most experienced DLMP. Right?

a17_0403934.speaker: Evans
a17_0403934.text: Hey, can you guys open the hatch out there. [Pause.] Take your picture. [Long Pause.]

a17_0403934.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0403934.text: Ron, at first glance, it doesn't look like you have one onboard, a picture of the latch. We're still looking though, but I don't think we have one.

a17_0403934.speaker: Evans
a17_0403934.text: Well, it was kind of the conclusion I came to there, when I didn't find it in the systems data - Hey, I got a little bit to tell you about that. Oh, those little ones underneath the power bungee.

a17_0403934.speaker: Evans
a17_0403934.text: Okay, if you look at the docking latch number 4 up beside of that - Oh, kind of a J-hook looking thing. There is a snowman. In other words, a great big fat thing with a head on top of it. And if you consider the fat thing with the head on it as a snowman, well then, the snowman's head is pointing out a 9 o'clock, on that one. Whereas one that's fully cocked and latched over there, the snowman's head points up at about 11 o'clock. And [pause], okay, there's a lever that comes right out of the bottom of the power bungee, it looks like, and then it comes out of the bottom, then [garble] of that l

a17_0403934.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0403934.text: Ron, we've got just a line drawing here and we've still haven't got with you on what's what according to the drawing. Maybe you can hold off until we get a model of the latch, then we can stay with your description.

a17_0404503.speaker: Evans
a17_0404503.text: Yeah, I know it, it's up to you. [Garble] [Pause] [Garble] I want to float up in the tunnel. Do you want to float up and look?

a17_0404503.speaker: Evans
a17_0404503.text: Yeah, the congestion I had all day yesterday is just about gone.

a17_0404739.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0404739.text: Gordy, you'll be happy to know that putting the LMP's camera together is 500-percent easier in zero gravity.

a17_0405301.speaker: Evans
a17_0405301.text: Hey, Jack, if you get a chance, take a picture back this way.

a17_0405301.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0405301.text: Putting the cue cards up now, and the camera, by the way, Gordy, operated for two frames and the Reseau looked clean, lens looks clean and everything's fine with it.
