a17_0410059.speaker: Evans
a17_0410059.text: First up too. The regular type, huh? [Long pause.]

a17_0410059.speaker: Cernan
a17_0410059.text: Okay, Gordo, we're on the top of 1-15, we're ready to go ahead and transfer the power and we'll give you a call.

a17_0410059.speaker: Evans
a17_0410059.text: Okay, the LM Power circuit breaker is In. What the - let me know what you want [garble] Okay, going to Off, Reset. Okay, back to Off. And, I got the old Master Alarm again. Yeah? The pressure's been - I don't know what it is.

a17_0410059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0410059.text: Okay, Houston; we got a good transfer.

a17_0410059.speaker: Evans
a17_0410059.text: Got it again by hitting the panel. [Long pause.]

a17_0410059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0410059.text: Okay, we've got considerable conversation going on here about that docking latch, and it's not at all settled yet. But the primary thing we want to guard against is the possibility that it is malfunctioning and that we get it latched down on the ring and can't unlatch it, and, therefore, have problem with undocking, or possibly even prevent it. So, we'd like you steer clear of that until we come up with a final solution. No experimentation, please. Over.

a17_0410059.speaker: Evans
a17_0410059.text: Okay, I understand. I'll leave them alone. And just one little other bit of information to let you know. The handle itself is not free at this point to come on back down like it's - you know. Like, if it were fully cocked, the handle itself would be free to come back down. It is not free, I did not try to put a whole lot of pressure on it, but it's not free.

a17_0410059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0410059.text: Okay, Houston. Glycol Pump 2 is On, it's been on about a minute, and we've got good talkbacks from batteries 1 and 4.

a17_0410059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0410059.text: Okay, Jack, you can go ahead and switch on - onto high taps on 1 and 4.

a17_0410059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0410059.text: Okay, 1 and 4 are on high taps.

a17_0410822.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0410822.text: You faded out, Jack. Say again on glycol pressure. [Pause.]

a17_0410822.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0410822.text: Well, you can cut off the decimal. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: No, wait a minute, I got to go get it. Which one you on? A? Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Jack, I'm Simplex Alpha. Okay, try it again. I got the - how me. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Jack, you're cutting out on everything, and all I'm getting is the end of your transmission there. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay, I got counting - 1, 2, 3, 4.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Jack, you read Gene? Okay, you - you were loud and clear after your first two words in every case, just like you were cutting out on VOX. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: We got it all...

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Got it all that time. You got it all that time there now, do you read me too?

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Well, that's interesting. Let me adjust the squelch on this one here. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay. Seems to work. I can't hear the squelch on any of them. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Jack, go VHF A Transmitter and Receiver, Off, and B Transmitter, Voice, and leave the Receiver, On.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Voice, On, and Off on B now.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay. [Pause.] TR.

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay, I'm on B now. [Pause.] Okay, [garble] get some level. How's that? [Garble].

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay. You're loud and clear, Ron. How me?

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: Okay, loud and clear that time.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay. And my - my VHF Alpha had to go to 2 on the Squelch, and I'm in 3 on Bravo.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: [Garble] okay?

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: You're loud and clear, Gene.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay [garble] but not much.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay. How do you read now?

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay I got it.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, I took it B to 2. So it's the same kind of thing I guess.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay for four minutes in voice, is low bit rate check [garble].

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Houston, how do you read Challenger? Counting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Over.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Challenger, Houston. You're loud and clear, although we have a lot of background noise. Not sure whether that's getting through. Do you know if Ron is still on VOX?

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: [Garble] Challenger to give you a call [garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Hello, Houston, America. How do you read?

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: America, this is Houston. Over.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay, stand by, and Challenger's going to give you a call on S-band, and VHF checks are both Go on A and B.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay. I think our site lost lock on Challenger, we are getting some data. We'll stand by for another check.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Do you acknowledge that? I heard him the first time.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, you ought to be getting in [garble] low bit rate. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Houston, this is Challenger. Counting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. How do you read?

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Challenger, Houston. You're loud and clear, with the background noise. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: They don't have a good uplink Gene. I had signal strength. And now I don't have any at all.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Houston, Challenger gave you a call, but he does not have any uplink signal strength at all.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, and we'd like him to hold this configuration right there, until we get the site straightened out and we understand what the problem is.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: [Garble] 2.2.

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Okay, understand hold configuration there. He just got about 2.2 on the signal strength.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Geno. [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: And tell them I heard their transmission to you. No, a few minutes ago. [Pause.] I was at zero signal strength and I heard their transmission, at least one of them. The first time they acknowledged, that I was going to do it. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Did you shift my hose back? [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Hello, Challenger; this is Houston. Do you read me?

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Houston. I read you. You're weak but clear. Signal strength is fluctuating. When you call me, it fluctuated down to about 1.6. Over. And it's 2 now.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Jack. You're loud and clear. The background noise I've been mentioning, although I guess you haven't heard me mention it until now, is what we expect in Down Voice Backup and Low Bit Rate. How have you read this transmission all the way through? Over.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Did he say "say again?" Gene? Gene, did he say "say again?" I got a little bit - oh he's got three point...

a17_0411100.speaker: Evans
a17_0411100.text: [Garble] they're not talking to us [garble].

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: What? [Pause.] Okay, Houston. I've got 3.4 on the signal strength, and try me again.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Challenger. You're coming in loud and clear. How do you read me?

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Houston. I know you tried to transmit. I could just barely tell that. I could see the signal strength vary down to 3. You were modulating, apparently, but you're not getting through to me.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Challenger. I'm transmitting simul now in both S-band frequencies, and it sounds to us like for some reason when I transmit, the uplink signal starts to break up. It's just the way you see it. Over.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Gordy. You're breaking up there. Still modulating, but I cannot read you. Would you - would you tell America what you said?

a17_0411100.speaker: Cernan
a17_0411100.text: Yes, Gordy, we - we read you in America loud and clear on that simul.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: Okay, Geno. [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: Is he talking, Gene? [Long pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: As soon as he starts trying to talk, the signal strength drops off about 0.4. Now, I have had - I heard him loud and clear one time when he called you guys.

a17_0411100.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0411100.text: America and Challenger, we're going to hand over to a different site and try that here in about 30 seconds.

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: What else do we have to do, get some of these mags stowed? [Pause.]

a17_0411100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0411100.text: We've got to stow the mags. Here, put the PPK where it belongs.

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Hello, Challenger; this is Houston through Bermuda. How do you copy?

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Challenger, this is Houston. How do you read me?

a17_0412434.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0412434.text: Do you want to [garble] up the camera [garble] tow our LCG back there [garble].

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Okay, Jack. I think he answered us, but he was completely lost in the noise. I could just barely make out some answers, somebody talking. Could he hear us okay?

a17_0412434.speaker: Cernan
a17_0412434.text: No. If he did hear you, he didn't answer.

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Okay. It was my imagination then.

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Challenger, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Hello, Challenger; Houston. How do you read? [Long pause.]

a17_0412434.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412434.text: Hello, Challenger. This is Houston. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, how do you copy. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0412931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412931.text: Can you tell Jack, ask him to verify he's on aft Omni?

a17_0412931.speaker: Cernan
a17_0412931.text: Okay. I'll have him verify he's on aft Omni. [Pause.]

a17_0412931.speaker: Cernan
a17_0412931.text: [Garble] earlier when he was [garble] that he had good signal strength [garble] he would transmit [garble].

a17_0412931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412931.text: But on this last set of checks, we didn't hear anything at your end.

a17_0412931.speaker: Cernan
a17_0412931.text: There was one time earlier when he had zero signal strength where he said he could hear you transmitting to us very weak but clear.

a17_0412931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412931.text: Hello, Challenger. Hello, Challenger; this is Houston. How do you read?

a17_0412931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0412931.text: Okay. You're loud - well, you're about 3 by, Gordy, but very clear.

a17_0412931.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0412931.text: Okay, Jack. We're getting you about 1 by 1 in the midst of a lot of noise, but we could tell you're sounding much better.

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: No. I've got 2 now signal strength. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, this is Houston. Going up to you through Bermuda, and your - you should come down through Goldstone. How do I sound now? [No answer.] [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: You're 1.8, 1.8. Yep. Never heard him. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Hello, Challenger; Houston. How do you read? [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Gordy received me, didn't he? [Pause.] Well, he started to say something; then he dropped off.

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Now he's up. Haven't heard him. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: America, Houston.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Okay. We're going to go back to Goldstone, both up and down, and we'd like Jack to do step 406 on the checklist; in other words, go to Voice, S-Band Voice to Voice, the Biomed to Right. And we're going to give it a try in the normal configuration. Over.

a17_0413328.speaker: Cernan
a17_0413328.text: They want step 406, gentlemen. Biomed, Right; and S-Band Voice to Voice.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0413328.speaker: Cernan
a17_0413328.text: Okay, he's going there now.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Cernan
a17_0413328.text: Houston, do you read Challenger?

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Roger, Challenger. Read you weak but clear. How do you read?

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Okay, Houston, You just came in loud and clear. How do you read?

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Okay. And that time, you're loud and clear, Jack and sounds real good.

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Okay, Gordy. Let me say once again, way back when we first started and Gene was talking to you, I heard one of your answers, weak but clear, with zero signal strength showing here. Now, that might have been through Ron's VOX, I don't know. Since then, you've been able to modulate the signal strength, with occasional weak words. And - and then, when that signal strength was up around 3.2, where it is now, then you came in loud and clear with a broadcast. I answered you, you said about three words, then dropped off completely. And then we - we changed configuration.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Okay, Jack. That correlates with what we've seen here in the way of signal strengths dropping in and out. Stand by, and I'll see where we want to go from here.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, Houston. We'd like you to do step 7. We'll check out the telemetry High Bit Rate. [Pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Okay; step 7. [Pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: And, Challenger; Houston. Making a voice check. How do you copy?

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Roger. You're loud and clear. How me?

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: You're loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, Houston. We're looking at the High Bit Rate for a minute here while we're waiting. Would you check the Cross Tie circuit breakers, panel 16? Verify they're Open.

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: That's verified. Cross Tie's Bus and Bal Loads, Open.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, Houston. We'd like you to accomplish step number 8. [Pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Roger. Step 8. [Long pause.]

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read the Challenger? 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Over.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Challenger, you're loud and clear. How me?

a17_0413328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0413328.text: Loud and clear.

a17_0413328.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0413328.text: Rog.

a17_0414601.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0414601.text: Challenger, Houston. Go ahead with step 9. Report the ED Bat voltages. [Pause.]

a17_0414601.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0414601.text: Okay, Houston. ED Bats A and B are 37.2.

a17_0414601.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0414601.text: Roger. [Pause.] Okay. And go ahead with step 10, and then we'll go back and try to find out what's wrong with Down Voice Backup. [Long pause.]

a17_0414601.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0414601.text: Go ahead and check the sequence camera, if you haven't already, Jack, and then we'll have some steps for you to check out what was wrong with Down Voice Backup. [Pause.]

a17_0414601.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0414601.text: Sequence camera - sequence camera is Go.

a17_0414601.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0414601.text: And I'm ready for your step.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Challenger, Houston. We'd like the Ranging switch to Off/Reset, and the Voice switch to Down Voice Backup, then give us a call. Over.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay. Off/Reset on Range, and Down Voice Backup on Voice.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Gordy. On Down Voice Backup, how do you read? 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Jack. You're readable. You're [pause]. Okay, Challenger, we read your transmission, but you're just about - just about lost in the noise. Give us another count, please.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Houston; this is the Challenger. You were loud and clear, loud and clear. No different from the transmissions in Voice, and counting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. How do you read? Over.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Jack. It got a lot better. You're - you're perfectly readable now. Sounding good. [Pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: That sounds good. [Long pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Jack. Would you go to High Bit Rate?

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Roger. Challenger's High Bit Rate. How do you read High Bit Rate?

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay. Still the same. Loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay. We'd like Biomed, Off now, Jack.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Roger. Going Biomed, Off. Okay, Houston. How do you read the LM? Down Voice Backup; Biomed, Off; PCM, Hi. Over.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Jack. You're loud and clear.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Gordy. And that was hot mike, so that's working fine up here. And you're loud and clear, also. [Pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Jack. Let's try PCM, Lo, now. [Pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay. Talking to you Down Voice Backup; Biomed, Off; and PCM, Lo. How do you read? Over.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay. Same old, loud and clear.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, Gordy. Certainly is clear up here. You're coming through 5 by at signal strength 3.2, and - all appearances up here, that previous problem was an uplink. But I guess you were not reading me. is that correct?

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Well, I was - The answer is yes and no at various times. We think, though, we have a good handle on the problem.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay; very good. [Long pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Are you ready for us to press on here, Gordy? We're all stowed and - in pretty good shape in the LM.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Okay. We'd like you to check one more switch first before moving on. Check the Updata Link switch to Off. [Pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, That is verified Off.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Want you to stand by a minute or two Jack, until we verify a funny-looking parameter here on that uplink switch. [Pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Standing by. [Pause.] What's that? No, they want - they got something looking funny on the uplink - they're [garble] I guess on the uplink switch.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: Challenger, Houston...

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: They want to look at it.

a17_0415036.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0415036.text: That was a bad call. We were reading the data wrong. You're clear to press on with the checklist now on page 1-20.

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay. We'll press on. Geno, here is your jettison bag. You can get back to Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0415036.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0415036.text: Okay, S-band PR Off, VHF Off; I can hear you. [Pause.] PM Off.

a17_0420211.speaker: Cernan
a17_0420211.text: Okay, Houston. We just transferred to CSM power, and the caution warning light did go off. [Pause.]

a17_0420737.speaker: Cernan
a17_0420737.text: Gordo, we're about wrapped up here in Challenger. It looks like there's some life in - in the old bird, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0420737.speaker: Cernan
a17_0420737.text: Okay. We'll give you a call when we - when we get the hatch closed. Ron's doing some housekeeping in the Command Module, and we're going to take it slow getting back in.

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Okay, Houston. The drogue is going in. [Long pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger, Ron. We've got a couple of questions for you about those - about the latch. Good old latch number 4 gave us a problem I guess, huh? [No answer.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: America, Houston. [Pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: America, go ahead.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Ron, can you take a look at the latch number 4, and is the hook back away from the ring approximately one inch, as opposed to resting against the ring? [No answer.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: America, Houston, did you copy my question? [No answer.]

a17_0421601.speaker: MCC-H
a17_0421601.text: We're going back to air-ground one. [Pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Okay, I heard somebody going to air-ground one that time, and...

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger, Ron. Got a couple of questions on those - that latch number 4 if you can answer it for me. [No answer.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: America, Houston. [No answer.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: America, Houston. We're back with you after some site changeover. How do you read?

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Okay; loud and clear. How me, Bob?

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Real good, Ron. On that number 4, latch number 4, is the hook backed away from the ring about 1 inch as opposed to resting against the ring? Do you have about an inch clearance on that hook right now? [Long pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Well, there's about ½ inch.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Okay. Understand about ½ inch. In what position was the latch handle when the hook was first moved back, Ron? Was it kind of like in a normal stroke-back, or was it just flopping back? [Pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: No, when I first looked at it, the latch handle was - see, the hook itself was over the ring when I first looked at it.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Rog. We understand that...

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: The hook was over the ring, and the - and the latch handle was flush, you know. It looks just like a normal - hooked docking latch, you know.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Rog. Understand.

a17_0421601.speaker: Cernan
a17_0421601.text: And, Bob, this is Gene. I can confirm that it did not fold back easily, because I - I checked it yesterday. I didn't check - I checked to see that the hooks were over as well as where the handles would fold back, but I obviously didn't check to see whether that one was seated. But the handle was locked.

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Yes, that's right.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger. Understand. And the first thing you saw was the depression in the bungee. is that - is that affirm?

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Yeah, that's affirm. And the bungee is depressed about 3/8 - 3/8 to a ½ inch you know.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: You can push the - you can push the hook about an inch away from the ring, but the normal - just a resting position on the thing is about a finger's width or ½ inch from the ring.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger. In other words, the loose - The hook is loose so it flops a little bit; you can move it back and forth. Is that affirm?

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Yeah. I can move it from about ½ inch to an inch from the edge of the ring - clearing the edge of the docking ring.

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Roger. Ron, when you pulled the hook - when you pulled the handle back, did you reach and pull the hook back with it, or did it come back with the handle like a normal pullback then?

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: No, the - the hook did not come back with the handle. The hook did not come back with the handle. Although, when I - when I pulled the handle back to - you know, which is - which is kind of a normally uncocked position - and then it wouldn't go any further, you know. It wouldn't go an farther. And then the latch itself - or the hook - the J-hook; I'll call it the hook. I moved it off off the docking ring back to this position that was about an inch or ½ inch from the docking ring. And it stays right there now. And I can't push it back up into the docking ring at all. Can't push the hook

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Okay. We copy that. [Long pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Okay, Ron. Our plan here is to leave it like it is. And we're going to think about it tonight, and we'd like you to just keep pressing on. Just leave it alone, okay?

a17_0421601.speaker: Evans
a17_0421601.text: Okay. Sounds good. It'll clear the docking ring; no problem. [Pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Cernan
a17_0421601.text: Houston, America. While Ron's putting in the probe and getting the hatch back in, I'm going to go ahead and maneuver. How's that sound?

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: That's real fine, Gene.

a17_0421601.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0421601.text: 042:24:30 - This is Apollo Control at 42 hours, 27 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We're estimating the change of shift press conference in 15 minutes; 15 minutes at 6:15 Central Time in the small briefing room. Spacecraft communicator now is Bob Overmeyer. During this past checkout of the Lunar Module, we've had considerable difficulty in some of the communications configurations in the way the downlinks and uplinks were set up. And some bit of difficulty in sorting out just what the nature of the problem in one of the docking latches is. People will be examining this through the night and durin

Spacecraft communicator now is Bob Overmeyer. During this past checkout of the Lunar Module, we've had considerable difficulty in some of the communications configurations in the way the downlinks and uplinks were set up. And some bit of difficulty in sorting out just what the nature of the problem in one of the docking latches is. People will be examining this through the night and during the checko

a17_0421601.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0421601.text: Bob, are you all going to want Omni or High Gain on this?

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: Stand by on that. [Long pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0421601.text: We're all locked up on the High Gain. We'd just like you to leave it on High Gain. The angles you see in the Flight Plan are in case it breaks lock. That's what you need for - with this attitude. [Pause.]

a17_0421601.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0421601.text: Okay.

a17_0423010.speaker: Evans
a17_0423010.text: Okay, Houston. The probe is installed. We'll get the hatch in now.

a17_0423010.speaker: Evans
a17_0423010.text: I'm not going to connect the umbilicals unless you really want to look at probe temperature.

a17_0423010.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0423010.text: Stand by on that, Ron. [Pause.] We concur on that, Ron.

a17_0423628.speaker: Evans
a17_0423628.text: Okay, Houston. The hatch went in nominally, once the probe installation strut was stowed in the right position.

a17_0424110.text: This is Apollo Control at 42 hours, 41 minutes. Apollo 17 now 144,002 nautical miles [266,692 km] from Earth. Velocity, 3,577 feet per second [1,090 m/s]. The change-of-shift briefing is ready to start in the News Center briefing room. We'll take down this air/ground line and tape any communications during the course of the briefing and replay them at the conclusion of the news conference. This is Mission Control, Houston, at 42 hours, 41 minutes.

a17_0424347.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0424347.text: 17, Houston. We'rm - We're recommending Quads Bravo and Delta for spin up.

a17_0424347.speaker: Evans
a17_0424347.text: Okay; Bravo and Delta. Thank you.

a17_0425734.speaker: Evans
a17_0425734.text: Okay, Houston. At 042:56:52.04, I started the stop watch, and also the watch read 18:30:01.

a17_0430224.speaker: Evans
a17_0430224.text: Okay, Houston. We've started on the heat select radial and lineal part - part of it. The little pie-shaped things are changing color as we go out. The lineal part of it - all of the chips seemed to have been concentrated on the front edge of the glass, and they're all pretty much in the linear direction or an XX-direction. At this point in time, I haven't seen any movement yet.

a17_0430224.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0430224.text: Roger, Ron. Aren't they concentrated the same way they were on the backup unit the other evening in the White Room - on the linear?

a17_0430224.speaker: Evans
a17_0430224.text: Yeah, all those chips seem to be - well - in an XX - I got the lineal direction, the lineal part of the experiment in the XX-direction. And all the chips are lined up in that XX-direction on the front or the top of the glass.

a17_0430224.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0430224.text: Roger. That's just the way you were in the backup unit the other day in the White Room.

a17_0431136.speaker: Evans
a17_0431136.text: Okay, Houston. We've started the cooldown in Light 5 position there. The radial cells, they all started to change color except the one from about 10 o'clock to 12 o'clock.

a17_0431136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0431136.text: Roger. Except from 10 to 12. We've got it. Did the lineal ball stay right in line there, Ron?

a17_0431136.speaker: Evans
a17_0431136.text: Yeah, the crystals or chips that are inside there didn't move at all. Yes, they're [garble]...

a17_0431136.speaker: Evans
a17_0431136.text: On the color patterns behind there - the one on the left, as you look at the unit - the color crystals only changed down to about 0.9 of the first square as you come down from the top. The rest of them are all black on that partic - on the left row.

a17_0431136.speaker: Evans
a17_0431136.text: So that's the maximum extent of the - that's the max extent of the heating.

a17_0431136.speaker: Evans
a17_0431136.text: You might check and see if the guys want to heat it a little bit longer the next time, when they do it in the PTC.

a17_0431136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0431136.text: Yeah. Roger, Ron. We're copying everything you're saying, and we've got all kinds of support here; we - in fact, we've got one backup unit here watching what you're doing, so we'll keep you posted on what we think.

a17_0431136.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0431136.text: Is the backup CMP operating it?

a17_0431136.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0431136.text: That's the way to do things.

a17_0431136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0431136.text: And, Ron, we'd like you to stay nominal on the heating time due to the film limitation.

a17_0431509.speaker: Evans
a17_0431509.text: Okay, Houston; 17 here. Is there enough film in there to allow me to keep the camera running while I try to fill up that flow pattern?

a17_0431509.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0431509.text: It's affirmative, Ron. You can leave it running.

a17_0431509.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0431509.text: 043:15:39 - This is Apollo Control at 43 hours, 16 minutes. Apollo 17 is 145,178 nautical miles [268,870 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 3,543 feet per second [1,080 m/s]. The crew is now in the midst of the heat flow and convection demonstration. This is the demonstration that's designed to provide more exact data on the behavior of fluids in a low gravity field. This type of investigation is really not possible on Earth where gravity determines flow of fluids. In space the flow forces surface tension. There are three test cells involved in this demonstration for measuring and observi

a17_0431539.text: This is Apollo Control at 43 hours, 16 minutes. Apollo 17 is 145,178 nautical miles [268,870 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 3,543 feet per second [1,080 m/s]. The crew is now in the midst of the heat flow and convection demonstration. This is the demonstration that's designed to provide more exact data on the behavior of fluids in a low gravity field. This type of investigation is really not possible on Earth where gravity determines flow of fluids. In space the flow forces surface tension. There are three test cells involved in this demonstration for measuring and observing the fluid

a17_0431539.speaker: Evans
a17_0431539.text: Okay, Houston. The first thing I noticed, as soon as I opened the Flow four turns, when it started running out a little bit, even - even without doing the inject. Okay; that's because the Inject thing was open just a little bit, but it's all right.

a17_0431651.speaker: Evans
a17_0431651.text: Okay, Houston. The first thing I noticed, as soon as I opened the Flow four turns, when it started running out a little bit, even - even without doing the inject. Okay; that's because the Inject thing was open just a little bit, but it's all right.

a17_0431651.speaker: Evans
a17_0431651.text: Okay; I'll try to squirt some fluid in there...

a17_0431651.speaker: Evans
a17_0431651.text: Okay; I'm taking it in quite slow. It's noted there are quite a few small bubbles coming out with it. So far, so good. It hasn't overflowed the - the first capillary ring. And it's taken off, and it's going by capillary action toward the bottom and toward the top.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; that's two turns now. The meniscus is still holding on the first inner ring - it looks like all the way around, at least the part I can see. The bubbles - big bubbles that have been coming out now, and also the fluid have taken over the right half of the bottom of the dish. We're starting to fill in a little bit, maybe a fourth of an inch - fourth of an inch circumference coming around from the left side opposite the injection port.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; I'll keep going here. We're about two and a half turns now. And it looks like all of the bubbles have already come out. We're getting real fluid now coming out. It's a real pretty picture anyhow.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; that's three turns. I don't believe we're going to be able to cover the entire bottom with the four turns. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay. That's four turns, and - it's covered up the right - oh, three-fourths of the floor of the thing and about three-eights of an inch on the left side of the - of the floor - three-eights of an inch annulus all the way around, except for the right - oh, say right two-thirds of the floor.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger, Ron. You can use more than four turns if you need it.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; let's go ahead and try to cover up the whole floor on the thing before we do it. The bubbles are in there, and I'm afraid they're going to stay un - unless they disappear when we heat it.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: There now it's - it's coming out with no bubbles now, and it looks like it almost formed a meniscus on top of itself - on top of where the bubbles were.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger, Ron. Is it continuing to spread out?

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Yeah, it's continuing to spread out now, and without pumping anything into it at all - I did that last turn fairly fast - and it seems to be spreading of its own accord now, and it should go on over and cover up the bottom, I think. Once it completely covers up the bottom, I think we should go ahead and start the heat High on this pattern.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay. Now the - Everything's all hooked together now. We completely filled up the bottom of the floor.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Hey, for some reason, the bubbles seem to be starting to break now.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. We copy that, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay. I don't know if it's coincidence or what, but all the bubbles are formed together, essentially in the center - along the plus-X-axis direction. And they're about 1 inch wide. And then they start about three-quarters - I mean three-eights of an inch in from the circumference.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; I was going to try to break the bubbles with a pencil, but if you try to push a pencil into the bubble, it just moves aside.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: So that being the case, I'm going to go ahead and start the - start the timer.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: We concur on that, Ron.

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: That's called the old push-a-bubble-with-a-pencil trick.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. Just need a sharper pencil, Jack.

a17_0432141.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0432141.text: 043:28:44 - Air-to-Ground is live now.
Air-to-Ground is live now.

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: Either that or a thinner bubble. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: This is the best Friday afternoon matinee I've ever been to.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: How about Friday evening, Jack? [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: Well, I've lost track. I don't think - I don't think there's any...

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Stand by.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Mark. That was 1 minute after the start.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: I'll give you another mark when I go to High on the - with the Select switch. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Mark it.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Each bubble looks like it's a locus of - it looks like it's starting one of the Bernu call - Bernoulli cells.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Say that again, Ron.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Okay; each one of those bubbles looks like it's the locus - or the start of one of the Bénard cells.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger.

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: So far, the bubbles aren't breaking.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: We copy that. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: Is Stu getting - did Stu get bubbles on his pattern, Bob?

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: We're not running it down here. We're just demonstrating on the demonstrator there, but Stu can tell you.

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: Oh, I thought you were running...

a17_0432141.speaker: Roosa
a17_0432141.text: Roger, Jack. Yes, I - you're talking of the one we - that we did, right?

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: That's right. Well, I am now. I thought you were running it down there also.

a17_0432141.speaker: Roosa
a17_0432141.text: No. Okay. The one that we did in flight - Yeah, I had - I had a lot of bubbles, but I couldn't get mine - Krytox out across the center. So, you all are already well ahead of what I did.

a17_0432141.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0432141.text: Gee, I'm sorry you had to admit that, Stu.

a17_0432141.speaker: Roosa
a17_0432141.text: Oh, you all just do such good work. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Another thing is, it seems to me like, in one g, the Bénard cells started completely back to the edge, you know, right back to the edge of the circle. And in this case, at least, they haven't filled in yet back to the edge of the circle at all. They all started out in the center and are working around the bubbles, and then it's now - just now starting to form a few of them where there aren't any bubbles.

a17_0432141.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0432141.text: Roger, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Roosa
a17_0432141.text: How large are the cells, Ron? [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: Well, they're varying considerably in size. I can see one that's about a half an inch across, and then the other ones - they've got a great big bubble in it, and yet the cell itself is down to maybe an eighth of an inch. The bigger ones seem to be on the outside; and, of course, there are very few bubbles on the outside also.

a17_0432141.speaker: Roosa
a17_0432141.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: And the bigger ones, generally right now, are averaging about - oh, a fourth to three-eights of an inch in their cross - cross section [garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0432141.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0432141.text: 043:34:54 - This is Apollo Control...
This is Apollo Control...

a17_0432141.speaker: Evans
a17_0432141.text: The cells tend to be somewhat polygonal. Let's see, we've been going 6 minutes - 4 minutes into the heating part of it and the cells are polygonal but they don't seem to be quite as straight-lined as they were on the ground.

a17_0433946.speaker: Evans
a17_0433946.text: Okay; now the Bénard cells are starting to form in that outer annulus that went all the way around.

a17_0434551.speaker: Evans
a17_0434551.text: Okay; we went back to light 4 now. And we never did get any real polygonal cells formed around the outer annulus. And even the cells that were formed on the thing, it seemed like the particle flow within the cells was very slow when you compare that with the way it was in one G.

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Okay; I'm trying to - suck the stuff back in the - the entry tube there, and it looks like part of it's coming in. [Pause.]

a17_0434759.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0434759.text: Roger, Ron. We copy that. [Long pause.]

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: And the camera is down to about 50 percent here, so I'm going to go ahead and turn it off now.

a17_0434759.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0434759.text: Roger, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0434759.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0434759.text: Ron, if I didn't tell you, we concur with turning the DAC off there.

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Okay; yeah, I got you. I'll turn it off. [Long pause.]

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: You know, I just happened to think, after I've already sucked part of those bubbles back in there, we've got enough fluid in there to pump it out the next time without sucking that back in there, don't we?

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: I'm sorry, Ron. Say that again.

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Don't we have enough of the Krytox fluid without sucking that back in there? Maybe I can just wipe the Krytox off with some Kleenex, and maybe there won't be any bubbles the next time.

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: Okay; stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: Ron, I guess we understand you've pulled some back in, but you haven't pulled any of the bubbles. Now, if you pull any more in, you're going to start the bubbles back in. is that correct?

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Yeah; that's correct.

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: Okay; why don't you stand by here on that then?

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Let me see - I'll see if I can push the bubbles out of the way here with something.

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: Okay. The consensus is that we would like to not pull the bubbles back in. I think you've got a good idea.

a17_0434759.speaker: Evans
a17_0434759.text: Okay.

a17_0434759.speaker: Roosa
a17_0434759.text: It's the old keep-the-bubbles-out-of-the-Krytox trick.

a17_0440328.text: Say, Bob, say again those jets you're recommended for PTC.

a17_0440328.text: We recommended Bravo and and Delta for spinup - B, D.

a17_0440328.text: Okay; do the rates look okay to you? [Pause.]

a17_0440328.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0440328.text: Jack, when you get done with the PTC area here, we'd like you to get out the Flight Plan Supplement. We'd like to get a food report from you all on your food intake for today.

a17_0440328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0440328.text: I thought we gave you that in the morning. Happy to do it, but...

a17_0440328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0440328.text: You want a special report? Is that what you want?

a17_0440328.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0440328.text: We'd just like to have it - prefer tonight. [Pause.]

a17_0440328.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0440328.text: It sounds like you don't think we're eating enough.

a17_0440328.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0440328.text: Ron, would you check your Noun 78? [Long pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0441327.text: Jack or Ron, when you come around, we'll ask you to stow the High Gain on our call, and we'll be wanting Omni Bravo.

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: And are you ready for the trotting gourmet's report?

a17_0441327.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0441327.text: Roger. Everybody's here with all ears.

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: Okay. The CDR today had scrambled eggs and three bacon squares and a can of peaches and pineapple drink for breakfast. And then later on in the day, he had peanut butter, jelly, and bread with a chocolate bar and some dried apricots. [Long pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: And the LMP had scrambled eggs and four bacon squares, an orange drink, and cocoa for breakfast, and potato soup, two peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, and a cherry bar, and an orange drink. [Long pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: And that hero of the matinee, the matinee idol of Spaceship America, had scrambled eggs, bacon squares, peaches, cinnamon toast, orange juice, and cocoa for breakfast. That's how he keeps his form. And, for lunch, he had a peanut butter sandwich and citrus beverage. [Long pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: And that's it, since there's nobody else up here. [Pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0441327.text: Roger. We copy that. We'd like you to stow the High Gain at this time and Omni Bravo. [Long pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0441327.text: Jack, we appreciate all your information, and we'd like to just pass on some recommendations here from the ground that we'd like you to keep on with your regular menu as much as possible. And, if you do cut anything off, we'd like you to concentrate on eating the meats, the juices, and the fruitcake, which are the most effective for maintaining your electrolyte balance. [Pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Cernan
a17_0441327.text: Okay, Bob. We understand what you're saying. We're shooting at eating - eating it all. It's just a lot of food, that's all.

a17_0441327.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0441327.text: Rog. We understand, Gene. Also, on that group of foods, peanut butter's great for the bal - electrolyte balance, also; so you're doing okay. [Pause.]

a17_0441327.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0441327.text: I knew it was good for something. It couldn't be that good without being good for something.

a17_0441327.speaker: Cernan
a17_0441327.text: I think we're all trying to make a concentrated effort also to keep quite a bit of water down.

a17_0452950.text: Yeah. Rog. [Pause.] Yeah, it'll be up before then. We'll watch you fill the pan. We just - while you're taking time wiping it and all that, that's when we - we don't want to use up the film there. [Long pause.]

a17_0452950.speaker: Evans
a17_0452950.text: Okay. I'm with you. Actually, I've already cleaned out the - the little area there.

a17_0452950.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0452950.text: Roger. I've got 1 minute on my timer right now - about 01:27, actually.

a17_0452950.speaker: Evans
a17_0452950.text: Oh, thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0452950.speaker: Evans
a17_0452950.text: Well, we'll start at 2 minutes.

a17_0452950.speaker: Evans
a17_0452950.text: Well, now all of the little metal chips in there are parallel to the YY axis.

a17_0452950.speaker: Evans
a17_0452950.text: They're still on the front face of the lineal cell.

a17_0452950.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0452950.text: You're still on the front page with the [garble].

a17_0453841.text: This is Apollo Control at 45 hours, 38 minutes. Distance now 149,941 nautical miles [277,691 km] from the Earth; velocity, 3,405 feet per second [1,038 km].

a17_0454750.speaker: Evans
a17_0454750.text: Okay, Houston. The DAC is Off now.

a17_0454750.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0454750.text: Yeah, Ron. If it's not too much bother, it's one of those nice things to have. The PI would like you to take a picture with the - with the 35-millimeter indoor of the orientation of the heat flow as it's mounted. See if you can get that, if it's not too much problem.

a17_0454750.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0454750.text: And that should be magazine SS, which is the same one you'll use for - with the ALFMED tomorrow.

a17_0454750.speaker: Evans
a17_0454750.text: Okay. I opened the flow about four turns. A little bit is running out - one big bubble in it. And I still have a little bit left over, even though I wiped it out pretty good awhile ago. The meniscus is up to the bottom ring, and I think we put in eight things in there where it's going to try to get the meniscus up to the top baffle. Is that correct?

a17_0455116.speaker: Evans
a17_0455116.text: There must have been a few more bubbles down in there again. That was two turns now, and I've got it about half full all the way across.

a17_0455116.speaker: Evans
a17_0455116.text: But, maybe there's just about eight or 10 bubbles in it. [Long pause.]

a17_0455116.speaker: Evans
a17_0455116.text: [Garble] That's three turns. The fluid is essentially [garble] so far. And we're still going on the first - fourth turn now, and it's still develops a meniscus around the lower baffle - the smaller baffle.

a17_0455456.speaker: Evans
a17_0455456.text: Okay. Looks like about six of the bubbles have developed into three, for some reason.

a17_0455456.speaker: Evans
a17_0455456.text: Oh-oh. It was doing real well there. Then on seventh turn, a bunch of bubbles came in again.

a17_0455724.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0455724.text: Ron, I might have given you a bad call before. We don't want the DAC on until just before that 2-minute mark here, where just prior to going Experiment/Heat Select - Flow Pattern - Low. At that point, is where we want the DAC on. [Pause.]

a17_0455724.speaker: Evans
a17_0455724.text: Okay. You want the DAC on when it starts heating up.

a17_0455724.speaker: Evans
a17_0455724.text: Okay. You, know - I may have lost track of turns here, but I think we've got - really got 7½ or 6½ turns in here. And it still hasn't overflown that first lower baffle. I've got a tremendous concave - convex surface on the fluid, but it still hasn't broken the meniscus of the first baf - baffle.

a17_0455724.speaker: Evans
a17_0455724.text: Okay. I'm going to go ahead and take it another turn, because it was my understanding we wanted to try to get it in the second baffle, anyhow. So, I'm going to take another turn of Krytox and put some more in there.

a17_0455724.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0455724.text: Ron, if that - if that doesn't do it, they're saying you might want to take a pencil or something and stir it up a bit and try and break it up from lower baffle into the upper baffle. [Pause.]

a17_0455724.speaker: Evans
a17_0455724.text: (Chuckle) Okay. I'm afraid, I may have it all over the place if I do that, but I'll try it.

a17_0455724.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0455724.text: Ron, just a question while you're watching it here. Do you have any bubbles in the lineal cell?

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Yeah. This one is going to be interesting. There are about, oh, a dozen, nine to a dozen - small bubbles right next to the inject board and then about the same number right in the center of the convex portion of it.

a17_0460256.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0460256.text: Roger, Ron. Did you - we didn't copy your answer to our question about any bubbles in the lineal. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: No, I didn't get to the question on that. In the lineal unit there are no bubbles whatsoever.

a17_0460256.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0460256.text: Roger. Thank you.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: And there might have been very slight movement. Matter of fact, I can see just a very slight movement, even now. The particles, in there, they're still lined up in the YY direction essentially though, although it looks like some of them may have deviated from the front of the lineal unit back toward the center, or toward the back of the lineal unit, as you call it. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Well, I missed the 2-minute start time there, but I can keep track of it here.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: So we'll start the DAC, and then I'll turn this to Low at 02:45. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We got a hack on it, Ron. If you started it, we started our clock.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. [Pause.] You know, just for future reference here, if we like to do things in zero g and without jarring or jiggle, we want to make sure that the switch actuates with a minimum of pressure.

a17_0460256.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0460256.text: Roger, A good point.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: [Laughter.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: You have enough light to get that thing?

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. That's just now starting to develop. Look like circular cells, great big ones. And then some of the bigger ones are subdividing now. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We got that.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: The bigger ones are even - some of them are even getting bigger. One of them is - oh, about three-quarters of an inch in diameter, and it hasn't divided yet, at all. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Those are real good comments, Ron. I was in just talking with the experimenters, and if you've got nothing else to do, giving us some sizes of those cells would certainly be very beneficial. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. Frame 27 was taken at an elapsed time of about 4 minutes. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We got that.

a17_0460256.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0460256.text: Stu, this is Jack. I was taking the pictures. I took four pictures about 20 seconds apart - of the sequence just after he started it. And that ended with - or started with frame 26.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. Frame 26 for 4 seconds - I mean for 4 frames. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. That one cell I spoke of that was about three-quarters of an inch in diameter now is about an inch long and maybe three-quarters of an inch wide. Each - All of the cells seem to be bigger, in general. They're bigger this time. There is two small ones at about an eighth of an inch and - and along one side. The other one is a half-inch, a half-inch - oh, a quarter of an inch, a half inch, and then a circular when you get around the outs - out - annulus of the cup. Then you start getting circular sides instead of straight sides. All of the flow comes from the little center spot and flows ou

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We - we copy that...

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: In this case, all of the bubbles have disappeared, except two. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Ron, is the smallest cell you see about an eighth of an inch across?

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: The smallest cell I see is a four-sided one; it looks like a diamond. And it's an eighth of an inch on one side, an eighth of an inch on the other side, and maybe 3/16 on the other two sides.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. That sounds - that's a good description, Ron. I know on mine some of the smaller ones didn't show up in the - in the film, and we were not - not sure what size they are. So you might, before you quit, bracket the - the smallest or the biggest cells by your estimate of the size.

a17_0460256.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0460256.text: 046:10:17 - This is Apollo Control at 46 hours, 10 minutes. Apollo 17 is 150,976 nautical miles [279,608 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 3,375 feet per second [1,029 m/s].
This is Apollo Control at 46 hours, 10 minutes. Apollo 17 is 150,976 nautical miles [279,608 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 3,375 feet per second [1,029 m/s].

a17_0460256.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0460256.text: [Garble] any rate, frame number 31, frame number 31 and frames 24 and 25 show orientation of the experiment.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: And the information first half of the experiment. The orientation was 90 degrees from this one, [Laughter] in that the lineal cell was on the right, and the lineal cell was aligned with the XX axis.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay, Ron. We got - We had a drop in our signal strength there, and we did get your last comment about the orientation. We missed some comment about the frame numbers; I think came from Jack.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. Something's a little different on this one here. Right at the top of the flow circle, it looks just like a finger. It's a curved surface that goes out and almost touches the - the circumference of the dish. And it looks just like if you're holding your finger up and looking at it. It's that type of a shape to it. It comes back down, and it's about a half an inch wide. The flow again emanates from a source that is almost on the fingertip, you might say. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We copy. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. Somehow, that fingertip finally touched the complete circumference, and the tip of the finger disappeared.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. My - my small one-eighth inch - or one-eighth of an inch sided diamond joined with another one, now, and one side of the diamond is gone. I still have three sides of the diamond and the fourth side of the diamond, or the upper right-hand corner of the diamond, you might say, has disappeared and goes on with another little square - or rectangle. One - one end of the rectangle is about 3/l6 of an inch long; the other two sides are about three-eights of an inch long.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Ron, what's the location of that - of that diamond and rectangle in the - in the circular dish? And is it near the edge, or is it towards the center?

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: There are almost - No, it's almost in the center. Towards the center. Almost in the center. On the left edge, as you look at the piece of equipment, as you're looking at it, there are absolutely no patterns at all. There is a flow. You can see a stream of flow. Whoops. I can get up then and start looking at it. I blew on it when I was talking. You can see a stream of flow from the circumference in toward the outer group of cells. The outer group of cells is at least half an inch from the circumference though, at that point. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay, Ron. We're copying all that. [Long pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Yeah. I think there's a general migration of - of the cells. Kind of toward the bottom of the circle, if you want to look at it that way. They seem to be stretching kind of in that direction, too.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. You're saying that's toward minus X?

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: First thing [hears Roosa].

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. They're migrating toward plus Y.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: I'll - I'll try to make all directions, with respect to - with respect to the right-side-up of the equipment, you know.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We've got you.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: And the first finger I talked about was at 12 o'clock. It has joined the edge now and almost disappeared. The second finger was - still essentially the way it was - is getting slightly closer to the edge. There's maybe - oh, less than 1/32 of an inch between the tip of the finger and the edge. And it goes out at - at 2 o'clock. Okay, from 3 o'clock on around to about 7 o'clock, the cells - it's in a shadow, and I can't see for sure if they're touching the edge or not, but it looks like they're probably essentially touching - the [garble] the edge. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: And then from 7 o'clock on around to 12 o'clock again, none of the cells are touching the edge at all. And they're - oh, an average of three-eighths of an inch from the outside circumference. [Pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We're getting all that, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: And, Ron, we'd like to verify that the fluid is up to the second baffle.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: That's verified. It's up to the second baffle.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay...

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: All I had to do was start it in one position, and as soon as I started it - started it in one position, it whipped all the way around it. From the point I started it, it went all the way around in both directions.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. That sounds beautiful. That ought to be a good data point for something.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Yeah, right.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: I think that in the low flow here, evidently things are even a little bit slower than they were in the high rate - in the high - in the high heat rate. But my little diamond now, is almost joined with the rectangle. And I think given half a chance, it's tending to go into another five-sided figure.

a17_0460256.speaker: Roosa
a17_0460256.text: Okay. We copy.

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: 17 - Just about enough time. Let's see. [Garble].

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Yes. You'd better go too. Let's see, it's 17, 18...

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: We started to move your switch without jiggling things. [Laughter.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: And we start to cool down at 18:40 on the watch.. [Long pause.]

a17_0460256.speaker: Evans
a17_0460256.text: Okay. As we're cooling down, the flow patterns tend to join together, so far. The ones on the outer periphery dissolve into straight lines. Straight lines are emanating in a radial direction from the center of the circle.

a17_0462410.speaker: Evans
a17_0462410.text: And, Houston, if you're listening; or DSE if you're listening. Had a little bit of film - oop, there's the end of film right now. May as well stop it. Hey, I went to High for a little ways. [Pause.]

a17_0462410.speaker: Roosa
a17_0462410.text: Okay, Ron. You came back in; I didn't get all of that. Understand you ran out of film. And say the other.

a17_0462410.speaker: Evans
a17_0462410.text: Well, I still had a little bit of film when the cooldown - the 2-minute cooldown period was left, so I went back to High on the Flow Pattern just to see what would happen. And it looked like they were starting out with - again larger-sized cells developing into smaller ones. And, initially, all of the cells were about a half an inch in diameter, and they were closer to the periphery of the dish than they were in the Low Flow position. [Pause.]

a17_0462410.speaker: Roosa
a17_0462410.text: Okay. We copy that, Ron. After - after you went to High - after the 19 minutes - how long was it before you started seeing a change? [Pause.]

a17_0462410.speaker: Evans
a17_0462410.text: It was within a minute there. See, it cooled down fairly rapidly at the end of the 2 minutes. All of the cells had essentially dissolved. You had some radial lines on the outer perim - The cells that were on the outer side degraded into a strictly radial lines, back to the second row of cells. The row of cells that were on the inside kind of joined together and all ended up into one or two large cells about an inch - or about three - ¾ of an inch across.

a17_0462410.speaker: Roosa
a17_0462410.text: Okay. Sounds like real good data...

a17_0462410.speaker: Evans
a17_0462410.text: I still have it in High, and the pattern that's developing is almost identical to the - what was happening in the Low, except it seems to be happening at a faster rate.

a17_0462410.speaker: Evans
a17_0462410.text: [Garble] triangle or a little diamond developed down there and then - and it disappeared. Only this time, it kind of joined with a different little cell, but it was the same cell next to it. I still have the big one. It's about an inch long, at 11 o'clock, as I had before. I still have a finger that's developing about 12 o'clock, and another one about 2 o'clock. And they seem to be migrating again toward the bottom of the dish. [Long pause.]

a17_0462410.speaker: Roosa
a17_0462410.text: Okay, Ron. It sounds like you've really wired that experiment in great shape, and all the - and everybody's real happy with the - with the data. I guess now you might as well tear it down and press ahead.

a17_0463132.speaker: Roosa
a17_0463132.text: Okay, Ron. We're back with you now, and everybody's real happy about the data and experiment. And it looks like you did a super job, and you might as well tear it down and press ahead. [Pause.]

a17_0463132.speaker: Evans
a17_0463132.text: Okay. I still got it in High, and I'm kind of sucking the fluid back down the - the intake. And as I get the fluid thinned out, low and behold there's a whole bunch of bubbles underneath there. And each bubble is a source for one of those little cells. It's the internal source. [Pause.]

a17_0463132.speaker: Roosa
a17_0463132.text: Okay, Ron. We got that. You may have made a breakthrough for science.

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: Ron, just a reminder that we're scratching that page 3-45 that - from 46 to 47 - that's scratched out. And from then on all the times, you just subtract an hour from it, if you haven't done that already.

a17_0463407.speaker: Evans
a17_0463407.text: Ah, let's see. Yeah, we've already done that, Bob. Thank you.

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: Rog. Just a reminder on that. And EECOM's over here trying to figure out if you changed the canister or not. Just a reminder on that one.

a17_0463407.speaker: Evans
a17_0463407.text: Okay. We'll get that as soon as I get this out of the way. Okay?

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: Sure. While you're back there - Panel 100 and that - you might park the optics. We see they're not in Zero. [Pause.]

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: And along that same line, Ron, we did notice several times while people were watching through the optics that they went to Zero. And it's no problem if the rates are low, but just a reminder that we don't want to bump them into the stops with any kind of a rate. [Pause.]

a17_0463407.speaker: Evans
a17_0463407.text: Yeah. I concur with that, Bob. I guess I didn't realize we were doing that.

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: We just picked up some data points down here that people - You were all looking around, I guess, and you might - it's easy to miss that Trunnion going to Zero, I guess. [Pause.]

a17_0463407.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0463407.text: I'm ready to update your weather in the Western Pacific, if you're interested.

a17_0463407.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0463407.text: Still can't quite figure out what that circulation around New Zealand means. It looks like it's merging with some more weather to the southeast. I suspect it's stormy there, but I still - It's not a terribly well-developed storm, although it seems to be broadening in its extent. Australia is completely free of any significant weather and almost completely free - free of clouds. The - There appears to be a front - although right now it does not look too intense - approaching from the southwest. And it looks like it's about 5 degrees of longitude south of the southwestern tip of Australia. [Paus

a17_0463407.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0463407.text: Roger. We see that on the prog here, Jack.

a17_0464002.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0464002.text: Jack, we've been out of comm here. We've missed any of your last report here.

a17_0464136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0464136.text: Ron, did you ever get your P23 data from today.

a17_0464136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0464136.text: Okay. Just got some updating information for you, if you want to listen to it. I don't think you need to copy it down.

a17_0464136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0464136.text: Okay, Ron, the effective horizon was 25, plus or minus 6 nautical miles, which is real fine. The substellar pointing error was 1 arc-minute, plus or minus 1 arc-minute, which is less than the 1-sigma error. The marking data was extremely consistent, and all techniques and procedures were excellent. And the horizon updates from the current onboard value of 28 - is not required, so you're extremely good P23. Outstanding.

a17_0464136.speaker: Evans
a17_0464136.text: Hey, that's good to hear. Great. Thank you.

a17_0464136.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0464136.text: And I do have one input from your other half. There's a concern that if you spill grape juice on your flight suit, it's hard to get out. So be sure - and when you're eating - drinking grape juice, you want to make sure you learn how to drink it right.

a17_0464136.speaker: Evans
a17_0464136.text: [Chuckle.] Okay. We - we'll try that, for sure.

a17_0464136.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0464136.text: 046:46:58 - This is Apollo Control at 46 hours, 46 minutes. The display which shows distance and velocity is referenced to the Moon at this time so these numbers I'm about to give you will be Moon-referenced and not Earth-referenced. Apollo 17 is 80,322 nautical miles [148,756 km] from the Moon. Velocity, 3,349 feet per second [1,021 m/s]. The crew is in a meal period at this time and we don't expect much conversation for some time. Earlier today, while the Lunar Module was being checked out and during a test of simultaneous dual communications capability from Challenger and America, a portion
