The display which shows distance and velocity is referenced to the Moon at this time so these numbers I'm about to give you will be Moon-referenced and not Earth-referenced. Apollo 17 is 80,322 nautical miles [148,756 km] from the Moon. Velocity, 3,349 feet per second [1,021 m/s]. The crew is in a meal period at this time and we don't expect much conversation for some time. Earlier today, while the Lunar Module was being checked out and during a test of simultaneous dual communications capability from Challenger and America, a portion of the conv

a17_0465040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465040.text: I need to make a correction. Roger. I need to make a correction. It looks as if that storm area that was in New Zealand yesterday has moved up across the two islands and is now sitting northwest. It's getting a little hard to identify the smaller islands in the Pacific, but - pretty sure I've got it in the right place now looking at the map. And it is northwest of New Zealand. And it looks like New Zealand's probably having reasonably good weather today, although I suspect it rained last night.

a17_0465040.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465040.text: Roger, Jack. That's interesting because on my prog it doesn't show a thing down that area. This just may not be up to date here yet.

a17_0465040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465040.text: Well, there may be nothing down there except some cloud patterns and - but that's all I can see, of course. The front that's south of Australia now - I presume front - just looking at a fairly well-developed, although narrow, cloud line, is about 5 - about 10 degrees south of Perth right now, southwest of Perth and runs on a northwest-southeast line - over to a point about 10 or 15 degrees southwest of Tasmania. And then it intersects a curved front that runs from there up to - to Tasmania, and then back around down south of New Zealand about 10 degrees.

a17_0465624.speaker: Cernan
a17_0465624.text: Say, Bob, this is Gene. I got some new sensors on. You might want to take a look at them.

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Roger. Good show, Gene. We were just wondering about that, and I'll bug the guys on my left here and make sure they're looking at them. [Pause.]

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: We're not getting any data yet, Gene.

a17_0465624.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465624.text: Bob, we're starting to get [garble] from just off Luzon on the northeast trend [garble] seen so far of a shadow line of fairly thick high clouds overlying some thick lower clouds behind the front.

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Roger. You might have - be of interest onboard there, the FIDOs... [Long pause.]

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Jack, we've been having comm dropouts here on this Omni as you swing around on us.

a17_0465624.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465624.text: Okay. What - where did I leave you, Bob?

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Well, I'm not sure because we picked up a number of different bits, and then we dropped it all.

a17_0465624.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465624.text: Did you get the overcast over Korea and Manchuria bit?

a17_0465624.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465624.text: Okay. That generally - South China looks clear. I haven't had a real good look at it yet, it's out on the limb. It's clearly, however, overcast over Korea and Manchuria. It does not appear to be frontal weather there, though. The dominant front in the northwestern Pacific stretches on a northwest line from just off Luzon on up as far as I could see to the terminator. And it seems to be an extremely strong front with what I would guess is heavy air-mass weather all along it. And up to the east-northeast of Japan, there's an excellent example of a shadow line from some fairly thick high clouds o

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Roger, Jack. We've got it on our prog here. We don't show the one on the northeast part of Japan, but we do show a front prog for tomorrow morning going off of Taiwan and - right from Taiwan eastward - past the Ryukyu islands and just on into the northern Pacific there. Looks like pretty heavy cloud mass over there.

a17_0465624.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0465624.text: Roger. That's the one I'm - Roger. That's the one I'm looking at. Extremely heavy. And right now it - in fact starts about at Luzon. It looks like Taiwan is almost on the back side of it.

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: Yeah. That's what our prog - it shows it right on Luzon and then Taiwan's clear.

a17_0465624.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0465624.text: We'll keep up with you yet there, Jack. Say, you may be interested. We've got 9 hours of good tracking on the - after the midcourse - and we show a perilune of about 52 [nautical] miles [96 km] which confirms a good midcourse.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Apollo 17, Houston.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: Go ahead, T.P.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Yeah. I was going to say, is that talkative commander onboard?

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: How are you doing down there?

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Well, I feel lots better. Like I told you Geno, I think that you were the jinx on Gemini 9 for all the delays. Over.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: No way; you got a longer history than I do.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Everything's looking great.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: Yeah, it's looking good onboard. We're - I think we're pretty well squared away. We've got our stowage in shape, and we're in the house-cleaning routine. And that's about 50 percent of the battle.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Right.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: The weather down there didn't look too good today. How's it been?

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Well, as it started out, it was below minimums this morning and finally, this afternoon, it cleared up. But it was strictly zilch this morning and starting last night. There's another front due in here later tonight.

a17_0471219.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471219.text: Yeah, we've been watching that one.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Well, Jack, you're turning into a very trained weather observer besides being a geologist.

a17_0471219.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471219.text: Oh, I'm enjoying it immensely, Tom, as you may have gathered.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Right.

a17_0471219.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471219.text: Very interesting place to watch; I'll tell you.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Absolutely superb.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: How are things on the home front, T.P.?

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Geno, things couldn't be better.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: Well, you might sound all the good words from us.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: Oh, will do. I plan to drop by and burn a cup of coffee tomorrow.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: I'd love to invite you up here for supper.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: And I wish I could join you. I could make another couple of remarks, but they'd be X-rated; so I shouldn't.

a17_0471219.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471219.text: Okay. I'll accept that.

a17_0471219.speaker: Cernan
a17_0471219.text: You notice I haven't yet.

a17_0471219.speaker: Stafford
a17_0471219.text: [Chuckle] I'm very well pleased, Geno. Your - your language is superb.

a17_0471738.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0471738.text: 17, Houston, just a couple of words. We'd like you to know we're real satisfied with all the LM data that we saw during the LM activation work today, and, looking at it, the data looked real good.

a17_0471738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471738.text: Great, Bob. I was - you had me worried there for a while with that comm. Do you have a good idea what caused that?

a17_0471738.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0471738.text: Yes, we're sure about 99.9 percent of it was just ground linkup.

a17_0471738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0471738.text: Yeah, that's certainly the way it acted onboard.

a17_0471738.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0471738.text: I guess there won't be any need to go back and change the checklist on that, but there's a lot to be said for maybe going to a real good stable condition and then getting a good firm checkout before you go into that downvoice backup mode and things like that. And I think that's what we'll do in the future.

a17_0471833.text: This is Apollo Control at 47 hours, 18 minutes. That completes the tape from this afternoon. At this time, Apollo 17 is 79,293 nautical miles [146,851 km] from the Moon with the lunar referenced velocity of 3,343 feet per second [1,019 m/s]. The Flight Director has just gotten another update on the S-IVB impact prediction, based on tracking to date. The newest prediction is that the impact will occur at an elapsed time of 86 hours, 59 minutes, 55 seconds; at 3 degrees, 58 minutes south latitude; 12 degrees, 35 minutes west longitude. While that tape was playing, there were several conversation

a17_0473107.text: This is Apollo Control. We're back live now with air/ground.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Houston; 7 - 17

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Go ahead, Jack.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Yeah, I'm just a little curious about the difficulty on holding the Omnis. Is that about the same as past missions, or are we losing a little bit more than usual? [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: We're going to have Ed here give us a description for a minute, so let me stand by. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Jack, according to that - to our stalwart INCO over there, due to this new 210 (-foot antenna) down at Tidbinbilla, we're holding actually longer than in the past history.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Okay. I just guess I've never been on this end before.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. Do you - do you hear it onboard when we break lock there? [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, with the Squelch Enabled, we lose all the background noise. And we know when we're picking you up because we start to get background noise again.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. In other words, you - you are able to stop talking or something when you - when you know we're breaking lock then.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Well, if we happen to be talking when you break lock - no, unless we're watching the meter, we won't. We lose you when you get about 55 - say 60 percent signal strength. And apparently we're not talking to you when we have less than that.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. Yeah, INCO gave me a briefing tonight and showed me what chart to watch so I can look at numbers when to talk. I've been talking to myself too much, lately. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Yeah, they have a beautiful chart there for that purpose.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: I never really wanted to be an INCO, but I guess I was forced to tonight. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: There are lots of comments for that one, Bob; but I'd better not say anything.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Ed would never speak to me again.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Well, that's right. We can't X-rate the transcripts, so we'll just have to take - take it easy. [Long pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Say, Bob, I've got another question about the Challenger.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Go ahead, sir.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: [Music] Yes, sir. The battery voltage on low taps, strangely enough, was just like the simulator; but I had expected that the simulator might have been wrong - that we would have seen higher voltage there. Is that - is that about what you guys expected? [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. They said they expected that because the extra time on the pad that they're running. That 2-hour-and-40-minute delay is coming into play again.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Oh, yes, yes. That's right. Good. I forgot all about that. Something made that slip my mind.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Well, things have been going so well that I can't blame you forgetting that. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: [Garble] Stanley Holloway's crazy Flight Plan updates that we've just forgotten that we were ever late.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. Say, by the way, we like the music in the background. Sounds pretty good. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Yeah, we sort of - didn't - we didn't get it out at all until today. [Music: Whipped Cream by Al Hirt] I don't know whether we forgot about it or too many other learning things going on. It's - it's quite pleasant.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Rog. I don't think you forgot about it. I think you were just glued to those windows.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Well, I still am, as a matter of fact. The old Earth's coming by. And, say, I mentioned a couple of fronts that joined together about 20 degrees south of - of - the south coast of Australia. And it looks like that's a fairly healthy storm center developing down in there - conceivably may migrate up across Tasmania and maybe up - up the Sydney-Brisbane coastal area in the next few days.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. Where's the exact center of that, Jack? it took me a second to get my prog out here.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Well, just a second. Let me give you better from the map.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: While you're looking at your map, I just might mention to Gene, I just talked to your - your better half over there, and everybody's fine and happy. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0474549.text: Great. Always like to hear news like that, Bob.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: Bob, did you get that - 15 to 20 degrees south southwest of Adelaide?

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: 17, Houston. Are you into your pre... [No answer.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: 17, Houston. Are you into your presleep checklist yet? [No answer.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: 17, Houston. Are you into your presleep checklist now?

a17_0474549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0474549.text: We're just about ready to get started, Bob. We're running a little bit behind, but - we'll catch up here.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Okay. No sweat.

a17_0474549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0474549.text: [Music] Trying to get some more of this good food down.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger. Keep saying those words. The people on my left appreciate that. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0474549.text: Yes, but it does take a while.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: I'm sure of that. [Pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Evans
a17_0474549.text: You know what we really need is Rita to fix it for us.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: That's affirm. I'll go along on that. [Long pause.]

a17_0474549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0474549.text: Okay, Bob, I'm going to cycle H 2 Fans 1 and 2.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Okay, we're watching.

a17_0474549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0474549.text: Fans are Off.

a17_0474549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0474549.text: Roger.

a17_0475915.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0475915.text: Roger, Jack. We copy that. November November frame 140. And you ought to be on 142 when you go to sleep, I guess, huh?

a17_0475915.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0475915.text: 048:09:36 - This is Apollo Control at 48 hours, 9 minutes. Apollo 17 now 77,623 nautical miles [143,758 km] away from the Moon and the lunar-referenced velocity, 3,333 feet per second [1,016 m/s]. Major activities during this shift have been the heat flow and convection demonstration which has been performed twice during this shift. a17_0481446.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0481446.text: Roger. One final word. I got those pictures; and, I tell you, that typhoon off - north of Borneo - looks like it's right off the coast of - the east coast of Vietnam now, and it's about as tightly organized and solid as anything I can remember seeing in photographs. It looks as if, from yesterday, it's moved quite a bit to the west.

a17_0481446.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481446.text: Roger. We concur. The prog for 12:00 - Let's see, that's about 6 hours from now - shows it to be right over the Vietnam area, the Viet - Vietnam peninsula there. So it looks like it's moving the way they're progging it, huh?

a17_0481446.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0481446.text: Yeah; well, it's right there. Yeah, it certainly is. It's - it's moved from just a little bit west of Luzon over to the coast there. So it's a pretty healthy storm.

a17_0481446.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481446.text: Roger. It looks - on the prog chart here - it looks real tight. It's a very - very centralized thing and real tight circular.

a17_0481446.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0481446.text: Oh, yeah, you better believe it. It is really - it is tight. It - it's really - really no bigger than the - in terms of cloud pattern - no bigger than the - say, South Vietnam itself.

a17_0481446.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481446.text: Roger. How're you getting that, Jack? Are you looking with the monocular now?

a17_0481446.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0481446.text: That's affirm. [Pause.] Monocular still gives real good resolution on the cloud patterns. [Music] Naked eye, you just see the masses; but with the 10-power monocular, it's perfectly adequate for seeing the kind of patterns we're talking about.

a17_0481959.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481959.text: Well, guys, I guess I won't get the chance to say goodnight to you because Parker's going to come in to put you to bed.

a17_0481959.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481959.text: And we'd - we'd like you to clear...

a17_0481959.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0481959.text: You can still say goodnight, Bob.

a17_0481959.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481959.text: Say goodnight, Dick, huh? One last word. You know, we're always hounding you guys - really don't mean to - but we - we'd like to see a clear DSKY so something doesn't burn out. Don't know the exact words on that, but...

a17_0481959.speaker: Cernan
a17_0481959.text: Okay, we - we'll give you a clear DSKY.

a17_0481959.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0481959.text: We'll see you tomorrow, troops. And we had a good show today, and we'll have more tomorrow. [Long pause.]

a17_0482825.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0482825.text: Well, you're just in time to put us to sleep. And I'll give you one last little old observation here. Extremely bright zero phase point right off the northwestern corner of Australia right at Carnarvon, it's as bright as I've seen. They must have a pretty good surf or something going in there.

a17_0482825.speaker: Parker
a17_0482825.text: Okay, 17, we copy all that; and I gather you're going to sleep at this point.

a17_0482825.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0482825.text: Well, we're going to try, Bob. I don't think any of us are real sleepy right now, but we're going to give her the old space try, here; and I'm sure we'll be asleep before long. Ron is on watch; and, if you don't wake him up with your voice, give him a crew alert. He says he'll wake up with a Master Alarm.

a17_0482825.speaker: Parker
a17_0482825.text: That's a healthy sign. All right, guys; if I stick around long enough in the morning, I'll wake you up.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Okay, Robert, are you happy with your high - antenna configuration?

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: That's affirm. INCO is happy.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Okay, you have anything else for us? I'll take care of our sleep configuration if you don't.

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Okay, stand by. I'll go around the MOCR here with white.

a17_0483325.speaker: SC
a17_0483325.text: [Laughter.] [Pause.]

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Okay. A lot of happy people down here with nothing to ask you.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Okay. Nice to have everybody happy. And you - that includes the - the biomed on the commander, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Okay, I guess they're happy. [Long pause.]

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Okay, are you going to sing to Ron in the morning to wake us up?

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Depends on how soon you guys decide to wake up in the morning. I'll be around for 8 hours anyway.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: What's your expected GET of awake?

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Stand by. [Long pause.] Okay, 17, it should say 56...

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: [Garble] 56.

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Go ahead.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Yeah, we're just going to say the same thing.

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Okay. Should show 56 on your clock. [Long pause.]

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: In fact, Dr. Kranz, here, just decided that you guys get another half hour in the morning if you wanted it. [Pause.] But you better tell us now because we'll wake you up at 56 and ask you if you want the other half hour then, unless you tell us.

a17_0483325.speaker: Cernan
a17_0483325.text: Yeah, why don't you give us another half hour; and if we happen to wake up and want to move around, well, we'll do it.

a17_0483325.speaker: Parker
a17_0483325.text: Okay; We'll wake you up at 56:30.

The Flight Plan calls for the sleep period to end at 56 hours Ground Elapsed Time, however, we don't plan to give them a call until 56:30, giving them the option to sleep for an additional 30 minutes. a17_0572223.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0572223.text: Apollo 17; oh, Apollo 17; it's morning. Time to get up. Over. [No answer.]

a17_0572223.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0572223.text: Hello, Apollo 17; do you read? Over. [No answer.]

a17_0573914.text: Here goes the tone up on the air/ground circuit from network.

a17_0573914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0573914.text: Hello, 17. Hello, 17. How do you read us this morning? [Pause.]

a17_0573914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0573914.text: That's the understatement of the year. [Pause.]

a17_0573914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0573914.text: Never let Evans be on watch. [Pause.]

a17_0573914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0573914.text: I think we'll go along with that from here on.

a17_0573914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0573914.text: [Laughter.] That was some party last night, Gordy. Man, that was a humdinger.

a17_0574507.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0574507.text: Okay, we're starting out late, as you know; but there's nothing ahead that we can see that's time-critical. So you might try to hurry a little, but don't - don't go to any great lengths to try to catch up with the Flight Plan. We can slip the LM telemetry activation without any problem. Over.

a17_0574507.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0574507.text: Okay, we got you. Our biggest problem this morning is keeping Ron from going back to sleep.

a17_0574507.speaker: Evans
a17_0574507.text: By the way, my sleep report is [garble] looks like I had about 7½ hours of pretty good sleep.

a17_0574507.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0574507.text: And if you believe that, you're really a [garble].

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Okay, Houston; 17. I don't know if you're ready for this or not, but we have a few reports for you.

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Okay. On your CDR: PRD, 17028; he claims 7½ hours of good sleep. He had a Seconal before going to bed, and since the last reporting, has had four containers of water. [Pause.]

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Okay, with respect to food - let's see, we gave you a intermediate report yesterday. Do you want that repeated?

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Well, I'm not sure I can differentiate what I said yesterday, so I'd just better give it all to you. This is yesterday's complete report.

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: CDR was scrambled eggs, three bacon squares, peaches, pineapple-grapefruit drink, peanut butter, jelly, bread, chocolate bar, orange drink, apricot - that's dried apricot - one frankfurter, a third of a fruitcake, half a beefsteak, butterscotch pudding, orange drink, and tea. [Pause.]

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Let me know if I'm too fast for you.

a17_0575220.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575220.text: No, we've got it all on tape. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a17_0575220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575220.text: Okay, with respect to food yesterday - LMP: scrambled eggs, four bacon squares, orange-pineapple drink, cocoa, potato soup, two peanut butter, two jelly, two bread, cherry bar, orange-grapefruit drink, beefsteak, orange drink, and tea.

a17_0575220.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575220.text: Jack, we're just about to switch antennas now. Why don't you wait until we get through it before continuing.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay, Jack. I think we're back with you again.

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: Okay; got you. LMP: PRD, 24064; 7½ hours very good sleep, 1 hour intermittent. Had a Seconal. I took two aspirins yesterday. And since the last reporting, I've had four containers of water. [Pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: Okay. Old CMP - the man of the hour, one might say. Scrambled eggs, bacon squares, peaches, cinnamon toast bread, orange juice, cocoa, peanut butter, jelly, bread, cherry bar, citrus beverage, fruitcake, butterscotch pudding, orange drink, turkey and gravy, two frankfurters, and tea. You might say he was a little logey. [Long pause.] Okay. CMP: PRD, 15027; 7 and a - let's [pause] make that 8 hours of very good sleep. He claims he didn't get to sleep for a while. Seconal, and he's had five containers of water since the last reporting.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Jack, if - future reports if it's any easier, we can go to negative reporting. If you're fairly close to the menus, just tell us the differences. Whatever is easiest for you is fine with us. [Pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: Okay. Well, now that we're eating well, that may be the best way to do it.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay. I have the - your consumables status, if everybody that's interested is listening.

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: Go ahead, Gordon.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay. Your RCS is running right along at 1.3 percent above the Flight Plan line. On your cryos, the O 2 tanks 2 and 3 are right on the lines. Tank 1 is still, as before, about 4 percent below - below the line but looking real good. On hydrogen, you're a little above on one tank - on tank 2 - a little bit below on tank 3, but the average is right with the Flight Plan lines. So consumables look good. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: Okay. That's good to hear. And, I see that our old SPS oxidizer pressure has dropped some more. I guess the old - the helium is working it's way in there - or out of there.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay. That's the way it looks to us. One final thing. Management has informed me that since you've been so late getting to work this morning, we are going to have to dock you all a day's annual leave.

a17_0575746.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0575746.text: All of us! [Pause.] I can un - I can understand that for the commander, since he's always the commander, but I do not understand why the LMP loses a day - an hour. [Pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Cernan
a17_0575746.text: Hello, Houston. This is America.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Hello, Geno. Good morning.

a17_0575746.speaker: Cernan
a17_0575746.text: Hello, Gordo. Request is that I handle the disciplinary problems up here; how's that?

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Geno, we'll have FAO work on a good time in the Flight Plan later here to work in a captain's mast.

a17_0575746.speaker: Cernan
a17_0575746.text: Okay; [chuckle] that'll be great. Hey, Gordy, for the record; I swallowed three of those - those gas pills yesterday.

a17_0575746.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0575746.text: Okay.

a17_0581830.text: And, Houston, I've started the dumping.

a17_0581830.text: And, Houston, we're going to dump A on the water dump - Waste Water Dump.

a17_0582833.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0582833.text: Houston, we're starting a - O 2 purge.

a17_0582833.speaker: Cernan
a17_0582833.text: Hey, Gordo, we'll get everything cleaned up in the Flight Plan, including eating, up to 59 hours where we start checking the Delta-P and pressurizing the CSM for LM entry.

a17_0582833.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0582833.text: Okay. We see you doing all that now, and we're just checking things off as you call them. Sounds good.

a17_0582833.speaker: Cernan
a17_0582833.text: Okay. And then when we'll clean all that up - regards to what the time will be, we'll pick up the 59-hour mark then.

a17_0583527.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0583527.text: Roger on the fuel cell purge.

a17_0583927.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0583927.text: Roger. While we're getting organized to eat a little bit here, I'll give you your morning weather report, if you want it.

a17_0583927.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0583927.text: Okay, Gordy. That little storm - fairly big storm - that was off the coast of northwest Africa yesterday, has moved inland and presumably is giving those people up there some weather. Might even be getting some snow up in the Atlas Mountains. It's still fairly well organized and inland a few hundred miles - or the edge of it is inland a few hundred miles. The people at the Cape of Good Hope ought to be seeing some clouds that are forerunners of a large circulation system that's south-southwest of them - that, although large, seems to have most of its heavy clouds to the southeast of the center

a17_0583927.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0583927.text: Jack, take a breather there. We got an antenna switch coming.

a17_0584510.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0584510.text: Okay Jack, we're back with you and listening. [Pause.]

a17_0584510.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0584510.text: Okay, Gordy, I can't see you right now. I think that was about the extent of it. We'll get some food and, while I'm eating, I'll look at it and see if there are any more details.

a17_0585144.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585144.text: 17, Houston. I have the morning news here, whenever you'd like to hear it - if you would.

a17_0585144.speaker: Cernan
a17_0585144.text: Go ahead, Gordo. We'd like to hear it now.

a17_0585144.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585144.text: Okay. First, a look at the weather in the local area. It's going to be mostly cloudy through Sunday, with a chance of showers here today - but much warmer. I'll have to wait until we get through the Omni switch here, and then I'll be back with you.

a17_0585503.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585503.text: Okay, 17, continuing on with the weather. It should be - get up to the upper 60s [F, approx 18 - 21°C] here in Houston today. It was foggy when I came to work, but understand the Sun is out now and the fog is burned off. On the international/national scene: There's another reported snag in the negotiations between Dr. Henry Kissinger and North Vietnam's Le Duc Tho. The two have discussed the peace terms since Monday; but, so far, little news concerning the talks has been released by either side. They meet again today. A judge in the Pentagon Papers trial of Daniel Ellsburg has declared a mistr

a17_0585503.speaker: Cernan
a17_0585503.text: Yeah. That crash in Chicago, can you tell me a little bit more about it?

a17_0585503.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585503.text: I read real briefly in the paper, just before I came in, that it did crash in a populated area. It was a very brief report. I don't think the final details have been published yet. I'll check to see if we've got anymore in. [Pause.]

a17_0585503.speaker: Cernan
a17_0585503.text: Okay. And I guess you know where - at least my wishes go for that Cowboy game, don't you? [Pause.]

a17_0585503.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585503.text: I'm not sure that I do. [Pause.]

a17_0585503.speaker: Cernan
a17_0585503.text: I'll just let you make an assumption.

a17_0585503.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0585503.text: Okay. We've got an antenna switch coming here.

a17_0590421.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0590421.text: 17, Houston. I have a little more on the plane crash, if you'd like to hear it. [Pause.]

a17_0590421.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0590421.text: Okay. It was a United Airlines jet, 61 people aboard. And it crashed into a south-side Chicago neighborhood while trying to land at Midway. Most of the 55 passengers - There were - well, I'm not sure I'm getting all the numbers right here. But it said here that most of the 55 passengers were found dead in the debris of a - and it was a Boeing 737 about a half a mile away from the airport. One of the victims was representative George Collins, a Democrat from Illinois - who was returning from Washington to organize a children's Christmas party. The weather, at the time, was a 500-foot ceiling an

a17_0590421.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0590421.text: And a little news about - about your trajectory. Since the midcourse 2, you've been looking real good. You've - you're homing in on 53½-mile perilune. We're discussing midcourse 4, which - if we do it all - is going to be very small. It's looking like about a foot and a half per second right now. And I guess if we do it, it'll only be because it will save us Delta-V at LOI. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0590421.speaker: Cernan
a17_0590421.text: Okay, I was just looking. Those dumps really knocked us for a loop, didn't they?

a17_0590421.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0590421.text: Yes, it - it's driving your PTC out.

a17_0590421.speaker: Cernan
a17_0590421.text: Yeah, we're at almost 40 degrees now.

a17_0591050.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0591050.text: Gordy, has the temperature been pretty cold down there?

a17_0591050.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0591050.text: Here, in Houston, it warmed up considerably last night - yesterday afternoon and last night. And this morning, it's probably in the 60s [F, 16-21°C] somewhere.

a17_0591832.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0591832.text: 17, Houston. I have some words about the troubles we had during the LM comm checks yesterday, if you have a free moment to listen. [Pause.]

a17_0591832.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0591832.text: Okay. We think we've got a pretty good handle on what the problem was - and that was, that the - the LM communications gear, we think, was jumping on the voice subcarrier, rather than the main carrier. And the symptoms we had point to that. What would happen is, when I would try to transmit, then it - it would lose lock as soon as I put modulation on the voice subcarrier. During the checks today, we're going to try to verify that the system is indeed working okay. And we can do it without any changes in the onboard procedures by - purely by procedures that will be handled at the ground site an

a17_0591832.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0591832.text: Sounds good, Gordy. We'll just take her slow and easy when I get over there today and make sure we understand it.

a17_0591832.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0591832.text: Okay, Jack. And there's no - there's real no voice check scheduled, and we don't think any are required. We can tell what we need to do without any voice checks from here.

a17_0591832.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0591832.text: Gordy, you're breaking up. Talk to you as soon as we get another Omni.

a17_0591832.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0591832.text: While I got you, I took three pictures of the Earth I thought I might have moved one of them. And we're on frame 145. [Long pause.]

a17_0591832.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0591832.text: That's affirmative, Jack. I copy. You may not be reading me through the Omni switch.

a17_0591832.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0591832.text: Okay, that was mag November November.

a17_0592349.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0592349.text: Houston, 17. Do you want us to go into a battery B charge?

a17_0592349.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0592349.text: Let me check, Jack. That's affirmative. Go ahead

a17_0592349.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0592349.text: Battery B is being Charged. And, Gordy, different than the last time - the charger amps is moving up very slowly. Started out at about 0.2 and now is 1 amp - little more - it's still going up. Before, it jumped right up to about 2 amps. is that expected?

a17_0592349.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0592349.text: Oh [garble] we'll check on that. Stand by. [Pause.]

a17_0592349.speaker: Cernan
a17_0592349.text: Gordy, the LM/CM Delta-P is 0.6. You still want to take the Command Module up? [Long pause.]

a17_0592349.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0592349.text: Geno, that'll be fine. You will not have to jack up the Command Module pressure.

a17_0592349.speaker: Cernan
a17_0592349.text: Okay, I think I'll maneuver to attitude then. [Pause.]

a17_0592806.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0592806.text: Jack, the way the amps are going to look when you put the charger on is a function of the state of the charge of the battery. And what you described is about what we'd expect, considering where the battery should be. [Pause.]

a17_0592806.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0592806.text: Okay; that's what I figured. It's up about one and three-quarter amps now.

a17_0592806.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0592806.text: And it appears to be stable.

a17_0592806.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0592806.text: Gordy, I'm in the process of - I'm in the process of putting biomed sensors on.

a17_0593044.speaker: Evans
a17_0593044.text: Hey, Houston; 17. Thanks to a little South Carolina boy we had up here last time, we've got some grits up here. And they're really not too bad. A little butter on them and - A little bit dry. Of course, you could add a little more water to them and they'd be a little better, but not bad at all.

a17_0593044.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0593044.text: I can't believe I'm hearing that from a real Yankee [Pause.]

a17_0593044.speaker: Evans
a17_0593044.text: Of course, Kansas is not exactly Yankee.

a17_0593044.speaker: Cernan
a17_0593044.text: Let me tell you, that does not apply to the little old farm boy from Chicago.

a17_0593044.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0593044.text: As you students of American history may recall, Kansas caused a lot of the problem we had with those two people.

a17_0593044.speaker: Cernan
a17_0593044.text: And grits is causing the rest of it. [Long pause.]

a17_0593044.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0593044.text: 17, Houston. We see that you're making a maneuver uncoupled in pitch, and we'd rather you make it coupled to keep FDO happy. Over.

a17_0593044.speaker: Cernan
a17_0593044.text: Yeah, that was my fault, Gordo. I screwed up here.

a17_0594250.speaker: Evans
a17_0594250.text: Houston, Emergency Cab Repress is Off.

a17_0594250.speaker: Cernan
a17_0594250.text: We're reading you loud and clear. The Emergency Cabin Pressure Select is Off. And we're about ready to open the Equalisation valve.

a17_0594250.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0594250.text: Okay. And we're ready for the High Gain.

a17_0594250.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0594250.text: 059:44:30 - This is Apollo Control; 59 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time into the mission of Apollo 17. The crew, at this time, making preparations for entry into the Lunar Module.
This is Apollo Control; 59 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time into the mission of Apollo 17. The crew, at this time, making preparations for entry into the Lunar Module.

a17_0594250.speaker: Cernan
a17_0594250.text: Gordy, that's the High Gain. How do you like it?

a17_0594250.speaker: Cernan
a17_0594250.text: Okay, Gordy. I was reading 0.2 on the Delta-P and the hatch is cracked.

a17_0594840.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0594840.text: Hey, Houston; 17. How do you read the LMP's biomed?

a17_0594840.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0594840.text: Jack, the EKG looks great. Your ZPN looks like a sensor may be loose. [Long pause.]

a17_0594840.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0594840.text: And we'll be handing over here in...

a17_0594840.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0594840.text: Okay. We're in the process of getting the probe and drogue out. I pushed on the sensors real hard again, and see if that helps it.

a17_0594840.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0594840.text: Okay. We'll take a look. [Long pause.]

a17_0594840.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0594840.text: That helped it. Don't worry about it, until we call you again.

a17_0594840.speaker: Cernan
a17_0594840.text: [Garble] on that one, Gordy. [Pause.] You've always been one of those smooth talkers.

a17_0595450.speaker: Evans
a17_0595450.text: There's all - yeah - they're down there somewhere.

a17_0595450.speaker: Evans
a17_0595450.text: Okay. The probe is out. And we'll try the drogue now.

a17_0595753.speaker: Cernan
a17_0595753.text: Okay, the - the drogue is out, and we're going up to take another look at Challenger.

a17_0595931.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0595931.text: Somebody left their lights on in here.

a17_0600318.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600318.text: Okay, Ron. When you get a - a moment, when it's convenient, we'd like you to go up to the latch number 4 there, the one that's been giving us trouble, and we'd like you - well, we think it's just half cocked and we'd like you to stroke it. We think it will probably cock on one - with one more stroke. We'd like you to stroke it at least twice more to verify that it is fully cocked. And as you do stroke the handle, we'd like you to notice approximately what point in the - in the throw that the resistance increases. I think that summarizes what we want you to do, if you keep us advised as you go

a17_0600318.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600318.text: We - we're going to leave it cocked then from here on until redocking after rendezvous. Well - we don't want to - we don't want you to fire it.

a17_0600318.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600318.text: Houston, we're transferring to LM Power.

a17_0600318.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600318.text: Okay, Houston. I'm going to give them LM Power. I'm going to go Reset and Off.

a17_0600318.speaker: Cernan
a17_0600318.text: Okay. While my compatriots are carrying out their respective tasks, I'm going to go off the air here for a - a few short minutes. And give you a call when I get back.

a17_0600318.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600318.text: And I'm in step 3, Gordy, on 2-2.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Houston. America here. I'm up by docking latch number 4 now.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: Okay, the handle itself is free swinging at - to a point about 1 inch beyond the backside of the J-hook.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Roger.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: And, I'll go ahead and try to cock it now. [Pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600725.text: Gordy, ED Bats are 37.2 and 37.2, and the Bus Voltages are 26.2 and I'll bring on the high taps.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Jack. Sounds good. [Pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: And, Houston, as we all suspected, it has one cock on it, or it had one cock. Now it's fully cocked. And the handle itself is free swinging. The plunger has depressed, oh, almost three-quarters of an inch from the top. And it is no longer parallel with the surface.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Roger, Ron.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: Okay. When you look back in the side of it there, that little J-hook with the snowman in it, the snowman's head points - as you look directly at the side of it, it points - the snowman's head is at 8 o'clock and the connecting link from the one that connects to the one that goes into the plunger to - to the little fat J-bar there, is parallel with that slot, so that the point of the J sticks out. So it is, indeed, fully cocked.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Ron. Sounds good and that's where we'd like to leave it.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: Okay. Will do. [Long pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600725.text: Okay. Step 5, 2-3.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Houston. Step 5 complete. Glycol pressure is 21. It's down about a psi from yesterday.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Jack. Copy.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: And, Houston, is magazine II a good one to use for a - some opportunity interior photos?

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Let me check, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: That's affirm; II sounds good. [Pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: Hope so. Looks like that's the only one I have. [Pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Do you - do you recall when you did the heat flow on HH, if you used all of HH up on that experiment?

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Don't get it out to look, but I just wondered if you remembered.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: That's affirm. It - No, it ran out. It didn't - I got the complete cooldown part of the ex - of the experiment on HH and then switched to High. And I got about 2 minutes of High before the film ran out again. High power on the - on the...

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Ron. Thank you.

a17_0600725.speaker: Evans
a17_0600725.text: After the main part of the experiment was complete.

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0600725.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0600725.text: And, Jack, we're copying LM data now.

a17_0600725.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0600725.text: Okay, Gordy. Beautiful. I was just going to say step 6 is complete.

a17_0601646.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0601646.text: Roger. I just was thinking while I was waiting here that the cleanliness of these two spacecraft is certainly a tribute to the - all the people at Grumman and Downey and at the Cape, who worked so hard to put them that way.

a17_0601646.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0601646.text: Okay. We'll make sure they hear about it.

a17_0601932.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0601932.text: Challenger, Houston. We're - we've looked at the LM data and it looks perfect, no problems at all. What we're doing right now, though, is - is - the checkout on the carrier and subcarrier lockups on the LM comm. So far, we've had no trouble with it, but we haven't quite completed the routine we wanted to try. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0601932.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0601932.text: Okay. I understand, Gordy. No - no hurry here.

a17_0602534.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0602534.text: Okay, Jack. We've completed our investigation of the comm, there. It all looked good. You can press on page 2-4. [Pause.]

a17_0602714.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0602714.text: Say, Gordy, I see I neglected to pull the Bal Load circuit breaker when I went to - after going to high taps. You want me to go back and show you that again?

a17_0602714.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0602714.text: That's the Bal Loads breaker on 16, so the buses were tied together.

a17_0602714.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0602714.text: Jack, there's no need to go back. Just keep on going.

a17_0603140.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0603140.text: America, Houston. We're all ready for the E-MOD dump, if it's convenient to you. [Long pause.]

a17_0603140.speaker: Evans
a17_0603140.text: Houston, this is America. I guess that's for me, isn't it?

a17_0603140.speaker: Evans
a17_0603140.text: And, Houston, we have 50 percent remaining on magazine India India.

a17_0603140.speaker: Evans
a17_0603140.text: And they're all taken at 6 frames a second.

a17_0603140.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0603140.text: Okay, America, we've got the dump. [Pause.]

a17_0603140.speaker: Evans
a17_0603140.text: Okay. Understand; you have the dump.

a17_0603140.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0603140.text: 060:35:45 - This is Apollo Control; 60 hours, 35 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. LM checkout apparently going along quite well at this time. The balky docking latch has been recocked and will be left in that position until redocking after Lunar Orbit Insertion - after the landing. Apollo 17 is now 53,438 nautical miles [98,967 km] out from the Moon. Velocity now 3,286 feet per second [1,002 m/s]. Meanwhile, back at the Earth, spacecraft is now 177,980 nautical miles [329,619 km] from the Earth. At 60:36, standing by; this is Apollo Control.

a17_0603545.text: This is Apollo Control; 60 hours, 35 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. LM checkout apparently going along quite well at this time. The balky docking latch has been recocked and will be left in that position until redocking after Lunar Orbit Insertion - after the landing. Apollo 17 is now 53,438 nautical miles [98,967 km] out from the Moon. Velocity now 3,286 feet per second [1,002 m/s]. Meanwhile, back at the Earth, spacecraft is now 177,980 nautical miles [329,619 km] from the Earth. At 60:36, standing by; this is Apollo Control.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: Hello, Gordo. This is Geno. I'm - back on the line.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: Yeah, I was just testing out survival techniques in space.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: And we've got the LM back on CSM power.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: Gordo, it's called education of necessity.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: Okay. I guess the LM looked pretty good to you, huh?

a17_0603545.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0603545.text: Yes, sir. It looked perfect. And we also went through the little communications main carrier, subcarrier lockup check, and the - and the comm system worked perfectly, so there's no problems at all to report.

a17_0603545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0603545.text: Okay, fine. We'll start in - with the - Jack donning the PGA, and then I'll follow him.

a17_0604038.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0604038.text: Gordy, how'd that ZPN turn out?

a17_0604038.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0604038.text: Let me get another check, here. [Long pause.]

a17_0604038.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0604038.text: Okay, Jack. It looks fairly good right now. Don't bother changing anything.

a17_0604038.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0604038.text: Well, I'm just going to be in a position to work on it in a little while and if the occasion arises, I could.

a17_0604038.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0604038.text: Okay, we'll keep that in mind, although it looks reasonable at the moment. It has shown some - at some times, it's gone to - from edge to edge on their scale but it's come back in right now. I'll find out later if they want to do anything.

a17_0604038.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0604038.text: Okay, the - the electrolyte pads may be still expanding a little bit so I'm going off the air briefly to start getting into the suit. And I'll talk to you in a little while.

a17_0605348.speaker: Cernan
a17_0605348.text: Okay. We're up to frame count 151 on magazine November November. They've been pictures of the - primarily of the CSM out the LM windows by the CMP.

a17_0605348.speaker: Cernan
a17_0605348.text: He's been up there fooling around for a while. We may have to check it out and see what he did.

a17_0605742.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0605742.text: All that dropout there was because Ascension had a problem. We're now over on Madrid, and you're sounding good.

a17_0610114.speaker: Cernan
a17_0610114.text: Okay, Gordo. Jack is in his suit, unzipped at this time. I'm going off the air, and Ron'll come on and keep you informed as to how we're going.

a17_0610307.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0610307.text: Houston. How do you read the LMP?

a17_0610307.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0610307.text: Okay. I'm in my suit, presently unzipped. Didn't seem to be any problem at all.

a17_0610307.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0610307.text: And, Gordy, I think I found a problem with the biomed sensors. And when I come out of the suit, I can fix it. I put a little of that bacterial cream on the sensor places last night as a preventive mechanism, and I think it's just a little greasy to hold the sensor.

a17_0610908.speaker: Evans
a17_0610908.text: Okay. Gene's got his suit on and he's going across to the LM now.

a17_0611526.speaker: Evans
a17_0611526.text: Okay. This is CMP. I'll go off the line here, for a little bit, until I get my suit on again.

a17_0611526.speaker: Evans
a17_0611526.text: And Jack's still on the line up there at the LM now.

a17_0611737.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0611737.text: Okay, Houston. We're both zipped now, and it went quite easily.

a17_0611737.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0611737.text: 061:21:03 - This is Apollo Control at 61:21 Ground Elapsed Time. Position and velocity on the spacecraft: now 51,982 nautical miles [96,271 km] from the Moon; velocity, 3,288 feet per second [1,002 m/s]; distance from Earth, 179,437 nautical miles [332,317 km]. Crew completing their checkout of the Lunar Module, getting partially suited in their Pressure Garment Assemblies or space suits, if you will, for the installation of the probe and drogue, and closeout of the tunnel into the Lunar Module. At 61:22, up and live on the air-ground circuit, this is Apollo Control.

a17_0612103.text: This is Apollo Control at 61:21 Ground Elapsed Time. Position and velocity on the spacecraft: now 51,982 nautical miles [96,271 km] from the Moon; velocity, 3,288 feet per second [1,002 m/s]; distance from Earth, 179,437 nautical miles [332,317 km]. Crew completing their checkout of the Lunar Module, getting partially suited in their Pressure Garment Assemblies or space suits, if you will, for the installation of the probe and drogue, and closeout of the tunnel into the Lunar Module. At 61:22, up and live on the air-ground circuit, this is Apollo Control.

a17_0612938.speaker: Evans
a17_0612938.text: CMP. I've finally got my suit on now.

a17_0612938.speaker: Evans
a17_0612938.text: I was just saying - the CMP. Got my suit on now. And I had a little trouble with the donning liners getting stuck - stuck in the zipper; but I figured out how to get them out of the way now.

a17_0613840.speaker: Evans
a17_0613840.text: Okay, Houston. Gene has his suit pretty well on now.

a17_0613840.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0613840.text: We reviewed the data on the E-MOD. Everything looks normal. One thing you might do is - no big thing, but you might zero Noun 26. It's still loaded, left over from the EMP you used in the P23 yesterday.

a17_0613840.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0613840.text: Gordy, this is the LMP. How do you read?

a17_0613840.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0613840.text: Say, when I was switching batteries, I noticed switching from low to high taps that there were some reverse-current indications. Sure that's nothing to be concerned about; you probably expected those, right?

a17_0613840.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0613840.text: 061:49:38 - This is Apollo Control. From all indications on telemetry here in Mission Control, the crew, at this time, have - has closed the Lunar Module hatch and at - should be reinstalling the probe and drogue assemblies. And finally the Command Module hatch, thereby closing out the tunnel. Apollo 17 now 177... whoops, would you believe our space digitals have gone back to Earth reference momentarily. At any rate the spacecraft is 177,966 nautical miles [329,593 km] from Earth, traveling at a velocity of 2,652 feet per second [808 m/s] in - with reference to the Earth. And as soon as the sp

a17_0614938.text: This is Apollo Control. From all indications on telemetry here in Mission Control, the crew, at this time, have - has closed the Lunar Module hatch and at - should be reinstalling the probe and drogue assemblies. And finally the Command Module hatch, thereby closing out the tunnel. Apollo 17 now 177... whoops, would you believe our space digitals have gone back to Earth reference momentarily. At any rate the spacecraft is 177,966 nautical miles [329,593 km] from Earth, traveling at a velocity of 2,652 feet per second [808 m/s] in - with reference to the Earth. And as soon as the space digital

a17_0615530.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0615530.text: America, Houston. We'd like to terminate the charge on battery B. [Pause.]

a17_0615530.speaker: Cernan
a17_0615530.text: Okay, we'll get that in a minute, Gordo.

a17_0615849.speaker: Cernan
a17_0615849.text: Okay, Gordo, the charge should be terminated on Bat B.

a17_0620402.speaker: Cernan
a17_0620402.text: Okay, Gordy, I - I'm looking around, but I can't figure out what that Master Alarm is. I didn't see any O 2 High Flow and I didn't see any lights, and we did get it down in the LEB.

a17_0620402.speaker: Cernan
a17_0620402.text: Okay, I saw SPS Pressure blink on that one. [Pause.]

a17_0620402.speaker: Cernan
a17_0620402.text: Yeah, Gordy, she's triggering continually on SPS Pressure. [Pause.]

a17_0620402.speaker: Cernan
a17_0620402.text: Yeah. I can't reset it, and a minute later she's coming up with a blink on SPS Pressure. [Pause.]

a17_0620402.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0620402.text: Okay, Gene. We think it's the - well, we - we're sure that it's the oxidizer pressure is right on the trip limit. We're almost certain it's due to helium absorption.

a17_0620826.speaker: Cernan
a17_0620826.text: Okay, Gordy. We got the SPS Pressure light on steady now.

a17_0621525.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0621525.text: America, Houston. If you give us Accept, we'll give you a new state vector. Nothing much wrong with the one you've got, but we're just going to tweak it up.

a17_0621525.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0621525.text: And one other question. Do you have the LM closed up now? We're seeing some heater currents that are a little higher indicating maybe the light's still on. And we're just trying to understand where the LM is at the present time.

a17_0621525.speaker: Evans
a17_0621525.text: Okay, I just closed the hatch, just about the time you started talking there.

a17_0621525.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0621525.text: Okay, we'll take a look at the currents now.

a17_0621803.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0621803.text: America, it's your computer, and we did the Verb 66. [Pause.]

a17_0622902.speaker: Cernan
a17_0622902.text: Say, Gordo, what's the trend in thinking on that SPS light - to leave it lit or to bump the pressure up?

a17_0622902.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0622902.text: Well, I - Ed Mitchell must be at work. We were just talking about that subject. I'll call you when they come up with a final decision.

a17_0622902.speaker: Cernan
a17_0622902.text: Okay. And Ron has put the - has closed the LM hatch. He's put the drogue in. He's put the probe in, and he's putting the CSM hatch in as a one-man exercise - suited. So he's doing the whole thing, and he's still in his suit. Our suits are stowed.

a17_0622902.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0622902.text: Okay, Gene. We got one question here, that - just - just waiting for a convenient time to ask, and that was - wondered if, with reference to the wakeup problems we had this morning, if you'd clarify just exactly why Ron didn't hear our crew-alert Master Alarm. Do you know exactly why? [Pause.]

a17_0622902.speaker: Evans
a17_0622902.text: Well, it's not the Seconal. As much as I hate to admit it, the Power/Audio Tone was Off [chuckle] in my headset.

a17_0622902.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0622902.text: Okay. We kind of suspected that - that one.

a17_0622902.speaker: Evans
a17_0622902.text: So - Okay; that lets you rest a little bit easier. And just to prevent something like that from happening again - or if it should happen again - what we'll do, we'll hook up the tone booster, which we didn't have hooked up last night.

a17_0622902.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0622902.text: Okay. We concur. Sounds good. [Long pause.]

a17_0622902.speaker: Evans
a17_0622902.text: Yeah. I woke up and I saw that light there and I thought, "Gee-whiz, I just got it in time." Until I tried to push - push out that caution and warning Master Alarm. And burned my end of my finger.

a17_0622902.speaker: Evans
a17_0622902.text: I was also in a sleep restraint and upside down with a zipper in the back. And I had a little problem getting my hands out to start with, also.

a17_0622902.speaker: Evans
a17_0622902.text: Hey, Houston, Cabin Repress is back to Both now - I mean Emergency Cabin Repress.

a17_0623620.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0623620.text: Gordo, if you don't have any objections, we'd like to go ahead and secure the High Gain, and go on to PTC while Ron's doffing his PGA.

a17_0623620.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0623620.text: Let me check and see if we have any. [Long pause.]

a17_0623620.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0623620.text: Sounds good to us. Go ahead and, per Flight Plan, spin it up.

a17_0623620.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0623620.text: And I didn't want to mislead you. I mean, you can get ready to spin it up. We'll give you the Go to spin up.

a17_0623905.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0623905.text: Okay, Gordy. You want to leave the High Gain 'til you call? [Pause.]

a17_0623905.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0623905.text: Okay. Jack, this is a good attitude to go to Omni Bravo, and you can go ahead and secure the High Gain. [Pause.]

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: America, Houston. The rates look good; you're Go for spinup.

a17_0624443.speaker: Cernan
a17_0624443.text: Okay; great, Gordo; we're Go for spinup. We've - we've got a show in here that very few men have ever seen, and that's a CMP trying to get out of his suit by himself.

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: Wish I was there to watch.

a17_0624443.speaker: Cernan
a17_0624443.text: It really is a story to behold.

a17_0624443.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0624443.text: Needless to say, we're both very impressed.

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: America, Houston. Use B/D roll for spinup.

a17_0624443.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0624443.text: Okay, Houston. This is the LMP on biomed. How do you read?

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: Okay, Jack. Let's take a point check here. [Long pause.]

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: America, D-2 Roll is not on. You need the Delta Roll jet.

a17_0624443.speaker: Cernan
a17_0624443.text: Yeah, I'm still working on it, Gordo. I was just deciding whether to spin minus or plus; but I guess we ought to spin minus, as per the Flight Plan.

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: Okay. Okay, the LMP's EKG and ZPN look good. And on the SPS light, we recommend not doing anything with the system. We want you to go to Acknowledge so the - get the light out of your eyes, and then just fly there in Acknowledge on the Caution and Warning. [Long pause.]

a17_0624443.speaker: Cernan
a17_0624443.text: Okay, Gordy. We're in Acknowledge, and - I presume, probably after LOI, we'll be able to go back to Normal, right?

a17_0624443.speaker: Cernan
a17_0624443.text: Is that an abnormal amount of helium ingestion, or do you think that's about right?

a17_0624443.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0624443.text: It's - it's absorption, and that's normal.

a17_0625204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625204.text: Okay, now that we got another look at you, Gordy, it looks like Houston might be right on the fringes of either being clear or clearer. The entire Gulf is pretty nice. Florida looks pretty clear, and Mexico looks pretty clear. There's a big air mass of cloud that looks like it picks up somewhere around the coast at Houston, heads on up north, and then covers most of the Midwest and the East, from about the middle of Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia on north. It's clear enough now to even see the coral reefs down off of Florida. And it looks like west Texas is probably also pretty clear, at le

a17_0625204.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0625204.text: Okay, sounds like the whole crew is turning into weathermen. [Long pause.]

a17_0625204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625204.text: It's one of the better views we've had of the States, I think, even though we're quite a ways out. [Pause.]

a17_0625204.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0625204.text: Roger. [Pause.] Looks like your subso - subspacecraft point is just about Peru right now.

a17_0625204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625204.text: Yeah, we're - looks like we're looking straight down on the center of South America, pretty close to what you're saying. [Long pause.]

a17_0625204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625204.text: Gordy, you want to bring us up to date briefly on how you plan on handling this time update again?

a17_0625204.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0625204.text: Okay. I'll do that. Let me - but let me practice before I start here. Just a minute.

a17_0625204.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625204.text: Okay. I'm primarily interested in those parts of the Flight Plan which we're going to eliminate. [Pause.]

a17_0625733.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0625733.text: Geno, I'll read you the PAO release; they summed up pretty well, and I'll just use their words here. The time has been made up in two increments. The first one of 1 hour and 45 minutes in the Flight Plan. The crew activities were jumped ahead by 1 hour, and they essentially began doing those things that were called for 1 hour later in the Flight Plan. They will again jump ahead an hour and 40 minutes, and that will occur at 65 hours. By that time they will have completed all those activities required up through 67 hours and 40 minutes in the Flight Plan. Or, in other words, they'll have comple

a17_0625733.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625733.text: You're lucky; we're going to lose an Omni.

a17_0625733.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0625733.text: Okay. I'll hold off there for the rest. [Pause.]

a17_0625733.speaker: Cernan
a17_0625733.text: Gordy, never mind. I think I got the gist of it.

a17_0630413.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630413.text: Okay. What we're really going to do is - [chuckle] really is simple. At 65 hours, we're going to do the update of 2 hours and 40 minutes. And the procedures are shown in the Flight Plan at 67:35. There just happens - happens to be really no - no activities we have to reschedule in the intervening time. So, after the update is complete, we'll be right on the Flight Plan, both time-wise and activity-wise. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0630413.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630413.text: Okay. We're looking at it. Going to have to squeeze my shave in somewhere else, I guess.

a17_0630738.speaker: Duke
a17_0630738.text: Hey, Gene; Houston. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: Go ahead.

a17_0630738.speaker: Duke
a17_0630738.text: Hey, you got to break - you can cast the tying vote. Which was the best description: the water bag or the clock one? [Long pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: Oh yeah. Now I remember. You got a little - give a little credit on this last one, I guess, to - to Public Affairs, because I don't think Gordo could have thought that one up all by himself. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Duke
a17_0630738.text: Very diplomatic.

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: [Garble] Considering I - I was trying to do - to do Charlie's technique step by step, I guess I got to give him little bit more credit from the gymnastic point of view. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: That sounded like one of Gordy's aircraft schedules.

a17_0630738.speaker: Duke
a17_0630738.text: Amen. [Long pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0630738.text: 063:09:18 - This is Apollo Control at 63 hours, 9 minutes...
This is Apollo Control at 63 hours, 9 minutes...

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: [Garble] they were moving another Saturn V out on the pad.

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Jack, we lost all of that due to the antenna switch. Say again. [Long pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Jack, we missed your last transmission...

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: Gordo, you listening?

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: ...due to the antenna switch.

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: You say you got it, or you're getting it?

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: No, we missed it. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Cernan
a17_0630738.text: Okay. I said you can look right down at the Cape area - that's the Cape that we know - in Florida, and - little disheartening because the last time I was up here looking back from this angle, they were moving another Saturn V for another Moon trip out on the pad already. But I guess they're working pretty feverishly out there on B.

a17_0630738.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0630738.text: 063:11:19 - This is Apollo Control; 63 hours, 11 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Charlie Duke was on the spacecraft's communicators console for a while there, discussing the clock update description that had been read up earlier by Gordo Fullerton asking for a judgement on the part of the crew as to whether that description was better than...

This is Apollo Control; 63 hours, 11 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Charlie Duke was on the spacecraft's communicators console for a while there, discussing the clock update description that had been read up earlier by Gordo Fullerton asking for a judgement on the part of the crew as to whether that description was better than...

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: Gordy, this is Jack. I think Gene was right. You got some - probably scattered cloud weather, but not very far away from you there's a pretty heavy mass of clouds. It may be the forerunner of that dry cold front you were talking about yesterday, which I can see stretching over into Sonora. But where it hits the stateside, it's got quite a mass of clouds associated with it. It looks like they're moving in your direction.

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Okay, Jack, thanks for the warning.

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: Clear behind it, in Arizona and New Mexico and maybe southern Colorado, it looks like there may be another front stretching, or maybe it hits northern Arizona and Utah and up through northern Colorado, and on in to Canada, trending northeast.

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: You're calling it right on, Jack. I'm looking at the surface chart, and that's about what we see. [Long pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: Looks like a low might be developing on that one - a wave up in northern Colorado and - although the clouds are a little hard to read.

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0630738.text: 063:13:41 - And that was Lunar Module Pilot Jack Schmitt.
And that was Lunar Module Pilot Jack Schmitt.

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: Our sub - or our zero phase point [pause] About 20 degrees west of Bolivia, our sub - our zero - zero phase point, and it is quite a bit brighter than yesterday and looks as if, and more general, as if maybe the seas have picked up in that region a little bit.

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0630738.text: 063:14:26 - Some more real-time weather reporting.
Some more real-time weather reporting.

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: One of the more unusual features is developed - as I see - has developed in the southeast Pacific just north of the Ross Sea and that is a very striking mushroom pattern on a very large scale. It has north/south clouds streaming - streamers from the Ross Sea. And when it gets up about the latitude of Tierra del Fuego, but quite a bit west of that land, it branches out to the east and west in a large mushroom pattern. And it looks like the top of that mushroom may be a curved cold front that's pushing its way up into the southeast Pacific. It currently - the eastern edge of that front is probab

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0630738.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0630738.text: I'll get some shots of that next time around. That's a spectacular pattern. You almost get the feeling that the cold airmass moving out of Antarctica streams for a while north/south. And then it picks - The cloud patterns change and as it starts to migrate, the winds start to change from east to west, Maybe that's where it encounters the jetstream.

a17_0630738.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0630738.text: Rog.

a17_0630738.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0630738.text: 063:18:04 - This is Apollo Control. Going through an antenna switch at the present time.

a17_0631804.text: This is Apollo Control. Going through an antenna switch at the present time.

a17_0631939.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0631939.text: America, Houston. I have a couple of miscellaneous items here. [Pause.]

a17_0631939.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0631939.text: Okay. We'd like you to disable B2 and D2 just for a drill here. [Pause.]

a17_0631939.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0631939.text: Also, the SHe tank looks exactly nominal, as far as the rise rate goes, to us. [Pause]

a17_0631939.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0631939.text: And to summarize your film budget situation, have three magazines: KK, LL, and MM are budgeted for the scheduled photos such that they have only five, 19, and one, respectively, frames left over after you've done all the scheduled pictures. And November November, we think, has just - has just nine frames remaining now. The two nonscheduled magazines are OO and PP; 160 frames each. Those are the ones provided for optional use. We have 44 additional frames scheduled out of November November, scheduled during lunar orbit. There's only nine left in it now, so we'd like to save at least 60 frames o

a17_0631939.speaker: Evans
a17_0631939.text: Okay; mighty fine, Gordo. Plan on Oscar Oscar for that magazine.

a17_0631939.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0631939.text: 063:23:04 - This is Apollo Control at 63:23 Ground Elapsed Time. The space digitals display here in the Control Center still showing Earth to spacecraft distance and velocity. Distance 180,309 nautical miles [333,932 km], velocity relative to Earth 2,593 feet per second [790 m/s]. A few moments ago the Lunar Module pilot Jack Schmitt who is a professional geologist, put on his hat as an amateur meteorologist and described some of the global weather systems visible from their vantage point out beyond 180,000 miles from Earth. Still up live and standing by at 63:24 Ground Elapsed Time, this is A
