a17_0633401.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0633401.text: I - Cal Tech will never forgive me; I'm a little hesitant on my elementry optics. But I just put Ron's polarizing filter in front of the monocular, looking at the Earth and rotate 90 degrees, and from max to min in terms of brightness, there's a remarkable change. And I suspect that means that the Earth is polarizing light enough to see it. The main thing that happens is that the oceans get considerably darker when I rotate the filter towards the dark position anyway. The continents don't seem to show any obvious change, but the oceans and the zero phase point darken - oh, I would guess by a f

a17_0633401.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0633401.text: Rog. I was just trying to think of a reason. Is it uniform change over all ocean areas, or is it more of a change in some areas than others? [Pause.]

a17_0633401.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0633401.text: Well, I'd say that the subsolar point shows the greatest change, but you can still - the zero phase point shows the greatest change. But all the oceans get darker.

a17_0633401.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0633401.text: Very interesting. We are just about to switch Omnis.

a17_0634200.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0634200.text: Gordy, I figure you're getting an optics briefing ready for me, right?

a17_0634200.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634200.text: I haven't had anybody volunteer one. Strictly some layman theories going around, but nothing official. [Pause.]

a17_0634548.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634548.text: America, Houston. Just got started on the Cowboy-Redskin game, about 5 minutes into it. The Cowboys are ahead 7 to nothing. They scored the first time they got the ball. [Long pause.]

a17_0634548.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0634548.text: Gordy, you started talking before we had an Omni. Try it again.

a17_0634548.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634548.text: Okay. The Cowboy-Redskin game just got started. It's now 7 to nothing, Cowboys. They scored the first time they got their hands on the ball. [Pause.]

a17_0634548.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0634548.text: Okay. I think we got most of that. It happened again, though. [Pause.]

a17_0634548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0634548.text: Did you say it was 7 to nothing, Cowboys?

a17_0634548.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634548.text: That's what I said. They scored the first time they got the ball. It's - the game's just about 5 minutes old.

a17_0634548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0634548.text: Outstanding. I thought this was Saturday. Isn't - isn't today Saturday?

a17_0634548.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634548.text: It is, but the college is all through, so the pros are playing on Saturday now.

a17_0634548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0634548.text: Beautiful. Seven to nothing, huh? Go get 'em, Cowboys. [Pause.]

a17_0634548.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0634548.text: But, he would say the same thing for Washington, I'm sure.

a17_0634839.speaker: Evans
a17_0634839.text: Okay, Gordo, my apologies on the CMP's in-suit drinking bag. There was, in fact, water in it. However, somehow, when we put the suit on, the water bag had gotten turned sideways, I guess, is the way to explain it. It got turned sideways such that the suction tube was crimped sideways. And, as a result, there's no way that you could get any water to go through the tube.

a17_0634839.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634839.text: Okay. You're talking about the problem we had there just before launch, right?

a17_0634839.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0634839.text: Okay, and for your information, the PTC looks good. It ought to hold. [Pause.]

a17_0634839.speaker: Evans
a17_0634839.text: Okay. Mighty fine. I lost my scissors. If there's anything you can do to help me find them, it'd be appreciated.

a17_0635220.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0635220.text: Got a game plan update for you here. It's now 14-nothing, Dallas; still in the first quarter. [Pause.]

a17_0635220.speaker: Cernan
a17_0635220.text: God, you're sure a bearer of good news, Gordy. That's great. [Pause.]

a17_0635220.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0635220.text: Gordy, I just - this is Jack. I just tried the red filter on the front of the monocular and about the only major thing I noticed was that the cloud patterns over the landmasses seemed to be enhanced. The contrast between cloud and land, particularly green land is enhanced. Otherwise, all it does is make the red - the Earth look a little red.

a17_0635220.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0635220.text: 063:56:04 - This is Apollo Control at 63 hours, 56 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Space digital display still showing the Earth reference numbers. 181,123 nautical miles [335,440 km] out from Earth. Velocity, 2,573 feet per second relative to the Earth. There will be a change of shift press conference in the News Center Briefing Room at approximately 4:15 with Flight Director Neil Hutchinson. And at 63:56, standing by; this is Apollo Control.

a17_0635604.text: This is Apollo Control at 63 hours, 56 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. a17_0640413.speaker: Cernan
a17_0640413.text: Hey, Gordo; this is Gene. [No answer,]

a17_0640413.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640413.text: Roger, Geno. I think we've got you now. Go ahead. [No answer,]

a17_0640413.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640413.text: Okay, Geno. I think we got you...

a17_0640413.speaker: Cernan
a17_0640413.text: Okay. I just happened to be throwing a few switches, and I see our helium tank temperature on quad A is about 95 or so. And the others are quite low. Is that because of our attitude there during - the LM checkout?

a17_0640413.speaker: Cernan
a17_0640413.text: Okay. I also see the tank that - package temperature a little higher on that quad too. But, being close to a hundred it seemed a little unusual. You're - you're happy, right?

a17_0640413.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640413.text: That's affirm. No problem. We've been watching it, and it seems to be coming down now.

a17_0640907.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0640907.text: Houston, you want the H 2 Heaters to Auto and the Fan 3 to Off, now? [Long pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640907.text: It's now 21 to nothing, Cowboys. Second quarter. [Pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Cernan
a17_0640907.text: Super Bowl, here they come. Watch out now. [Pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640907.text: Should remind you that the Commander in Chief is a Redskin fan. [Pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Cernan
a17_0640907.text: I read about that. That's why the Cowboys need as much help as they can get. [Long pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0640907.text: Gordy, in the continuing saga of looking at the Earth through rose-colored glasses, I tried a blue-colored glass, and it - as you might expect, completely masks out the continent. The land areas are just not visible through the blue. Otherwise, the ocean and clouds - or the contrasting ocean and clouds remains about the same.

a17_0640907.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0640907.text: And, Gordy, I tried putting all the filters we had together to check the Sun for sunspots, but just not quite enough light attenuation to do that.

a17_0640907.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0640907.text: Okay. For a while I thought you were a human weather satellite. Now I think you're a human Earth resources satellite. [Pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0640907.text: Well, about all I can say is I'm a satellite I guess. [Long pause.]

a17_0640907.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0640907.text: Gordy, it looks as if the distribution of water and ice in the ri - Ross Sea has changed in the last day or two. I didn't - don't remember looking at it yesterday specifically, but it seems to be different today than it was the first day.

a17_0641949.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0641949.text: Yeah, about this icepack in the Ross Sea. The - as I remember a couple days ago, there were two clear areas, triangular in shape and quite elongate, that were projecting out into the sea from the innermost part of the bay, or of the - from the continent. Today those are not apparent, at least the first look I made. And it looks like there's an elongate, more irregular clear area that is roughly parallel to the Antarctic coastline within the sea itself. [Pause.] We'll check that a little more closely and see if that's right.

a17_0641949.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0641949.text: Okay. Seems like kind of a quick change for something like ice, doesn't it?

a17_0641949.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0641949.text: Yeah, and that's what bothers me. That's why I wonder if I'm not being fooled by cloud patterns or something.

a17_0641949.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0641949.text: I'm looking at a satellite picture here, which I guess is around 12 hours old though. But over to the east of Australia, maybe about a continent width east of Australia, there's a really striking long frontal system - striking because it's so long and so straight, sort of west-northwest, trending west-northwest and east-southeast trending. Can you see that?

a17_0642333.speaker: Cernan
a17_0642333.text: Okay. Now Jack and I may be talking about two different frontal systems or patterns, but the one I think you might be referring to is the one I referred to yesterday as a ruffled parrot's beak. Actually two of them tied together, one starting up probably southeast of Australia and - and then heading down with a long arcing frontal system to another clockwise rotational parrot's - parrot's cone, I should say, down around - near the tip of South America, between it and Antarctica. There's one strong tributary front heading up to the north-northwest from the western side of this big, arcing, fron

a17_0642333.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0642333.text: Okay. I - my picture cuts off right about the - oh, two-thirds of the way south in Australia, that latitude. So most likely we're talking about the same thing, but I can't verify the southern part of it.

a17_0642333.speaker: Cernan
a17_0642333.text: There is some tremendous - on the western side of that curve front is a tremendous clockwise rotational airmass. It must cover hundreds of square miles. The one down near - near the continent of Antarctica, down there, near the tip of South America, seemed to be squashed slightly as if there is possibly some - some squashing or effect coming off - off the South Pole area near Antarctica. I think, if I turn around and look at it the way Jack was looking at it, it's a cap of a mushroom. Only instead of simply curving in underneath the cap, it has clockwise rotations on both sides as it curves un

a17_0642333.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0642333.text: Gordy, I just took two pictures of the Earth at the present time, and those are, right now the camera is on frame 153.

a17_0642333.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0642333.text: Gordy, where did you say your ATS satellite picture left off to the west?

a17_0642333.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0642333.text: Okay. To the west, it goes clear on over to - to Africa. But to the south, it cuts off about 30 south, or not quite all of Australia. [Pause.]

a17_0642333.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0642333.text: Okay. [Long pause.] Yeah, that mushroom pattern we've been talking about, on either edge - either end of the cap - and the mushroom points north - is a major cyclone circulation system. And also taking - moving, in one case - or trending, in one case, to the northwest and the other to the northeast, there are linear cloud patterns. Gives it a very symmetrical and a striking appearance. I hope it shows on those pictures.

a17_0642333.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0642333.text: Okay. It doesn't show on the one I got. Maybe a later version will have that one. Because it cuts - it's cut off on this one.

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: To put this update in simple terms - at 65, I guess on our clock, you'll update it to about 67:40, right?

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: Does that mean we have to eat 2 hours and 40 minutes earlier? [Pause.]

a17_0643259.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0643259.text: Oh, you got me there. I - You haven't been eating - you haven't eaten since breakfast. is that right?

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: Oh, yes, sir. We just finished. We'll take another go at it, but I feel I've spending my life here eating.

a17_0643259.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0643259.text: Yeah. Well, we'll leave it up to you on this special case here.

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: Okay, I think we'll take - a - a jab at supper here later in the day as per the Flight Plan.

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: Gordy - the whole suiting operation, I was really very pleased with. Jack and I both got in our suits very easily, and one by one we went into the LM, and that's where we zipped each other up. And we really had little or no trouble. We took our time. We got all configured in terms of changing our pockets around and whatever else we needed to do. And, actually, I think it's much easier to get suited than it is to get unsuited, personally.

a17_0643259.speaker: Cernan
a17_0643259.text: Ron stayed suited and did the entire tunnel work. And then went - did it by himself - and then totally doffed his suit and stowed it by himself, also, to sort of extend that little exercise.

a17_0644631.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0644631.text: America, Houston. The halftime score is 28 to 3, Cowboys.

a17_0644631.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0644631.text: Okay, I'll keep talking [laughter]. The - I've learned that when you get to the ALFMED and pull it out there, you'll see some tape around the emulsion shields. Those are three rectangular areas in front of your eyes and to either side that contain the photographic emulsion. This tape is around the edges of each of those three areas to help seal out light leaks. You haven't seen it before. Leave the tape on there. Don't pull it off. Over.

a17_0644631.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0644631.text: Gordy, I just took a series of pictures of the Earth with the 35-millimeter using the polarizing filter in the two positions. And the frame count is now 39. I took six pictures. And with the filter, on the first of each pair, in the Down position. The second's in the Up position. And I changed the f-stop from - the first set at f/4, the second set at f/2, and the third set at f/8.

a17_0644631.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0644631.text: Okay; we got all that, Jack.

a17_0644631.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0644631.text: And, Gordy, you might ask one of the experts around there in - is the lightmeter in the 35-millimeter integrating over the interior spot, or over the hairline spot? The larger one.

a17_0674042.speaker: Cernan
a17_0674042.text: Gordo, we're - we're ready any time you are for that update. And after we get the TFM and everything squared away, we'll go into ALFMED.

a17_0674042.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0674042.text: Roger. Stand by on that, Geno; and we'll be with you in a minute.

a17_0674042.speaker: Cernan
a17_0674042.text: Hello, Robert. How are you today?

a17_0674042.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0674042.text: Real fine, Gene. You're sounding great.

a17_0674343.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0674343.text: Geno, we're ready for the clock update. We'd like P00 and Accept. And we've got two loads to put in, so it will take a couple of minutes here.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: And, 17, we got that Flyby PAD now. If you're still ready, we're ready. [Pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Okay. Is this a full PAD or just a change to the other one?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: It's just a change, Jack. It's a change to Noun 83, the GET I , and a change to the bottom line, the GET of .05g. Just two changes. [Long pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Okay, go ahead.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Jack, if you just add 2 hours and 40 minutes to each one of them, that's it. The GET I is 081:54:43.49. The GET of .05g, 156:04:03. [Long pause.] Jack, I guess I read 81. I was looking at the old PAD. It's 83 - 083 - on the GET I .

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: You're too fast for me. I was just going to chew you out.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Sorry about that, Jack. I got it around the room.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: Okay, Bob. We got all of our clocks set onboard.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Roger. Understand.

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: What was the exact amount of that update time?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Two hours, 40 minutes; 2 plus 40. [Pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: Okay, 2 plus 40, exactly. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Okay, Bob. We're going to work up an appetite with the ALFMED today.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: Hey, Bob. May be a little premature - but I don't think so - but I think there was some good thinking into that update, looking at the Flight Plan up until now and where we go from here. I don't think we - we overlooked a thing.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Roger. Like I said the other night, we gave Tommy a gold star on that one.

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: Except I think he and Rita got in - in cahoots.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: A little soon for supper, huh?

a17_0675142.speaker: Cernan
a17_0675142.text: Yeah. We just finished lunch, and it's about time to eat again.

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: That's known as the simulator step-ahead. [Pause]

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Can you give us our distance from the Moon - from the Earth?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Roger. Stand by on that. [Pause.]

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Are we about 5,000 miles closer now?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Don't you wish.

a17_0675142.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0675142.text: Well, isn't that what - isn't that the way these step-aheads work?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0675142.text: Normally, yes. But this one didn't work that way. [Pause.] Jack, you're at 183,000 [nautical] miles [339,000 km]. It's really amazing how time flies when you're interested in your work, isn't it?

a17_0675142.speaker: Overmyer

Right between the two of them. [Pause.] The sine wave was - maybe two wiggles in it, and it was about a fourth of an inch long. [Pause.]

a17_0690841.speaker: Evans
a17_0690841.text: Mark; Ron. Seemed like I looked up, and as I looked up, there was one in the left eye about 12 o'clock just a flash. On the outer periphery.

a17_0690841.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0690841.text: 069:15:34 - This is Apollo Control at 69 hours, 15 minutes. Apollo 17's distance from Earth, 184,987 nautical miles [342,596 km]. Velocity, 2,477 feet per second [755 m/s].

a17_0691534.text: This is Apollo Control at 69 hours, 15 minutes. Apollo 17's distance from Earth, 184,987 nautical miles [342,596 km]. Velocity, 2,477 feet per second [755 m/s].

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Mark; Ron. [Garble] down about 06:30; just a flash.

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Mark; Ron. Left eye, about 03:30, three-quarters of the radius out. A very dim flash. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Mark; Ron. Left eye. Starting at 5 o'clock on the circumference going to 3 o'clock at about three-quarter diameter - three-quarter radius, I mean. Just a straight line. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Did I say left eye? I guess I did. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Okay, the motor quit. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Is that it? [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Yeah, I can get that, Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: Okay. Conclude experiment. Doff blindfolds. ALFMED Power switch Off.

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Okay, you want to take a picture of it first?

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Mark it. Power switch is Off. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Say, Bob or Stu.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay, add - to add to today. Not last night, but - I guess the first night I was in bed - I definitely saw some of these - because I had a hard time going to bed, to start with - I saw some of the same peripheral horizon-type things you said were not the type of data you were looking for; but I also saw a - some sets of the streaks. And probably the one most imposing thing I remember is - and the last one I remember before falling asleep - was the fact that there was a very bright spot that flashed right between my eyes like a very bright headlight - like a train coming at you, only with a fla

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: But then, as today, I saw some that flashed and lit up the horizon and some that lit up peripherally; and I guess, as you say, that's a different kind of data, but I did see them there and they impressed me.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Okay. We got all that, Gene.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay.

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: And it might be interesting to know I've never seen it before today. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Hey, Gene, we - we appreciate all the data. We were just trying to make the data fit the curve; you know the old trick [Pause.].

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay, I just wanted you to - just told them like we saw them. That's all.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: I will say one thing, though; no question in my mind but that they're there. Last trip I took, I guess I just wasn't looking for them or paying any attention to them. Maybe they were there and I ignored them because of other things. But they're there.

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: Okay, all you flash bugs down there - or flashbulbs I guess is the word - frame 50. I just took four pictures to show - two on the side and two on the bottom - to show the position of the ALFMED, and one of them of each set was focused on the ALFMED. The others were focused on the other - the other set was focused on the struts.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: And when you don't have anything else to do, why don't you have somebody predict where the S-IVB is. I think I've got her spotted - behind us and above us with respect to the Earth and our travel from it.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: FIDO just went out and shot himself, but we'll get working on it.

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: Oh, don't worry about it. Shoot. I thought you guys might have an idea off-the-cuff there.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: No, what's humorous on this, Jack, is they have really been working on that S-IVB impact point, and they've really been - it's been a - a real difficult problem for them so far.

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: I'll tell you, I bet you Ron could give you a star sighting on it [laughter]. I looked at it through the monocular and sure looks like the S-IVB.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Jack, we're not doubting you at all. We could probably start cranking it right now. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Jack, are you sto - you all stowing the ALFMED now or are you done?

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: What's that, Bob?

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Are you all done with the ALFMED now, Ron?

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Yeah, I've got to get it to - get the plate moved back down there yet.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Okay, Ron...

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Take the blindfold off first so I can see what I'm doing.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger. I just want you to know. We've got a real long update coming up to you here on the LOI abort charts and that - and it's going to be, probably, a difficult read-up. And you're the most familiar with the charts; you probably would want to take them. But whenever you want to take them, they are on - charts on page 3-81, 3-82, and then the cue card for LOI limits. Whenever you want to take them. It'll be a lengthy one.

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Stand by, Bob. Let us get squared away from the ALFMED; then we can get going on that.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: No, I don't want to hurry you, Ron. I just want you to know what - when - just get yourself comfortable and be ready to take them whenever you want them. It's going to be a lengthy time, though. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Okay.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Hey, Bob, I'm looking at what - what Jack was talking about; and it's definitely not a particle that's nearby because there is another one I can look at and get a three-dimensional comparison with. It's a - it is a bright object, and it's obviously rotating because it's flashing. It's way out in the distance, as I say, because there are particles that are close by and it's obviously not one of those. It's apparently rotating in a very rhythmic fashion because the flashes come around almost - almost on-time. And it's - as we look back at the Earth, it's up at about 11:00 about - oh, maybe 10 or

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger. We don't doubt it, Gene. And we might work out a set of gimbal angles or something here; maybe we can get a look at it through the optics.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay. And I - I - I just want to emphasize that it's definitely not - not one of these particles that tends to look like a star out there. It's something physical in the distance. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: [Laughter.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: [Laughter.] Oh, yeah. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: [Garble] thing off. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Yeah, guess I am. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Hey, Gene. If you can call up a Noun 20 so we know the spacecraft attitude, and if you can reference the object you're looking at out of your window, with - with respect to body axis and let us look at your - your - give us a mark, somehow, and give us your Noun 20s, we can try and get a tie-in and start locating - locating this object down for you.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay, I'm looking it out - looking at it out the center window - the hatch window - and I'll give you a hack when it crosses the XX axis at the center window; and I guess it's up maybe 45 degrees

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Okay, give us a hack and we're copying your Noun 20s right now.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay, Jack says pitched up about 30 degrees but...

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: No. 45 because...

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Yeah, he agrees. It's 45 degrees pitched up, and I'll give you a hack when it crosses the XX axis. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Okay...

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: Mark it. It just crossed through the...

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Mark. We got it.

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: ...let's call it the X-Z plane of the spacecraft. One unique thing about it, Bob, is that it's got two flashes. As it comes around in - in rhythmic fashion, you get a very bright flash; and then you get a dull flash. And then it'll come around with a bright flash, and then a dull flash.

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: That's the side and - of the S-IVB - and then the engine bell, Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0691802.text: The commander doesn't think that I can see the engine bell on that thing.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Roger, Jack. Is that with the monocular you're looking at it?

a17_0691802.speaker: Cernan
a17_0691802.text: He couldn't see the engine bell if he had 10 monoculars. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: Okay. I've got the cable restowed now.

a17_0691802.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0691802.text: Say again, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0691802.speaker: Evans
a17_0691802.text: And, Gene, where's your blindfold? Got it?

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: Bob, couple of revolutions ago when I was looking at it, I had a much brighter view and I believe I was looking at it broadside. It looks to me like it may be flashing more or less end-on now. It's much, not - not as bright, although it's getting brighter. But it's not as bright now as it was a while ago.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: We've actually been noticing that, I think, for about 24 hours or so. I just - hadn't put it together as maybe being the S-IVB. I thought it was just some other particle out there.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger, Jack.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Hey, Robert, what's the final Cowboys score?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay; I was just going to update that. The Cowboys won it 34 to 24. And by winning it, they wrap up the wild-card slot in the NFC; and so both Washington and Dallas will be in the playoffs.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Sounds good. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: Bob, that line of clouds I called a fir tree pattern that swings up towards Hawaii - Hawaii, if you will - has - also has a mushroom pattern on the top. It has the appearance as if two major air masses, one going from west to east and the other from east to west, have converged along that line, and the joint movement of air at the interface being south to north. And up in the area of Hawaii, I think, it tends to mushroom so that the pattern then goes back to flow from west to east on the east side and from east to west on the west side.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: In a little while, we'll probably get a pretty good look at a - what looks like a very concentrated intense storm that, I think, is just - just east...

a17_0693525.speaker: Evans
a17_0693525.text: And then we'll put them, once we get updated a little bit. Yeah, I'll get out of VOX in a minute. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: I was looking for the Flight Plan and stuff. And the little books. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: Say, Bob.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0693525.text: Houston, 17. How do you read?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Go ahead, Jack. Read you loud and clear.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, Bob, you want to update the LOI card and Flight Plan 3-82 and 3-81; is that right? [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Which one do you want to start on?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: I would say 3-81 is the most difficult one to start on. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, in that case, why don't you start on the board - on the cue card?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay. We can start on the cue card. Your - your druthers.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Yeah, go ahead. I'm ready.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay, on the LOI limits. The V GO column - let's go right down the V GO column; I think that'd be the easiest way to do it. Where it says, "V GO 2980," change that to "2986". [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Why don't you just keep going?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay. The next one going straight down the line, "2721, 2521, and 2316". That's, all the changes on the V GO line.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay; and all those changes were in Mode I?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: That's affirmative.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger. Now under the burn time column, [pause] the first one opposite the 2986, the burn time remains the same. Do not change that one. The next one changes...

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Go ahead.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Zero plus 40.

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Which one is that, Bob? I missed you.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay. Where it says, "0 plus 28," change that to "0 plus 40". [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, press on through them all now.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Change the "0 plus 53" one to "1 plus 10". Change the "1 plus 31" to the number "1 plus 40". Over. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay. I got - in order - burn time 0, and then 0 plus 40, 1 plus 10, and 1 plus 40.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger. V-measured column: the first one, the zero does not change. The next one - in this order: "265, 465, and 670". Over. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay. I got 0, 265, 465, and 670.

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: That's affirmative, Gene. That's the changes to the LOI limits cue card. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, Bob, I think we got all that. I guess Delta-V measured down there in the bottom - 2980, should be 2986, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger. We felt that wasn't - that - that is - correct. To be technically correct, it should be 2986 at that last one. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, I guess we're coming in just a sukosh hotter, huh?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: You'll see from the curves that we're going to have to update, that you're a lot closer to the free-return trajectory. [Pause.]

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, why don't you go ahead on 3-81?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Okay, this is the tough one. The first thing we're going to do is plot a couple or three points here in the Mode I - 2-hour - the Mode I 2-hour line changes, also. So you might want to draw a line at a LOI Delta-V DVM of 265, 265 and draw that straight up the curve. [Pause.] That'll be the no - the new...

a17_0693525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0693525.text: Okay, the LOI Delta-V magnitude of - DVM of 265 huh?

a17_0693525.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0693525.text: Roger. That will be the crossover point from the Mode I 2-hour to the Mode I 30-minute.

a17_0694854.speaker: Cernan
a17_0694854.text: Okay, Bob, I've got a - 265 vertical line drawn and I expect I can extend the Mode I 2-hour abort to that limit.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Now you're going to have a new curve, so don't bother to draw in the old curve. We're going to give you three points to plot and draw a straight line in between them that will create a new curve.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay. The first one is at - the point is defined with a Delta-VM of zero and an abort Delta-V of 1525, 1525. [Pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay, the second point is defined by a Delta-VM of 150; an abort Delta-V of 1810. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay, and the last point is defined by Delta-VM of 265; an abort Delta-V of 2105. [Pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: The curve defined by those three points will be your LOI plus 2 hours abort Delta-V.

a17_0694854.speaker: Cernan
a17_0694854.text: Okay, and that - that last point is just the DPS available curve with 265.

a17_0694854.speaker: Cernan
a17_0694854.text: Okay, it's drawn in and I...

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay, now we got a curve 1.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: I'm sorry I cut you out. Did you have something else you want on that?

a17_0694854.speaker: Cernan
a17_0694854.text: No, it's good. Our curve's in.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay. Curve 1 is two points defining it. The first one is Delta-VM of 265, abort Delta-V of 1855. [Pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: And the second one is a Delta - Delta-VM of 400, abort Delta-V of 2065. [Long pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay. Those two points form the curve 1 of the Mode I 30-minute.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay, now curve 2 has three points defining it. The first point is identical with the end point of curve 1. It's 400 on the Delta-VM and 2065 on the abort Delta-V.

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay, the second point is 530 for the DVM and 2245 for the abort Delta-V. [Long pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: And the last point is DVM of 670 and a Delta-V - abort Delta-V of 2475. [Long pause.]

a17_0694854.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0694854.text: Okay; and if you draw a line up the page at the DVM of 670, that is the end of the Mode I 30-minute and everything to the right of that you're in Mode II. [Long pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: Hello, Houston. Are you reading yet?

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: Okay, Bob, curve looks good. I just checked the DPS/APS crossover on the DPS available, and it comes out with what you gave me on the card - about 2521.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Roger. And just one minor point. Across the top, on the velocity to be gained, you can bias all those numbers - add a six to every one of them across the top, to be technically correct. [Long pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: The next thing we have on that, Gene...

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: [Garble] correct, I could have done that before I - before I plotted the curve; but that's good. We understand, and we got it down.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay. The next thing I've got is - that whole update column in the little block there is all updated; and we probably ought to get a readback on all these numbers, Gene. I can give it to you right like a regular PAD, just from the - right down from the top to the bottom, and then read it back to me. I think that'll be the best way, don't you?

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: Okay. Ron's going to go ahead and take them; and we'll double check them, and he'll read them back.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay.

a17_0700013.speaker: Evans
a17_0700013.text: Okay, just go ahead and start at the top and go down.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay. I'm starting at LOI ignition time. 88:54:26.8. Pitch is minus 43, yaw 112. GET abort ignition, 89:24:26.8; roll 217, pitch 6, yaw 25. Minus 42 on the Pitch, 110 on the yaw. 216, 6, 18. High Gain angles again. Minus 75, Yaw 250; GET abort ignition there 90:54:26.8; 153, 17, 19. [Pause.] Next time there is GET abort ignition for the LM FDAI angles there - 90:54:26.8; Roll, Pitch, and Yaw angles, 202, 29, 330. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Evans
a17_0700013.text: Okay, Bob, here we go on the readback. I'll just read them right down the line. 88:54:26.8; minus 43, 112, 89:24:26.8; 217, 6, 25; minus 42, 110; 216, 6, 18; minus 75, 250; 90:54:26.8; 153, 17, 19, 90:54:26.8; 202, 29, 330. Over.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Roger, Ron. A real good readback. The - on the next page, on page 3-82, the data there is exactly the same as the LOI limit cue card - the changes. We can read it up to you individually or you can take it from your cue cards; your choice.

a17_0700013.speaker: Evans
a17_0700013.text: No, we'll change it from the cue card.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0700013.text: Bob, since they won't let me write anything, I tried looking for the Moon near the Sun with the filters and could not see it.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0700013.text: You sure you're sending us to the right place?

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Roger, Jack. Hey, I've got some information on that S-IVB that you're looking at. The azimuth was in - was in within 1 degree of what you called when we looked - checked out on your angles.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Hey, Jack. Houston. [Long pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: 17, Houston. [Pause.]

a17_0700013.speaker: Evans
a17_0700013.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: This was for Jack and Gene. The Trench has computed the S-IVB location in reference to your body axis; and the azimuth was within 1 degree, very close, and the - we calculate it should have been out of that window at 62 degrees from the X-axis, and you reported 45 degrees, which is just a 17-degree error. It's real close there. You know, just eyeballing it like that.

a17_0700013.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0700013.text: That's great. Then that is the S-IVB, huh?

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay. Well, we - you might check it this way, Jack. Line up the star Denebola and Rigel - say again, Regulus; I'm sorry, Regulus - Denebola and Regulus. And then, on that line, go perpendicular to that line right above Ri - right above - right above Regulus, and that should be the S-IVB. It forms one point of a right triangle with Denebola and Regulus.

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: What you're saying is, it's the eye of Leo the Lion.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: That's affirm.

a17_0700013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0700013.text: Except we can't see Leo the Lion very well.

a17_0700013.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0700013.text: Okay.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: And, 17; Houston.

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Go ahead.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: We've got a rather lengthy Flight Plan update series here. We can read up to you any time you want. Just a reminder that we're sitting here waiting with it. Your call. [Long pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Generally what is it, Bob?

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: It's changing a number of attitudes all through the Flight Plan, 84:32 - 84:35; changing Verb 49 maneuver, things like that, due to the TLC change here on times and that. [Pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Okay, where are you going to start?

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Okay, it's at 84:32. Standby 1. [Long pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Jack, Flight just told me we can wait on this if you want until some other time in the Flight Plan. We want to get into this Experiment Checklist with the pa - pan camera, mapping camera film cycling. Or we can do both of them concurrently. [Long pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Cernan
a17_0701016.text: Hey, Bob, let's get the camera cycling out of the way first, and then we'll pick up the Flight Plan updates.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Roger. We concur with that.

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Okay, Bob, I'll get to that camera in just a second. The coast of Australia is starting to come into view. Still looks pretty clear. We'll give you more on that later, probably. That cyclone I talked about yesterday in the vicinity, I believe, of the Solomon islands, looks even better organized than yesterday. It's really tightening up. Starting to look very bright and dense right in the core, not too dissimilar from Therese. Although it has a little broader extent in the southeast quadrant. [Pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Roger, Jack. Trying to match that up in my prog here. I can't find it.

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Well, you didn't have it there yesterday either. It certainly looks like a tight little storm now though.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Jack, would you mind repeating that location of that.

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Can't give you much on the progress...

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Well, I'll try to give it to you a little better later. It's the one I was talking about yesterday as being in the vicinity of the Solomon islands. That's somewhat east-southeast of New Guinea.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Yeah. Roger. I've got 'em. [Long pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: I think before we go to bed, we'll probably be able to update the progress of the - that front south of Australia, also.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Oh. Roger. I've - I've got a pretty disorganized area to the east of New Guinea. It's probably right over the Solomons. Looks pretty disorganized on our satellite photo - from, let's see, I guess that was this morning sometime. [Pause.]

a17_0701016.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701016.text: Well, there's a lot of cloudiness in the equatorial regions, the intertropical convergence zone in there. This is south of that, sort of on a - I'll talk to you later.

a17_0701016.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701016.text: Roger.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Houston, how do you read 17?

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Loud and clear, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay, S-Band Aux TV to Science.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mark it. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay, SM/AC Power is coming On. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mark it. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mapping Camera to Standby.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mark. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: And the Pan Camera Power is Power; barber pole - gray. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Self Test is to Heaters. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: And, do you want the High Gain? [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: That's affirmative. Minus 50 on Pitch and 270 on Yaw. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay, there she is, all locked up. PCM Rate's going High.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay. When you're ready, I'll do the big deal here.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. Stand by for my cue on that, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Okay, Jack; we're ready.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay, Mapping Camera - Mapping Camera's On.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. We mark it. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay; and Pan Camera Self Test - going Self Test. Got a barber pole. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: And the Pan Camera Self Test - or talkback is gray.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. We'd like Reacq on the High Gain, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: You got it.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Thank you.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Sorry, I didn't read the checklist. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mapping Camera is Off. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Jack, say your last.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Mapping Camera went Off at 2 minutes, and the Pan Camera Power is Off.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. And we'd like to select your checklist angles now on the High Gain, please.

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Do you want those on the dial? You don't want me to try to acquire there, do you?

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0701901.text: Okay, SM/AC Power's going to come Off here, now.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Evans
a17_0701901.text: Okay, SM/AC Power is Off; and how is my ZPN doing? [Pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Jack, say again your question, please.

a17_0701901.speaker: Evans
a17_0701901.text: This is Ron. How is my ZPN doing?

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Oh. Roger. Let me take a look here. [Long pause.]

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Hey, Ron, we don't - we don't want to say it's bad, but we're glad you're talking to us because we want to make sure you're with us.

a17_0701901.speaker: Evans
a17_0701901.text: [Laughter.] Okay. Let me [garble] a little bit then.

a17_0701901.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0701901.text: Roger. We think we've got a bad skin - skin sensor interface there, Ron.

a17_0701901.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0701901.text: 070:26:35 - This is Apollo Control at 70 hours, 26 minutes [means 27 minutes]. Apollo 17's distance from Earth, 186,663 nautical miles [345,700 km]; velocity, 2,436 feet per second [742 m/s].

a17_0701901.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0701901.text: 070:27:45 - This is Apollo Control at 70 hours, 27 minutes. We have another update on the S-IVB stage; impact time and coordinates. Predicting an impact time of 89 hours, 39 minutes, 38 seconds at 4 degrees, 21 minutes south; 12 degrees, 12 minutes west.
This is Apollo Control at 70 hours, 26 minutes [means 27 minutes]. Apollo 17's distance from Earth, 186,663 nautical miles [345,700 km]; velocity, 2,436 feet per second [742 m/s].

This is Apollo Control at 70 hours, 27 minutes. We have another update on the S-IVB stage; impact time and coordinates. Predicting an impact time of 89 hours, 39 minutes, 38 seconds at 4 degrees, 21 minutes south; 12 degrees, 12 minutes west.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Roger.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: It's getting very tightly wound in the - the clockwise sense, and [pause] and is - is just where there was a less well-organized pattern yesterday. Although maybe it's moved northward a little bit.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Roger. We understand, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Our zero-phase point, Bob, is about 10 degrees - make that 15 degrees longitude east of the Solomons and has a - is a - fairly - low intensity at this time. I'll keep an eye on it as it approaches that storm area and see if it changes. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay - I'll be ready for them - Bob, just one last thing on that line of clouds that stretches up toward Hawaii. They're very - look very thick and dense based on the structure you can see as that - as the terminator approaches them. They cast a pretty strong shadow to the west.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Rog. I see those on our satellite photo. They look pretty - pretty thick in there. I'm strictly an amateur talking to you, Jack, but it looks pretty thick in there. [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Yeah, right.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: How about some flight - when you come around again, can you start the Flight Plan updates?

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Any time you want them, I can start them.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, the first one is at 84:32 in the Flight Plan. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: 84:22. Go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: 84:32. 32. Add the following...

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay...

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Roll right 12 degrees, in parentheses, to a roll of 150. [Pause.] The purpose of this change is to avoid...

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Say again the - say again the number in parentheses.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: R, roll of 150, 150.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, at 84:32, "Roll right 12 degrees to roll 150".

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Roger. And in parentheses here, just a comment, it's to avoid gimbal lock during Verb 49 maneuver directly below it. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay; go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay. At 84:35, the Verb 49 maneuver, change the attitude to "Roll 320, pitch 010, Yaw 324." And we want the High Gain Antenna angles: Pitch, minus 29; Yaw 17. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay. 320, 010, 324. High Gain: Pitch, minus 29; Yaw, 17. And that's at - that's for the Verb 49 maneuver at 84:35.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: That's affirm. And it goes without saying, scratch out - scratch out "Omni Alpha" there.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Got you.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, the next one is at 85:42. 85:42.

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: This is just a couple of notes here. The P52 stars we got in the CMS are 16 and 17. Gyro torquing will take 10 minutes, 47 seconds; 10 minutes, 47 seconds. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, the stars will be stars 16 and 17. Torquing will take 10 minutes, 40 seconds - 47 seconds.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: That's affirmative, Jack. Okay, at 85:44, over there on the right where it says, "LOI REFSMMAT attitude," change that - "Roll, 064; Pitch, 135; Yaw, 005." Over. [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, got you. Change is to Roll, 064; Pitch, 135; Yaw, 005.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, Jack, and let's take a break here, and you can go ahead and secure the High Gain and give me Omni Bravo, and call me when you're ready for some more of these. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, Jack. The next one is an addition at 86 hours, 86 hours. We just want the following words: "Manually pressurize SPS." Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay; did you get that last one, 86 hours?

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Roger. 86 hours, "Manually pressurize the SPS."

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: That's affirmative. And just for your information, that's because we need a couple hours of data on it. Like to look at it a couple of hours prior to LOI. Okay, the next one's at 87:20. [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Go ahead.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay. Where it says, "Manual roll left to 30 degrees," change "30 degrees" to "63 degrees," 63 degrees. [Pause.] Change the roll angle...

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: All right.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: ...from "050" to "001". [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, that's roll left 63 degrees and the roll is 001.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: That's affirmative. And the new High Gain angles will be Pitch, minus 27; Yaw, 339. [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, minus 27 and 339.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, just a little bit below that - where - at about 87:27 or 87:30, where it says, "Manually roll right 30 degrees," change the "30" to "63", 63. Change the roll to "064". [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay, roll right 63 degrees. Roll will be 064.

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: That's affirmative. And scratch out "Omni Alpha" and add "High Gain antenna: Pitch, minus 29; Yaw, 17", Yaw 17. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0703035.text: Okay. That's High Gain: Pitch, minus 29; Yaw, 17. [Pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Roger, Jack. And the next one is over at 89:03. We've got a comm attitude. [Long pause.]

a17_0703035.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0703035.text: Okay, that attitude there should - it's pretty close. Roll 165, Pitch 060, Yaw 338.

a17_0704508.speaker: Evans
a17_0704508.text: Roger. Always know those fellows are working with us.

a17_0704508.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0704508.text: Roger. And, Ron, you've got - we've got good data on you now.

a17_0704508.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0704508.text: Bob, Gene just told me I may have confused you on the clouds that I told you I could see near the terminator with a good shadow - and the shadow's on the eastern side as the - the terminator approaches.

a17_0704940.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0704940.text: Read you loud and clear, Jack.

a17_0704940.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0704940.text: Okay, I mentioned earlier, I can't remember exactly when, that it looked like the wa - pattern of water in the Ross Sea - clear areas within the Ross Sea icepacks had changed, and I feel more strongly about that now. It looks like it's opened up considerably. The tri - long - elongate triangular areas, two of them that were there a couple of days ago, seem to have merged, and you also have clear water along most of the inner portion of the shoreline of that sea.

a17_0704940.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0704940.text: Roger. Must be getting towards summertime down there.

a17_0704940.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0704940.text: Well, I'm very surprised that it's changed shape as much as that, and it could be that that triangular pattern was caused by a cloud bank that split what is now open water and made it look as if it was icepack.

a17_0704940.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0704940.text: Hey, Bob, can one of the guys there give me a - a hack on when - when the terminator should cross Hawaii?

a17_0704940.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0704940.text: Do it in either GET or CST, either one.

a17_0704940.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0704940.text: We'll crank it up to you in GET.

a17_0704940.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0704940.text: 070:53:20 - This is Apollo Control; it's 70 hours, 53 minutes. Apollo 17 is now 187,288 nautical miles [346,857 km] from Earth. Spacecraft velocity is 2,421 feet per second [738 m/s].

a17_0705320.text: This is Apollo Control; it's 70 hours, 53 minutes. Apollo 17 is now 187,288 nautical miles [346,857 km] from Earth. Spacecraft velocity is 2,421 feet per second [738 m/s].

a17_0705320.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705320.text: Ron, we missed a Noun 05 in there. Can you give us a Noun 05? [Pause.]

a17_0705320.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705320.text: Ron, Houston. We missed the Noun 05 on the data - can you give us what your Noun 05 was?

a17_0705320.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705320.text: You can go ahead and torque, Ron.

a17_0705617.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705617.text: Rog. We've been listening to the playback of the DSE tape from the ALFMED period, and all three of you sound pretty good on that. Gene is still clearer than the rest, but all three of you sound real clear and very readable.

a17_0705617.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0705617.text: Excellent. That'll make up for my note taking.

a17_0705617.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705617.text: Roger. [Pause.] And also, Jack. You had a question earlier about the different response of sea and continental areas when viewed through monocular polarizing filter, and I've got a note here from John Dietrich that kind of explains it.

a17_0705617.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0705617.text: Okay, let's hear what John has to say.

a17_0705617.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705617.text: Okay. This is pretty much referencing the time you were looking at it, and here it is. "Ocean scenes near the bright area off Bolivia, which is the spel - specular point, include a high proportion of polarized light. The spacecraft-Earth-Sun geometry now is approximately equal to the Brewster angle which is nearest 53 degrees, where maximum plane polarization due to reflection occurs. Therefore, a high response of scene brightness to changes of filter position can be expected. Continental scenes are dominated by Lambertian or diffuse reflectors, which are characterized by low proportion of pol

a17_0705617.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0705617.text: Okay. That sounds very good. It's sort of like the contrast between the lunar surface response and - the oceans being more like that, I guess, and the - between the lunar surface and terrestrial land surfaces.

a17_0705617.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0705617.text: That's very good, very interesting. Thank - thank John for me. I should have thought about that, but I've been away from it too long.

a17_0705617.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0705617.text: No problem. Okay; the terminator over Hawaii at 73:45 GET. [Pause.]

a17_0705617.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0705617.text: 071:02:44 - This is Apollo Control at 71 hours, 2 minutes. Apollo 17's distance from Earth now 187,507 nautical miles [347,263 km]; velocity, 2,416 feet per second [736 m/s].
