This international youth tour began December 2nd in Washington D.C. and is being conducted under the auspices of the National Aeron

a17_0710244.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710244.text: Go ahead. Read you loud and clear, Jack.

a17_0710244.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0710244.text: Roger. Gene and I are going to stir your cryos - Gene and I are going to stir your cryos for you.

a17_0710244.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710244.text: Okay, we'll be watching for it.

a17_0710921.speaker: Evans
a17_0710921.text: Okay, Houston; Apollo 17 here. We have canister number 8 in the Bravo.

a17_0710921.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710921.text: Roger; 8 in the Bravo. We got it. You made EECOM happy tonight there, Ron.

a17_0710921.speaker: Evans
a17_0710921.text: Okay, and I'm still looking for my scissors.

a17_0710921.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710921.text: What did you do, misplace them? Or do you want me to look up and see where they're supposed to be?

a17_0710921.speaker: Evans
a17_0710921.text: [Laughter.] No. They were stuck in the hand controller number 1. That little thing you're supposed to put the lap belt and things in there. It was stuck in there last night when I went to bed, and I got up this morning, it was gone.

a17_0710921.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710921.text: Scissor, scissor, who got the scissor, huh?

a17_0710921.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0710921.text: [Garble] waiting for him to get up.

a17_0710921.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0710921.text: Well, I've got a - I've got a feeling they're still with you somewhere.

a17_0710921.speaker: Cernan
a17_0710921.text: All sorts of things happened on his watch.

a17_0710921.speaker: Evans
a17_0710921.text: Yeah; we won't talk too much about that.

a17_0711530.speaker: Evans
a17_0711530.text: Houston, are you watching Jack's EKG? [Pause.]

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: Say again, Ron; we missed that.

a17_0711530.speaker: Evans
a17_0711530.text: Roger. Are you watching Jack's and my EKG?

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: Roger. Let me punch the Surgeon here.

a17_0711530.speaker: Evans
a17_0711530.text: We're doing a little - we're doing a little bit of exercising, now.

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: Oh, we can see that in the cryos. We know you're doing exercises. Let me go over and get the numbers here. [Pause.]

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: Jack, you had 120 on the heart rate. [Pause.]

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: And, Jack - guess you can pass the word to Jack we refined that Hawaii terminator number through the Pacific fleet and called it all around. It is actually at 72:55 GET. [Pause.]

a17_0711530.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0711530.text: Okay, Jack. We got you at 130 right now.

a17_0712050.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712050.text: Houston, this is the LMP. What was the last number you saw on my heart rate?

a17_0712050.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712050.text: Okay, you peaked at 135, and we had you at 130 for several minutes. [Pause.]

a17_0712050.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712050.text: Jack, just for interest, in that time you got banging around so hard there, you caused the heaters in the H 2 to shut off. The - the pressure went up until the heater shut off.

a17_0712050.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712050.text: Well, that's what you wanted, wasn't it?

a17_0712050.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712050.text: Good thing there's not another mission or we'd have to Flight Plan this kind of thing for your EECOMs.

a17_0712050.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712050.text: That's right. Got to conserve at all cost.

a17_0712050.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712050.text: Who's sitting on your right tonight?

a17_0712050.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712050.text: Got a big Moon over there.

a17_0712433.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712433.text: Say, Bob, I took another picture of the Earth and forgot to give you the GET on it. That was about 15 minutes before the end of the ALFMED experiment, if you can go back that way.

a17_0712433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712433.text: Let me see, Jack. We - the last thing we had was right about the end of it. We had you in Sierra Sierra, frame 50. And you had four pictures then. is that before that or after that? Okay, those four were for the ALFMED, weren't they?

a17_0712433.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712433.text: That's affirm. No, this was with the - the Hasselblad, the EL camera.

a17_0712433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0712433.text: We had FAO working on matching that one up.

a17_0712827.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0712827.text: Roger. That weak front that I talked about south of Australia yesterday has moved north, but it looks considerably weaker than it did yesterday even. Just a very thin line of clouds - very thin line of clouds that now is touching the - the tip of Australia, south of Perth.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Houston, 17. I think maybe you dropped out before I said that little weak front moving north-northeast, south of Australia. The western end of it is just touching the coast of Australia, south of Perth, but it looks much weaker; and I, right now, would not expect very much weather out of it.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Okay. That - I can't tie up with you on that one, Jack, because my prog doesn't go down that far; it only stays up in the landing area. And my satellite photo doesn't go down that far south either. So, I can't touch up with you on that one.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Okay. Well, it - it looked stronger yesterday, and it might have developed. Now there is a larger disturbance at the southeastern end of that front, still south of Tasmania; although, I suspect, unless it stays on a pretty northerly course, it will not affect the weather on the east coast of Australia very much.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Jack, just thought you might be interested. I called some friends of yours in Tucson, and everybody's fine there and wanted to say hello and tell you everybody's fine and getting along real good. [Pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Thank you very much. Good to hear. They've learned to take care of themselves pretty well, haven't they?

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: They sure have. They - they're - they're having a little trouble with the squawk box, and we'll get working on that and it's - they're having trouble reading a little bit, but they're keeping up with us.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: That's nothing new.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Roger.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: But try to fix it, please.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Oh, we'll - definitely on that one. [Long pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Bob, Ron got you all - the Earth down there zeroed in in the sextant, and it puts my little binocular to shame. I tell you, it's a fine instrument. And I'll just confirm that the - that disturbance over the So - Solomon islands is an awfully tightly wound little storm system. And right now, I finally have seen New Zealand for the first time in a couple of days, for sure. And the South island's got some, probably high cirrus over it. North island looks pretty clear. That's the end that I can get right now.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Roger. We saw you looking at Regulus there; we didn't realize you were looking at the Earth instead.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Ron's been looking for the booster. And he called me down and asked me to look at the Earth. He's been holding out on me.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Roger.

a17_0713106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0713106.text: Pass the torch of weather forecasting to Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Hey, Jack. I also have some words for you and Gene. Got some advice from the home front. The thing to do with Ron in the future is to hook up a Baby Ben and a metal dishpan. It works every time, if you want to wake him up. [Pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0713106.text: No. I think that's not a good way. [Long pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Ron, everybody's fine over at El Lago. They are doing great. Listening to every word.

a17_0713106.speaker: Evans
a17_0713106.text: Very good, Bob. Thanks very much. [Pause.]

a17_0713106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0713106.text: Hey, Bob. We got two of those flashers out there. They could be SLA panels. I don't know. They're alike in intensity and - and pretty regular in the - in the intensity, bright and dim flashes they come out with, and they're widely separated. One is about the position we called at the first time; the other one is - oh, as I'm looking at the Earth, far to the left. Closer to the center window now.

a17_0713106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0713106.text: Roger.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Houston, 17.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Go ahead.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Yeah, Bob, what is your - analysis chart, if you have it - surface analysis chart show for Hawaii today? [Long pause.]

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Stand by on that. [Pause.]

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Jack, according to the...

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: The reason I ask is that for using your term - Go ahead.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: No, go ahead on that, Jack.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: I was going to say, using your terminator time as a partial - mark for where Hawaii ought to be, Hawaii ought to be, it looks like that cyclonic circulation at the north end of the cloud bank I described, approaching that area, would be just about on the Hawa - Hawaiian islands. [Pause.] I'm curious if they're getting some weather down there now.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Stand by right now; I've got my weatherman right beside me here.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Also, that major front we talked about last night as being east and south of Japan has progressed even farther and is, oh, maybe 20 degrees longitude - about 20 degrees longitude from the Hawaiian islands. And I'm making some guesses on exactly where Hawaii is.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Roger, Jack. We've got nothing adverse in the Hawaiian area at all. Just a lot of winds, high winds and surface winds and surface roughness, but we don't have any bad cloud area in the Hawaiian area. [Pause.] I'll get the Hickam sequence report here shortly, Jack.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Okay, [garble] a little bit. The - our zero-phase point is now centered just a little south of the disturbance near the Solomon islands. And I see no distinct change in the intensity of that zero-phase point over what I had talked about a couple hours ago.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Roger, Jack. The Solomon islands disturbance and everything is confirmed on this chart that I've got. It's very definitely confirmed in there.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Okay. Well, it's a lot more obvious today than it was yesterday; but even then it was showing pretty strong circulation. It is starting to wrap up, look very much like Therese did yesterday.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Roger. I'm sure of that. The one right off of Vietnam is also pretty tight, isn't it still?

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Well, we can't see that one yet.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Australia in general is still very clear except in the northeastern portions where it looks like they've got scattered clouds; but it looks like a pretty nice [day] over Australia.

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Rog. Looks that way from the satellite photo from the last couple days. Looks pretty nice down there.

a17_0714106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0714106.text: Right.

a17_0714106.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0714106.text: 071:46:36 - This is Apollo Control at 71 hours, 46 minutes. Weather reporter, Schmitt, is 188,524 nautical miles [349,146 km] from Earth and the spacecraft from which he is observing is traveling at a speed of 2,392 feet per second [729 m/s].

This is Apollo Control at 71 hours, 46 minutes. Weather reporter, Schmitt, is 188,524 nautical miles [349,146 km] from Earth and the spacecraft from which he is observing is traveling at a speed of 2,392 feet per second [729 m/s].

a17_0714106.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0714106.text: Jack, in looking at the sequence reports for Hickam and Hilo and that area, it looks like they just got their standard 3500 scattered, 4500 broken clouds, maybe a rain shower or two. But just their standard tropical fluffy clouds.

a17_0715233.speaker: Evans
a17_0715233.text: Bob, I don't know whether I told you or not, but we ended up with the LMP and the CDRs suit in the bottom of this suit bag. My suit is in the top, and I sure don't have any idea how in the world the other crews got three suits in there. I guess they never did because these things are plumb full right now, of suits, in the suit bag. And it's a good thing we lengthened them. I don't have room for anything else inside the suit bag. The water bags and - you know - contingency water bags, and my g-suit, and those flight things are - I found a place to stick them all around the wall on the outside o

a17_0715233.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0715233.text: Bob, you made some comment earlier about the weather. It may have been Hawaii, but you broke up.

a17_0715233.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0715233.text: Roger; I just got the sequence report for Hawaii, and Hickam had 3500, scattered; 4500, broken with minor rain showers; and Hilo had about the same. And basically, it's just their tropical puffy weather out there. The typical nothing. No frontal-type weather - no cyclonic-type weather.

a17_0715233.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0715233.text: Okay. Well, it may be just patterns induced by the - the wind currents, or maybe I don't have the position of Hawaii quite right.

a17_0715233.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0715233.text: Well, it's - it's possible. You know they do have high winds out there, and I've seen it, just flying in that area in the past, where those broken clouds get pretty close together at times. It almost looks like a solid overcast. And especially when you look at it from an angle, they all blend together. [Long pause.]

a17_0715233.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0715233.text: I hope you're going to save all those charts you're gathering together as we talk about it on this outbound leg. Be interesting to compare them and the pictures we take sometime in January.

a17_0715233.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0715233.text: Jack, the Weather just was out here, and they told me that's exactly what they're doing. And if your time will permit in January, they'd like to go through and maybe help piece them all together, but they're going through these transcripts and they're gathering all their satellite pictures and plotting what you're seeing versus the satellite pictures etc., etc. And they'd like to go over it with you when you get back.

a17_0715233.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0715233.text: I'd love to do that. I hope, in general, we're getting the directions right. And at least, I know I thought I'd worry about the descriptions, and it's hard to place points on the globe, particularly in the Pacific, if you can't identify land masses near them or have those nice little latitude and longitude lines painted on the Earth.

a17_0715233.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0715233.text: Well, that's right. We'll - we'll put in a request for some lat/long lines out there.

a17_0715233.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0715233.text: Jack, we're going to have a slight changeover from Goldstone to Honeysuckle at 72 hours, so we will probably break by.

a17_0715233.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0715233.text: Okay. Bob, you know you're - just the last turn or so, you started to break up occasionally as if you might be getting a bad mike button or something.

a17_0720247.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0720247.text: 17, Houston through Honeysuckle. How do you read? [Pause.]

a17_0720812.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0720812.text: I was just playing with the polarizing filter again, and it looks as if - when you have the knob on the filter parallel to the - roughly parallel to the polar axis of the Earth, - you get maximum darkening. And, of course, the opposite 90 degrees to that you get maximum lightening of the globe. And, in the - in the case of Australia, it also appears to lighten and darken, but not to the extent of the - of the ocean areas.

a17_0720812.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0720812.text: It could be that in the more desert climates you get finer grain material on the ground and give you the response that John Dietrich had talked about.

a17_0721059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0721059.text: I rechecked that little story I was trying to give you about the ice pack there in the Ross Sea.

a17_0721059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0721059.text: And whether I was right a couple of days ago or not - whether I was right a couple of days ago or not in the patterns, right now there's a lot of open water between the ice pack and the inner or, let's say, southern and south - eastern shore of the sea that I don't recall being there the other day.

a17_0721059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0721059.text: I don't know whether you have any connections with all the Marines stationed in Antarctica, but maybe somebody knows what the ice pack's been doing the last few days.

a17_0721059.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0721059.text: I'll - I'll see if we can find out, Jack. I don't think we've got any gates in Antarctica, though.

a17_0721059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0721059.text: Well, that way you can't lose any.

a17_0721059.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0721059.text: Rog. Well, they never stole the continent.

a17_0721059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0721059.text: Sounds like pretty good duty, Bob.

a17_0721059.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0721059.text: 072:14:40 - This is Apollo Control at 72 hours, 14 minutes. Apollo 17 now 189,167 nautical miles [350,337 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 2,377 feet per second [725 m/s]. And, we're just over an hour away from the time that Apollo 17 will enter the lunar sphere of influence. Flight Dynamics Officer Bill Boone has re-computed the time for that event. That will occur at 73 hours, 17 minutes, 45 seconds.

a17_0721440.text: This is Apollo Control at 72 hours, 14 minutes. Apollo 17 now 189,167 nautical miles [350,337 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed of 2,377 feet per second [725 m/s]. And, we're just over an hour away from the time that Apollo 17 will enter the lunar sphere of influence. Flight Dynamics Officer Bill Boone has re-computed the time for that event. That will occur at 73 hours, 17 minutes, 45 seconds.

a17_0723111.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0723111.text: Yeah, I - I may have misled you earlier about a storm system south of Tasmania. It's - If there is one, it's just developing, and it's probably 20 degrees of longitude south. As I recall yesterday, there was some indication that a couple fronts were joining forces and moving in that direction. Today, the weaker and more western front appears to have dominated the system, and the only area where there seems to be cyclonic circulation developing is - is that point way south of Tasmania. That conceivably might move up and affect New Zealand in a few, in a couple days, but right now I don't see ho

a17_0723111.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0723111.text: 072:45:46 - This is Apollo Control at 72 hours, 45 minutes. Apollo 17 now 37 minutes away from entering the lunar sphere of influence. Present distance from Earth is 189,878 nautical miles [351,654 km]; velocity, 2,360 feet per second [719 m/s].

a17_0724546.text: This is Apollo Control at 72 hours, 45 minutes. Apollo 17 now 37 minutes away from entering the lunar sphere of influence. Present distance from Earth is 189,878 nautical miles [351,654 km]; velocity, 2,360 feet per second [719 m/s].

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0725526.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0725526.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: I just wanted to give you fair warning, Jack, in case you all feel a bump there when you're about ready to go to sleep there. At 73:17:45, you'll cross that magic line into the lunar sphere of influence.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: What's the number, Bob?

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Bob, do you read us?

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Roger. We read you loud and clear. [Pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: We're reading you, Jack. How me?

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: You're reading Gene. How me?

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Okay, sorry. I'm reading - reading 17 loud and clear.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Okay, this is Geno. What was that number on the lunar sphere of influence?

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: 73 hours, 17 minutes, 45 seconds: 73:17:45. [Pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Okay, Bob. You're a little intermittent. Anyway, what you mean is we start hauling the mail I gue[garble]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Roger.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: I guess we hit our slowest point. How fast are we going now? [Long pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Gene, you're pretty slow today. You're at 2,354 feet per second [717 m/s].

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Yes. That's - that's quite a drop from that 35K [11K m/s] that the S-IVB put us on.

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: That's for sure. [Pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Say, Bob. What do you hear from my home front? Anything? [Pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Talked to Tracy a little while ago, and she's listening to the box quite often and enjoying it, and everybody's fine there.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Bob, you're continuing [garble]. We're getting every third word. [Long pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Gene, do you read me any better on this one? [Long pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: How do you read me now? [Pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: I think you're still [garble] off.

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: Rog; you're breaking up on us, too. Let's check it through here a minute.

a17_0725526.speaker: Cernan
a17_0725526.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: We were wondering who was going to be wearing the headset tonight, Jack. Who's got the duty? [Long pause.]

a17_0725526.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0725526.text: 17, Houston.

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Hey, Bob. You reading us now? [Long pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: 17, Houston, did you call?

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Yeah, I just wondered if you're reading us now, Bob.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Rog. Reading you now loud and clear. I was just off a minute there, talking to Barbara on the phone. Everybody's fine on the home front, Gene.

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Okay, what did you say Tracy said earlier?

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: She just said she's tickled pink and listening - listening on the squawk box. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: I guess that's the way a 9-year-old daughter should be in a case like this, huh?

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: In case she's not listening, tell her not to forget to feed the horses.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Roger. [Pause.] Barbara said I should find some nice young female voice around here to tell you she loves you, good night. But I figure we'd better not do that. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Okay; enough said. [Pause.] I guess what we don't need right (chuckle) right now is a nice female voice.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: I'm sure of that. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: We're just happy, health - healthy, hungry, and homesick. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Well, you got a lot of work to do, and you better not say you're hungry. The doctor about went through the overhead over here when you said that.

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: That's a cliché.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Bob, just in general, how is the spacecraft looking to you? Pretty good, I hope. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: That's affirmative. We - we haven't found anything I guess we're - stopped getting those spurious Master Alarms here for a while. So that - that was the only witch hunt we were having right there, was trying to find that. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Yeah, they disappeared. The ones we've had recently seem to be real ones.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Hey, guys, we're just still trying to figure out, who is going to wear the headset and got - who has the duty tonight?

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Oh, I'll wear it tonight, Bob.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: That Gene?

a17_0730433.speaker: Cernan
a17_0730433.text: Yeah.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0730433.speaker: Evans
a17_0730433.text: And, Houston; 17. You ready for some onboard read-outs?

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: You better believe it.

a17_0730433.speaker: Evans
a17_0730433.text: Okay. Bat C, 36.8; Pyro Bat A, 37.0; and Bravo is 37.0. RCS Alpha, 93, 91, 91, and 94. Over.

a17_0730433.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0730433.text: Roger. Got 'em all, Ron.

a17_0731138.speaker: Evans
a17_0731138.text: Houston, we're cycling the H 2 fans, now. [Pause.]

a17_0731138.speaker: Evans
a17_0731138.text: Okay. We're cycling the H 2 fans.

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Okay, Bob, we're going to turn out the lights now and hit the sack.

a17_0734309.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0734309.text: Okay. Have you gone through the presleep checklist, getting ready on the comm and all that? [Pause.]

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Yeah; that's affirm - the presleep checklist. [Long pause.] Am I what?

a17_0734309.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0734309.text: We're not getting any biomed data on - supposed to be on Ron, I guess. We're not showing any biomed data. [Pause.]

a17_0734309.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0734309.text: 17, Houston. How do you read me?

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Yeah, I'm reading you, Bob. What did you say I might want?

a17_0734309.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0734309.text: You might check the sensors on Ron, We're not getting any biomed data. Is he unplugged?

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Well, that's because he's - Yeah, he's unplugged. Give him a chance to get hooked up and change some leads here.

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Everything else - the presleep check - the presleep checklist is complete. I'm going to leave the comm cap on tonight. Our tone boost doesn't work, so I'll just be on comm all night. [Long pause.]

a17_0734309.speaker: Cernan
a17_0734309.text: Do you have any biomed on Ron? [Pause.]

a17_0734707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0734707.text: Got a busy day tomorrow, and we'll - we'll be with you then.

No anomalies in the performance of the spacecraft. All systems in very good shape and we're either up to or slightly ahead of the Flight Plan values on consumables at this point. During the shift, a number of the flight controllers will begin working on some of the data the crew will use on awakening to place the spacecraft in lunar orbit; that event scheduled to o

Flight Surgeon reports that the crew appears to be resting comfortably at this time. Command Module Pilot Ron Evans is wearing the biomedical harness during this sleep period. And Commander Gene Cernan has the watch, wearing the headset that would receive any call from the control center. Apollo 17 is 27,178 nautical miles [50,334 km] from the Moon. And we're watching the velocity gradually build up under the growing affect of lunar gravity; up now to 3,411 feet per second [1,

a17_0773701.text: This is Apollo Control at 77 hours, 37 minutes; continuing to maintain the watch while the crew aboard Apollo 17 gets some sleep. The midcourse correction opportunity occurs at 83 hours, 55 minutes in the Flight Plan. And the Flight Dynamics Officer

a17_0783710.text: This is Apollo Control at 78 hours, 37 minutes. There's been no change in the spacecraft status during the past hour. Everything continues to function normally and we have about 2½ hours remaining in the crew's sleep period. The Flight Dynamics Officer reports that we've got a midcourse correction if it's performed prior to Lunar Orbit Insertion of about one half foot per second [0.15 m/s] or less and that very small maneuver, if performed, would occur at 83 hours, 55 minutes. a17_0793710.text: This is Apollo Control at 79 hours, 37 minutes. Now about an hour and a half away from the scheduled time for crew awakening. And it has again been very uneventful, very quiet sleep shift. With the flight controllers here in Mission Control monitoring spacecraft systems. Everything continuing to perform almost perfectly as planned; everything nominal. And our flight dynamics display at the present time is showing the spacecraft distance related to Earth; Apollo 17 now 198,800 nautical miles [368,000 km] from Earth, traveling at a speed again with respect to Earth of 2,168 feet per second [661

a17_0804101.text: This is Apollo Control at 80 hours, 41 minutes. We have about 18 minutes remaining before the scheduled crew awakening time. However, we're planning to give them at least an additional 15 minutes of sleep and perhaps 30 minutes additional. The Flight Dynamics Officer hopes to delay a decision on the need for midcourse correction 4 until additional tracking data is available. That maneuver, if it's performed, remains very small - on the order of a half a foot per second [0.15 m/s]. And the decision revolves around what height of approach pericynthion we'll have with or without the maneuver. Tra

a17_0812505.text: This is Apollo Control at 81 hours, 25 minutes. We're planning to put a call through to the crew in about 5 minutes to awaken them. And Apollo 17, at this time, is about 17,350 nautical miles [32,132 km] from the Moon. Spacecraft velocity, 3,567 feet per second [1,087 m/s]. After awakening the crew, we will be discussing a minor problem that's been noted during the sleep period. This involves a - a heater - a heater cycling in one of the three cryogenic hydrogen tanks that supplies hydrogen to the fuel cells. The nature of the problem is a heater that is cycling more often than normal. These h

a17_0813028.speaker: Parker
a17_0813028.text: Apollo 17, Houston. Did you call? [Long pause.]

a17_0813028.speaker: Parker
a17_0813028.text: Okay, good morning. It's LOI day, Apollo 17. [Pause.]

a17_0813028.speaker: Cernan
a17_0813028.text: Hello, Robert. You gave us an extra half hour.

a17_0813028.speaker: Parker
a17_0813028.text: That's affirmative. We're presently still debating on midcourse 4, Geno, and at the present time, it's small, about a half a foot per second [0.15 m/s]. We're expecting a final decision on whether it's necessary or not in approximately 1 hour at 8 - 82:30. We'll let you know then, but it will be small, and so we decided to give you an extra half hour sleep. [Pause.]

a17_0813028.speaker: Cernan
a17_0813028.text: Okay, Bob, without me having to look it up, when will it come if it comes?

a17_0813028.speaker: Parker
a17_0813028.text: Stand by. 83:55, so we'll give you about 1 hour and 25 minutes advance notice.

a17_0813028.speaker: Cernan
a17_0813028.text: Okay. Well, we'll start stirring around.

a17_0813028.speaker: Parker
a17_0813028.text: Okay, give me a call when you want to talk to people. [Long pause.]

a17_0813955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0813955.text: I'm not sure we're ready to talk yet, Bob, but I just thought you'd like to know we got a pretty spectacular view of - of Africa today. We can see the Sinai, can see the Red Sea, the Sea of Aden, and for the first time I think we can not only see the Mediterranean, but we can see the - most of the Southern European countries, Turkey and Greece and up into Italy and some of those places. Can't quite see Spain because you're just about on the horizon. And for the most part, it looks like the weather throughout the Mediterranean and Northern Africa looks pretty good.

a17_0813955.speaker: Parker
a17_0813955.text: Okay, we're copying that. And, if you guys are willing to do a little switch flipping this early in morning, we'd like you to turn on the Pan Camera heaters, which means if somebody's down there in that vicinity, it's SM/AC Power, On, and the Self Test switch to Heaters. Over.

a17_0813955.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0813955.text: You want the SM/AC Power, On, and the Self Test switch to Heaters?

a17_0813955.speaker: SC
a17_0813955.text: Okay, we got both of those.

a17_0813955.speaker: Parker
a17_0813955.text: Gee, I didn't wake you up, did I?

a17_0814843.speaker: Cernan
a17_0814843.text: Okay, Bob. The LM/CM Delta-P is 0.6.

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 17. How do you read?

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Loud and clear, 17. We're with you.

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Okay, we didn't get you there for about 5 minutes, Bob, with good up-link signal strength. Were you guys having a problem?

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: No, not that I know of. We were getting a lot of noise down here, and we seem to think that you guys were prob - assumed you guys were turned away from us or something. But we're with you.

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: No, you might think about that one a little bit. We had a very strong up-link - signal strength, as good as right now. And Gene was trying to call you, off and on, for several minutes and we didn't get any response. But sounds real good now.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Okay, sorry about that. [Pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Evans
a17_0820040.text: Hey, Bob. Good morning. It's a good chance to talk to you for once.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Yeah, for once, yeah. Talk to me now this next hour and I won't talk to you again for another 3 or 4 days, Ronald.

a17_0820040.speaker: Evans
a17_0820040.text: [Laughter.] Okay.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Nice to be able to talk to somebody for a change...

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Bob, your friendly medical officer...

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Go ahead.

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Go ahead, if you've got something to say.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Speak.

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Okay. Your friendly medical officer has all the good words starting with the CDR and the food. Are you ready to copy?

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Ready to copy. [Pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: Okay. It was a big day yesterday, eating-wise. CDR had sausage patties, pears, and cocoa for breakfast. And a quarter - one-fourth cheese spread, one-half bread, and one-half cereal bar, and one orange beverage for lunch. Tomato soup, half a hamburger, half mustard, vanilla pudding, and an orange-pineapple drink for dinner. [Pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Okay, copy that. [Long pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: [Garble] 5 hours of good sleep, and two more containers of water.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Okay, 17, I got the CDRs food and then you broke up, and I got 5 hours of sleep and two containers of water. Was there something between? [Pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: That's affirm, your - his PRD reading, 17032.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Okay, copy that. [Pause.]

a17_0820040.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820040.text: And I think, Bob, we're coming around a different Omni, so I'll wait on the rest of it.

a17_0820040.speaker: Parker
a17_0820040.text: Roger, That's affirm.

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: Okay, Houston; 17. How do you read now?

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, read you again; go ahead. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: Okay, for the LMP, the food eaten - Well, let's see, I guess it's a toss up; eaten versus not eaten, so I'll give you what I ate. Sausage patties, grits, pears, pineapple-grapefruit drink, coffee, and let me make a note that the package of peaches in that pack had been - was broken in the package. Also, chicken - I had chicken soup, ham, bread, orange drink, and four bacon squares. For dinner, I sort of ate some leftovers and grape drink, corn chowder, chocolate pudding. And I've had - well, stand by. [Pause.] The PRD reading: 24080; and 7½ hours of very good sleep last night. I took a

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, copy all that, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: Okay, the CMP, the chowhound of the kennel here, had: sausage, grits, fruit cocktail, orange beverage, and coffee. He had ham, cheese spread, peaches, cereal bar, and orange-pineapple drink. Later on, he had tomato soup, half a hamburger, half mustard, vanilla pudding, sugar cookies, grape drink, and tea. And he has a complaint this morning, much like mine, that his apricot package had broken in the bag; and, although not too significant itself, it makes everything else pretty sticky.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: I copy that. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: Okay, CMP medical is 15031 PRD; he had 7 hours restless sleep, and he'd like a comment from the doctors on how that looked on his biomed; and he had a Seconal, and he's had four containers of water.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, we copy all that one also. Jack, you guys still going to fit in your space suits? [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: If you'd stick around - you'd know we tried those on yesterday.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Roger; copy. Tried to talk to you guys yesterday morning, but I didn't quite make it there, there was a problem apparently some place. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: That's all right, we're stuffing him with food so he can't sleep.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, and the comment concerning Ron's sleep from the Surgeon, Jack, is that he was restless the first hour and had periods of restlessness during the night, but we logged him for about 7 hours of sleep also. But we did see periods of wakefulness, some of which were maybe up to 10 minutes long. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Evans
a17_0820653.text: That sounds about right; that's good, thank you. If I can't tell how long I'm awake and, you know, how long you were really asleep.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: I'll tell you, Ron, if you wake up during the night, you might sit there and stare at the second hand then maybe you could count and tell how long you're awake.

a17_0820653.speaker: Evans
a17_0820653.text: [Laughter.] Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, we owe you guys a consumable upstate - update. And on RCS consumables, your RCS fuel remaining is still 1.4 per cent above the Flight Plan; that's a slight improvement over the 1.3 per cent from yesterday. [Long pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: I guess everything else is about like yesterday. Is that right, Bob?

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Roger. The consumables are still about the same. And if you guys will wind your watches, we'll consider the postsleep checklist finished.

a17_0820653.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0820653.text: Okay, and Geno has got his null bias check for you.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, Roger on that. We're waiting. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Cernan
a17_0820653.text: Okay, Bob, made two checks over a period of 100 seconds. One was minus 99.0 and the other was minus 98.9.

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: Okay, we copy minus 99.0 and minus 98.9? Geno. [Pause.]

a17_0820653.speaker: Cernan
a17_0820653.text: And...

a17_0820653.speaker: Parker
a17_0820653.text: And we'd like Omni Charlie, please there, 17.

a17_0821525.speaker: Parker
a17_0821525.text: And, Apollo 17; Houston. We'd like to recommend you go Squelch, Off, at this time, if you haven't; and we'll keep calling you the Omnis to change as you rotate there. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0821525.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0821525.text: Okay, Bob, we've been flying normally with it enabled; maybe you think that's the problem? [Pause.]

a17_0821525.speaker: Parker
a17_0821525.text: Stand by on that and, while we're thinking about that, can we confirm that the only medication you've had is a Seconal for you and a Seconal for Ron, and nothing for the Commander?

a17_0821525.speaker: Cernan
a17_0821525.text: This is Geno, that's right; I did not take any Seconal last night. One thing I wanted to talk to you about though, I - I took one antigas pill after breakfast, I took one after supper, and I took one prior to going to sleep, which were probably within an hour apart. If you've got a better solution than those gas pills, I'd sure like to hear it.

a17_0821525.speaker: Parker
a17_0821525.text: Understand that, Gene. We'll get back with you, I guess, on that later. [Long pause.]

a17_0821525.speaker: Parker
a17_0821525.text: And, Jack, as far as turning the Squelch, Off, they do believe that we're better off with that for margins and general management at this distance with the Omnis. As soon as we pull out of PTC and go on the High Gain, we'll be much better off. [Pause.]

a17_0821525.speaker: Parker
a17_0821525.text: And, 17; Houston. You can do without your water dump now. We're in good shape. We'll dump at 94 hours. [Pause.]

a17_0822012.speaker: Cernan
a17_0822012.text: Bob, does that mean we can go ahead with the urine dump on schedule?

a17_0822012.speaker: Parker
a17_0822012.text: Say again there, Geno, on the urine dump. [Long pause.]

a17_0822012.speaker: Parker
a17_0822012.text: Say again, Geno, on the urine dump.

a17_0822012.speaker: Cernan
a17_0822012.text: Rog. Can we press on with it on schedule?

a17_0822012.speaker: Parker
a17_0822012.text: That's affirmative, sir. It's just that we don't need to do the water dump, that's all.

a17_0822440.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0822440.text: Hello, Hou - Houston; 17. How do you read?

a17_0822440.speaker: Parker
a17_0822440.text: Roger. We have you back again, 17.

a17_0822440.speaker: Cernan
a17_0822440.text: Okay. We may play the S-band squelch by ear, a little bit. We got an awful lot of noise when you guys drop off the line. So, if that's all right, we'll just use it as required. Also, I'm on frame 163 on the Hasselblad, and I just completed two pictures of the Earth about 5 minutes ago. And there's one that I did not report late yesterday at about 72:30 GET. A set of two pictures of the Earth.

a17_0822440.speaker: Parker
a17_0822440.text: Say again that time. Was that 78:30? You were sleeping then.

a17_0822440.speaker: Parker
a17_0822440.text: Okay. Copy that. And part of the reason we had a little problem that - this - this last time, Jack, was we planned to call the Omnis and we didn't get the word around down here. And we didn't call the Omni to you in time. We're still planning on doing that, and I think we'll be more coordinated next time. [Pause.]

a17_0822440.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0822440.text: Okay. We'll bear with you. [Long pause.]

a17_0822440.speaker: Parker
a17_0822440.text: And, Jack, I presume that's magazine November November. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: And, Apollo 17; Houston. For your information, we are scrubbing midcourse 4; and you can stay in PTC until 83:30, which will be about when you start to get ready for LOI anyway. We'll give you a call on that.

a17_0823235.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0823235.text: 082:33:32 - This is Apollo Control. Apollo 17 now 14,948 nautical miles [27,684 km] from the Moon. And CapCom Bob Parker just advising the crew that we will not require a midcourse correction prior to Lunar Orbit Insertion. The Flight Dynamics Officer had been reviewing tracking data and establishing another vector, as he calls it, on the trajectory. Based on that last vector, it appeared that a midcourse correction of something less than a half of foot per second would be required, if performed. And Flight Director Gene Kranz, made the decision to cancel the midcourse correction prior to Luna

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Hey Bob, we're about three quarters of the way through eating. You got some news for us?

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Stand by. I'll see. Did you catch the midcourse-4 scrub?

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Yes, sir. Apparently, you're not getting some of our acknowledgements.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay, must be. Captain Young here wants to tell you that it's raining outside; and the paperboy apparently hasn't come in yet. Omni Delta, please. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Cernan
a17_0823235.text: I'm surprised he didn't get his papers delivered before he came in.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Roger. I suppose I should apologize to all the paperboys after saying that, but the news is still being put together for you guys. And - stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: And, Geno, some advice to you on the gas pills. I guess - suggestion down here from the Surgeon is that one thing we ought to be sure to do is chew the pills thoroughly. It apparently is - helps in their effectiveness quite a bit; and Dr. Young, beside me, also suggested if you're chewing chewing gum, you might cut down on that a bit because he thinks this might be causing some gas.

a17_0823235.speaker: Cernan
a17_0823235.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Cernan
a17_0823235.text: I might add that both of those alternatives have been - worked on.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: We thought probably so. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Bob, although we're getting close to concentrating our attention on the Moon, it doesn't decrease the interest in looking back at the patterns of activity we can see on the Earth. That storm I talked about yesterday that was in North Africa, looks like it has left that area and has moved in - maybe, if it's there at all, it's just over the - Iberian Peninsula, and maybe Gibraltar and that area is getting a little activity today.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay; copy that, Jack.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: It does not look very well organized, but - it's not very well organized right now, but - it's right out on the LM, and it's hard to get a good view of it.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: The storm I guessed yesterday - I thought might be moving into the Cape of Good Hope looks like it's dissipating and also staying south of that area. The whole of Africa is essentially clear, except in the southern part of the intertropical convergence area where there's scattered patches of - of fairly dense clouds. They're probably getting scattered rain showers of some kind in there this morning. Some of those extend farther south than I've - than we've seen them - down into South Africa. There's a - On one of the earlier revs, although now it's at the terminator, it looked like there was a

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Roger. Omni Alpha, please. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay, you got it.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay. And, Jack, while you guys are finishing your lunch - your breakfast there, excuse me - Are you all on your headsets?

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Yes, sir. Go ahead.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay. Let me brief you on a little funny that we we saw last night. And I'll start the briefing by mentioning that, at the present time, it is not a great concern; but just to keep you up to date with what's going on, let me mention it to you. About 70 hours, which was probably about the time of your last exercise period, we saw three funnies with the hydrogen tanks - as I say, none of which is causing any great concern. The first of these was a shift of the limits of the pressure switch, the one that turns the heaters on and off. Remember, there are two of those switches, one on tank 1 and on

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay, Bob. I understand that. You know, I wonder if we ought to stop stirring the cryos the way we've been doing it. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: That - that has been suggested, but, again, it's not very clear that any of these things are terribly correlated. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay. Also, you know, if you want to reduce the activity on that switch - depending on how much you need to have it done during quiet periods, such as eat periods and things like that - we could go to manual operation.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Negative, Jack, because the switch - Omni Bravo, please, 17.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: If you pull out your schematics there, you'll find that the - no matter what you do, the - you can turn the thing off, in fact, and the switch will continue to operate the motor switch - the pressure switch will continue to operate the motor switch off the Service Module buses. There's nothing you can do. The only thing you'll do if you go from Auto to Manual or Off is you'll keep the current from going to the heaters, but the motor switch will still operate.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay. Thank you for the education. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: And I've been corrected. The frequency of the pressure oscillation was more in the vicinity of a cycle every 4 or 5 seconds. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: And Seven...

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Bob, let me ask a couple of questions to make sure...

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Go ahead.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Make sure I understand this. You're not sure whether the heater cycling and the pressure cycling were correlated. Is that correct?

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.]

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: In a cycle every 4 or 5 seconds, is it possible for the heaters to affect the tank that fast?

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: That's not possible, so the only thing that really - we think could - The tank is too much of a heat sink to do it that way. What may have happened was that if you set up an oscillation - a mechanical oscillation in the tank - through - one way or another, that this could then have acted back up on the motor. But the motor switch in driving the heaters could not have reinforced the oscillation because the tank is too much of a heat sink.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay. When did you say this happened with respect to our exercise period?

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: That's not well pinned down, 17. We do know it hasn't occurred since about 71 hours; and it did occur at approximately 70 hours, which was about the time of your exercise period. But we haven't been able to correlate that exactly with the start of or the finish of the exercise period.

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Well, you know you should be able to do that because of the biomed on - at least on me, and Ron was on, too. But, as soon as I started exercising, you should have the biomed data on my heart rate. It was an unscheduled exercise period. We just went into it before an eat period there, I think. Let me check back.

a17_0823235.speaker: Parker
a17_0823235.text: Okay. And we can check back and inform you more specific on what the times were there in terms of your exercise period, also, I might - Omni Charlie, please, there, 17. And we might mention that oscillations like this have been seen on the ground under somewhat different circumstances, but oscillations like this have been seen on the ground in ground tests previously. And I might say, also, that as far as other things in the spacecraft are concerned, everything looks absolutely normal or nominal, as the case may be, and in great shape and emph - I'd emphasize again that we've seen none of this

a17_0823235.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0823235.text: Okay, Bob. That was, as you say, pretty close to the exercise. I can't pin it down in the checklist exactly, but it was somewhere after ALFMED was complete and before we changed that canister. I think we changed that canister a little early, about 70:50. So I think the medics should have pretty good data on when we were exercising. And the reason I say that was because the way we were - I was exercising anyway - I'm sort of running in place against the LEB and conceivably could have gotten an oscillation going in the tank.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Omni Delta, 17. [Long pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: And, 17, we did a little - a little investigation of times down here. We found that at 71:12 you were exercising at 130 beats per minute there Jack. And we think the exercise period ended about 10 minutes later at 71:22. The H 2 tank funnies started at about 71:37 with the pressure switch shift and 71:42 with the oscillations. Over. So, there it's - oh, at least 15 minutes after the exercise period was over.

a17_0825254.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0825254.text: Okay. I just wanted to clear my reputation, Bob. [Pause.] Now it's perfectly clean again.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: As clean as ever, anyway. [Long pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Okay. 17, I guess we decided we'd let - we'll run the Omnis down here instead of having you guys push them all the time. So if you'll select Omni Bravo at the present time, then we'll take over and run the Omnis for you. [Pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0825254.text: Okay, Bob. It's not too big a deal. If anytime you think you want to talk to us continuously, go ahead and call them, if we're not busy.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Okay. Copy that. Let us know when you're ready. I've got a PAD here for you guys to copy, but there's no big hurry on it. Finish your eat period and give us a call. [Pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0825254.text: Okay. I'll be with you in about 5 minutes.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Say again there, 17,

a17_0825254.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0825254.text: Be right with you, Bob.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: All right.

a17_0825254.speaker: Cernan
a17_0825254.text: And, looking at the Flight Plan, we're going to go ahead and change a canister; and we've got the H 2 purge Line Heaters, On. We're going to configure for the urine dump. We'll go ahead and do our - stop our PTC at 83:30, and then we'll do our P52. [Pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Roger. Copy that. [Long pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: And, 17, that P52 at 83:10 was primarily intended for the MCC-4. There's some more following, anyway, before LOI. So we suggest you scrub the P52 at 83:10. [Pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Evans
a17_0825254.text: Okay, fine. I may just do a little OJT without torquing.

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: That's your business. [Long pause.]

a17_0825254.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0825254.text: 082:57:10 - This is Apollo Control at 82 hours, 57 minutes. We're completing a shift handover at this time in Mission Control. The team of flight controllers, headed by Flight Director Gerry Griffin, coming on now to replace the Gene Kranz team. The spacecraft communicator on the upcoming shift is Astronaut Gordon Fullerton. We do not plan to have a change of shift press briefing at this shift change.

This is Apollo Control at 82 hours, 57 minutes. We're completing a shift handover at this time in Mission Control. The team of flight controllers, headed by Flight Director Gerry Griffin, coming on now to replace the Gene Kranz team. The spacecraft communicator on the upcoming shift is Astronaut Gordon Fullerton. We do not plan to have a change of shift press briefing at this shift change.

a17_0825254.speaker: Cernan
a17_0825254.text: Bob, when we come out of PTC, then you want us to go right to the SIM door jett attitude?

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: That's affirmative, 17.

a17_0825254.speaker: Cernan
a17_0825254.text: Okay, and you want us to do that about 80 - 83:30, huh?

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Roger. That's affirm.

a17_0825254.speaker: Cernan
a17_0825254.text: Okay.

a17_0825254.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0825254.text: Bob, what PAD are you going to give me?

a17_0825254.speaker: Parker
a17_0825254.text: Okay, I've got a - coming up, pericynthion - plus-2-hour abort PAD here.

a17_0830133.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830133.text: Yeah, Bob. Here's 17. Say, for a while here, why don't you guys go ahead and manage the Omnis. I think we can get things done a little better; and when it becomes inconvenient for us to switch, we'll let you know.

a17_0830133.speaker: Parker
a17_0830133.text: Okay. You want us to call them to you - is that what you're saying by you manag - we manage the Omnis?

a17_0830133.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830133.text: Yes, we lose 5 or 10 minutes going around here without comm, and it usually breaks up seemingly when somebody has something to say, either you or us.

a17_0830133.speaker: Parker
a17_0830133.text: Roger. Okay. That's fine. Stand by.

a17_0830133.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830133.text: That's up to you guys, but, it seems to me, it would be more convenient.

a17_0830133.speaker: Parker
a17_0830133.text: Okay; things are good now, Jack. Do you want to copy this pericynthion-plus-2 PAD at the present time?

a17_0830133.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830133.text: Yeah, I'm just about ready, Bob.

a17_0830133.speaker: Parker
a17_0830133.text: Okay, give me a call when you get it. [Pause.]

a17_0830133.speaker: Parker
a17_0830133.text: And, while you're getting ready there, you might think back to yesterday afternoon just after the exercise period; and the question that's raised is whether you were running the DAC or some other miscellaneous equipment at that time which might have caused some high current usage - or erratic current usage. [Long pause.]

a17_0830133.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830133.text: We'll think about that, Bob; but offhand, none of us can remember doing anything like that.

a17_0830615.speaker: Parker
a17_0830615.text: And, 17, your faithful night shift CapCom is signing off. I'll talk to you on the surface tomorrow. Good luck. [Pause.]

a17_0830615.speaker: Cernan
a17_0830615.text: Thank you, Robert. Looking forward to seeing you there.

a17_0830615.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830615.text: Boy, he doesn't stick around long, does he? And he wanted to read that PAD to me; well, that's too bad. Okay, Gordy, I can take the PAD now.

a17_0830615.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0830615.text: Okay, Jack. It's pericynthion plus 2; SPS/G&N. Weight is 66373; plus 1.18, minus 0.14; ignition time is 090:49:55.82; plus 1787.5, minus 1891.7, minus 2396.8; attitude is 237, 126, 332; and all the rest of the PAD is NA. GDC Align stars are Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. Ullage is none. Remarks: number 1, burn docked; number 2, assumes LOI REFSMMAT. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0830615.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0830615.text: Okay. Pericynthion plus 2, SPS/G&N; 66373, 1 - plus 1.18, minus 0.14; 090:49:55.82; plus 1787.5, minus 1891.7, minus 2396.8; 237, 126, 332; rest of PAD is NA; Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. No ullage. Remark 1, burn docked; 2 is LOI REFSMMAT assumed.

a17_0831508.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0831508.text: America, Houston. I have the morning news if it's a convenient time.

a17_0831508.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0831508.text: Okay, first of all the weather. It's raining fairly - fairly heavily all night; there's a lot of water standing around. Temperatures here are in the high 50s, but it's supposed to get a little cooler tonight with a low in the 40s. I think you know how the Dallas-Redskin game came out - the only thing additional mentioned here is that chances look good now that Washington and Dallas may meet in the rubber games for the National Conference representative in the Super Bowl. In the other pro game yesterday, a field goal by Don Cockroft was the difference in a 26-to-24 win by Cleveland over rival C

a17_0831508.speaker: Cernan
a17_0831508.text: Thank you, Gordo, appreciate the news. Sounds like things are still happening down there. [Long pause.]

a17_0831508.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0831508.text: Got some more parochial news here...

a17_0831508.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0831508.text: No, we just - I just wanted to tell you we're starting our waste dumps.

a17_0831508.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0831508.text: Okay. A little more parochial news. I have your oxygen consumable status here. Tank 1 is still running 4 per cent below the line; the other two are right on the line; really no news there. Same with the hydrogen; all three are essentially right on the preflight lines. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0831508.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0831508.text: Okay, that's the way we like to hear it.

a17_0831508.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0831508.text: We'll bring all of it home if we can.

a17_0832849.speaker: Evans
a17_0832849.text: Okay, Gordy. How would you like a hydrogen purge this morning?

a17_0832849.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0832849.text: 17, we do want the hydrogen purge; go ahead.

a17_0832849.speaker: Evans
a17_0832849.text: Okay, hydrogen purge is in process. You'd never believe it, dust collection container assembly serial number 5725 developed a hole in it. [Pause.] Fortunately, with a lot of dexterity, I was able to put a piece of tape over the hole. [Pause.]

a17_0832849.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0832849.text: Okay. I guess that's why we sent men into space.

a17_0832849.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0832849.text: Gordy, while the purges are going on here, I might mention, a little while ago, I looked at the Earth through a Polaroid colored glass again and had a full view of Africa. And it appeared as if, in the red and yellow portions of Africa, that the land areas darkened considerably more than those areas that are green or foliated, and that would be the central portion; that is, they darkened with the orien - handle on the lens going in a north-south rather than east-west.

a17_0832849.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0832849.text: The land areas, though, still do not show as marked a contrast as do the oceans.

a17_0833437.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0833437.text: Okay, hydrogen purge is complete. Heater's going Off.

a17_0833437.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0833437.text: Gordy, it looks like the cloudiness and possibly the showers associated with the intertropical convergence over Africa are moving as far south as Johannesburg right now. It's quite a distinct change from even an - an hour or so ago - a couple of hours ago. They're down into an area where, presumably, they're not normally found if vegetation indications are any criteria. And also, in the Atlantic - South Atlantic near Goa island, there seems to be a possible storm developing as part of what was probably now a fairly weak front. And whether or not that will develop into anything and move in towa

a17_0833437.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0833437.text: It looks as if our old friends at Ascension are enjoying a fairly nice day out there.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Jack, this is Houston. We recall you mentioning the purge complete and the heaters, Off. We just wanted to be sure that you did leave the H 2 purge line heaters, On, for 10 minutes after terminating the purge. Over.

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Thank you, Gordy. I'll turn them back on.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Who's sitting over there reminding me of all these good things this morning?

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Well, that was a combination effort by John Aaron and Charlie Dumis.

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Wow! You've got a real powerful team there.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: You bet. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Hey, you really ought to get them a cup of coffee though sometime this morning.

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Gordy, also curious who's wa - who's watching Challenger this morning?

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Well, let's see.

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Not much to see, I realize, but I'm sure somebody's there.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: We need Omni Charlie, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Well, we've got the first team on - the gold team - your LOI and landing team, and the LM guys are Merritt and Thorson. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: You cut out on the telmu. Who is it?

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Merlin. Merlin the Magician. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: I'm sorry, Gordy, you clipped off the first again.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Merlin Merritt, the magician.

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Oh, yes; of course. [Pause.] As I recall, he's the only one that really understands Thorson. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: He says he doesn't think anybody understands Thorson. [Long pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: Well, we're sure looking forward to having a chance to make those guys work a little bit. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: They say - well - Merlin says he is, too. I don't know about Thorson. He's out of the room at the moment. [Pause.]

a17_0834009.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834009.text: He's probably spilling coffee in SPAN.

a17_0834009.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0834009.text: Rog.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: Gordy, for some reason, it's a lot easier to tell the difference between the Antarctic Continent and the icepack.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: Maybe the glancing Sun is picking up the breaks in the icepack and giving it a different appearance.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: The continent itself - all you can see are very - what appear to be very gentle differences in - or subtle differences in shading, possibly indicating rolling relief due to a photometric darkening along the - as a function of local phase angle. [Pause.]

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: And except, maybe, for the area just - well, no - even there, I didn't the [garble] - it looks like the whole visible continent is clear of clouds this morning. Possibly some clouds just east of the Ross Sea, which is just coming into view, I think.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: I know we don't have many listeners in Antarctica, but it looks like they're having a - exceptionally fine day over the portion of the continent we can see.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: That weak front I mentioned in the South Atlantic stretches from the apparent storm center around Goa island - I'm not sure about that pronunciation either - up just to the coast of South America from Brazil, where it reaches its maximum eastward extent.

a17_0834846.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0834846.text: Our sub - our zero-phase point of the spacecraft is in the middle of the South Atlantic. And it's moderately bright, although there is no central bright point at all - a fairly large area, but moderately bright. The seas down there may be moderately choppy or rough this morning.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Houston, 17.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Go. [Pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, Gordy. You might say "uh" before you - you start your sentences because you're clipping your first word. The question I had was the Pan Camera - we're on 1-6 of the Experiments Checklist and need your word on whether you want the Pan Camera, Off, at this time - Self Test, Off.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Uh, Stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: We'd like you to leave it in Heaters.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, we're leaving it in Heaters.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, Houston. The S-Band Aux, TV is to Science...

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Roger.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: ...and I'm turning the IR, On.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Jack, we'd like Omni Alpha.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: How do you read on Omni Alpha?

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Okay; you're readable, fair amount of noise. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Hello, Houston. How do you read?

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Jack, this is Houston. You're clear with some considerable noise. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Houston, how do you read 17?

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Apollo 17, Houston. Still reading you with a lot of background noise. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Hello, Houston. How do you read?

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: 17, Houston. Weak but readable.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, we'll have you up on that High Gain pretty soon. I'm turning the IR, On.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Roger; Roger; Roger. IR, On. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Say again, Gordy.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: We copy. IR, On. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: America, we'll take the High Gain now. Pitch, minus 15; Yaw, 188. Over.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: America, Houston. Let's try the High Gain now. I see you're moving it. Minus 26 and 199. [Pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, I think we've got a main load block now on the High Gain. How do you read?

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: You're loud and clear, Jack. It looks good here.

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay, Gordy. Let me keep going here. I did not turn the IR on because I thought you said something. IR is going On now.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Okay. What I said is, "Roger. IR, On." [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Coming on. [Pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Mapping Camera going to Standby.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Okay; Standby on the Map Camera. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0835427.text: Okay. I'm waiting your cue for Pan Camera Power, to Power.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Roger. We're still locking up on the data. We'll give you a cue. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Okay, Jack. You have our cue for Pan Camera Power to Power. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Evans
a17_0835427.text: Okay. Pan Camera going to Power. [Long pause.]

a17_0835427.speaker: Evans
a17_0835427.text: Okay, Gordo. We're in the SIM bay door jett attitude.

a17_0835427.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0835427.text: Roger.

a17_0835427.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0835427.text: 084:06:12 - This is Apollo Control; 84 hours, 6 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Present distance from the Moon...

a17_0840612.text: This is Apollo Control; 84 hours, 6 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Present distance from the Moon...

a17_0840612.speaker: Evans
a17_0840612.text: Pan Camera Power is going to Boost.

a17_0840612.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0840612.text: 084:06:31 - Velocity, 3,763 feet per second [1,147 m/s]. Next major maneuver is Lunar Orbit Insertion, which presently is scheduled for 88 hours, 54 minutes, 22 seconds Ground Elapsed Time. Total Delta-V or change in velocity, which will be retrograde, of 2,988 feet per second [911 m/s]. Service Propulsion System engine burn time of 6 minutes, 38.08 seconds. Mother Earth is 206,059 nautical miles [381,621 km] behind Apollo 17, and locked up on the High Gain Antenna at this time so we should have fairly good communications all the way through the SIM Bay door jettison and until the spacecraft p
