a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Oh, down there. Oh. [Long pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Me to you. [Long pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Houston. I'm in Vox now. Do you read?

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Yes, sir. You're loud and clear. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay. On panel 181, the Logic Power Main A, Main B circuit breakers are Closed.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Roger.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay. Logic Power number 1 is going to Jett, number 2 to Jett. Standing by for your Go, Houston.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay. Stand by. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay, America, you're...

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: What happens now is...

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: ...Go to jett the SIM bay door.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Jack, let me know when you've got the camera ready.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Houston. You say we are Go to jett the SIM bay door a little early, huh?

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Well, stand by. I think we're backing down here. Stand by 1 second.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: No. I checked it at one frame.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: You might check it.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay, America. Once again, you're Go to jett the door, and you can do it early, if you wish.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Gordo. We'll do it on - on Ron's mark down there.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay.

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Hey, Houston. You know this attitude - this attitude has the Sun right into window 5 - it's probably going to be on the lens of the camera. I'll - I'll try to shade it the best I can, but I don't have an awful lot of hope for these pictures. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: I think we're probably stuck with it, Jack, because we need to be in this right attitude, for the clearance and... [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Ron. Let her go.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay. SIM door Jett 5, 4, 3, 2, 1...

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Jett.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Houston, there it goes, I got it out the hatch window and it looks like it was a clean jett. It's rolling and pitching and yawing, slightly. There is a lot of garbage that came out with it.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Can you take a picture, Gene? [Long pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Let me see it.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Ah - ah [laughter]. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: You take a picture. Yeah, there it goes.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Hello, Houston. How do you read?

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: It's really...

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Loud and clear. Sounding good.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay. Did you get the word we got a clean jett?

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: That's right, Geno. Sounds good.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay. The door's moving - the door's moving directly away from us, mostly rolling. And it looks like it was a very clean - clean separation.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Yes. Boy, we got a good bang out of it. You could hear that - that pyro going, I think.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: And it's rotating - what, about the long axis? Yeah. Rotating about the long axis.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Houston, the garbage that I said went with it was just a small amount of debris, I'm sure around the sealant pyro area. There was one, oh, about a 4-foot-length piece of, oh, 1 or 2 inch tapelike material that also went out with it.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Roger, Gene.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: [Laughter.] Okay. What do we do with these Logic Power switches? Don't they go back to Off now?

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Door Jett's Off, down.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Okay. You go on to the Deploy/Retract on number 1.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Deploy/Retract on number 2.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Fuel Cell Reac Valves are Normal. I'm sort of glad we had those in Latch.

a17_0840914.speaker: Evans
a17_0840914.text: Yeah, me, too, 'cause that's a pretty good bang. [Long pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Yes, they're all gray.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: You've loaded the wrong pitch angle there in Noun 22. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Well, I'm - I got 10 degrees loaded; that's what we've got copied down here in the change. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Maybe it's our mistake. Let us check here, Geno.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Okay, we got 320, 010, and 324, and before I go into the muver - maneuver, I'll roll right about 12 degrees. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Bad call, Gene. Our error; you're right.

a17_0840914.speaker: Cernan
a17_0840914.text: Thank you, sir. [Pause.]

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Okay, and the UV Spectrometer is going to go On here.

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Mark it.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Roger. Mark the UV.

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Okay, and the IR will be Off on your cue.

a17_0840914.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0840914.text: Okay, Jack, that'll be 12 or 15 minutes from now.

a17_0840914.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0840914.text: Okay, just give us a call.

a17_0841943.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0841943.text: Okay, the 100-Watt O 2 Heater circuit breaker's coming Open.

a17_0841943.speaker: Evans
a17_0841943.text: O 2 Tank 100-Watt Heaters; 1, Main A, Open; 2, Main B, Open.

a17_0841943.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0841943.text: Okay, O 2 Heaters 1 and 2 going to Auto, and 3, Off.

a17_0842151.speaker: Cernan
a17_0842151.text: Okay, Gordo. We'll wait until 50 past the hour and pick up the LM/CM Delta-P; we're still reading 0.6.

a17_0842151.speaker: Cernan
a17_0842151.text: And we're in the process of maneuvering and I guess I'll start to see if I can't get you some biomeds.

a17_0842151.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0842151.text: I don't know whether you were watching the LMP on the door jett, did you see a jett on my heartbeat?

a17_0842151.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0842151.text: Well - we'll check this data here, Jack.

a17_0842151.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0842151.text: I guess I was remembering erroneously 15's comment that it was very quiet, but I - of course, Ron reminded me they were in the suits. [Pause.]

a17_0842151.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0842151.text: Okay, Jack. John Young was talking about the same thing here, but we didn't see anything on your EKG.

a17_0842151.speaker: Evans
a17_0842151.text: And Houston, 17 here. Mag Bravo Bravo is indicating 20 - let's see - indicating 76 per cent now - 76-per cent full.

a17_0842151.speaker: Cernan
a17_0842151.text: And, Gordo, we are watching the 8-ball.

a17_0842151.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0842151.text: Roger. We're keeping an eye on it, too.

a17_0843315.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843315.text: Okay, you've got it to Auto. I think we may have a new discovery about microphones up here.

a17_0843315.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0843315.text: Oh, is that right? What's that?

a17_0843315.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843315.text: Well, Gordy, it looks as if you could improve your voice quality by putting fingers over the end of the mike booms. At least that works on the intercom.

a17_0843315.speaker: Evans
a17_0843315.text: That's the old tape recorder with fingers over the end of the mike. That's the tape recorder without the fingers over the end of the mike.

a17_0843315.speaker: Cernan
a17_0843315.text: Yes, it went on right away.

a17_0843517.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0843517.text: America, Houston. We're ready for the IR to Off.

a17_0843715.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843715.text: Hey, Gordy. Who's operating in the trench in front of you today?

a17_0843715.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0843715.text: Okay. It's the LOI and descent team, Presley, Green, and Deiterich. [Pause.]

a17_0843715.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843715.text: They're a trio of musketeers, if I ever heard of one.

a17_0843715.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843715.text: All they lack is a French accent. [Pause.]

a17_0843715.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0843715.text: A New York accent is about the best they can do. [Long pause.]

a17_0843715.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0843715.text: I wasn't going to exercise any value judgments, Gordy.

a17_0844059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844059.text: Jack, this is Houston. I have a preliminary LOI PAD anytime it's convenient.

a17_0844059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0844059.text: Okay, Gordy. I was just checking to see if I could find the Moon, and I still can't see it out there.

a17_0844059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0844059.text: I'll be with you in 30 seconds.

a17_0844059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844059.text: Okay. This is a preliminary LOI, SPS/G&N. 66361; plus 1.21, minus 0.12; 088:54:22.71; minus 2798.8, plus 1045.7, minus 0037.3. Attitude is all zeros. H A is 0170.1, plus 0052.5; 2988.0, 6:38, 2981.7; sextant star 45, 252.1, 13.5. Boresight star and all the rest is NA. GDC Align stars: Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. Ullage, none. Remarks: The LM weight, 36312; and single-bank burn time is 6:51. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a17_0844059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0844059.text: Okay. Preliminary LOI, SPS/G&N. 66361; plus 1.21, minus 0.12; 088:54:22.71; minus 2798.8 plus 1045.7, minus 0037.3. All zeros; all zeros; all zeros; 0170.1, plus 0052.5; 2988.0, 6:38, 2981.7; 45, 252.1, 13.5. Set stars are Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. No ullage. LM weight is 36312, and single-bank burn time is 06:51.

a17_0844059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844059.text: One correction on the ignition time. The seconds are 22.77.

a17_0844059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844059.text: That's affirmative; otherwise, good readback. [Long pause.]

a17_0844059.speaker: Evans
a17_0844059.text: Okay, Houston. At 84:45, we've got about 2½ to 3 minutes at 1 frame a second on mag Bravo Bravo, through the celestial adapter of the Earth.

a17_0844059.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844059.text: Okay, Ron. We caught that. And if you're looking for the Moon, according to our figures here, it should be visible out window number 1 about 30 degrees off the boresight axis. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0844059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0844059.text: Okay, got you. I'll try again.

a17_0844059.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0844059.text: Oops. It's right there. That's good.

a17_0844916.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0844916.text: America, Houston. I'm ready with a TEI-4 PAD anytime it's convenient.

a17_0845356.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0845356.text: Okay, TEI-4, SPS/G&N; 40090; plus 0.50, plus 1.17; 097:20:47.45; plus 2004.8, minus 2951.1. minus 1547.3; 202, 083, 312. Rest of PAD NA. Sirius and Rigel; 133; 200; 030. Four jets, 12-second ullage. Remark 1: burn undocked; 2: no DOI assumed; 3: landing site REFSMMAT; 4: LOI REFSMMAT attitude 180, 220, 338. Over.

a17_0845929.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0845929.text: America, Houston. If you give us Accept, we'll pop up a state vector - a preliminary state vector and a Verb 66, preliminary target load, and an LOI REFSMMAT. Over.

a17_0845929.speaker: Cernan
a17_0845929.text: Okay, Houston. This is America. How do you read the commander on biomed?

a17_0845929.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0845929.text: Stand by. I'll take a look here.

a17_0850244.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0850244.text: America, Houston. Looking at the O 2 pressures, we think maybe Tank 3 Isol Valve got jarred closed. Would you check the barber pole over on panel 278. If it's barber pole, would you reopen the valve?

a17_0850244.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0850244.text: Gordy, we checked that. I'll check it again. We checked it right after the jett. [Long pause.]

a17_0850244.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0850244.text: And, Gordy, it's gray. Would you like me to cycle it? [Pause.]

a17_0850244.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0850244.text: That's affirmative, Jack. Go ahead and cycle it Open.

a17_0850244.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0850244.text: America, Houston. It's your computer. You can go back to Block. [Pause.]

a17_0850244.speaker: Evans
a17_0850244.text: Okay, we're back to Block. In the Delta-V test, I got a minus 22.0, and I'm on a bias check right now.

a17_0850637.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0850637.text: America, Houston. The biomed looks good on all three of you. [Pause.]

a17_0850637.speaker: Evans
a17_0850637.text: And the null bias check, on a plus 100, it went to 100.4. I'm working on a minus now.

a17_0850637.speaker: Evans
a17_0850637.text: Okay. The minus 100, it ended up minus 99.5.

a17_0851038.speaker: Evans
a17_0851038.text: Gordy, the Emergency Cabin Pressure Regs are Off.

a17_0851038.speaker: Evans
a17_0851038.text: Okay, Equalization valve in the tunnel has come Open. [Pause.]

a17_0851311.speaker: Cernan
a17_0851311.text: Okay, Gordy, the LM Tunnel valve is in LM Press, and Equalization valve is Closed.

a17_0851311.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0851311.text: Roger. And was it a 0.6 Delta-P when you started this, as before?

a17_0851311.speaker: Cernan
a17_0851311.text: That's affirm. It was 0.6 and now it's down to - we been seeing it as about 0.1.

a17_0851311.speaker: Cernan
a17_0851311.text: And, Gordy, I've got the Emergency Cabin Pressure Regs back to Both.

a17_0851745.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0851745.text: Okay, Gordy, we're changing mags on the - the EL camera, and mag November November is being stowed with 59 frames on it - or 59 frames used - 159.

a17_0851745.speaker: Cernan
a17_0851745.text: Gordy, you can record that as the second commander's P52, that came up all balls.

a17_0851745.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0851745.text: Okay, we'll get a hard copy. [Long pause.]

a17_0851745.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0851745.text: Okay, we got the 93s; you're clear to torque.

a17_0853735.speaker: Cernan
a17_0853735.text: Okay, Gordo, there's the gyro torque angles.

a17_0853735.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0853735.text: Okay, we're copying them down. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0855031.text: This is Apollo Control; 85 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Here in the Control Center, the Flights Dynamics Officer Jay Greene, just passed up to the Flight Director Neil Hutchinson the latest predicted figures for the S-IVB impact. Present predictions on time are for the S-IVB to impact at Ground Elapsed Time of 89 hours, 39 minutes, 43.4 seconds. a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: America, Houston. America, Houston. We've lost the High Gain and data. Go on Omni Alpha. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Hello America, Houston in the blind. Go Omni Alpha [garble]. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: America, this is Houston. How do you copy?

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Clear, and we're Omni Alpha. If you don't answer this transmission, we'll try the High Gain again.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Jack. We're reading you now. I heard you say Omni Alpha. Say again the first part.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Roger. We've been reading you. I think you're on VHF, however. Would you like us to reacquire on the High Gain?

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Stand by. I'll check on that. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Jack. We'd like you to try the High Gain at a Pitch of minus 29, Yaw 17, Manual and Wide. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Gordy, we're on the High Gain.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Jack.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: How do you read?

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: I'm reading you - I can read you, but there's still a lot of background noise. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Like VHF would sound, but I'm not sure I believe it. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Jack, we just commanded Normal voice. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Gordy, did we end up somehow out of Normal voice?

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Jack, we'd like you to try a Normal acquisition. Go Auto and Narrow on the High Gain. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, that peaked it up, Auto and Narrow.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, you're loud and clear now.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Gordy. You said that you had to command Normal voice. Did we get a spurious command in there some way? [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, we had - we did all that ourselves to establish voice through Ascension; no problem. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Gordy. How did you reach us when you finally started calling?

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Jack, we didn't do anything to cause the problem there, we were up-linking through Madrid and downlinking through Ascension. Did you see anything onboard that could have caused the loss of lock?

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: No, sir. We had good signal strength. It wasn't peaked for the High Gain. It was more like an Omni signal strength, about 70 per cent. And we called you several times after the switch in lines, and then finally you came through clear, but with some background noise and sounded like VHF. I presume it wasn't, now. And when you called, I went to Omni Alpha, with no change in signal strength, still about 70 per cent, and you were still coming up the same way and apparently didn't hear us. And then the High Gain - with High Gain acquisition, it's been pretty clear.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, that's the way - that story's the way it sounded to us. And we're looking around here to see if we can figure out a reason for our loss there.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, and I'm ready to pressurize the SPS, if that's what you want.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, let me make sure here. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Jack. We're ready for it. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, you want me to just use SPS Helium Valve 1? [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, Gordy. We're going to On with SPS Helium Valve 1. We checked the circuit breakers, they're In.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Okay.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay, pressure's com - pressure's up; Fuel Pressure is stable at 175 and Oxidizer at 175, and the light is out. And we're back to Normal on Caution And Warning. And the Valve now is back to Auto.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Roger. And looks - it looks good here. We're reading 184 oxidizer and 185 fuel. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Hey, Gordy, this is the LMP. I got a question for you.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Shoot. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: I'm just wondering if - I'm showing about 85 amps, and is that a good normal power load with - I presume the O 2 Heaters are On now.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Just a second, we'll check that. [Pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: I'm just trying to reestablish my references here for LOI.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: EECOM says the Heaters are On and that's the normal load.

a17_0861215.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0861215.text: Okay. Very good. Thank you, sir.

a17_0861215.speaker: Evans
a17_0861215.text: Houston, 17.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Go ahead.

a17_0861215.speaker: Evans
a17_0861215.text: Roger. We got about an hour sitting around here. We can go to wide deadband, if you want, if you'll remind me to go back to narrow again when we need to.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Let me check on that. [Long pause.]

a17_0861215.speaker: Evans
a17_0861215.text: Might save a teacupful of fuel.

a17_0861215.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0861215.text: Ron, we suggest just staying where you are on the deadband; there's no problem on fuel.

a17_0861215.speaker: Evans
a17_0861215.text: Okay. Mighty fine, Gordo. Thank you.

a17_0862742.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0862742.text: America, Hou - Houston. We just finished a site handover. And we're seeing some excessive counts on the UV. We'd like to chase the problem a little, and to do that, we'd like you to turn the UV Off for 5 seconds and then back On. Over.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: Hello, Houston, I've got the limb of the Moon.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: Got the limb of the Moon out the - got it out the center hatch and we're just barely seeing a - barely seeing the horizon of the Moon. But, boy, is it big.

a17_0864630.speaker: Evans
a17_0864630.text: Well, that must be a - what - you know, talk about a sliver of the Moon, that is a sliver of a sliver.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: Gordo, we're coming in right down on top of it. What's our perigee, did you say? 53 miles?

a17_0864630.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0864630.text: Roger, that's about right. Don't worry. You'll miss it.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: I just want to hear you say it because I'm going to hold you to it. [Long pause.]

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: As long as you shadow your eyes from the Sun - the Sun is just about laying on the horizon of the Moon, and as a matter of fact, as I watch it, I can watch the horizon - the amount of - of daylight terminator get larger.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: Gordy, unless I get proven wrong here, I think we'll be able to watch it all the way in as long as we can keep shadowed from the Sun.

a17_0864630.speaker: Cernan
a17_0864630.text: I'll tell you, when you get out here, it's a big mamou.

a17_0865201.speaker: Cernan
a17_0865201.text: Gordy, it's a - it's a sight to remember. Not just because of the uniqueness of the view, but because we all got to ask ourselves if we really know where we are and what we're really looking at right this moment, and when you answer that question is yes, it certainly becomes an epic sight in your mind.

a17_0865201.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0865201.text: My congratulations to the trench for solving another rendezvous - rendezvous problem.

a17_0865201.speaker: Cernan
a17_0865201.text: Gordy, can you tell us how far we are right now from the - from the Moon?

a17_0865201.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0865201.text: Sure we can; stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0865201.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0865201.text: Right now, you're about 5,000 miles [9,200 km] from the surface. [Pause.]

a17_0865201.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0865201.text: I think I got a visual on the SIM bay door now out window 5. It's just about directly off our present plus-Y axis.

a17_0865201.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0865201.text: Okay. Must be way out there by now. [Pause.]

a17_0865201.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0865201.text: Oh, yeah. It's a long way out there; just flashing.

a17_0865731.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0865731.text: Gordy, what's the MOCR having for dinner Sun - this Sunday? [Pause.]

a17_0865731.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0865731.text: Well, let's see. I guess we haven't sent out for hamburgers, yet. There's a few brown bags in sight, but that's about it. [Pause.]

a17_0865731.speaker: Cernan
a17_0865731.text: Gordy, it doesn't look like I had a chance to go to church today, but under the circumstances I guess it'll be okay. Next time you see the good Father you might have him put a good word in for us.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Gordy, is - in our present attitude I'm seeing the lip of the Moon convex down toward our minus-X axis. That's out of the hatch window. Can you tell me which is the north and which is the south pole?

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Okay. Stand by.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Yeah, I'd be all squared away if - if the Moon were on Jack's side, because he's got that end on his head, but I'm a little mixed up now.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Roger. I understand your problem. [Long pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Gordy, I - I'm thinking the - the top of the - the LM towards the Sun is probably the north. [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Hello, Gordy. I - I think I got it. Window - the - the north has got to be on the right as I look at the limb of the Moon opposite the Sun. Because when we go into retrograde attitude, it's got to be over there. I think I can see Korolev without any problem. It's a little bit north of the - of the equator.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Gordy, are you still with us?

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: That's affirm. I'm with you, and I'm getting lots of advice here.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Okay. Okay. I'll bet you are. But I - I think I got it oriented. You can literally watch yourself fall down in. As we get closer, if we're going to have a view like this, it's going to be pretty dramatic. Because, recalling the way you climb on out of the Moon when you leave it, if you can see. And I can remember remarks at that time, "Gee, if we could see it like this when we came back in, we'd have to close our eyes." If we can see this thing coming in like I think we may be able to see it at 50 miles, it isn't going to look like very much. [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Rog. We agree.

a17_0870756.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0870756.text: And we're even considering the win - putting - Gordy, we're consider - Gordy, we're considering putting the window covers up. [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: You're chickens, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: It's going to be one of those high - high - angle energy conversion roundouts.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Rog. From our information here, if you're looking at the Moon so that the - the dark limb is up, then north should be to the right.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Yeah. I - I concur, and that's the way it is.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Roger.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: The horizon is just steadily growing bigger.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Does it look about the same as last time? [Pause.]

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: What do you mean, 'last time?' Couple years ago?

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Right.

a17_0870756.speaker: Cernan
a17_0870756.text: Gordy, we never saw it coming in a couple years ago. We saw it, as I recall, a day out, and we saw just a - a shadow of the limb. But we - to my best re - recollection, we never saw it this close. As a matter of fact, we went into darkness prior to going into LOI, and this time, much to my amazement, we don't. But I see now that we won't, and I see why. I'll tell you, everyone who's seen that view leaving knows how fast you climb out. And by golly, the closer we get to it, the faster we're coming in.

a17_0870756.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0870756.text: Rog.

a17_0870756.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0870756.text: 087:16:11 - This is Apollo Control at 87 hours, 16 minutes Ground Elapsed Time in the mission of Apollo 17. Some 1 hour and 38 minutes until ignition on Lunar Orbit Insertion. Presently, the spacecraft is 4,243 nautical miles [7,858 km] away from the Moon. The Moon is getting larger, as noted by the crew. They considered closing the window shades in the spacecraft. Velocity's now 4,544 feet per second [1,385 m/s]. Some numbers on acquisition of the spacecraft. With the burn - a normal burn, the acquisition on the east limb of the Moon would be at 89 hours, 16 minutes, 29 seconds. Without a bur

a17_0871611.text: This is Apollo Control at 87 hours, 16 minutes Ground Elapsed Time in the mission of Apollo 17. Some 1 hour and 38 minutes until ignition on Lunar Orbit Insertion. Presently, the spacecraft is 4,243 nautical miles [7,858 km] away from the Moon. The Moon is getting larger, as noted by the crew. They considered closing the window shades in the spacecraft. Velocity's now 4,544 feet per second [1,385 m/s]. Some numbers on acquisition of the spacecraft. With the burn - a normal burn, the acquisition on the east limb of the Moon would be at 89 hours, 16 minutes, 29 seconds. Without a burn, it would

a17_0871611.speaker: Cernan
a17_0871611.text: Gordo. The - the widest-most part of the convex horizon probably covers a good couple of degrees. I can now see relief on the - on the horizon itself against the dark space.

a17_0871611.speaker: Cernan
a17_0871611.text: And the rim of Korolev is readily visible standing out by itself in the - in the darker or the unlit part of the - of the Moon. I can see the central peaks or mountains very well lit up. [Long pause.]

a17_0871611.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0871611.text: Okay, Gordy. This is Jack. Is there any reason not to start the checks at about 87:43?

a17_0871611.speaker: Cernan
a17_0871611.text: Okay, Gordy. What I - what I called a - a central peak or range in there must undoubtedly be that inner ring, but it - the way it was lit up in the sunlight gave you a definite impression that it had an enlongated central range.

a17_0871611.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0871611.text: Roger. And for Jack, no problem starting early on the checks.

a17_0872336.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0872336.text: [Garble], Houston. Going to [garble] put the UV Cover Open. How long?

a17_0872336.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0872336.text: Okay, Jack. And we'd like 5 minutes of operation with it Open.

a17_0872540.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0872540.text: Okay, Houston; 17. I've started the secondary glycol pump, and I neglected to make a check on evap OP temperature. Do you have that, and did we get a decrease?

a17_0872540.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0872540.text: Stand by. [Pause.] That looks okay, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0872813.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0872813.text: And you're looking at the torquing angle. [Long pause.]

a17_0872813.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0872813.text: Okay, Houston. I'm going SPS Pressure Indicator to 2.

a17_0872813.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0872813.text: Okay, Jack. And you can close the UV cover, and go ahead and roll back to 064 Roll. And you're clear to torque the P52.

a17_0872813.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0872813.text: Okay, Houston. Going back to SPS Pressure Indicator 1.

a17_0873231.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0873231.text: America, Houston. We - we still see the UV door open. Have you closed it yet? [Long pause.]

a17_0873231.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0873231.text: America, Houston. I have the LOI and map update PADs when you're ready.

a17_0873459.speaker: Cernan
a17_0873459.text: Okay, Gordy. What do you have, a map update on page 3-83 of the Flight Plan?

a17_0873459.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0873459.text: Okay. It's for rev 1. AOS [Acquisition Of Signal] without burn is 089:07:46; with the burn is 089:16:29. [Pause.]

a17_0873459.speaker: Cernan
a17_0873459.text: Okay. Without the burn is 07:46, and with the burn is 16:29.

a17_0873459.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0873459.text: That's affirmative, and then I have your LOI maneuver PAD. [Pause.]

a17_0873459.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0873459.text: Okay. LOI, SPS/G&N; the weight is 66361; plus 1.21, minus 0.12; ignition time is 088:54:21.74; Noun 81, minus 2798.8, plus 1044.9, minus 0042.5; roll, pitch, and yaw are all zero; Noun 44, 0170.1, plus 0052.5; 2987.7, burn time is 6:38, 2981.4; sextant star is 45, 252.1, 13.5; rest of the PAD is NA. GDC Align stars are Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. Ullage is none. Remarks: LM weight, 36312; single-bank burn time is 6:51. Over. Stand by on the readback. Okay. We'll take Accept, and give you the up-links while you're reading it back.

a17_0873459.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0873459.text: Okay, Gordy. Here's your readback. You've got Accept. It's LOI PAD, SPS/G&N; 66361; plus 1.21, minus 0.12; 088:54:21.74; minus 2798.8, plus 1044.9, minus 0042.5; 000, 000, 000; 0170.1, plus 0052.5; 2987.7, 6:38, 2981.4; 45, 252.1, 13.5; rest of PAD is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 122; 354; 000. There's no ullage. LM weight, 36312; single-bank burn time, 6 plus 51.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: It's your computer, America. You have a state vector, a Verb 66, and a target load. Go back to Block.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Okay. It's in Block, Gordy. We're finishing up on the bottom of 3-79.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Okay.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: And back at this roll attitude, I've got the big old Moon again, and from where I sit, it looks like we're right on target. Fifty miles above target, I'd like to add.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Okay. That sounds good. [Pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: The limb is, of course, still growing and a little more rapidly. And what I can see of the - of the limb that's not blocked out by the Sun, it's getting obviously much larger in the window.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Roger.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Now I guess it depends on the shadowing of the Sun as to whether or not we're going to see too much. I think retrograde, we ought to see quite a bit once we get over the terminator. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Gordy, there's enough of the lighted portion of the Moon where you can see the relief - not just a shadowing relief, but the actual relief of several craters as they stretch across the terminator, both to the north and to the south. I can see even more definite relief now on the horizon, just to the north and behind Korolev - on the black horizon against space.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Roger.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: The - the unlit part of the Moon, as you might expect, is just as dark from here as is deep space itself.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Roger.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: It's black, I might say at this point. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: America, Houston. For your information, your altitude is about 3,000 [nautical] miles [5,500 km] now. [Pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Okay, 3,000 miles. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Gordy, the - the limb has much more three-dimensional relief now. Towards us, you can - you can get the feeling that the horizon - the lighted portion of the horizon definitely does flow in our direction. And although you can't see the unlit portion of the Moon, you get a feeling that there's a great deal more of it a lot closer than that which you can see.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Roger.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Okay, Gordy. The pre-SPS burn sim prep is complete.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: And I'm going to give my buddies a chance to look at it now.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: I never thought I'd see a geologist speechless at his first near - near shot at the Moon, but I haven't heard a word from him yet.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Rog.

a17_0874106.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0874106.text: This geologist turned engineer for about an hour. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: He's probably speechless because there's no clouds to talk about. [Long pause.]

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Gordo, everything's looking good onboard. We're just waiting for about 88:05. We'll be in our maneuver at that time.

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: Okay. Everything looks good here also.

a17_0874106.speaker: Cernan
a17_0874106.text: Okay. [Pause.] And is your LOS of about 45 still good?

a17_0874106.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0874106.text: I'll doublecheck that.

a17_0875013.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0875013.text: America, the Flight Plan is correct on LOS. To be exact, it will be 88:43:40.

a17_0875013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875013.text: If - if you guys could get an idea down there of the needle you're threading when you shoot for 50 miles at a quarter of million, you'd be mighty proud of yourselves, I'll tell you, we are.

a17_0875013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875013.text: I guess I really ought to wait and tell you that at 89:16:29.

a17_0875013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875013.text: Say, Gordy. Do you have any idea what our relative speed is to the - to the Moon at this time?

a17_0875013.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0875013.text: Yes. It's 5,000 feet per second [1,500 m/s]. You're presently 2,660 [nautical] miles [4,930 km] up. [Pause.]

a17_0875013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875013.text: I assume T. P. is there, and - and I guess John is, too. I don't know if John saw this coming in on 16, but I know they can recall what we saw leaving on 10. And other than the fact that you can't see as much of the Moon, it's just as impressive.

a17_0875013.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0875013.text: Rog. I was just talking to John about it a couple of minutes ago. Their view on 16 was - they didn't have any sunlit Moon, but they did have some pretty good Earthshine. [Pause.]

a17_0875013.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875013.text: Well, he - he knows what I'm talking about then.

a17_0875659.speaker: Cernan
a17_0875659.text: Gordy, it's an unbelievable view through the monocular now. You can really see down in the depths of some of the larger craters and with a great deal of clarity. And you can see the - some of the higher ridges actually rolling right over the horizon as they go away from you.

a17_0880531.speaker: Cernan
a17_0880531.text: Hey, Houston. As much as I hate to, I think we're going to have to maneuver out of this attitude.

a17_0880531.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0880531.text: Rog. As you take your last look there, you're presently 20 - just a little over 2,000 [nautical] miles [3,700 km] up, and you're coming down about 4,500 feet per second [1,400 m/s]. [Pause.]

a17_0880932.speaker: Cernan
a17_0880932.text: Gordo, there's only one better view than this.

a17_0880932.speaker: Cernan
a17_0880932.text: Right at the moment anyway. Right at the moment anyway, is to be out there and watching this spacecraft maneuver in attitude and - and watch it burn over the lunar surface. I get the feeling someone is watching.

a17_0881324.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0881324.text: Apollo 17, Houston. We just had a site handover. That's resulted in the LOS time changing 19 seconds. It's now 43:21. [Pause.]

a17_0881324.speaker: Cernan
a17_0881324.text: Okay; 43:21, and we are - we're on Omni Charlie,

a17_0881324.speaker: Cernan
a17_0881324.text: And just to round out things as we pitch back into LOI attitude, lo and behold from over the top of the LM came the Earth.

a17_0881324.speaker: Cernan
