a17_0892610.text: Roger. It's in Normal.

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: [Garble].

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: Looking out over that way. [Garble]. Right here.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Macrobius, Macrobius, my friend.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: No, it's Microbus [sic].

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay, I'm loaded up for your terminator, Ron. What's - is it not out of 105, or what? Is it - Okay, 80-millimeter or...

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: [Garble] Millimeter [garble] f/11 at 1/500 [garble]

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: 80-millimeter.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Five frames over the terminator, huh?

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: 12 frames.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: 12 frames. Very good. How soon do I start?

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Well, about...

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay, about 5 minutes, all right.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Gordy, you'd be interested - there's a crater that just on - on the west rim of Crisium. Relatively fresh rim - fairly crisp rim - but no strong ray pattern. There's no ray pattern apparent at all. It looks like it's pre the plains material around it - that - since they come right up over the - right up to the edge of the crater in one spot.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: There's Posidonius right here. [Garble].

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: That is Posidonius.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: Just at the terminator.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: That's right. That's what I'm looking at.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: Jack, do you want to start [garble]?

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Not Posidonius, Proclus. That's what I'm describing. You know I - You're looking where?

a17_0892610.speaker: SC
a17_0892610.text: [Camera shutter and wind-on.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Only recognise 41.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Infamous Proclus. [Pause.] Okay, you give me a mark when I'm - Hey, look at the...

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Okay, I'll give you a mark, Jack.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: At the Cauchy Rilles here. Man, is that neat.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: See that... [Camera shutter and wind-on.] [Garble].

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Let me see. [Pause.] Going to have to...

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: One right there with the shadowed peak in there. Right?

a17_0892610.speaker: SC (faintly)
a17_0892610.text: You got a [garble]. [Pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Yeah, yep, yep. Yep, yep. [Pause.] And that's out of this window, huh? I'm not - sure I'm seeing it yet.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Manischewitz! Look at those terminators.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Shadows.

a17_0892610.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0892610.text: 089:38:44 - One minute Mark to the S-IVB impact.
One minute Mark to the S-IVB impact.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: There's the mare domes for the central craters. They're certainly obvious. In - northern part of - Let's see...

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: The lineations that trend to the northwest through this entire - entire section - they go through the... [camera shutter and wind-on] mostly through the highlands.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Well, I...

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: I can get the pictures. Is it directly out of window 5? Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: We've got about another minute and a half. I'm going to proceed here at 41.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: It'll be right underneath the groundtrack. It's right under it.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Well, that's the way we're going. I'm taking them east-west.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Okay. I [garble]

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: O - yes. [Pause.] Okay.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Hey, Jack, we're at - coming up on 40. [Long pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0892610.text: 089:40:03 - We had Loss of Signal right on-time with the Instrument Unit of the Saturn IVB which...
We had Loss of Signal right on-time with the Instrument Unit of the Saturn IVB which...

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: [Garble] about a minute to PRO on P20.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Yes. We're at 40 - Okay, I'm with you, Gordo. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: SC
a17_0892610.text: [Camera shutter and wind-on.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0892610.text: 089:40:27 - Seismic signals beginning to come in.
Seismic signals beginning to come in.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Okay, you got it. [Pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Don't forget to Pro, Ron; you've got - you got 8 seconds.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Mark it - 41. Okay, I guess you can.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Goes. With the usual FAO flight planning, that was a good time.

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: Roger.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Hey, you can even see horizon in the - Earthshine out there.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Boy, you sure can. You can see an Earthlit horizon out there into the dark part of the Moon.

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Can you see the landing site? I think it's going to be in the darkness.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: You know, I - it - The shadows are so contrasting here, Ron, that I... [Pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Give me that thing a minute. [Long pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: [Posi]donius. There's le Monnier, the landing site. I can't...

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: No, it's just - it's just dark.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Isn't it a little north of track?

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: No, I think it's right below us, Jack. I think it's right smack below us.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: In darkness...

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Yeah, I yeah, it is. I can't - I think I'm looking at Littrow right there, right below us, [camera shutter and wind-on] but I can't quite tell.

a17_0892610.speaker: SC
a17_0892610.text: [Camera shutter and wind-on.]

a17_0892610.speaker: SC
a17_0892610.text: [Camera shutter and wind-on.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: If I could see Vitruvius, I'd have a better handle on it. [Camera shutter and wind-on.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: A reminder to go to f/4 and 1/250 on the last six pictures.

a17_0892610.speaker: Cernan
a17_0892610.text: Roger. That's Posidonius all right, le Monnier; we're here early.

a17_0892610.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0892610.text: Boy, I tell you, there's no question that right at the terminator you - you pick up relief that you normally would not believe is there in the mare. I remember Bill Anders talking about the appearance of a sea swell within the mare itself and that's certainly clearly shown right at the terminator. Plus you start to see the shadows from all the very small craters that otherwise don't show up as much more that just little depressions, if that.

a17_0892610.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0892610.text: Okay. We need Accept so we can give you a landing site REFSMMAT. [Pause.]

a17_0892610.speaker: Evans
a17_0892610.text: Okay, you have it.

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Yep. [Camera shutter and wind-on, twice.] Okay, I think that'll do her. Okay, Houston. I cheated. I took three extra pictures, and those were at 2.8 and a 250th at the end.

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: And [pause] your - actually your times might have been a little off, because I was just about ready to lose the terminator because of the maneuver - we maneuvering or have we? Yeah. But, I think we got a good set going up to the terminator.

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Plus a couple of shots - a few shots on the CEX mag Quebec Que - No, mag Kilo Kilo as we came around the Moon and that number's now on 20. Kilo Kilo is 20, and Quebec Quebec is 42.

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: Okay, we need the IR, On, now.

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: It's your computer; the uplink's in there, and you can go back to Block.

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Yep, enough - enough tourist activity. [Long pause.]

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Warm in here, isn't it? [Long pause.]

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: America, a couple of items. Would you verify the S-Band Aux TV switch is in the Science position? And one other thing, we think you were in Low Bit Rate during the burn. [Pause.]

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Okay, it's in Science and we very definitely were in High Bit Rate during the burn by the checklist.

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: Roger. We may have a problem there because it looks like Low to us on the data. We'll check further. [Long pause.]

a17_0894352.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0894352.text: Hey, Gordy, there was - Ron questioned - brought up the question or possibility of not having gone to Command Reset; but, just before we left you, you'll probably be able to see that I went Command Reset and turned on the tape, because I remember seeing the tape motion.

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: Okay, Jack. We're discussing it - what happened there.

a17_0894352.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0894352.text: America, you can go back to Block.

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read 17?

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay. Before we really got concentrating on the burn, and I had an opportunity to - we all had an opportunity to look at Korolev, at a very low grazing Sun, one of the striking things was the - to me was the extreme absence of relief, the very smooth surface that existed in Korolev, independent, of course, of the craters that are penetrating that surface. And it looked like there was a ring in the floor - outsi - next to the wall, about maybe sixth of a crater radius, that was somewhat brighter at the low grazing Sun, suggesting it may have had a different slope. And I believe I'm correct in s

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: Okay; understand. One quick word from FAO's...

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: ...film watchers here, has to do with optional photographs. We'd rather you take the optional photographs on either OO or PP and reserve KK for the scheduled photographs. And, as it stands now, we've got to reserve 80 frames on either OO or PP for scheduled photography. Over.

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay, you have to keep track of that. We need - I was hoping we had an optional capability on our first rev, and we'll work it out.

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: We do. We just want to put them on OO.

a17_0895152.speaker: Evans
a17_0895152.text: That's right; just stick them on OO. [Long pause.]

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: Jack, the problem on the high and low bit rate there was a synchronization problem between you on the burn checklist and us on the ground on our pre-LOS command. No hardware problems, and I don't think it will be a problem in the future.

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay. But you did lose the high bit rate. is that correct?

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: That's affirmative. We just had low bit rate during the burn. [Pause.]

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay. I may have jumped the gun on you there a little bit. But I thought we were supposed to do that just before we went AOS - LOS. I think I did it about a minute before.

a17_0895152.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895152.text: Okay. It was almost identi - simultaneous with our sending the command. You've got about 4 minutes to start looking at Copernicus coming here.

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay. Thank you. We're just - Sun's just setting. [Long pause.]

a17_0895152.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895152.text: Okay, I have a visual on Copernicus.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: And by the way, the S-IVB crunched in on time, and it's been ringing the ALSEP seismometers like mad for some time now. [Long pause.]

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: VOX, and that's VOX. How do you read the LMP, Gordy?

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Loud and clear, Jack.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Thank you. Okay, good. All right, I've got a visual on Eratosthenes and Copernicus. The - they're obviously different-age craters in this light. You can see the ray patterns in Copernicus moderately well. You can even tell that they do cross Eratosthenes. Stadius shows up as a very clear dark area to the southwest of Eratosthenes. Now, one of the things that we mapped on the southeast and south rim of Copernicus were dark albedo areas within the ejecta. And those are apparent here, very clearly. And also, within - on the upper portion of the rim and on the benches, in that quadrant. The walls

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Roger, Jack.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: This is in the southeast - southeast quadrant I'm referring to. Copernicus H is also very obvious as a dark-rimmed crater, relative to the albedo of the ejecta blanket. And the northwest quadrant, which we mapped as a smooth floor material and somewhat darker albedo, is just as apparent here, although all the contrasts, of course, are less. [Pause.] The main thing that you can pick out in Earthshine are albedo distinctions. Now - now we - we - I remember that we also, at one time - and I can't remember whether it made the final map or not - mapped an arcuate fault structure, based on the chang

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Roger.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: There is a general streaking - radial streaking - within that arcuate dark area that radiates radially from the crater, and if I had to project, the dark area would - north - whose northeast terminus is the arc in the crater, I'd project it off to southeast about crater diameter and a half, maybe. [Pause.] Now there's - I'm getting - essentially directly overhead, and again the dark spots within the crater wall are still apparent, and the streaming or the radial elongation of these spots is clear. Now, on the lower wall - that's below the first bench - I can see four of these dark areas, and o

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Okay...

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: In the middle of the...

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: ...Can you see anything of the - that stuff we were wondering about in the central peaks?

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: No, Gordy, I can't. The - there's very little indication of relief in Earthshine and particularly at this high Sun ang - high Earth angle, pardon the expression.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Roger.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: The central peaks, they do stand out, though, as a much lighter albedo area within the crater. It looks to me like the best thing you can do in Earthshine is work with albedos. Knowing the general topography from the - from the pre - earlier photography. We're coming up on Kepler now. Copernicus is out of my view in window 5 - Maybe Ron sees it. Do you, Ron?

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: No, it's out of my view now, too.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Okay, we, we...

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: Can you see Reinhold over there?

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Reinhold, I was not conscious - Yes, I can see Reinhold. Reinhold is one of the craters just like Copernicus that may have contributed ejecta into the Apollo 12 soil. Do you see anything...

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: An S - an S-IVB - 16's S-IVB hit out there to the south, I think.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Well, I don't...

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: No, I don't think you'd see it.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: I don't see anything that would indicate that. Reinhold is an Eratosthenian Age crater, as you may recall. It's crossed, very obviously even in this light, by the Copernican rays, which is prime - the main way we determine the age, other than it doesn't have any rays itself. Although, on the good photography we now have, we know it has secondary crater patterns around it.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: You're not looking at the same crater I am then.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Reinhold is right down here, Geno.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: Where are you looking [garble]?

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Well, it's south of Copernicus.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: Okay, I'm looking up here.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: South and a little west.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: I don't have the same view you have.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Okay, I can see Lansberg now. And I'm afraid I can't shed any light, pardon the expression, on the old question we've had about the age of Lansberg relative to the mare.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Okay.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Kepler ray pattern is very striking in this light, An anastomoting - mosing series of - of bands which only average being radial. In most cases, they're a little off radial, but by joining together, they give you a general radial pattern.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: I just wanted to see a...

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Okay. Out the window 4, I have an excellent view of Kepler. Once again, albedo differences, such as the - are very clear - such as the distinction between the wall - light - or brighter wall materials and the rim which, in itself, is brighter than the surrounding mare. We can look right down some of the rays, and the rays are not completely linear. I'm looking now to the northwest. Gene, you can see Aristarchus way up there in the northwest. See it?

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: Yeah. It's coming into [garble].

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: You ought to have a good view of Aristarchus. Very bright, up in the northwest part of our field of view.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: The inside of that crater almost looks as if it's backlit.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: That's right. Well, it should be [chuckle]. Strangely enough.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: And - but I want - these rays when contrast to the - maybe the feeling one would have that they are - once they get started, they form a linear pattern across the surface. They don't seem to have done that. As a matter of fact, they're quite strikingly curved along their pattern. They'll break from the general radius they're out on, curve away and then curve back. Some - all - let's see, there are one - one, two, three, four - four rays that go from out - to the northwest of Kepler, all of which show that nonlinear characteristic.

a17_0895705.speaker: Cernan
a17_0895705.text: Yeah, they're all radial, though.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: They are radial, in general. But when you look at them in detail, only portions of them are radial. And a single ray, which you can follow continuously, will bend and then curve back.

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: The - it's unique. We've got rays from - I guess those must be Copernicus over here - those long ones out to the right, which you might not be able to see. Kepler and Reiner are all - all intermingling up here.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Yeah, this is the area now we're going over where the gamma-ray work on 15 indicated a relatively high radioactivity. And - not yet, it's...

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: Houston, America here. Do you see the torquing angles?

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: I was going to look for the Hortensius domes near Copernicus, but got sidetracked with Kepler and missed them.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Okay, [garble] torquing angles, Ron.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: They are not obvious, though, in looking in the general direction...

a17_0895705.speaker: Evans
a17_0895705.text: Okay, I'll torque it to 8:45.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Roger.

a17_0895705.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0895705.text: Okay, we're getting out into Procellarum - Oceanus Procellarum proper now and, before long, should pick up the medial ridge that makes that mare so distinctive from the other mare. Actually, the ridge, it stretches something like 2,000 kilometers north to south, if you want to tie a vari - a number of things together. And, probably is the lun - the Moon's closest analogy to an oceanic ridge, which has - which have been in the news over the last decade.

a17_0895705.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0895705.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Once again, the topography of the Procellarum mare is not clear in this light. It's just not quite enough light to give you a strong, distinct shadow, at least not yet at this Earth angle.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay. And as you get the camera set up for the orbital science pictures of Galois would want to change and use magazine OO instead of KK. That's listed in the Flight Plan at 90:20.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Okay, we'll - we'll do that. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Okay I'm - out of the window 4, I'm able to see some of the Reiner Gamma materials, and it's - awful hard to say more than just the fact there is a very clear light-colored pattern off to the north - of our position at any rate. I think all I can say is that I've seen it. I can't give you much information on it.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: We can see the area where Marius Hills should be, although it's not an obvious topographic feature in this light. Still see Aristarchus off up there shining like a star, if the Moon could have stars.

a17_0900950.speaker: Evans
a17_0900950.text: Okay, Houston. I'm going to torque those cos - coarse align errors out at 1, 2.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: And...

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: You squared away?

a17_0900950.speaker: Evans
a17_0900950.text: It's good to be able to see some stars out of the telescope. It's the first time I've been able to see any.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Gordy, we have a - a very clear zero phase point for the Earthlight. It's certainly not a strong contrast for the Sun, but it's out there. And within it, again, the fresh craters tend to brighten - quite a bit more than the surrounding mare. Still looking at Oceanus Procellarum. And now, out window 3, up to the northwest, Grimaldi is starting to show up - a very obvious dark area within the highlands of that part of the Moon - and one of the darkest mare regions that we have seen on the - on the Moon. It's comparable, at least in the photographs, to that of Tsiolkovsky.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Normally, of course, we think of the dark mare as being the younger basalt flows that - on the Moon, but in our case, of course, young means something on the order of 3 billion years or older.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: For our interp - If we can extrapolate from the samples returned by other missions. [Long pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Amazing how far over - now the highlands to the west of Procellarum are - still are bright, and the contrast between fresh craters and the normal highland are very - are very obvious still in Earthlight, particularly along the zero phase point with respect to the Earth. Reiner Gamma now is - is coming a little bit closer to our orbit track. In the horseshoe - in the - larger and more western end of it; the dark horseshoe is quite clear in this light. It's a west - or northwest-pointing horseshoe, as is the complete trend of that strange feature. I think Ron is going to have an excellent chance

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okeydoke. [Long pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: Say, Gordo, something I just noticed here in working with the GDC what have you. I - looked at the PC gauge, and in the PZ - PC position, there is a continuous bias on it now of about, oh, 7 percent, and if I switch to ALPHA, it goes to zero. We never saw that bias before this last burn.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger, Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Hey, Gordy, I'm looking right up the western edge of the Procellarum mare where it contacts the - the high - western highlands of the Moon, and we're just about to fly a little bit south of Grimaldi. That edge is very irregular. There is no obvious indication that it - there are large basins that have been flooded by mare that have formed that edge, but, again, the topographic distinctions possible in this light are small. Now I'm starting to see that there are shadows in the craters.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: That's the small craters. [Pause.] There, in the Mare Procellarum closest to Grimaldi, there are two arcuate rilles. Looks like they're probably V-shaped in their cross section. I'm sure we've seen those on the photographs much better than I can see them here. Those - the rille patterns, though, do seem to project over into the highlands.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: To the north of that - to the north of that bay of mare. Just interrupt.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Hey, I just saw a flash on the lunar surface!

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Oh, yeah?

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: It was just out there north of Grimaldi. Just north of Grimaldi. You might see if you got anything on your seismometers, although a small impact probably would give a fair amount of visible light.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay. We'll check.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: It was a bright little flash right out there near that crater. See the crater right at the edge of Grimaldi. Then there is another one north of it. Fairly sharp one north of it is where there was just a pin prick of light.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: How about putting an X on the map where you saw it.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: I keep looking occasionally for... [listens to Fullerton] yeah, we will. I - I was planning on looking for those kind of things. Starting to see the edge of Orientale, Gordy. Way off to the west. [Pause.] Hey, just yell, Gene, anytime you... [Long pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Gordy, to the north of Grimaldi there's a large basin that is about the same size but only incompletely filled with mare in its northeastern quadrant. The rest of it looks like a fairly irregular and hummocky floor material of some kind.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: But it's almost the same size as Grimaldi. It even looks like it is a little bit deeper, but, of course, Grimaldi has considerable fill. Grimaldi on its eastern edge has some of the graben, or its rim, if you will, is cut by three or four anastomosing grabens that make it look like some of the bench areas in the larger basins. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Okay, the first ring of Orientale is showing up. The inner - the next ring in is extremely obvious; got some very bright east - east-facing slopes.

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: I'll turn off the intercom. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: It has some very bright east-facing slopes, and you can see the bands of mare that are filling the - both the first bench area and the inner bench. [Long pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Any time you need us, Gordy, just interrupt me.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay; we'll do that. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Now, as I look north along the first bench, that's the first bench from the outside, one inside the Cordillerian ring. I better check that; I may have my names mixed up. Got Orientale, there - handy? [garble] see. Should be on there. Yeah, this is what I need. What's the name - they got a name on that ridge, there? That's Rook Mountains. Yeah, the Cordillera. Yeah, that's right. Looking just west of the Cordillera on the first bench, as I look north, in this light, which is casting some shadows now, Gordy, over in here, it looks extremely smooth. Now this is not mare; it's lighter albedo, ligh

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: I won't try to give you a trend on the hummocks because I think the shadows are biasing my view; they do appear to be north-south trending, but I think that is because of the shadow patterns. This is a spectacular sight, you guys; you ought to take a look at Orientale. One of the largest fresh basins on the Moon. It still is probably 4 billion years old, or 3.8 at any rate, if our dating criteria are any - any good. It has the outer Cordillerian ring and the inner ring called the Rook Mountains - very, very nicely shown. There are massifs on that inner ring, the Rook Mountain ring; there are m

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: No. I didn't say anything.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Okay; I thought I heard your key. Okay; in the inner portion of Orientale, as we approach a terminator, the lighting is still excellent. Matter of fact, it appears brighter than what we were looking at over at Copernicus. Now, part of that may be we're seeing much sharper relief since the slope - Earth-facing slopes are nicely lit, and the backfacing slopes, of course, are in shadow. The first portion of the bench inside the Rook Mountains is partially filled by mare. Now, the higher land in there is very smooth - in a gross sense, is a very smooth hummocky terrain, cut by roughly circumferent

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: There are also some radial grabens; I just now picked one up, which we've also seen on the Orientale photographs taken by Lunar Orbiter. It's amazing how fresh appearing this basin looks, considering its great age. But it's - it probably is not - had any more violent a history than Imbrium. Now, we're getting up, just about to go over a delta-rim crater that's out in the basin. I don't remember the name of it offhand [Kopff]. But it's - be familiar to some of the geologists who have mapped this basin. It does not appear to have a strong impact ejecta blanket around it. It's filled with mare, a

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Roger.

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Delta-rim crater just as has been, I think, discussed in the literature, has just that, delta rim with no obvious ejecta blanket around it, compared to other larger craters within the basin. We're directly over that crater right now. It's filled with mare, very smooth mare. Matter of fact, within that fill, I can see no - no craters. [Pause.] Getting very close to the Earth terminator, but you see good texture in the ejecta blanket of the large crater [Maunder] in the north part of the inner basin of Orientale. The radial ridge and valley patterns are very clear; the concentric coarse hummocks

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: Better let him say something before AOS. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: I ain't got nothing to say.

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: Houston, I guess we're getting close to AOS. We're getting close to AOS. Do you have some words for us?

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay. We show about 9 minutes to LOS. We'd like to clarify one thing, and that was on this tape recorder commands and high and low bit rate. And we just want to make it clear that preburn the 6-minute callout is High Bit Rate, Record, Forward, Command Reset. Did you - did you tell us a few minutes ago that you did indeed do all those at about 6 minutes? [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Yeah, Gordy, I certainly thought I did, but I can't specifically - I know the High Bit Rate was there, because we switched to Low later. I can't - I'm afraid I can't specifically verify the Command Reset.

a17_0900950.speaker: Cernan
a17_0900950.text: Gordy, I can specifically say that when those - after the bus stars came on, we called that out. I'm almost sure Jack did get it, because I had him then check the helium valves and the nitrogen - helium and the nitrogen valves.

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: Okay. We're just trying to make sure if we - or to determine if we do have a switch problem. The INCO did send Low Bit Rate, Command, just prior to - to LOS there before LOI, which is the way it's called out in the Flight Plan. And then you should have come along later with a Command Reset, setting the switch to High Bit Rate, and the Command Reset switched into High Bit Rate mode, and for some reason it did not go into High Bit Rate. [Pause.]

a17_0900950.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0900950.text: Well, you want to test it out here, before we go around?

a17_0900950.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0900950.text: That's a pretty good thought. I think we will. On stand by. We'll give you - we'll figure out how we're going to do it here.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay, Jack. We just now commanded Low Bit Rate, and you're in Low Bit Rate. We'd like you now to select High and Command Reset. [Pause with pulsing noise on comm link.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. Gordy, you also have an oscillation in uplink signal strength and a clicking in the - in the audio. Do you read? We just went steady and at about 60 percent - 70 percent signal strength.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Roger. We hear that.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. I'm going to - you want me to go ahead and command High and Command Reset?

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: That's affirmative. The High Gain just went Wide Beam, but we're still reading you loud and clear. Go ahead in High Bit Rate and Command Reset.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. High Bit Rate; Command Reset. [Long pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay; it seems to have worked properly, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: ...after AOS...

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: We're going to do a Verb [garble].

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay, Gordy. I may not have got the Command Reset at 6 minutes. I - I - I just can't tell you right now.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay; I want to assure you it was no big problem as far as the burn goes. No great loss there. [Pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: I hope not. [Long pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: America, Houston. About 5 minutes to LOS now. We'd like to have you go ahead and get the jet inhibits and the covers open as shown in the Flight Plan so we can see that before we lose you. [Long pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: Okay. IR Cover, Open, and - Well, let's inhibit the jets.

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Oh. Two On. Go ahead.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay; Gordy. IR Cover is coming Open.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Mark it.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Roger.

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Going On.

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Okay. After AOS, Omni Delta.

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: Yes, and D-4. The ones with the arrows on them.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay; UV Cover coming Open...

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Mark it.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Bs are Off.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: And you want me to stay in High Bit Rate?

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: That's affirmative. You're there.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. We're there; we've got tape motion.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Gordy, the deadband - or the A/C - B/D, A/C roll has been changed, and you should have the proper jet configuration now.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay. We see it; it looks good, Geno.

a17_0903425.speaker: Cernan
a17_0903425.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: IR and the UV. Might as well open up the Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter, too.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay; if you're still with us, we're going to Open up the Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Okay, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. We're going to Extend the Mapping Camera. [Pause.]

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Roger on that.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Okay. Okay.

a17_0903425.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0903425.text: Mark. Barber pole.

a17_0903425.speaker: Fullerton
a17_0903425.text: Roger.

a17_0903425.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0903425.text: 090:40:03 - This is Apollo Control. We're estimating a change of shift briefing at 3:45 Houston time. One minute and 16 seconds away from Loss of Signal on this first lunar revolution. Participants in the Flight Director change of shift briefing will be Gerry Griffin who has been in charge of the Gold flight team, Dr. Royce Hawkins the Flight Surgeon, and Charlie Dumis the EECOM. At 90 hours, 40 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control.

a17_0903425.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0903425.text: 090:41:00 - This is Apollo Control at 90 hours, 41 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Will be up again in about 47 minutes or approximately. The tables are not up on the display here on the next Acquisition of Signal as to the next time the spacecraft comes around on the second lunar orbit.
