a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: Gray? Gee, that was a minute and 30 seconds.

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: Oh, yes. Manual and Wide. 2 Minus 5, 15.

a17_0903425.speaker: Evans
a17_0903425.text: Yes, Omni Delta.

a17_0912340.text: This is Apollo Control at 91 hours, 23 minutes. We're 23 seconds away from acquiring Apollo 17 on it's second revolution of the Moon. During this pass, we will send up a DOI-1 PAD. That's instructions to the crew for the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. We should be acquiring any time now. We'll stand by for the first call.

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Houston. We're with you in Omni Delta. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: ...that is much darker than the others...

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Ron. Read you loud and clear. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Robert. We should have gotten everything right on up through AOS here in the Flight Plan.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Good show.

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: And the Pan Camera should be running right now. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Houston. America here. We stopped the orbital photo path, frame 59. And at about the sub-stellar point, we took 59 to 66, and frame 67 was taken of the, oh, the dark slide on the corner of Lobachevsky. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: What have we got coming up there, Jack?

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, America. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Those frames that Ron mentioned - this is Jack - that he mentioned were taken of a area where there's a much lighter gray albedo. Rather than the tannish gray, it's pure gray material that generally is on the rim crest of a number of craters. It may be related to the swirls that we see elsewhere.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Did you go High Gain yet? Three minutes [garble].

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. 42, 43, Pan Camera, Stop.

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Bob, we're...

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Pan Camera, Off, on cue.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, America. We're tracking you on the map here, watching it.

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Al-Biruni has got a - variations in the - in its floor, variations in albedo. It almost looks like a pattern as if water were flowing on a beach. It's that irregular. Not in great areas, but in small areas around on the southern side, and the part that looks like it's a water-washing pattern is of a much lighter albedo, although I cannot see any real source for it. The texture, however, looks about the same.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Jack. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: And Houston, America. For your info, it took an hour - an hour [laughter] - a minute and 45 seconds for the map - your Mapping Camera to extend and a minute and 45 for it to retract.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Ron. Copy. 1:45, extend and retract. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Bob, what's our altitude now?

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Looks like you're crossing - you're just about 90 [nautical] miles, but we'll firm that up here, Gene. You're 90.8...

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Okay.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: ...America.

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Okay; thank you. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Bob, this is Jack. And the question of these irregular swirls that we've got in Mare Marginis, and we are looking just north of Nep - Neper now. I tell you, in the mare, there just is no visible relief. Although there seem to be some sinuous systematics anyway to the distribution. Like, there'll be a very dark area associated with the light area. And that dark area is darker than the mare. I think the pictures will show that. Now, in the highlands, however, the - the light albedo areas, which are very comparable, that appear to be swirl-like patterns of the same type, seem to be associated wit

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Jack. We understand, and we're standing by. We have a DOI PAD and some other updates.

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay. We'll go back to work. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: America, Houston. We'd like Pan Camera, Off. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: You're reading our minds, Bob.

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: It's Off.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger.

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: It's off.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Pan Camera'S Off, and we'd like Accept. We've got the DOI target load, the CSM state vector, PIPA - and an SPS tailoff constant. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Okay; you've got Accept, Bob.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Gene. And there will be no PIPA bias.

a17_0912340.speaker: Cernan
a17_0912340.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Bob, I can start with that PAD if you want to.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger. We're standing by. I'll start with DOI-1. Are you ready to copy? [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Go ahead.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Purpose: DOI-1, SPS/G&N; 40035; plus 1.90, minus 0.64; 093:11:36.60. Noun 81s; minus 01916, all balls for Delta-V Y , Delta-V Z is plus 0047.8; 000, 228, 000; 0058.9, plus 0014.5; 0197.4, 0:22, 0192.1; sextant star is 45, 187.5, 19.1. Let me say trunnion again; it's 19.1. The rest of the PAD is not applicable. Set stars will be Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Four jet, 15 second on the ullage. Other comments: overburn limits, Delta-V 17 - seventeen feet per second; burn time, 2 seconds. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Bob. Ready for a readback. DOI-1, SPS/G&N; 40035; plus 1.90, minus 0.64; 093:11:36.60; minus 01916, all zeros, plus 0047.8; all zeros, 228, all zeros; 0058.9, plus 0014.5; 0197.4, 0:22, 0192.1; 45, 187.5, 19.1. Rest of PAD is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Four jets, 15 seconds ullage - Overburn limits: Delta-V 7 - 17 feet per second; burn time, 2 seconds.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Jack. Good readback. Okay; I've got a map update for - at 93:38 in the Flight Plan. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay; go ahead. I have it.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Ron. AOS without burn, 93:31:37; with burn is 34:24. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. Without, 93:31:37; with burn is 34:24.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Ron. I've got a - You can go back to Block, Ron. And on that same page with the J-3, I've got the T-horizon and TCA.

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay; ready to copy. Go ahead.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Okay. You can go to Block on the computer. T-horizon time 93:48:04; TCA minus 20 is 93:50:44. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. T-horizon, 93:48:04; TCA minus 20 is 50:44.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger. Good readback.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Ron. Over at 93:52, 93:52, we've got a difference in the Noun 89 value.

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay; go ahead.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Okay. the Noun 89s have changed to the following: Noun 89, the first one, plus 20.284, plus 15.151, minus 001.96. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. It's a plus 20.284, and a plus 15.151, and a minus 001.96.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Ron. And here's a note for you. The landmark is F Crater, located on landing site - picture 4 of 4 in the Lunar Landmark Maps. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. Understand. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Okay; and I've got a TEI minus 5 PAD. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay; go ahead. TEI-5.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Roger, Jack. TEI minus 5: SPS/G&N; 38570; plus 0.49, plus 0.92; 098:39:43.24. Noun 81s, plus 2329.8, minus 2403.1, minus 1152.8; 193, 099, 318. The rest of the PAD is all not applicable. Set stars, Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Ullage four jet, 12 second. Comments: burn undocked; assumes a DOI. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay, Bob. TEI-5, SPS/G&N; 38570; plus 0.49, plus 0.92; 098:39:43.24; plus 2329.8, minus 2403.1, minus 1152.8; 193, 099, 318. Rest of PAD NA. Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Ullage: four jets for 12 seconds. Comment 1: burn undocked; comment 2: assume DOI.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Good readback, Jack.

a17_0912340.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0912340.text: Okay. What else can we do for you?

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Stand by 1, here. I've got an addition for Ron on that comment about that F Crater landmark. Let me get it. It's right here, and I'll come right up to Ron on it.

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay; I'll stand by. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Ron, this additional comment will have - the crater is 8 nautical miles north of your track. You will lose the landmark at a 36-degree elevation angle. Over. [Pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Okay. It's 8 miles north, and I'll lose it at 30 degrees. Okay; so that'll be pretty quick.

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Thirty-six degrees; pretty quick still. [Long pause.]

a17_0912340.speaker: Evans
a17_0912340.text: Is that the one on Family Mountain?

a17_0912340.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0912340.text: Stand by on that, Ron. Let me look at the book here. And I'll get Farouk to help me out on that one.

a17_0914640.speaker: Evans
a17_0914640.text: Okay, Houston. I've got F Crater, now. I'm all squared away. Thank you.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Okay, Ron. It's - it's right in the middle of that landing site 4 of 4 which is right before Ignin in the book on your - on the Landmark Tracking Book. And it's right dead center on that page.

a17_0914640.speaker: Evans
a17_0914640.text: Okay, I've got it now. I wrote down 404; it's 4 of 4.

a17_0914640.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0914640.text: Okay, Houston. We've got a good shot of the landing site.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Rog. Understand. And Roger, Ron. [Long pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0914640.text: The shadows, Bob, go all the way across the Scarp and very long pyramiding shadows go all the way past Family Mountain. It looks like the Sculptured Hills are lit up on this side, but it almost puts the entire North Massif in shadow, from where I stand. [Long pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: America, Houston.

a17_0914640.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0914640.text: Quite an interesting place to land down there.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: America, Houston. [Pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Cernan
a17_0914640.text: We can now, I think, see contrast down in the shadow. [Pause.] And the only part of the scarp that's visible - I think Jack picked it out - as being right where Lara is.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Roger. America, Houston.

a17_0914640.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0914640.text: Roger; go ahead.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Roger. Just some words in your - You'll be going through your systems checklist here and you'll probably see that it says dump the waste water if it's greater than 85 percent and you are at about 89.6 percent. We'd - we'd like you not to dump the waste water until the nominal time in the Flight Plan. Do not dump the waste water during this systems check. Over.

a17_0914640.speaker: Cernan
a17_0914640.text: Okay, and I understand that was about 94 hours as I recall.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: That's affirmative. That's where the nominal time is and that is where we'd like it dumped.

a17_0914640.speaker: Cernan
a17_0914640.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Cernan
a17_0914640.text: Bob, that's a - a fantastic black-and-white shot of the landing area with the shadow stretching across most of it.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Roger. Understand. [Long pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Cernan
a17_0914640.text: Bob, I can now see down in through the shadow. I can see - Bear Mountain, I can see - I can't really make out the - the slide yet. Most of the North Masstif - Massif are still in shadow due to the - due to the Sculptured Hills. And just at the point where we can start really to see through the shadows and see the - some hummocky terrain on the North Massif, it just went out of my next reach. But, I did see some sort of albedo change that went across the canyon about in the vicinity of the - of the scarp. [Long pause.]

a17_0914640.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0914640.text: Bob, with respect to the landing site - this is Jack - when we had near - or were closer to low phase angle, approaching it - when I first had it in view - there was a clear lightening in the area of the light mantle. It was not sharply defined, but around the crater Lara and Nansen and to the west of the scarp - there was very clearly, slightly brighter - reflectivity.

a17_0914640.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0914640.text: Roger, Jack.

a17_0914640.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0914640.text: 091:54:51 - Apollo 17's orbit is 168.8 by 52.5 nautical miles [312.6 by 97.2 km]. Present altitude; 154.9 nautical miles [286.9 km] and moving towards apolune.

a17_0915451.text: Apollo 17's orbit is 168.8 by 52.5 nautical miles [312.6 by 97.2 km]. Present altitude; 154.9 nautical miles [286.9 km] and moving towards apolune.

a17_0915627.speaker: Cernan
a17_0915627.text: Houston, America. The Mapping Camera and Laser Altimeter covers are Closed. I'm going to Enable A-1, A-2, and C-2.

a17_0915627.speaker: Evans
a17_0915627.text: Yeah, it looks like the old gravity gradient worked there or something. I didn't see it get out of attitude at all. Did you all see any movement at all? [Pause.]

a17_0915627.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0915627.text: Max error was about 0.2 - 0.3 of a degree, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0915627.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0915627.text: I'm sorry, Houston. I should have cued you on changing the SPS pressure indicators. You want to see that again?

a17_0915627.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0915627.text: Jack, it's not required to go back and do them again. We watched it on telemetry.

a17_0915627.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0915627.text: Okay. I'll try to remember to be a little more informative.

a17_0920852.speaker: Evans
a17_0920852.text: Okay, Houston. There are the torquing angles.

a17_0920852.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0920852.text: Roger. We see them. They look good. [Pause.]

a17_0920852.speaker: Evans
a17_0920852.text: Just for another little matter of interest - once the Earth is in the field of view, which it's about - looks like it must be about 12 degrees from Regulus - it's so bright, that it blacks out any - blanks out the telescope for any star recognition. However, it worked real good, in the sextant. You can see the star real well. You just have to assume it's Regulus, though.

a17_0920852.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0920852.text: Roger. Would that star angle difference...

a17_0920852.speaker: Evans
a17_0920852.text: And the first - the first star angle difference was - you know, you can get a little bit lax about it - if you want to spend a little time at it, you can get five balls every time, looks like.

a17_0920852.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0920852.text: Rog, Ron. With that star angle difference on the second one, I can assume it was Regulus. I think you're safe in your assumption.

a17_0920852.speaker: Cernan
a17_0920852.text: He had to do it, or else I'd have to go down there and do it.

a17_0920852.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0920852.text: 092:11:02 - This is Apollo Control at 92 hours, 11 minutes. Apollo 17 now at the highest point of it's orbit; 168.8 nautical miles [312.6 km]. 37 minutes remaining before Loss of Signal on this revolution.
This is Apollo Control at 92 hours, 11 minutes. Apollo 17 now at the highest point of it's orbit; 168.8 nautical miles [312.6 km]. 37 minutes remaining before Loss of Signal on this revolution.

a17_0921406.speaker: Evans
a17_0921406.text: Okay. Mighty fine; we'll go ahead and maneuver to attitude then.

a17_0921406.speaker: Cernan
a17_0921406.text: Houston, I think I've put the wrong number in on the Pitch. We'll correct it. It's 228, isn't it?

a17_0921406.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0921406.text: 092:16:37 - This is Apollo Control. Apollo 17 is maneuvering to the proper attitude for Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. This will put the crew heads down.

a17_0921637.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 17 is maneuvering to the proper attitude for Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver. This will put the crew heads down.

a17_0921809.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0921809.text: America, Houston. We'd like the High Gain to Auto. [Pause.]

a17_0922148.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0922148.text: America, Houston. We'd like you to hold off switching to Omni Charlie until we cue you on that. [Pause.]

a17_0922148.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0922148.text: Was there any indication on the seismometers of an impact, about the time I thought I saw a light flash on the surface?

a17_0922148.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0922148.text: Stand by that - we'll check on that, Jack.

a17_0922148.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0922148.text: Don't worry about it. Some - I thought somebody was looking at it. It could have been one of the other light flashes. [Pause.]

a17_0922148.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0922148.text: Rog. We copied the time and...

a17_0922148.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0922148.text: Okay, I got it marked on the map, too.

a17_0923119.speaker: Cernan
a17_0923119.text: Okay, Bob. The star sextant checks out okay.

a17_0923119.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0923119.text: 092:33:02 - Flight Director Pete Frank now checking all flight control positions for a Go/No-Go on the Descent Orbit Insertion burn. He's getting a Go from all positions.

a17_0923302.text: Flight Director Pete Frank now checking all flight control positions for a Go/No-Go on the Descent Orbit Insertion burn. He's getting a Go from all positions.

a17_0923441.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0923441.text: America, Houston. You are Go for DOI and you can leave the High Gain selected. We're holding good.

a17_0923441.speaker: Cernan
a17_0923441.text: Okay, Robert. DOI. [Garble] the High Gain.

a17_0923441.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0923441.text: Ro - Gene, say again. You were way down in the mud on that one. Can you say again, please? [Pause.]

a17_0923441.speaker: Cernan
a17_0923441.text: Roger; understand. We are Go for DOI, and you have the High Gain.

a17_0923441.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0923441.text: Hey, Bob, I know I've argued against this kind of thing, but you got tenths on that burn time? [Pause.]

a17_0923441.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0923441.text: Jack, just some words from the back room on you. The - There may have been an impact at the time you called, but the Moon is still ringing from the S-IVB impact. So it's masked any other - would mask any other impact. So they may be able to strip it out at a later time, but right now they don't see anything at your called time.

a17_0924037.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0924037.text: Bob, log us for a picture of the Earth at 92:40 on mag Oscar Oscar. And we're on frame 68.

a17_0924037.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0924037.text: You've got a lot of healthy weather out there in the Pacific today. Looks like most of those things we talked about yesterday, up in the Hawaii region and also in the south, have intensified.

a17_0924537.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0924537.text: America, Houston. We're about 3 minutes until LOS and everything is looking great. No changes since our Go for DOI. We'll expect to see you at 93:34:24.

a17_0924537.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0924537.text: 092:49:03 - This is Apollo Control at 92 hours, 49 minutes. And, we've had Loss of Signal as Apollo 17 goes behind the Moon. During this pass [means the previous pass], Jack Schmitt saw a flash just north of the crater Grimaldi at an elapsed time of 90 hours, 18 minutes and thought it might be a meteor impact. We could not confirm that; however, the Moon was still ringing from the S-IVB impact and would mask out other activity on the seismometer recorders in the science support room here. Apollo 17 will perform the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver behind the Moon just after the start of the th

a17_0924903.text: This is Apollo Control at 92 hours, 49 minutes. And, we've had Loss of Signal as Apollo 17 goes behind the Moon. During this pass [means the previous pass], Jack Schmitt saw a flash just north of the crater Grimaldi at an elapsed time of 90 hours, 18 minutes and thought it might be a meteor impact. We could not confirm that; however, the Moon was still ringing from the S-IVB impact and would mask out other activity on the seismometer recorders in the science support room here. Apollo 17 will perform the Descent Orbit Insertion maneuver behind the Moon just after the start of the third revoluti

a17_0924903.speaker: Cernan
a17_0924903.text: [Garble] the burn. [yawn] Well, there comes the Sun up already?. Probably. That'll be on our [garble]...

a17_0933000.text: This is Apollo Control at 93 hours, 30 minutes. We're a minute and a half away from acquisition without a burn; 4 minutes, 10 seconds away from acquisition given a nominal Descent Orbit Insertion burn. Acquisition between those two times would indicate a partial burn of some kind. We'll leave the line up now.

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: Whereabouts are we, Jack? I don't have a map.

a17_0933000.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0933000.text: We're 107 degrees west now - east, 107 east. And AOS is like - [garble] - like in 1 minute. I'm sorry, like in 3 minutes - 3 minutes.

a17_0933000.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0933000.text: 093:31:55 - We've passed the no-burn AOS time and do not have a signal. That's an encouraging sign that we did perform a maneuver.
We've passed the no-burn AOS time and do not have a signal. That's an encouraging sign that we did perform a maneuver.

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: Well, we are - our field of view is.
One minute to nominal AOS.

a17_0933000.speaker: Evans
a17_0933000.text: What - Noun 89, Gene?

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: There's Al-Biruni, isn't it?

a17_0933000.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0933000.text: 093:33:24 - One minute to nominal AOS.

a17_0933000.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0933000.text: 093:34:25 - We have a signal, right on the money.
We have a signal, right on the money.

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: Hello, Houston; America.

a17_0933000.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0933000.text: America, Houston. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: Okay. The burn was good on all counts, 22-second burn. It was on time, V GX , 1982; roll after the burn, 357, 225, and 003. Residuals were plus 0, plus 0.2, and plus 0.1. Delta-V C is 0.1, and that was with Delta-V total set into the EMS. Should have been - should been zero and the residual on the EMS was plus 0.1. Oxidizer's 305, and Fuel is 311 and an Unbalance of 150 Decrease. We're in a 59.1 by 14.9 [nautical-mile orbit, 109.5 by 27.6 km].

a17_0933000.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0933000.text: Okay, America; sounds great. [Pause.]

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: It looks pretty great. [Long pause.]

a17_0933000.speaker: Cernan
a17_0933000.text: We're getting back down among us where us plain folks belong.

a17_0933000.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0933000.text: Roger.

a17_0933000.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0933000.text: 093:36:45 - Those orbital numbers are an on-board readout, we'll confirm those in a few minutes after some tracking.
Those orbital numbers are an on-board readout, we'll confirm those in a few minutes after some tracking.

a17_0934100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934100.text: Houston, this is the LMP. There seem to be two general kinds of ray patterns: those associated with a lot of secondaries and light colored, and those that have no visible secondaries. And that's independent, yet, from the irregular light-colored areas we've been calling swirls.

a17_0934100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934100.text: Houston, there also - a lot more - there is - there is a lot more of that light-colored swirl-like irregular material, or discoloration - if - whatever you want to call it, in the back side highlands, particularly as we approach Marginis, than I had previously gathered from the available photography.

a17_0934100.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934100.text: And there still seems to be no relief associated with it. Although, in many cases, it seems to follow ridge lines, or crater rims part way. In other cases, it's quite irregular in its distribution.

a17_0934100.speaker: Evans
a17_0934100.text: And bank A, that time, with the chamber pressure, was up to 95.

a17_0934100.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934100.text: Roger, Ron. And we got tracking data on you; has a 13.1 perigee - peri - perilune, rather.

a17_0934100.speaker: Evans
a17_0934100.text: Okay, that's great, Bob, and we're still looking at that zero bias on the DC meter of about 5 to 7 psi.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Some of the boys might be interested to know that in a place where the Sun is just grazing the slope - it's a steep slope on the north rim of Crisium, I can see the horizontal lineaments that were such a controversy on 15.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger. Understand. The north rim of Crisium?

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: [Garble] big one with the central peak.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Roger. There are some very steep slopes that just have grazing Sun on them now, and with the binocs, you can see that horizontal lineation pattern.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: There it is. T-horizon will be good. Yeah. Okay, I've got the edge of Crisium now. [Garble.] Getting hills on the side of Crisium, there. [Pause.] Sure a lot smoother-looking material than I thought it would be.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Ron, you're about 1 minute from T-horizon.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, Bob. Thank you. Oh. [Laughter.] Here.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: And, Ron, we - we're copying you on VOX, we believe. Is that affirm?

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Yes, that's right.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: You're not supposed to copy the other guys, though. Are you copying the other guys?

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: No, just you, Ron.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: I may have been talking loud. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Okay, Ron. You should be at T-horizon.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Mark. T-horizon.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, that's pointing at the horizon all right. I don't see the crater, yet. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, I can see the rims of Microbus [sic] A and B. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, I really don't see it yet. I can see Microbus A and B, real well. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, I'm going to pick out one and start marking on it.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That's the wrong one. Okay, now I see what I'm supposed to mark on; okay.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay? [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: No, the ones I just wrote in there. Right? [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay? And, lets [pause] now I'm going to take a look and see if it looks like a cinder cone. Hey! There's Maraldi Gamma, the mound sticking up there right beside Maraldi. Hey, you guys are going to have some good hills to run down in there. [Long pause.] Can you see it all - at all, coming up?

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: [Garble] north. That crazy radar is going to be in the way - the LM [laughter]. Okay, it's going through the landing site, now. The shadow is just up to [pause] You can really see the scarp on there.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: See what they mean by Sculptured Hills, Gene? See the knobby characteristics in that...

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: Yes. That'll be [garble]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: ...area down there. That's part of the Sculpured Hills.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: That's a massif there, too. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Now, we're just over the rim of Serenitatis, looking over the Graben Plains...

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: There, you can just see. I'm going to switch to 17-1. 3, 4, 5, 6 - just got six of them on 17-1 and then the other three were were on F - F Crater; 17-1 was just barely in the - Sherlock was just barely beyond the shadow.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: This is all supposedly covered with the dark mantle, Gene, what you're seeing down there.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: Yeah, the Sun angles are so that you can't tell the difference in albedo.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: And look at those mare ridges, though.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: I tell you, that's looking out into the gray...

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: That's the old Littrow site.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: ...gray desert down in there. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: I think so. I think we're just about ready to climb.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: I think the terminator's giving you the feeling of that, maybe. Ain't nothing out there.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Jack, Houston. Can you see any albedo difference in the landing site area between the dark massif and the light area?

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: We can't see any difference between - in the low areas, between the dark mantle and other materials right now. We're right at the terminator.

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: Yeah, but Jack and I weren't really looking at the landing site. I think Ron was.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Yeah, you could really see a difference between the - the South Massif and the - the mantle material around through there. The mantle is not nearly as dark as it looks on the pictures, though. But the massif, South Massif especially, looked almost a whitish color. I guess it's because the, partly the Sun was shining on it. But then...

a17_0934549.speaker: Cernan
a17_0934549.text: Could you see anything that looks like the slide?

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Oh, yeah. You can see the slide on the thing and definitely see the scarp going across through there. I was primarily concentrating on looking for the various craters so I didn't spend that much time, you know, concentrating on how the thing looked. But in the marks on the thing, the first about four or five marks were on F Crater and then I saw Sherlock about halfway through it and I got about five marks on the Sherlock for 17-1. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: [Garble] Gene. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Houston, in crossing Crisium and Marginis, it looked fairly clear that with the small fresh craters, and I don't have a good size estimate right now - I think I'm looking in terms of 100 or 2 meters. You can distinguish where blocks have been thrown up by them, or not - possibly giving depth of the local regolith from the pictures you'll get in there.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger, Jack. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: And, also, on that lineation question, not only, where the Sun grazes a - a slope do you see the horizontal lineations, but they're at the southern end of the shadowed area on a slope. You get a couple other lineations showing up at least in a couple places I saw. One would be parallel to the slope - that is cross-contour, and the other was at a - an angle to that direction - oh - say of about 30 degrees. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger, Jack. We're copying you loud and clear and no problem with comm at all. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Okay. We just had sunset.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: And, Houston; America. On mag Bravo Bravo, 75 to 70 percent were utilized on J-3 and F Crater and 17-1 through the sextant.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger. Just want to confirm, Ron. You started on J-3 and then you went to F Crater and... [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Yeah. I went to F Crater and then back to Sherlock or 17-1.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Actually, on J-3, I took four marks on a crater that was to the west of J-3 and then I finally saw J-3 and started marking on it.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger, Ron. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Okay, Houston. Mag Oscar Oscar is 85.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger, Jack. Thank you.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: And, there - okay; and there's a number of pictures - Now, just a minute, let me try to give you a general feeling for where they were taken. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Okay; a number of the last pictures that were taken on that series, or that rev, were taken between - say about 115 east, and... [pause] oh, about 100 east and they show several examples of the light-colored or swirl...

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Coming up now.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: ...alterations to the surface. And that's in highland country where that is a distinct gray against the tan-gray or tan highland background - general highland color.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Okay, Jack. I got that. [Long pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: And, all my pictures, Jesus [laughter]. [Pause.]

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Ron, Houston. We'd like you to move up and do the waste water dump starting now and the O 2 fuel cell purge.

a17_0934549.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0934549.text: Okay, we'll get to that and mag Quebec Quebec is on frame 50.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: Roger. Copy.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, you want to dump the waste water on the front side?

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: That's affirm, Ron. We'd like to get a start dump now, so we have it dumped prior to the camera pass, or...

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Oh, okay.

a17_0934549.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0934549.text: We want to get a dump prior to the UV work there, Ron.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: Okay, that's right - I'm sorry, I forgot about that.

a17_0934549.speaker: Evans
a17_0934549.text: [Garble] how [garble] going to go, with Battery Vent to... [pause] Okay, Battery Vented, Battery Vent is Closed and going to Dump A.

a17_0940330.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0940330.text: Pan Camera Power going Off. [Long pause.]

a17_0940330.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0940330.text: Okay, Houston. Beginning the fuel cell purge - O 2

a17_0940330.speaker: Cernan
a17_0940330.text: Bob, any objections to making that Verb 49 maneuver, now? [Long pause.]

a17_0940330.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0940330.text: America, no objection to going to Verb 49 maneuver any time. Just do not open the UV door until the 94:45 Flight Plan time.

a17_0940330.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0940330.text: 094:08:50 - This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 8 minutes. Apollo 17 now is maneuvering to the attitude from which the ultraviolet spectrometer and the infrared scanning radiometer experiments will be performed. The start of those experiments on this pass will be after LOS, behind the Moon.

a17_0940850.text: This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 8 minutes. Apollo 17 now is maneuvering to the attitude from which the ultraviolet spectrometer and the infrared scanning radiometer experiments will be performed. The start of those experiments on this pass will be after LOS, behind the Moon.

a17_0940850.speaker: Cernan
a17_0940850.text: Hey, Gordo. I think we're still in LM Pressure up there in the tunnel. You want us to go back to LM/CM Delta-P?

a17_0940850.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0940850.text: Okay, Gordo's off. I'll have to wait a minute here, Gene. [Pause.]

a17_0940850.speaker: Cernan
a17_0940850.text: God, for a Sun - for a Sunday night, you're - you're hard to get along with.

a17_0940850.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0940850.text: Wise Marines end up - wise Marines end up in Antarctica.

a17_0940850.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0940850.text: Roger. Can't do that. They don't have any gates down there.

a17_0940850.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0940850.text: That sounds like a job you could probably handle.

a17_0940850.speaker: Cernan
a17_0940850.text: Listen, after that answer, I'll build one down there for you.

a17_0940850.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0940850.text: Thank you, sir. Hey, you can go to LM/CM Delta-P.

a17_0941228.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0941228.text: America, Houston. The fuel cell 3 purge can be terminated. [Pause.]

a17_0941228.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0941228.text: 094:15:48 - This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 15 minutes. Apollo 17 is just south of the Oceans of Storm - Ocean of Storms now. Shortly, we'll be coming up on the crater Grimaldi again. That's where Jack Schmitt saw a flash on the last pass. We're showing an orbit of 58.9 by 14.3 nautical miles (109.1 by 26.5 km) at the present altitude of 28.1 nautical miles (52.0 km).

a17_0941548.text: This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 15 minutes. Apollo 17 is just south of the Oceans of Storm - Ocean of Storms now. Shortly, we'll be coming up on the crater Grimaldi again. That's where Jack Schmitt saw a flash on the last pass. We're showing an orbit of 58.9 by 14.3 nautical miles (109.1 by 26.5 km) at the present altitude of 28.1 nautical miles (52.0 km).

a17_0941548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0941548.text: Hey, Bob. Who you talking to us with, Honeysuckle or Goldstone? Honeysuckle, I'd guess. [Pause.]

a17_0941548.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0941548.text: We're talking through Goldst - Goldstone, Gene. [Pause.]

a17_0941548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0941548.text: Okay, looks like about a toss-up from here. I'll tell you, there is really one heck of a big low-pressure area developing somewhere off the coast of California, Washington, or Canada, out in the Pacific Northwest part of the country.

a17_0941548.speaker: Cernan
a17_0941548.text: We were watching it earlier today, but I tell you, now, it's really dragged in some other clouds with it. It must cover an enormous distance and it's got some real spectacular circulation.

a17_0941548.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0941548.text: Just for curiosity, are you using a monocular on that? [Pause.]

a17_0941548.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0941548.text: Bob, it's - it's got a trailing front. I can't really see the States, or even the North American continent, because...

a17_0941548.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0941548.text: Stand by, Jack, we'd like to - or Gene. We'd like for you to terminate...

a17_0941548.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0941548.text: Okay, I was just going to say, it's got a - looks like a tremendous trailing front. Roughly, north-northwest, south-southeast, and it looks like it may just sweep up the - the western coast. It's hard to tell how far off the actual center rotation or even a front is. I just remember from earlier this morning, when I could see landmasses, that it appeared to me to be off the Pacific Northwest out in the ocean.

a17_0942221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942221.text: Jack, Houston here. We've just been kicking around with Farouk, and if you get - if you want to, during your - any of your free time, if you have any, you might look at Copernicus with your binoculars and see if the dike goes all the way - all the way across. He would recommend using the binoculars. Don't take any of your eat or sleep time at all, but you might get a chance on this one eat pass to, as you go by there. [Pause.]

a17_0942221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942221.text: Okay. I'll give her a try. You might give me a couple minutes' warning the next time around.

a17_0942221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942221.text: I'm not sure the attitude is too good for that. I wish I'd thought of it this round.

a17_0942221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942221.text: Rog. Well, we were pretty busy coming up on it this time. I think the - that's why we mentioned the attitude may be okay during the eat period. We don't want you to break away from your eat period unless you see you can spare the time. [Long pause.]

a17_0942221.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942221.text: Just looking at the southern edge of Grimaldi, Bob, and we probably have it covered on photos, but there's a nice tangential to slightly circumferential graben along the southern wall and climbs out over the western rim and off the eastern rim, and that graben is premare - premare.

a17_0942221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942221.text: Okay, I copy on that, Jack, and as long as we're talking about Grimaldi, you might just rem - we'd like to have you brief Ron exactly on the location of that flash you saw. We'll probably ask him to take a picture of it, maybe during one of his solo periods. [Long pause.]

a17_0942221.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942221.text: Hey, Bob, before we get awfully involved, just let me tell you what our motive is here in the next couple of hours. That's to eat and get done what's in the Flight Plan, and come our rest period, we're probably going to turn out the lights and make sure everything's done by then so we can start it on-time tonight.

a17_0942221.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942221.text: Yes, that's a definite - we concur with that definitely, Gene. Don't want you to work into your sleep period. [Pause.]

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Gene, Houston. [Pause.]

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: Go ahead.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Gene, last night you didn't use a tone booster, and the word you gave us was that it had - it wasn't working, and we're just wondering if you want - we're thinking about working up a test board to see if - did you test it out thoroughly to make sure it wasn't working, or was that just your desire not to use it?

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: We tried it, Bob, and it did not work. The only reason I'm reluctant on a test is I just don't want it to take much time.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: I don't think it would take much time. The only thing I could say is it would - you know - two obvious things I'm sure you checked them, Gene, would be the utility power and make sure you had the right lamp tests on when you tried it, and that's the only - I'm sure you did it, and that's the only obvious thing - maybe a circuit breaker or something like that.

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: Well, we checked it both on the left side and on the right side with two separate Utility Powers and verified that the Master Alarms came on with the test on both sides, and nothing ever happened.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Rog. I was sure of that, Gene. Just wanted to make it - put everybody at ease that it's just not working. [Pause.] That was essentially the test. Just forget anything we said about tests. [Pause.]

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: Okay.

a17_0942719.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942719.text: What test?

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Rog. Got you guys trained up there, finally. [Pause.]

a17_0942719.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942719.text: Arf, arf.

a17_0942719.speaker: Evans
a17_0942719.text: Houston, America.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Roger. Go ahead, Ron.

a17_0942719.speaker: Evans
a17_0942719.text: If I don't find my scissors here one of these days, I think it takes about four bolts on either side of the - you know the optics, where they stow the optics? it looks like there are four little tool E bolts that'll come out. And I think maybe they might be back behind there, I don't know. [Pause.] See, there's a great big slot up at the top of that - oh, it's at least an inch - inch between the top of the optics thing and the top of the spacecraft. I looked back in there with a flashlight and can't see anything, but it's a big hole back there anyhow.

a17_0942719.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0942719.text: I think the commander might have something to say.

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: Hey, Bob, just ignore everything he said. We'll leave him a pair of our scissors, and he's just worried about being hungry.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Roger. Those are your EVA scissors, too, aren't they?

a17_0942719.speaker: Cernan
a17_0942719.text: But, he is not - Yeah, but we can handle - we can handle it with one down there. He is not taking the spacecraft apart to find his scissors, and I will not let him go hungry.

a17_0942719.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0942719.text: Roger.

a17_0942719.speaker: Evans
a17_0942719.text: Okay, either way.

a17_0943546.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0943546.text: Hey, Bob, before we lose you, how did the Oilers do today? [Laughter.] [Pause.]

a17_0943546.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943546.text: That's affirmative. Played one of their better games, I guess. [Pause.]

a17_0943546.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0943546.text: How about the Chicago Bears? You got their score handy?

a17_0943546.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943546.text: Hey, Jack, how about if we pick you up during the eat period. While you're eating, we'll brief you of the whole NFL situation for today. Okay? [Pause.]

a17_0943546.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0943546.text: Well, we are eating. I guess we wait until we come around next time. Okay.

a17_0943546.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943546.text: Oh - I - well, the Bears were [garble] losing but...

a17_0943546.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0943546.text: Bob, we'll wait and you can get up the late evening news prepared for us here the next time around.

a17_0943546.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943546.text: Okay. Have your gourmet dinner and I'll give you the news.

a17_0943813.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943813.text: America, Houston. We're going to lose you here in about 2½ minutes. We'll see you at 95:28, according to the Flight Plan, and you're looking good. We don't have anything, any anomalies or anything against you right now. You look great. [Pause.]

a17_0943813.speaker: Cernan
a17_0943813.text: Thank you, Robert. We'll see you coming around the horn.

a17_0943813.speaker: Cernan
a17_0943813.text: Hey, Bob, if you could, it might be appreciated with a word or two from our home fronts.

a17_0943813.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943813.text: Yeah, yip. You didn't let me do it. I was going to give them all a call while on this LOS here, Gene.

a17_0943813.speaker: Cernan
a17_0943813.text: It's that thing again. I bet you were concentrating on the dot.

a17_0943813.speaker: Evans
a17_0943813.text: There he goes. Which way is he going to go?

a17_0943813.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943813.text: Hey, guys. The Bears 21 to 12 over Philadelphia.

a17_0943813.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0943813.text: Thank you. We're going to watch your signal get cut off here.

a17_0943813.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0943813.text: Roger. Was touch and go on that because at one time they're losing that game.

This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 41 minutes. We've had Loss of Signal on the third revolution. Ron Evans performed some landmark tracking on the front side of the Moon during this pass and we got some Earth weather reports from lunar orbit, believed to be a first, in the Apollo series. And spacecraft is in the attitude now to perform the Ultraviolet Spectrometer and the Infrared Scanning Radiometer experiments. We - we expect to acquire Apollo 17 next at 95 hours, 28 minutes. Will come back up then. At 94 hours, 42 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a17_0943813.speaker: Cernan
a17_0943813.text: Okay, Ron, you can go - after Jack does that Telcom Group 2, AC2.

a17_0943813.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0943813.text: 094:41:08 - This is Apollo Control at 94 hours, 41 minutes. We've had Loss of Signal on the third revolution. Ron Evans performed some landmark tracking on the front side of the Moon during this pass and we got some Earth weather reports from lunar orbit, believed to be a first, in the Apollo series. And spacecraft is in the attitude now to perform the Ultraviolet Spectrometer and the Infrared Scanning Radiometer experiments. We - we expect to acquire Apollo 17 next at 95 hours, 28 minutes. Will come back up then. At 94 hours, 42 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a17_0943813.speaker: Evans
a17_0943813.text: What's that? Is that High Gain, Manual?

a17_0943813.speaker: Cernan
a17_0943813.text: Manual; plus 23 and plus 260 - plus 23 and plus 260.

a17_0952707.text: This is Apollo Control at 95 hours, 27 minutes. We should be acquiring Apollo 17 on it's fourth revolution of the Moon in about 45 seconds. We'll stand by for the first words.

a17_0952707.speaker: Evans
a17_0952707.text: Well, I guess - do I want to be Auto? Okay.

a17_0952707.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0952707.text: 095:28:25 - We have a signal and are receiving data.
We have a signal and are receiving data.

a17_0952707.speaker: Evans
a17_0952707.text: You're right. Very [garble] right.

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: Hello Houston, America.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Hello America. Reading you loud and clear.

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: Bob, the Flight Plan is complete through 95:30.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: And Bob, the IR cover came open about 1 minute late.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay, Understand. [Pause.] Might be interested, the latest tracking data has you at about 14.1 [nautical miles] perilune. It's coming up closer to your CMC data. [Pause.] And, America, we'd like to have the H 2 tank, H 2 tank 1, fans off. We'll be letting that pressure decay on that. We'll be bringing them back on prior to sleep period.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay, that's Off.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: I've got a number of PADs and Flight Plan update any time you're ready for them, if you want or you can hold off it awhile. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: Why don't you start with Flight Plan updates Bob?

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay, At 97:30, 97:30. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: Okay.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: You should have a pen and ink change there that says UV cover, Close. After that add UV, Off. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: Okay, got it.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay, now, just a note, or you can jump way ahead to 106:51, where it says delete, see where it says UV, Off, just delete that, or else make it a verify, because it will be off during that whole period. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Cernan
a17_0952707.text: 106. Yeah, I'll just put a verified by that. 106:51.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger. The next thing I've got are the PADs. The TEI-12 and TEI-19 PAD. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: First one is TEI-12, SPS G&N: 38570; plus 0.49, plus 0.92; Noun 33 times, 111:54:42.86; plus 2543.8, minus 1765.6, minus 0795.0; Roll is 186, 109, 328. The rest of the PAD is not applicable. Break - Break Jack, we'd like an Accept on the computer please. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: You got it.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay. The set stars are as always, Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Four Jet, 12-second on the ullage. Three notes: Burn undocked, assumes no Circ, longitude of the Moon at T IG will be minus 140.19°. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Bob, give me note two again please.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay, Jack, the three comments are: assumes burn undocked, assumes no Circ burn, and the Moon at T IG , the longitude will be minus 140.19°. Over.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay, I got everything, but number 2. All right, here's your readback. TEI-12, twelve that is, SPS/G&N; 38570; plus 0.49, plus 0.92; 111:54:42.86; plus 2543.8, minus 1765.6, minus 0795.0; 186, 109, 328. Rest of the PAD is NA. Sirius and Rigel; 133, 200, 030. Ullage is 4 Jets for 12 seconds. Remarks: (1) burn undocked, (2) assume no Circ, (3) longitude, lunar longitude at T IG minus 140.19°, .19°.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger. Good readback, Jack, and I've got the TEI-19 PAD, if you're ready. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay, go ahead.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: TEI-19, SPS/G&N; 38023; plus 0.49, plus 0.86; the T IG time, 125:46:47.22; plus 2456.3, minus 1925.3, minus 0731.3; 186, 108, 325. Rest of the PAD is not applicable. All the notes are the same as on the TEI-12 PAD, except the longitude is minus 147.62. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Stand by 1. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay. Here's your readback. TEI-19, SPS/G&N; 38023; Plus 0.49, plus 0.86; 125:46:47.22; plus 2456.3, minus 1925.3; minus 0731.3; 186, 108, 325. Rest of PAD is NA. And the remarks are the same as for TEI-12; that includes set stars. And the only change is in 3, which is lunar longitude at T IG of a minus 147.62. Over.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: That's a good readback Jack. I've got a LM DAP read-up here for you. [Pause.] They recommend this be copied on page 1 of the LM Data Card Book, Jack.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Well, strangely enough, the LM Data Card Book's in the LM.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Yes, I figured as much.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: We'll put it in our Activation Book. Let me find the right page.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Let me find the right page.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Evans
a17_0952707.text: No, I'm putting on my harness. The next thing is AOS.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: And, Jack, the computer's yours. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay. LM DAP information: LM weight, 36714; CSM weight, 38078. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay, the DAP load is LM weight, 36714; CSM weight, 38078.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger, Jack, and I'd like to correct one call on my, the TEI PADs. There is one other difference between the TEI-19 and the TEI-12 under notes. And the TEI-19 assumes the circ burn, over. [Long pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay, that's corrected to assume circ on the TEI-19.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger, Jack. I'm sorry on that. I've got some notes from the Flight...

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: That's alright, Bob.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Got some notes for Gene from the Flight Surgeon. He promised an update to you on some meal recommendations here on food, if you'd - you might want to copy this into the supplement. [Pause.]

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Okay. Just standby one, please.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Roger.

a17_0952707.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0952707.text: Bob, let's - let us take a look at the landing area and we'll be right back with you.

a17_0952707.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0952707.text: Okay. Just whenever you want it, there's no hurry on this at all. Jack, you just might put a little note there somewhere for yourself that Copernicus is at 96.03 if you want to look at it.

a17_0954545.text: Apollo 17's coming up over the Taurus Littrow landing site now.

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Now we're getting some clear - look like pretty clear high-water marks on the...

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: There's high-water marks all over the place there.

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: ...on the north part of Tranquillitatis in here - mare onto the highlands.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: Yeah, there's high-water marks all over that - that - I think that's Maraldi there. [Pause.] Are you sure we're at 13 miles up?

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: You're at 14.1 [nautical miles, 26.1 km], to be exact there, Ron.

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: [Laughter.] Looks pretty low.

a17_0954545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0954545.text: Gee, I wonder what it feels like to be at 8 to 10.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: You're going to find out, I think. [Long pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: I tell you there's some mare ridge or scarps, very sinuous - just passing one. They not only cross the low planar areas but go right up the side of a crater in one place and a hill in another. And it's not at all like a fault scarp. It looks very much like a constructional ridge. And it has the sinuousity of a, pardon the expression, rattle snake.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Roger. Does it look like that one we saw on the track the other day?

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Yeah, very much like that one that you almost caught. Look at that. There's a tongute - there's a tongue depressor - several of them - grabens in here. We must be out on the edge of Serenitatis now, right?

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Yeah, we show you on the edge of Serenitatis, Jack.

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Rog. I just - we didn't get a view of the site, though, going over this time. I think it was off to the north of us just a tad. [Pause.] That's the best example of a mare - a mare-like ridge that was as clearly constructional as I would want to see it. Out on the mare, it's never quite that obvious. But there, it climbed up over a hill and then back down again.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: And that was just east of the - an area just east of the edge of Serenitatis and probably a little bit south of the landing site. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0954545.text: Say, Bob, rather than copy specific recommended changes or deletions to a diet, can you have a general comment that's any different than what I already understand?

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Right. It's no problem.

a17_0954545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0954545.text: If not, I would rather delay it.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: No, it's no problem, Gene. Two quick comments: the next couple of days, delete the peach ambrosia and the mixed fruit bar, and don't delete anything from the LM menu. And make sure you get all the water in for rehydration, and take - bias it if you think you get 30 percent gas, then put in 30 percent more so you get all the water that is required. And take two anti-gas tablets after each meal instead of one. That sums it up.

a17_0954545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0954545.text: Okay - Okay. Very good. I'll - I'll handle all those words according to their need.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Roger.

a17_0954545.speaker: Cernan
a17_0954545.text: Appreciate them, though. [Long pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: Houston, America.

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Go ahead.

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: We're shooting magazine QQ, frame 50 - frame 50, 51, and 52. We're taking - looking south at the terminator. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Ron, we need to get looking at the Pan Camera here, per the Flight Plan. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Evans
a17_0954545.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Okay, Bob. Power on the Pan Camera now. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Mark it. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: Roger. We got it.

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Okay. And has my biomed been looking all right?

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: That's affirmative. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0954545.text: America, you can turn the Pan Camera, Off. [Pause.]

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Okay. Pan Camera going Off.

a17_0954545.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0954545.text: Mark.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: Okay, Bob. Let's see. Will Copernicus - will be north of our track. Is that correct?

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: I believe so, from my charts here, but let me doublecheck that. That is affirmative. Tommy just gave me the up on that one. [Long pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: If you guys got time to listen, I can update you on the home front while you're wor - looking out the windows. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Let's see. For the CDR, they're eating beans and cornbread over at Nassau Bay tonight. Probably a good thing they're eating beans there, Gene, because you're feeding 25 tonight. And the horse is getting fed, also. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: Beans and cornbread? It's a good thing I'm eating up here.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: You better believe it. And, of course, everybody sends their love. And over in El Lago, they're...

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: Well...

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Go ahead, Gene.

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: I was just going to ask you to return mine for me, would you?

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Oh, you better believe it. They're listening to the squawk box. You don't have to say anything to me. And over in El Lago, Jamie's says - is saying her prayers ending them with, "God bless America and Challenger from now on." And John is saying, "There's Daddy's rocket - makes it go pitch, light out." And of course, everybody sends their love...

a17_0960029.speaker: Evans
a17_0960029.text: They're great.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: And they're all listening right now if you'd...

a17_0960029.speaker: Evans
a17_0960029.text: Tell John, though, that I shaved the other night.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Roger. He'll be listening, hearing that. They're all over at the - in Nassau Bay at a big meeting of the Flight Plan. The Parkers are briefing the Cernans and the Evans on the Flight Plan tonight. And out in Tucson, for the LMP, it's kind of cloudy and cold out there today. It's colder than normal. Everything's working fine on the speaker out there, Jack, and they're just listening, and Mother - your Mother is really tickled and just pleased as all get out.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: That sounds like Mother. And I just got a real good view of Copernicus, but I'm afraid I can't help you out on that structure in the central peak. Just a little too dark.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Okay.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: But it's a fantastic sight at this altitude. It is a big crater. It looks like it's about 80 kilometers in diameter.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: I'll drink to that.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: And put down a verify on those dark deposits in the wall. And also on the southeast wall, there's one right on the rim. I think we mapped that one, too, but I'll have to go back and check.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Okay.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: That one looked like it had a crater in it. [Pause.] However, they all tend to be elongate radially, with respect to the crater. But that's about all I can add now. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: Bob, I'm glad, the squawk box is fixed. And, of course, send my love and best wishes out there to Tucson.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: That's a Roger, Jack. You guys might also be interested, here in the Houston area, all of the ground voice or air-to-ground is being carried on FM stations a hundred percent of it. And KUHT, the television station, will cover the - educational TV station - is going to cover 100 percent of the EVAs, all three of them, for all the time. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: That sounds great. We hope we can provide them with as much education as we can entertainment.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: We're counting on it. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: I guess Parker's all we had left down there to brief them on the landing site, huh? [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: I won't even comment on that one.

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: [Chuckle.] Okay. I figure he will later. [Long pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: I'd like, also, to send my best up north to the Bellwood - the Bellwood area up there, because I think there's a squawk box up there, too.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Beautiful. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960029.text: And, Bob, it's - all in all, it's been a pretty exciting day. I think a pretty accomplishing day, and certainly a rewarding day on our part. It's also been a long day, but we're hoping that it can only be superseded by tomorrow. And judging from what we've got in store, it might very well be.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: I think that sums up the day. It's a day of anticipation for what's going to happen tomorrow. Everything's gone off real well here, and we're just glad you're in the orbit you're in and ready for tomorrow.

a17_0960029.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960029.text: My goodness, Bob. This is Jack. It's awful hard to spend much time up here anticipating. The events come so fast and certainly are exciting and rewarding, each one, one at a time. But obviously, tomorrow is going to be the biggy.

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a17_0960029.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960029.text: Ron, we're watching your 52; and just be advised you do not have to do the option 1.

a17_0960029.speaker: Evans
a17_0960029.text: Okay. Real fine, Bob.

a17_0960926.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960926.text: Bob, I'm not sure whether it's entirely proper, being a bachelor, but I'd like to send my regards to everybody - all the families listening to squawk boxes tonight. [Pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960926.text: Bob, we're going right over the Procellarum Ridge now, if I'm not mistaken, out in the middle of Mare Procellarum. And we're low enough now that you can see some of the terrain.

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Okay.

a17_0960926.speaker: Schmitt
a17_0960926.text: That is - that is, some of the hills and rilles and valleys associated with that ridge system.

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Roger. Break - Ron, we've got the 52, and it looks good. You can torque.

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: Okay. I'll torque it 10, 3, 0.

a17_0960926.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0960926.text: 096:11:08 - This is Apollo Control. Gene Cernan's remark about up north in Bellwood is a reference to his mother, Mrs. Andrew Cernan, who is following the course of the mission at her home in Bellwood, Illinois.
This is Apollo Control. Gene Cernan's remark about up north in Bellwood is a reference to his mother, Mrs. Andrew Cernan, who is following the course of the mission at her home in Bellwood, Illinois.

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: Houston, America. You want an E-memory dump?

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Roger. We're standing by. We're ready for it.

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: Okay. Verb 74 - sync. [Long pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Cernan
a17_0960926.text: The GDC is aligned, and we verified that the LM valve is in LM/CM Delta-P.

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Roger. We got you. [Long pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: The E-MOD is finished, Ron.

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Ron, we're ready to uplink the jet monitor program and one of the burn constants. [Pause.]

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: Okay. You have CMC and Accept.

a17_0960926.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0960926.text: Okay.

a17_0960926.speaker: Evans
a17_0960926.text: P20 and Accept.

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: While you're eating or getting ready to eat, I can update some of the news with you tonight, if you're away from the windows. Or are you all still looking out?

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: Okay. There's not a whole lot of news on the wire tonight, matter of fact. President Nixon received a firsthand report on private Vietnam peace negotiations today from a key member of the US negotiating team, General Alexander Haig, Jr., Henry Kissinger's Chief Lieutenant. Haig flew back from Paris to report to the President, while technical experts from both sides held an unusual Sunday meeting in the French capital. Presidential Assistant Kissinger will resume his talks with North Vietnam's Le Duc Tho on Monday after a 1-day recess. And former President Harry Truman continued to show some si

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: And did you get a spurious Master Caution and Warning? [Pause.]

a17_0961628.speaker: Cernan
a17_0961628.text: No. Ron was retesting our bleeper again.

a17_0961628.speaker: Cernan
a17_0961628.text: And it's one of those that works in lunar orbit, I guess. It doesn't work during coast because it's working now.

a17_0961628.speaker: Cernan
a17_0961628.text: Sounds like there's going to be some good football games coming up.

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: Yes, indeed. You really can't call...

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: That's the Oakland - Oakland and the Jets.

a17_0961628.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0961628.text: Ron, the up-link is complete. The EMP is running, and the computer's yours. [Pause.]

a17_0961628.speaker: Cernan
a17_0961628.text: Okay, Bob. We got it back.

a17_0962410.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962410.text: Ron, we'd like the H 2 Tank Fans, On, and that will be the sleep configuration. H 2 Tank 1 Fans, On, [pause] and leave 3 in Auto.

a17_0962410.speaker: Cernan
a17_0962410.text: You want H 2 Tank 1 - You want 1 and 2, On?

a17_0962410.speaker: Cernan
a17_0962410.text: Okay, that leaves us with Tank 1, On; Tank 2, Off; and Tank 3 in Auto. Is that what you want?

a17_0962410.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962410.text: Roger. If you're calling the H 2 fans; that's what we want.

a17_0962410.speaker: Cernan
a17_0962410.text: Yeah, H 2 Fans, Bob; I'll say it again. H 2 Fans: 1 is On, 2 is Off, and 3 is Auto.

a17_0962410.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962410.text: That's a good configuration, and that will be the sleep configuration.

a17_0962410.speaker: Cernan
a17_0962410.text: Hey, Bob, it looks like we might make - getting to sleep on time tonight, and - well, we will make it. And I think it goes without saying, we definitely want to get up on time tomorrow.

a17_0962410.speaker: Evans
a17_0962410.text: I'm going to have the tone booster plugged in, and also I want to make sure the suit power and audio power and all that stuff is on.

a17_0962932.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962932.text: If Ron's listening, just some words about the Mapping Camera extend/retract times. We came up with slightly different times than what he'd called and we were wondering if his were just ballpark or whether he had timed it? In either case, the times are a little bit long on extend/retract which is a little cause for worry about that - the Mapping Camera may fail and later on downstream, we may want to change our operating mode on that Mapping Camera and he might want to time it a little closer. If he - if he can - the chance should come up.

a17_0962932.speaker: Evans
a17_0962932.text: Hey, Bob, that's a good point on the thing. Those weren't exact times and, as matter of fact, we looked - kind of looked away and it was about in - you know, somewhere around that - that period of time. We looked away and when - when we looked back, it was gray again, so - next...

a17_0962932.speaker: Evans
a17_0962932.text: ...next time we extend them, I'll get a good accurate indication.

a17_0962932.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962932.text: We'll believe the strip chart. We'll take the strip chart data. We've got 01:24; 1 minute, 24 seconds for extend and 01:51; 1 minute, 51 seconds for retract. And both those are a little bit on the high side. [Long pause.]

a17_0962932.speaker: Evans
a17_0962932.text: Okay. I would believe the strip charts.

a17_0962932.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962932.text: Rog, Ron. You all are about 4 minutes from LOS. [Pause.]

a17_0962932.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962932.text: Okay, we might lose you a little bit earlier than that. INCO. [Long pause.]

a17_0962932.speaker: Overmyer
a17_0962932.text: Okay, we may lose you a little early due to the SIM bay attitude and we'll pick you up at 97:22. [Pause.]

a17_0962932.speaker: Cernan
a17_0962932.text: Okay, Bob. Once more around at 97:22.

a17_0962932.speaker: Mission Control
a17_0962932.text: 096:34:22 - This is Apollo Control at 96 hours, 34 minutes. Apollo 17 has turned the corner a little early, about 50 seconds early. We've lost contact with the antenna because of it's attitude, about 50 seconds early.
