A17A1220706.text: There is the parting that I mentioned, still of somewhat unknown origin, and we'll try and get a sample along a parting plane. It's clearly evident in one of the bigger blocks.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: (Working at Jack's side of the Rover) Hey, Bob, just as we stopped the Rover, I went on Aux(illiary) water. Do you want me to turn my primary water off? I don't have to, do I?

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: No, no; no need to. [Water from the Aux tank flows through the Primary tank.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: That's what I figured. Just wanted to cover all bets. Okay, Jack. I think, I've got my housekeeping done. 122:08:28 Schmitt: Okay. Get your hammer. We're going to need it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I've been carrying it all day, it's about time I used it. Okay.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Bob, you're going to want a core at this site?

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Roger. We'd like to get...Number 1 priority will be some block samples, including any dirt that was on the blocks, if there is such. And then the second priority is a rake soil sample; the third priority is a double core. Then, also in there, the pans, of course, and other documented samples. But the double core is there, although it is third priority.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay. [Gene and Jack are carrying two different varieties of drive tubes which they can push or hammer into the ground. The majority were "lower" sections which have a hardened bit to resist damage from buried rocks. The others were "upper" sections which can be threaded into lower sections to make double-length cores. When using either a lower section by itself or an upper/lower pair as a double core, they will attach an adapter at the top and then one of the extension handles. This way, they can hammer on the extension handle and then extract the core without having to bend over.] [In the ch

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Gene, do you think...(Pause) Got your gnomon, huh?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Yep, I've got my gnomon, and I've got to give them a TGE (reading). When you said "bring a hammer," I came (over without starting the Traverse Gravimeter reading, which is the last task on CDR-27 )...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I'm sorry.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: No, no problem.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Well, I shouldn't have...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: The two go hand-in-hand.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Nothing disrupts your thought patterns more than somebody saying something.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Well, listen, this is my first geology stop. I guess I'm entitled to do that; Bob, you ready for a mark? [Gene is about to initiate the gravimeter measurement.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Roger.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay. Mark it. The light's flashing.

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Copy that. Video Clip ( 3 min 30 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, you got one (a boulder) picked out?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yes, let's see if we can work on that one. It's at the edge (of the crater), but we can chip at the parting plane. And that's one of the things that's come up that I think is of interest; we've got to figure out why they have that foliation in them.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Boy, that rock is one of the more vesicular ones I've seen around.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Well, they're all about that, Gene. They're either that or mixed with that variety. In the same boulder you'll (sometimes) see a non-vesicular....or, relatively non-vesicular (component). Okay, that's the... 122:10:18 Cernan: Watch your shadow. [Jack is photographing the sunlit face of the rock that they are about to sample. Gene, who is about to take a cross-Sun stereopair from south of the boulder, is reminding Jack not to get his shadow on the rock. On the site map, this boulder is at about 7 o'clock on the crater rim, relative to a 12 o'clock north. Gene's cross-Sun stereopair is AS17-134-

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: ...that's the down-Sun. (Pause) Ooh, locator's right into the Sun. Okay. [A "locator" is a photograph which includes an object of known size - the Rover or the LM - and/or an identifiable horizon feature which can be used to locate the sample site. Jack's "locator" is AS17-136- 20740 .] 122:10:31 Cernan: Right at that overlapping fracture, huh?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah. Let me get where I can maybe save the rock (fragment if it flies off). If you can hook your...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: That's what I'm going to do. I'm going to try and get it right...Right up on top is where I'd like to...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: If you hit it on the right side, it'll go this way, maybe. (Pause) There you go. Good man.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Piece right there. (Pause) I can get another one, too.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Try another one.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Don't lose that one. (Pause) Let me get that one for you.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I can get it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Got it?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Whoops. (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Can you keep it in sight here for a minute? Is that it? 122:11:13 Schmitt: Yeah. (Pause) [At the end of his pan, Fendell finds them working at the boulder Jack was examining earlier. Jack collects the first fragment with his scoop while Gene hammers on the top, northeast corner of the rock. It appears that Gene is standing a little downhill just inside the lip of the crater to their north.] [Cernan - "You just had to get yourself in a stable position to be able to swing the hammer. Because of the restriction of the suit, there was basically only one pendulum plane in which you could swing the

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I'm (garbled).

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Oh.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: It's coming. (Pause) [Gene hits the boulder with three sets of five blows. He manages to knock off a small fragment. Apparently, the hammer is turning somewhat in his hand. Although he has his back to us, he does seem to re-adjust his grip after each set.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: That's all right.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I'll get that one, wait a minute.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Be careful down in there. 122:11:49 Cernan: The whole thing is going to fracture off here, in a minute. Just want to...(Pause) [Gene strikes the rock seven more times, a little below the first site. He then rests. He has been balancing on his right foot, with the edge of the crater just to the right of that foot and with his left leg stuck out to the side as he hammers on the north corner of the rock. It seems a very precarious stance, particularly so close to a rock-filled crater.] 122:12:01 Schmitt: Trying...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: It's trying to fall. [Gene hits the rock five more times. The strokes are audible through his suit.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Don't wear your hand out. (Pause) [Cernan - "You had to hold onto the hammer and that meant you had to squeeze your finger against the pressure in the gloves. After you did that for a while, your hand and your forearm muscle would get sore. So you'd have to take a rest; not because your shoulder was sore or you were out of breath, but because of your hand and forearm. We were in pretty good shape at the time; we did a lot of training that exercised our forearms before we started; but gripping was still very tiring."] [In response to a question, Gene said that, while driving the Rover, he did n

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: That's good, Gene.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Wait a minute. Let me give one more whack. The whole thing is...(Pause) [He hits the rock three more times.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: No, that's too tight. Let me get that other piece...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Tipping the first sample out of the scoop into a bag) Okay. Bag 476 is the rock sample with a little bit of the soil near it. Of a chip...A chip off the rock, and it's the...Watch it, Gene. [Gene has been standing inside the crater, north of Jack and a meter below him, picking up a chip.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Here's the other chip. (Pause) If I go down there, that thing (the crater) is about 15 feet deep.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Right. (Pause) Got it. [Gene puts the chip in the bag Jack is holding.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay? Now, do you think you can chip off the other side of that plane, up on the edge? 122:13:01 Cernan: Yep. Yep. [Gene climbs easily out of the crater, then stumbles slightly on a fist-sized rock.] [Cernan - "Because of all of the stuff in front of you - your PLSS controls, your camera, your sample bags - it took a concerted effort to see exactly what you were stepping on. Like everything else you did on the Moon, you had to plan ahead a little bit. Here, it was just difficult to get up that little incline and I had to take a lot of little choppy steps. That gave me better balance than tryin

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Then we'll get the soil, and maybe just a small rock, non-chipped. Video Clip ( 3 min 33 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Let me tell you, my hands from that drill...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yes, I'm sure they are.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: ...really know I've been out here today. (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Sample bag) 476, Bob.

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Copy that, Jack. [Gene hits the south-top corner six times and knocks off a sizable sample.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: It's from the southeast side of the parting plane...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: There it is, a whole big slab, right there. [It's a flat, hand-sized piece.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, very good.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Oh, look at those dark minerals in there. Are those dark black?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, they may be ilmenite or fresh pyroxene. (Pause) We'll look at it. 122:13:36 Cernan: Gives the impression of pyroxene. [Schmitt - "Both pyroxene and ilmenite are dark minerals because of their iron and magnesium content."] [Jack has retrieved the sample with the scoop and is now trying to stick the scoop in the ground so that he can have both hands free.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, you want my bag (that is, does Jack need to get at Gene's SCB)? (Pause) I tell you, if you work on any kind of slope, like this little crater...(Pause) [Jack opens Gene's SCB and puts the sample bag in it.] [Cernan - "Early in training, we learned from working together that when the other guy is wrapping up a sample, you should turn your back and lean over so that he can drop the sample in the SCB. If you just walk away to do something else, he's left standing there with his hands full. The reason you have to lean over is mostly because the suit makes it difficult to reach up very high.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, I'm going to leave it (Gene's SCB) open for a minute.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: While we get that one. I'm going to have to...You're going to have to use your tongs on that one, I think.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I got it. [Gene has handed Jack an empty sample bag. They are facing west, away from the Rover and the TV camera.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: And, 17, a reminder to factor into your thinking, this is only a 30-minute stop, and there's about two-zero (20) minutes remaining. [Gene uses his tongs to grab the sample.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yes, sir. But we got to sample something.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Here's a big one. Get him (meaning Bob) the bag number, too.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Bag 454. Okay, and the flashes are from inside of vugs and re-crystallized vesicles. They look like pyroxene flashes; they could be ilmenite.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I'll get my "after" picture. [Fendell pans away from them.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay; and let me get in there and get some soil.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, let's get it first.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: From the north side. Whoops. Okay, the bag tore around that; it's pretty jagged rock, but I think it'll hold.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Pretty good slab.

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Having put the sample in Gene's SCB) It's in yours.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay. [Fendell has pointed the camera at them again.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: It's in Gene's sample collection bag. And a scoop sample...(Pause) You got a bag handy, Gene? [Because of the stiff suits, holding a bag with one hand and pouring samples into it with the scoop held in the other hand is a bit difficult. Here, Gene and Jack are working as a team, Gene holding the bag while Jack works the scoop. At Station 3 on EVA-2, a revision of the station activities leaves Jack sampling on his own, at a noticeable cost of efficiency. Later in the mission, Jack devises a reasonably effective method of solo sampling. Jack moves west and a little below the rock. He bends his k

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, bag 455. Bob. Is from the west side of the rock. It's under a slight overhang of the rock.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Finishing the thought) In a shadow, anyway. [To receive the sample, Gene flexes his knees slightly; however he doesn't hold the sample bag very low, as Dave Scott often did on Apollo 15.] [Schmitt - "There was a long-standing interest in the possibility of getting samples of permanently-shadowed soil so that the solar-wind chemists could look at material that hadn't been directly exposed for some period of time. I don't know if anything ever came of it, but we talked about it a lot over the years."] [As of 1991, very little has ever been published with regard to the shadowed soil samples. As

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, that's from about 1 centimeter down...1 to 2 centimeters. And the next one is down to about 5...5 or 6. (Pause) And it's got some chips in it. [Jack uses a one-handed scooping motion.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: That's bag 456, Bob. 122:15:55 Parker: Copy that. [Jack stumbles and spills some of the sample.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Shoot. (Pause; Jack laughs)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, I know. I know.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Moving out of the field-of-view) Oh, shoot. (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Hey! 1.2 kilometers is a long way from the LM. Look at the Challenger down there. Makes you get a feel for how big this valley really is.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I'd rather not. (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay. I'll help you.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I got it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Turn around and let me help you get these in your bag.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I learned how. [Jack has probably dropped the scoop and may, at this point, have devised the trick of stepping on the head to raise the handle to an easy-grabbing height.] Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: You learn of necessity out here. [Cernan - "You learned how to maneuver; you learned how to walk; you learned how to bend over to help each other; you eventually learned how to swing the hammer better; you learned how to pick up soil samples. You learned how to make your movements more efficient and productive."]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: (Putting the sample bags in Jack's SCB) Okay. See if we can't fill this up for Christmas. (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, let's...You happy there?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Yeah,.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Let's get your "after"...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay. [The "after" is AS17-134- 20396 .] [The sample is 71055 , a 670 gram piece of vesicular ilmenite basalt. Journal contributor Yuri Krasilnikov has created a before/after animation ( 352k ) from 20394 and 96. See, also, a side-by-side comparison with the second "before" photo AS17-134- 20395 .]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: And if we can, we might get just a block instead of breaking on it, and then we'll go to the rake. Let's go around to the... [What Jack is suggesting is that, rather than pounding on the rock to break off another sample, they pick up a manageable piece off the surface. Gene retrieves the gnomon; Jack moves around to the east rim of the crater.] [Schmitt - "A block is a rock of almost any size, as long as its big enough that it clearly doesn't fall into the general size range of particles in the underlying regolith"]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Bob wants a core here, too, huh?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, but the rake's next, as you might imagine. Geno, now this stuff here looks a little less vesicular. Why don't we try that one? [Jack is standing at the east rim, gesturing at the rock around him.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Hey, look at this rock, where the vesicularity changes from a hummocky vesicularity to a very fine vesicular. Look at this. [Jack goes toward Gene, who is out of the TV picture. AS17-134- 20403 is a close-up Gene will take at 122:23:13 , after he and Jack get two chip samples. The approximate location of the contact between the two parts of the rock is labeled in a detail .]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Let me try and crack...See that? The change?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, that's what I'm after; that's it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Let's see if I can't crack...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: That's it. That's what I saw in that other boulder.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Let's see if I can't crack the corner and get that contact.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah. Or get a piece of both. I think you can get...if you can reach down there.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: See if I can't get a...(Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: That's a contact in a rock.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yep. [They are between the Rover and the first boulder that they sampled. Gene has set the gnomon on the ground south of the knee-high boulder and is taking "before" pictures from the south. In general, a contact is a surface defining a change in rock character within a single rock mass. Here, there is a change in vesicularity across the contact. They are not as close to the rim as they were before. Gene has taken a cross-Sun stereopair of the rock, and Jack has taken a down-Sun. Gene's "befores" are AS17-134- 20397 and 20398 and Jack's "before" is AS17-136- 20741 ).]

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Beautiful. And, do you guys see any 2-meter boulders around there?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: We just sampled one. [Houston is puzzled that the TV hasn't shown any of the large boulders (large enough to have been seen in the Apollo 15 pictures) at the place where Houston thinks they are. Jack is saying that they just sampled a boulder, albeit, one less than a meter high.] 122:18:08 Cernan: Well, I wish (garbled) get over here and try and knock it...

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Well, if that one showed up in the photos, I wonder why those down near the ALSEP didn't show up.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: No, we're not where you think we are. We're not sure where we are. [Journal Contributor David Harland notes that, as Jack implied at 122:02:14 , it is more important that they are collecting samples near Steno than it is to know exactly where they are. The Station location can be determined in post-flight analysis of the pans.] [Gene kneels east of the boulder and tries to get positioned so he can use the hammer effectively]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Gene, can you get down into that? Need some help?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, just give me the shovel to hold myself with. Give me a shovel. (Pause) [Takes the scoop in his left hand, moves his knees back a foot or so and leans forward on the scoop while wielding the hammer with his right. We can't see his right hand, but he evidently breaks off a piece with just a blow or two.] [Cernan - "Without the suit, I probably would have reached out with my left hand to brace myself on the rock, but that would have put me too close to the rock to hit it properly in the suit. So I used the scoop for support."]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: How about that one? Yeah.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Get that little piece.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, I see it. [Gene rises, apparently by pushing back against the scoop handle.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: It's pretty hard. See if I can't...It's low and hard to hit.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: How about coming around from this side?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Well, I got the gnomon in the wrong place really. 122:19:01 Schmitt: Let me see your...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Can you reach it? [Jack takes the hammer.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Well, I'm going to lean on the rock maybe. [Jack leans on the rock from the southwest.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I got that other little piece in sight. [Jack gives the rock two sharp hammer blow and a sample breaks loose.] [Schmitt - "Note the value of geological field experience!"]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, I got that piece in sight, too. Let me...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Get them both with your...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Let me get them both right now. [Gene uses the scoop to collect the fragment he broke off.] 122:19:21 Schmitt: You can stick that (scoop) in the ground if you...(Pause) (To Houston) Okay, this is a sample of the more coarsely vesicular rock. (Pause) [Still leaning on the rock, Jack examines the fresh face and then looks over at Gene. He does so mostly by turning his head inside the helmet; there is some slight rotation of Jack's body in that direction.] [Gene has raised the sccop to his left hand so he can grab the sample.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: You got it in your hand?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I got them both (in sight). I think, actually, we got a sample of both sides; but I wouldn't bet on it. [Jack delivers one sharp blow on the east face and knocks off a piece.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay, I just got a chunk of that side. (Long Pause) [After hitting the east face twice more, without dislodging anything, Jack tries to change his grip by tossing the hammer but misses and almost drops it.] [Gene collects the first fragment Jack knocked off. Because Gene is holding the top of the scoop handle in his left hand, he rests the scoop head on his left hand and then moves his right hand down the handle toward the head to shorten the distance he'll have to raise his right arm to tip the fragment into his left hand.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, I got both of these.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Using the hammer to point to the fragment he dislodged from the east face) See that rock right over there on the little mound, just projecting out of the edge of it?

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Where are you looking?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Right over there.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Here?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: No.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Here?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Where I'm pointing.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: (Moving the scoop a foot eastward) There?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: There you go; you just about touched it. Right there, that piece. Video Clip ( 3 min 33 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, let me get these in a bag here. (Long Pause) [Gene hasn't yet collected the east-face fragment. He plants the scoop so he can get a sample bag off his camera. Jack hammers the rock four times without success. Even an experienced field geologist doesn't always dislodge the piece he wants.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Well...

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I'll get that piece.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: (Pushing himself upright) And that's the samples from either side of the contact anyway.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Can you get a bag... [Evidently, Gene was unable to get a bag, perhaps because he is holding the samle in his left hand.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: They're pretty small (samples). (Pause)

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Give me the hammer, and get a bag and I'll...

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: You take the hammer.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: I got these in my hand I want to put there.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Okay. Bag 477 is the coarsely vesicular rock.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Are two of them there? I hope two of them fell in.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: No, I only got one.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay, here's that other one. It had to fall right here.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: I don't think it ever...There it is; get your tongs.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Right here?

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Now you're full of dirt in the scoop; you just covered it up.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: (Using the scoop) Got it; I got it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Here, put it in here with the dirt. That's good. A little dirt never hurt anybody. (Holding the sample bag low) Got it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: There it is.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Got it.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: Okay.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: 477 are two chips. They're small, but I think they'll (tell you) if there's any compositional difference.

A17A1220706.speaker: Cernan
A17A1220706.text: (Preparing to collect the east-face fragment, pointing with the scoop) Are these two are the ones you saw? That right there? (Pause) That's what you pointed at. [Gene uses the scoop to pick the fragment off the surface, trying to get as little soil as possible.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah, I think you got it. 122:21:34 Cernan: Okay. I'm going to take a close-up stereo on that contact.

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yeah. Definitely. [Jack puts the sample bags in Gene's SCB, then gets another bag for the last sample. Before taking his close-ups, Gene takes a cross-Sun "after", AS17-134- 20399 , and a "locator", AS17-134- 20400 , toward the Rover.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Parker
A17A1220706.text: Okay; and, Jack and Gene, when you get done with that boulder, we'd like you to move on to a rake-soil sample, please; and that'll be a kilogram sample, please. [That is, they will use the rake to collect about a kilogram of soil, about enough to fill one sample bag.]

A17A1220706.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1220706.text: Yes, sir; we're going to. We're going to. (Pause) In bag 478 is the chip from the more finely vesicular rock. Both of them are coarse. It's a small chip; but it'll tell the story, I think. [Jack puts this sample bag in Gene's SCB.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 14 min 42 sec )

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Dust, dust, dust, dust. (Giving Jack the scoop) Here you are. I'll go ahead and get a close-up (garbled)...

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Get a close-up, and I'll get the rake. I'll get started on the rake.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay. [Gene goes to the Rover; Jack goes to the Rover, out of the picture.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Gene, if you can pick up one more rock in that picture, with your tongs, let's bag it.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: I'll get it.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: As you come back. [Schmitt - "I was just telling Gene to bootleg another sample. If he picked one up out of the area he'd just photographed, then Houston could probably identify it."]

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: And, 17; we'd like to have you guys...

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Sure wish I could read this (camera setting).

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: ...driving in 10 minutes, please.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Nag, nag, nag.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: That's right, that's right, that's right.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Boy, I can't see my camera (f-stop) setting, it's so full of dust.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: (To Bob) Okay. I guess you want to sort of (get the rake sample)...out in nothing's land here, huh? (No answer from Houston) I can bag it for you, Geno.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Roger. 122:23:13 Cernan: That's all right. I want to get this close-up here. [Fendell finds Gene again; he is taking pictures. His close-up photos of the second boulder are AS17-134- 20401 to 20404 .]

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Okay, I've moved about 5 to 8 meters northeast of the Rover. And as soon as Gene gets here with the gnomon...(Pause) Video Clip ( 3 min 18 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Coming, coming. (Pause) [Gene gets a sample with his tongs. The operation of his yo-yo is clearly visible. Gene goes to Jack northeast of the Rover, out of the TV picture. Fendell pans to follow Gene.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Bob, I've got a sample that was laying next to that boulder. I did not get an "after" picture of it; but, as I was taking my cross-Sun pictures, it is on my side of the boulder just 4 or 5 inches, covered with the dark mantle.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: I think we probably disturbed that one. It'll probably show up in the "befores".

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay, where do you want a rake. (Pause)

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: And that (meaning the extra rock sample)'s in bag 479.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Okay.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Gene, let's rake right out there.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Look, let's go ahead and bag that one (that is, put it in Gene's SCB); and I'll get the gnomon out there.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Okay.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Bob, as you might have seen from the camera, up towards where we think Emory is you get a pretty high concentration of boulders up there.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Okay. And I think that that's where we thought we were, a little bit closer to Emory than you are.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Well, we thought about going on up there; although we're in a pretty good area here, too, from the standpoint of boulders.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Yeah.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Again, I think...(To Jack) Facing the Sun. [Jack is just in view; Gene is reminding him to position the gnomon color chart so that it is fully sunlit. A photograph of Jack positioning the SEP transmitter, AS17-134- 20438 , is a good illustration of Jack's posture at this point.] [Cernan - "It was even awkward to get the gnomon down on a level piece of ground. You didn't want to drop it from a foot or two up, so you had to bend one knee, get the other leg out to the side, and lean sideways, very much like you sometimes had to in order to use the hammer. It was another one of ways you learned ho

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: I think for the most part, large and small, all the fragments seem to be filleted or even mantled by the dark material. [Schmitt - "Filleting is a natural consequence of the continual gardening of the upper regolith layers by the impacts of small meteors. Any boulder that's exposed will have material thrown against it that will collect at the base. The original thoughts about the 'dark mantle' material was that it had been put down very late, that it was very young; and that it might have been filleting the boulders. Of course, the truth is that the regolith and the dark material were intimate

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Let me get out of your way.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Boy, I've got to clean my camera; I can't even see. (To Jack) What area are you going to rake?

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: To your left of the...Well, ahead of the gnomon and to your left, there. [Schmitt - "As with any of the other sampling procedures, you took a set of pre-sampling documentation photographs and then drug the rake basket through the regolith until you had a reasonable number of small fragments. Studies of samples from some of the early missions has suggested that, in the walnut-sized fragment population, you got more fragments from outside the immediate area than in any other size range. So the rake was designed to maximize the yield of these 'exotics'."]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay, I got it. [Fendell pulls back on the TV zoom, bringing both of the astronauts into the frame. Gene and Jack are both taking "before" photos of the rake area. Gene's pictures are AS17-134- 20405 to 20407 and Jack's are AS17-136- 20742 and 20743 .]

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: (Referring to Gene's remark about the prevalence of filleting) Okay, Gene, we copy that. That's a good observation. And I also gathered that most of the rocks look pretty much the same.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: That's what I said.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Yeah, except a change in vesicularity...

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Roger.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: ...in terms of the size of vesicles, where I described one as being a more hummocky vesicular-type rock. The first time I've noticed any of the dark minerals was when we took that one big, flat chip off that boulder.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Okay; copy that. [Jack takes the first rake swath, standing with his right foot forward and his body turned to his left, dragging the rake with his right hand as he moves backwards.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: I didn't look at it that close to see what it was.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Copy that, guys. [Jack finishes the first swath. The rake is not penetrating very far into the soil.] 122:26:14 Cernan: I'm going to get a pan, Jack, while you're doing that.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Okay.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Good idea, Gene. (Long Pause) [Jack takes three more swaths, shaking dirt out between the tines after each one. Gene's pan consists of frames AS17-134- 20408 to 20431 .] [Frames 20425 and 20426 are two views ( 554k ) of Jack with a large collection of small rocks he just collected with the rake. In the first, he has his left hand under rake head where it is attached to the extension handle and is about to lift it up to horizontal so he can carry it over to Gene. In the second picture, he is a lot closer to Gene, who will get a sample bag out once he finishes the pan.] Video Clip ( 2 min 41 sec

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Man, are there some good targets for the 500(-millimeter camera) around here. (Pause) We've got to get those Massifs with the 500. (Pause) [Jack takes swaths number 5 and 6; the bottom of his SCB is loose.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: And, 17; again, a reminder...

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: And, Bob, I'm really only penetrating about, at the most, 3 centimeters into this area with the rake. I've picked up a very good sample of boulders (fragments) but most of them were in that distance of the surface and projecting out of it.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Okay; I copy that.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: You ready, Gene?

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: A couple of more (pictures), Jack. (Pause) Okay, coming at you (with a sample bag). Bob, the pan is complete. I'll give you a frame count shortly.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Copy that, Geno.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: There's two bags, I think. [Gene is not in the TV picture.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Two bags full. First bag is 457...

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Copy that. [Fendell pulls back on the zoom so that Gene can be seen.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: ...457. (Pause) Don't let me lose them. That's enough. Give me a couple of small ones.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Okay.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay, that's good. That's good. Okay. (Pause) [Gene puts the sample bag in Jack's SCB.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Here, they are. [Neither Gene nor Jack is sounding punchy any more.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: (Getting another bag) Okay, and bag 458 is the rest of the rake sample. They're all fragments.

A17A1222211.speaker: Parker
A17A1222211.text: Copy that. Now we need the kilogram of the soil.

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay, Bob. All the fragments, of course, are completely covered with the mantle (meaning soil); and they are slightly...oh, maybe 20 percent vesicular. I just took a glance at them. But, for the most part, they appear to be rounded to subrounded fragments. (Pause)

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: (To Jack) Okay. Let's get the kilogram. (Pause) [Fendell pans up and then down; neither Jack nor Gene is in the picture when he finishes.] Video Clip ( 3 min 44 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 37 Mb MPEG )

A17A1222211.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1222211.text: Okay. (Pause) Aghh! Well, shoot. Start all over. [Apparently, Jack has poured most of the soil onto the ground, not into the bag. The rake has solid metal sides so that, rotated ninety degrees, it can be used as a big scoop.]

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Try it again. 459 will get the kilogram, Bob.

A17A1222211.speaker: Cernan
A17A1222211.text: Okay. (Pause) Here's your charge. I think we're learning, (and) that's half of the first EVA. Okay, Bob, we are rolling. Mark it.

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1222922csm.text: (I'll) get some more. [Fendell pulls back on the zoom again and finds Jack using the rake.]

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1222922csm.text: Yeah, yeah, I can close it.

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1222922csm.text: That's a good kilogram. [The sample bags are square and were designed to hold rocks up to 11 cm in diameter. The volume of such a rock is about 700 cc's and bags could clearly hold a greater volume of soil. Soil poured loosely into a bag would have a density of no less than about 1.3 kg per liter and, consequently, a kilogram would occupy a volume of no more than about 800 cc's.]

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1222922csm.text: Well, I just can't even read my camera anymore. I've got to learn how to control the dust. Okay, that's in (Jack's SCB).

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1222922csm.text: I tried to blow the dust off my camera! [Not a very useful thing to try when wearing a helmet.]

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1222922csm.text: I think it's going to be hard to get a double core here. We could try a single right there. (Pause) 122:30:18 Cernan: Bob, we got time to get the core?

a17_1222922csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1222922csm.text: Negative. The core has been deleted. We'd like for you to get your second pan, Jack, and then we'll press on. 122:30:27 Schmitt: Okay. (Pause) [Jack retrieves the rake and goes to the Rover. Gene takes the "after" picture, AS17-134- 20432 .] [Jack had planned to take two pans at Station 1 - one at the start and one at the end - but, for some reason, did not take the initial pan and, instead, went over to the boulders to examine them right away. Although Parker may suspect that the first pan wasn't taken, he doesn't know that for certain. The two pans, had they both been taken, would have provi

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: Okay. (Pause) Here's your charge. I think we're learning, (and) that's half of the first EVA. Okay, Bob, we are rolling. Mark it.

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: Okay, copy that, Jack...(correcting himself) Gene. (Pause) Traverse to Station 1 Apollo 17 Journal Return to the LM and SEP Deployment

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Okay, where did they want it (Meaning the seismic charge) deployed?

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: Six-tenths of a kilometer.

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Back, huh?

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: Rog. It'll be at a range of 0.6, guys.

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: You've got a block right ahead of you.

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: I got it.

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: Okay. And remember you'll be taking photos coming back here, Jack...

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Okay.

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: ...if you get a chance (as per LMP-33 ).

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Yes, sir. Thank you. I got a few going out, Bob, but they weren't too well spaced. [Schmitt - "The basic use of the photographs was supposed to have been the location of observations, although nobody's ever done very much of that analysis. I think, also, that these traverse photos were added as a response to the problem that the Apollo 16 (means 15) crew had in knowing where they were, at least on their first traverse. And, finally, if you weren't doing anything else but riding, you might as well take pictures and get more information and documentation. There was plenty of film. And some of th

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: Okay. And I assume you've got the low-gain antenna aligned.

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: Yes, sir; it's aligned. Okay. That's got to be Trident, Jack, because that's too big for anything else. (Pause)

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Okay, Houston. There's the classic raindrop pattern over this fine debris. I'd say that the surface definitely is sorted: the fine regolithic material forming one fraction and then the blocks another. The blocks are probably...Those blocks greater than 2 centimeters in diameter, in general, make up (that is, cover) less than 10 percent of the surface. But there are some big ones, fairly uniformly distributed. There are blocks a meter in diameter.

A17A1223634.speaker: Parker
A17A1223634.text: Copy that. [AS17-135- 20540 will be taken at the SEP at the start of EVA-2 and shows the raindrop pattern quite well.] 122:38:36 Cernan: Hey, Jack, that big crater out there at 2 o'clock (relative to his current heading, which is roughly north) has probably got to be Sherlock. That's got to be Sherlock over there. [A detail from AS17-136- 20783 shows the view in the general direction of Sherlock. I suspect that Sherlock is hidden by its own rim and that the obvious crater in the middle distance is a nameless foreground feature. A detail ( 518k ) from Pan Camera frame 2309 shows Steno in the ce

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Yeah, probably. I think the only place I've really identified that we can go to is to Station 6.

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: Yeah, but we've got to get on a high vantage point here one of these days.

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Yeah. (Pause) Well, I think we'll find Camelot without any problem.

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: (Guffawing) Yeah. [Cernan - "In looking at some of the pictures that Jack took on the way back to the LM, it's really obvious how difficult it was to know where you were in that three-dimensional environment. You could get up on high spots and orient yourself; and you always knew where you were in the valley - where you were in the 'big picture' - and where you were in relation to the LM. But the Rover Nav system really allowed you to go where you wanted to go fairly precisely. Getting back to the LM would have been easy enough without the Nav system. You could follow the Rover tracks back and

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: Okay, watch. I'm going through it.

A17A1223634.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1223634.text: Okay. No problem.

A17A1223634.speaker: Cernan
A17A1223634.text: No, I'd rather straddle or go through those little ones. [Gene would rather have pitch motion than roll.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1223908csm.text: Thank heavens.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, Bob, here's another crater about the same size we sampled (at) the last station. And it doesn't have as many blocks, but it does have blocks. And from this distance, their vesicular texture and their light color shows up very well. I suspect they're the same general kind. There's a glass-bottom crater. [Schmitt - "The glass-bottomed craters generally had a glass-lined central pit, a shelf surrounding that, and then the rim."]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. You got a range and bearing, there, guys, please.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Copy that. [Checklist pages CDR-30 and LMP-32 are identical, each containing a sketch map of the return traverse.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Did you take a picture, Jack?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [The photo may be AS17-136- 20784 , which Jack probably took at about 122:39:09.] 122:39:47 Schmitt: You're pointed right at Station 6, I think, Gene. [In a labeled detail from AS17-136- 20795 the dark boulder is on the left and the Station 6 boulder is on the right.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: I think you may be right. There's that boulder. I just want to get up here where I can (garbled)...

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Not the one on the (boulder) track but the one over there to the right of that. (Pause) Unless the one with the track...I've got mixed emotions (as to) which is 6. 122:40:04 Cernan: Look over there to the left. You see that. (Static)

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1223908csm.text: Ron, are you out - glued to a window, or are you just eating now?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah. [Gene probably turned the Rover to get a better view. At about this time, Jack took AS17-136- 20797 to 20799 .] [Frame AS17-136- 20799 shows the LM. A detail , rotate 15 degrees to the right, shows the LM subtending about 0.05 fiducial spacings or about 0.5 degrees. The LM is 7 meters tall, implying a distance of about 0.8 km. This is consistent with Gene report of a range of 0.7 km at 122:41:07, below.] [The sequence from 20797 to 814 is presented in a PDF document ( 13 Mb PDF ).] [For a long time I thought Jack took 20797-20799 at about 122:41:36 , when Gene noticed the white mantle of

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: That's Trident. Man, I'll tell you. [On CDR-30 , Trident is the trio of craters just to the left of the sharp bend in the planned return traverse at 296/0.5.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Look at this thing. That looks like the same kind of rock except it doesn't have any vesicles. 122:40:19 Cernan: There's some white stuff in that rock. Just let me take a quick pic (static, probably as Gene turns). See that one right in front of us? Take a picture of it.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Oh, you mean this one, here.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Oh, that's a big zap pit, isn't it? Take a picture of that? [This rock is almost certainly the large one on the right in AS17-136- 20800 . It also appears near the left edge in 20798 .]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah, they're big zap pits. Same rock with big zap pits. (Pause) I've got to change the (focus)...I was too close. Although there are...I think those are zap pits. It's a little hard to say.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Looks like a big chip out of the rock.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: They're white halos; it just has more of them.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: But it's a big one; it's about an inch and a half or 2 inches across.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: I tell you, I've got to go and get my size and geometry squared away. [Cernan - "The further away things were, the harder it was to judge size and distance. Things always looked closer and smaller than they really were. After a while you began to recalibrate your brain, but it was always deceptive."]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, 17, how about...

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Going through this one?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: ...range and bearing?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: (To Jack) Yep. (Responding to Bob) Okay. 341/0.7. Bob, we're moving at about 11 clicks (kilometers per hour) right now.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Copy that. Beautiful. Remember the charge goes off at 0.6.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Doesn't sound like...(Answering Bob) Okay. (Pause)

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, we want to... 122:41:36 Cernan: Oh, there's the mantle. There's the white (means "light") mantle. Jack, look over there. Can you look to your left?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah, it does. Yeah.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: That's the white mantle. [A portion of the western valley floor is covered by light-colored material which, in overhead photographs, appears to be the result of a South Massif avalanche. During the second EVA, Gene and Jack will drive onto the light mantle and up onto the Jefferson-Lincoln-Lee Scarp, collecting samples and photographic evidence which will support the avalanche interpretation and give a 100 million year age.] 122:41:42 Schmitt: Swing around that way.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Call it a slide or not, but that's the white mantle. Whoo! That's my first real good picture (means 'view') of it. That is something! [Frame AS17-136- 20806 shows Gene beginning to turn to the west. He may have done so to avoid the rock on the right - the top of which can be seen beyond the TV camera in 20805 - and noticed the white mantle off to his left. Frame 20810 is the fullest view to the west. After Jack takes that frame, Gene turns back toward the north.] 122:41:52 Schmitt: Okay, I got some of that. Okay, how are we doing? [Jack is asking Gene about their range from the SEP transmitter

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. I got a couple of shots right out in there.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. Coming right around to you.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Oh, that's good. Hold that heading. Whoa. That'll be good.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Right here?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah, whoa. [They're stopping so Jack can deploy the seismic charge.] 122:42:15 Cernan: Okay. Let me get my...Okay, I got my "locator".

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, now (for) this one we want me to get a partial pan until something's identified. [Horizon features in the photographs can be used to triangulate the deployment site. Gene's locator shots are AS17-134- 20433 and 20434 and Jack's photo at the same location and orientation is AS17-136- 20814 >. See, also, a comparison .]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. We'll do that. We've got to turn that way anyway.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, pin 1, pull, Safe. Pin 2, pull, Safe. Pin 3, Mark it, pull, Safe.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. And I copy that as charge number 7.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: That's affirm.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. And we'd like a frame number when you get done there, Jack, after you get it (the charge) on the ground.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, stand by. (Pause) (To Gene) Okay. I think we'll miss that. [Jack has tried to put the charge far enough out to the side so that they won't hit it with the Rover. Training photo 72-H-1411 shows back-up LMP Charlie Duke deploying a charge from his Rover seat.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. Bearing (and range) is 339/0.6. 122:43:12 Schmitt: Okay, start a pan around it, Gene...

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Copy that, Gene...

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, let me get it out...Okay, I'm going to start slowly around it.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay. [Gene is driving the Rover in a slow, clockwise circle while Jack takes pictures. This is the "partial pan" listed on CDR-31 . Although there is virtually no chance of the charge going off if they hit it in the Rover, the antenna needs to be upright so that it can receive the detonation signal from the Central Station. As Gene discusses at 141:36:23 , the front-and-rear steering dictates a right-hand turn to avoid the charge.]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Going to miss it?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Yeah; by a lot.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, taking your pictures?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Yes, sir.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: (Static) (Garbled) wheels cleared it by...got to be a lot. (Pause)

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1223908csm.text: Is my low gain dropping out? (Pause) How much are my wheels missing it by, going around?

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Lots. About a meter. Okay. 122:43:44 Cernan: Okay. We're on our way. The low gain is set again. (Pause) Okay, we're heading on back to SEP.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, and a frame count there, Jack.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, the pan was more or less complete at 146.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Copy, 146 on (magazine) Hotel. (Pause) [Jack gave Bob a frame count of 95 when they were about to leave Station 1 at 122:33:08 . He had just taken frame AS17-136- 20776 . That implies that Jack 'more or less' completed the pan with 20827 . An examination of the frames suggests that Gene started driving off in a northwesterly direction after Jack took 20828 . A comparison of details 20828 and 20813 ( 391k ) indicates that 20828 was taken from a spot a bit farther north than 20813 but along much the same line-of-sight. In 20828, the Rover tracks laid down after Jack took 20813 are off-camera to

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: Bob, you know, the more I look at this - (To Gene) watch out for those babies there - at this dark dust, if you will, the more it doesn't seem like the kind of thing you'd expect to have been derived from the underlying bedrock. But I think you're going to have to play that game in the lab right now. [Schmitt - "By itself, the bedrock isn't dark enough to give you the dark mantle; and, if you grind it up, it's going to get even lighter in color."]

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, I copy that. Can you...

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: We'll see how it works out later.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Roger.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1223908csm.text: It just seems dark and much too fine grain. You don't have the impression that you're getting the size distribution you'd expect to get by having all these blocks around.

a17_1223908csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1223908csm.text: Okay, I copy that.

A17A1225539.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1225539.text: (Looking at his checklist) Okay, I'll deploy number 2 and 4. And, let's see, that's number 1. (Long Pause) [Gene appears briefly in the TV picture; he is at his seat, holding the dustbrush . The number 2 reel is the west arm and number 4 is the north arm. Number 1 is the east arm, and number 3 is the south arm.]

A17A1225539.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1225539.text: So this one must be number 2. It is. (Pause)

A17A1225539.speaker: Cernan
A17A1225539.text: Okay, I'm almost there, Jack. (Going to the front of the Rover) Let me run around and dust! (Pause) Let me tell you, this dust isn't going to be fun tomorrow! [Cernan - "The dust on the battery covers and everything else was thick enough to write in. With a working fender you'd always got a light film of dust; but this was 'dirt' dust."] [ Fendell pans past Jack, who is now south of the Rover. His shadow appears to be 15-20 feet long.]

A17A1225539.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1225539.text: Okay, I won't bore you with details on why you see the antenna all over the ground (chuckles), but it has to do with one-sixth g. (Pause)

A17A1225539.speaker: Parker
A17A1225539.text: Roger, Jack. Understand you dropped a couple of the antenna reels. [In Houston, Bob is being told that the antenna reels and wires can rapidly become a "Chinese Puzzle" unless they are untangled very carefully.]

A17A1225539.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1225539.text: You know, Bob, they're very...(Responding to Bob) More accurately, I dropped three of them. Bob, you know this fine-grained dust that we're in could be ground-up pyroclastic. It might grind more easily than other things, and the blocks are those that have been excavated from below that pyroclastic by the larger craters and some of the smaller ones in the area. [Schmitt - "There was a great deal of fine material in the regolith and, as it turned out, much of that was due to the orange and black pyroclastic glass which was present throughout the dark mantle. Just from the appearance of the area

A17A1225539.speaker: Cernan
A17A1225539.text: Mark, gravimeter reading. [Gene crosses in front of the panning TV; he is headed for Jack's position.]

A17A1225539.speaker: Parker
A17A1225539.text: (Responding to Jack's pyroclastic theory) Roger, Jack. That would make a nice story, wouldn't it?

A17A1225539.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1225539.text: Well, you'd think glassy pyroclastic might turn into regolith a little bit faster than some of these other things. But we'll check that one out.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1225813csm.text: Ron, you're less than a minute to Lunar Sounder, Operate and Standby.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: You want (antenna reel number) 2?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Two, and you get 1. Right there. [Jack will take reel 2 and deploy the western arm; Gene will take reel 1 and deploy the eastern arm.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1225813csm.text: And, Jack, did you get the reels straightened out again?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Yeah, they're okay.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1225813csm.text: Thank you.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: How can you stop a crew like this?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1225813csm.text: I don't know any way.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: In all modesty, I mean. (Pause) [Fendell finds Gene, who is picking up an antenna reel with his tongs.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, Geno, I'm on my way. Pull gently on that thing (the SEP transmitter) because it's awful easy to knock it over. I had that geophone module all over the place. [That is, when Jack was deploying the geophones at the ALSEP site, any tension he got in the cables tended to move the central module.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: I can't tell whether I'm pulling gently or not. [Fendell is watching the SEP transmitter, which moves a couple of inches in Gene's direction. When Gene and Jack get to the ends of the wires, they will sight back across the transmitter at each other to make sure their lines are straight.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Any time you feel a tug, stop. (Pause) [The transmitter moves a couple of inches east again.] Video Clip ( 3 min 33 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1225813csm.text: (Seeing the motion) Careful, guys.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: At least we're pulling at the base. (Pause) [The antenna wires may be attached low on the unit; it shows no signs of tipping over but, rather, just slides through the soil.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Mark it.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: I better watch what I'm backing into. There's a lot of holes around here. (Pause) [The two remaining antenna reels are visible in the TV, hanging from the north face of the transmitter. Fendell pans counter-clockwise away from the transmitter, and then reverses direction.] 122:59:28 Schmitt: Well, it happened, Bob. I'm glad we Velcroed those tabs. (Pause)

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, I'm at the end, Jack. Are you having...

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Well, what happened was (that) which we thought might happen. It twisted on my...I'll be there in just a second. [Neither Cernan, Schmitt nor Parker remembers what it was they "thought might happen."]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, I want f/11 at 1/250 (of a second exposure) and 74 feet (focus). (Pause) Well...Ah, ah, ah, ah. Ah, ah, yes; you're pulling it over.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1225813csm.text: You can go Recorder, Off, now, Ron.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: I'm not. You are.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: No, I'm not. I've got all sorts of slack in here.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay. Recorder - is Off.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, it's okay. (Pause) All right.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Are you out there?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Yes. [Fendell gets as far as the South Massif in his clockwise pan and reverses direction again.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, let me back up a skosh and take the slack out. And I would say, offhand...Oh, boy. That's about as close to a one-sixth-g orthogonal...at least, not orthogonal yet, but straight-lined. (Pause) That's it Jack, here. Stay there, and I'll take a picture.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: I thought you did. 123:01:05 Cernan: No. Okay, I got it now. [Fendell pans past Gene, who standing up-Sun of the Rover. His picture of Jack and of the east/west antenna arms is AS17-134- 20435 .]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Hey, if you try and stick that thing (the reel) in (the ground), Jack, you're going to fall over. Just set it down, and we'll stay away from it.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Yup. You talked me into it.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: That was a good idea, but...That's a good straight line. [They head back to the transmitter. There is no evidence that there were any anchors or flags for the ends of the SEP antenna wires. Jack suspects that they had decided, late in training, to stick the reels into the ground to serve as anchors and/or markers. Evidently, the attempt to use them as anchors was unsuccessful. Gene remembers that they planned to use the reels as markers. Bob agrees.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay. Radar's coming Off, Data System is coming On.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: (Singing) We were strolling in the (pause) Taurus one day...Well, we've had lots of good ideas in our time. [Mick Hyde calls our attention to the fact that Jack uses the word 'Taurus' here, rather than 'park' as originally transcribed. Jack sang another variation of "While Strolling Through the Park One Day" at 121:35:45 , using the word 'Moon' to replace 'park'. The pause in the rendition here suggests that he was trying to think of an alternative to 'Moon'; but his tone of voice when singing 'Taurus' and the disclaimer that follows indicate that he isn't happy with the choice.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: High Gain Antenna is going to Power.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Oh, boy; the thing that makes me sick is losing that fender. I can stand a lot of things, but I sure don't like that.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Manual, Wide.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, I get (reel) number 4.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Where is it? Is that the one on the ground?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: It's probably the one on the ground. Got it? (Pause)

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Is that the right one?

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Well, 3...No, this is yours.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: No. Take it; doesn't make any difference. [Fendell finds both of them at the transmitter. The checklist calls for Jack to take reel 4 to the north and Gene to take reel 3 to the south. However, reversing roles will not matter at all.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, I'm deploying the...The LMP's deploying reel 3 for your photography purposes. Video Clip ( 3 min 56 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 39 Mb MPEG )

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay. SM/AC Power is coming On.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1225813csm.text: Roger. Copy that. [Jack heads south; Gene drops his antenna.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Oh, (subvocally) shit. [Journal Contributor George Giusti, noting that I had failed to transcribe Gene's complete transmission, writes "My contemporaneous notes of 12/11/72 record Gene actually saying 'Oh, shit!'. Since I was in my teen years during Apollo 17, I am sure that I was particularly acute to listening and recording any profanity I would hear. (My wife likes to say my immaturity has only improved over the years!). In listening to (Larry) Haskin's (video) tape and replaying my own tapes recorded at the time, I do hear Gene mentioning the 'forbidden' word, although somewhat subvocally.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: (Turning to face Gene) Hey, push that (?) in.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: (Garbled)

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: (Taunting) Ha, ha, ha. Ha, ha, ha. Serves you right. (Pause) [Jack returns to the transmitter; Gene retrieves the antenna with his tongs.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: Mapping Camera is Standby. Self test to heaters.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: This doesn't push. [Jack doesn't remember what "this" was; nor what "that" might have been at 123:02:30.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Okay, I'm ready to stroll. (Long Pause) [Jack heads south again. Gene goes north. Fendell follows Jack, who lopes directly away from the transmitter. The dust he kicks up scatters sunlight toward the TV. Jack seems to be going down a slope away from the Rover, but probably isn't.] [Cernan - "The TV camera was mounted about chest high (about 45 inches), so it's hard to say if that has any effect on your impression. Maybe it's just difficult to get a perspective on the surface. You don't have anything familiar to help you get a reference. For example, if you've got a little rise in front of you,

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: UV is On. IR is On.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: [Cough] UV Cover is going Open. Barber pole and a gray.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1225813csm.text: IR is Open. Barber pole and a gray.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Da da, dee do. 123:03:25 Cernan: (Pleased with himself) I found a brown rock that I'm going to bring back!

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Please do. [Jack stops and looks back.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: I think it's the back side of a piece of glass, but it's brown. [As we will discover at 123:28:18 and following, this is actually a piece of foam packing which protected the Rover high-gain antenna or some other piece of equipment during the trip from Earth. Ever since Gene discarded the pieces of foam near the LM, gas trapped in the foam lattice has been heating in the sunlight. Evidently, at some time since then, one or more pieces exploded and/or vented, throwing at least one fragment the hundred meters out to the SEP site.]

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: (Looking back) Well, I think I'm more or less on your (Rover) track. It wiggled a little bit.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1225813csm.text: Well, we're...(To himself) Oh, oh, oh, ooh, stop, Geno. Okay, Jack, wait a minute. That looks orthogonal to me.

a17_1225813csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1225813csm.text: Got your picture? 123:04:03 Cernan: Will have in a sec. Wait a minute. Every time I do something, I change the setting. Okay, I got it. (Pause) [Jack drops the antenna on the ground, and heads back toward the transmitter. Gene's picture is AS17-134- 20436 .]

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1231520csm.text: Hey, Ron. You can go to Block. The computer's yours.

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1231520csm.text: Jack, did you copy my comments about putting that thing (the football-sized sample of the boulder) in the SRC perhaps?

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231520csm.text: Well, it was pretty big. It's in the big bag now. We can do that.

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1231520csm.text: Well, I'd get the other samples - the small ones and particular(ly the) soils - in the SRC first.

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231520csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) (To Gene) Are you through (parking)?

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231520csm.text: No, I'm going right about here. Now I'm done.

a17_1231520csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231520csm.text: Okay, Bob, 086 (bearing to SEP), 0.5 (distance driven since resetting, mostly in laying out the antenna pattern), 0.1 (range to SEP), 108, 102 (amp hours). Standby one. Okay. Amp-hours are at 108, 102; volts are 74 and 75. Batteries are 108 (degrees) and 123. Motors are all off scale low, all four of them. MP3 Audio Clip ( 19 min 19 sec )

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: (To Bob) Okay, the SEP receiver temp is four-five. Four-five.

A17A1231710.speaker: Parker
A17A1231710.text: Copy; four-five. Beautiful. 123:17:15 Schmitt: (To Gene) You know, I think they left some Velcro off of this thing (the SEP receiver), Gene. There's no Velcro holding those (thermal cover) flaps down. [During the traverses, the radiator on the top of the SEP is normally covered with thermal blankets held down by pieces of Velcro glued to tabs on the covers and to the thermal bag enclosing the body of the SEP receiver. The glue holding the Velcro on the thermal bag has failed and the covers are now loose.]

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Isn't there?

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: No. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: I've got to get the brush and dust that thing. (I'll be) a minute or two. Okay, let me get the high gain. (Long Pause)

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: (Facetiously) I feel I'm gonna take some core tubes tomorrow.

A17A1231710.speaker: Parker
A17A1231710.text: I have a feeling you've got a couple left over, don't you? [Jack was scheduled to use a drive tube at Station 1, but didn't for lack of time.]

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Bob, you got...

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: (Responding to Bob) Yep.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Bob, you got the high gain.

A17A1231710.speaker: Parker
A17A1231710.text: Okay, thank you.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Is that my bag (SCB-1), Jack, you got?

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: Yes.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: (Not having felt Jack take it off) That's pretty good. 123:18:26 Parker: Okay, let's put all the stuff in that bag (SCB-1), Jack; both the stuff that's in yours (SCB-2) and the stuff that's in Gene's. RealVideo Clip (8 min 38 sec) RealVideo Clip ( 2 min 50 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG Clip ) [TV on. Gene has parked the Rover roughly between the LM and the U.S. flag.]

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: Okay. (Pause) Two samples from under the LMP's seat.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Put these (unused sample bags) under the seat. Clean you up here while I'm at it. Oh, man, I tell you, it's going to take us half a dozen Sundays to dust. Look at that fender; that's terrible.

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: Okay, we do not bring up the LM ECS canister. Is that correct?

A17A1231710.speaker: Parker
A17A1231710.text: That's correct, 17.

A17A1231710.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1231710.text: Okay. (Pause) [Jack is referring to a replacement lithium hydroxide (LiOH) canister for the cabin Environmental Control System (ECS). The canisters remove carbon dioxide from the cabin air and need to be replaced at intervals through the mission. One replacement is stowed behind the ascent engine cover in the cabin, two others are stowed in the MESA. They will take one up to the cabin at the end of EVA-2 and the other at the end of EVA-3. At the moment, Jack is getting EVA Pallet 1 out of the MESA. Jack remembers that the pallet contains their food for the next 24 hours, along with such things

A17A1231710.speaker: Parker
A17A1231710.text: And, Jack, confirm you have the scissors in the ETB.

A17A1231710.speaker: Cernan
A17A1231710.text: Okay, and (garbled)

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1231900csm.text: Are we going to leave tank 3 - I mean, tank 2, H 2 Fan, On, all the time?

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1231900csm.text: Rog. H 2 tank 2 Fan, On, for all night.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Okay, you want to get my bag off?

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Yup. If you're ready.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Yup. (Pause) I've got to put those samples in the SRC...(correcting himself) in your bag (SCB-1); and we'll save this one (SCB-2), I guess.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Wait a minute. Let me clean you up.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Okay.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Did you get me cleaned up?

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Yeah, you've lost your...

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Wait a minute.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: ...your strap though, here.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1231900csm.text: Only thing we've got, Ron, is it looks like you've got to get the Bat B off the Charge and then - configure the comm, and you are all ready to bed down.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Wait a minute, now. (Pause) Okay, (can) you get my hook back up over here?

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Okay, turn around. Your hook's up, but I'm not sure I closed your other one.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: Take a look at it. 123:19:46 Schmitt: Yeah, your Velcro's (garbled). Okay, you're good.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: There you go. Okay, you're filling which bag? The...

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1231900csm.text: Okay. Battery B relay's breakers In. Charger's Off.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1231900csm.text: Putting them in the bag that goes into the SRC...

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: That's SCB-1.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1231900csm.text: Roger. [ Fendell pans to Jack, who is at his Rover seat. After all the samples are transferred to SCB-1, Gene will put it in the SRC.]

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: (To himself) Okay; let's see, (scanning checklist pages CDR-34 and ) off-load LM(P) PLSS, core cap dispenser, tools. (To Jack) Okay, as soon as you get that, I'll take that SCB-1 from you, and I'll close SRC-1.

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1231900csm.text: Okay; and I gather you didn't have any Rover samples today, did you, Jack?

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1231900csm.text: I've still got my tongs here. I got...

a17_1231900csm.speaker: Schmitt
