a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Your water hose.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Come around behind my shoulder.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Won't fit in there. (Pause) Okay, it's in there (that is, the OPS hose is connected) and it's locked, (garbled), and the dust cover is on.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: And now, we get to put your Purge (valve) in: 208.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Make sure it's in Low.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: It is, and Low, and the pin is in. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) And you like it where? Down a little bit?

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: No. Same place just... No, let me show you.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Right there?

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay; there. In.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Verify it's still in Low. Locked.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: And locked.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. That's good.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Let's get another zap of (drinking) water here. (Long Pause) If I have any more water I'll float out there.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: (Laughs) Good Navy man.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Be a good place to fill with water, you'd make a nice rec(reation) site out of this valley. You could put some cabins up on the side of the massifs. Nice flat bottom, no trees.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: No snags. [That is, there would be no submerged stumps to catch a fishing line.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: The fishing ought to be pretty good if you stocked it.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Have a Bear Island and a Family Island. [Jack named Bear Mountain for a peak near his boyhood home in Silver City, New Mexico. And he picked the name (West) Family Mountain to honor all of the NASA families. Bear Mountain is much smaller than either of the massifs and, if Taurus-Littrow could be flooded, it would become an island. The mountain that originally was named (Old) Family Mountain is also much smaller than the massifs.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: (Laughs) We're going to (have to) fill up the other end though, so it doesn't drain out.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Looks funny like that.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Lock it and turn your Descent Water, Off. (Long Pause) [They are turning off the flow of water from the supply tank in the Descent Stage. Next, they will don their helmets and gloves.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Snaps, snaps, snaps; the whole world is held together with snaps!

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, I've got my hand lubed. You can position your mike. [Although they have a lubricant that they applied to the glove-locking mechanism, the so-called quick disconnects, at the wrist, they had taken care of that before the rest period. Here, Gene is literally greasing his hand to try to prevent skin abrasion as he works in the glove.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: (Descent) water is going off.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. [Gene will now help Jack don his helmet.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Position your mikes. Now, before we turn the (PLSS) fans on and use (PLSS) battery power...Let's just look ahead; we got helmets ready to go... Drink bag position you're happy with.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Yeah, more or less a little far out, but I think...

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Make sure you've got the plug out.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. Plug is out. (Pause)

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: My end's right, now, but (garbled) even get it out.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Feel a little pressure in there. You might let out.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. And then we'll lower our protective visor and secure tool harness and self-doff straps. [The self-doff straps are attached to the sides of the visor assembly and can be used to release the tool harness.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, and that's...

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: That's already stowed. Okay. Let's start with you first. You can turn your...Let me get your LEVA then you can get it over your head and turn your O2...(correcting himself) your fan on, rather.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. (Pause)

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, you ready (for your helmet and LEVA )? (Pause) Okay, check all that...Wait. What is this right here? (Pause) Okay, now let me make sure it's in front of everything.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1401316csm.text: Roger. We got you. See any lava marks on the crater rims, there?

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: The alignment is way over here. Let me...

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: That's good.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. That's aligned right there. Oh, boy. That will never do. With that down in there.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, it's still clear.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Starting. (Pause) Manischewitz. (Pause)

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: I think it's caught on the food stick . You ought to open it up.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: I think you're right.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. Get it all the way off.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. Now let's try it. (Pause) Looks like it's going to be much better. Get it in back. (Pause)

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Want to make sure that thing is on! Nope, not happy yet. (Pause) Not happy yet.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Well, (do you) want me to squat down?

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1401316csm.text: [Garble]. Okay, Power is going On.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: I tell you, I got my fingers on it all the way around. Okay. It's locked. It's aligned. Better put your (PLSS) fan on here pretty quick. Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Fan's on.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, let me get you dressed up back here. (Garbled) center doesn't work, you're going to keep this thing...

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1401316csm.text: How about the freshness of the wall and ejecta materials, and the brightness of the rim deposits on Aitken while we have a minute here.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: And I'm vertical. [Oxygen enters the suit from the PLSS through vents at the neck ring and in the suit chest. There is a chest-mounted diverter valve which allows the astronaut to select the relative amount of flow through the vents and, in the vertical position, all of the flow is into the helmet through a vent at the back of the neck.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: You are vertical all right. Aghhh. Okay. You're covered down there. You are locked. Okay...Whoo! Okay? Guess it's my turn. (Pause) [Jack will now check Gene's suit and help him don his helmet.]

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Yup. Let's verify all these things.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay. Got your comm. That's your OPS; that's your inlet; that's your oxygen or your exhaust; and (that's) your purge valve.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay.

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1401316csm.text: And your water

a17_1401316csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1401316csm.text: Okay, let me take a look at all yours. Okay. That's locked. (Pause) Locked. That's locked; you're vertical. That's locked. That's locked. That's locked. Okay. Get my helmet on. The main thing is to get this stuff back over here.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1402251csm.text: You know something - the observation that I think is pretty significant is the fact that most of the 30-kilometer craters on the back side of the Moon seem to be fairly fresh. And any of them that are fresh - by fresh I mean you don't have any real definite ray pattern to them, but you've got a real smooth - not smooth but streaked straight - slope, 45-degree angle going down into the crater and the crater wall. And then you get down to the bottom of the crater, and you got a flat floor down there or sometimes there is a domical type of a floor. And the domical material down there doesn't rese

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1402251csm.text: Geno, we don't see your (PLSS) fan on. If you've got your helmet on, you ought to have your fan on.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Thank you, Bob. Good call.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: The royal MOCR "we". [When a sovereign says "we give our consent", use of the so-called "royal we" indicates that the statement is made on behalf of the institution of the sovereign and not the individual who is the sovereign. When Bob tells Gene "we don't see your fan on", he is passing on a message from Flight Director Gerry Griffin, who has been told about the fan by the people monitoring the PLSSs. Here, Jack is jokingly acknowledging the sovereignty of the entire Mission Operations Control Room (MOCR) or, perhaps, of Griffin.]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Boy, grease and lunar dust really make a nice mobile graphite material. (Long Pause) [Gene is applying grease to either his hands or to his wrist rings - or both. The fact that there is no hint of Jack lubricating his wrist rings during any of the EVA preps suggests that Gene is greasing his hands. Nonetheless, Gene and Jack did lubricate the seals after each of the EVAs and the following applies.] [Cernan - "Once we'd been outside, there was always a lot of dust on the suits. You could just scrape the dust off with your hand. You couldn't help mixing at least a little dust in with the seal lu

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. I'm locked on the right, verified. The old gauntlet's coming on. 140:24:06 Cernan: Okay, and I've got my cover (glove) on over here. Get yours? [The cover glove resembles a fingerless golf glove and is worn over the EV glove for abrasion protection.]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Well, I'm getting one of them anyway.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: I can get the other one for you. (Long Pause)

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. Number 2. (Pause) (Garbled) And it's on, and locked and locked. Verified. (Long Pause)

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1402251csm.text: No, just now coming up on Crisium. I just now see it out of window 5. Just off the southern edge. Let me try window 3; I think it might be better.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: I may be learning how on these, finally. [Cernan - "I think that most of the time I had to help Jack with his gloves. Partly, perhaps, because of the size of my hands and also because I'd put gloves on so many times going back to Gemini. It was pretty easy for me. Jack could get one on with the other hand bare; but it was tough for him to get the second glove on. So I usually helped him; it was part of the buddy system that was so important."]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay, I'm looking at the eastern edge of Crisium now. As you come across there, it looks there might be - a little bit darker - You know, I keep seeing browns all the time up here instead of grays - gray tones. Maybe that's just the way I interpret them. They are - to me kind of a brownish tint to them, and it's a darker brown than the - the stuff to the - to the south of the ridge system there.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. Mine's on and locked. If I can get my black band on here. [Schmitt - "This was a band that we put on our arms, over the suit, I think for our watches."]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: I think I'm learning how, Geno. Crazy. (Pause) Like a trained "band putter-onner". Okay. I feel pretty good. Need some help?

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: No, mine's all on.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: I can't figure that out. Must be easier in one-sixth g.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: (Laughs) Get my gauntlet donned. And that's dirt protecting dirt. [Schmitt - "The gauntlets went about halfway up the forearm, protecting the bearing areas of the gloves."]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: (Punning) Don't throw down a gauntlet, Gene.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: That's dirt protecting dirt. Okay. It's all on, Jack.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. Where did we leave off?

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Right up here (on Surface 4-6 , left-hand column). PGA is not biting, LCG's cold; let's leave it cold. Well, I guess you've got to open it (the ECS LCG pump circuit breaker) now. We've got to disconnect the (LM) water. [PGA is the Pressure Garment Assembly, the suit. They are still connected to the LM water supply and have been cooling down as much as possible before disconnecting. They will not turn on the PLSS cooling until they have the hatch open. In this case, they will be off cooling for about 12 minutes.]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: You ready?

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Jack...

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Shall we do it?

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: ...I'm ready.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Let's do it.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Disconnect it.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: (Laughing) It's disconnected.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay, and did you disconnect your (water hose)...

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Let me come around...

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay, let's turn around and let's help each other. Let's get the...

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: It's still...(Kidding Gene) This 3 degrees pitch up - 5 degrees pitch up - of yours, its an awful nuisance, Cernan.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Hold that for a minute. [Gene is connecting Jack's PLSS water hose and is asking Jack to hold the LMP LM water hose that he has just disconnected.]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: I don't know why you don't learn how to land one of these things.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Hold that for a minute...It was a pitching deck. (Straining) Okay, that is in. Boy, it's in. Locked...(although it) took a lot to "in"-ing, though. Okay. Dust cover is covering it. [Schmitt - "There was a cloth dust cover that protected the connection between the PLSS water hose and the suit."]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1402251csm.text: Well, this ridge system is running east and west down here. The color boundary isn't nearly as apparent in Crisium as it is in Serenitatis. Except that right under me right now there's kind of a subdued crater-type thing and with a southern part of a ridge. The ridge runs east - west, and it looks like we've got a flow coming out of it. Let me see if I can get a quick picture of that one. Well, lost my camera [laughter]. Here it is. Oh, it's too late; it's gone now. You know something, you see this subsolar point, it's kind of - zero phase - zero phase point, I mean, is following me right alon

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. (Pause) You know those chamber runs we had were probably some of the best training we ever did. I hate to say that, because it was some work. Push that...Hang on. There you go. [Jack is referring to training exercises conducted in a LM that was inside a vacuum chamber. He is now connecting Gene's PLSS water.]

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1402251csm.text: Okay. Keep trying.

a17_1402251csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1402251csm.text: It was just a little sluggish. Let me verify it. MP3 Audio Clip ( 7 min 20 sec )

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: (Is it) locked?

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Yeah, (it) won't turn. (Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Oh, every time you do that, my stomach gurgles. (Laughs) [This one of the few places in the transcript where Gene, Jack, and I cannot agree on the speaker identification. To me and to Gene, the speaker at 27:44 sounds unmistakably like Gene. Jack disagrees and points out that the remark is more characteristic of things he, Jack, would say. However, the context indicates that Jack is still checking Gene's water hose and, therefore, I have decided to believe my own ears. No matter who is right, the following comment still applies.] [Schmitt - "The hose connections were over my stomach and, with

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay...Let me turn around to stow. (Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: You can stow that, and mine's over here. (Pause) Okay. (Reading) "Attach our PLSS water hoses. PLSS diverter valve, Min." Want to verify that? (Pause) And, "connect PLSS water hose, verify lock, PLSS diverter valve Min, and PLSS pump (on)." Okay?

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Wait a minute. I want to make sure this (hose) is out of the way when I come in (at the end of the EVA). (Long Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Okay. The color on Picard is - is definitely darker. It's got a darker rim, darker material that goes out to - oh about a half a crater and some points extending out to a crater diameter. And then from the south arcing around to the west to - to the northwest corner, you got some light-colored material on top of that.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Now, you want my diverter Min?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Want your diverter...

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: It's Min.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: To Min. Your (PLSS LCG) pump on and Press Reg's A and B, Egress. (Pause) [Cernan - "In the normal configuration, if the cabin had started depressurizing, the O2 regulators would have started pouring oxygen into the cabin to make up the difference. But, in the Egress configuration you were telling the regulators that you were depressurizing on purpose."]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Pump's on.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. [The PLSS pump circulates water through the Liquid Cooled Garment. They will leave their sublimators off until the hatch is open.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: And I'm getting a little bite (in his PGA).

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: And mine's on (that is, his PLSS pump). Okay, the next thing is to turn your PLSS O2 On, anyway.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Oh, okay. Let me go to Egress. Egress.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Egress on the Reg's.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: The Reg's are Egress .

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. You ready on my mark. [They will do a suit pressure integrity check for one minute. The cabin is kept at its normal 4.8 psi pressure and the suits are pressurized an additional 3.85 psi as a safety check. Then, as the cabin is depressurized, the regulators bring the suits down in parallel so that they lock up at 3.85 absolute for surface operations. The cabin/suit air is pure oxygen, and there is no danger of the bends.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Wait a minute.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Tell me when you're ready.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: (If I can) find it. [Jack may be trying to reach the oxygen control on the right-front-bottom corner of his PLSS.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Say when.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Well, where is it? That's that. (Pause) Okay, let's go ahead.

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Yes, you can. In the area where you have the white thrown out on top, you essentially got a - as - as you go down the crater wall, you've got a white streak that goes all the way around it, and then you've got a dark layer underneath that. And then a white layer on below that.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay mark it. Get it? If not, I'll get it for you.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: No.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Here. Let me get it for you.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Wait a minute. I didn't get it. No, there it is. Okay, I've got it.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. We going at the same time. I've got us marked. Okay. "PLSS O2, tone on; O2 flag. Press(ure) flag clear 3.1 to 3.4. Cuff Gauge 3.7 to 4.0."

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Do you need me to watch the panel or you got it?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: No, no sweat I've got that.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: We'll have to get the PLSS O2, Off (to start the integrity check). I'll get mine; I can reach yours real easy. I can get it at a minute. As soon as we get up, I'll get it.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Yeah, I can reach it, I think, now. [After they get the suits pressurized, they will turn off the PLSS oxygen and watch the suit pressure decay. There will be a small decrease due to breathe-down and to slow migration of oxygen into various nooks and crannies in the suit. A decrease of significantly more than 0.1 or 0.2 psi in one minute would indicate a suit leak.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: And we're going up to high pressure here when we start dumping the cabin. (Long Pause) [Once they start depressurizing the cabin, the suit regulators will not be able to keep pace and, for a short while, the relative pressure will be more than 3.85 psi and the suits will be extraordinarily stiff.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Well, the central peak material is - you know, it's more smooth-type stuff. This stuff in the crater walls is - fine, straight sloping, except where it's slumped down. Where it's slumped down, it's just kind of piled up - a jumble of - type stuff, you know?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: I'm coming through 3.5 (psi) now...3.4 really.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Just off the peg here.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: My press flag did clear.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: There's mine. (Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Turn mine off. (Pause) Okay. Mark it. It (Gene's oxygen)'s off.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Where are you?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: About 3.85 (psi). Okay, when you get up, you can turn yours off. Give me a hack, and I'll check the time.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Mine's off.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Check your pressure.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: I went at 20 (seconds), you went at 30 (on the second hand of Gene's watch or the LM Digital Event Timer). (Long Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Some of the - Ah, I was looking at the volcanic - or the dark-rimmed craters, and some of them have what I'd call a - an ejecta pattern around them; and the others just have kind of a raised rim with no apparent blocks. The one to the west - let's see, southwest - of that little V that sticks out there by Yerkes - that hill that sticks out there by Yerkes - now, that's the one that, to me, looks like it has an ejecta pattern around it with blocks. It's about a - oh, a thousand-meter crater.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: It looks like it's a little tighter.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: That was the suit loop we were checking yesterday up in orbit, though.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Yeah, but you know we got two tenths (of a psi pressure decrease). Yesterday, too. (Pause) I did.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay, I'm coming down to 20 more seconds, you got 30 more seconds (to watch the suit pressure decrease).

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: I'm only about a tenth (of a psi), I guess. (Pause)

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay; 1 minute for me Houston; (3).85 (down) to about (3.)72.

A17A1402734.speaker: Parker
A17A1402734.text: Copy that, Geno.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. That it?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Mark yours.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. And the LMP was (3).8 to (3).7.

A17A1402734.speaker: Parker
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: And I'm back on.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay, and we'd like your Go, Robert.

A17A1402734.speaker: Parker
A17A1402734.text: You're Go for Depress. [They will now bring the cabin pressure down from 5 psi to 3.5 psi and will watch the response of the suit regulators. They are in the middle of the right-hand column of Surface 4-6 .]

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Jack, (on circuit breaker panel) "16, Cabin Repress, Open; and Cabin Repress valve, Closed." [By opening the circuit breaker and closing the valve, Jack will make it doubly impossible for the ECS to repressurize the cabin when Gene opens the dump valve .]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay, Cabin Repress. Circuit breaker first, right?.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Circuit breaker first. "Cabin Repress, Open."

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Yes, I can just barely see Macrobius. And - [garble] it be better out of window 3.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Let me turn around here. Okay, it's open.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. And " Repress valve , closed."

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. It's going closed.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: And then stay over there (on the right side of the cabin) as far as you can, 'cause I got to get the overhead dump valve . [Schmitt - "There were two valves we could use to dump the cabin oxygen for depressurization. There was one in the forward hatch , but the one we used was overhead on the docking hatch and was easier to reach. And that wasn't closed until we came back in."] [Cernan - "These were just little accordion valves, each with a small lever that we used to break the seal. Air pressure in the cabin was enough to keep them shut, but the surface area was small enough that you could op

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay, I'm over as far as I can get. I can turn around and give you more room.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Yeah, turn around and you'll have to look at the Cabin (pressure gauge).

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Watch yourself there.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: You went awful weak all of a sudden. Are you... [There is no change in Jack's volume as recorded in Houston.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Hello. How do you read?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Very weak. Give me a call again.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Very weak?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. My volume (control on the RCU ) got...

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: You got to hit your volume.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay, now.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Let me get over here...

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Wait a minute.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Is that enough?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: No, your arm's in the way. (Pause) Okay. I can get at it now.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: You want to go to...Let me get that..."Open, then Auto at 3.5." Okay, go ahead.

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay. Coming down. I can see it (the valve) open.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: There it is. That's 5 (psi). 4 and a half. 4. Stand by. Mark it (3.5 psi).

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay, it (the dump valve )'s Auto.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay, about 3.4. And, I (garbled). Watch; looking at a watch.

A17A1402734.speaker: Evans
A17A1402734.text: Oh, here's a Macrobius A and B. Course, J-3 is up there. The two dark craters - well, the one just - north, I guess, of Macrobius A, and also north of J-3 - now that's the one that has the dark mound around it. It's got a small dome down in the center. It - it doesn't have any ejecta pattern around it - you know, no rays, no nothing. To me, that looks like - it sure looks like a cinder cone to me. You get that same type of feeling. The dark halo that goes around it goes out for at least a crater and a half diameter. The raised dome down in the center of the crater is about a fourth of a crater

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: And my cuff gauge went up to 5.0. Good. (Pause) Suit circuit's at 4.6. That's okay. And I'm decaying. Are you decaying?

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: I'm decaying. [They have bled the cabin pressure down to 3.5 psi and are holding there while they watch the suits react. The EVA clock starts once they are satisfied with the suit integrity and then begin the final depressurization.]

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: Okay. (As per 4-7 ) We can start our watch . (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 20 min 49 sec )

A17A1402734.speaker: Cernan
A17A1402734.text: Okay.

A17A1402734.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1402734.text: My watch is started. At 5:30, more or less (Central Standard Time in the afternoon of Tuesday 11December 1972).

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay. Overhead (or) Forward Dump valve , Open.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: (Straining) Okay, baby! It's open all the way. [Cernan - "I'm really stretching to reach back up to get the valve because now the suits are even harder than they were when I first opened the valve."] [The Overhead Dump valve is behind (aft) and slightly to the left of the hatch handle ( 652 ) in a photo taken of the LM Simulator displayed at the Cradle of Aviation Museum.] [By definition, this valve opening after the suit integrity check is the start of the EVA.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay, and pressure's coming down.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. I believe it.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: We get a tone and an H2O flag. (Audible pop) You just popped your (suit) Relief (valve), I think.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Yeah, I'm at my relief pressure now. (Pause) [Once the cabin pressure gets low enough, sensors in the PLSSs will take note of the fact that the sublimators are still off and will generate warning tones and will show H2O flags on the RCUs. In addition, the pressure difference between Gene's suit and the cabin has gotten high enough that his pressure relief valve has opened.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: What's Cabin (pressure) now?

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Cabin is one point two (psi). (Pause) One (psi). (Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Well, let's see if I can partially get this (forward) hatch open.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: It's point seven (0.7 psi cabin pressure) still.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1403501.text: See any color tones on that crater at all, Ron?

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Point five. (Long Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Evans
A17A1403501.text: Yeah, the color on that particular - color of that is the same color as you see in Maraldi and as you see in the - the landing site. And that is what I - what I consider the dark - tannish - tannish-gray type of material. And again, the fresh craters around Maraldi still look kind of bluish to me, not as much as they did yesterday, but they still look kind of a - have a bluish tint to them from the reflection of the Sun. In other words, they are fresh craters and they are about the size of - one of them is about the size of MOCR, and the other one is about the size of Sherlock or Camelot.

A17A1403501.speaker: Mission Control
A17A1403501.text: 140:37:39 - America is over the landing site now.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Point three. You got it (open) at what...About point two yesterday?

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Why don't you move over as far to the right as you can...

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: ...so I can bend down (to reach the handle on the forward hatch). ["Lean" would be more accurate than "bend".]

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Well, I think that's as good as I can do.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. That's good. I can reach it. No; too much pressure on it yet.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay. About point three. (Long Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay. There's my H2O flag. [The cabin pressure has dropped low enough for sublimator operation and the flag is telling Jack that there is no feedwater flow into the sublimator. The flag is, therefore, telling Jack three things: that he has no feedwater flow, that the cabin pressure is quite low, and that the PLSS warning system is working.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Well, in that case, let me see if I can't get this. Oh, man!

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Get it opened?

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: No.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: It's unlocked, isn't it?

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Yeah, I unlocked it earlier.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Still point two. (Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Yeah, it's unlocked. (Long Pause) Here it comes.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: There goes all the junk out there again. Guess that's ice. [Cernan - "This was one of the reasons that it was a good idea not to leave things lying around in the cabin. Once the pressure got down low enough - 0.1 or 0.2 psi - you could lean down and use the handle to open the hatch. Then the rest of the air rushed out and anything lying around just zapped out the hatch with it."]
America is over the landing site now.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Probably cleaned some of the dust out, I hope. [Schmitt - "Anything that wasn't tied down flew out. I don't remember any of the dust going out; it was down below the floor so it was a little harder for it to flow out."]

A17A1403501.speaker: Evans
A17A1403501.text: Okay. Maraldi Gamma looks just like the rest of all of the surrounding hills around there. I think that's just a - some of the - what do you call it, the Sculptured Hills type of material that has been - was high and has been inundated by mare flow at one time or another. It had - mare flows kind of come up around it.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Yeah, there goes a lot of junk. Sure wish it would clean the dust out. But it isn't. It's cleaning everything else out. [Cernan - "The floor we stood on wasn't the pressure hull of the spacecraft but, rather, was a fitted floor made up of panels with cracks between them The dust got down in there and it was impossible to clean it out."]

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay, Geno. We turn our PLSS (sublimator) water on.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: If we can get to it. (Pause) (That) feels like a water valve.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. Mine's on.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: LMP's water's on.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay? (Pause)

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Open...

A17A1403501.speaker: Evans
A17A1403501.text: Next time I guess. Right now, I'm looking at the ridge system around the annulus of Serenitatis. And the dark material stops before you get up to - Oh, what's the crater that sticks into the side of Serenitatis and sticks out beyond the eastern edge of Serenitatis? Anyhow, the dark material stops before you get to there. The dark material only goes up to - let's see - There's a definite rille. There's a wrinkled ridge and at the east of the wrinkled ridge, there are two craters, about 20 kilometers in diameter. And then farther east of that is the - the rille. A graben, it looks like that goes

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: We're right there.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: What?

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: My water flag is clear!

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: That just means you've got feedwater pressure.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. (Reading) "Open hatch. Rest until cooling sufficient; verify PGA 3.7 - 4.6." Now mine's coming through 4.8; let me stand there a second. [Cernan - "It took the suit regulator a while to get itself down to 3.85 psi and, until then, you were working with an extra stiff suit and there wasn't much point in trying to get down on your knees to get out."]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: "CWEA status, PREAMPS and ECS."

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Rog. [The warning lights are telling them that the ECS is off and that the cabin is depressurized. This is primarily a confirmation that the warning system is functioning.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: (Is the) Water Sep Component Light on?

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Rog.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: I mean "affirm". Get my terminology straight here. [Schmitt - "The actual meaning of 'Roger' is 'Understood', but it tends to be used as a substitute for 'Affirmative'; most of the pilots tended to use 'Roger' wrong and this was just me, trying to get it right."]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay, Jack. I'm going to start doing about a 90 here. [Gene will turn ninety degrees so that he can get his feet through the hatch.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: Okay. Let me...I need to turn around (and face inboard) as soon as you do so I can help you get under that (DSKY housing). (Pause) That's better.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay; it knocked it off. Okay. I'm out of the way now, if you can move your left leg. [Jack needs to get as far to the right side of the spacecraft as possible so that Gene can open the hatch with Jack standing behind it.]

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. I got an O2 Flag. And it's cleared. The pressure is 4.6. (Pause) Okay, Houston. If you're happy, CDR is going to get out.

A17A1403501.speaker: Parker
A17A1403501.text: Roger. We're happy, Geno.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay.

A17A1403501.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1403501.text: (Sub vocal) Okay, I'm going to get back out of your way. (Pause) Okay. Hatch is full open.

A17A1403501.speaker: Cernan
A17A1403501.text: Okay. [Jack means that the hatch is open against his legs as far as it will go.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. We're in the Tacquet area now, and in this case, the wrinkled ridge system that's out in the middle does not make a change in the color boundary. The color boundary is completely out to the outer edge and is - in the area of those - the rilles. Those are - There's kind of arcuate rilles, straight rilles, and in the Tacquet, yesterday, I said this was Sulpicius Gallus, but it's Tacquet - Tacquet area, but [garble]...

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: And you're still...Your scraping your (PLSS)...just a little bit. Just get your buttons down there. That's good. Okay. Oh, hey, remind me to fix your...

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: PLSS straps.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: ...your donning straps. [At 40:09, Jack's "get your buttons down" is another reference to the Bill Mauldin cartoon discussed at 123:58:20 .]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. (Pause) That is ice, by the way, Jack. (Pause) [The cabin air cools rapidly as it escapes through the open hatch and some of the moisture condenses on the hatch opening and other surfaces. This ice will soon sublimate.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh, man! I tell you, with a stiff suit...I'm still at 4.5 (psi). But, I am out here on the porch.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh, man. Okay, I'm out here.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: (Reading cuff checklist page LMP-4 ) I've assisted you. (Pause) Here comes the jett(ison) bag whenever you're ready.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Well, let me get...Okay. I'm all set. Man, I wish this suit would come down to 3.8. Here it comes. Okay, any time. (Pause) Give it (the jett bag ) a swat; there you go. [Once Gene gets out on the porch, Jack can swing the hatch partially closed, move to the other side of the cabin, and then swing the hatch fully open. He has just put the jettison bag in the hatch opening and pushes it farther out with his boot.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1404009csm.text: Yeah, the color difference - again the - You know, I just - I just now noticed that when I get down at this Sun angle, out in front of me, I got one color, and then I look straight down and I have a different color. But in this Tacquet area, you've definitely got some cinder cone type - No, I don't want to say cinder cone, but anyhow - volcanic. And it almost looks like a breached cinder cone right next to - I think it's Melrose [?] - is the name of that - that crater - the big one that's right on the edge of Serenitatis. I'll find it on the map and mark it for sure. But just to the east of th

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh, the beauty of (garbled)...

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay; let me look at something here. (Pause; Gene chuckles as he looks in his checklist, probably looking at the abbreviation list ) [Schmitt - "There was probably some kind of humorous picture that the support crew had inserted into the checklist at this point. Heaven knows what it was. I don't know where those checklists went. But the support crew kept sticking things in there, particularly Bob Parker. At the end of every section we could count on finding 'This is the end and not the beginning', because Gene had come up with a slogan for our mission 'This is the beginning and not the end' an

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: What's that?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: I was just turning my checklist pages.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh. Here you go.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. (Reading CDR-4 ) Jett bag . I need...What you got next; ETB?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: ETB.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Can you reach it?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Yeah. (Now, I'll) get it hooked up here. (Pause) [Gene is attaching the Equipment Transfer Bag (ETB) to the lanyard - called the LEC or Lunar Equipment Conveyor - with which he will lower the ETB to the surface, in part to protect the cameras in the bag and, in part, to free Gene's hands as he goes down the ladder.] [Schmitt - "It was a lot easier using two hands going down the ladder. It wouldn't have hurt if you fell; or, I don't think it would have except it might have damaged the PLSS."]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. Turn the tape recorder off (as per LMP-4 ). (Pause) Tape recorder's off. [They will turn the tape recorder back on at about 163:03 during EVA-3 preparations.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Big hook. That's a legacy of Gemini IX. [Cernan - "This was probably a hook on the lanyard that I was hooking onto the ETB or that I was using to attach the lanyard to the ladder. We learned on Gemini IX that, with the pressurized gloves and the lack of dexterity, we needed big things that we could get a hold on, not little things that you had to open with your finger tips. We learned a lot in the early days about the kind of equipment you needed to work with in the pressurized suits."]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: (Reading LMP-4 ) "Max (sensitivity on the comm circuit). (Pause) EVA decals." (Long Pause) [Jack is making a final check of the circuit breakers and switches.] RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 47 sec ) 140:42:44 Cernan: ETB is hanging. (Is) that all I need?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: I think so. You hit your comm again.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: No, I didn't; I'm okay.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: What happened to the static? Did we lose Houston?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: We read you loud and clear.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Hello, Houston. (Hearing Bob) Oh, you must have switched to...Oh, I don't know.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1404009csm.text: Hey, Ron, I - I blew that. Menelaus is west of Tacquet up there.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. I'm going down the ladder.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: All of a sudden, all the noise is gone; that's very good. (Pause)

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: "Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17." I think I'll read that every time I come down the ladder.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. All the circuit breakers are verified. Noise is back.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. My visor's coming down.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Utility lights are off. We're not going to use the (16 mm) camera. (Pause) [Here, Jack is referring to the sequence camera, which is mounted in his window primarily for taking one-frame-per-second movies of landing and take-off.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, I get to get out (as per LMP-4 ).

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, Houston. On this fine Tuesday evening, as I step out on the plains of Taurus-Littrow, Apollo 17 is ready to go to work.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Roger, Geno. Good deal.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: (Refering to CDR-4 ) And the first thing I'll do is give you a TGE (Traverse Gravimeter reading). Let me turn it on. And you want a reading. Okay. It's on. Bob, and the reading is 222, 262, 207; that's 222, 262, 207. [The gravimeter is on the ground, in the shade of the LM, near the ladder. Gene had made a reading just before climbing the ladder at the end of EVA-1, and then put the instrument in the Standby mode. This reading is an instrument check.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Roger. We copy that, Gene.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Looks good from here, Jack. Keep coming. [Jack is getting out of the LM.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Come on, hatch!

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh, what a nice day. (Somebody burps)

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: (Both laughing) Funny, there's not a cloud in the sky. Except in the Earth.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: (To himself) Take it nice and easy today and get accustomed. Whee!

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1404009csm.text: Do you have - do have any dark - do you have any dark halo craters near Sulpicius Gallus?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: (Probably on the porch and closing the hatch) Okay. [Schmitt - "Getting out the second day was actually more exciting for me than the first was because it looked like we were actually going to have a chance to do something useful (laughing) rather than just deploy the ALSEP. I don't think getting out was an 'adrenaline pumping' type of excitement because your checklist kept you organized and moving from one thing to another. I think the real adrenaline was Launch, Translunar Injection, Lunar Orbit Insertion, Powered Descent Initiation, Landing, Lift-off from the Moon, and Trans-Earth Injection

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: I'll be right there, Jack, to get the (PLSS) antenna - as soon as I turn the LCRU on. [The LCRU is the Lunar Communications Relay Unit, hanging on the front of the Rover.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. I'm on the ladder. Door is closed. (Pause) [There is a dump-valve handle on the outside of the hatch.] RealVideo Clip (20 min 36 sec) by Mick Hyde Video Clip 3 min 36 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG Clip ) by Ken Glover

a17_1404009csm.text: (Reading CDR-4 ) Okay, (TV) Power switch is Internal. I'm in Mode 3. LCRU blankets are open 100 percent. AGC is 4.0 plus, and power is about 1.8. Temps are about 1.6 or 1.4. [The TV comes on, showing Gene's footpan. As usual, Ed Fendell - who is operating the camera from Houston - starts with a counter-clockwise pan.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. And we have a good picture there, Geno. Thank you.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Already, huh?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Already.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Well, let me just tweak you up a little bit. Okay, I've got you tweaked, right in the middle. [Gene has centered Earth in the high-gain antenna boresight.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Thank you. And, Gene, after you finish closing up both those battery covers up front there, why don't you go back and give us that (Rover battery) temperature reading and then put the breakers in and then give us another temperature reading on the batteries. [Fendell now finds both Gene and Jack at the back of the Rover.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Yes, sir; I'll do that. Jack, here, let's get the (PLSS/OPS) antennas (as per CDR-4 and LMP-4 ).

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: You want to get...You want to hang on (to) the Rover? [Jack is asking Gene to lean on the Rover so that he can reach his antenna.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: I guess...Well, okay.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: I think it's easier.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. High Gain to Auto. Let me see, 22 Noun 70 to Enter. Okay. Let's see, plus 52.25. plus 52.25. Up-link. Verb 58 Enter. [Garble]. Proceed to [garble] gets out of the way. Okay. D-Caldera was taken on picture number 28. It was f/8 at 1/500, and then I took three more before that. They're terminator photos, looking north across Sulpicius Gallus and farther north. And they were 1/500 at f/16 to start with and then f/11.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Now, I'm low, so get mine, now. I'm (standing) in a hole. (Long Pause)

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay; you're up.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Standby...get down there yet. Got to secure the flaps. Okay, you're all right. [Jack now bends his knees so that Gene can free his antenna.] [Cernan - "Getting those antennas free was no easy task in the gloves."]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, you're up.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. [Jack moves to the SEP receiver , mounted on the geopost at the right rear of the Rover, behind his seat. He is now on LMP-5 ]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, (SEP) Power switch is going to Standby. And the temperature is 80 (degrees Fahrenheit or 27 Celsius). And I'll close the blankets.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Copy 80 on the SEP. 140:47:54 Schmitt: That's affirm. (Pause) You know what happened? The Velcro came unbonded. That's why those (dust covers) don't hold down. We probably ought to get a piece of tape on those. Because they've got a set and it's going to get dusty. The blankets...There's no Velcro left to hold the SEP blankets down, Bob. [The top of the SEP is at about chest height. The glue holding Velcro fasteners onto the SEP dust covers failed sometime during the first EVA. The unit has an internal temperature sensor which will shut it down if it gets too hot - greater than about 108F - an

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, I copy that, Jack. [Jack goes to the LM ladder to get the ETB.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Do you have a reading on the gravimeter?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Yeah, I took a reading, Jack.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: It's measuring right now, Jack, we'll get it later.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: All right.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. I hope I didn't hit it with some dust.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Hey, it is not measuring, Bob...

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Oh, that's right. Sorry about that.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: ...All I did was take a reading. I turned it on and took a reading.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: You're right, you're right, and I'm wrong.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay, Bob...

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Hey, Bob.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: ...the (Rover) battery temperatures are 0 and 0. Video Clip 3 min 36 sec ( 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG Clip )

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Copy that. Okay. [There had been some concern about the battery temperature indicators and this is a check to see if they are giving proper zero readings with the batteries off.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: Bob, there's your pendulum. [Schmitt - "Bob Parker and I had talked about getting a TV picture of a pendulum motion in one-sixth gravity. The lanyard was hanging down and so I just gave it a little push so that he could have his pendulum."]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. [Because nothing is hanging from the lanyard to make it a classical pendulum, Jack's push excites multiple modes of oscillation.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1404009csm.text: It's not a very good one. I'll work on that. (Pause) Are you going to be there for a minute, Gene?

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Just putting these batteries in. I'm done on this. [Gene leans across his seat to close the battery circuit breakers and read the battery temperatures.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: (To Bob) Oh, you'll be glad to hear this. We got 70 (degrees) on battery 1 and about 92 on battery 2.

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1404009csm.text: Beautiful! Beautiful. 70 and 92. I copy. [At the end of the first EVA, the temperatures were 108 and 123 degrees, respectively. Clearly, the combination of Gene's dusting and the wax cooling system has been effective.]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1404009csm.text: Yes, sir! Let me just verify this (navigation circuit breaker) is in, Jack, (as per CDR-4 )and I'll be all done. Okay. You've got it. I'm all done. RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 49 sec ) by Marv Hein 140:49:39 Schmitt: Okay. (Pause) Okay, here's your old fender. [Gene has gone toward the LM to open Sample Return Container (SRC) 2; Jack removes the replacement fender from the ETB and lays it in Gene's footpan. Gene is now on CDR-5 .]

a17_1404009csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1404009csm.text: Okay. Image Motion - let's see - I think that was barber pole plus three before. There it is. 3 - 4...

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1405237csm.text: Ron, just for your information, we're playing back the voice playback from the last rev, and it'll be recorded in house. It is readable, and we can read it.

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1405237csm.text: scissors . (Long Pause) [The flashing light indicates that the gravimeter is leveling itself in preparation for making a measurement. a17_1405237csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1405237csm.text: Okay. And, Jack, you're getting ready to take care of the charge; remember EP-4 goes between the Rover seats, and EP-5 we're going to put on one of the footpads in the Sun. Probably either the minus-Z (east) or the minus-Y (south) footpad, whichever is more convenient. Probably the minus-Z is. Just as long as it is sitting in the Sun is the important thing on the (choice of) footpad.

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1405237csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [As was discussed at 138:21:35, there are two charges in a transporter that Gene mounted on the Rover before driving out to the ALSEP site. EP-4 is a 1/8th pound charge which Jack will now put between the seats for deployment early in the upcoming traverse. EP-5 is a three pound charge which they will save until EVA-3 and, for now, Jack is getting it and the first transporter out of the way so that he can mount a second transporter - containing charges 1, 2, 3, and 8 - on the Rover.]

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1405237csm.text: Boy, oh boy! Going to be a...(Pause) Why won't that come out? (Pause) Well, Bob, I'm having a little trouble getting the LCRU (replacement) battery out (of the MESA). I'll have to go back and use two hands. [The MESA bounces as Gene pulls on the battery, one handed. He has an SCB in his other hand which he now takes to the Rover.] [Schmitt - "The LCRU batteries were stored in the MESA section of the descent stage, and we had to put in new ones for every EVA."]

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1405237csm.text: And your - your grounded friends down there are busy working around the LM right now and doing some loading the Rover and that, getting ready for the EVA-2 work. They're out on the surface and loading the Rover.

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1405237csm.text: Okay. That sounds like a familiar problem.

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1405237csm.text: Well, you got any familiar answers?

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1405237csm.text: Someone who's been there before (John Young) says you just got to work it back and forth until it comes loose. [Jack goes to the MESA with the ETB, followed shortly by Gene.]

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1405237csm.text: Okay. (Pause) I can get that, Jack. I've got to...

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1405237csm.text: How's my - yeah, right. How's my ZPN? All I did was move it. I didn't put in a new sensor yet. Do I need to put on a new sensor?

a17_1405237csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1405237csm.text: Yeah. I've got to work here anyway. (Long Pause) [Jack takes the EP transporter - containing EP-5 - to the east LM footpad. Gene is still struggling with the LCRU battery. It is too far inboard for him to get a good grip with two hands.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 20 min 49 sec )

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Okay, Bob, it's on the minus-Z and the...One corner is facing directly into the Sun. Video Clip 3 min 01 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1405548.text: Okay; copy that.

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: That's EP-5.

A17A1405548.text: Roger that. And I copy (charge) number 4 was put between the seat.

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Yeah, it's between the seat, or will be very soon.

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: Boy, this is ridiculous. Ridiculous. [Gene is puffing audibly.]

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Whoops, I need that other (EP) transporter. [The charge transporter is stowed in the equipment bay on the northeast face of the LM Descent Stage.]

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: (To himself and the world in general) Well, it's nothing worth getting upset about it, but it sure makes you start out...When you shouldn't have to this way.

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Come on, just don't wear your hands out now.

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: Yeah. [Cernan - "In listening to this part, I can still feel the frustration of trying to get that damn little LCRU battery out of a storage area in the MESA. The problems you want to deal with are the ones that are worth solving, not something little that's avoidable. Of course, the real world is always a little different than the training. The training is good because you can try to look at every possible aspect of what you're going to be doing. You anticipate problems, you get proficient, and you get productive; but you're always going to run into new and different situations and, when you

A17A1405548.text: Need a little help?

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: No, I think I can do it, just got to wiggle...

A17A1405548.speaker: Parker
A17A1405548.text: ...jiggle it gently and sort of let it come free there. It's a matter of it wedging itself in, of course, on the parallel rails.

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: Yeah. I...I see what's happening, Bob. (Pause) It's still ridiculous. (Long Pause) [Jack comes to the Rover from the east; Gene is still struggling with the battery.]

A17A1405548.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1405548.text: Ron, the ZPN data isn't too good. It's the sensor sponges need to be replaced, if you didn't already replace them.

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Bob, did you hear my comment about the...about the SEP receiver?

A17A1405548.speaker: Parker
A17A1405548.text: Roger. That the blankets won't stay closed. We're talking about that down here.

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: Boy; a bag of peanuts! Whew!! Man in space. Without them we'd be lost. [In 1997, I suggested to Gene that "bag of peanuts" was a reference to the small, plasticized bags of peanuts that the airlines serve that are all but impossible to open. He agreed.] [Gene turns into the Sun, now holding the 8x4x2 inch battery by a loop handle.]

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Without them we wouldn't have the LCRU and the MESA probably. (Chuckles)

A17A1405548.speaker: Cernan
A17A1405548.text: Manischewitz. Okay. Let me see what I can do for you while I'm here. Okay. (Consults checklist) "LCRU battery under seat, dustbrush to LCRU. Okay. I'll go get that; then I'll get to work." (Long Pause) [Gene gets the big brush off the ladder hook where he had left it at the end of the first EVA. A17A1405548.text: Hey, Bob, what's my shadow length right now? (Pause) [Schmitt - "My shadow was the only long ruler that I regularly carried around with me. And, knowing that everybody underestimates distance on the Moon, I asked them to be ready to give me my shadow length so that I could see what it looked like and know what it really was. And it always looked a lot less long than it really was."]

A17A1405548.speaker: Parker
A17A1405548.text: Stand by. I'll ask. (Pause) We'll get it for you momentarily. (Pause) [Gene goes to his Rover seat with the battery.]

A17A1405548.text: (Consulting his checklist) Now, I got to do some more stowing on you when you get that on. (Pause)

A17A1405548.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1405548.text: Okay. They're in the...(Pause) Where do you want me?

A17A1405548.text: Your left side.

a17_1405908csm.text: Okay, Ron. Here's your word on some magazines here. X-ray X-ray has to be left for the Zodiacal light. a17_1405908csm.text: Okay, Jack. We've got four-point-five meters or one-five feet.

a17_1405908csm.text: 15 feet!? Is that how long I am on the ground? No wonder I've misjudged distance! Zap! [Gene waves into the TV.]

a17_1405908csm.text: Hello there. (Pause) Okay, Jack. And do we have the new charge transporter on the pallet? [Fendell pans away counter-clockwise.]

a17_1405908csm.text: Copy that. I won't ask if we got the L.C.R.U. battery. That one, I did see.
