a17_1405908csm.text: Okay. Copy that. And I guess we'd suggest that, if you haven't talked about it already, that you work on the fender before you do the Geo Prep. You don't have your cameras and bags to worry about at that point.

a17_1405908csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1405908csm.text: Okay. Would that be a good time for Jack to go to the ALSEP, do you think? Or do you think we both have to do this fender?

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1411147csm.text: Hate to say it, because it's very dead serious work, but I'm kind of watching a lunar comedy as the - the two lunar stalwarts are trying to plan the new fender on the vehicle down there.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: No, I want to keep it above this center...the hub here...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah, Okay.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: ...for steering purposes. See this...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Is that fixed for the...Well...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: I'll take a look at it. I'm going to tighten it down so it stays, then I'm going to take a look at it. I might turn this thing down, too.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah; I was just going to suggest that. (Pause) [Gene has the inboard clamp positioned.]

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: Let me take a look before I get it too tight. Well, I'll tell you, that's going to help some. [Gene gets his arm out of the way and leans in for a close look.]

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yup. It may do the trick.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: I can't see what's under this rail too well, but I know that clamp is on. It's on tight.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Gene, it looks...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: (Reaching in) Let me move this...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Move your left hand a little. Okay. Tighten that now.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah. Well, they lost a fender, and it was throwing dust up on Gene. It's just ridiculous how much dust they got on them, so they - they just decided they just had to go ahead and do something.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: Get this out of the way.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Looks as if...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: Let me loosen it, and get it a little straighter.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah, I think you need to straighten it.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: Boy, I had it tight.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah, but you know you've got another piece in there so...

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah, that's why it's crooked, it's over those pieces.

a17_1411147csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411147csm.text: Yeah. Well, you might want to move it...If you could move it this way about a...(about) an inch, you'd be past the ridge you got.

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: (Consulting his checklist) Now, I got to do some more stowing on you when you get that on. (Pause)

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Okay. They're in the...(Pause) Where do you want me?

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Your left side.

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: I mean...Which way are you going to turn? [They are mostly hidden by the gate. Jack is facing southeast; Gene is northeast of him, mounting equipment on the left side of his PLSS.] 141:16:33 Cernan: Oh, man, does that Velcro get tough. (Long Pause)

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay, you've got a core cap dispenser. Stand by; let me fix these for you while I'm here. Okay. Here's your doffing harness on this side. Don't move yet, I've got something I've got to do to you.

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Okay. [Gene gets something from the gate, probably the drive-tube rammer.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay; turn around, I'll get your harness on the other side. [By getting Jack to turn around, Gene will have sunlight on the right-side straps he's trying to adjust.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Let me get yours too.

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, there you go. [Jack starts adjusting Gene's straps, working in shadow.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay, you've got a cap dispenser, you've got a (drive tube) rammer, and you've got...Well, I guess SCB-8, if I'm not mistaken.

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Yeah, that's all right, they got it. (Pause) Okay. That's one. [Jack goes around Gene to the other side.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay. You can give me SCB-5 then, and...

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Yeah. (Pause) Can you move...Move a little bit. There you go. (Pause) [Jack pushes Gene away from the Rover a little so that he can get at the gate.] Video Clip ( 4 min 04 sec 1.1 Mb RealVideo or 40 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Okay. There you are. (Pause)

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: You got it? [Gene starts to move away.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: No.

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: I'm sorry.

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: In fact, I've got to tighten up your (straps)...

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: We've got to take a picture of that fender if it works. [Fendell pans the TV upward.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Wait a minute. No...If you weren't so tall. You just invariably stand so I have to get in a hole! Okay. Now let me tighten up your whole shooting match (meaning "everything") here. It's loose again. Hang on. (Pause)

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: Okay. [Fendell returns to them.]

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: Between Velcro and snaps, the world could never fall apart. Okay, (it's on).

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: All set?

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: You're set. 141:19:01 Cernan: Okay. I'm going to get a hammer, and then I'll get the TGE .

A17A1411600.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1411600.text: I'm going to get my camera, and I'll go to the SEP site (140 meters east of the LM). [Gene gets the hammer from the gate, puts it in his shin pocket .]

A17A1411600.speaker: Parker
A17A1411600.text: Okay. Why don't you start to the SEP site, Jack... 141:19:xx Cernan: Hey, Jack, when I start running...(Stops to listen to Bob) 141:19:xx Parker:...And, also, I presume that the dustbrush is on the Rover now. [Jack gets a 70-mm camera from his seat and leaves. He is now on LMP-7 .]

A17A1411600.speaker: Cernan
A17A1411600.text: It is.

A17A1411600.speaker: Parker
A17A1411600.text: Okay. Copy that.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1411918csm.text: [Garble.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Jack, when I drive out there why don't you watch the rear wheel.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: I will. Give me a yell when you start to drive.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. (Watch) both the steering and the rooster tail. [Gene goes to read the gravimeter.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Oh, I hope it (the TGE reading he's about to take) is not all zeros. Okay, Bob. 670, 017, 701; 670, 017, 701.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) [Fendell pans away.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay; and the SCB is good. It's closed. It's in the shade. (Correcting himself) Or "SRC", I guess. [Fendell finds Jack jogging to the SEP site. He is using a foot-to-foot, loping stride as he runs.] 141:20:03 Parker: Okay. And, Jack, when you get out to the SEP site, you might give us a reading on what the solar panels look like...How they survived the night with the tape on them.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: I wouldn't think of not doing that. I'm curious myself. (Pause) [The SEP gets its electric power from three small solar panels which Jack and Gene taped open at the end of the first EVA. It has been about 18 hours since Jack taped them at 123:09:08 .] RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 58 sec ) 141:20:32 Cernan: Okay. The TGE is on the LRV.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. Copy that. [Cernan - "I don't think we had nearly as many acronyms in the Navy as we had in NASA. NASA won the prize. The Navy used them for the names of commands, like 'ComNavAirPac' which means 'Commander, Naval Air-forces, Pacific'. But I tell you, going down to NASA meant learning a whole new language: an acronym for everything. And for the longer ones, like LCRU, you just turned them into words and said 'Lacru'. It's funny, but a lot of acronyms became so much a part of the NASA lingo that if you stopped somebody and ask them 'What does LCRU stand for?', they couldn't tell you. Peop

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: (Reading CDR-7 ) Okay. I'm making an inventory. I've got the LCRU battery. Okay. We('ve) got (seismic charges number) 1, 3 and 2 and 8; LCRU blankets are open 100 percent. Battery covers are Closed. Dustbrush is on the LCRU. TGE is on the Rover. Jack, can you verify we got the right mags and a polar filter? Polarization (filter).

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1411918csm.text: Just talked to the home front a little while ago, and everybody's fine, Ron. And they were able to get the squawk boxes squared away, so she should have been listening to you for last couple of passes - all on the [garble]. The problem was it wasn't able to shut off one loop or the other, so today we've been - they've been able to get all - just the CSM loop in there for - during the AOS periods.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: Yes, sir. I verified that.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. Very good.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: You better put that 500 back under the seat. 141:21:02 Cernan: Yep. That's where it's going. [Jack reaches the SEP. Once again, it looks as though he is below the Rover, even though there is really no appreciable elevation difference. He has covered the 140 meters is a bit less than 2 minutes; his average speed, then, is a modest 4.5 kilometers per hour.] 141:21:05 Schmitt: Well, Bob, it looks like (the SEP) tape survived. As I stand behind the panels, the left-hand panel may be tilted at about...well, less than 5 degrees. Probably about 2 or 3, but that's all. Looks pretty good right now.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay; beautiful. Thank you. Good fix.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. [Training photo 72-H-1410 shows Jack at the SEP transmitter.] 141:21:30 Cernan: Okay, Bob, I'm going to take the TV from you.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. Copy that, Geno.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: And the (SEP) transmitter's going on.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Copy that, Jack.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1411918csm.text: Hey, good. We can say that's because the guys went to the Moon, see?

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: (Laughing) If I can do it without destroying it. [Gene moves the TV camera just as Jack bends his knees so he can reach down far enough.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Yeah. That's hard to do out there, Jack. (To Bob) Okay. TV camera going Position 1. [TV off.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: Transmitter's on. (I'll) fix the level there. Okay. The level is on the inner ring again. The gnomon has moved a little bit, but not much. But you would expect that, I guess (because the Sun has moved about 9 degrees in the eighteen hours since they deployed the SEP). [This gnomon is a small post on the top of the SEP transmitter which casts a short shadow on a scale for alignment purposes.]

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1411918csm.text: About 5 min - 4½ minutes to LOS now, Ron. We went around the room, and all systems look good and you're just looking great.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1411918csm.text: Yeah. Seeing the other end of the gnomon up there in the sky (the Sun) has moved a little bit.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1411918csm.text: Yeah. That's what I said.

a17_1411918csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1411918csm.text: Okay. (70 mm) camera, tongs, and I'll drive. West leg, heading 270. (Pause) Camera is on. Bob, I'm on...I guess (frame) 26. Yes sir, frame 27, mag Charlie. [Mag C, or Charlie, is Apollo magazine 137. Jack is using Mag Golf, which is Apollo mag 135.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: (To Gene) And, I guess you're going to hand me EP-4. (I'll) get rid of this (LRV sampler). [Jack will keep the LRV Sampler within reach, attaching it to the accessory staff. He probably would not be laying it in his seat pan since it would be hard to reach while seated.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. 282 is the preferred (meaning "the proper heading") but that's too small (a difference) to bother torquing, Gene; you're good as is. We're ready for you guys to go. [This difference in heading has the potential of contributing up to a 100 meter southward bias to estimates of the LM location made from Rover readouts at the more distant stations visited during this EVA. This point is discussed in full at 164:48. If Gene did not do the correction - and that point is not crystal clear in the following dialog - all LM bearing readouts given during this EVA should be decreased by one degree.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. That looks good because I have to come left just a skosh there to proceed parallel down the west line.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We're ready for you guys to go. We presume you have the SEP photos, Jack.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Yes, I do.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. And you can give us a frame count, if you want. Remember to pick up EP-4 when you get in the Rover.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We got it, and the frame count is 17.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Copy 17 for the LMP, and we need a Nav reset to verify there, Gene.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: I did Nav reset; I'm reading all balls. And it is back off.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. And did you happen to check the SEP temperature when you turned it on, Gene? (Correcting himself) Jack? The receiver?

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: No. I didn't; I didn't. Doubt if it changed much since I called you.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We'll catch it at Station 2.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay, Jack, we got transmitter and receiver both on, huh?

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Low gain antenna is 240 and we're ready for you guys to leave. Give us a mark on the leave. [A sketch map of the initial portion of the traverse is shown (identically) on LMP-8 and CDR-8. The average heading during the first six kilometers of the traverse will be 260 degrees, ten degrees south of west. As discussed previously, there is an offset in the low-gain antenna's pointing indicator to compensate for the Earth's position in the local sky and, therefore, the reason for the 240 degree pointing - rather than 260 - is not obvious. They also are carrying a more detailed cronopaque map,

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Here you go, Jack; we need...The SEP receiver and transmitter (are) both on, huh?

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. And, Gene, remember we want a mark when you pass the end of the antenna.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Gonna drive fairly slowly, huh?

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Yep, until I get past the end. I got to get my heading changed about 10 degrees to parallel it. We're still in the same relative position, Bob.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Very good.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We are moving right now.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We're marking that.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Slowly. (Long Pause) Okay. Stand by, Bob.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Mark it.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Copy that. [Gene has driven about 32 meters along the antenna arm in about 40 seconds. His average speed, therefore, was a bit over 4 kph. During the drive toward the LM, Jack takes AS17-135- 20550 and 20551 , the latter showing a large, partially buried boulder northeast of the spacecraft.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We want to go past the LM at heading 260, Jack.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Well, we want to get at 080 (bearing) and 0.4 (range) and get rid of this charge. [Details of the initial stage of the traverse are given (identically) on LMP-9 and CDR-9.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay, 17, a couple of words there as you drive along. Let me give them to you early here. One, we didn't bother to change all the numbers on the checklist; but, by and large, because we think we're 200 meters east of where we were (planning to land), you should probably increase all those numbers except for the explosive package numbers by about two-tenths to get the distance at which you will come across these areas. Again it's about 0.4 (or) 0.5 (km) that we expect to deploy EP-4. The more important number though is that it's 0.2 west of the ALSEP. As you pass the ALSEP, you might note what

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Range is the one that changes on...No, wait a minute.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: I got it. I'll get it.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Which is it? Range changes every half...on the half kilometer?

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Yep. (Pause) Distance.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Let me go around your (garbled).

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Roger, Jack. The range is what changes in the middle at 50 meters and 150 meters. [The Rover has digital indicators for bearing, distance driven, and range. The range indicator changes from 000 to 001 at 50 meters, to 002 at 150 meters, and so on. The distance indicator changes at 100m, 200m, and so on.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. The fender fix is working so far.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Beautiful.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Let me get around your flag. There's your flag way out there, isn't it? [This is the flag marking the southernmost geophone that Jack deployed during the first EVA.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Yeah. 141:33:10 Cernan: (To Jack) Let me get around that. Man, that's really giving the ALSEP some room. [Jack's three traverse photos taken during this interval are AS17-135- 20552 to 20554. They show some large boulders south of Geophone rock.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Yeah. Okay, Bob; we're still seeing the light-colored gabbroic rocks. I think the reason I said 50 percent (plagioclase) was because, in this light, they look light-colored, and that's probably largely because of the zap-pit halos.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. I copy that, Jack.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: In the hand lens, it looked like a standard gabbro.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: And, Bob, I'm full out at about 11...

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay, you can turn right, now. [Gene has been driving more or less south to get around the geophone and will now turn west.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: I'm full out at about 11 clicks (11 kilometers per hour) right now.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Beautiful.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Oops. You drove (garbled under Bob).

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Can you give me a call as you pass by the ALSEP as you get ready to deploy the charge, please?

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We're almost due south of the ALSEP now.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay,...

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: (Garbled under Bob) got to work my way through here. 141:34:00 Parker: ...copy that. Go about 0.2 kilometers further than that. (Pause) [Jack's eight traverse photos taken during this drive west to the charge deployment site are AS17-135- 20555 to 20562.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: (To Gene) It's a little rocky out here.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Yeah, it sure is.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: In the area we are now...Did you get a distance? That was...

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. We just clicked to (zero-zero)-four. I want to move over this way just a skosh.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Yeah. Okay, (we're) just south of my geophone 2 flag now.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay. If you just clicked to 4, let's go to 6 then, just past the click on 6. [That is, at a range of 550 meters.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. And they want about (a bearing to the SEP transmitter of) 080. (Pause)

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Plenty good enough. I got to start heading right out here, right toward my topographic...

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Hole-in-the-Wall should be just to the left of the notch (in the rim of Camelot). 141:34:51 Cernan: Yep. That's exactly where I'm heading. RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 6 sec )

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: And I think we're coming up closer to the rim of Camelot. It's starting to look like a crater now.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Okay; very good. [Schmitt - "The drive up to the Camelot rim was a very gradual climb, unlike Cone Crater on Apollo 14 which was a crater on a knoll. The LM was probably on the ejecta blanket of Camelot, so it would have been hard to judge a change in slope. Generally, the terrain here was much flatter than on either Apollo 14 or Apollo 16, which were the highland sites. The average (vertical) variation at our site was perhaps a meter or a meter and a half; and there's one picture of the LM, taken looking back into the Sun, and there is a little low ridge blocking out the lower part of the LM.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Looking down-Sun, I see no major albedo changes except for the very fresh craters which are brighter. By maybe 20 percent. The surface...

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan

A17A1412909.text: Okay; can you swing right out over there...

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Yeah.

A17A1412909.text: Okay.

A17A1412909.text: How's that?

A17A1412909.text: Okay. And I'll set it right there in that...Can you move forward, and I'll get it in that little depression.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay.

A17A1412909.text: All right. Take a look. Bob, one stop here for about 2 seconds.

A17A1412909.text: Okay. Retracted. (Pause)

A17A1412909.text: Okay. Try it...Push it in once more.

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. The best I can do. I'll just lock...I'll twist it down on there and maybe it'll hold.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Okay. Twist it tight. (Pause) I got the rod. (Pause) [Jack seems to be twisting the UHT into the sampler head.]

A17A1412909.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1412909.text: Okay. I'll just have to be careful.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan

A17A1412909.text: Okay.

One other thing I might mention to you guys as you're driving here, Jack, before you start talking again, is that, as you go by Camelot, you might keep an eye out for blocks along the rim there, because, remember, we may be wanting to come back and move Station 5 to an area where there's blocks, unless there are blocks at the present, nominal Station 5. A17A1412909.text: Okay, Bob. Okay. We'll keep you informed.

A17A1412909.speaker: Cernan
A17A1412909.text: Bob, I got the thing "two-blocked", and I'm averaging probably 10 to 11 clicks. It's not exactly straight-line navigation, but I think I can hold most of it.

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker
A17A1412909.text: Roger. Beautiful. [Cernan - "I don't remember if 'two-blocked' is an old Navy term or what. But it means 'I've got it all the way out, hell bent for fire.'"] [Journal Contributor Dean Eppler adds, "I believe 'two blocked' refers to the use of a two-pulley block-and-tackle, as was often used on sailing ships. When you pull out sufficient slack that the two blocks are drawn together, you can't pull any more out, and are "two-blocked," or have gone to the absolute limit. Hence Gene's use of the phrase when describing the LRV at max throttle."

A17A1412909.speaker: Parker

A17A1412909.text: Okay. Copy that, Jack. Very good.

A17A1412909.text: Okay. Thank you.
