A17A1430419.text: Roger. [Gene has placed the gnomon near Boulder 2 but then goes downhill to take a couple of pictures of Earth, which he could see above the rock as he approached it. He leans backward to take the shots. These are AS17-137- 20910 and 20911 .]

A17A1430419.speaker: Evans
A17A1430419.text: We're passing over a - well, generally a hilly type of terrain, and then just before we get into Grimaldi area, it looks like we're out into a plains-type material, again, interspersed with a hummocky-type. I guess that hummocky - is - hummocky stuff is associated with Grimaldi.

A17A1430419.speaker: Parker
A17A1430419.text: Okay. Copy that, Jack. Press on. [Jack leaves the Rover but forgets the scoop and comes back to get it. Gene moves the gnomon.] 143:08:33 Cernan: Okay, Bob, I'm at another boulder up the slope here. It looks quite similar to the one we just sampled, except there is a lot of flake fractures on it. Non-uniform, non-directional, but quite different, at least from that other rock, in terms of its fracture pattern. The texture looks to be quite similar. Boy, I'm glad I don't have to walk to the top of this thing (the South Massif).

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Hey, look, Gene, on these rake samples, there is just no point in carrying a rake all the way up here...

A17A1430419.speaker: Parker
A17A1430419.text: Negative, Jack, as long as you're above the break...

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: ...because all we needed was a break in the slope.

A17A1430419.speaker: Parker
A17A1430419.text: As long as you're above the break in the slope; that's right.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Well, that's all right. It's being done; but let's watch those kind of calls please.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: (Acting the peacemaker, smoothing ruffled feathers) They can't appreciate the toughness of going up this slope, though. We can; we've got to tell them that.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Well, we did.

A17A1430419.speaker: Parker
A17A1430419.text: Yeah, that's what we were saying. Don't go above just at the base of the break in the slope, Jack. Don't climb all the way up there with it.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Oh, relax! [Schmitt - "I made a suggestion right at the beginning about where to do the rake sample; and they were coming back as if they never heard that. It seemed at the time that Bob wasn't screening requests from the Backroom and that he should have said, 'Hey, he's already told you that.' That's why I was getting annoyed."] [Cernan - "There were just so many things going on in that Backroom and in the Control Center; Jack's been back there and he knows it. There were a lot of things that Bob had to filter out and there was a lot of time pressure. Coordination was the key and I think it w

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Okay, we're all set, Bob. No problem. (Pause) (Garbled). [Jack switches to a two-footed hop as he gets on the steeper slope below the boulder. After a few hops straight uphill, he starts moving cross slope.]

A17A1430419.speaker: Evans
A17A1430419.text: Ah, she's pointing in the wrong direction.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: We want to get away from that big rock (to get the rake sample) because it's probably shedding. Hey, that's a different rock, Gene.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Yeah. Well, it looks like the same texture, but it's got that flaky fracture pattern all over it. I'm going to get a (flightline) stereo while I'm at it. 143:10:08 Schmitt: Yeah. (Pause) [Jack plants the scoop in the ground. Gene is taking a series of cross-Sun pictures showing the entire south face of the boulder. These are AS17-137-20912 to 20923. David Harland has assembled frames 912 to 914 .]

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: This ought to cover any samples I take off of that thing. (Pause) I'm going to get myself a zap of cold water. (Pause) Man, we've got to be a million miles away from the LM. [Jack leans on the boulder for a close examination. Gene double waves to reach his cooling control .]

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Okay, this is a crystalline rock, Houston. It's got nice white halos around the zap pits. The (centers of the) zaps are not dense black glass, but a dark greenish...a very dark greenish-gray.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Are those halos or fragments?

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: No, they're halos. Well, there are fragments, I think, also. But, right now, (I'd say) it's fairly crystalline, but it is heterogeneous. Matter of fact (laughs) there's a big fragment of a porphyry caught up in this thing, I think. [A porphyry is a rock with two distinct crystal sizes.] [Schmitt - "We had learned from the rocks brought back on the earlier missions that the zaps were a very good indicator of what was underneath because, not only did they shatter the crystalline fragments, but they knocked off the patina. There was a light, brownish patina on all of these rocks that we had found

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Did you get a locator, by any chance?

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: I haven't done a thing.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Okay. Well, I want to start taking some (samples). [Fendell pans away counter-clockwise.]

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Gene, we got to get some of that.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: That's what I want. That's where I'm going right now.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: And there's a chunk there we can get. That's a big fragment within this crystalline rock,...

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Take a picture of that...

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: ...an inclusion.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Take a picture of that and then your locator, I'll get it. [Jack's down-Sun "before" is AS17-138- 21038 and his "locator" to the Rover is 21039 (scan by Kipp Teague). In the "locator", notice the disturbed soil around Boulder 1. Note also, Jack's footprints farther to the right. This was his path back from the Rover with the rake. Wessex Cleft is in the far distance above the Rover.] Video Clip ( 3 min 24 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Go ahead (and get a sample). I've got it (that is, the locator). (Pause) Got it?

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Yeah, I've got it.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Beautiful. Looks like a porphyry!

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Boy, it does look like a crystalline rock. 143:11:58 Schmitt: Looks like an andesite porphyry is what it looks like. [Schmitt - "This is a good example of using the appearance of terrestrial examples to help in a description. 'Andesite' implies a specific composition but, when you're in the field you're not so much saying that you think it's that composition as you're saying what it resembles based on your experience. I think that, somewhere else, we've talked about the trouble some members of the scientific community gave Buzz Aldrin when he said something looked like mica. There's absolutely

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: (Garbled) got some very large crystals in there. They're very reflective, elongated crystals.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: (To Houston) It's a relatively angular inclusion. It's about a half a meter in size, and it's a square cross section. Well, it's irregular; but generally square cross section. It's in bag 516, and it looks like it's a high feldspar rock. It may be an anorthositic gabbro, but it does look like a porphyry. [Schmitt - "I've just noticed that, at the start of this speech, my words were slurred, almost as if I were very dry or had too many drinks. I may have just been getting tired, because I'd just climbed the slope."]

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: There's a big chunk where I've got...I can't get it out, though; it's buried in the rock...Oh, a half-an-inch, elongated...I can't see whether they are colorless or not, but they are certainly reflective crystals. See that up here? See right there?

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Yeah.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: And then in the big rock, you've got massive things - like this big fragment here - that's 5 inches across.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Well, that may be a spall point, Gene; that's a lighter color, in general, because of a zap or something.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Let me get some more samples off it.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Yeah, we need to get some of the host rock here.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Okay. We'll get a piece here.

A17A1430419.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1430419.text: Okay now, you're still sampling the one we just got. So we'll get another one (of the same inclusion). Okay. The same kind...The contact of that (inclusion with the host) rock looks like it might be finer grained, but it's about the same...in 517. That's the inclusion side of the contact. (Pause) Keep going after the other one, Gene, I'll get this in your bag. [Houston is discussing a ten-minute station extension. Fendell is looking into Nansen.]

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Bob, you could probably see this rock if you look over this way. We're high enough.

A17A1430419.speaker: Parker
A17A1430419.text: Yeah, we saw it, Geno. Quite a sight; quite a goodie.

A17A1430419.speaker: Cernan
A17A1430419.text: Okay. Let me see if I can't get this one here. There it is.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1431417csm.text: Old heaters sure work on these optics. They're always nice and warm when you take them out.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay. The host rock for the inclusion - which appears to be also crystalline but may be a re-crystallized rock of some kind...

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Can't see it too well.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: ... (of) metamorphic...(It) also looks like it's (got a) high plagioclase (content)...high feldspar, anyway. That's in bag 518. And that was a fairly loose but in-place fragment along a fracture zone. Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay,...

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Will you hold this a minute? I'm going to try to get the rest of it up there.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay, 17. And for your thinking in the next few minutes, you might also factor in the question the Backroom raises about taking 10 minutes out Station 4 and adding it into this station, given the wealth of interest that seems to be occurring here. You might think about that. You haven't been to Station 4, so it's a little hard to judge. But if you think 10 minutes can be very profitably spent, you might as well do that.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay, Bob, we'll think about it. This is a medium-green.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: I can't get any more of that.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: ...anorthositic gabbro, and it looks like it has some pastel-green olivine crystals in it. (To Gene) Did you get it?

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: We copy that. [Fendell is still looking into Nansen at high magnification.]

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: I can't get any more of it, Jack, up there. I can't reach it.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay, and that small chip of that is in 519. It's the same host rock, much like the previous sample.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: There's a good sample for you.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay. (To Bob) And another chunk of the host...Oops, be careful.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Yep.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: It's still there.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Yeah, I've got it.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: I need to get rid of this (sample)...

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay? [Fendell pans clockwise.]

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: It's in there. I haven't closed your bag (Gene's SCB) yet. (Pause) And we've got to get one soil sample up the hill here. Oh, we're going to get the rake...

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1431417csm.text: Looks like Menkar.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: We ought to get a soil sample, though, up here, so...

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: We'll get the rake sample right over here on this slope.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: (Having just chipped off a rock fragment) Where did that thing go, Jack?

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: Right here.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay. Was that last sample in 518, as well?

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: (To Jack) There it is. That's it right there.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: (Responding to Bob) No. We haven't put it in yet.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1431417csm.text: Bob, that will go in 499.

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1431417csm.text: Copy that. (Pause) [Fendell examines the North Massif.]

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1431417csm.text: (To Gene) Can you get it? (Pause) Okay. (To Houston) Bob, this is a fairly uniform-looking rock. It does have some widely-spaced fractures across it. It's clearly crystalline and has crystalline inclusions in it. MP3 Audio Clip ( 11 min 38 sec )

a17_1431417csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1431417csm.text: Okay. Canopus. Canopus. Okay, take me to Canopus.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Here, Jack...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Copy that.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Might get the soil from around that thing.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Bob, both rocks look like they might be in the anorthositic class...

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Your bag is still open part way, too.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: ...of rocks. It's just that one has the appearance of being a finer grain matrix. Looks like a porphyry in the boulder.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. And a reminder, as you photograph it, to remember that the photograph in the southwest quadrant there will be the best ones. Around the corner on two sides there will be the best ones to show the structure through the whole rock.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Yes, sir. (Thinking about what Bob has just said) Oh, the southwest?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: South and west.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Roger.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: South and west. Yeah.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Roger.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: No, the west's in shade.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: No, no. You mean the...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Southwest...

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: South and east.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Roger. The southwest face...Or it faces not quite south. [Fendell is looking at the sky.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I've got a stereo. I'll just continue my stereo around here. Hey, Jack, you can get way under there, and I know you could get soil. I don't know how long it's been shadowed, but it's been shadowed as long as this rock's been here. Video Clip ( 2 min 32 sec 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I'll do that.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Way out under there. I've got to stereo this one. I've already got it.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Well, I'm getting it from this way, and they like that. Did we kick any dirt in under there? [Soil kicked under the overhang will contaminate any shadowed samples. One of the aims of collecting these samples is to look at the influence of solar wind exposure on the relative abundances of various elements and, of course, an admixture of unshadowed soil would, of course, muddle the analysis.] [Cernan - "In the suit, shuffling around, you're not the most agile person in the world and, if you're not careful, you'll kick dust onto a pristine surface that you want to sample. When you're working, you

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: No. I don't...No, I don't think so. Go way down in there. Let me get a couple of "after" pictures. Yeah, we want to get two sides of these rocks, and you can see their structure. (Pause)

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I've got that (picture), Gene.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay. [Gene has just taken AS17-137- 20924 .]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I took those. I took that stereo. [Fendell reaches the rear of the Rover. Jack has taken AS17-138- 21040 , 21041 , and 21042 .]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay, and if I could remind you guys to get a pan...

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Did you get under there?

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: ...from up there before you leave the high uphill area there. There's no point in climbing up there twice. Remember?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I think so.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yes, sir, Bob. How much time we got here now?

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Stand by. (Pause)

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: (To Gene) Okay. You got your bag?

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. We got 12 or 13 minutes left at this station; unless you take that extra 10 minutes that we were offering you.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Let's take it, Bob.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: We got to get the rake.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Let's take it; we'll need it. [Fendell is looking at Earth over the Massif.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay. Let me try again (to get the overhang sample).

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I don't know whether I can or not.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Do you know how far under you're getting, by any chance?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Yeah. (To Houston) I got under an east-west overhang about 20 centimeters...Way back. Quite a ways back; it goes even farther, but that's about as far as I can reach back and sample

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: That's enough, Jack let me...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I copy that...

A17A1431707.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1431707.text: Okay, we just got a beautiful picture of the Earth from the - from the Rover. Just spectacular picture of the Earth.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: That's in bag 500. [Post-flight analysis of this 106-gram soil sample ( 72320 ) indicates that it wasn't completely shielded from the Sun and is comparable to fully exposed soil collected nearby.] </blockquote

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: And, 17, if you want to take a minute, you might look up in the sky and notice that our (TV) camera is taking a beautiful picture of Mother Earth.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Isn't that pretty over...Can you see the Massif, too?

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Now we're coming down to look at the Massif. Had a beautiful picture of the Pacific there? Ed (Fendell) finally found it. Now we see the Massif. [Schmitt - "Ed had been in charge of the Communications Console for as long as I could remember."] [Cernan - "The Earth looked big; and, like the Moon looks down here, it probably wasn't as big as it looked. Yet, because the Earth's beauty was so predominant, there was also a feeling that it was the most precious possession a man could stow in his memory. There was the beauty of the colors of the oceans and the clouds: multiple shades of blue, from th

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: (Probably having stowed the sample in Gene's SCB) Okay.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: And, Bob, I took an "after" picture (AS17-137- 20925 ) of where Jack just got that soil sample under the rock from; and I'm on (frame) 60.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Copy that.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Are you through with the gnomon?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yeah. Video Clip ( 3 min 15 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I'll set it up for the rake.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I'll go up there and get a pan, Jack.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay. You get that pan...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: I didn't get that soil bag number, Jack.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: We've been here...(Answering Bob) 500.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Copy that. (Long Pause) [Fendell returns to Jack, who is positioning the gnomon at the rake site.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: We're on a pretty good slope, Geno.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: You betcha. And do I know it.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: (To Gene) Hey...Bob, how long have we been at this station? [Jack plants the scoop.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Stand by. (Pause) You've been here about forty minutes right now. Can you believe it?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Is that right?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: All ready? Jack...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: And we're going to give you that extra 10 minutes out of Station 4.

A17A1431707.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1431707.text: You sound - you sound...

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I can't believe we've been here...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: That leaves you about 20 minutes; then you'll have to be moving. [As indicated on CDR-11 ( 26k ), Station 2 was scheduled to be a 50 minute stop. They been here for about 38 minutes so far. They had planned to arrive at Station 2 at 2:02 and leave at at 2:52 minutes. They arrived at 2:08 and, with the extension, they should leave at 3:08. They will actually leave at about 3:12.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Boy, this pan may be looking right smack in the sides of the Massifs. Only way you can get it is to lean back, and I can't lean downhill. (Long Pause) [Jack is taking down-Sun photos of the rake site. The rake head is sitting on the ground with the handle sticking up at about a forty-five degree angle. The rake head is quite heavy, about 1.50 kilograms compared with 0.82 kilos for the extension handle. The "before" pictures of the rake site are AS17-138-21043 to 21046.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: (Warning Jack and making a mis-identification) Hey. Watch out for that crater behind you there, Geno. 143:22:04 Cernan: I'm standing in the crater so I can get level.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Yeah, we see that. [Gene's pan photos are AS17-137- 20926 to 20956 . He is standing about 10 meters upslope from Boulder 2. Frame 20942 is a good shot into Nansen. David Harland has assembled a high-resolution portion of the pan ( 2.9 Mb ) showing Nansen, Boulder 2, and the Rover, using scans from original film provided by NASA Johnson and processed by Kipp Teague. The frames are AS17-137- 20938 to 20955 .

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Well, I have some good pictures of Nansen, anyway, and...(Long Pause) You know, I look out there, I'm not sure I really believe it all.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Bob, my down-Sun pictures on the rake were taken at f/8. I'm sorry.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay, copy that. We'll take it into account. [A nominal down-Sun picture of a rake sample would be taken at f/11, at a distance of eleven feet, and at 1/250th of a second exposure.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: This isn't an easy (task)...Okay, I got to get out of my shadow or I can't see what I'm doing. (Long Pause) [Jack gets the sample by dragging the rake uphill. He stands facing the mountain, slightly uphill of the gnomon, and begins each stroke with the rake at his side and then pulls it forward. It looks like a very awkward motion. At the end of the stroke, he hops forward and drags the rake a little farther.] [Schmitt - "Any tool that you have to drag along the ground is going to be difficult to use and, by this time, anything you had to do with your hands wasn't easy."]

A17A1431707.speaker: Evans
A17A1431707.text: Okay, hey, real fine. You know the guys at lunar surface don't even have any ZPN, you know. They left it up here.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I'll be right down there to bag that rake (sample) for you. 143:23:22 Schmitt: I got to get it first. [After finishing the pan, Gene turns and takes three photos of the Earth over the South Massif. These are AS17-137- 20957 , 20958 , and 20959 . He then takes two more pictures of Earth over Boulder 2. These are AS17-137- 20960 and 20961 .]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: (Laughing and joining Jack) Man, I tell you; can you come downhill in a hurry. Going uphill is a nice job. Bob, I'd say we can meet our walkback constraints, if anyone's interested.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I expect it's all downhill from here.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Well, no, sir. Not exactly;... [A major consideration in traverse planning was the possibility of a Rover failure that would force the crew to walk back to the LM. For return under an hour, it was assumed that the crew could achieve an average speed of 3.6 km/hr and average metabolic rate of 1560 BTU/hr. For longer returns, the assumed averages were 2.7 km/hr and 1290 BTU/hr. The assumed metabolic rates included a 20 percent safety margin and were used determine how quickly the remaining supplies of oxygen and cooling feedwater would last.] [A figure from a 22 August 1972, pre-flight planning

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Can you guys see the LM, or are you too far down to see the LM?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: ...that's why I said we could meet our walkback constraints. (Responding to Bob) Oh, no. The LM is over about three rises in the Scarp before we can even see it.

A17A1431707.speaker: Evans
A17A1431707.text: Oh, there's old 13. Take 14 out, so we - put [garble] in the bottom.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay, I thought that might have happened.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I'm not even at a level of the last hill we came over.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I don't know if you've looked up that way (with the TV).

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Roger. We had a feeling for that. I was just checking. (Pause)

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: We can meet them (the walkback constraints), but I wouldn't stretch them.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. (Pause) [Schmitt - "By this time in Apollo, the walkback constraints had been well established. My main effort was to make sure they weren't too constraining. Left to their own devices, some of the planners would have been much more conservative than was necessary."] 143:24:33 Schmitt: Not many small, walnut-sized fragments in here, Bob. Gotten about seven or eight (in the rake sample).

A17A1431707.speaker: Evans
A17A1431707.text: Hey, that sounds like an excellent idea. Thank you.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I copy that. (Pause) [Schmitt - "The people examining samples had concluded that there was a significantly larger variety in the walnut-size range than there were in the major rocks that were scattered around. Apparently, rocks thrown into a site from distant places were concentrated in the walnut-size range."] [After finishing each rake swath, Jack has been moving sidehill to stand on the just-raked ground and begin the next swath. He had started the series with a long swath at 143:22:42, took nine more short ones requiring only a step or two each. Now, he finishes the series with an ex

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Gene, you got a bag?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yes, sir. Right here. How you doing?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: My hands are getting tired.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yeah. Bag 501. (Pause) [Jack gets another short swath.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: No, there aren't a lot; but that'll fill up a bag. [Throughout the EVAs, the astronauts show a tendency to speak more loudly to Houston than to each other, despite the fact that, in both cases, there is a radio link through the LCRU.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Evans
A17A1431707.text: Okay, we're 11 - out - picked nice small ones, I gueas. None of them have been stuck so far.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: This (a) kilogram-of-sample site, too? [Jack is wondering if he is now supposed to use the rake to get a bag full - roughly a kilogram - of soil.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I'll have to look (at the checklist); I think so. I think they all are, aren't they?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Practically. [Jack pours the rocks in the bag that Gene's holding. The checklist does not explicitly call out a kilogram of soil at this site.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: And this is one that we would like to get the kilogram of soil from, Jack.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay. I'll use my scoop for that. [Jack gets his scoop.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Bag 501.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Copy that, Gene. (Pause)

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay, what do we have left here?

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: (Consulting his checklist) We want to get a...I got the high pan. (Pause)

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I don't know how we used up all the time, but we did.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay, (on) my pan, by the way, I got extensive vertical coverage down into Nansen, Bob. [Jack angles the scoop head.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. Copy that, Gene. Thank you.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Well, the soil's getting into my (scoop hinge)...

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I don't know where the hour went that it took to drive here. [Gene gets another sample bag.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Evans
A17A1431707.text: Good thing I looked. Okay. And P52. Get gyro torquing angles. Let's see, we had 7 and 14 angles, wasn't it. We're not torquing now - we torqued at 190. Okay. We went to Auto, got to do a GDC Align. Okay. We'll go Manuel and Wide. Tens 25. Okay. We're configure. Okay. Lima Lima for 21 frames. Well, let's see. About to finish that one up. Verb 62 is not here though - Caged. Good. Let's see.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Maybe time's different in space. "Adventures in space and time."

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: We changed 2 hours and 40 minutes. I don't know whether that makes us older or not. [Jack gets a scoopful of soil but drops some as he lifts the scoop. Gene's "we changed 2 hours and 40 minutes" is a reference to a delay in launch from Earth. Not wanting to alter the timing of events at the Moon, NASA decided to have them fly a quicker-than-planned trajectory to the Moon so that they reached lunar orbit at the planned time. In addition, NASA put all of the mission clocks ahead by 2:40 so that, while we are currently at 143 hours, 26 minutes on the mission clock, it has only been 140 hours, 46

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Ooops...(Pouring) Awrrrrrr...

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Try again. I got half of it. I got three-quarters of it. 502, Bob, will be the kilogram. [Jack gets a second scoopful.] Video Clip ( 2 min 32 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Copy that.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: And that's a sample down to about 5...about 4 centimeters. Don't get (the sample bag) too close to your camera. Okay.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Oh, that's a big bag full. Want to put it in mine? [They have been putting most of the samples in Jack's SCB and Gene is offering to take some of the load.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: It's all right. I can't feel it (that is, the weight of the SCB). You might as well...(Pause) [Jack presents his SCB to Gene, who is twisting the sample bag shut.] [Cernan - "We tried to distribute loads but, compared with the weight of the backpack, the weight of the SCB never bothered me. In one-sixth gravity you just couldn't put that much into one of the SCBs and I just never felt like I was carrying any extra weight."] [At the end of the EVA - and after some redistribution of samples - they report SCB weights of 24 and 35 terrestrial pounds. At the end of EVA-3, they report two other bags

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: How's your cooling? Okay?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Cooling's fine. My hands are tired.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Well, that's natural.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay,...

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay. And guys, do you see any more different blocks up there that are worth sampling before you go on down on to the flats (down near the Rover, below the break in slope) and sample the light mantle?

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: We haven't had a chance to look around any more than you've heard.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: You want a rake in the light mantle here? [Fendell pans away.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: We want a rake in the light mantle. You might as well get that down by the Rover later on.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: (To Gene) Get an "after" (photo)...Get an after, Gene. (Calling after him) Gene, get an after.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yeah. Got it, got it, got it, got it.

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Then you might look around...

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I'm sorry, Bob. Go ahead. [Fendell returns to them.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: ...for a couple of documented samples there, up on the slope of the Massif, before you move down the flatter, light mantle areas by the Rover. Just do the other sampling.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: We will. [Jack starts downhill; Gene takes the "after", which is AS17-137-20962.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Okay, Bob. Jack got the "befores" on the rake and I got the "after".

A17A1431707.speaker: Parker
A17A1431707.text: Okay; we have that. (Pause) [Jack stops at two rocks slightly uphill from Boulder 3.] Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (34 sec; 0.4 Mb)

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Okay, Bob, here are two rocks side by side, a meter or two in diameter. And one is the anorthositic gabbro, if I can use the term; and the other is that two-cycle breccia. [Here, Jack is using 'anorthositic gabbro' to describe light-colored, crystalline material such as that found in Boulder 2. The 'two-cycle' breccia is the blue-gray material of Boulder 1. Gene comes downhill using the two-footed kangaroo hop.]

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Man, that's the way to come downhill.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Just don't stub your toe.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yeah, that's the way to come downhill. [Cernan - "When you were going uphill, you had to take little steps and get your toes dug in. Because you didn't have as much weight holding you down as you would have on Earth and because you're center-of-mass was so high because of the backpack, it was harder to keep your balance. But coming downhill, the only trouble was - like being on a ski-slope - if you came straight downhill using that kangaroo hop, you'd get going really fast. And, if you stubbed your toe, you'd go tail over tea kettle."]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Hey, Gene.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: Yeah. 143:28:21 Schmitt: Set up right there (Boulder 3). Let's get that...Let's get that big clast.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: There's a fracture right in there I want to get the...Oh, the clast.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Yeah.

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: (Very pleased by Jack's discovery) Yes, sir. Good eye, good eye.

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: Big white clast in the two-cy(cle)...(correcting his terminology) in the gray-matrix breccia. [Gene positions the gnomon.] 143:28:35 Cernan: Good eye! Man, that's a prize. Let me get this over here so I can (garbled). [Jack plants the scoop and takes a down-Sun "before" of Boulder 3. This is AS17-138- 21047 .]

A17A1431707.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1431707.text: I think you can even get it. [Jack is saying that he think that Gene can chip the rock with the hammer. Gene backs away to take a cross-Sun stereopair, AS17-137- 20963-64 , while Jack takes the down-Sun. Throughout the sampling of this boulder they demonstrate just how good a sampling team they have become. They don't talk a great deal about what they are going to do; they both know what needs to be done and more or less who is going to do what.] [Schmitt - "The purpose of the training, in my mind, was to make everything that could be routine be as routine as possible so that you didn't have t

A17A1431707.speaker: Cernan
A17A1431707.text: I can get both sides. I want to get this big...Yeah, I think I can get that. I'm going to try. (Pause) [Jack turns to the east to take a "locator" of the Rover (AS17-138- 21048 ) then turns back to the rock and takes another before (AS17-138- 21049 ).]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Grabbing the fragment with the scoop) Got it. [Gene hits the east face twice more.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: There's two more pieces.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Before we cover them up, let's get them. I got to get a sample of that mother rock. [Jack gets one of the fragments, flexing a knee so that he can get low and skim it off of the surface with the scoop blade.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay, there you go. The other one's right there. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Now, Let me see if I can't get a sample...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Want to try to hit that one more time. I think we've got another one coming there. [Gene takes two whacks on an east corner.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: There's another little one. (Pause) [Jack gets the sample.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: That looks almost like a rhyolite from here. I don't believe it, though. [Schmitt - "A rhyolite is a volcanic rock, usually having large crystals in a fine-grained matrix, low in iron-magnesium silicates, high in quartz and feldspar. This inclusion wasn't a rhyolite, but had a similar texture."] [Gene hits the corner eight times.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: No, that's not going to come off.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I think that's it. Got a bag? (Pause) [Gene lays the hammer on the rock and gets a sample bag from his camera bracket.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (To Houston) Okay, this is a fine-grained, but crystalline, white clast in the (blue-)gray breccia; and it's mixed with soil. We had to pick up a little soil. 503. [Gene takes the scoop from Jack, grabbing it near the head, and pours the fragments in the sample bag.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Evans
A17A1432935.text: [Garble] Tank Inlet to Auto. Potable Tank Inlet is Open. Waste Tank Servicing is Closed. Repress Package valve is Off. Better than the simulator. [Garble] Regulators are both Closed.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: I guess they're all there, aren't they?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I think they are. There are three clasts, anyway...(Correcting himself) three fragments that we got off. Chips. [Gene puts the bag in Jack's SCB.] [Sample 72415,0 is a brecciated dunite clast weighing a little over 32 grams. It is described in Volume 1 of the Catalog of Apollo 17 Rocks , as being pale, yellowish-to-greenish gray (colors 5Y 8/1 to 5GY 8/1 in the Geological Society of America (GSA) Rock-Color Chart) . The sample location is shown in a labeled version of AS17-138-21049 from the Apollo 17 Sample Catalog, Part 1 ( 29 Mb PDF ). Post-mission photos S73-16198 and S73-16199 give two di

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Let me get a piece of the rock it's in. And I'm going to take a close-up stereo of that.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay. Don't get it...Okay. (Long Pause) [Gene gets the hammer and knocks a piece off on the third stroke. The piece comes off to Gene's left and he tries to grab it. He manages to touch it and, in so doing, knocks it into Jack's left wrist. The fragment bounces off of Jack's wrist and slowly falls to the ground behind him.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: See it?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Yeah. (Pause) See it!? You hit me with it!

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Well, I tried to catch it. Bob, you still there? [Gene puts the hammer in his shin pocket .]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Roger. Still there. Listening with great delight. [Jack collects the fragment, about ten feet southeast and slightly uphill.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Look at the size of the piece that came off there, though, Jack.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I got another piece of it up here. [Perhaps four feet east and two feet uphill.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: And I'd roll that downhill... [Gene examines the ground northeast of the rock, the direction he thinks it will roll.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay, the host rock for that inclusion of white material will be in bag...What is it? [Gene gets a bag.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: 504. Two chips with soil. (Pause) [Jack pours the samples in the bag. The samples are 72430-35. The largest of these is 72435, a 161 g, clast-bearing, impact melt. It is described as being gray (N4 in the Geological Society of America (GSA) Rock-Color Chart) in Volume 1 of the Catalog of Apollo 17 Rocks . Public Affairs reports that crew heart rates are in the 90s.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Getting heavy?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: What? The bag?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: No. Just the scoop.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Just make sure they're closed so they don't...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I wore my hand out holding that camera together coming out here. [Gene puts the sample bag in Jack's SCB.] 143:31:56 Cernan: We're getting some samples this time. I want to get an "after", and I want to get a close-up stereo of that. And I'm going to get some pictures around this block, too. [Gene is standing just north of the rock; Jack moves east just far enough to get his shadow off the rock. Gene's "after" is AS17-137- 20965 .]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay. There's an "after" and now I'm going to get sort of a close-up stereo around it. That ought to do it. [Jack turns around and moves a few steps east and a little downhill to a small crater full of rocky debris. Gene's close-ups are AS17-137- 20965 to 20973 . He has used his tongs to make sure he is at the right distance from the rock for a good focus. The best of these pictures is probably 20971 .] Video Clip ( 3 min 36 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Hey, Bob, while he's doing that, there's a real good example of a pit-bottom crater up here even on this talus slope. I'll try to take a stereo of it.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, Jack, that sounds great. I guess there's always a problem of getting the in-place glass, if you think that's appropriate at this point. Word along those lines, though, is we'd like to have you in the Rover moving in 11 minutes; so it's probably not appropriate at this time on that. [Jack moves two short hops downhill for another stereo picture. In all, he takes three pictures of the crater: AS17-138-21050 to 21052.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay, there isn't any glass in this crater. (Gesturing) You can see it with your TV.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay; copy that.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: It's just bigger than the average crater. And it still has that pit, the pit being about a third of the inner diameter of the crater...make it a fourth of the rim diameter, that's easier.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Copy that. [Gene is now SW and a little uphill of Boulder 3.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Jack?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Can I look at that closely?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Look at what?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Hold the rake a second. (Pause) [Jack hands Gene the rake and leans on the boulder.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: We got to be moving in how many minutes, Bob?

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: We'd like to have you moving in one-zero (10) minutes, which means: allow the usual 3 or 4 or 5 minutes for close-out before that time.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay, we'll get hustling. [Jack gets up with some difficulty, using the rock and the scoop for support.] Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (1 min 26 sec; 1.0Mb)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay, Bob, that white-colored inclusion we sampled looks like a strange...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Look out, Jack. [Standing uphill of the rock, Gene pushes it with his right foot. Jack moves quickly out of the way to the east. The boulder rocks forward slightly then falls back. Gene gives it a harder kick and the boulder turns over twice as it rolls.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: It's the old boulder-rolling trick. [Schmitt - "There was a lot of boulder-rolling discussion on the field trips . Mostly, Gene just rolled this one for fun but, by doing so, he exposed the soil underneath and we got a sample of it."] [On Apollo 12, Conrad rolled a rock into Head Crater in order to generate a signal for the ALSEP seismometer. And, on Apollos 15 and 16, the crews turned boulders over so that they could sample the soil underneath.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: How about getting a soil sample under there? [As it reaches him, Jack kicks the rock toward the north but it is stopped by a small rise. He tries another kick, but with little effect.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Don't hit the Rover.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Get that sample under there, Jack. Under that rock.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay. Got a bag?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Got a bag.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: The soil from right underneath the rock - down to about 4 centimeters (depth) - (is going) in 505. [Gene is standing a little uphill, so Jack has to raise his arm quite high to pour the sample into the bag. Jack skims a second sample while Gene closes the first bag.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: And I'll try to skim it here a little, too. (I'll) get the upper centimeter.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Bob, this big white clast, I'm not sure there aren't some smaller ones in some of those other big boulders. That's just an intuitive guess. [Gene has the second bag open, just as Jack raises the skim sample.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Oh, there are.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: But we never saw any as obviously big and gross as this one. [Jack does a little jump to get the skim sample out of the scoop and into the bag.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Fact is, this particular boulder I photographed, I had three of them other than the one we sampled. And that's 505 and 506, in that order. [Jack presents his SCB.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay; we copy that.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: On the soil.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: And by now, probably the best thing for you guys...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Bob, that rock...

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: ...to do is to go back to the Rover and pick up the rake sample. Go ahead, Jack. [Gene has the samples in Jack's SCB and turns to get the gnomon.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: That...(Turning uphill to get the rake) (To Gene) I'll get it (the rake).

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (To Bob) That white clast...I looked at it, and it has light, pastel-green, fairly-rounded crystals in a fine-grained white to light pinkish-tan matrix. And you can figure that one out. Looks like olivine in something. [Schmitt - "As it turned out, it was olivine in olivine; almost a pure olivine rock. So it's interesting that I made that guess up there. Olivine has a vitreous luster and a light greenish color but, again, in this case it was chunks of olivine in a crushed matrix of olivine that had been through the mill for four-and-a-half billion years."] [Gene is using the kangaroo hop to ge

A17A1432935.speaker: Evans
A17A1432935.text: Okay, intervalometer. Got to start counting 8 seconds here. Let me [garble] it pretty quick.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Roger on that. Sounds like a rainbow.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: It might be a...(Responding to Bob) No, the colors aren't that distinct, Bob. I'm just giving you shades. Video Clip ( 3 min 44 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 37 Mb MPEG )

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay; Roger. [Jack reaches the Rover. He has been carrying the scoop in his left hand with the handle forward and the head back and pointing at the ground. He tosses it like a baton, getting it to rotate so that, after he catches it, he can mount it on the gate with the head pointing up.] [Schmitt - "You got to where you were doing things like that all the time. Things moved very slowly and the best flexibility you had in any part of the suit was in the wrist; so you took advantage of it."]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Hey, Bob, have you panned down into Nansen and seen this rock that's, oh, 30 or 40 meters from us? To give you an idea of the kind of upslope filleting you have on some of those boulders.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, we'll...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: It's down to your right.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. We'll send Ed (Fendell) over there to look at it.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Well, I'll help him (by manually pointing the TV). I don't think you got enough time. [Jack stows the scoop; Gene stows the gnomon and then goes to turn the TV.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, we'd like you guys to get going on the rake sample. We'd like light mantle on the rake there.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Talking to Gene under Bob) Where's your gnomon? We've got to get a rake sample.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Headed north from the Rover) I'm going to have to move out here a ways, Geno.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay. Coming right there. (Pause) [Gene points the TV into Nansen.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Right there is what I'm looking at.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. We're going to check it out; thank you. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: (Getting the gnomon out again) And there's no sense trying to get 500's up...Well, we'll see what happens. [Gene takes the gnomon to Jack.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. Also, there's no time to get 500's either, unfortunately. We're planning on Station 4, which will be a better perspective distance anyway.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, I was going to say there's no sense in trying to get them up the Massif; I don't think you'll see anything up there. 143:37:16 Parker: Okay. (Pause) [Jack is taking a black-and-white pan from the second rake site northeast of the Rover. Jack's pan consists of frames AS17-138- 21053 to 21073 .] [David Harland has assembled the portion showing - from left to right - Gene, the Rover, and Nansen .] [Frame 21069 is a great picture of Gene.] [Frame 21073 shows the Station 2 boulders.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Gene...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: You getting your pan?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, I said...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Where do you want it (the gnomon for the rake sample)? [Fendell pans counter-clockwise.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Well, right over there where there's some fragments. And you get the...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: I'll get the "before" and the "locator". [The cross-Sun "befores" of the rake site are AS17-137- 20974 and 20975 . They show Jack taking his pan. Frames 20976 and 20977 are "locators" to the Rover.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay, and then I'll get the "down-(Sun)". (Long Pause) [Fendell pans clockwise.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Evans
A17A1432935.text: Solar corona.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Laughing) (It's) tiring to take pictures.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah. Let me tell you, you just got to think an order of magnitude bigger than what you're normally are accustomed to thinking.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay, pan's complete.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Let's get the rake sample so we can move on. (Pause) Bob, I couldn't get those 500's anyway. It would require me to pitch up (lean back) too far, and there's no way I could do it. [Fendell finds Gene and Jack well north of the Rover.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. No, we're definitely not in favor of that, Gene, at this area.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: I know. I'm just mulling it over, but there really isn't any way I could get them.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. [Jack is taking swaths by running forward three or four steps, dragging the rake behind him. Each of the swaths, then is about two meters long.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Boy, I tell you...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: How are your hands? Let me rake that a little bit.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Well, it's all right; there just aren't any rocks. Should have brought the scoop and used the old shovel trick. [Jack has made at least five rake swaths by this time.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: There's a couple; keep going. (Pause) There sure aren't (many), are there?

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, do you have any feeling (that) you have that hard layer underneath there like you did yesterday, when you raked at Station 1, Jack?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: There's one under the gnomon you can get.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Several I thought were rocks turned out to be clods.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, that's what most of them are is clods. How do you get clods if it's never been wet? You're not getting any. You've had three in there ever since the last four scoops.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: There just aren't many. [Jack raises the rake to pour the fragments in the sample bag Gene is holding. He has taken at least seven swaths.] [Schmitt - "We were out on the light mantle, which we thought was an avalanche. If it is an avalanche, you wouldn't expect many rock fragments; they would have worked their way downward in a gas-lubricated avalanche (flow) and all that would be at the surface would be fines. If the surface were old enough, you would find a few fragments, all of them thrown in from elsewhere."] Video Clip ( 2 min 32 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, copy 507, very few.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Three rocks. Yeah, you got about four rocks about 2 inches and smaller. [One of the rocks is a 51-gram 'impact melt breccia' - sample 72735 - that is at least 3.85 billion years old.] </blockquote

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: And let me get the down-Sun which...

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, let's just get the soil and...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (To Gene) Okay. And we want to get the soil.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: ...press on. We'd like to move in 3 minutes, 3 minutes.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay, you got it (the down-Sun picture)?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Yeah. [Jack's down-Sun "after" of the second rake site is AS17-138-21074.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay. Let me put this in your bag (SCB) and...Forget the soil.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Puzzled) Forget the soil?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: He wants us moving in 3 minutes. So let's go.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Well...

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: No, get the soil, guys. Get the soil. Don't forget the soil; get the soil.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, we want it.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: (Hearing Bob) I'm sorry, I thought you said to skip it.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (To Gene) Got your bag?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: (Just getting a bag open) Yep.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: May be a little messy.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: That's all right. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (Pouring) One-scoop-Schmitt, they call me. That's good.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: (To Bob, calling) That's bag 508. [This 885-gram soil sample is 72701 . Its composition is similar to other sample taken in the 'light mantle' areas visited during this traverse.] 143:40:44 Parker: Copy that. [Gene opens Jack's SCB after getting the sample bag sealed.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: You'll have to start putting some of these samples in my bag. You're getting a full bag for Christmas here.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Is it so full we ought to change it?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yep. Let's do that after we get to the next station, though.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Well, okay. [Schmitt - "I suspect that I didn't want to drive a long distance on the Rover with a full SCB; if the top came open we could have lost samples."]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: We ought to start moving out of here.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, let's go. [Jack starts toward the Rover using a high-speed, long-stride lope which he has earlier described as a cross-country skiing stride.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Let me get one "after" of the area.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: That we messed up. (Pause) [Having taken AS17-137- 20978 Gene starts back to the Rover, carrying the gnomon.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Beautiful station, guys; just simply beautiful. Almost deserves a Falcon code. [Gene is going at a rapid pace. Fendell follows him for a while, then does a final site pan.] [Schmitt - "Gene started out doing the kangaroo hop for a little ways and then went into a left-foot-forward skip. He wasn't getting very high off the ground because you can see his toe kicking dirt almost every step. Anybody wanting to estimate how fast two relatively tired people could go should look at this sequence. This one sequence could give you a lot of information about walkback. I'm glad we didn't have to do that.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Man, I'll tell you. (Laughing) Falcon 109. I couldn't help that, Bob; it's just too beautiful. (Pause) [Cernan - "It was a good station; we got a lot done. We'd joked around with the Falcon code - which I'd learned in the Navy - during training but, you notice, it was Bob who brought it up. There were about twenty Falcon phrases, and Falcon 109 was 'Beautiful; just fucking beautiful.'"]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Hey, Jack, will you look where we kicked up this stuff. There's some light...Well, I can't see it now, I'm looking...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I can see. There's a light-colored fragment (means "layer") I think we break into.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah, we kick it up.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: They're light-colored clods. [Schmitt - "The way I responded to Gene makes me think that I had noticed the buried layer of lighter material and had filed it away in the back of my brain while we were working. And it's a good thing he brought it up, because otherwise we wouldn't have noticed it at this point."]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: And when I was walking uphill, I really wasn't sinking in - probably - more than an inch or two. [Schmitt - " I think Gene is comparing the depth of his footprints in the light mantle with those he made in the talus slope where we sampled the boulders. From the fact that we got (rock) fragments on the talus slope but not in the light mantle tells me that we had a finer material on the light mantle and I expect we were sinking in farther down there. This section is confusing, there's a lot of (verbal) shorthand."] 143:42:00 Schmitt: You want to take this bag off of me?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: I'll get one out. We can use this one. Video Clip ( 3 min 41 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yeah. Because we want to get rolling. (Pause) [Fendell looks into Nansen again.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, 17, there's a couple of things here, while your getting undone there. There's our housekeeping to close out. Change those bags. We'd also like to get the SEP turned on, and you might read us the temperature when you turn it on. And other than that, stowing the TV and low-gain (meaning to say "high-gain") antenna and you're on your way. We've taken care of the gravimeter already.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Did our (gravimeter) reading change much, Bob?

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Which one? [Schmitt - "I was wondering if we got a big gravity change as we got up onto the Massif. We did, but I don't know if anybody ever told me about it."] [There is no further discussion of the Station 2 gravimeter reading anywhere in the transcript.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: (To Gene) Make sure that's locked on there. 143:42:42 Cernan: Yeah, it is locked; make sure the cap's locked. (To Bob) Okay, bag 8 is on the gate, and Jack's getting bag 4.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay; copy that. (Pause) [That is, Gene is putting SCB-4 on Jack's PLSS. Note that Jack had been wearing SCB-8.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Boy, I know my camera's going to be...

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: You copy on the SEP receiver turn on and temperature?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Right.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: (To Jack) Is my bag closed? (Responding to Bob) We got that, Bob.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Your bag is closed.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay...

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay. 17, take all that back, we've just had a change of heart back here. And we're not going to turn the SEP on, just cover it up. And you might give us a temperature reading as you go by; that'll help us think what to do with it. [Schmitt - "They were realizing that the SEP was running awfully hot and, probably because we were going to retrace our tracks, they thought that they might save it for the final traverse by leaving it off and covered."]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: It's about 98.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Copy 98; then leave them both off. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay. [The SEP has cooled down from 105 F during the stop.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: 17. John (Young) and Charlie (Duke) are kind of advising you to put that full SCB(-8) underneath the seat to make sure the top doesn't bounce open and lose some of those rocks. [They have just mounted SCB-8 on the gate.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Well, you can't take better advice than from those who have been here!

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Roger on that.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Their advice has been pretty good, so far.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: I won't pass that on to them. I think they...(Pause) 143:44:15 Cernan: These locks (on the tool gate) are clamming up (with dust), Jack. I can't unlock that one now. (Pause) Can you lock that one? (Pause) They're all getting sticky. [Fendell finds them at the gate. The locks referred to here are clamps to hold SCBs on the gate.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: That one just didn't want to work any more.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Let me see.

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: It isn't moving either way.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: This one was sticky, too. Let me see. (Pause)

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Out's Open, right?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Huh?

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Out is Open...

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Out is Open, yeah. Let me try once more, if I have to...

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Here I got it.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay, those are really getting dusty. I'll hit those with a dustbrush next time around. (Pause) [Jack carries SCB-8 to his seat.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Charge that time up to John and Charlie! (Pause) [Jack is saying that they wouldn't have lost the time if they hadn't been told to remove the bag from the gate and put it under the seat. Of course, a little lost time would be minor compared with lost samples.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1432935.text: Okay. What haven't we done?

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay. I got to get the (TV) camera. Okay, Bob, I'm taking your camera.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Okay, looks like it's in the right place, you won't have to turn it around. Good coordination. [Fendell has the TV pointed down and aft, the proper position for the traverse.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Yes, sir. Okay. We read the TGE ; I'm going (LCRU) Mode 1. [TV off.]

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: Roger on that. Okay; we lost the picture. (Long Pause) And give me a call when you guys get rolling.

A17A1432935.speaker: Cernan
A17A1432935.text: Okay.

A17A1432935.speaker: Parker
A17A1432935.text: And we'd like frames when it's convenient on you guys.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: (Looking at the traverse map, LMP-14 ) Okay, Geno, more or less follow our tracks back until we get over the big hump and then we can start picking our way to (Station) 3. I've got 3 pretty well spotted.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay; low-gain is set, and heading about 035...Oh, let me set this thing out of the way again. This has been giving me more trouble.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: What's that? The hammer?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yeah, the handle.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Oh, getting caught in there? [The hammer is in the pocket on Gene's right shin and is probably catching on the bottom of the console.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay, Bob. We're ready, we're rolling. You need any readings?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: No, no readings called out (in the checklist). And when you get going, I'll give you a little advice on what we're going to do on the way to Station 3. [They are now about 3 hours 12 minutes into the EVA. As indicated on CDR-15 ( 29k ), they had planned to leave at 2:52. Half of the twnety minute difference is due to the 10 minute extension that Houston offered and Gene accepted. The plan is to shorten Station 4 by those 10 minutes. A figure from an EVA-2 planning document by P.E. Reynolds of Bell Labs ( 50k ) shows the planned Return Distances and EVA Elapsed Times at various stages in the EV

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Well, let me tell you a few things first, Bob.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Okay, start telling me. [Cernan - (Laughing) "This is a typical exchange between Jack and Bob. Sometimes it almost got to be a test of wills."] [Schmitt - "We were there to learn. I wanted to be sure that I didn't get distracted and forget some pertinent observation. The Backroom wanted as much information as we could give them and during this time when we were driving away from the station was a good time to do the equivalent of making some field notes."]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: I think those two...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: We're rolling!

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: All right. Those two major kinds of blocks that we sampled there...(they were) about the (only) two varieties we saw in the area, (and) it's a long extrapolation I realize, but they do resemble in color, and I believe in texture, the blue-gray rocks and the light-tan rocks up on the Massif. So I feel confident that - fairly confident - that we sampled at least the two major units visible from a distance in the South Massif. [Jack sounds a little tired.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Excellent. Excellent.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: I think that there is some...(correcting himself) a lot of post-mission work to be done on correlating the angularity and possibly even the albedos of the rocks we sampled with those on the Massif. We should have good pictures of both from a distance and up close.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Okay. I'm reminded...

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: So we may be able (garbled)...

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: ...that extrapolation is the nature of our art.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: (A slow, deliberate laugh) Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha. [Schmitt - "I think that this is the pilot laughing at the scientist's admission of imprecision."]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: And, Bob, I'm not going to...How am I on the film?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Oh, my golly! Look at that valley!

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Stand by. I'll get that for you, Jack...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: I think there's a...

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: I think you're doing fairly well, now. And before you guys get too far, a couple of comments we want to do on the way. There is a Rover sample stop in your checklist, it used to be at 073 and 6.3; it's the first thing there, halfway out to Hole-in-the-Wall. And we're now going to have that Rover sample stop at 078 and 7.0. That should be along your tracks going home. So, about 078 and 7.0, we'll have the Rover sample stop. And the gravimeter people have won today, and we're going to stop and get off the Rover and get a gravimeter reading at that location. We're taking out (time from) some stop

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Okay. I'll take pictures, then. [The planned Rover sample stop is not shown on the checklist map on LMP/CDR-14 but, rather, on the list of traverse tasks on LMP/CDR-15 . AS17-138- 21075 and 21076 are taken during the next minute or so.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Bob, we're on the top, coming off the highest lobe of the Scarp looking back into the valley. And it's quite a scene back there, but we still cannot see the LM. (Pause) That may be it. I don't know. [They are about 300 meters from Station 2.] 143:50:16 Schmitt: Hey, turn a partial pan; I know it's into the Sun. [Jack will take a series of pictures as Gene turns the Rover in a circle. These pictures are AS17-138- 21077 to 21092 . Because of the glare of the Sun, the up-Sun frames - 21079 and 21080 - don't show much detail.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Evans
A17A1434649.text: And I forgot to look at the central peak on that thing other than the fact that I can remember the - the high-water mark. If - you've really got to check that high-water mark to make sure it's a high-water mark and not a talus slag - occasional talus slope. I've got to check that for sure.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Wait a minute. Wait a minute. Okay. Let's take one from right here. I want the whole thing (that is, the whole valley). (Pause) You ready to start?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Yeah, I got it.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Start taking. Take the whole thing.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Go ahead.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Get around this crater.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: I got a pan down the valley. This is just going to be right into the (Sun)...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yeah. Don't take that one. Get it up as we come around. You get it?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: There we go.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay. That's the one we want. And you got the valley?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Yeah. Keep going. [The whirring sound of film advancing in Jack's camera can be heard.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Keep turning around over there, and I'll get that Scarp. That's beautiful.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Isn't that something? Man, you talk about a mysterious looking place. (Pause)

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: They can cut some frames - some parts of those pictures out - and make a nice photograph. (Laughing) (With the) TV camera, (and) maps (in the way). (Pause) [The pan turned out to be relatively uninteresting because of the Sun glare. Pictures taken during the next minute or two are AS17-138- 21093 , 21094 , and 21095 .]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Okay, looking at the light mantle: No more comments except that by that rake sample and just looking, there's certainly are fewer fragments than we saw at Station 2. The main thing that we can tell about the light mantle and when we're on it, of course, is the light-colored craters. The fresher craters all appear to be light colored. As they get older, the albedo goes down and potentially (that can be explained if the craters) have been dusted with material from the dark mantle or from other sites. Either that or it's just the lunar patination that we're all familiar with. [The light color of

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Say, Bob. Give me that bearing and range again for the...

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: 7.0 right here.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: ...up on the hill. How about 071 and 7.0? Will that do?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Yeah. I think that that will be enough to hack it.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Well, if not, we can go down there.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: No, no, no. Good Lord. Stay on the road you're on.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Well, I'm not on any road, but I'm stopping here.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: I thought you guys were making a road.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Roger.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Let me turn it off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Yeah, also...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: (Garbled) 9.8 and 7.0.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Okay. And the Rover numbers (roll and pitch) should be fairly flat for the ole gravimeter.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Uh, oh.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: (Responding to Parker) Well...That means we have to change here.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Hey, right over here to my right...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Maybe it's the best we can do, but it's still going to be on a slope.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Well, I'll level it off on a (garbled)... [Because they will take the gravimeter reading without putting the instrument on the ground, Gene is trying to level the Rover by using a crater rim to prop up one or more of the wheels.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: (Garbled)?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Yeah; go ahead. I'm off (the Rover). Do you see...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yeah, I see it. Right there.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
