A17A1434649.text: On the rim of that crater that's built up a little bit? (Brief static)

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Right up here.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: What's your...Can you tell your roll?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Okay, now that's about zero (roll) right there.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: What's your roll?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Let me turn this off. Boy, this roll indicator isn't very...Oh; zero.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Zero?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yeah.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: I'll punch it (the gravimeter). You'll change it (the roll) as soon as you get off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Now it's zero. [Note, that it is very difficult to decide who has said what during the last few lines, a fact which also makes it difficult to decide what has been happening. The person speaking at 143:53:54 sounds like Gene, but this section doesn't make sense unless the speaker is actually Jack or, alternatively, unless Jack didn't get off the Rover at 143:53:28.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Oh, you got to get off anyway.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Do I have to get off for this?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Roger. Both of you get off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: (Because of the) gravimeter reading.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Why should I have to get off?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: So you don't move the ole gravimeter. [This is evidently not standard procedure and, at least in this instance, improvising costs precious time.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Think you can hold still?

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yeah. I'll hold still.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: No. Negative on that, Gene.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Okay, Bob. (To Gene) Give me your sampler 'cause that's the other thing I have to do.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Yeah. We'll get Rover samples, at least.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Unless you need me off?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Roger. We want Gene and Jack both off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Evans
A17A1434649.text: Okay. There's Chaplygin [garble]. Okay. Marconi. The - There's Marconi. There's Marconi. Vil'ev and - Dellinger and Panne - Something like that.

A17A1434649.speaker: Mission Control
A17A1434649.text: 143:55:54 - Ron Evans in America is on his 29th lunar revolution. We'll be acquiring him in 14 minutes. In addition to the experiments that he's been performing he's been doing a considerable amount of visual science descriptions. Ron is on his Flight Plan.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Well, if you need me off; Jack, just punched it.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Okay. Hold still. They don't know anything about your PLSS noise. [Jack is suggesting that vibrations produced by Gene's fans and pumps might disturb the TGE .]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: I better get off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Yeah, I think you oughta.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Gene, we'd like both of you off.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Got that. (Long Pause) [This location is plotted as Station 2a in Figure 6 and Figure 7B in the USGS Apollo 17 Professional Paper.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Don't push it yet...Did you?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: No. (Pause)

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: (Now off the Rover) Okay. Go ahead and push it.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Let me wait until it settles down here. [They may be standing at the gate, waiting for the Rover to quiet.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: This thing is all (garbled, possibly "taped shut"), isn't it? This thing doesn't change. [There had been some discussion of taping the SEP covers at 140:47:54 , but no decision was made. Unless Jack did some taping without comment - which seems unlikely, the covers won't be taped until the start of EVA-3 at 164:00:57 . Consequently, the identity of "this thing" remains a mystery.]

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: No, that should be good...

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Yes, it does change.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: A couple of times.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Huh?

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Cycle it a couple of times.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: No, the settings.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Oh, I don't know...Yeah, they'll change. Okay. Quiet Rover. Gravity. Mark it.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Copy that.

A17A1434649.speaker: Cernan
A17A1434649.text: Say, Bob, I need a quick f-stop for the 500.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Standby.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: It's the same film.

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Stand by.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: Hey, Bob, can I punch it (the gravimeter) again?

A17A1434649.speaker: Parker
A17A1434649.text: Ah...Yeah. Go to Standby and then punch it again.

A17A1434649.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1434649.text: You don't have to wait for it to time out, do you?

a17_1435554.text: Ron Evans in America is on his 29th lunar revolution. We'll be acquiring him in 14 minutes. In addition to the experiments that he's been performing he's been doing a considerable amount of visual science descriptions. Ron is on his Flight Plan.

a17_1435554.speaker: Parker
a17_1435554.text: Okay. And, Geno, f-stop for the 500 millimeter should be the same as for the 70.

A17A1440802.speaker: Parker
A17A1440802.text: Do you want to give us another range and bearing right now?

A17A1440802.speaker: Cernan
A17A1440802.text: Do you get the feeling that we're the only ones out here, Jack? Looking around...(Responding to Parker) 073 (bearing to the SEP transmitter), 10.3 (distance driven), 6.6 (distance to the SEP transmitter).

A17A1440802.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1440802.text: Bob, I have a feeling that whatever darkens the...Ooh, there's a beautiful little glass-lined crater...pit-bottom crater. Whatever darkens the light mantle is not a one-time-only mantling of darker material. It's something that happens over a period of time, continually, because craters of all sizes and apparent degradation are darkened and there are lighter craters that are light to varying degrees. It seems to be a continuum of albedo change.

A17A1440802.speaker: Evans
A17A1440802.text: The hardest part about taking pictures is that you've got to make sure you look through the viewfinder, make sure the other half of the camera isn't looking into the side of the window.

A17A1440802.speaker: Cernan
A17A1440802.text: You know that little crater on the side of the North Massif that we're thinking about going to doesn't look nearly as light-colored or haloed as it does in (overhead) pictures, does it?

A17A1440802.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1440802.text: You mean Hanover? Yeah, (I agree). No, (it isn't as light-colored as it seemed in the overhead pictures). (Pause)

A17A1440802.speaker: Cernan
A17A1440802.text: Now, let's see where we are, I don't want to run into that big crater at the foot of the (Scarp)...

A17A1440802.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1440802.text: I think you're almost to the rim.

A17A1440802.speaker: Cernan
A17A1440802.text: Yeah, I want to go down here if I can. My tracks are over there to the left, I haven't crossed them yet.

A17A1440802.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1440802.text: 073, 6.3 (bearing and range to the SEP transmitter).

A17A1440802.speaker: Parker
A17A1440802.text: Copy 86. (Pause) [Jack's most recent picture is AS17-138- 21113 , which shows the outer (east) bounding ridge that defines Hole-in-the-Wall.]

A17A1440802.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1440802.text: Boy, that's a sight, isn't it?

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441012csm.text: Houston, it's coming in. Rooster Tail [garble] - Yes, dark striations, vertical - [clipped]tion up and down the a - area rim. And it looks like there's a black - but they all look green. You know, it looks kind of a green-gray in this type of light, back on this side. And a green-gray material down in the center of the Rooster Tail, on the floor of the Rooster Tail. And the floor is about one-fourth of the diameter. Turn this thing off - 60 - minus - Peirce, scale 250, 8-second intervalometer, and I lost my intervalometer. Count 8 seconds, I guess. Stuck it around here and it disappeared. Noth

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: That's spectacular. [Gene has turned north and they can now look along the scalloped, multi-lobed edge of the Scarp toward Hanover and the North Massif. Jack's next five photos , AS17-138- 21114 to 21118 show all of these features with considerable clarity. Gene's photo AS17-137- 20980 was also taken at about this time.]

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: I don't know why something that's all approximately the same hue should...

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: The lack of color has got to contribute to the inability to judge distance. [Cernan - "Ever since I've been back from the Moon, I've attributed the difficulty we had in judging size and distance to the lack of references like telephone poles, roads, trees, and so forth. I'd forgotten that I said this about the lack of color contributing to the problem, and I'm sure it's true. It's interesting that I made the observation at this point in the traverse. Here we were, high up on top of the Scarp in very hummocky, rolling terrain, looking out across the valley and across to the North Massif. You've

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: See the lobes coming out...(See what looks like) lobes coming out from the Scarp. The Scarp, rather than being a line in there on the plain, appears to be lobes. I got a couple of shots of that. Whereas when it gets up on the (North) Massif, it's a fairly continuous curve; although it does appear to be younger; at least there's less relief on it for the first few kilometers of that bend there (on the North Massif). [Schmitt - "We don't know for sure, but the Scarp is probably an actual fault scarp and, out to about halfway across the valley, toward the South Massif, the landslide material is d

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: We're going to have to go down like the way we came (up) because there's that big crater down at the bottom, I'm afraid.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441012csm.text: Yeah, I think we agree with that suggestion, too.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: Bob, the so-called Scarp impresses me as less of a scarp than a series of lobes which roughly have a north-south trend. And we've been driving over various hummocks within those lobes. (Pause)

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441012csm.text: Okay, copy that.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: I think we made a gross mistake in not trying to let them get TV. My heading hasn't changed much at all here. They would have had a spectacular view. Look at it out in that valley, Jack.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: Good lord. I still don't know where the LM is...I see it, I think. The shadow...A blob. It's the only sharp shadow out there right in the...because you sure can't make out the craters from here, can you? Okay, hold on. Over the hill and down the rail. (Pause) Man, I tell you, this machine is fantastic.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: Yeah. Watch it. (Laughs) [Jack's six photos , AS17-138- 21119 to 21124 cover the northward drive to this point.] [The next six photos , AS17-138- 21125 to 21130 show the descent to the bottom of Hole-in-the-Wall.]

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: Quite a machine.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: Likes to spin when you turn going down hill.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: Quite a machine. (Pause)

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: I think you've got something right ahead of you.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: I got it.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441012csm.text: See the instant rock.

a17_1441012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441012csm.text: I got it. There's that crater (at the bottom of Hole-in-the-Wall). It doesn't look nearly as bad from here, but it sure is deep when you get up there. I'll meander around and over this next little lobe then I'll head down that next one - the first lobe we came up - and then along it.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441554csm.text: 250 lens on this.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I'd rather not.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Oh, I don't know, I'm impressed. (Pause) Okay, now where we got to go? (I'm headed) 345 (NNW) roughly. And we want to go to (a bearing and range of) 087/6.1...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay. You're...I think you're headed right...right for where we want.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yep.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: See that bright crater? You can just start to see Station 3 over there now.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, navigation says I've got more than 90 degrees...I should be increasing range. Bob, we're at 079, 11.5, and 5.7. [Gene wants to go to 087/6.1 and is currently at 079/5.7. He is driving on a heading which is a bit more than 90 degrees from the LM bearing and, therefore, is increasing both his range and bearing.] [Cernan - "This is the way I think when I'm flying an airplane: to increase both bearing and range, I need to be more than ninety degrees to the left of the LM bearing. And if I wanted to stay at the same range and increase my bearing, then I'd 'fly an arc' and keep my heading at 9

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, beautiful, guys. Really going smooth.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: And I'm headed northwest.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Roger. In fact, we understand it's been going so smooth down here that they haven't even spilled any coffee in the SPAN room yet this mission. [Schmitt - "The SPAN room was where the troubleshooting started when there was a problem. It was an engineering room, and I used to spend a lot of time in the SPAN room with other missions when I was helping out with various engineering problems. One time I was in there with George Abbey - and I can't remember now quite why it happened - but, up above their consoles, the people in the SPAN room had a pegboard where they stuck all their messages, and it

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Thorson must not be on duty. [Schmitt - "Dick Thorson was the guy who was on duty in the SPAN room the day I spilled the coffee"]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: I'm glad we don't have any (coffee) sitting on the LCRU! [See an account of the Famous SPAN Coffee Spill from the Apollo 17 Fifteenth Anniversary Reunion.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Right over there is Station 3, I think. Oh, actually, I guess...Hmm. (Pause) I guess they would want it...Is there?...I can just start to see two craters...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: You know what the problem is?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: ...that are closer to Lara.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: I got a full planar view of the high-gain and I can't see a thing out there.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: That's right. [Two frames taken at the end of the EVA-3 traverse indicate the nature of Gene's problem. AS17-134- 20476 is a tourist picture of Gene taken from in front of the Rover and shows the TV antenna mounted forward of his seat. Jack was standing fairly close to the vehicle and the antenna isn't as tall as it appears in this image. AS17-143- 21924 , taken from behind the Rover gives a better indication of the antenna's potential for blocking Gene's view. In this frame, the antenna is pointed to the side and doesn't block Gene's view very much. However, on this drive to Station 3, the an

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Full planar view. All I can do is see underneath it. (Pause) Gonna take it (a crater) broadside. See, I can't see a lot of craters now that they're out in front. Oh, I guess I can see them, most(ly). Here's a nice sharp little hole; look at that.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Yep. Bob, the texture of the light mantle - (that is, the) surface texture - is really no different on the Scarp, on its flank, or out here to the east of the Scarp. Fragment population, crater population, everything looks about the same. If there is such a thing as a light mantle, it seems to be uniform across the Scarp.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, I copy that, Jack.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: There are your tracks. Hey! We crossed somebody's tracks! [AS17-138- 21136 shows the outbound tracks and 21137 shows the Scarp lobes.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: We sure did. We just made a loop.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Hope they look like yours.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: That was at 081/5.7.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, copy 081/5.7. Do they look like your tracks?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, here's another set.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, this is where we went to the big crater and I came southeast in order to get around it, remember? We saw that hole?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Look at that big turn I made. Ha ha! That was a quick change of mind when we came over that ridge.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Yes, sir.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, we're still headed northwest, Bob. (Pause) [Jack's last five photos taken during the drive to Station 3 are AS17-138- 21138 to 21142 .]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1441554csm.text: How'd the photos go, going right across Arabia there, on this last - little bit of go, Ron?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, Bob, I guess one thing we don't have a handle on yet is - (and) I think we sampled them once in a Rover sample - what are the fragments out here (that are) mixed with the light mantle?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, I copy that.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I think I got one at our last gravimeter stop, a small one, and I guess there's one other Rover sample, but, at Station 3, we probably ought to make sure we get a representative suite of those fragments.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Roger. Agree to that.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Hey, Bob, how long have we been out?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Say there again, Gene? (Pause) How long have you been out?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: How long have we been out?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Three plus four five, (that is, three hours, forty-five minutes since depressurizing the cabin to below 3.5 psi).

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, Bat Charger, Off. And A looks about 37 volts. Relay Bus is going Closed.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Thank you. We're at 083/5.7. (Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, it certainly doesn't look like the geology of Norway, but it certainly is interesting. (Pause) [Jack had done his Ph.D. dissertation work in Norway for a year and a half. Several of the names he gave to features in the valley have Norwegian origins.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: That must be Lara right there, huh?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: On the left. You can see the blocks on the other side of her.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: That's right. I told them about those earlier. That's the only...I think, Gene, you want to bear a little bit...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Hold on...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: ...a little bit to the left. See those two craters, two bright craters, that are just this side of Lara?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: You're pointed right...almost right at them, now.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: No...well...I'm not...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, I can barely see them now through that high-gain.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: But I can see...I know where we're going now.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Those are the two I think they wanted us to be at, and I think that's a good choice - if we can get up there.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Ah. I want to get some 500s (of) the way that scarp flows up on top of...Well, it looks like it flows up on top of the North Massif. Now it may look like the North Massif may drape material down upon it. Look at that.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, (pause) not really. The texture is so different. It just doesn't look like as old a surface.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: But definitely different. (Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) Wish they had never said anything about pictures, because I've tended to not take enough (in order) to do better.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, but Jack, you're doing quite well in the picture department...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: (Giving a range and bearing) 085/5.8

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: ...You're not getting too far behind or ahead. Copy that (bearing and range), Gene.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: No, but I mean I'm not sure I'm getting the coverage I should.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay. We'll look at the frame counts when you get to Station 3.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Oop, oop! (Pause) Oh, there's another big crater with a pit in it. 144:21:31 Cernan: (Nonchalantly laying claim to a lunar speed record) What was it, 17-1/2 or 18 clicks we hit coming down the Scarp, Jack?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I don't...(Laughs) I'm in Min cooling now. (Pause) [Cernan - "I may have been exaggerating a little about 17-1/2 or 18 clicks, but I know we were going at least 14 or 15 clicks coming down there. We were really moving. (Smiling) But, then, what can I say? There it is, documented: 17-1/2 or 18 clicks."]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Oh, look at that. Wait until you get over here and look at that South Massif. [Unless Gene has mis-spoken, he has turned enough that he can look south toward the mountain.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, I really saw them that time. And where the swirls, they really show up, are about a crater diameter from Firsov - crater diameter to the west. And I talked about it on the tape. But, basically they're kind of concentric swirls in that area with light and dark. And the contrast between the light and dark is - is something tremendous. The dark is not a mare dark - tan, but it comes real close to it.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Is that...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, I don't know where we're going to get a good...(Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, let's see. You know, that big block up there might be worth going to.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: 087 at 5.9. I think that's the best station we've got right here.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Let's see what's over on your right. Let's see if we can get at that scarp over there. [Gene is driving in a northwesterly direction and "on your right" could be north along the Scarp.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I've sort of lost track (of the two bright craters)...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: We're about there (pointing at the map).

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: I think we expected you guys to be a little bit farther north...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: I think we want to be more to the left.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: ...We were guessing a heading (means "reading") of 080 for the bearing (to the LM) which really kind of says you were going a bit farther north than this. [Parker is confused. 080 was the bearing at the cancelled LRV stop. Houston estimates that Station 3 will be at 089/6.1. Gene is currently at 087/5.9, a short distance southeast of where they want to be.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, there's that fresh crater, there, Jack. [They are planning to stop near one or the other of two fresh, 15-to-20 meter craters in the area. One of them is in sight.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: (Realizing that what Parker has just said doesn't make sense) 080? [Cernan - "We were going north and, as we did, the bearings to the LM were going to get higher and higher. We would have had to have gone south to get to a bearing of 080."]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Roger. 080 is where we think...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: All of a sudden I've lost track.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Standby.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: There's nothing wrong with that except that...(Pause) I think we ought to go back to that big block.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Heading 080 is...Heading north is not going to...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Roger. I just realized that, Geno.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: I'm 087 now!

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, I realize that, Gene; my mistake. Somebody's got a wrong thing down here.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Gene, I think...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: That's the Hole-in-the-Wall (stop). My mistake.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I think we need to go back there a little bit.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, we're at 087/6.0. I think that's probably (garbled). Let me get up on the top, here.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, 17, that's a great stop. That was my mistake, I was reading the Hole-in-the-Wall coordinate.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: All right, Bob, we've got us some boulders over here that are in the light mantle.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay. When do I want to jump to f/11 going across those highlands, huh? At - on the western edge of Crisium?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, now, let me brief you on Station 3. It's going to be a very brief station to make up for the...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: We can see a little bit down into Lara, now, too.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, it will be a brief station to make up for the time we added on at the... [For the next few moments, we have a period of overlapping conversation. Gene, with Jack's help, is orienting the Rover so that it is level and the sun-shadow device reads zero. They will ignore Parker until they are finished. Some of the Rover dialog is lost under Parker.]

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: How'd we get up here, again?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: I just drove (garbled). (Pause) (Garbled) 045 (Garbled)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: ...First of all, remember we want to get the Nav update. Let me go into a heading of 270 more or less and give us the Nav readout so we can start that here.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: (To Jack) Can you get where you want to from here? No, this is no good. I wanted to get a high spot. (Pause) Yeah, let's...Let me park down here, Jack.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, you should have stayed up there.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, I want...(Pause) This is good right here. (Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: It's not going to be very level for the gravimeter.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Gene, remember, we want to head for the west so we can get the Nav update.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: (Garbled) you park right out here and we can work those blocks right up behind us.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: (To Parker) Okay, you want a Nav update here?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Roger. That's affirm.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: (To Gene) You need to get your (low-gain) antenna.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Why don't you get off, Jack? Oh, I was looking at the wrong dang (checklist page)...Oh, no, I'm not. Okay. I'll get a Nav update (as per CDR-15 ). (Pause) (To Jack) Get off and look around. I'll give them a Nav update, Jack, and we'll press on. (Pause) Yes, sir, you're right, Bob. (To Jack) Hey, get your (scoop)...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay. There is absolutely no color variation on these flow fronts or scarps, or - By golly, flow fronts, looks to me like. Just looking north, right from the Picard X.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I will. (Long Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Go ahead.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: What do you need? Take your scoop or whatever you need.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Oh, you're going to move?

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah. I want to give them a Nav update real quick.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: Oh, I'm sorry. (Pause) Okay. I've got the scoop (off the gate). [They are now about 3 hours 50 minutes into the EVA. As indicated on CDR-15 ( 29k ), they had planned to arrive at 3:19. A figure from an EVA-2 planning document by P.E. Reynolds of Bell Labs ( 50k ) shows the planned Return Distances and EVA Elapsed Times at various stages in the EVA. I have added the data for the actual EVA as dashed lines. The PLSS O2 and H2O walkback limits are shown as diagonal lines on the righthand side and, as they arrive at Station 3, they will have to leave again in no more than about 42 minutes because

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay. And, Jack, an update for you. We're going to want you to do some documented sampling on your own. I'll get with you guys on the rest of the station plan, shortly. Go ahead, Gene, we're ready.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: (To Gene) Okay, I ought to get the gnomon, I guess.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Okay, let me find a level spot; I'll come back towards you.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: I'll get it. (Pause)

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Well, there is no (level spot). Well, okay, if you got any...

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1441554csm.text: No, go ahead, make your park.

a17_1441554csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1441554csm.text: Yeah, I'm looking for a level spot, but my God, there sure aren't very many.

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: We can sample the rim materials of this crater. (Pause) Bob, I'm at, let's say, the east-southeast rim of a, oh, 30-meter crater - in the light mantle, of course - up on the Scarp and maybe 300...(correcting himself) 200 meters from the rim of Lara in a northeast direction.

A17A1442630.text: Okay, I copy that.

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: It probably shows up as a bright crater on your map. There's only about a half a centimeter of gray cover over very white material that forms the rim.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay. And, Gene, give me a call when you get parked and I'll give you an update on what we want to do.

A17A1442630.text: Okay. 087, 12.7, 6.0; 105 and 100. On the battery temps: 100, 120. The rear motors are off scale low and the forward motors are 0 and 240.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay. We copy that.

We'd like to get one pan and the gravimeter, and then we'll leave this station. We're going to absorb some of the time we spent with the extra gravimeter reading and some of the time we absorbed at Station 2 in the longer stay time in sampling at Station 3. That's our plan. So it will be CDR for the CSVC - or the

A17A1442630.speaker: Evans
A17A1442630.text: Yeah, do we go north of Macrobius Alpha?

A17A1442630.text: Bob, you got (pause) any preference up in this area where you want that long can?

A17A1442630.text: Negative. That's something that was sort of near the Scarp, but you're parked so near the Scarp and that's something, remember when we do it in solo, we only did it with the Rover, so you'd have to stay right there beside the Rover and do it. No expectations of doing it otherwise. [Schmitt - "Gene needed someplace to lay the long-can cap. When we did it together, I'd hold the cap."]

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: Well, that's what I figured.

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: Gene. I think you're in good shape.

A17A1442630.text: Yeah, I don't have any other choice.

A17A1442630.text: I'm right...

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: ...you're right on it because the projection of it would be uphill a little bit. [They are parked just east of the top of the Scarp. Fendell pans counter-clockwise.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: Yeah, I'll be right on the side of it. I'm parked on the side of it if it exists.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay, and, Jack, what's your frame count?

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: (Having difficulty reading the indicator) Well, (pause) 122.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1442630.text: Bob, I've dug a trench in the...

A17A1442630.text: What do you need, Gene? (Pause) (Realizing whatever it is that Gene needs) Oh, yeah. (To Bob) Bob, I dug a trench in the side of this crater. I've got down-Sun pictures of it. There's quite a marbling of light and dark soil or fine grain material. It looks as if there's a uniform, about 3-centimeter (thick) layer of light material over that marbled light and dark. On the very top surface, there's a half centimeter of light gray, and when I say "dark", I mean a "medium gray". [Fendell briefly catches Gene on his way to the gate. Jack's cross-Sun and down-Sun "before" pictures of the trench are

A17A1442630.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1442630.text: Roger. You're quite a bit north of the site. You are over Li - Littrow. In fact, you're north of Littrow.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay, copy that. Sounds like a great sample site.

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: Okay, I'm going to start sampling the soils, and then I'll get you the fragments. [Fendell finds Jack on the rim of a small, raised-rim crater northwest of the Rover.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay, I presume that we'll at least have the single upper core which we can use to sample that stuff in the soil. [Here, Bob is referring to the light-colored, subsurface material which, presumably, is similar to the material Gene discovered at Station 2 and at the Scarp gravimeter stop.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: And we...

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: Oh, there's no guarantee (that we can reach it). This is a crater rim.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay. And, Gene, are you still near the Rover?

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: Yeah, I am.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay, we'd like to get the SEP blankets opened, Gene, and dusted if they're dirty, so they can cool some more.

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: (Unhappily) Oh, boy!

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: (Sympathetically) Yup. [Fendell looks at Jack, scooping soil with his back to the Rover. The low-gain antenna is in the way.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: (Resigned to the dusting) Okay! Now I can't give you the gravimeter reading while I'm working on the Rover, so I'll have to time it when I get away from it.

A17A1442630.speaker: Parker
A17A1442630.text: Okay. Roger on that. I think you'll be pounding on the hammer for a long while while you can take the gravimeter reading. [Jack pours soil in a sample bag; he gets about a half cup.] Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1442630.speaker: Cernan
A17A1442630.text: Yeah. Well, we'll see. Let me get your brush back. (Pause) [Jack plants the scoop in the ground and closes the bag.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: Okay, bag 520 has a skim sample of the upper light-gray soil. Don't know where I'm going to put these things, I've got to come down and get a bag. [Jack goes to the Rover to get an SCB. There are sample bags hanging from his camera.]

A17A1442630.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1442630.text: Have you punched the gravim(eter)?...No. [The gravimeter will remain on the Rover for this measurement. If Gene had started the measurement, Jack couldn't have gotten an SCB off the Rover without ruining the measurement.]

A17A1442630.text: No, I can't punch it until I get out of here. (Long Pause) These (SEP) switches are in Off and Standby, right?

a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, that's where they are and the temperature is about 104 and...

a17_1443426csm.text: No, it was Standby.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, it doesn't matter whether it's Standby; it won't be (garbled) that temperature anyway, but put it Off.

a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. It might have gotten hit when I changed the blanket. (Pause) [Fendell is looking at a small crater north of the Rover.]

a17_1443426csm.text: Yeah, 17, the PLSSs look great.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, back to Intermediate. How's Ron doing?

a17_1443426csm.text: They're both looking...Stand by. (Pause) Ron's doing great, too. He's sitting here busily...

a17_1443426csm.text: No, no.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Go ahead.

a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. I found it.

a17_1443426csm.text: Copy that. (Pause)

a17_1443426csm.text: Bob, I forgot to give you the core numbers, but I will. [Gene takes a stereopair of the drive tube from the south. These are AS17-137- 20981 and 20982 .]

a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. (Pause) And don't forget to put your little note in the long can there. [Gene puts the camera on Jack's seat so that he can work more easily with the core and the long can.]

a17_1443426csm.text: Oh, I'll get the note in there. I'll get it in there. (Pause) Nobody will ever know! (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "There was no note. a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, Bob, 524 is what I think is a blue-gray rock, probably the breccia. It got a little dust covered.

a17_1443426csm.text: From just off the rim of this little crater. [Gene examines the end of the core and then brings it to the TV camera.]

a17_1443426csm.text: Roger. We see a long thing in your hand there, Gene. Now, the tip is in his right hand, pointing

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt

a17_1443426csm.text: (Might) just as well fix this bag now. Let me get this bag. It's going to come off at the bottom if I don't. It's going to come off again. I don't think the harness is tight enough now.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: Want to tighten the harness? [Fendell is examining layering on the East Massif.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Yeah. I got to, Jack.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Let me get your harness. I might just as well do it, so it's right. (A little exasperated) If it's worth doing at all, it's worth doing right. (Pause) [Cernan - "This is something that my father used to say, and I'm glad I said it on the Moon. 'If it's worth doing at all, it's worth doing right.' And then he'd add: 'Or you're just going to have to do it over again.' His name was Andy. Andrew George Cernan. And he also used to say 'I'll only ever ask of you to do your best.' Whether it was in studying, or playing football or playing the clarinet - which I tried to do but never did very well. 'Y

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Now, let me try getting that bag back on. No, don't bend over; I can't get down there.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: You're plenty short enough.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: Thanks. Thanks a lot. (Laughs)

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: This bag, that hook...There's something changing the geometry.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, don't worry about it too much, guys; I'm sure the bag will stay on without the hook.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: (Garbled under Bob) (Responding to Bob) Yeah, it will; (that's) the conclusion I just came to.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: You through?

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Yeah, go ahead. (Long Pause) [Fendell pans past Jack, who is going to his Rover seat. Fendell then looks north along the Scarp toward Hanover.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. I have the camera Off. Yes, it's dark down there. I'm not getting any more pictures. Okay.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, Bob, what I know is a blue-gray breccia is in bag 525.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1443426csm.text: Mapping Camera to Off. Wait 30 seconds, it says. Okay. We're rolling left.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, copy that. (Pause) And, Jack, (are) you just scooping up little rocks along the surface there...in your little xenolith mode? [A xenolith is a foreign rock; and Bob is suggesting that Jack collect as many different types of rocks as he can find.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Bob? 144:46:03 Parker: Go ahead, Gene. [Fendell finds Jack back at the near rim of the crater. An SCB is now on the ground beside him.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1443426csm.text: (Responding to Bob) Yeah, you read my mind. I do want to get one of these light-colored rocks, though.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Go ahead, Gene. [Jack goes to the north rim of the crater and gets a scoopful of soil.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Bob, when I broke the cores apart, there's just a lot of dry clods; and the bottom core's full, the top core about - oh, I got to look - it's dark down there, but about an inch (to an) inch and a half of the core has just zero-g'd or one-sixth-g'd itself right out. [That is, a small amount of dirt fell out of the core tube. Meanwhile, Jack's scoop has fallen to the ground. In order to free both hands for closing a sample bag, he leaned the scoop against his thigh, but it slipped off and fell.]

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay. Mapping Camera to Standby. Off, barber pole, gray. Laser Altimeter, Off. Okay. We've already in CMC Free, and we're rolling left.

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1443426csm.text: Okay, we copy that. I guess we still just cover it, and see what we got. Might just again trying compacting it after that's through...after you're done with the lower core. Video Clip ( 3 min 30 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

a17_1443426csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1443426csm.text: Yeah. I'll do that. (Long Pause) [Facing cross-slope, Jack bobs down onto his uphill (right) knee and grabs the scoop. He has no trouble getting back up. He then goes to the SCB to stow the sample.] [Schmitt - "Facing up a slope like that, it was easy to get down and back up."]

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: You don't mind a little dirt here and there, do you, gang? (Pause)

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: No. (Long Pause) [Jack leans back to get his PLSS over his heels and kicks upright. He makes it, but drops the SCB in the process. He goes to one knee to retrieve it but stumbles and falls on his chest. He gets up successfully and goes to the scoop.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Oh, dadgummit! (Pause) Well... [From later evidence, Gene is having trouble re-attaching the rake to the extension handle. Meanwhile, Jack's unused sample bags have fallen off his camera again.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Hey, Gene, would you go over and help Twinkletoes, please? [Jack drops the SCB on the ground.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: I tell you, you fix that camera bracket so the bags stay on and I'll be a lot better off. [Jack turns away from the TV camera while he examines his 70-mm camera to see how dirty it is.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Roger.

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Want some help, Jack? I'll be there.

A17A1445105.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1445105.text: No, we haven't caught any, anomalies in the film usage.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: No! I don't need any help.

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Okay.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: I just need better bags.

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Jack, you might worry about whether your camera lens is dirty or clean, Jack. I don't know what you'd do about it.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: I'm very worried about that.

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: I don't know what you'd do about it, but you might worry about it.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: I don't have a thing to do...(Pause) It's clean. (Pause)

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Well, I'll be a son of a gun!

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: What's your problem?

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: (Chuckles) I can't get this thing (the rake) locked on.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: What the...

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: The rake!

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: The rake!?

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Yeah. That should lock. And I turn that like that. There it comes. [Gene is attaching the rake to the extension handle; he had removed the rake head so that he could attach the extension handle to the drive tube. Jack is now facing south, still trying to clean his camera.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Jack, if you haven't started your pan, could we get an EMU check from you? [Schmitt - "This request for an EMU check was actually a code phrase which meant 'In our opinion, you need to slow down a bit; and, if you want to give us an EMU check, we'll take it.'"]

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: Well, it's about 50 percent. About 3.85.

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Okay, copy that. 144:53:05 Schmitt: And no flags. (Long Pause) [Jack starts a pan from the rim of Ballet Crater. When facing uphill he has to bend his knees and get on his toes to properly point the camera. When facing downhill, he only has to bend his knees. Figure 6-108 ( 47k ) from the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report is a planimetric map of Station 3 and shows the pan location.] Jack's Station 3 Pan ( frames AS17-138- 21150 to 21177 ) [Cernan - "There wasn't anything very exotic about taking pans. In training, we'd use real film and get it developed to see how we did. Basically, you wa

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: (Talking to the rake) Come on. Get back in there (into the stowage bracket on the gate). Okay, that's all put away. That (rammer) goes back on your back. [Gene needs to put the rammer on Jack's PLSS. He had used the rammer to push followers into the drive tubes to compact and constrain the soil.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: Why don't you go over towards Jack, Gene, and then the two of you can pick up the scoop and the bag together and get back towards the Rover after that?

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Yeah, I'm cleaning up his seat here. I'll do that. Video Clip ( 4 min 21 sec 1.1 Mb RealVideo or 43 Mb MPEG )

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: I think I can hack it. [That is, he thinks he can manage by himself.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: And then, at that point, we're ready for you guys to leave. [They are now about 4 hours 20 minutes into the EVA and have been at Station 3 for 29 minutes. As indicated on CDR-19 ( 29k ), they had planned to leave at 4:04. A figure from an EVA-2 planning document by P.E. Reynolds of Bell Labs ( 50k ) shows the planned Return Distances and EVA Elapsed Times at various stages in the EVA. I have added the data for the actual EVA as dashed lines. The PLSS O2 and H2O walkback limits are shown as diagonal lines on the righthand side and, at the present moment, they are only about 10 minutes from the

A17A1445105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1445105.text: Whew...Okay. (Pause) Jack, I've got the rammer I've got to put on you. I'll just leave it on your seat right now.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: Okay. [Jack finishes the pan.]

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: We're watching you, Jack.

A17A1445105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1445105.text: What's that?

A17A1445105.speaker: Parker
A17A1445105.text: I said we're watching you, but don't let that inhibit you.

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1445439csm.text: You know, I just noticed something that I didn't know before.

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445439csm.text: Bob, I don't let anything inhibit me. And I don't stay mad very long. [Schmitt - "I was acknowledging that I'd been mad at him."] [Jack gets the scoop by stepping on the head, thereby raising the handle.]

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445439csm.text: Well, there's an easy way to do everything.

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445439csm.text: The question is can you hang on to it once you've done it? (Pause) [Jack manages to grab the upright SCB without trouble this time and then tries to get the unused sample bags. Gene arrives with the tongs.]

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445439csm.text: Let me get those, Jack. Don't get down there. Let me get those.

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445439csm.text: (Facing away from Gene) Where are you? They don't stay on my camera anymore. [With his tongs, Gene easily gets the sample bags. Jack goes to the Rover.]

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445439csm.text: Well, we'll fix it. There's no reason why they shouldn't, according to this. (Garbled)...

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445439csm.text: (Garbled) the samples from that...Oh...I need it...I gotta go up there. Wait! (Calling loudly after Gene) Take an "after". Cross-Sun, from over to the north of the gnomon.

a17_1445439csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445439csm.text: Oh, I got it; I'll get it. If you'll mount this thing (the SCB Jack was using). [Gene goes to the Rover.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1445855csm.text: Ron, while you're sitting there watching this manuever to completion, I've got some read-up from the orbital science report for the CMP if you would like to hear it?

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: Turn around. [Fendell finds them at Jack's side of the Rover.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: We may have to think about a fix there.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: We might be able to fix that in the cockpit.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: Okay, are we all through, have you got...

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1445855csm.text: ...(we'll) worry about that when you get back in (the LM). (Pause) [Jack waves into the TV.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: Oh, I guess I need to get another film mag, huh?

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1445855csm.text: Okay, how about frame counts on both you guys before you start? [Jack goes to the gate.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1445855csm.text: We suggest magaline...(correcting himself) magazine Juliett, please.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: (Laughing and indulging in some word play) Okay, we'll get "magaline" Julieing. [This is Apollo magazine 133.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: Fire, fire, two frames. You know, I'd enjoy this if it weren't so much fun. [Jack advances the film two frames so that, when he removes the magazine, he won't lose any pictures.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1445855csm.text: Hey, beautiful. Man oh man. That sounds like all that stuff's working good. Outstanding. That's good - good to hear.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: Okay, you going to change your mag.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1445855csm.text: Okay, tank 2 Fans are going On.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: (I'll) shoot a 500 while you're doing that. (Jack laughs) No sense in me sucking my thumb.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: (Laughing) Any time you want to do something, though.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1445855csm.text: ...we'd like to press on as quickly as possible. [They will reach the walkback limit in about 4 minutes.] [Fendell finds them at Cernan's seat. Jack hands out the 500-mm camera.]

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1445855csm.text: Take a portion of the Scarp over there you can see.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: We are, Bob, but he's got to change his mag.

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1445855csm.text: I'm going to stand here and look around. Video Clip ( 2 min 52 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

a17_1445855csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1445855csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [Jack has a film magazine from under Gene's seat. He has taken the dark slide out of the new magazine and has put the dark slide on his seat. He then removes the old magazine and puts that on the seat.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 22 min 07 sec ) 145:01:05 Cernan: Okay, I'm picking up with (500 mm) mag - or (correcting himself) with frame 56 - and I'm going to try to get a little bit of where the Scarp overlaps the North Massif. I can't see much of it...(Pause) All I could get was three frames of that. Now I'm picking up the South Massif. (Long Pause) [Jack has finished loading the new film

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay, how are you coming, Jack?

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: Okay. Oh, I ought to put that (used mag) in there so you've got room for your (500 mm) camera.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: You got a final frame count there, Gene?

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: (To Gene) Okay, I'm all set. (Pause) [Jack goes around the back of the Rover to his seat.] 145:02:51 Cernan: Okay, Bob. When I finished the South Massif, I was on 94 and now I'm on 99. I took five more pictures back over to the northeast. [Gene's photographs of Wessex Cleft and the Sculptured Hills peak to the east are AS17-144- 22072 ) to 22077 .]

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: We copy that. (Pause) And we assume you guys are ready to go by now.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Yes, sir. And, Bob, they were all (taken) with the lens cap off.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Splendid. [Schmitt - "I think that during training, somebody took a bunch of pictures with the lens cap on, and it was always a big joke afterwards. On the 500-mm, you don't look through the lens to sight it. So you could leave the lens cap on and not know it. It was built that way because, with your head inside the helmet and the camera outside, the camera was a long way from your eye and a viewfinder would have been useless."] [At other stations when we get to see the 500-mm being used, a gunsight is visible on the lens barrel.] [Cernan - "With the 500 mm, unlike the 70 mm, if you moved it j

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Okay. And, Jack, what's the heading say?

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: (To Gene) Why don't you fix that high-gain so you can see?

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: We'll get the reading we need for the Nav update. Do you think you can give us the heading right now? [TV off.]

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: Okay, heading is four (pause) one (41)...I think. I'm at a little bit of an angle. Better let Gene do it for you.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Okay. We're waiting.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: I've got some parallax. I think it's four-one, though.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: What you looking at?

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: The heading.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: 043 is what I gave 'em earlier.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Yeah, we were wondering if it drifted while you were there, because we're going to give you, now, a...

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Bob, let me...

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: ...going to give you one to update it, if it has drifted at all.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay, it did drift, 041 is a good number.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Okay. Stand by. (Pause) Okay. That's fine. No torque necessary, Geno.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: I'm strapped.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: You liked the drift, huh?

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: Great.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay. Oh, Dadgummit!

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: What's wrong? Oh, the hammer (caught again under the console)?

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Yeah. Every time. Okay, let's go.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: All right, sport...

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: I'm going to head...

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: We didn't really do all the things we wanted to do, but I think we did everything we could.

A17A1450105.speaker: Parker
A17A1450105.text: We did everything we wanted to (garbled).

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay, let's get ready to roll.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: (Garbled) flight line stereo.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Okay, Bob...Oh!

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: (Looking at LMP/CDR-19 .) You got the TGE , (TV) camera...The low gain is 060.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: You get the gnomon in?

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: Didn't you get it? Wait a minute.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: You took the "after". It's not sitting out there.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: No, I thought I handed...Didn't you stick it in?

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: Yes, I stuck it in. I got it.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: Okay. We can look back. (Laughs; Pause; Static)

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: (Garbled), Bob. [Gene is probably reporting that they are rolling.]

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: I sure thought I handed it to you, Geno.

A17A1450105.speaker: Cernan
A17A1450105.text: You did, and I put it in.

A17A1450105.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1450105.text: Okay, that's good. (Pause) Okay! Whoo-boy, rest the old hands. (Pause)

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1450541csm.text: Hear it rattling. It must be pretty close to attitude. Yep.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1450541csm.text: Rog. You've got a 50 18 on the DSKY.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1450541csm.text: Okay, we've recommendations for Minimum (cooling) for you. Gene...(Correcting himself) Jack.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1450541csm.text: I think I am in Minimum.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1450541csm.text: Yeah, I'll go to Minimum. Yes, I will. (Pause)

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1450541csm.text: And give us a mark rolling, please.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1450541csm.text: Yeah, Bob, I gave you one. We've been rolling for about 30 seconds.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1450541csm.text: We're at 087 and 5.9 on the range.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1450541csm.text: Copy that. And the drive to Station 4 will be nominal and we'll get a Rover sample at about 094/5.1 but it will be the track as indicated on the map and the cuff checklist. (Pause) [The checklist calls for a drive of 0.6 kilometers on a heading of 069 from Station 3 to reach an LRV sample point at 089/5.1. After getting the sample, they will drive 1.5 kilometers on a heading of 052 to Shorty.]

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1450541csm.text: [Laughter.] I just said it doesn't shake, rattle, and roll as much as it did when - when the other guys were on there.

a17_1450541csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1450541csm.text: 145:10:07 - And Ron Evans in America are about 13½ minutes away from Loss of Signal on the twenty-ninth lunar revolution. Ron will be getting his evening meal within a few minutes, and in about an hour and a half will begin his rest period.

a17_1451007.text: And Ron Evans in America are about 13½ minutes away from Loss of Signal on the twenty-ninth lunar revolution. Ron will be getting his evening meal within a few minutes, and in about an hour and a half will begin his rest period.

a17_1451007.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451007.text: Okay. (I) ought to cut left up here a little bit.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1451209csm.text: Ron, we need Reacq and Narrow and the dials at 25 and 195 as is in the Flight Plan.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: Bob, I couldn't tell whether that was just...It looked like that might have been a crater that had got to bedrock. There may have been a high point, or let's say a thin point, in the light mantle, and it got down to bedrock. But I can't...It's the most blocky-rimmed crater we've seen for a long time.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Yeh. All these others are nowhere near that...Look at that.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: No. It was about 15 meters in diameter. (Long Pause) [This is stop LRV-5. When the bag was opened after the mission, the contents were subsequently split into Apollo samples 74110 through 74119. As indicated in - or can be inferred from - the Preliminary Science Report, samples 74110 - 74114 contain the soil that was in the bag while samples 74115 through 74119 are described as "friable clods", an indication that most of the "fragments" around the crater are regolith breccias - or "instant rock" - formed from soil compacted in the impact that dug the crater.] 145:12:51 Schmitt: Bob, there are

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Bob, (are) you still reading?

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: Roger. (Making a mis-identification) We're still reading you, Jack.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay. Are you reading us through the LM or through the low-gain?

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: As far as I can tell, we're reading you through the low-gain. It's been working just great tonight, Geno.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay, that's great...

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: (In a tone of mock outrage) Tonight? [Jack is noting that, while it may be nighttime in Houston, it's daytime at Taurus-Littrow.]

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: ...because I just scraped bottom on the LCRU. If it's still working, I'm glad to hear that. (Static)

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay, we're 093 and 5.2. We're almost there. Going to be right on the rim of that crater. (Pause)

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay. And, 17, the word from the Backroom is: with that last Rover sample you got, we'd like to go straight to Station 4. We won't get the one here at 094 and 5.3...(Correcting himself) 5.1, excuse me.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: Bob, I thought the purpose was to sample the light mantle?

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: We talked to them about that, but they...

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: We didn't sample light mantle at that last one.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: I agree. I talked to them about that. But they are so anxious to get to Station 4, I guess they don't want to do it.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: Well, how about it, Gene? A little real time (crew decision)... [Cernan - "It's hard to recall, but I've got to believe that we were forced into that decision because we had already stopped and had positioned ourselves to get that sample. And, when you're there, it makes sense to get it. And, heck, it didn't take 30 seconds."]

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: I think we got to, right here.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: I think we got to.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: 094, 5.1. You got your picture?

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: Yeah. [This may be AS17-133- 20218 .]

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: That's good enough.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: You happy?

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1451209csm.text: We'll get the sample (pause) anyway.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: That's good, Jack. (Pause) Sample is in 42 Yankee.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: And we are rolling! And give me a bearing and a range to (means "at") Station 4.

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1451209csm.text: Roger. It will be bearing of 100 and range of 4.6. [The checklist indicates a Shorty location of 101/4.1. The actual Shorty stop will be at 102/4.4. See, however, the discussion at 145:23:32.]

a17_1451209csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1451209csm.text: Okay. We're now at 094 and 5.0.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, Houston. Shorty is clearly a darker-rimmed crater. The inner wall is quite blocky but...Except for the western portion of it, which is less blocky than the others. The floor is hummocky, as we thought it was in the (Apollo 15) photographs. The central peak, if you will, or central mound, is very blocky and jagged. And the impression I have of the other mounds in the bottom is that they look like slump masses that may have come off the side. [TV on.] [Schmitt - "The tiredness is clearly gone from my voice. Getting there provided a new surge of adrenaline. Visually, this was a lot more exc

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay; copy that and...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: That's just what they look like. I'm not sure that...They have a bench appearance.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay, and the number 1 and 2 priorities at this station will be samples from the crater rim and the pan from the crater rim. Over. [Gene leans in front of the rearward-facing TV to dust the right-side battery covers. The tasks planned for Station 4 are listed on cuff checklist page LMP/CDR-21 . Because of the imminent discovery of orange soil on the rim of Shorty, this list of tasks will be abandoned.] [Cernan - "(Watching the video) This is very interesting. You can see a reflection in my visor of me dusting the battery covers."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, we've got a large boulder of very intensely fractured rock, right on the rim, right near the Rover. [Jack is moving toward the boulder.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It looks like a finely vesicular version of our clinopyroxene gabbro. It's obviously crystalline and has generally that same appearance. There is, in one spot here, some inclusions of a darker gray rock also intensely fractured. The fracture systems, I think, will show up well in the flightline stereo. [Gene has finished with the battery covers and moves to his side of the Rover.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Bob, do you have TV?

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Rog. We have TV, and you might brush the (TV) lens for us before you run away.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, I'll get it. I've got to get my battery covers cleaned. [ Fendell pans to Gene dusting the left-side battery covers.] 145:26:02 Schmitt: Okay, I'm going to take a pan while I'm waiting for you. [Jack is not going to try solo sampling this time.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: And we're going to want the SEP opened and dusted as well here. With the switches turned off. [Gene dusts his RCU . The brush looks like a 6-inch paint brush.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: O-kaay! O-kaay.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Oh, hey! (Very brief pause) [Jack has just seen the orange soil. He is cautious, having been fooled by sunlight reflected off the LCRU at the Scarp stop.] 145:26:25 Schmitt: Wait a minute...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: What? [Fendell starts panning slowly counter-clockwise.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Where are the reflections? I've been fooled once. There is orange soil!! [Schmitt - "The orange soil was several meters away from the Rover, up closer to the boulder. The orange spots of light that I saw reflected off the LCRU at the Scarp stop were tiny things; the Mylar covering the LCRU was crinkled, and you only got small spots every once in a while when the Sun angles were just right. When I spotted the orange soil, I probably hadn't even started the pan. What I probably saw was the scuff marks I'd made when I went over to the boulder. Actually you could see the orange through the regolit

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Well, don't move it until I see it. [Cernan - "Quite frankly, when Jack said he saw orange soil, I began to wonder if he hadn't been on the Moon too long. Until I saw it myself."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: (Very excited) It's all over!! Orange!!!

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Don't move it until I see it.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I stirred it up with my feet.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: (Excited, too) Hey, it is!! I can see it from here!

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It's orange!

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Wait a minute, let me put my visor up. It's still orange! [Cernan - "Like a pair of ordinary sunglasses, the visor attenuated the light but didn't really change the colors. If it was red, it was red; if it was blue, it was blue. But you could see the colors better with the visor up. I do that flying; I take my sunglasses off if I really want to see things clearly. So lifting up the visor was a natural thing for me to do."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Sure it is! Crazy!

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Orange!

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I've got to dig a trench, Houston. 145:27:00 Parker: Copy that. I guess we'd better work fast. [Gene passes in front of the panning TV, on his way to the SEP receiver. At some point during this exchange, Jack starts his Station 4 pan .] [With regard to the timing of the pan, what seems likely is that Jack went over to examine the boulder and then moved back part way toward the Rover to start his pan. Because he always started his pans with a down-Sun shot, he would have been facing the boulder and would have seen the disturbed orange soil before actually taking a picture. Having made his repor

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Hey, he's not going out of his wits. It really is.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Is it the same color as cheese? [This may be a serious question. Many American cheeses are orange.] [Schmitt - "You'll have to ask Bob, but I think he was thinking of green cheese, as in 'The Moon's made out of green cheese.' My guess is that he wasn't convinced that we weren't trying to pull their leg again. And for good reason, because every once in a while we'd do that, either inadvertently or advertently."] [Bob says that it was a serious question - but with a joke thrown in.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Temperature on the SEP's about 102. 145:27:15 Schmitt: It's almost the same color as the LMP decal on my camera.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay. Copy that. [A detail from Gene's Station 1 photo AS17-134- 20425 shows an orange "LMP" decal on the side of Jack's camera. See, also, AS17-134- 20426 . A similar 'CDR' decal can be seen on the top of John Young's camera, just behind the lens, in a detail from Apollo 16 training photo KSC-71PC-776 ; and an 'LMP' decal on Charlie's camera in a detail from Apollo 16 training photo KSC-71PC-777 . In a 2004 exchange of e-mail, Jack wrote that the orange color in the detail from KSC-71PC-776 "looks pretty close." Compare the color of the various 'LMP' and 'CDR' decals with the color of an f-st

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: (Looking toward the orange soil near the boulder) That is orange, Jack! (Pause) 145:27:34 Cernan: Boy, this brush is getting harder to get on and off, too. But I sure don't want to lose it. Man, I may start putting that under my seat. (Pause) [Frame AS17-133- 20248 in Jack's pan shows Gene replacing the dustbrush on the LCRU.] Video Clip ( 3 min 07 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Well, zap me with a little cold water. Okay, the SEP has been dusted. I think I gave you 102 or something like that (for the SEP receiver temperature). [Schmitt - "The dust is going to get into anything that's not hermetically sealed. After a while, moving parts don't move any more with dust in them. We had a bracket for the dusting brush, and that bracket was now full of dust and he couldn't get the brush handle in it. One lock on the gate was no longer usable; and I was having an awfully hard time getting my scoop on and off."] [Fendell finds Jack just west of the Rover finishing his pan. He

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Fantastic, sports fans. It's trench time! You can see this in your color television, I'll bet you. 145:28:25 Cernan: How can there be orange soil on the Moon?! (Pause) Jack, that is really orange. It's been oxidized. Tell Ron (Evans) to get the lunar sounder over here. [Schmitt - "I don't know what Gene had in mind, but I suspect that the sounder was just an instrument in the Command Module that he remembered that you could point at something. But the sounder wouldn't have had anything to see here, because of it's coarse resolution, if nothing else."] [The Apollo Lunar Sounder Experiment (ALSE

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Well, I'm going to clean their glasses so they know we're (not crazy)...(To Fendell) Can you wait a minute on that pan you're taking? [Gene moves the TV so that he can dust it.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I already took it.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: No, I mean the television camera. (To Fendell) I'll put you back where I had you. (Pause) Now, I'll put you right (back) where you finished your pan. [Gene re-positions the TV.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: You know (pause) that orange is along a line, Geno, along the rim crest.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: What? Circumferential?

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Yeah. Man, if there ever was a (chuckles)...I'm not going to say it. (And then does, anyway) But if there ever was something that looked like a fumarole alteration, this is it.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: (To Bob) Okay, let me give you a gravimeter. Mark it.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay, mark the gravimeter.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: And she is flashing. Oh, never mind, Bob. I'm going to go to Standby. I got to get my gnomon. (Pause) [In getting the gnomon, Gene will disturb the Rover and, therefore, the gravimeter. Therefore, he doesn't want to start the measurement until he has the gnomon. Fendell returns to Jack, who is digging his trench.] [Schmitt - "What we dug was half of a trench. That is, we'd only try to maintain one wall - the east-facing wall - and tear down the other one so that you could see in."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Hey, I think we hit one of those things we've got to reconsider on, Houston.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Yeah. The problem is we're looking at PLSS constraints right now, as luck would have it, of course. [At 145:37:01 Bob will tell Gene and Jack that they will have to leave no later than 145:57. They are currently about 4 hours 56 minutes into the EVA and the dash lines in the walkback diagram ( 50k ) indicate that they will have to leave at about 5 hours 24 minutes.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Mark it. Gravimeter.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Roger. Copy that. [After Fendell gets Jack in the TV field-of-view so they can watch him digging the trench, the TV starts tilting down.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: What's wrong with the TV? Aren't you watching this? (Pause) [In Houston, Ed Fendell tells Flight "It's gone (meaning 'tilted') down on me, and I can't tilt it (back up). Journal Contributor Bertrand Ouellet suggests that Bob said "dived", rather than "died". I"m not convinced I can hear the 'v' sound but, this context, either word describes the situation.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: It seems to have died slowly there. (Pause)
