A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Well, stand by. [Gene raises the TV, thereby disturbing the gravimeter.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Now, I'm going to give you another Standby and another Mark.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay. (Pause) Video Clip ( 3 min 10 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Standby. On. And Mark it.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that. [Fendell returns to Jack; the orange is faintly visible in a video tape copy made in 1989.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, Bob, I've trenched across the trend of the yellow...(correcting himself) or the orange. There is light gray material on either side. [Gene joins Jack and looks west into the trench.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Oh, man, that's incredible!

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, Gene, we're going to have to...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: That's incredible.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: You need to get a down-Sun color...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: That's incredible.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: ...as well as...I'll get my black-and-white.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I'll get it. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "I think there have been others, but this is a particularly good example of where Gene deferred to me in organizing how we would approach a geological problem, just as I would defer to him on the Rover stuff and things like that. It worked out pretty well; that had all been sorted out, almost without us knowing it, during the training cycle."] [Cernan - "You can't specifically train for every moment of the mission, so the key is that you train for knowledge of each other and you train for teamwork. And, when you come up with something new and different, you

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: We also got to get that rock up there. [This is the two-meter-high boulder a few feet west of the trench.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, we'll get that. Okay, let's start sampling that trench. We've got to get...That's...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: ...That's phenomenal. Look at where the contact between the gray and the...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Yes. Right, and it's on both sides (of the circumferential band)...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Before you disturb it, let me just get a couple of close-ups of that. [Gene does a deep knee bend to get the close-ups from a few feet southeast of the trench. These photos are AS17-137- 20987 to 20989 .] [Cernan - "You can see here how I could bend down without kneeling - without getting to a static position - to get some close-up pictures. In one-sixth gravity you can go down slow enough and you can waver in that almost-kneeling position - uncomfortable and hard to sustain - long enough to get a couple of pictures at a 125th of a second."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Hey, can you get a down-Sun? I think your color will be best down-Sun.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Okay.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Go to f/11. Get a little closer, Geno, if you think you're minimum. (Pause) There you go. (Pause) 145:32:20 Cernan: Let me get one more. [Gene goes a few feet east for the down-Sun, AS17-137- 20990 .]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Hey, you want any of this bagged in the can, Bob? Canned in the bag...or whatever it is?

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Stand by. They're debating that right now.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: (Garbled)

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Roger. Let's get the short can for some of that and...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, the color is...(Listens to Bob) Okay, let us get the... 145:32:42 Cernan: Better sample it first, then we'll get it. (Pause) [They move in to sample: Jack with the scoop, Gene opening a bag.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It's quite indurated. [Jack means that the soil is cohesive. He goes to his upslope (left) knee to scoop soil from the bottom of the trench; but he spills some of the soil getting up.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Aah...Go back and get that one. Go get a new chunk!

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I'll go get a new chunk. [Schmitt - "It came out in chunks. It was cohesive. It eventually fell apart as they worked with it in Houston, but it was cohesive enough that when we put it in the bags it was in chunks."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Give me that, and get a new one. Give me that. Get some more. [About a cup full of the orange soil has stayed in the scoop; Jack pours it into the bag.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I'm going to slow down here.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yep, just take it easy.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I can't see into this. [Jack is standing east of the trench, casting a shadow on it.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I can't see when your shadow is there.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Can you get around on the other side?

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yep.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Because I can't see to sample. (Pause) [Jack goes to the south end of the trench, Gene to the north. Jack goes to one knee to sample. He gets off balance with his right knee off the ground and, in the process of jumping to his feet, kicks surface material into the trench.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Oh. Well. [Jack does a deep knee bend and gets a sample this time.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, that's it. (Pause)

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: See if you can get a sample right across that contact too. [Jack pours the sample into the waiting bag.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I will. Okay, bag that one.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Bag 509 has got the orange material from, oh, about 2 to 3 inches down. [Gene closes the bag while Jack extends the trench southward to well past the edge of the orange band. Gene then puts the sample in Jack's SCB.] Video Clip ( 2 min 29 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that. (Long Pause) Okay, we're suggesting Intermediate (cooling) for you, Jack. [Jack is working hard. He gets another sample.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay, the light gray, which is on either side...We sampled the... [Jack pours.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Want me to get some more?

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, a little more. [Jack gets a sample by scooping sideways, knees bent.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: All of this is getting mixed a little bit with about a half-centimeter thick light-gray or medium-gray covering over the whole area. [Jack pours, and then presents his SCB for loading. He changes his cooling while he waits.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Bob, the gray material that's adjacent to the red material is in - what would I say - (bag) 510.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I had it, and I can't see it now.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: And the LMP is Intermediate.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: And that orange band is about a meter wide, I think.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: About a meter. [Schmitt - "Post-mission analysis showed that the orange soil turned out to be very small, spherical beads of glass, rich in titanium and low in silica and with the intensity of the orange color apparently related to the titanium/iron ratio."]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: You can't get to the bottom of it though, can you?

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I haven't been able to yet.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: [Moving to the north end of the trench] Just to be sure, why don't we sample this side of it, too.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Then I'm going to go get the can.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay...One...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: If I can remember where we put it. Bob, where did we put the small can? [Gene opens a bag; Jack pours.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It's in bag 7 under my seat.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Okay. (Commenting on the amount of soil Jack has poured in the sample bag) That's good. [The short can or Special Environmental Sample Container ( SESC ) is 13 cm tall and has a 6 cm inside diameter. Like the long can (CVSC) used to transport one of the Station 3 drive tubes and, like the rock boxes (SRCs), the short can has a knife edge/indium seal to protect the sample from terrestrial and spacecraft gases. In order to increase the chances of getting a good seal, both the knife edge and the indium are protected with Teflon covers which Gene will remove just before he closes and latches the l

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: 511 has the gray from the other side of the orange band.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: And the other side happens to be the crater side.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: That's right. North side. [Gene puts the sample in Jack's SCB.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Okay. Why don't you look around a minute, and I'll get that can. [Gene goes to the Rover.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay. I'm going to see if this goes on down here as a zone. (Pause) [Jack comes about halfway back to the Rover then drags the scoop north along a crater radial.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It looks like it's an ellipsoidal area if my footprints are any indication.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: 17, Houston. We'd like to get the double core here instead of the small can. Double core, please, instead of the small can.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Okay. Video Clip ( 3 min 56 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 39 Mb MPEG )

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Did you want it in the orange? [A chorus of voices in Houston says "Yes".] [Schmitt - "The reason I asked the question was not so much because I disagreed but, as I did several times during the EVAs, I wanted to make the Backroom think a little bit, just to make sure they thought through some of the options they had. Based on the information we had up to this point, it looked like something vertical in the rim of the crater; and, fortunately, we did what they suggested and didn't change because, otherwise, we might not have hit the underlying black soil."] [Twenty years after the fact, Gene qu

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Roger. That affirm. We can put cores in gray soil all the time. [Jack is removing the scoop from the extension handle so that he can attach it to the drive tubes.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Well, it's a vertical stratigraphy. Do you want to go sideways a little with it? (Pause) Or you just want to get it as deep as you can, huh? [What Jack means by "vertical stratigraphy" is that the orange soil deposit appears to have vertical contacts.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: I expect we want to get...Let's go as deep as we can in the orange, please, there, Jack. And the one problem at this station, Jack, is not that...

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: (Responding to Bob's "deep as we can") All right. [Jack goes to the Rover.] 145:37:01 Parker: ...we can decide priorities between this station or any other station. It's the fact that we're running up against the walkback constraints here in just a very few minutes, about two-zero (20) minutes.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay. [They are currently about 5 hours 03 minutes into the EVA and the dash lines in the walkback diagram ( 50k ) indicate that they will have to leave at about 5 hours 24 minutes.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Okay, Bob, and the bottom (core) will be 44, and the top will be 35. [Jack turns to look into Shorty; Fendell camera pans clockwise toward the crater.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that. (Pause) And after the core, we'd like for you to go over and sample some of the big rocks there on the rim, if you could very quickly. That'll be the next order of priority after that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: We will.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yes, sir. [Gene crosses the TV picture, carrying the core tubes.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: And I'm not sure whether your pan will look down into the crater or not, Jack. But if it didn't, we'd like to get another one from there. Hey, there's the crater (on the TV).

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: It (the 70-mm pan) did (include the crater).

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, look into it yourself and then, I'll also get you a stereo pan before we leave. I can do that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Roger. That's some crater!

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: (To Gene) Got your hammer?

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Yeah. I've practiced too long on taking stereo pans of craters, without getting one here.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I got mine from right down there, Gene. So...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: What is that right there?

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: What?

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: That right there.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: I don't see. Oh, it's a piece of glass, probably.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Boy, it sure is.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Hey, how about right up here, (just west of the trench, for the core)? (Pause) You know, we just about got [laughs] to the upper edge of this little ellipsoid zone. I think we're going to have to...We've messed up most of it. Let's try right over here.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I've got a little piece of glass in my pocket. [Once he gets back in the LM, Gene will describe his piece of glass in some detail at 149:12:10.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Bob, the upper portion of the core is going to be a little bit disturbed, because we've walked around the area so much.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: That was a little piece of black glass... RealVideo Clip (6 min 00 sec)

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: (To Gene) You may want to get uphill...

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: ...solid black glass.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Okay. That...Did you get a...Hold it, and I'll get a shot.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: Take your picture. [This photo, like the others Jack has taken since finishing his pan, is badly overexposed.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: That's about as far as I could shove it in (by hand).

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Okay. And, 17, while you're doing that, was the gray mantle over the top of this, or was this showing all the way through to the surface?

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: No, it was over the top. About a half a centimeter over the top.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: He's getting about 3 centimeters a whack.

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Very good.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I'll tell you, it's a lot harder going in than that double core was back there (at Station 3).

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: Yeah, it's pretty hard. (To Bob) It acts like it's inherently cohesive. It breaks up in angular fragments. MP3 Audio Clip ( 16 min 37 sec )

A17A1452348.speaker: Parker
A17A1452348.text: Copy that.

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: The central portion of the zone actually has a crimson hue, or a red hue. Outside of that it's orange. And outside of that, it's gray. Video Clip ( 3 min 15 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: (Breathing heavily) Wait a minute, Jack. [Fendell returns to the astronauts. Jack is facing west with his back to the camera; Gene is facing him. The core tube is out of sight between them.]

A17A1452348.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1452348.text: That's all right, take it easy. I'd offer to hit it, but I don't think I can, my hands are so tired.

A17A1452348.speaker: Cernan
A17A1452348.text: I'm going up to Max (cooling) here for just a minute or two.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: The central portion of the zone actually has a crimson hue, or a red hue. Outside of that it's orange. And outside of that, it's gray. Video Clip ( 3 min 15 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Breathing heavily) Wait a minute, Jack. [Fendell returns to the astronauts. Jack is facing west with his back to the camera; Gene is facing him. The core tube is out of sight between them.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: That's all right, take it easy. I'd offer to hit it, but I don't think I can, my hands are so tired.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'm going up to Max (cooling) here for just a minute or two.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, let me hit some more. Ready?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Yeah, go ahead. [Jack is holding the core tube while Gene hammers it, and Gene is very anxious about that. He stutters a couple of phrases before he gets the thought out.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Why don't you ...I'm afraid ...Jack, it's stable enough. Why don't you get out of the way? I'm afraid if I leave go of this thing, you'll get it in the head. [Jack moves out of the way to the south. Gene raises the hammer to level with the top of his helmet and swings down to hit the top of the extension handle at about waist height. He is hitting with the flat of the hammer to get a better chance of connecting.] [Cernan - "You had to hold the hammer tightly with your fingers. It was like gripping your golf club too tightly: all your muscles tighten up and your swing goes to hell and you get t

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay. Have at it. He's still getting a centimeter a whack, poor guy. Let's see. I didn't get a locator, I better get a locator. (Pause) Oh, it's in the (pan)...No, it isn't. (Pause) [Usually, a locator is a shot taken at the sample site of either the LM or the Rover.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: The only thing I question is our ability to get it out. (Pause) [Gene stops to rest. Jack takes a picture of the Rover as a locator. Gene then hits the core a half dozen times more and stops. Jack's visor is halfway up.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Breathing heavily) Man, that's really hit bottom.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Has it?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yeah. 145:41:19 Schmitt: Okay, do I have core tubes on me now? I mean caps?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yes.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Caps.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: And the rammer.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yes.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay...Only... [Gene hits the core seven times more.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: That's all the way down. But, I really...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: That's it. Thanks, Geno.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...I really wonder about getting it out.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Well, we'll give it the old college try.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yeah, we ought to be good at getting cores out by now.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: It'll come out.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Whew! Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: It wouldn't dare not come out. Wait a minute...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Is there enough to hold on to?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Whoops. Which side you got?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I was just getting this out for you. Let me. I can get this side better. [Gene stands south of the core, facing east, and grabs the tube in his left hand. Jack stands to the north, facing west, and grabs with his left hand.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: You ready?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Go. Okay, pull slowly. [The core comes out about a foot with apparent ease.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Slowly so I can cap it all right. Let me get a cap.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay. Hold it. Hold it. Let me get a cap. Turn. [Gene gets a core tube cap off of the left side of Jack's PLSS.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: All right, get the cap.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay. Now, wait a minute.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Are you ready?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, very slow. Even the (outside of the) core tube is red! [Jack finishes pulling the tube out of the ground.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Look at that!

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Even the core is red! The bottom one's black and orange, and the top one's gray and orange! [Jack raises the bottom of the tube for Gene to examine and cap. See, also, training photo 72-H-1229 .]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: The fact is, the bottom of the core is very black compared to anything we've seen.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Hey, we must have gone through the red soil because it's filled, but it's filled with a black material. [Schmitt - "Post mission analysis showed that the black soil was mostly beads of devitrified (crystallized) glass of the same composition as the orange, but with a different cooling history."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Let me see, Gene.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Dark gray, almost a very, very fine grained...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: That might be a magnetite...

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Fantastic. [Schmitt - "It turned out to be ilmenite."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Garbled)

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I got it.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Fantastic.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Go ahead.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Capping the bottom of the core) But it, it, it...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Let me...God, it is black isn't it?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yeah. I've got to get it so I can get the...Boy, it is black and is it contrasted to that orange stuff.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Very black. Well, not very black. It's a good dark gray.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Very dark bluish gray.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Yeah...contrast.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, turn that thing so I can push this cap a little bit. Just turn.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Which way?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Either way. Just turn the whole tube. [Schmitt - "I think Gene had gotten the cap partially threaded on and wanted me to finish the threading by turning the tube in my hand while he held the cap."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Oh, okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: It's just easier to turn the tube than my hand...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Laughs)

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...some more. I don't want this cap to come off. Okay. I'm going to Intermediate cooling. Okay. Now you don't have any caps, so let's take this back to the Rover. [This time, Gene doesn't have to use the double wave to reach his cooling control.] [Cernan - "You can see in the TV how much inertia I got into my arm to get it back there. I didn't move back slowly at all. I already had my hand chest high and I sort of raised my hand and then moved back very rapidly. You just couldn't go back slowly and sneak up on it. Other times, when my arm was down more, I'd have to do the double pump; but, her

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Where's the hole?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Why don't you take a picture of the hole, while you've got a camera there? Video Clip ( 1 min 58 sec 0.5 Mb RealVideo or 19 Mb MPEG )

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Be careful with that (core).

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yep. [Gene goes to the Rover.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: The caps are in SCB-7. They're under the LMP's seat.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Standing south of the core hole) Well, the hole's mostly in shadow.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Responding to Bob's confirmation about the caps) Yeah, I got them Bob.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: ...And, 17, for your thought...We have to be leaving here... Not "like". We have to be leaving here in fourteen minutes. On the move, because of walkback constraints. [They are currently about 5 hours 10 minutes into the EVA and the dash lines in the walkback diagram ( 50k ) indicate that they will have to leave at about 5 hours 24 minutes (145:57). The walkback constraint is based on the assumption that they would average 2.7 km/hr. They are 4.4 kilometers from the LM, so the walkback would take them 1 hour 38 minutes, getting them back at 7 hours 2 minutes with enough margins for an unhurrie

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: And we'd like to get a quick sample of the basalt up there on the rim, and Gene's stereo pan, and then press on. And I emphasize that it's walkback constraint we're up against in 14 minutes. 13 now. [Jack gets about halfway to the Rover when Bob gives the go-ahead to sample the boulder. He turns, gets the gnomon, and positions it at the east base of the boulder.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay, Bob, I'll sample it by hand. But it'll be documented. And I'll get it in a bag in a minute since I don't have any.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Come back this way when you do. I need that rammer again.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Oh, okay. Well, I better come there first, I guess.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Well, I don't need it right this second...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Why don't you leave the core there Gene, and you can take your stereo pan while Jack's getting that sample. And then you can get together and ram the core home. [Schmitt - "When we knew we only had a little bit of time, we got things done a lot better than when we did a station for no specific purpose, like Station 3. Station 3 was a disaster. We got a lot done, but it was a very poor use of time. This one was both productive and fun."] [Jack is standing southeast of the boulder taking photographs. These photos are also badly overexposed and the next usable photos he will take will be once he

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (At the Rover, disassembling the core) Okay. Bob, the bottom of the upper core is also dark. [Jack moves to take down-Sun pictures of the boulder.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that. (Pause) Sounds (like the orange layer is) a little thin. (Long Pause) [Jack leans on the boulder to examine it, then pulls off a hand-sized sample. He then moves southeast to take some "after" pictures.] [Schmitt - "The boulder had been intensely shocked. It was falling apart."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: And, like you might expect, the top of the bottom core is dark, too!

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: How about that. (Pause) [Jack picks up the gnomon and heads for the Rover.] Video Clip ( 2 min 47 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG ) RealVideo Clip (9 min 16 sec)

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Garbled; pause) If I ever saw a classic alteration halo around a volcanic crater, this is it. It's ellipsoidal; it appears to be zoned. There's one sample we didn't get. We didn't get the more yellowy stuff, we got the center portion...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Let me get those caps, Jack.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: What's holding...That's what's holding it, holding it from coming out. [Gene is trying to get a core cap out of the dispenser.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Let me) steal a (sample) bag.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay. (Pause) Here. [Gene hands Jack a sample bag. Jack's visor is up and we can see his face. He has probably had the visor up ever since he first found the orange soil.] [Schmitt - "Here, when I was bagging the sample, I was using the RCU and the top of my camera as a work bench that was immediately available."] [John Young did something similar while collecting samples prior to the start of the A16 EVA-1 traverse.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (To Gene) Okay, I got it. (To Houston) Okay, the basalt (from the large boulder) is in bag 512. 145:46:21 Parker: Copy that. (Long Pause) [The pockets on the side of Gene's SCB are clearly visible. Gene picks up something with his tongs.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: I'm getting in your bag (SCB) here, Gene.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Got it? (Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Jack, our lock is on the outside here, so we ought to watch this gate. [Gene is at the left rear of the Rover. Jack is gathering the gnomon legs in his fist prior to stowage.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: What happened?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Not going to worry about it. This (gate) lock is on the outside of that lever lock. You'll see what I mean when you look at the lock. (Pause) Okay, I'm going to go get my pan.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: The cores are not rammed yet. You want to ram them while you're here? [That is, compact the material in the core by ramming a "follower" on top of the soil so that it won't get shaken and mixed.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: What did you do with my extension handle? Oh, it's...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Here. And if you want to ram them (probably handing Jack the rammer)...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...here you are. They're not rammed. [Gene heads east; Fendell follows him.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: I'll get them.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, Bob, I'm going several meters around to the east and (slightly) towards the south to get this pan.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that. [Gene takes this pan from about 40 meters east of the Rover.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'm going upslope. I'm circum...I'm on the circum...Oh, you know, on the rim. And I'm up. Oh, that ought to be a beautiful shot, if I could see what my settings are.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay, the lower core is "chucky-jam" full. (A favorite expression of one of Schmitt's college professors, R. H. Jahns.) I don't think I've budged that thing. Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) [Fendell catches up with Gene at the southeast rim of the crater.] 145:48:21 Parker: Okay, and, Jack, I copied - aside from three trench samples - I copied one single bag of basalt samples. Is that correct? [The TV picture shakes as Jack works at the Rover.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: That's right. 512.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that. 145:48:37 Cernan: (Looking west) Hey, Bob, from where I am, (I can look at a place) about 100 meters around the west side of the rim of this crater (where) the mantle on the inside of the rim turns from this gray material we've been sampling, in here, to a very dark gray material. And there's a lot of orange stuff that goes down - radially down - into the pit of the crater. [Schmitt - "A first-rate observation."] [Cernan - (Tongue slightly in cheek) "I really do appreciate getting an A-plus on the quiz. I really wondered; it's taken a long time (nearly 19 years) to find out how I di

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Hey, Bob, those cores didn't feel like the follower went down at all.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Shouldn't it have gone a little bit?

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Not necessarily, if it's pretty compact stuff. You were having a hard time getting it in.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Well, I thought there was a little space up there, but maybe I just didn't feel it.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Not very much...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: I don't think there's much danger of them coming apart. [Gene finishes his Station 4 color pan . The frames are AS17-137- 20991 to 2102 7. Frames 21009-12 show Jack working at the Rover. Journal Contributor Yuri Krasilnikov has animated the sequence.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay. Great. 145:49:34 Cernan: I got to take a couple of more pictures at that contact slope over there. You can't see it from where you are, Jack, but I guess we got to leave. Otherwise it would be nice to sample that dark stuff up on top. [Gene moves about ten feet west. As he moves, he kicks flat sheets of dust a few inches off the ground. The sheets reflect sunlight into the TV camera, creating a short-lived patch of light.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: We need you guys rolling in 7 minutes.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: We can get a...Oh, I bet I'm out of film! Well, I got them all anyway, Bob. I'm at (frame) 162. I'm out of film. [Gene heads back toward the Rover.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Gesturing toward the west) That stuff (inside the crater rim) - and you're looking at me with the camera - that stuff is up toward that boulder. About as far away from that boulder on the other side as we are on this side. And we want a hack at that boulder, too. Jack, let's see if we can't get that boulder, anyway. (Pause) But I don't have any film.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Guys, we don't have that much time.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I know, Bob, I know. (Pause) There's a lot of little pieces - not a lot - but enough that I've seen five or six of them. Little pieces of obsidian-like glass. I got one in my pocket. Unbagged. Undocumented. (Pause) This boulder that you were looking at with the TV, I'm going to take a sample. Undocumented.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: I got it! I got it!

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Oh, you got it?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Yeah.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Yeah.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Let's go.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'm sorry, I didn't know you got that. (Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Bag 461 has another sample of basalt that I picked up right near where we dug the trench.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy 561 (sic). [Gene grabs the TV and turns it to point into the west portion of the crater.] Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, Bob, I'm going to give you something with the TV. I want to show you where that dark material starts.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: (Putting a sample in Gene's SCB) Hold still, now.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (To Bob) Okay. As you look at the inner rim - as it goes down (cough) to the right - you see a lot of boulders, a lot of rocks - that are protruding out. Where that rock pattern thins out, just beyond that is an orange - a visible orange - radial pattern, and then beyond that is a definite change in albedo where you get the gray material, and a definite change in the number of rocks on the slope.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Gene, Roger...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: And that particular...

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...material can...(Hearing Bob)

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: And if...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...and that particular material...(Hearing Bob again) That par...(Stopping a last time for Bob) Let me finish, Bob! That particular rim material there continues around to the due north, and then there's a drastic change again where you see the inner rim completely terraced with this boulder fill.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay, copy that, Gene...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: And I can't bet on it, but I can see it...

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: ...and you can talk about it when you get home.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay. As long as you're happy, I am.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Wait, Gene. Wait, wait, wait.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I got to get the film changed, Jack...

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: All right, Gene, change the film at the next...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: ...(garbled).

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: ...station. We can save time that way.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: All right.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: And we would like the SEP turned on before you leave...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (Garbled).

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: ...and we'd like EP number 1 taken, Jack, so you can deploy that at Victory. [This is another explosives package for the seismic experiment.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'll get your scoop for you. Have you been leaving it cocked like that?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Yes. [The scoop head can be rotated by squeezing a pair of flat plates on either side of the pivot. By pushing the plates, a locking mechanism releases. There are detents at angles to the handle of 0, 40, and 90 degrees. Here, Jack has been using the 40 degree detent.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Of course, we haven't been taking any SEP measurements, and I don't know what difference it makes. (Long Pause) [Fendell finds Earth, which is a bit more than half illuminated.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, everything is locked on. I guess I owe you a reading, Bob? [Gene's "I guess I owe you" was said so quickly that, despite numerous listenings, none of us could figure out what he said until, during a final review of the manuscript, I was finally listening to it in the right frame of mind. Bob's next statement makes it clear that he didn't understand what Gene said and thought he was talking about comm quality.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: We've been reading you loud and...

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: (The gravimeter reading is) 670, 012, 501; 670, 012, 501.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay, we copy that, Geno, and...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay, got the...

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Charge number 1 and we need the SEP, On...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: We got the gnomon, we got the rake...(Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: SEP on, Jack? I'll get charge number 1 for you.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay. I'll get the SEP on.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'll just hand it (the charge) to you (after Jack is seated).

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: And what's your frame count, Jack?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Charge number 1.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay, (SEP) power's On, recorder's On, the temperature is one-twelve (112).

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: I copy that. (Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Can you get it (the charge), Geno?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yep. (Pause) You get in (and) I'll hand it to you.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: And then I'm going to get the TV.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: And, Jack, what's your frame count, please?

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Wait, Bob, I can give you that on the Rover. [TV off]

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Okay. I thought you were on there.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, camera Mode switch is 1; (TV) camera's going Aft. Well, I guess that's the breaks of life. Low-gain I'll set when I get on. I'll give you (Jack) this (charge) when you're ready. First thing I got to do, Bob, is change film at the next station.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: That's affirm.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: And, Bob, LMP is at (frame count) seven-five

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Say again, there, Jack, I missed that.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Seven-five.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that. Thank you. (Pause)

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I must be getting fatter, you know it. [The seat belt feels snug.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Fatter?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Well...

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Depends on how you get in. (Garbled) your hammer.

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, we got a (warning) flag on the Rover. [The warning flag is a thin metal plate, hinged at the top of the control console and held down by a spring. It is painted with diagonal red stripes and is triggered by thermostats in the batteries, nominally at 125 F, and in the drive motors at 400F. The warning flag can be reset.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Your hammer's caught again. [Schmitt - "We could see part of each other's footpan, but not all of it because of the console."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: That's all right. We got a flag on the Rover, and I'm reading 136 on battery number 2. [On the first day, the battery temperatures had been higher than expected and, prior to the second EVA, engineers at the Marshall Spaceflight Center in Huntsville had re-examined the question of battery sensitivity to temperature and advised the Flight Director and the crew that temperatures below 140 degrees Fahrenheit (or 60 Celsius) wouldn't be a problem.] [Schmitt - "The temperatures were getting up there; but Marshall also had pretty good safety margins on those batteries. The fact that they were gettin

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Say again on that one, Gene. [Schmitt - "My first inclination in the MOCR would have been to turn around and say 'Did anybody get that?,' rather than call right up and distract the crew."]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: I'm reading 136 - make that 132 - on battery number 2, and we did get a flag.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Copy that. Ballet Crater Apollo 17 Journal Traverse to Station 5

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Okay, Jack, I'm going to make a very sharp right turn here, because I do not want to go down that hill (into the crater).

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: Okay. We're moving, Houston.

A17A1454008.speaker: Parker
A17A1454008.text: Roger. You're moving exactly 37 seconds early. [As indicated by the dash lines in the walkback diagram ( 50k ) they had to leave by about 5 hours 24 minutes, which is about 145:57. Now that they will drive nearly three kilometers toward the LM at a much higher average speed than the assume walkback speed of 2.7 km/hr, walkback will no longer be important constraint for this EVA.]

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Early!? I could have gotten that dark mantle on the other side of that crater. That's all it would have taken me.

A17A1454008.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1454008.text: So you saw a radial orange (soil distribution inside the crater wall), huh?

A17A1454008.speaker: Cernan
A17A1454008.text: Yeah, it was. Radial, Jack. You could see it very...It'll be in the pictures. Oh, man, I can't drive into that heading (because of sunlight reflection off the LCRU.) Let me get my... [Gene will drive 1.5 kilometers east from Shorty to get to Victory Crater, where they will make a very brief stop to deploy the seismic charge. However, because of the bright Sun, Gene will tend to tack, turning slightly north and then slightly south to avoid the worst of the glare. A capture from LROC Quick Map shows the location of Victory relative to other EVA-2 traverse sites.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay, Jack, I'm going to make a very sharp right turn here, because I do not want to go down that hill (into the crater).

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay. We're moving, Houston.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Roger. You're moving exactly 37 seconds early. [As indicated by the dash lines in the walkback diagram ( 50k ) they had to leave by about 5 hours 24 minutes, which is about 145:57. Now that they will drive nearly three kilometers toward the LM at a much higher average speed than the assume walkback speed of 2.7 km/hr, walkback will no longer be important constraint for this EVA.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Early!? I could have gotten that dark mantle on the other side of that crater. That's all it would have taken me.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: So you saw a radial orange (soil distribution inside the crater wall), huh?

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, it was. Radial, Jack. You could see it very...It'll be in the pictures. Oh, man, I can't drive into that heading (because of sunlight reflection off the LCRU.) Let me get my... [Gene will drive 1.5 kilometers east from Shorty to get to Victory Crater, where they will make a very brief stop to deploy the seismic charge. However, because of the bright Sun, Gene will tend to tack, turning slightly north and then slightly south to avoid the worst of the glare. A capture from LROC Quick Map shows the location of Victory relative to other EVA-2 traverse sites.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: That was on the inside of the crater?

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: On the inside rim of the crater.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, that's where the surface stuff keeps slumping off as it's exposed, probably. [Jack and Gene had both been so busy that they hadn't been able to listen carefully to each other's conversations with Bob. In Gene's case, he had completely missed the fact that Jack had already sampled the boulder; and, here, Jack wants to confirm the details of Gene's observation - which he may have only half heard - of the radial pattern of orange soil.] [Schmitt - "I can't say I remember this exactly, but I'm confident that, as we were driving away and I was finally taking a deep breath, I was beginning to

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Quite a station, men. We thought...

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: I'm going to get myself...Okay. I'm Min.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...Station 2 was a good station! (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay, I'm Min. Man, I'll tell you, that heading is going to put us right...Okay, Bob, give me a...Dang. Wait a minute.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: The heading you should be generally taking...

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Where we at?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...toward Victory is 090, Gene.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay, can you give me a bearing and range at Victory?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay. Stand by.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (To Gene) Did you get the TGE read?

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, I did. I got it read. They got everything (they wanted at) that station; but not everything I'd like to give them.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay, it's going to be...

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Houston...

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...105 and 3.1. [They will actually make their stop at 106/3.2. Houston has again revised it's estimate of the SEP transmitter location and, indeed, now knows where it is to high accuracy.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay. (Pause) Man, I tell you that LCRU is terrible when it flashes into you.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Well, you can always zigzag.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, that's what I've got to do. I've got to tack into that Sun. (Pause) [Cernan - "Driving up-Sun was mean. It was like what happens in flight when the Sun's directly overhead and you look down. You just lose your visibility because of the glare."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: I got it. 145:58:02 Cernan: Okay. We got to go to Victory. [Jack's photos taken during the traverse from Shorty to Victory ( 18 Mb ) are AS17-133- 20268 to 20280 . The first frame is overexposed but Jack set the camera properly before he taken 20269. ]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Houston, I didn't have time to really think at that station; but that could...I think, based on having seen the alter(ation)...If I hadn't seen that alteration and all I'd seen was the fractured block on the rim - which looked like the stuff (the blocks) in the bottom - I might have said it was just another impact (crater). But having all the color changes and everything, I think we might have to consider that it could be a volcanic vent. [Schmitt - "I started to talk too soon. I should have waited a few minutes; but I imagine the adrenaline was still flowing. I was trying to get to a point in

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Roger. It surely was different, anyway.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: I'm not sure how we prove it. We didn't have time to prove it.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: We noticed. (Pause) I guess that's the breaks of the game, sometime.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Hey, Bob, I forgot your numbers at Victory. How about giving them to me again?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay. 105, 3.1. And it'll be a heading of 090...

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay. Thank you.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...that's the general heading in that direction.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: I guess we always have Station 9 to look forward to, guys. That may be the same thing...We'll probably be out of time when we get to that one, too. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Nobody likes a pessimist. (Long Pause) [From the evidence of the overhead photography, there was a suggestion - as had been made for Shorty as well - that Van Serg Crater could be a volcanic feature. A visit to Van Serg (Station 9) is planned for EVA-3.] [Schmitt - "We were pretty quiet in here (for about forty-five seconds) and it seems to me that we were in a bit of a letdown after Shorty. We'd been on an emotional high and had been going so fast and needed to stop talking and take a deep emotional breath."] [Cernan - "Being on the Rover was one of the few places where you could relax. Physi

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Hey, Bob, a note on those (battery) radiators: I have been dusting the covers at every stop, whether that's any help or not.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay; we copy that. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay, sports fans. We're still about on the...Well, I think we moved...Yeah, we moved out into the Tortilla Flat area, I guess. (It's) not very flat.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: That's affirmative. (Pause) [In the overhead photographs, Tortilla Flats is a dark area between the main body of the light mantle to the west and a thin finger of light mantle to the east.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Those kind (of shallow craters) I can go through...If I can see them coming.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: 102, 3.8. And where's Victory?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Dead ahead. [Schmitt - "Victory is a 'V'-shaped depression that was probably made out of three craters. It commemorates Winston Churchill . Although it's a political symbol, I think we actually got that one by the nomenclature committee."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Boy, Victory is going to be subtle, I'll tell you. (Pause) Bob, how long we been out?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Stand by. 5 (hours) plus 26 (minutes); 5 plus 26.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Hey, Bob, I recommend that, if we ever do this again, let me get off and pick the charge off when we want to deploy it. It really adds to the fatigue of the hands.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: I tell you...

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Couldn't you just hook it onto your fingers?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: We copy that, Jack. And Charlie (Duke)'s got a big smile on his face here. (Pause) [At the House Rock stop on Apollo 16, at 167:32 of that mission, Duke hooked his sample bags onto his middle finger because the mounting bracket on his camera had failed.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (Dramatically) Mark my words. [Schmitt - "This sounds like something that somebody might have said repeatedly during training, but I don't remember anything about it."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: There's Victory over there, I'll bet. See that's the long edge.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, yeah. I can't see over there, but...

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: ...got too much Sun in my eyes.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: That's the right way to go. That'll be about it, too, (on range and bearing). (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Man, I don't think I've really seen the LM, except (garbled)...

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (Garbled) big rock in front of you.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: I got it.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay. (Pause) Well, you can't tell much about the countryside going into the Sun, can you? [Schmitt - "What I had hoped to do, as we crossed the edges of the light mantle on either side of Tortilla Flat, was to pick up anything at the contact that we might use to identify it. And, in retrospect, because we hadn't been able to see a sharp contact on the (down-Sun) drive to Station 2, with the Sun in my eyes there was just no way I was going to make any useful observations in here. So that's why there's not much information coming out of us at this point. Going down-Sun to Station 2, we had the

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Put your upper visor down. That'll give you a whole different perspective.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: It doesn't vise very well. It's stuck. (Pause) [Schmitt - "The upper visor was the middle (laterally) part of the visor assembly that had a sunshade on it. It was fitted in a slot and you could grab the sunshade and pull it down. Mine had gotten a lot of dust in it."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: That's got to be Victory over there, Jack.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yep. (Long Pause) [In 20272 , Victory can be seen just above the TV camera.] [Cernan - "In looking at some of the pictures that Jack took during the drive, you see things in one picture that you didn't see in the last. Everything was new. Every time you went over another hill, every time you went over a saddle, or went into another valley, you came into something that you didn't know was there or didn't expect to look like it actually looked. It was true exploration of a virgin territory; particularly with the mobility that the Rover gave."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: We're at 103, 3.4.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: That is Victory.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (To Bob) We're still seeing the pit-bottom glass...(Starting again) The glass-lined, pit-bottomed craters. How's that (for terminology)? (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Otherwise known as...

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: That's geology-ese if I ever heard it.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...the GLPBC.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Took you a while (to come up with the acronym), didn't it?

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: It's 11 o'clock (p.m. Central Standard Time) down here, guys.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: It's 11 o'clock up here, too, Bob. [Schmitt - "A coincidental thing at this point in the transcript is that Professor McKinstry - after whom Van Serg Crater (Station 9) is named - had done a paper on geologese in which he made fun of what geologists sometimes use as terminology."] ["These pit-bottom craters really were quite common. I think that the depth of the bench in a pit-bottom crater varied with size. So I suspect, then, that it has to do with a relationship between the impact energy and the confinement of the regolith with depth. The more energy you have, the deeper it can penetrate be

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: There's a square boulder. Look at that one!

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, it's square all right...or at least one side of it is.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: No, three sides of it are square. It just fractured that way. That's by accident, looking at it. So how do we get over here?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Go left, probably. And along the rim.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, that's where I'm going to go. Hold on.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: I'm holding. (Pause; brief static) Whew! (To Bob) If Charlie is smiling because my hands are tired, why did he let me get the charge off? (Assuming a slightly sarcastic tone) Fine backup crew we got. (Pause) [Training photo 72-H-1411 shows back-up LMP Charlie Duke deploying a charge from his Rover seat.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: You guys didn't really mean to say that, did you?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: 106, 3.2 (bearing and range to the SEP transmitter). We're approaching the rim of Victory. (Static; pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: And the LMP frame count is somewhere around seven...Well, eight-five, maybe. [Cernan - "Dust was getting to be a big problem. This was a long EVA and we'd done a lot of driving. I don't think dust was a problem reading the Rover console because that was pretty vertical, but I noticed at one of the earlier stations I dusted the top of my RCU so that I could read it better."] [Jack's photos taken during the approach to Victory are AS17-133- 20278 and 20279 .] [A capture from LROC Quick Map shows the location of Victory relative to other EVA-2 traverse sites. Although Jack described Victory as th

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: That's Victory; look at it go to the left and look at it go to the right. That's Victory; we're right on the ridge.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah. Yeah.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay; and we're picking...

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: ...on a Rover pan, you guys...Copy that (bearing/range readout).

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: 106, 3.2. [The checklist location is 107/2.8.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay, let's see.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Tell me where you want that thing (the seismic charge) and we'll get a pan around it.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay, I tell you what. You see right ahead of you?

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (It) looks like a place you could spin a profile on.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah, I could do it. Right up in here.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: And deploy the charge. Tell me where you're going.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: I'm going, right here; you could put it in that hole. No, you don't want to do that.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Oh, that's all right. [Schmitt - "I don't think the antenna (on the charge) had to see the Central Station. There was a ground wave that would let you communicate. I think we had asked the Principal Investigator if there were any reasons - like coupling of the explosion - why we should avoid holes and he had said it didn't make any difference."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Just pick a spot and take your photos.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay, I've got them. Now, go just beyond there. Little bit more. That's good.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay? Okay, Bob, we're at 106, 3.2.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Copy that. (Pause) [Jack's photo of the charge location is AS17-133- 20280 .]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay. Pull out (the charge antenna); pin 1 is pulled and safe. Pin (pause) 2 is pulled and safe. Pin...Boy, these are stiff this time around. (To himself) Push it in. Try again.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: That's a big black box. Don't pull it too hard. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Aah. Stand by on pin 3, gang.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Copying that. Remember to push it all the way back in, Jack, and start from scratch.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: I did; I did; I did. I remembered; I remembered.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Good, good, good. [Parker says that Jack had sometimes had trouble with the charges in training.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: But now I can't get to the...

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Your hands are tired. Let me try it once.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: No, it's not that. It's just...It's coming. Got it! Pin 3 is out and safe.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: And look at the orange flag. Zowie! [Each of the charges has an orange strip attached to the tip of the antenna for photo-identification.] [Schmitt - "The engineers were also afraid that we would come back along our track and run over one."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: That's what you guys were sampling at Station 4, I bet.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Huh? Yeah, it's about that orange, only not quite as bright. Same shade. Okay. Okay, let me turn my (Rover power) switch on. Hey, Bob... [Public Affairs reports that they are only 12 minutes behind the nominal (EVA) timeline]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Wait a minute, wait a minute. Let me get that (charge) out a little more (away from the Rover).

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Bob, there's no question but that we're at Victory.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Say again there, 17.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: It's the first crater that looked like I thought it would.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: Okay.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: (To Jack) Okay. You ready?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Let me change my (camera) setting here.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Go ahead 146:07:51 Cernan: Okay, let's get a nice Rover pan here. [Gene will turn the Rover in a tight circle while Jack takes the Rover pan . The frames are AS17-133- 20281 to 20300 . See, also, the images collected in a PDF document ( 22 Mb ).] [Frames 20291 and 20292 show their inbound Rover tracks.} Frames 20293 and 20294 show the west arm of Victory.] [Frames 20296 and 20297 show the east arm.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay, turn the other way first.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Gene turns clockwise while taking the pan and, here, Jack may be getting him into a good position for the start.]

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Take her slow.

A17A1455609.speaker: Parker
A17A1455609.text: And we'll get a Rover sample here before you guys leave, too, after the circular pan. (Static)

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: We will.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Slow enough?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah. (Pause) Look at the light mantle over there.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: You can sure see it now, can't you now?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [The frame showing the light mantle and the Scarp is AS17-133- 20289 .]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Getting your (camera) settings changed fast enough?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: I got it; yeah. (Pause) Okay. [Schmitt - "You had to change the f-stop. With the Sun directly behind you it was f/11. On either side of that it was f/8. And then f/5.6 back toward the Sun. The shutter speed was 1/250th of a second. When we had color film in one of the cameras - usually in Gene's camera - we were making the first use of a brand new Kodak Ektachrome film."] [Each of the film magazines has a decal on the top which shows recommended f-stop settings for aiming directions relative to the Sun. Jack's memory of the settings was correct. Smithsonian Institution photo by Jim Remar; cour

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay, let's get our Rover sample.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (To Bob) And the Rover sample will be from the same locality. (Pause) [Schmitt - "It had seemed to me for a long time that with the Rover we just weren't getting enough statistical coverage of the regolith across the area, and the Rover Sampler was a way to get more samples. I don't remember how many Rover samples we got, although it wasn't as many as I'd intended to get."]

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Boy, it's just a couple of meters from the charge, isn't it?

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: Yeah. I hope I didn't put too much soil in there for you (to be able to close the bag). Wait a minute.

A17A1455609.speaker: Cernan
A17A1455609.text: Okay.

A17A1455609.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1455609.text: (To Bob) Rover sampler works just as advertised.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1460925csm.text: America, Houston.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Not bad. [Jack believes that, at some point during training, he had requested a tool he could use to get samples from the Rover. "It was pretty much considered my baby.". Training photo 72-H-1227 shows Jack using the sampler from his Rover seat.]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Bag 43 Yankee. [This is a 384-gram soil sample, 75111 .]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Copy; 43 Yankee. And how about a frame count now, Jack.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: I will. Stand by. You're jumping the gun occasionally but not very often. [Schmitt - "Bob sometimes forgot to anticipate when the crew was busy."]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: (Having trouble reading the frame count indicator) One hundred and six.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Copy...

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: It's in the bag (SCB), Jack. Okay?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay. I guess we're ready to leave here, huh?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Well, if they don't want us to stop here, I guess we leave.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Roger. We're ready for you guys to leave there...

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: No, there's nothing else here now.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: ...and we're pressing on toward station 5.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay...Gene?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: (Looking at checklist page LMP/CDR-22 ) Okay, and I want to go about (on a heading of) 120. [They will drive about 1.9 kilometers on a heading of 120 to reach the southwest rim of Camelot.]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Gene.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Gene, can you swing out there and give me one look down north into Victory?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah, I can do that. I've got to go by that way anyway. (Pause) North.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Well, you know, just swing around and point north so I can look in there. [Because they can't twist the suits and have limited field-of-view, Jack is asking Gene to turn the Rover.] [Cernan - "Your helmet didn't move, so you had to turn your head. But the visor only let you look maybe 45 or 60 degrees to either side, so it was easier just to point the Rover."]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: I never got a good look at it.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Well, it's a series of three craters. There's some boulders on the talus slope of the easternmost...eastern slope of the west...eastern slope of the southernmost crater, the one we're closest to. (Pause)

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1460925csm.text: Stand by.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Now, how does that look to you?

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Well, it looks like...

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay, and there's the other...

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: I don't know what it looks like. The northwest end of the V has white...(correcting himself) light blocks on it - boulders - on the inner wall and right at the rim. And the northeast end of the V looks like it has somewhat darker rocks.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Part of that is shadow, but I think they are darker. And they look like about the same as down here near the tip of the V.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Got to be careful on that one, because there's one sloping away and one sloping towards us.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah, I know. I've qualified it.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay; we are rolling, by the way. And we're at 106 and...Well, we're still 3.1.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Yeah. Copy that. Thank you.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1460925csm.text: And the rim itself, though, of Victory is not blocky. There is some increase in fragment size, but that seems to be the result of some craters in the rim that have gotten below the debris that's covering it. I'd say that Victory's somewhat like Horatio in that it has blocky inner walls but essentially a normal block population on the rim.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay. And we've got a Rover sample going toward Station 5 (Camelot Crater) at about 103 and 2.5. (Pause) [This is a change from the location given on checklist page LMP/CDR-25 , a revision due to the fact that the LM is not at the planned landing spot. Evidently, the Backroom is interested in a particular geographic location for the sample.]

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1460925csm.text: Okay. 103 and 2.5.

a17_1460925csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1460925csm.text: Roger. And that'll be just a grid (sic) sample. [Schmitt - "I think Bob may have been mis-using a term here. And that may be reflected in my next comment. A 'grid' sample would have been a series of samples on a map grid. So I'm not sure what he meant."] MP3 Audio Clip ( 12 min 23 sec )

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: They're none of them just grid samples, Bob. (Pause; Jack laughs as Gene turns to avoid a crater)

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: You see, you can't tell how deep they are until you get up to them.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah.

A17A1461232.speaker: Evans
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Going to Block. TEI-49, SPS/G&N; 37568; plus 0.56, plus 0.96; and T IG 185:12:47.95. Delta V X : plus 2781.5, minus 1831.5, minus 0532.3; 80, 104, and 330; Rigel; 133, 200. Jet; 12 seconds. Lunar longitude at T IG is minus 178.34. Assume no plane change.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: That one I could have gone through. 146:12:46 Schmitt: Yeah. (Pause) Okay; Station 5 is Camelot. (Pause) Good old Camelot. [Long Pause; Jack hums at length from the Lerner and Lowe song 'Camelot': "Where once it never rained 'til after sundown," etc. Jack's traverse photos ( 23 Mb ) taken from now until the completion of an LRV sample at 146:17:04 are AS17-133- 20301 to 317 .]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Look at the size of that one. That's another one of those (GLPBCs)...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: There's another one on the right. Lookit.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Some of them have...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Well, that one doesn't have any fragments in the bottom of it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: No.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Looks like someone walked across it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. (Pause) I think that there's quite a variability in the thickness of the dark mantle in here. Did you...I didn't notice us crossing that one tongue of light mantle.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: No, I didn't either. We obviously did...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: I think we did. Right at Victory, but it didn't show up.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Looking into the Sun, you can't tell any difference anyway. (Pause)

A17A1461232.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1461232.text: While you're doing your presleep checklist, you may be interested that - at Shorty, the surface crew found some very, very orange soil, a great deal of it. Indicates strong oxidation and possibly indicates water and/or volcanics in the area. And they're really - Jack's kind of like a boy at Christmas time. I'll tell you, a little kid at Christmas time on that one.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: However, I tell you, I certainly get the impression there is a mantle. I would say that... 146:14:03 Cernan: Oh, I think so. [Jack's next six photos are AS17-133- 20307 to 20312 .]

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: I don't know what it is, but the dark mantle exists. (Pause) They're just...The craters...(Pause) These craters are just too big not to have thrown up blocks. And they're either subdued by the mantle or they haven't penetrated it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: And a lot of these blocks...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: And I think you probably have both. Excuse me, Gene.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: I'd say they've been subdued by the mantle. That really imposes an impression on me.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. There are those that appear that way; like Horatio, for example, or the big ones. But others, I think, are too young. They just don't penetrate. Particularly those that are big and have bright halos.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Well, yeah; but the only ones that look fresh and not (big) enough to penetrate are these little ones with the glass in then. 146:14:52 Schmitt: Well, there's been some big fresh ones. We'll look for one. [Jack's next five photos are AS17-133- 20313 to 20317 .] 146:14:57 Cernan: Now there's one with glass in it, probably.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. I think that's one...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: And without any blocks on it. That may not have penetrated.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. Yeah, that just has mostly the shock-indurated rock...instant rock. [The academically-favored term is "regolith breccia", soil fused into rock by an impact. "Instant rock" is better, though. AS17-133- 20316 may be a photo of this crater.] [Cernan - "We were having a little observational debate through here.
