Jack looked at things differently than I did because of his professional background but, on the other hand, I always thought my observations were as good as his. You describe what you see. Someone else might interpret what it is. I always felt I didn't have to tell them what it was; I

A17A1461232.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Ron, everything is - That's everything we've got from down here. Once you finish your presleep checklist, then you'll be clear to turn the comm off and - or turn the - the Down Voice, Off, and have a good night's sleep. And...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: We're coming up to 103 at 2.6 now, so we need a sample up here.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Okay.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay. 103, 2.5. Anywhere.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Roger. That's affirm.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay, let me slowly go to the right here.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Right out in that little inter-crater area, right out in there is good. If you let me guide you a little, I might get a rock fragment. Whoa, whoa, whoa.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: (Garbled)

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. That wasn't quite enough.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Pick a place. 146:15:42 Schmitt: Move ahead about...Yeah, right...Just...No, that's good. Straight ahead. Straight ahead. Good, good, good, good, good, good, whoa! (Pause) Now we'll give it a try.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Copy that.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: And that battery is still at about 132.

A17A1461232.speaker: Evans
A17A1461232.text: [Laughter.] Okay. Panel 9 is Receive, and we're in Duplex, and Squelch B is adjusted.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Copy that. We're allowed to go to 140, tonight.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: I don't expect we'll make it (past 140). I think we'll get done before that. Save that for tomorrow. I'll tell you those batteries deserve any temperature they want today, after going up that...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: That's the soil.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...that Scarp. (Pause) Okay. The soil is in 44 Yankee.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Copy; 44 Yankee. (Long Pause)

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: That block's too big. I can't get it. Too big!

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Get your picture? 146:16:51 Schmitt: No. (Pause) Okay, got mine. (Pause) [The sample documentation photos are AS17-133- 20316-7 . Gene doesn't have any film left in his camera and will change magazines once they get to Camelot.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay. What's the...Well, we'll find Camelot. 146:17:04 Schmitt: And 125's the LMP frame count. [Jack's traverse photos ( 13 Mb ) for the remainder of the drive to Station 5 are AS17-133- 20318 to 327.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Copy that. And just press on the same heading you've been carrying there, Gene, and that will get you to Camelot.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: We want the southwestern edge, huh? [ LMP/CDR-26 shows the planned Station 5 location based on Apollo 15 photographs.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Do you want to go where Station 5 is, Bob (that is, to the planned spot on the southwest rim)?

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: That's my understanding, Jack. So press on towards there unless I tell you otherwise.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Well, but you were talking about changing Station 5. I think Station 5 is a pretty good spot (as is).

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Roger. And I think that's where we want to go. I'm just trying to verify that. You can go in that direction, though. I'll get with you if it's not.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Okay. (Pause) It's probably the most concentrated boulder field on Camelot.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Okay. You know where it is, and we think it's about 092 and 1.6. [They will stop at 086/1.4.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: 092 and 1.6. You know this country...

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Roger. But you know where it is, so you'll find it when you get there.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...is rug(ged)...is undu(lating)...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: It's different. (Pause) Wonder where Horatio is?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Well, we're going to run into something in a minute if it's...It (Horatio)'s probably right over that rim on the right, Jack. Right off your right hand at 2 o'clock.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Right. I guess so. You know, it doesn't have boulders on it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: It should be over there. That should be it right over that rim. You know, I see why Al (Shepard) and Ed (Mitchell) had trouble walking up Cone Crater (on Apollo 14). You could stand right on the edge of the rim of a crater and not know it's there. 146:18:36 Schmitt: Yup. (Pause) [Jack's next five pictures are AS17-133- 20320 to 20324 , shows this part of the traverse.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: (Thinking back to Shorty) Man, that was spectacular. It's color on the Moon! Whooo!

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: It was really orange! (To Bob) Could you see that color on the television? (Pause)

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: No answer.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: I'll bet they couldn't.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: No, we couldn't see it, Gene. (Garbled) guys...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: (To Jack) Look at the Sculptured Hills. (Responding to Bob) Okay. I'm sure glad I went up to take that second pan (at Shorty) to see that stuff go radially down into the center of the crater at that contact.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah, that's good.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Hope that comes out.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Doesn't make any difference. It's there (whether the picture) comes out or not. Okay. Sculptured... [Schmitt - "That was the field geologist talking. When you're a field geologist and you say something's there and you put it on your map, you expect that people will trust you without a photograph. And Gene was thinking 'Nobody'll believe us unless there's a picture of it.'"] [Cernan - "A picture adds a lot to your description, particularly if you're in a hurry like we were at Shorty."]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Okay. Look at...Look at up...up the (Wessex) Cleft over there. You can see definite change in albedo now between the North Massif and the Sculptured Hills. Lookit, right up the valley. Well, you can't see it...Let me...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: (Laughing) You're right. [Jack's view may have been blocked by the high-gain; or Gene may have turned the Rover.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: You got to see this. See that?

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. But, again, that may be your photometric effects.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Yeah, one's an upslope and one's a downslope.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. Yeah. Just about right; but it's supposed to be darker in the cleft you know. (Pause) I guess I've been on...(To Bob) LMP's back to Minimum.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Roger. Thank you. (Pause)

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Whoa! Whoop, whoop, whoop!

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: I wish I had a movie picture of us driving.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: You're doing the driving.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Who's going to take it?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: That (movie) would be the classic of the century. (Responding to Bob ) Well, there must be somebody out there. (Pause)

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Bob, the fragment population - we're at 099/2.0 - is still about the one-percent category of...And it's hard to tell, going into the Sun, what kind of blocks you're dealing with. But my guess is - well, more than a guess - (is that) most of them look like they're slightly vesicular. And, in that regard, resemble the gabbros.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: There's a class of boulders that is flat topped and fairly-well rounded that is just about completely buried. Only the...Not more than (about) 5 centimeters of it projects above the surface. We've seen those off and on, both days. Remember, Geno?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Yeah.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: And they seem to be quite distinct. At least you notice them. Now, whether it's just a continuation of the mantling, I don't know. But most other boulders - the big ones - seem to project above the surface more than just that 5 or 10 centimeters. (Pause) [At 113:23:22 , about twenty minutes after the landing, Gene commented on partially-buried boulders he'd seen and tried to avoid during the final approach.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: I tell you, the Sculptured Hills just have that wrinkled old-face feeling.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. There are blocks over there though, aren't there?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: There's blocks, but I don't see any concentrated outcrops...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: No.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...or concentrated masses of blocks up on the slope anywhere...

A17A1461232.speaker: Evans
A17A1461232.text: Well, we'll get down here and clean the old suit circuit return valve.

A17A1461232.speaker: Mission Control
A17A1461232.text: 146:23:36 - We've said goodnight to Ron Evans.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Possibly...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...like you did on the Massif.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Possibly due... 146:22:26 Cernan: Oh. Do you think that's Camelot or not?

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: I think that might be Camelot. [Jack's next three pictures , AS17-133- 20325 to 20327 , shows the approach to Station 5. In frame 20325 , boulders on the rim are visible in the glare of the Sun.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Look at that!

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Nice shot.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Look at that. Right on the southeastern ...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Now, wait a minute.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...(Correcting himself) southwestern rim.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah, yeah.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: (Perhaps looking at LMP/CDR-22 ) Yeah, because Horatio's got to be on our right. Well, wait a minute, doggone it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: It's not Horatio, is it?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Well, we're at 094, 1.7.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Stand by. (Pause) [They are approaching the west rim of Camelot.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: No, I think that's Camelot. Horatio didn't...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: That's too...That's too...

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: ...have blocks that far up the rim.

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: ...Let me...Yeah, let me look in the bottom. I'll tell you. I remember.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: That kind of sounds like Camelot to us.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: (Garbled) these blocks (garbled)...

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. Yeah, that's it, Bob. We're coming right up at Station 5. Right at it.

A17A1461232.speaker: Parker
A17A1461232.text: Okay.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Only way to fly. (Pause) Okay. You going to park up on the rim so they can have a good (TV) panorama?

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Yes, sir. I'd like to get a little on the other side of those blocks, if I can.

A17A1461232.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1461232.text: Yeah, you better. Then they can look with the Sun on them (the rocks). [They will park just east of a group of meter-sized boulders. By parking east of the blocks, they will give Houston a view of them in full sunlight.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Yeah. Because, otherwise, they can't see that other rim over there. (Pause) [Gene also wants to give Houston a view of the blocks on the east wall of the crater.]

A17A1461232.speaker: Cernan
A17A1461232.text: Same heading. So, I'll be all right, there. Yeah. I'll get to the other side. Then they can look at these blocks and those across the way. I got to go around this block field, though. (Pause)

a17_1462336.text: We've said goodnight to Ron Evans.

a17_1462517csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1462517csm.text: Hey, Ron. Did you have some noise in the cockpit just now?

a17_1462517csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1462517csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Orange Soil Apollo 17 Journal Geology Station 5

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Not very level for the gravimeter. What's their (tilt) limit?

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: I don't know, but it's taken a couple better than this. (Pause) Now, I've got to change film. (Pause) Let me get things going here.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: I think I can get by this station without it. [That is, Jack thinks he can complete the station without having to change film magazines.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: How's our time, Bob?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: Stand by. We're talking about that now. Stand by. You've got 25 minutes at this station, guys. We've given you somewhat of an extension here. You're using up some of it back at the LM, but we've given you somewhat of an extension. You've got 25 minutes at this station. The primary priority will be subfloor documented samples, and then subfloor rake soil. (Pause) As you can imagine.

A17A1462525.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1462525.text: Rog. Understand.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Okay. [Schmitt - "Basically there wasn't going to be anything but the subfloor to sample here. Camelot is about a 600-meter-diameter crater, so it should have penetrated maybe 150 meters into the subfloor."] [The tasks planned for Station 5 are listed on LMP/CDR-27 .]

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: As you get off, we'd also like to open the SEP and again get that to cool. [TV on. Jack is at the gate.] Video Clip ( 3 min 50 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 38 Mb MPEG ) RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (15 min 36 sec)

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Okay. You wanted to turn it Off?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: That's affirm...

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Turn it off.

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: ...turn it Off, open, dust...

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: You want it off?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: ...the same thing we've been doing to it all aft(ernoon)...(correcting himself) all evening.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Well, it's midday here, Bob. (Pause)

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Leave it open and I'll dust it, Jack.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Okay. Oh, the (SEP) temperature; they'd like to know. [Jack goes to the SEP receiver behind his seat.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Temperature is still about 112. [Gene goes to the gate. Fendell starts panning counter-clockwise.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: Copy that.

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: You know, the thing I dread most? About close-out?

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: What's that?

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Is dusting you.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Yeah, I'm not going to be able to do much (about it) today, I don't think.

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Well, you know, we don't have nearly as much dust. Yesterday we were wallowing around in it. Today, we're...

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Who? Me! (Guffaws)

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: Okay, and, Gene, if you're not off the Rover, how about the rest of the Rover readouts? [Gene comes into view, going to Jack's seat.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Okay, Bob, I'm off, but I'll get them for you. I'm sorry. I look at them, and they all look good to me. And, you know, I keep forgetting to give them to you.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Bob, I have 135 frames. I think I can finish the station, don't you?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: Yes, probably. (Long Pause)

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: You know that SEP isn't getting much...Well, it's getting a little (dust) on it, but those mirrors don't clean off as nice as the LCRU mirrors. (Pause) [Fendell pans counter-clockwise past Jack, who is among the boulders west of the Rover.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Okay, Bob. This looks just like our old friend, the pyroxene gabbro, with the shiny ilmenite platelets in the vugs and partially recrystallized vesicles. The textural variations are planar, and they're primarily - or, subplanar - in the concentrations of vesicles. (Pause) [Fendell pans clockwise to Jack; Gene crosses the field-of-view, carrying the brush to do the left battery covers. Fendell finds Jack making his way through a field of boulders up to 6 feet in size.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Jack, I'm going to put this brush under my seat. It's just getting too hard to get off that place up there (on the LCRU bracket).

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Okay.

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Bob, what magazine?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: Magazine Delta, (Apollo magazine 145).

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Watch yourself through here, Geno. [There are a great many rocks underfoot.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Yeah. (To Bob) Delta, huh?

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: That's affirm.

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Okay, Delta. (Searching through the film supply under his seat) Bravo. There's Delta.

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: Boy, this is certainly a uni(form) subfloor, (just) as we mapped it (pre-mission). It's certainly a uniform rock type. I'll tell you. [Jack goes to the big boulder.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: The only variations are those gray zones which just seem to be either finer or (have an) absence of vesicles. Boy, I'm nose to nose with a piece of it right now. (Pause) Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG ) Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (1 min 16 sec; 0.9 Mb)

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan
A17A1462525.text: Say, Bob, where can I get a new set of bags? [Journal Contributor Bill Clancey notes with interest that Gene chose to ask Parker where to find unused bags, rather than interrupt Jack's work. Below, I have interwoven the conversation between the Flight Director and the EVA Controller with the ones between Bob and Gene and between Gene and Jack. Note that Jack, Bob, and the EVA Controller all know that there are bags under Jack's seat. Note, also, that the only voice that Gene and Jack hear from Houston is Bob's.] [ Flight Director : EVA, Flight.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Parker
A17A1462525.text: (To Gene) Okay, you want new bags...They'll be under Jack's seat. [ EVA : Go, Flight.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1462525.text: (Having heard Gene, which he doesn't always do when Gene is talking to Parker) Under my seat, there's some, Geno. [ Flight Director : (To EVA) He's looking for some kind of bags. (Having heard Bob and/or Jack and now asking for confirmation) Are they under the LMP's seat?] [Jack turns to look toward the Rover.]

A17A1462525.speaker: Cernan

A17A1463050.speaker: Parker
A17A1463050.text: Roger. And the present time, we drop the rake soil, we'd just like to get the kilogram of soil somewhere between the boulders - (in) as open (a location) as you can.

A17A1463050.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1463050.text: (Is) my scoop in that (picture)? 146:46:53 Cernan: It will be. (Garbled) Okay, it is now. [This is AS17-145- 22158 .]

A17A1463050.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1463050.text: (Responding to Bob) Oh, you want a kilogram?

A17A1463050.speaker: Parker
A17A1463050.text: Roger.

A17A1463050.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1463050.text: From between the boulders?

A17A1463050.speaker: Parker
A17A1463050.text: Roger. That'll replace the rake soil sample we were going to get. And we'd like you moving in 3 minutes.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Another scoopful.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Yeah. (To Bob) I'm sampling down to about 5 centimeters.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Copy. (Pause) [Jack gets a second scoopful.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Get your hand down, please. I'm coming down to you.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Oh, okay. (Pause) [Gene has been holding the bag too high for easy pouring.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: That's full. That's 467.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Pinch her down tight or that will leak out. (Pause) [Gene closes the sample bag and puts it in Jack's SCB.] 146:48:27 Cernan: Now let me get your big bag (SCB) tight. [Gene takes a moment to either secure the lid on Jack's SCB or to adjust the attachment to the tool carrier.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Okay, let me try to get a...(Pause) You got a shot of where my scoop was, didn't you? 146:48:39 Cernan: Yeah. Let me get an "after" of it, though. [Gene moves northeast to take the "after" but decides to do a pan, instead.] 146:48:44 Schmitt: Okay, Houston, we sampled about 3 meters southwest of the gnomon that was set up for the top-of-boulder soil sample. So it's a match pair, really, in that regard. [Gene turns to the east to start his panorama. These photos are AS17-145- 22159 to 22183 . This is a superb pan . The version presented here was assembled by David Harland and includes all of th

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: (To Gene) Don't forget your gnomon.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: I'm not. (Pause) Now I need to get a pan... 146:49:06 Schmitt: Are you getting a pan? 146:49:08 Cernan: I've already started it. 146:49:09 Schmitt: Okay, I'll go over near the Rover and get one. (Long Pause) [Jack runs around the south edge of the boulder field, out onto open, flat, ground. He is moving very easily. Fendell pans to Gene who is still doing his pan.] Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay, I got the gnomon. (Pause) When do you want us to leave, Bob? (No answer; pause) [Gene starts toward the Rover, coming directly east and picking his way between the boulders. Jack has started his B&W pan and catches Gene making his way back to the Rover in AS17-133- 20341 . In a detail , he is visible above the seat backs. See, also, a two-frame pan made from 20341 and 42. The photos in Jack's pan are AS17-133- 20339 to 20361 .]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Jack, do you read me?

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Yeah. (Pause) Hello, Houston. [Gene turns south to get out in the open.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Hello, 17. Loud and clear. We'd like you to leave immediately, if not sooner. (Pause) [Gene switches from a running gait to a skipping gait.] [Schmitt - "Gene doesn't seem to have picked up the rolling gait that you need to have in order to use a stride rather than a hop. And that may just be because he never did any cross-country skiing. It's a fairly natural motion, I think, for a cross-country skier."] [Cernan - "Each individual adapts in a different way, but the results are basically the same. Some guys skip; some guys hop. And you pick a way of getting around that gives you the greatest c

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: (Singing) Hippity-hoppity, hippity-hoppity, hippity-hopping over hill and dale. [Cernan - "I don't know where I got the song from, but it's got to be a thousand years old. Some cowboy singer or something. This was fun! My feet just got far enough apart for stability when I hit the ground and then I could spring up with both of them. I was doing a little bit of the cross-country stride in the beginning, but I wasn't doing it with strides as big as Jack's, going way left and way right like he did. You were less balanced like that than when you were skipping, so I switched."] [Gene now switches t

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: (Singing) Hippity-hopping along. (Pause) [In 1996, Andrew Chaikin discovered that the song Gene is singing is "Mule Train". He stumbled upon a copy of the words and music, albeit without information on the authors or publication date. The lyrics Chaikin found are: Mule Train. Mule Train. Clippity cloppin' over hill and plain. Seems as how they never stop. Clippity clop, Clippity clop, Clippity, clippity, clippity, clippity, clippity cloppin' a long. Journal Contributor Brian Lawrence provides a history of the song. "It was written by veteran composers Hy Heath, Johnny Lange, and Fred Glickman,

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay. My golly, this time goes fast!

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: That's affirm. [Schmitt - "It would have been nice to have had more time at Camelot, just like everywhere else. We hadn't seen much variety in the boulders we looked at and it would have been nice to go as far down the rim inside of Camelot as it was prudent to walk and then work our way - both sampling and observing - all the way to the edge of the boulder field and really see if there is any mineralogical or compositional variation. One of the hopes for the long-term future might be that these mare have stratified mineral deposits in them like the Bushveldt in South Africa and other places.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Okay, and when you leave here...

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Where did it (the time) go?

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: ...17, remember that we want to pick up...

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: I'm giving you (gravimeter) readings.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: ...EP number 8. (Responding to Gene) Roger. We're ready.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: (To Gene) Go.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: 06...(Correcting himself) 670, 031, and 401. 670, 031, and, 401.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Copy that. And when we leave we want to take EP number 8 with us, guys. We'd like the SEP turned back on and the blankets closed. (Pause) Okay, Jack, I guess that's your option, you may...

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Let me fix your...

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: ...stop and take the charge off when you get to the distance or, if it's only a short one, you might like carrying it in your lap.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Jack, I can hold it in my left arm on the seat.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: No, I'll get it! I'll get it!

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay, you want the SEP on?

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: That's affirm.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay, both DSEA (Data Storage and Electronics Assembly) and the other switch. You want the blankets open?

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: No, closed. 146:52:14 Cernan: Closed. Well, closed is...What happened to the Velcro on that other side? (Pause) I thought they mounted that thing so that...

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: It came off, Gene. It stuck to the Velcro. [When the adhesive holding patches of Velcro pile to the SEP Receiver bag failed, the patches remained mated with the hook patches on the covers.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: That thing that, (garbled). Okay, you (Houston) got the TG(E reading). We'll get EP-8. The (TV) camera's going (off).

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: We made a mistake earlier and it's too late to rectify it in carrying these charges. [Schmitt - "It was a mistake when I carried the charges for long distances, primarily the charge I'd carried on the traverse to Station 1 and the one I'd carried from Shorty to Victory. And, what couldn't be rectified was that my hands were already tired."]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Oh, I don't know...

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Negative, Jack...

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: We did. I wouldn't want... [TV off.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: If you don't have it off, we could stop and get off and get it, if you want to? But this is a short distance. You might want to carry this one.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: That's right, that's right. I say the mistake was made earlier. There's no problem now. [Cernan - "Jack was a little testy here. He was probably a little tired. And your hands do get tired from holding the camera and holding the bags."]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: (Reading LMP/CDR-29 ) Okay, traverse to LM, low-gain 100. [Gene will be driving on an average heading of about 090 to get back to the LM, and will use a low-gain antenna pointing of 100 on the indicator. LMP/CDR-28 is a map of this part of the traverse]

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Did you turn this (SEP receiver) on?

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: It's all on, all squared away.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Push that thing (probably the SEP cover) down and it'll stay. (Garbled). Well, sometimes it will. Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: And how about a frame callout before you get back on, guys.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Got it.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Yeah, I need some new...(Responding to Bob) Do you want me to get it (a new magazine) here? (Pause)

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: CDR's at fifty.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Copy that.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: A hundred and seventy.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Copy one seven zero.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: LMP's 170.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: And, Jack, it'd be my opinion, since you're just going back over the same path, that you came up this morning, it's probably not necessary.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Okay, I'll use it until it runs out.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: I've got a lot of film anyway.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: (To Gene) But when you leave me at...Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Parker
A17A1464749.text: Yeah, we'll let Gene take some of the photos near the bomb, or near the charge, perhaps. (Pause)

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Just jump up again and get your bottom... Yeah, there you go. You got to come this way quite a bit.

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Yeah. (Garbled) slope. [Gene never did give a complete set of Rover readouts; but he parked the Rover with some noticeable pitch and roll. See his remark about Rover tilt at 146:25:25.] [Schmitt - "It must have been tilted towards me - it usually was - and that made it tougher to get on."]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Your seat's rising with you, for some reason. There it is, I guess. You're all right. (Pause) Up closer to you. (Pause) [Jack is getting his seat belt on.]

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Okay.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay?

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Let's go. (Long Pause) [Cernan - (Tongue in cheek) "I always parked the Rover sloping towards Jack. It didn't make it tougher; it made it easier. It was lower to him and he didn't have to jump as high to get in. All he had to do was lean uphill. That was a Commander's prerogative. I particularly liked to drive on slopes with him on the downhill side."]

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Okay, the switch is coming On. (Pause) Okay. (Reading CDR-29 ) Traverse to LM: 12 minutes, 085/1.4. That's...Man, that (Rover indicator) says 086/1.4 to the LM, and my checklist (says) 085/1.4. We must have landed where they wanted us to! [The checklist location of Station 5 is 088/1.2. They parked very close to the planned spot and the 086/1.4 reading is the actual location relative to the SEP transmitter. Gene is looking at checklist page CDR-29 , which indicates a planned drive of 1.4 kilometers to the LM - including some extra distance to get around the southern rim of Camelot - on an init

A17A1464749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1464749.text: Just about.

A17A1464749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1464749.text: Hey, Bob?

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: And give us a mark when you're going.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Oh, I'm sorry...

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Bob...

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: And we don't have...

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: We've been going about a minute. [Gene probably started to move at 146:55:39.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Okay, copy that. And we don't have battery temperatures there, if you could quickly give them to us.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Okay, I never did give you that. It's 110 and 136.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Copy that, good enough. Thank you. (Pause)

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Never did get that for you.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: That's okay.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: But I tell you, the inner wall of Camelot to the east is certainly blocky. [They are driving along the south rim of Camelot looking at the east, inner wall of the crater. Jack's photos of the east rim and associated ejecta are AS17-133- 20363 and 20364 .]

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Well, there were a few blocks where you guys were, too.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: (Garbled) mantle, too, Jack.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, well, I don't know, you could see the other wall, too. It's...

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Hey, here's some Rover tracks!

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: (Melodramatically) Hey, somebody's been here before.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Okay, and, 17, what we're looking for is deploying charge number eight at (bearing) zero eight two and zero decimal four on the range.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Okay.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Okay, we're at 083 and 1.1. We're just about abeam the eastern rim of Camelot. And there is Challenger!

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Hey, hello, Challenger. You can even see the ALSEP.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: I think I'll go this way. (Jack laughs as Gene avoids a crater; Pause.)

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Gee, it seems like a short day. (Laughs)

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Well, I'll tell you, the time went fast.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: (To Bob) Okay, you've heard about this country (on the outbound trip to Station 2). (Pause) Hey, looking over there, though, there's no...We're about, oh, 50 meters from boulders in Camelot. And their appearance from this distance is the same as what we sampled at (Station) 5. I think we've pretty well identified the subfloor, Bob.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Okay, sounds like we have and sounds like from the very deepest - even from the bottom of Camelot - it looks like it's about the same.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: It sure does. (Brief static) I can't say I understand it. But that's the way it appears right now.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: You can't say what, Jack? (Pause) Okay, understand that.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: I can't say that I understand.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Copy.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Whatever filled this valley, it certainly was different than the Massifs. I think we've proved that. And, it presumably. At least everything I see indicates that it was an igneous extrusion of some kind. Either that, or the whole valley's been tilted and we're looking at some strange cross section - planar, more or less, relative to the other mountains - of a crystalline body that was formed at depth. But I don't think that's likely.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Man; we've covered 19.3 kilometers, Jack.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Is that what we planned to cover?

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: That's outstanding.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: (To Jack) I don't know. What did we plan to cover, Bob?

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Stand by. But we've been everywhere we've planned to go, so, we must have gone just about as far as we've planned to go.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, but it's a straight line. I don't know what the wander factor was, but I'm sure it was pretty high.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: 17.6, they're telling me. So we went a little bit out of our way. [In driving around craters, Gene has added 1.7 kilometers (or about 10 percent) to the straight-line, station-to-station distance. At some point during this part of the drive, Jack takes AS17-133- 20365 and 20366 .] [Cernan - "Adding a kilometer and a half or more to our projected travel distance from station to station is not too surprising. I call it the wander factor. When you're driving around, you've got to drive around craters; when you're driving up the scarp, you've got to take particular routes which are accessible and

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Well, it's all mileage.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: 0.7 and what was the bearing? 083? [Jack is asking about the place where they will deploy the charge.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: 082, I think, but we want oh-point-four. [Gene's "oh-point-four" isn't very clear.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Zero decimal four. Zero decimal four, guys...you...

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Oh, zero decimal four.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, that's the range.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, that's what I said: 0.4.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: But you want to bear north, don't you, a little?

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, I want...What'd you say, 082, didn't you, Bob?

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: That's affirm. That'll be close enough. It's probably be right on your track, there.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Okay. Well, I don't make a habit of following myself. I like to cover new ground.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Okay, copy that. 147:01:36 Schmitt: Watch out for that new ground there. Looks like in the...Look at the Italian flag! [This is a pennant affixed to the antenna on charge they deployed at the start of the traverse - at 083/0.5. Neither Jack nor Gene remembers why they called it "the Italian Flag". Like the flags on all the charges, it was international orange in color.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Hey, there is one there. I saw the box before I saw the flag. (Pause) No, I didn't, I saw the flag first, I've got to admit it.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Come on now!

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: I got to admit it, I saw the flag first.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: The boss said you saw the flag first. [Schmitt - "During the design phase there was probably some discussion over whether one really needed the flags. And the reference to the "Boss" may mean that Shepard or Slayton finally ruled that there had to be flags. I think that Gene did see the box first; and then we corrected the record, facetiously, so that it was consistent with what the Boss said we had to see first, namely the flag. Of course, I'm guessing and making this up, because I don't remember this incident."] [Gene doesn't remember the incident either, but suggests that the "Italian Flag"

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: I'm 082 and I'm 0.5. I'll just head right in towards the LM. Man, I want to stay away from ALSEP, I see the big boulder (Geophone Rock), so I'll...

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Okay. 147:02:04 Cernan: I'm going to go around...

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: 0.5. Okay, you'll have to swing (to the) right after we deploy, probably.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Yeah. (Pause) [See Gene's comment at 141:36:27 about having to turn right to avoid the charges. Photo AS17-133- 20367 is taken toward the north, perhaps as Gene maneuvers so that Jack can deploy the charge.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Whee! (Pause)

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Did we ever get any glass out of the bottom of those craters?

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: No, we haven't, we've got to try to do that before we leave. (Pause) There haven't been any good... [This chance remark probably triggers Jack's decision to get a glass sample as described at 147:19:46.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, sometime you'll have time to do that, I guess, guys. I'm not sure when...(Pause)

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: (Zero point) four! Okay.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Okay, let's put it in that little depression there. See right ahead of us to the right?

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Okay, 08...Well, she just went to 1. Okay, 081/0.4. [Jack has been watching the indicator and, since the digit just changed, they are about 350 meters from the SEP transmitter - plus or minus a residual Nav system error of about 50 meters or so. The actual distance is 440 meters, an indication of the superb performance of the navigation system over a closed, 30-kilometer course.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Okay.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Can you...

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Got your pictures?

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: I'm getting them. (Pause) Okay. Now just swing into that depression and I'll put it there. (Pause) Beautiful. Whoa, whoa. Okay, charge number 8.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: You didn't get a (locator) picture to the LM then, did you?

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, I did. I got several of them. [These picture are included in the series AS17-133- 20368 to 20373 which Jack took prior to the charge deployment.]

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Well, we don't have to take any more, do we? MP3 Audio Clip ( 19 min 13 sec )

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: No. (Pause) Okay, antenna is deployed. Pin 1 is pulled and Safe. And, let me check that. It's dusty. Yeah, it's Safe. Pin 2 is pulled and Safe. Pin 3, pulled and Safe.

A17A1465648.speaker: Parker
A17A1465648.text: Copy that.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: I guess as long as it didn't go off, it's safe.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Ooh, don't bang it. (They both laugh) I don't care what they say, that's a charge. (Pause) You're having great luck with those.

A17A1465648.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1465648.text: (Garbled). Okay, the LM was in the approach shot, I believe. Let me...Go ahead and turn around.

A17A1465648.speaker: Cernan
A17A1465648.text: Yeah, I got to go around anyway. (Pause) This way I can get a running shot of (static). (Garbled) right in the middle of it. Let me get them both in it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: No. (Pause) Okay, antenna is deployed. Pin 1 is pulled and Safe. And, let me check that. It's dusty. Yeah, it's Safe. Pin 2 is pulled and Safe. Pin 3, pulled and Safe.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Copy that.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: I guess as long as it didn't go off, it's safe.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Ooh, don't bang it. (They both laugh) I don't care what they say, that's a charge. (Pause) You're having great luck with those.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: (Garbled). Okay, the LM was in the approach shot, I believe. Let me...Go ahead and turn around.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, I got to go around anyway. (Pause) This way I can get a running shot of (static). (Garbled) right in the middle of it. Let me get them both in it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, I ran out of film, too.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Oh, boy.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Now that's pretty well located.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Garbled).

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: When you come around, take a picture of the LM on your camera. 147:04:23 Cernan: I will. I'll take it right out the front looking right at the thing. [Gene is taking a picture of the charge with the LM in the background. This is AS17-145- 22184 .] [Jack's last two pictures are AS17-133- 20374 and 20375 .]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, and give them a frame count. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Five-six. (Pause) Bob, I've got the "locator" of the charge and the LM all in the same order here, and I'm one more than what I just gave you. I can't look at it now.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, one more than what you gave me at Station 5 (which was frame 50). Understand. 147:04:55 Schmitt: Okay, Bob. You want me to go to the gravimeter now? [Here, Jack is referring to the LSG, the gravity-wave detector.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Roger. And if you guys will start out, we'll drive you by the ALSEP, Jack, and if you'll get out at the ALSEP, we'll have you take a look at the surface gravimeter and Gene can press on home to the LM.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Jack, I'm going to drive you in this way, and then I'll drive all the way back around that one geophone. [Gene probably is driving in toward the Central Station from the southwest, coming between the south and west geophone lines. Then, on his way to the LM, he will have to go all the way back out and around the south geophone line to avoid running over it.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Shall I...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: (Garbled) to the north, you could drive in toward the heat flow, towards that big rock, if you can see that.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, well, okay; that's as good as anything.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Bob, you want me to get some ALSEP pictures?

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Negative. (Pause) Okay, and Jack, you can stand by...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: I got a (warning) flag.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...for a feedwater dump (means "flag") very shortly. Okay, (PLSS) Feedwater, go to Aux(illiary), please.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: I just got it. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Man, look at that mess of cable. I hope that thing (the ALSEP)'s working, Bob.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Every...Well, a lot of it's working. We've just got to try and see if we can't level this thing (the LSG) tonight. When you get off there, Jack, I'll talk to you a bit about procedures for that. And in the meanwhile, it's my understanding...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay; that's good, Gene...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...that the second UHT is not in the immediate vicinity, where it's accessible, is that right?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: No, it is, I can get it. [They have two Universal Handling Tools. They are using one as the handle for the LRV Sampler ; Gene tossed the other one in the general direction of the Central Station at the end of the ALSEP deployment.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay; if you can...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay, and watch my heat flow (cables) over there, don't trip over them (as happened on Apollo 16). (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, I'm going to take a pair of tongs. [There are two pairs of tongs. Gene is wearing one, attached to his yo-yo, and the other is almost certainly stowed in the tool rack on the back of the Rover.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Do you have any film at all?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: No, I want your camera.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You want my camera? (Pause) [As Gene confirms at 147:07:38, Jack is taking Gene's tongs and camera so that, as Jack relates at 147:20:13, he can collect a sample of glass on his way back to the LM.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Jack, you won't need (a camera)...We aren't planning on taking the ALSEP photos right now.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. And, Jack, we're not sure you went to Aux on your water yet.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Garbled; pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: (Responding to Bob) I thought I did.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, it's coming up, now, we see it coming, Jack, don't worry.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Gene, can you...(Responding to Bob) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You got what you want?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Let me take a set of tongs in case I drop something. [Again, Jack is planning to get a glass sample but isn't telling Houston.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Can you reach them?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Schmitt - "I may have been pulling out Gene's yo-yo and taking the tongs off so that he didn't have to fool with it. It would have been easier that way."] [This would suggest that Jack moved around to Gene's side of the Rover. Alternatively, he could have stayed at his side of the Rover while Gene removed the tongs from his yo-yo and handed them across. Gene's "can you reach them?" suggests the latter.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You got everything you need?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yep. 147:07:38 Cernan: (To Bob) Okay, Jack's got my camera and tongs, and I'm on my way.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Bob, I got a tone again.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, what's it say? Probably just your water (garbled) been building up... [Jack got a warning tone at 147:05:46 that his primary cooling water supply had run out and that he needed to switch to his auxillary tank . He made the switch at that time and, as Parker suggests, this repetition of the tone may a sign that there was a momentary interruption of flow after the switchover.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: I can't read my gauges. (Pause) [Jack probably has moved away from the Rover by now, on his way to get the UHT. The following dialog suggests that the top of Jack's RCU is covered with dust.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Want me to take...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Well, we better take a look. Okay, I'm coming over there (to the Rover). [Gene will look for a warning flag on Jack's RCU .]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: I think I just got my water tone, Bob.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, that's right, also.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay, AUX water's On.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: We got our tones yesterday. Can you see anything?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Well, not unless...Let me see, let me brush your...Bend over. [Gene hasn't dismounted and Jack is probably standing beside him.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You don't have a brush to brush off (because it is under Gene's seat). Okay, no flags. (Pause) Now, wait a minute. Okay. You got no...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Huh?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You got no flags.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: You look good to us, Jack.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Once more. A good look.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Jack, you look good to us.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No flags. All right, no flags, Jack.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, and, Gene, I think you need to go to Aux...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (To Jack) Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...if you didn't.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, I just did, Bob, and my water flag cleared.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, copy that...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No, it didn't. Not yet.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, it's probably still coming up. [Schmitt - "When you switched to the Aux tank, it took a little while for either the flow of water or the water pressure - whichever the sensor worked on - to build up enough to get rid of the flag."]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Jack, just be careful of the cables. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, you want me to get a UHT, huh?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: It's right over there by the...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, I know where it is...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: If it's quite close, but if it's not, don't bother, I think we can probably try this by hand.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No, it's there, Bob; he'll get it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Looking at CDR-30 ) You got a (parking) heading for me at the Rover (means the LM)? Is 017 good?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: (To Bob) You don't want me to kick the LEAM yet, huh?

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Negative. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "I was joking, of course; and I think this refers to some time in training when I accidentally kicked it."] [Bob agrees that this is a training reference.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Bob, I've got a UHT.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, when you go back to the LSG, Jack, we first of all would like a reading on where the bubble is in the circle, (that is) whether it's in the center. And what we're going to have to have, unfortunately, is to have the bubble centered in the inner circle (pause) because this is, apparently, a requirement, even though we didn't train to it. Apparently it's something that's come up, and it's going to have to be within the inner circle of the bubble. So, the first thing we need to do is, when you go up there, is to see whether the bubble is in the center of the circle. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Bob. (Pause) That bubble is centered!

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Okay, the next thing we want you to do is put the UHT in the socket there, and move the...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Hey, Bob.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...LSG from side to side...

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Bob...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...do not pick it up. Okay, go ahead, Jack.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: I did not have to touch it, it is centered.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, but now they're worried that it's stuck like your gimbal thing was last night (on the Central Station antenna). [Bob is referring to the "sticky level bubble" Jack encountered on the Central Station at 119:38:02 and again at 119:55:35 and following. In that case, surface tension had kept the bubble stuck to the outside of its dome.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: And, also, the thing is that maybe something's hung up inside and, by moving it, we can jostle it free. They do not want it picked up, but they'd like to have UHT put in there and sort of have the instrument rocked from side to side to again see the bubble move. And once that is done, to then press it down into the ground and again re-align it and put the bubble within the inner circle. Over. They would also like to see if the gimbal is free. [Schmitt - "They wanted me to press the legs into the surface. I suspect that, by this time, Joe Weber was absolutely panicked about his experiment. And

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: How much do you want me to rock it? How far should I let the bubble travel?

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Basically, we just want to see it move. (If) you go out to the outer circle, that's plenty. (Pause) And, again, you (garbled).

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: There's only one circle. Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Oh, I mean the outer rim of it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay, I did that. It's still centered and gimbal is swinging. [Schmitt - "I could see the gimbal by looking through the top of the instrument. I don't know why I said 'gimbal' because I was probably looking at the balance beam."]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, we copy the gimbal is swinging and we copy you moved the bubble out to the edge of the bubble level and come back into the inner circle.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: That's right. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Puffing rather heavily as he leans forward) Okay, Bob, I'm reading 089, 20.1, 002, 92, 88. Volts are 65 and 66. Batteries are 114 (degrees) and 138. Rear motors are off-scale low. Forward left is off-scale low and right is 210 degrees. [Schmitt - "Getting off the Rover shouldn't have made Gene breathe heavily. He may have gotten off and leaned way over to read the console. That might have cramped him a little bit and made him spit his words out."] [Gene is reading a bearing of 089 to the SEP and a range of 150 to 250 meters. The actual values are about 080 and 150, indicating a very small res

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Copy that. What's the first battery temperature there, Gene?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: First battery temperature is 114.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: (Unenthusiastically passing up the request) Okay, Jack. They apparently don't believe you when you said you aligned it last night and they're concerned the shade is not on 20 degrees. (Pause) [Schmitt - "There was a sunshade on the LSG that shadowed the hole in the top of the instrument that let it cool by radiating to the sky. Twenty degrees refers to our latitude and I guess I had to get the LSG leveled and then tilt the shade at the proper angle. It's amazing how you don't remember doing any of that. I remember going back to fix it, but not the actual deployment."]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Copy 114 on that battery temperature, Gene.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: It (the sunshade)'s on 20, Bob.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Okay; in that case, I guess you're free to come home.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Well, what is basically the problem with it?

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: They haven't been able to level it for some reason, and they were afraid that the thing wasn't level. They were hoping also maybe by moving it that you might jostle it a bit and it would come to level, but I think we'll just have to think about it some more. Their first presumption - the easiest solution - was to have it unleveled, which case we could fix it this way. But I guess that's not the case. We'll have to see what happens overnight. Give us a chance to follow the tradition of coming back to the ALSEP tomorrow.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Well, do you want me to change it's level a little bit...put it off level a little and see if you can work it. [Schmitt - "They were moving weights on the balance beam and my question was, could we do something to change the relative gravitational force on either side of the fulcrum to make it work. But I don't think they could have ever convinced themselves that it was a design problem in time to do something like that."]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: I don't think so, Jack. That doesn't sound very good to me.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Well, it might be some air (or error?) in the level bubble or something.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Why don't you just leave it there if it's centered with the level bubble within the inner circle there. That's the requirements as far as we can tell, and we'll just have to leave it overnight again. And why don't you come on back to the LM. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Gene, are you at the Rover?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yes, sir. I'm parked.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Gave you my readings.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. You gave me your readings and when you get done, let me know, because the first thing we want to do is work on the SEP (receiver) a little bit.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Stand by. (Pause) (You've) got TV. (Pause) Okay. What do you want to do to the SEP? [TV on.] RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (14 min 38 sec) Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, Geno. When you go back to the SEP now - and let's do this first and get it out of the way - you can probably do this anyway while Jack's coming home. When you open the blankets, remember that at the back of the SEP there was a piece of Velcro on the case and a piece of Velcro just inside the rear hinge on the covers, and this is what you sort of peel back when you go to remove the back end there so you can get the DSEA out? You remember that piece of tape there?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yeah. That came off. [Gene is dusting the right-side battery covers as per CDR-31 . Normally, he and Jack would have taken care of the SCBs before the dusting but, since Jack is out at the ALSEP, Gene is taking care of the tasks that don't require Jack's presence. Fendell pans away.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: That came off.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. This is on the side away from you as you stand facing it. Right?

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Oh, no. That's the side...Go ahead, Gene, I'm sorry. [Bob probably should have made sure Gene was in position to look at the SEP bag before starting this discussion.] [The SEP receiver rides on the Rover just behind Jack's seat, protected from sunlight and dust by a thermal bag. The receiver - like the TV camera and the LCRU - has a mirror on its top surface which allows the unit to cool. As indicated in Figure 15-20 from the Mission Report ( 26 Mb PDF ), the top of the thermal bag consists of a pair of flaps held down by strips of Velcro attached to the undersides of the flaps and to the fron

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay, go ahead.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Gene, if you stand facing it, in the back - away from you - there's a strip of Velcro on the case and there's another strip of Velcro on the blanket itself and this is the Velcro you have to tear off or to unhook, as it were, when you come to tear the blankets down to get the DSEA off. Remember that piece?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, but that's on the side away from me. I'm on the LMP's side and that's on the other side.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Right. That's on the other side of the top. And what we're interested in, number 1, is that piece of Velcro still mated or when you open the blankets to cool it, does that Velcro come open? Over.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Well, that's the Velcro that's so full of dust it comes open, Bob. [Gene is referring to the Velcro which holds the covers open, not to the pieces Bob is referring to that hold the back of the bag closed.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, and so what happens...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Trying to stay...It's hooked; it'll stay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Well, the feeling...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: I don't know if you can see that but it's...Well, you can't (because of the) back seat...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, well, feeling is that...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Bob, I swung the covers and they will stay open about 150 degrees. (Pause) [Fendell finds Gene leaning over the SEP.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: (Trying to figure out what Gene's saying) I...Stand by a minute. What you're saying is that the cover actually stands up a little bit in space.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Now, if you want the cover open, I can open it and normally it should swing 180 degrees, (that is) parallel with the top of the SEP.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay, but does that Velcro in back stay mated?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Well, the Velcro holds (and), the way that we've been opening it, it holds. (Hearing Bob) Yes, it's being mated and probably it holds the covers open 150 degrees! [Gene is uncharacteristically annoyed.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: No. That's okay. What the concern originally was, was that when this...

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: The Velcro...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: ...happened, the sunlight was getting down in the back there and warming up the back of the SEP. That's apparently not the case. Over.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No, that's not the case. The Velcro that came off is the Velcro that keeps the covers closed.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. We were concerned about both pieces of Velcro since the one had come off.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No. The other one is still on and it still holds and the back part of the SEP - where the DSEA is - is in the shade. [Gene dusts the SEP cover with the dustbrush.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. I copy that. Okay. While we're talking about this - and I'll get back with you - turn the DSEA and the receiver both to Off, please. (Pause) And read me a temperature, please.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: 112 degrees.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Copy that. And I mark them both off, right?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yes. (Pause) Bob, I just dusted it as clean as it'll get. Video Clip ( 3 min 18 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Thank you. (Long Pause) [Gene finishes dusting the SEP, then dusts the TCU. Fendell pans away counter-clockwise.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Hey, Bob,...

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Go ahead.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: ...I cheated on you.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: I was sure you would. What'd you do? 147:19:53 Schmitt: I just sampled the glass in the bottom of a crater. I documented it by shooting the LM across the crater at infinity and then shooting the crater with stereo at 11 feet and then a cross-Sun pair at 7; and then I sampled it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. [Jack borrowed Gene's camera when he got off the Rover at the LSG at 147:06:40. The "locator" to the LM is AS17-145- 22185 . Note that this crater is down in the swale between the LM and the ALSEP. Jack's up-Sun stereopair is 22186 and 22187 ; and his cross-Sun stereopair is 22188 and 22189 . He also shot a cross-Sun stereopair of "afters", which are 22190 and 22191 .] [Schmitt - "There's a little bell ringing in my head that I'd taken Gene's camera and tongs (at 147:06:41) just so that I could sample one of the glass-lined craters. That's probably why I didn't pay any attention to Bob w

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Then I took a cross-Sun (stereo)pair at 7 (foot focus) "after".

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: (Punning) I guess now "gnomon is a LM". [Schmitt - "Throughout training, I had used the pun 'gnomon is not an island', and Bob was one-upping me here."]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: It (the glass sample)'s very fragile. (Hearing Bob) That's right. It's very fragile, and I double bagged it. I don't know whether we can keep it or not.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. We'll hope.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: You may think about how to preserve it.

A17A1470319.speaker: Parker
A17A1470319.text: Okay. (Pause) [Gene goes to dust the left side battery covers.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: While you're thinking, I'll put it on my (Rover) floor pan, I guess. (Pause) Okay. What do I have to do here?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Get this bag (SCB) off me to start.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Get that bag off you to start with. (Pause) Be careful of that sample there. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Those are the cleanest battery covers in existence on a Rover right now, I tell you. (Pause)

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Noticing that Fendell is tilting the TV down to look) Oh, you don't believe me. Look at that!

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: What?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: They don't believe me.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Excuse me. Move forward just a little. And I'll get your bag. Here you go.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: (Noticing that the TV is still pointed down) Now you're stuck down there, aren't you? [Fendell tilts the TV up. Jack is beyond Gene, so we don't get to see much of the SCB removal.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: No you're not. Seems like you (would think) I may be going nuts talking to that moving machine (the TV) over there. (Pause) [There is laughter in Houston.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Boy, we don't need any hooks; I'll tell you.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: I know it. [Jack is having trouble removing Gene's SCB.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Can you stoop just a little bit?

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, all that stuff is getting...There (garbled).

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: (Garbled) get your hook (perhaps the Velcro strap that secures the SCB at the bottom)'s back.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, hook my harness back up so we don't forget that. 147:21:50 Schmitt: Velcro's closed. Okay. [One end of the Velcro strap is sewn on to the bottom of the PLSS. There is a Velcro patch on that end, and a complementary patch of the free end. The free end of the strap can be secured, out of the way, by pressing those two patches together. After finishing, Jack goes to the Rover gate.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: You know, (as) you look at those little sparklies in the soil we're walking on and they change colors on you.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Yep.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Greens to purples.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Iridescent. Iridescent sparklies. Video Clip ( 3 min 33 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Okay. I'll come over, and I'll unload your stuff. [Gene moves toward the front of the Rover. Fendell pans clockwise to follow him.]

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay. Now, we got more samples than we've got sense, I think. Let's see here (consulting checklist), you're taking care of the SEP.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Yeah, don't...That's all right.

A17A1470319.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1470319.text: Okay.

A17A1470319.speaker: Cernan
A17A1470319.text: Hey, Bob; the covers are open on the SEP.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Go ahead. What we would like to do here...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (To Jack) Got it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: ...on the close-out, guys. Let me read this to you first of all. In the SRC, we'd like the following stuff along with...Let's see...Stand by. (Pause) 147:23:44 Cernan: (To Jack) Is this (SCB) 9 or 6? [Fendell passes Jack at his seat, Gene at the gate, and then pans up to Earth.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay, guys. We're going to follow an Apollo 16 mode and put stuff in (the SRC) loose, because they'd like to segregate stuff in the following way. We'd like to put the long can and four core tubes in the SRC. I guess it's going to take a while just carrying stuff back and forth (between the Rover and the MESA). But they'd probably like to get this in because of the volatile stuff. They'd like to get the long can and three core tubes in the SRC; (that's priority) number 1. And then we'd like to get all the SCB-4 samples in the same SRC. Over. [The reference to "volatiles" means that the Backroo

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (To Gene) Oh, wait a minute. Wait a minute.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (To Bob) Yeah. You want...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: ...three plus the long can; that's four cores all together.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Right. Put those in the SRC...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: All samples from 4.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: All the samples from SCB-4.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (To Gene) These are 4. You want to get the core tubes in first, though.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah. I want to put these in. If you'd give me the...Yeah, I only got two hands. I'll come back by the time you dig them out. (Pause) 147:24:54 Parker: Okay, and then, 17, do you guys remember where the trench samples - the three trench soil samples - which bag (SCB) those were put in? (The one's) from Station 4? Over.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, let's see. I'm the only one who had (sample) bags, so I bagged them and put them in whatever bag Jack had (that is, SCB-4). I think.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Yeah. [Fendell returns to Jack at his seat. Gene is behind him, out of sight, at the MESA.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay, then that'll be SCB-4. So we'd like those in SCB-4...those are the ones that will go in the rock box and that's in agreement with what we want to do.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay, give me those other two cores, if you've got them, Jack.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Long can. (Long Pause) 147:25:51 Schmitt: The long can. Here's a...Oh. Got it? It's slippery.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, and we need one more core. Video Clip ( 1 min 57 sec 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 20 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: One more core.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Is) that right, now? Three core tubes and a long can?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yep, got them all.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: And then...Roger that. And then all the samples in SCB-4. We won't bother to try and sort them out, and then beyond that we'll fill them up with samples from SCB-5. Over. [Jack takes SCB-5 to the MESA.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Which one's that? That's 5. Let me get 4, first.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Here, hold this. I'll get it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, it's on the gate right there, just hanging. I just put it there. (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Going to the gate) Four is the one I had on there at Shorty? Or you had on at Shorty?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, you had it on. I don't know, but they should have that logged. I don't remember who had it on.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Well, now wait a minute. I took the trench. You held the bags.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: And I put them in you.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: You put them on me. Did I have 4 on at Shorty?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Yes!!

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: That's what they said.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: That's affirm. That's why we want SCB-4 dumped into the thing (the SRC). But it's a dirty bag, so we just want to dump the samples in. [Jack goes to his seat.
