He is wearing Gene's tongs on a yo-yo, which he seems to have been wearing as a contingency, even though he hadn't planned on using it.] [Cernan - "The yo-yo was about an inch or two high, a rectangular box, and it had a little strap that went under something (usually a hose) and came back around and snapped on itself. I wore mine all the time, so Jack must have been wearing one, too."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Okay; and you want 5 to fill it up. (No answer; pause) Okay, Bob...(Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. And, Jack, it probably would protect the glass a bit better if you put it in the SRC gently with the other rocks there. Particularly if you don't fill the SRC too full. But, again, we'll be putting SCB (5) samples in there to more or less flesh it out if there's not too many SCB-4 samples. [Jack pours samples out of an SCB into his footpan. He then grabs the tongs and picks up an unbagged rock that he may have just dropped. He puts the rock in an unseen SCB on his seat.] Video Clip ( 2 min 35 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Leave a space for a sample, I guess, Gene.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, you'd better give it to me. There's not much space. It's going fast.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: You're really...Well, can you leave one...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Where is the sample?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Well, it's over here.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: I'll get it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: No, I'll bring it to you. I just...(Pause) [Jack takes the glass sample to the MESA.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Is there some way to...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Just set it in there. (Pause) I'll set it. I'll be delicate with it. Take this bag back.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay. It's in the right-hand back corner of the SRC.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that. [Schmitt - "I must have known - and this changes what I've said before about the observation of glass in craters on other missions - because I talked to the people doing remnant magnetism and asked them it they didn't want an oriented sample of glass in order to see if there had been any modern magnetic fields. And I don't remember their having any enthusiasm for it; but, in my mind, that was a reasonably important sample to get. And that's probably why I was manipulating things to get a sample and all the documentary photographs and why I had some concern over protecting it."

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: You're just about full. You got some (samples) left in there (SCB-5)?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: I'll get some small ones and some big ones, too. [Jack takes SCB-4 to the Rover. Fendell stays with Gene at the MESA.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Don't fill it too full.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No. (Pause) Hey, we got some big rock samples. 147:28:54 Schmitt: Okay, Bob. SCB-6 and SC...Wait a minute. What's in (SCB) 6?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Six? Probably nothing. But tell us...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Well, there's samples in 6. [Gene is taking sample bags out of the SCB and is putting them in the SRC, the rock box.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. You should also have SCB-8 under your seat with samples in it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: This is what I sampled at...

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: At Station 3, maybe.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Six has the samples from...(Hearing Bob) Yes.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Let's take up SCB-8...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: We have more samples today than Carter... [Schmitt - "There was a brand of pills called Carter's Little Liver Pills, and there was an expression 'You've got more of such-and-such than Carter has pills.'"]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: And let's take up SCB-6; and why don't you dump out the Rover samples into SCB-6?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Well, one reason not to take 6 is I don't know if I can get it off (the Rover)! [Gene discards the SRC seal protector.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. And let's save SCB-4 because I think you may need that tomorrow. [Schmitt - "Bob thought he'd seen Gene throw SCB-4 to his left, not having noticed that I'd taken SCB-4 back to the Rover."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Four is on the rack, empty.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. How about SCB-5? Is that only partially emptied, or is it totally emptied?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No, it's about half full, Bob.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. We'll take that up with us. [Jack, who has been at the gate, goes to his seat carrying an SCB.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Bob, I've already...Let me tell you what I've done. I've got SCB-8 full.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Let's take it up.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Roger. On that. Video Clip ( 3 min 30 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: It's got Rover samples in it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: But I can't get them all. They won't all be in there.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay; eight.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Closing the SRC) Okay. Bob, the seal (on the box) was clean. It was clear, and I got your four cores...(correcting himself) three cores, plus a long can. I got Jack's glass. I got SCB-4 and a couple of samples out of SCB-5.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that. Sounds great. [Jack now picks up samples from his footpan and puts them in SCB-6.] 147:31:01 Cernan: Okay. Now where was I? You got me all out of whack, here.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: That's affirm.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: "Core cap dispenser." Okay, you're "clean" (and the) cosmic ray is done. [During the EVA-1 Rover preps (checklist page LMP-12 ), Jack had the option of deploying the cosmic ray experiment if he had time - and did so at 118:34:41. For the EVA-2 close-out, Gene's checklist page CDR-30 indicates cosmic ray deployment unless Jack had already done it.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: SCB-5...Yeah, okay. Now, Jack, we've got SCB-5 that's half full. What have you got over there?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Bring it over here, and I'll put it into 6. Six is a little more than half full.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, this is a little less than half full. Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: That ought to make one full bag. And these are big rocks so they'll come out easy. Where's that big, big rock we got? That's in one of those bags, too. Picked up a big rock. [Gene may be referring to the large sample collected at Station 5 at 146:42.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Here...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Here let me see if I can't dump it. (Pause) [Gene, at the Rover, dumps the contents of SCB-5 into SCB-6.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: How's that for a lunar dump? Huh?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Perfect. (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Going to the gate) I want to see if I can't dust (the bag latches on the gate)...Did you lock this one over here?...No.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Hey, don't lock those...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No, I'm going to see if I can dust them and make them work easier.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Boy, I'll tell you...I really had to pull. I pulled harder than I like to in a pressure suit. [Cernan - "The latches were starting to stick, so I was just going to dust them to see if that would help. Jack's comment, it seems to me, was that, in a pressure suit, you can sometimes apply more force than you would normally intend to. You're not outfitted to be a brain surgeon with tweezers. So the tendency to grab hold of something and pull harder than you might want to was a real danger; and what Jack was saying was that he didn't want to pull the latches off."] [Schmitt - "You're putting pressu

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: See if I can... 147:32:15 Schmitt: (Closing SCB-6) Okay, Bob. SCB-8 and 6 are going up.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay, and I understand 5 will be...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Or will go up.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: ...on the gate.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yes, sir, Bob. It'll be there.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Stowing the empty SCB) And 7 under the LMP's seat. 147:32:31 Cernan: 4 and 5 will be on the gate. You know, here's a problem for you tonight. You got any way of freeing up these gate hinges that lock the bags on? I'm dusting them, but they're not going to lock, any of them. They're frozen tight, just about.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that. We'll talk about it. [Jack takes SCBs 6 and 8 to the ladder so that he can put them on the LM footpad. One of them is partially open. As he pulls the SCBs out of his Rover footpan, he turns to his right so that he doesn't have to lift the bags very high.] [Schmitt - "I can't tell you why I was going sideways here, unless it was just the way I got started. A little overshoot on my rotation."] [Cernan - "When I was working around the MESA, there were a lot of times when I wanted, for example, to move five feet to the left, that I did not turn left and start walking straight on.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: If you do get them locked, you may never get them off.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. We'll give them something to work on overnight. [Houston never had any suggestions about the locks.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay, I'm dusting them right now. But I still can't free them up.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Man those are heavy bags.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Jack, have you got the top of the bag closed?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Garbled) bags.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Returning to the Rover) Yeah, what do you need?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. No. John (Young) thought maybe they were still open. He was worried. [Cernan - "Bob got out of this one by saying "John thought that they might still be open"; and Jack came back very nicely. If Bob had said "Jack, I thought maybe you had left them open", I guarantee you that Jack would have come back with some remark to Bob. That's just the way it went. Those guys could go after each other in a very sarcastic manner sometimes."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Oh, no, I latched them. I'll check them again before I go up.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Garbled under Bob)

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay, and we got no FSRs (football-sized rocks) underneath the seat. We understand. Roger.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: No. I just checked and they're all in the bags. And the Rover sample bag is empty. [Jack stows the maps under his seat.] Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Not nothing left. [Jack takes the Rover sample bag (an SCB) from the hook on the accessory staff where it normally hangs and shows his TV audience just how empty it is.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Bob, neither one of these bag latchers are going to latch on the back. I dusted them, but...

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay,...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: ...they're not going to work. I can't free them up...

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: ...we'll talk about it tonight...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: We'll use the seat. [That is, they can put samples under the seats.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: ...Don't worry about it now.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, we can probably use the seat. We've got a little more room than we had. Okay. Let me get something else done.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Taking a packet of sample bags from under his seat) I wonder if I ought to take a sample bag holder up there to see if I can fix that. To see if it fixes. [Jack takes the sample bags out of the holder.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Roger, Jack. I'd suggest that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Probably ought to, huh? [Jack opens his shin pocket , puts bag holder in the pocket, and closes the pocket cover.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay. (Reading CDR-32 ) (The SEP) receiver's been dusted and blankets are open; power is Off and Off. Okay. I'm going to take the TGE (Traverse Gravimeter Experiment) off (the Rover) now - or dust it and then take it off - and then just leave it there. Hey, congratulate Jose (John Young) on that fender will you? Because I think he just saved us an awful lot of problems. He and whoever else worked on it. [Jack puts the sample bags under his seat.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: He mumbled something very humbly about a thousand guys.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, tell him that's going to be my "bring home" present to him: a picture of his fender. [Cernan - "I brought the whole fender home!"] [The replacement fender is on display at the National Air & Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Ron Creel has provided a summary ( 1.3 Mb PDF ) of the fender extension losses that occurred on all three Rover missions.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay, Bob. Unused gear - which you have an inventory on (by a process of elimination) - is under the LMP's seat. (Pause) [Jack closes the seat.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Where am I (in the checklist)? [He is on checklist page LMP-29 .]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Taking the gravimeter to the ladder) I'm bringing the TGE over here, but I'm not pushing it yet.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Going to the MESA, looking at LMP-30 ) Cosmic ray's deployed! (Pause) [As is discussed at 118:35:03, deployment of the cosmic ray could have come then or now. Having had a spare moment after the flag deployment, Jack set out the cosmic ray experiment at that point in EVA-1.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Man, I got the sorest hands in the world, right now.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: How about on the Moon?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Carrying the ETB to the Rover) Bum, bum, bum, baa.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Nothing's in the big bag, is it?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Responding to Bob) I just can't compete with you astronomers. [Bob Parker was a member of the Astronomy Department faculty at the University of Wisconsin before joining the astronaut corps.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Just keep trying.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Nothing's in the bag, is it? Big bag?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Nothing's in the big bag.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay. 147:36:11 Schmitt: Unless there's one rock in there that disappeared yesterday. I don't know what happened to it. (Pause) [Jack is referring to a rock he collected east of the LM during the Rover preps at 118:31:10 . Shortly thereafter, he put it in the big bag but then, at 123:40:07 during the EVa-1 close-out, couldn't find it.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Hey, we forgot the polarizing filter work! [Gene returns to the Rover.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Nah, I saw it on the checklist, and I mentioned it to Bob, and he didn't come back with anything. And there was a...(Pause) [Gene called out the polarization filter when he checked under his seat at 141:20:35 to make sure (as per checklist) that Jack had transferred the filter from the ETB during the Rover preps. They were to have taken pictures at Shorty with the filter on Jack's camera but the activity was dropped without remark because of the discovery of the orange soil.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Consulting CDR-32 ) Okay. I guess I'm going to go ahead and...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Put those (unused sample bags) under that seat, please.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (At Schmitt's seat) Yeah, there's only one left.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: One? No, there's three or four...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: There's three left.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Just put them under there. Who knows, we may need them at the rate we're going.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. And, Jack, while you're unloading there,...

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Garbled) pull those (Rover circuit) breakers. [This item is on CDR-31 . The fact that they are getting everything done - albeit in almost random order - is a testament to this crew's thoroughness and to their training. They know what needs to be done and why and know how to use the checklist as an effective tool. On Apollo 12, Pete Conrad had some occasional difficulties because he relied too much on his memory and, at the other extreme, one can imagine people using a checklist as a crutch, as a means of covering up inadequate preparation. Here, Cernan and Schmitt are using the checklists - a

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: ...on the 500 millimeter you might squeeze off a few shots of the North and South Massif there, if there's any lineations visible.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay. I'll give it a try. Why, are we ahead of time? Video Clip ( 2 min 35 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: No, we're working right on time.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Why don't you give it to me while you're packing the ETB, Jack; I'll do it.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Am I behind you, now (in the checklist)?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, I'm going to start inventorying the Rover and pulling the breakers so...(Pause) [Gene gets the 500-mm camera. Jack is on LMP-30 and Gene is waiting to finish the last few items on CDR-31 .] 147:37:24 Schmitt: Man, we are so far off nominal on what bags (SCBs we've used)... (Laughs) I sort of didn't think. The checklist is going to have to be updated, I guess. 147:37:33 Parker: Totally. (Pause) [Gene raises the 500-mm camera to his face plate so that he can use the boresight mounted on the lens barrel as he photographs the South Massif. He takes a left-to-right sequence consisting of AS17

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Oh, I should call (and tell Houston what I'm putting in the ETB). Mag Charlie.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Mag Kilo.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Mag Bravo. (Pause) Mag Golf. (Pause) Mag India.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy all those. And tell Gene that we can confirm that his lens cover's off. [As can be seen in the TV, the lens cap is hanging free, attached to the barrel of the lens with a strap. After finishing a sequence of South Massif photos, Gene takes a portrait of the North Massif , taking three sequences of the summit area and finishing up with a sequence across the face of the mountain, starting to the left of the large boulder track. The images are AS17-144- 22105 to 22132 .] [Frame 22129 shows the boulder track.] MPEG Clip (1 min 32 sec; 9.5Mb)

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay. (To Gene) They confirm that your lens cover's off. [Needless to say, Gene can hear Bob perfectly well. The humor here is exceedingly dry.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (To Bob) The scissors are in (the ETB).

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that. 147:38:43 Schmitt: Lens brushes . (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Facing east) I hope this is the right setting. It is.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Laughs) Hey, try f/5.6 directly down-Sun...(correcting himself) or, up-Sun, at (the) Sculptured Hills there in the distance. (Pause) See where I mean?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, I'll get it. [Schmitt - "I may have been trying to get Gene to take an over-exposed picture into the shadowed areas on the Sculptured Hills."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Okay, Bob. (To himself) What else do I need here? Let's see. 500, mag R. (To Gene) (I) need mag R as soon as you're through.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Yeah. I think we've got enough of those now, Gene. Video Clip ( 2 min 38 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPEG )

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: (To Jack) You got the maps?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Yep, got them.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Some of these (photos) won't overlap, Bob, because I'm hurrying.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Don't smear them. [Many of the Apollo 16 500-mm pictures were badly smeared.] 147:39:46 Parker: Don't hurry and smear them. [Gene finishes with the 500 and puts the lens cap back on.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: They're not smeared, but I just didn't overlap some of them. (Hearing Bob) Okay. Everyone agrees to that. Don't hurry and smear them. (Jack laughs) I'll get those others, Jack, tomorrow.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. You got the maps in there, too, Jack?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Frame count, Bob, is...

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Answering Bob) Yes.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Frame count is 152 on the 500.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Laughing) (To Gene) Let go of it (the 500). There.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Dynamic. Did you cycle it twice?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No; cycle it twice. [Jack will expose two more frames before removing the film magazine and inserting the dark slide .]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Do you have the maps there, Jack?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (To Jack) Okay. I guess I'll go in and pull some Rover breakers.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. And...Roger. Copy that.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: (Leaning inboard over the Rover) Oh, boy. Pulling breakers is not going to be much fun. [Cernan - "Whether you're working in a pressurized suit or working in shirtsleeves, if I had to pick between zero gravity, one-sixth gravity, or full Earth gravity, in every case I'd pick one-sixth. Sometimes you'd have trouble getting as much leverage as you can on Earth; but, otherwise, one-sixth gravity makes things easier. The pressure suit, on the other hand, is a big inhibitant, particularly in restricting your dexterity. You can make the big movement and turn around and get from here to there with a

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: You want me to...You want the scissors or something (to use in pulling the breakers)? [Cernan - "These were surgical scissors with the rounded point, and they were the most common instrument in spaceflight."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No. (Pause) Oh, boy. (Pause) Oh, boy.

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Mag Romeo. [This is the magazine off the 500-mm camera, which Jack is now putting in the ETB.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that. You got the maps, Jack?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: (Laughing) You ask me that one more time Parker, and I'm going to get mad at ya.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Oh, I got to...Whew! What have you got over there? You got the scissors handy?

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, you want them?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: I got three of four breakers. Let me try this other one one more time. (Pause) Okay. I got it - with the old fingers.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that. All four of them out, Gene.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay; (circuit breakers) Alpha, Bravo... (Responding to Bob) Yes, sir. Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta are Open. I'll get the LCRU power.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. And, Gene, when you leave the (TV) camera, a reminder to face it away from the Sun and tilt it down. [Houston wants to minimize the area exposed to the Sun and get maximum cooling through the rest period. Gene is on CDR-31 .]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay. (Pause) [Gene points the TV camera in a generally westward direction and down toward the Rover seats.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Hey, Gene. That's not quite away from the Sun. Really it ought to be, you know, down-Sun. [TV off.]

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: I'll (static). I'll get it, Bob. (Long Pause) Bob, are you reading?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Roger. Loud and clear. (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: I read you, Gene.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Yeah. See, I just turned LCRU power off; they got to go through the LM.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: That's right.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Bob, do you read?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Loud and clear. (Pause)

A17A1472317.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1472317.text: Is this gravimeter working?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: No, it's not. I didn't push it yet. Hello, Houston, come on. Otherwise, I'll turn this power back on.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Read you loud and clear, Gene. Do you read Houston?

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, let me turn it on and talk to them. [Cernan - "From the tone of voice, you can hear that we were pretty tired. 'God damn it, let's get on with the show and stop screwing around.' You can hear the fatigue in our voices."]

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: We read you loud and clear, Gene.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Well, I just turned the LCRU back on. Are you reading us through the LM, now?

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Yeah, we came through the LM that time.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: Okay. I'm turning it off and the camera is pointed down and it's pointed effectively to the west. Down-Sun.

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Okay. Copy that. Very good. Thank you.

A17A1472317.speaker: Cernan
A17A1472317.text: LCRU Power's going Off. (Pause) Okay, LCRU Power is Off. (Reading) Battery covers. Open battery covers. They're all dusted already. [Don McMillan has provided an animation ( 0.8 Mb ) of the battery covers on his Virtual Rover being opened.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 14 min 56 sec )

A17A1472317.speaker: Parker
A17A1472317.text: Copy that. (Pause) 17, you read Houston?

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Copy that. (Pause) 17, you read Houston?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Uh-oh, I got to work on one battery. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: 17, you read Houston? (No answer; pause) 17, you read Houston? Over. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Hey, Bob?

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Roger, 17. Do you read?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Still there? (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Well, they're supposed to be going through the LM.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: 17, do you read Houston? (No answer)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Got something fouled up. (Pause) Maybe we got the switches wrong, or something, up there (in the LM cabin.) Don't think so, though.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: No.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: They talked to us first.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Let me give them a call. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: 17, do you read Houston? Over.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Bob, you want to try again. We're on the LCRU! (Hearing Bob) Yeah, we read you, but I'm on the LCRU again. We're not reading you through the LM!

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Yeah, I don't understand that. Stand by. (Brief pause) Press on with the rest of the close-out.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Well, I'll leave you on the LCRU, here. (Responding to Bob) Yeah, we're pressing on. Okay. For the first time, I've got to dust the center battery cover. All the others are good.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. Roger, 17. Do you read Houston now?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Well, yeah, but I'm on the LCRU. I don't know.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: No, now they say we're going back to the LM again. Press on with the close-out. [TV on.] Video Clip ( 0 min 29 sec 0.1 Mb RealVideo or 4 Mb MPEG )

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay, Bob. I'm going to go turn the LCRU power Off. And for the first time, I've got to dust the center radiator on the batteries.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Up until this time, they've all been real clean.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Copy that. 147:46:05 Cernan: Okay. Give me a short count. And in the interim I'm going to turn the LCRU Power, Off.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. Roger. 1-2-3, 3-2-1. [TV off.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay, 17, do you read Houston? Over.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay. We've got you.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay; very good.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yeah. We got you, Bob.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. We've got about two-zero (20) minutes before we have to be inside the LM there, fellows. Let's hustle on.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: (Joking) Oh, I think we'll just sort of take it easy, Bob. (Pause) Okay. The MESA's tidied.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Thank you.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I've got the (PLSS LiOH) canisters; pins are green.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Copy that.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: The LM (lithium hydroxide) canister's in the pocket (on the EVA pallet).

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Very good.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: And, let's see. (Looking at the bottom of LMP-30 ) I think I'm ready to dust. Could I help you?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: No, I'm leaving here right now.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. And, Gene, as you go by, how about giving us the SEP temperature readings. 147:46:59 Schmitt: (Garbled) I got to take these bags up.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: (Hearing Bob) Oh, me. I will. (Long Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: 17, Houston. It's awfully quiet.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay, Bob. Here's your reading. About one hundred and...About 108 to (1)10 degrees.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) Okay. We'll leave it there, as is, overnight. Thank you.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: And I'll give her one good little smack with the brush. And it's as clean as it'll ever come.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. Thank you.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Jack, you might just as well go cold water. There's no more use for it now, if you're warm.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: No, I'm not warm I'm just... Want to hand me that other SCB there? (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, man! [They both laugh. Apparently, Jack has decided to take one or more of the SCBs up to the porch.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh! The cover's open on this one.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: You wonder why it's hard to get up the ladder. [It's hard to get up the ladder because he's carrying a heavy SCB.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Don't hold it by the cover.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: (To himself) What do I want these tongs on for?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Give them to me. I'll take them down.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Just noticed them.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Don't want them (up to the cabin). Okay.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Thank you.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Don't take it by the cover. The (SCB) cover's going to come open. Take it by this.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Wait a minute.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Got it?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I got it.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay. (Pause) Probably got tongs on for the same reason I've got them on. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "What would explain the two sets of tongs is that I had Gene's from when he let me off at the ALSEP and, sometime during the close-out, he took the others off the gate for some purpose. And it could be he just did it to have them in case he dropped something."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: And, 17, we're ready for a grav measurement.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yes, sir, Bob. Just cleaning up the Rover. Getting our tongs out of the way (and back on the gate).

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: And for your information, at this heading (of 017), the westernmost battery cover, like I talked about yesterday, is just starting to cover the radiators. [The Sun moves very slowly in the lunar sky, and shadows move only about 12 degrees in 24 hours.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay; cover that...(Correcting himself) Copy that.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, hum-de-dum-de-dum! You know, I think it's another good day's work.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Uh-huh.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay. I dusted all that.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I just knocked as hard as I could, on my feet, several times.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: What you're going to say is you want me to brush you, huh? Let me keep this (gravimeter) out of the way so it doesn't get dusty.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Wonder if our bouncing around that gravimeter is going to disturb it like this. [At 147:59:32, Gene will give Bob a gravimeter reading. On every other occasion, Gene gave Bob a mark when he started the measurement, but not this time. The preceding statement suggests that, at this point, he has already punched the Grav button.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Shouldn't.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Got to do...Well...

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Want me down (off the ladder)?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: You got to do me first.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Yeah. (Jumping down the ladder) Plink.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: You're not nearly as dusty as you were yesterday; you're just dirty, that's all.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Well.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: I think I can get everything off my shoes by banging, if you'll just get my arms. I didn't really fall in much today, except maybe my left arm. But...

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I tell you, (if) we saw some of the things I think we saw today, we both fell in. (Laughs) [Schmitt - "This is a play on words. I meant that finding the orange soil was a lucky break."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Don't. Ow!

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: What? I hurt you?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yeah, you're hitting.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Well, you're right. Sorry. (Laughing) I don't have much control. [Jack is trying to brush Gene because, because of the stiffness of the suit and his general tiredness, what he is actually doing is hitting Gene.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: (Laughing) I know it. That's the way mine (his arm) feels. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: That's dirty. Under there. (Pause) I'm glad they can't see this. (Pause) [Schmitt - "I was referring to the 'intimate' nature of this part of the dusting operation."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, I stand out here and I look at that flag, and I look at the Rover, and I look at those massifs. It's still hard to believe.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: What did we deserve to do...(correcting himself) do to deserve being out here, huh? (Pause) Okay. That's not very good. Let me get some (of the dust on) your PLSS, here. Keep...Go forward just a little.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: This way?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: There you go. (I) think your sharp (Rover) turns are... [Schmitt - "I suspect that what I started to say was that he'd been throwing dust on our suits when he made sharp turns."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Hey, that fender is really a classic.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: (Punning) One might say it's a "young" fender, (because we) just put it on.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Do we need...Do we really need those clamps?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: No. [Gene is referring to the lamps clamps from the LM cabin that they used to fasten the new fender to the Rover. He is wondering if he'll need to take one or both up to the cabin after EVA-3.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: I can't think of anything we need them for. That light...but you can tie that light somewhere...

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: We don't...Well...

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: I might bring one back (in the LM, just in case).

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Yeah. We ought to leave one in tribute. To Dr. Young. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, that orange soil was something.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Huh?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: And the way it went radially down that crater. (Pause) Let me turn, and then take another look, and then I'll...Then you get up there. 147:53:35 Schmitt: You got quite a bit (of dust) around your hoses here.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: My hoses?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Okay, and I don't know what I can do about it, Geno.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, just give it a swat (garbled) front, too.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Well, I got it the best I could. Let me get the top of your LCRU there. [Jack means Gene's RCU .]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Mine's pretty good.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: (Correcting himself) Or, RCU.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yeah, mine's good. Okay. Let me get to your front.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: No, I didn't get your other arm here.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, okay.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I don't know that I can.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: It's the inside arm. I don't have anything on it. [That is, Gene's right arm which, being inboard on the Rover, doesn't get sprayed with as much dust.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: No, that's right. You don't. It isn't. It's about the same.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: When you fall out, you fall out on your other arm. [Gene is referring to his fall at the end of the Scarp Gravimeter stop as he tried to mount the Rover.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: There is some on that leg there.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Don't know what I'm going to do about it. (Pause) I think we're just going to have to make do. [Cernan - "Dusting was a major process. By now, we've already spent 5 minutes dusting."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Let me see what I can do with you. (Pause) Just look at me. (Pause) What is this rock, right here, by the pad!

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I don't know...I.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Did I just turn your comm? Do you still hear me?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Yeah. I've just been intending to mention that (rock) several times. Anybody that lands on a rock ought to have their head examined. Put their ladder (strut right on a rock)...

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Boy, where have you been again today?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Oh, I played some games there around Station 3. (Pause) I'm sorry. [Jack fell several times at Station 3, now known as Ballet Crater because of his performance.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Boy, oh, boy!

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Wasn't intentional.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Whoo.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: But (a) lot of your turns...

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Hold your arm up. Hold your arm up.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Lot of your turns threw dust...

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yeah, I noticed that. (Chuckles)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: ...on me.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: God dang that rock! If I was strong enough, I'd move it. Hey, I am strong enough. That's one we ought to bring home!

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Well, if we can't fill up the LM with anything else.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: That's about the size of the SRC. Stand up on the pad. (Pause) Oh, shoot! First time that's happened. [Cernan - " (Laughing) I just read this and said to myself, 'Now what's the worst thing that could happen.' It's dropping the brush in the dust. So I'm sure that that's what happened. It's just like with the hammer. You've got to hold on tight. And when you brushed, you had to brush hard. Your hands are tired, so you drop it. I'm positive I dropped the dustbrush."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Here, hold on to me. (Long Pause) [Jack is offering himself for Gene to hold onto as he bends to retrieve the brush.] [Schmitt - "I can remember that, by the time I finished trying to dust Gene, that was it for my hands. My fingers and forearms were so fatigued that it was really hard to do anything useful in the dusting operation, because you just couldn't stroke without losing your grip on the brush. There was some pain under your nails because they had lifted off the quick, but mainly you were just fatigued and holding that brush was just the last straw. Gene didn't talk about it as much as

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: I think it is.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: No, I mean you got a couple abrasions right on through the...

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: So do you. I wasn't going to mention them (and risk alarming anybody in Houston).

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Well, these are only a pin-hole thick, but...(Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: All I can say is it's better than walking. [Among its many advantages, the Rover delivers two relatively rested astronauts to each of the geology station. The only fatigue that the Rover ride didn't help with very much was the forearm and finger fatigue, particularly for Jack when he had to carry one of the charges.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, man, I'll tell you, we covered over 20 kilometers today, babe. How'd you like to walk up and down those hills and ditches at 20 kilometers? Okay. Can you...Turn towards me. I want to get the front of your legs one time. (Laughs) Come back.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. And, 17, Houston. How's the dusting coming?

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Man, you've had your day of dusting, haven't you?

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: (Answering Bob ) Well, we're almost there. I'm going to send the LMP in in about a minute.

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: Okay. We're getting to a point where we need...

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Oh, I tell you, I've spent more hours on the dustbrush ...

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: ...where we need to be inside in less than 10 minutes, with the thing (the hatch) closed up.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Yes, sir. We're on our way, Bob. [Cernan - "This didn't mean that lightning was going to strike in ten minutes. If there was something to do and I had to stay out there ten or fifteen minutes longer, I still would have been very comfortable. I knew our margins were very, very conservative and I never had a concern about running out of consumables or having to scramble to get in. It wasn't like the margins we had for fuel to land the LM which you could eat up very quickly. Sometimes we were pushed up against Houston's limits on consumables but, in reality, it was never even close."]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: (To Jack) That takes care of it. Knock (the dust off of) your feet off, Jack. Knock your feet off on the ladder.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Okay. [They've spent 6 1/2 minutes dusting, and will still take a lot of dust into the cabin.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: And don't forget the antennas, guys. [Bob is referring to the antennas on the top of the OPSs which need to be put in the stow position before they crawl through the hatch. On Apollo 15, Scott and Irwin forgot to stow Irwin's (PLSS/OPS) antenna , which then broke off.]

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Okay. I need the pallet. [This is the EVA pallet which contains replacement PLSS batteries and LiOH canisters, and food. Jack is now at the top of LMP-32 .]

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: (Responding to Bob) Oh, Bob, you're a beauty.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: How did you think of that?

A17A1474349.speaker: Parker
A17A1474349.text: John (Young) suggested it.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: John who? (Laughs)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: He strikes again. (To Jack) You'd (have) broke yours off sure, because I wouldn't have seen it as you went up (pause) unless I took inventory with my book, which I'll do here in a minute. (Consulting checklist page CDR-31 ) Open battery covers, taken care of; dusted LCRU; blankets open 100 percent. They've been open 100 percent all day.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Okay.

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: If I can just get up here.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Oh, shoot. I forgot a snap up there (on the antenna tie-down).

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Now, let's make sure we got all of those. I don't want to get hung up on anything.

A17A1474349.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1474349.text: Yeah. I mean I forgot to put the antenna under the snap...under the other thing. (Pause)

A17A1474349.speaker: Cernan
A17A1474349.text: Wait a minute, get the snap. (Pause) Okay. (Did you) get it? (Long Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: The reading is 670, 023, 501; that's 670, 023, 501. [This measurement is listed in the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science report, albeit without a starting time. Because the experimenters took this to be a valid measurement, we can conclude that Gene pushed the Grav button without giving Bob a mark. At 147:42:54 Gene noted that he hadn't started the gravimeter measurement and, between then and now, there is only one statement (at 147:51:09) which can be interpreted to indicate that a measurement had been initiated.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Okay. We got that. Go to Standby. Open the cover and dust the ( TGE ) radiator if it needs it. Or dust the radiator, period.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: It's dusted already; I took care of that. And I'm in Standby.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Final check. (Reviewing CDR-31 ) LRV. Blankets open 100; battery covers, open; samples off. We checked under both seats. Equipment stowed. (Pause to review CDR-32 ) Okay. You're all clean to go in. Okay. Dust SEP, blankets open; verify Power, Off; Recorder, Off. TGE , that's read; that's dusted. Tidy the MESA blankets. They're okay. (Pause) Okay, and I've got this (rock) box to bring up when I go. Okay, let's see. (Probably stepping out of the LM shadow) Oh, man, that (Sun)'s bright...Stow PLSS antenna; brush to ladder hook, EVA pallet to LMP. You got it. The pins are green; and (Grav) r

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Roger. [The S-IVB is the top stage of the Saturn V that boosted them out of Earth orbit for the trip to the Moon.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: SRC-2 is in my hand. The big bag is not required.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Roger that. (Pause) And we're ready to call you all in as you go through the hatch.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Jack's going in with the...(Hearing Bob) Okay, Jack's halfway through it now, and I'm going on up the ladder.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) [Four minutes have elapsed since Bob told them they had ten minutes to get the hatch closed.] [Schmitt - "It seems from listening to the tapes that we never showed any concern whatsoever about ten minutes to go or any other limitation on getting in; and I suspect it's not only that we had certain things we had to get done but, also, we assumed - and which was correct, I think - that there were significant margins in the oxygen and coolant supply."] [Table 9-II gives EMU consumable status for EVAs 1, 2 , and 3 . Both Jack and Gene will consistently use more oxygen and c

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Oh, my; oh me! (To Jack) How you coming?

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Just about there. (Pause) [Carrying the rock box, Gene only has one hand free to grab the ladder as he jumps up to the first rung.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Ohhhh! That's a nice one-handed first step. "Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17". I'm going to keep reading that. I like that message. (Calling to Bob) How's Captain America (meaning Ron Evans), speaking of Apollo 17? [Captain America is a Marvel Comics character who first appeared in March 1941. Publication of the series ended in 1949, had a brief revival in 1953. Captain America had a second revivial in 1964 and, as of late 2005, was still in publication.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Captain America is sound asleep. Just about to come around to AOS (Acquisition of Signal when the Command Module emerges from behind the Moon on the current orbit). We think he's sound asleep.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Hey, how does that always happen? That happened yesterday. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: He got up before noon this morning, too. [Gene and Jack got up on this day at 1:30 p.m., Houston time - a fashionably decadent hour.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Oh, okay. (Pause) Just take it easy, Jack, it'll...Here you go...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Pip pin didn't work. [This is a release pin on the EVA pallet.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Lot of things don't work when your hands get tired; that's the problem. Wasn't a bad day. How long we been out, Bob. Of course, we're still out. [The EVA won't be over until cabin pressure reaches 3.5 psi.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: 7 (hours) plus 27 (minutes), so far.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: 7 plus 27?!

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: (Garbled)

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: How does that grab you? (Pause) Well, we're getting anxious to get you in and get the hatch closed.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: (Garbled under Bob) Well, we understand that.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Jack's unloading the pallet and as soon as it comes out, I'll shove this stuff (the SRC and the two SCBs) in, and we'll be gone. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Just takes a certain amount of time.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Okay, Gene. Are the three SCBs inside the hatch already?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Bob, I don't think any of them are inside. Let's see...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: No.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: ...I've got 8 here and 6 here and we emptied the contents of 4 into the...

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Roger.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: ...SRC, and we emptied the contents of 5 into one of these other two bags. So we've only got two of them here, plus the SRC.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Roger that.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Five went into six.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Roger that.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: And we've got two of them hanging on the tail of the Rover. And I don't know what it is under Jack's seat right now.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Seven is under my seat.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: We copy that. Don't worry about it.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: One more (PLSS) battery (to get off the pallet), Geno, and it's yours.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: You always used to stand and watch me do this, anyway.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Yeah, but we had some long EVAs at the Cape but...(Pause) [Schmitt - "In training, when we went through these procedures, Gene didn't have anything to do. Somebody else handed me the pallet and I went through it, dutifully, simulating unloading and stowing material off the pallet. And, once or twice, we probably did it with the real hardware in the real LM, just to make sure it worked."]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: There you go. [Jack is pushing the empty pallet out through the hatch with his foot.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Just be careful of the...Let me get up there a little farther. Careful of that hatch. Getting to look like a regular garbage dump down there. [Gene has tossed the pallet down to the surface.] 148:04:47 Cernan: Okay. Ready (for an SCB)? (Pause) Sorry, babe.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: It's all right. [Gene may not have pushed the SCB far enough through the hatch for Jack to get it easily. Alternatively, it may have been tipped over.] [Schmitt - "It was hard to lean down to get the things Gene's was handing in."]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Now, this one (an SCB)'s going to come open if we're not careful. Let me see if I've got one more step to go up. No I think that's the last one. I'll just hold it here until you get it. (Pause) I could shove that in if I push it with the SRC. Jack, the cap'll come open. Be careful. (Pause) Okay. Here's that big silver box. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Can you push on that (box) a little bit?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Yup.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay, Bob, you've got the two SCBs - (To Jack) I'll push it in - (the) SRC, and there goes the ETB. [Schmitt - "I may have stuck the SCBs and the rock box on their storage rails to make room for Gene. Either that or I stuck them on the engine cover."] [Cernan - "I'll bet a million dollars that he wasn't stowing those things in the rack until we got into soft suits. It took too much time. The hatch had to go quite a ways open for me to get in so there wasn't much room under his feet, so I've got to believe that he stowed them on the engine cover."]

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Copy that. Now how about a CDR?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: There's only one thing left...(Hearing Bob) That's right, that's the only thing left out here.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Are you on a checklist?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: No, I'm not even on my checklist, but I guess...Yeah, I am; it says "Ingress". Let me knock some more dust off. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Let me get behind the door. [As he had at the end of EVA-1, Jack had the hatch fully open while he was getting the SCBs and other gear stowed. Now, in order to let Gene get in, he has to stand on Gene's side of the spacecraft and swing the hatch closed far enough that he can get over to his side of the spacecraft. He will then open the door against his legs so that Gene can crawl in.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Well, I'm going to take what dust I got in with me. Ohhhh! (Long Pause) 148:07:08 Schmitt: Push. There you go. (Pause) Keep your buttons close (to the floor). You're good. (Pause) Beautiful. Just float in. Hanging up a little on the purse , but that's all right. There you go. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: (Standing up) Ohh!

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: That's my arm I'm getting in the way, there. Let me get out of the way. [There is very little room in the LM for two suited astronauts.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Let me just check that (hatch) seal (for dust) before we close that. Okay. Can you get your arm up? Okay. There's no big rocks in it (the hatch seal), that I can see. Lots of dust on the floor.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Yeah, I think it's okay. Okay, the hatch is partially closed...

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Let me get it. I think it (the checklist) says to lock it, doesn't it?

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Well, we're supposed to close our water first. [They will now use the Post-EVA cue card. The items listed there are also listed on Surface 5-1 .]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. (Reading) " Forward Hatch , Close and Lock; dump valves both Auto, okay; Primary Water, Closed." Let me see if I can't get my (garbled) here.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Here, why don't I get yours and you get mine. [That is, turn each other's feedwater off.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. I just got mine. And if you'll turn, I'll get yours.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: (Softly) You'll have to do that.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: You'll have to put your right arm high; pick it up high. [The PLSS controls are on the bottom, right, front corner. There are actually three controls, each with a very different shape so that they can be distinguished by feel. The outer control is a two bladed nylon lever that controls the PLSS feedwater diverter valve and, therefore, the amount of cooling. Inboard of the diverter valve are two other levers, one to turn on the primary feed and the other to turn on the Aux tank. One is a flat blade and the other is a rod.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Oh, wait a minute.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: No, I can't reach you, Jack, unless you turn...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Don't move yet; don't turn around.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. [Cernan - "It was just incredible in there with two guys in pressurized suits, plus all the stuff on the engine cover. It was just very difficult even to reach behind him."]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Move over to the corner. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: (Make) sure I got the right ones. Far right, far left, secure oxygen. Okay. Your water's Off.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Water's off. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Now, stay there and I'll lock the hatch.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: I've got to get into position to do the other good things (that is, close circuit breakers on the panel on the right side of the cabin and reset ECS valves behind his station). You go ahead. Do you have enough room or do I need to turn?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: No, let me get down there. (Pause) No, I can't...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Let me turn back (and face inboard); get out of your way. Got it?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Hatch is closed and locked.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Okay. And remember, I think it's the overhead valve that you have (garbled) Open.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: That's right.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Yeah, you'll have to move over, Jack, so I can reach it.

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: And you ought to verify both, I guess.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: (To Jack) You're going to have to wait, then. [They hear Bob but don't respond.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Can you reach it now?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. No, you got to swing left...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Well, I'll have to...

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: ...(correcting himself) (swing to Jack's) right.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: I'll have to turn around, then. (Pause) How's that? Any better?

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Nope, you've got to...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay, for some reason I can't put my PLSS toward you.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: No, you can't. Just face front, if you can, and move as far forward as you can. [That way, Gene might be able to lift his arm behind Jack's PLSS and reach the valve.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Well, if I get my...I'm going to have to go all the way around, I guess.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Well, just...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Look, I've got to get the PLSS against the circuit breaker (panel)...

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Wait. I've got you just where I want you. Now stay right there, and shift your weight as far to the right (probably forward) as you can. (Pause)

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay, it's Auto...

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Okay.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: ...and (pause) it's locked. Okay?

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: All right.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Now, (reading) Cabin Repress (valve) , Auto. (Pause) Can't get it. I'll have to turn left, here.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Huh? [Gene is facing inboard and needs to turn left and face more forward so that he can get his arm down behind Jack to get the valve.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Let me turn left.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: No, I can get it.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Cabin Repress, Auto.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: It's Auto.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: And at (panel) 16, Cabin Repress breaker, Closed.

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: Closed.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Master Alarm and Cabin Warning Lights. Cabin's coming up, Bob, 0.5 (psi).

A17A1475932.speaker: Parker
A17A1475932.text: Copy that. (Pause) [The sound of the cabin filling with oxygen can be heard. The alarm and warning lights are expected because, when the Repress circuit breaker is closed, the system detects that the cabin is unpressurized.]

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: I've still got 15 percent oxygen (left in the PLSS).

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. Cabin pressure's increasing. Go " Pressure Regs A and B , Cabin." (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 01 sec )

A17A1475932.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1475932.text: A's Cabin.

A17A1475932.speaker: Cernan
A17A1475932.text: Okay. And your PLSS O2 (oxygen), Off, at cabin (pressure) greater (than) 2.5 (psi). It's there now. And you're probably getting (a) soft suit. (Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. Next thing, Jack, you can start verifying your white dots are out.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay. [They are verifying that all of the LM circuit breakers marked in the checklist with white dots are in the open position.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: And you can use your purge valve to depress, if you have to. [That is, he can remove the purge valve to depressurize the suit if the regulator hasn't done the job.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Well, I don't think I have to. Okay; white dots.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Wait a minute. White dot's plus, for you, EVA decals. [Some of the switches are marked with "EVA" decals to indicate the proper settings.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay, I'm good here, here, here.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: And, 17, congratulations. That was two EVAs and a half (worth of achievement).

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Thank you, Robert, but until I get my helmet and gloves off, I won't say anything. Okay, Jack. On 16, ECS Suit Fan 2, Closed.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Closed. [They are turning on a pair of fans which circulate oxygen through the ECS Suit Circuit.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Suit Fan Delta-P, Closed.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Closed. [And, now, they are turning on a sensor which responds to the pressure difference across the fans.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. Master Alarm just came on. Okay. And the Heaters (in the) MESA, Open. You can Open your MESA Heaters (circuit breaker). We're getting a Master Alarm, Houston. I don't know why.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: I think that's the...

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: You did get Suit Fan number 2?

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: ...Suit Fan Delta-P (sensor).

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. You've got Suit Fan number 2 and Delta-P. Okay ...

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: MESA (heater) circuit breaker is Open.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. That's why it (the alarm) came on; (because the fan isn't up to speed). ECS Caution/Water Sep(arator) component light should go out after that fan comes up. You can doff your glove.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Roger. We think that's what happened.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "Gene doesn't sound as tired as after the first EVA, but he's eager to get the gloves off. I'm sure I was tired, in part because our last stop, at Camelot, was a little tougher, physically, than some of the others because of walking through the boulders."] 148:14:09 Cernan: Well, I never thought I'd wear my EV cover gloves through two EVAs. [Cernan - "These were like golf gloves with no fingers. We wore them to protect the suit gloves against abrasion. They really took a beating. They weren't falling apart, but they were pretty well worn."] [They will take the glo

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Oh, I forgot all about them.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: No, I didn't. I thought about taking them off until I started chipping those boulders. And I'm glad I wore them.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Yeah, I think it's a good idea.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: As hard as it is on your hands, these cover gloves are just ripped to a nub. Glad it's not my gloves. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "I think we had planned to take the cover gloves off after the ALSEP deployment because that was supposedly the major wear. But, it would seem to me that it would have been imprudent to take them off given the way they were wearing. We were pretty active - we were doing lots of stuff - and, every time you gripped something, you were abrading the cover glove with that soil. Gene's wore more quickly than mine because of the brushing and the hammering. Of course, the cover

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: (You) might consider taking them off tomorrow.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Roger, 17. You're talking about your cover gloves?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Yeah. We're still wearing them, Bob. And, I swore (before the flight that) I'd take them off after the drill, but I used a bit of real-time common sense.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Okay.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay. Gloves are off. LMP's gloves are off. Need some help?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Yeah, a bit. (Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: I think you just about got it.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: No, you went the other way.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Did I go the wrong way? Yeah, I did. (Pause) What's wrong with that one?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: I don't know. [Schmitt - "It's hard to tell what was going on here, although it may have had to do with lock rings on Gene's gloves. As I recall, you pressed in on the ring and then turned. It was easy to do for yourself - when your hands weren't tired - but then you had to reverse your mind when you were doing it for somebody else, like tying somebody else's necktie."] [Cernan - "I think there were arrows on the rings. And I do think that that is what we were doing: helping each other because it was cumbersome to unlock your own glove with a gloved hand. Once you got one off, the other one wa

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Shouldn't have done that.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Hey...Let me get this. (Pause) I had them then.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Yeah, I'm sorry.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Well, you get that one, and I'll get these two. Get that one. I'll get this one. (Pause) (Garbled). Hold that thing.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay. Let me try this one, now. (Long Pause) It wants to go.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Let me try that. Yeah, that one (garbled).

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Got it?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Yeah.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: It's usually easier when you do it yourself. The angle's wrong. [Schmitt - "Boy, this is a classic of a discussion between two people who are looking at what they're doing and not communicating with anybody else. Maybe this was the glove lock rings."] [In February 1994, I examined an Apollo suit being prepared for public display at the Johnson Space Center in Houston. Operation of the wrist ring requires pushing, simultaneously, a pair of tabs toward the glove fingers and then, while holding the tabs in place, rotating the wrist ring to unlock it. The tabs are separated by about 2 or 3 inches

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Oh, boy! (Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: (The wrist ring is) starting to get a little stiff.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Oh, they came off. Now, they came off. (Relieved to have the gloves off) Oh, ho, ho, ho. [Cernan - "By the time the mission was all over, my hands were nothing but blisters. The skin on my knuckles was gone. Inside the glove, all the knuckle points were constantly scrapping and, although they hurt, I guess I didn't let it bother me when we were on the surface. You're hands are so vital to everything you do that the gloves were custom fit; but we still ran into these problems. We got down to blue-collar work and you couldn't design everything for the convenience of the astronaut. On the Shuttle

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Okay. Doff helmets, with visors. (Pause) Here; I'll get yours for you. Turn my way, if you can. (Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: I know how you feel.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: I don't know how they're so wet. I don't know whether it's...They're just soaking wet. (Pause) Everything is just twice as hard. [Gene's hands are probably wet.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Now comes the old hay fever, again. [Jack is anticipating having a reaction to lunar dust as he did after EVA-1.]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: That one (visor) up and that one down. (Pause) "Stow (helmets) in BRA". Let's get mine off, though. (Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (Garbled) Velcroed... Well, these things are off. Oh, man. Does that (dust) smell, doesn't it? You sure can pick that up. [Cernan - "There was a definite smell of spent gunpowder. I'll never forget that."]

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay. You got yours?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: I've got mine. (Pause) Okay, Bob. Now, (chuckles) helmets and gloves are off.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: (Cabin) pressure looks good, still. (Long Pause)

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Hello, Houston. Do you read?

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Roger, 17. Read you loud and clear, Challenger.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Very good, Robert. The helmets and gloves are off.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Absolutely outstanding crew, there.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Why don't you go home and get some sleep, Bob?

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Absolutely outstanding. I can't say more than that. And I mean it from the bottom of my heart (pause) or the bottom of my soul or something, my conscience.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Thank you, Bob. Well, it's all (of) ours. [Schmitt - "I meant that it was the achievement of the whole Apollo team."]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Bob, it's all your good training and help...

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: 7 (hours) plus 37 (minutes), from 3.5 (psi) to 3.5.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: As mission scientist, you're totally responsible.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: And the backup crew (Young and Duke) says that you are even better than outstanding.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Remember, it's in your contract. (Hearing Bob; laughs) Well, thank you. We enjoyed it.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Hey, I'll turn you over to Little Joe (Allen), here...

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: Ohhh, boy!

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: ...while I go talk to some people.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Thanks again, Bob. We... [Journal Contributor Brian Lawrence notes that, although Joe Allen is not very tall, the nickname "Little Joe" also comes from the character of "Little Joe Cartwright" in the very popular TV Western series "Bonanza".]

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: We've got a 9 and 1/2 hour EVA scheduled for you tomorrow. We're planning to spend 2 and 1/2 hours extra over there at Station 4 (at Shorty Crater).

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (Laughing) I hope those gloves that you've got packed in the back have got something in them (that is, a cold beer). (Laughing) Oh, let's read the checklist. See if we can go to bed on time tonight.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Oh, man.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: Okay. That might be a change.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: I feel better than I did last night, as a matter of fact.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (To Jack) Turn that light on.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: I'm going to turn you over to Joe.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: That (light) didn't do very much good.

A17A1481224.speaker: Parker
A17A1481224.text: See you guys tomorrow.

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (To himself) Okay. "Verify safety on dump valve." Yes.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay, Bob. Get some sleep, huh?

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (To himself) Yeah, I verified them both.

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: (To Bob) Sorry to be touchy, occasionally. [Schmitt - "I was referring to the times when I was annoyed with Parker, such as at Station 3."]

A17A1481224.speaker: Cernan
A17A1481224.text: (To Jack) "Descent Water Valve, Open."

A17A1481224.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1481224.text: Okay. (Pause) Water Valve's Open. 148:20:55 Cernan: Okay. Then you can take your purge valve off. (Pause) There's a little dust in that (purge valve fitting) tonight. Little stiffer. Wiped that out again. (Reading) "Remove purge valves, stow in purse . Disconnect OPS hoses." [They are removing the purge valves for cleaning. With the purge valve removed, the port in the suit is closed.]
