A17A1633344.text: That clip got away. Come towards...(Come back) in the cabin just a little. There.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay?

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Wait a minute. Okay. I got it. (Pause) Okay, you're in good shape. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, I'm on the porch. Whoo! I'm still at 4.3! [Cernan - "It was a strain getting out. It was easier for Jack because there was only one person and his suit's had longer to come down. I'm still at 4.3, here, with a very stiff suit."]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Roger. We agree on that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, I'm on the porch, Bob.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Copy that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: (To Bob) Okay, what do you want? What can I do for you, Bob? [Here, Jack is not talking louder to Bob than he is to Gene.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Standby Jack. We'll get a word to you in one minute. (Pause) 163:39:18 Cernan: Okay, Jack, in the...Well, I guess I ought to wait. (Pause) Get my L. E. C. ready for you. Okay. And everything looks normal on me, right now. Wait 'til I get pressure down a little bit. (Pause) Everything's normal, except a part of my nose itches I can't get to. [Schmitt - "We had a piece of Velcro put on the inside of the helmet that we reached over and scratched our nose on. Everybody seemed to agree that you needed that. Also, the mention of the LEC reminds me of a lot of work we did - probably pre-Apollo 11 and

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: I'll give you the jett(ison) bag anyway, Geno, while they're thinking.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I guess that's part of R&D (Research and Development). (Pause) Oh, yes, the jett bag . Santa Claus' bag again.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Jack. We'd like to have you stay in just a minute or so longer. We're trying to keep track here of the suit circuit pressure and see if it stabilizes or starts to drop. The one reg(ulator) has just has been intermittently leaking. We still haven't isolated it. And we think we've got it shut off, but we're still watching it. So bear with us just a minute or so.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: I'm bearing, Bob. [Before the rest period, Houston had run a series of checks on the Demand Regulators to see if one or the other of them had a slow leak that would explain a slow but steady rise in the cabin pressure. During the tests, the pressure build up stopped and, as Joe Allen told the crew at 150:46:46, apparently the leak had been cured by cycling the regulators.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Hey, what else...

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: I thought you isolated it last night. (To Gene) Okay. Let me give you the ETB.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Yeah. (Pause) Give me that and I'll be on my way, working on the TGE (the traverse gravimeter). Okay, got it. [Gene is on cuff checklist page CDR-4. After starting a gravimeter reading, he will change the LCRU battery, getting the new battery from under his seat, where he stowed it at the start of EVA-2.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Jack, and how about taking the Suit Circuit Relief Valve , cycle it just to Open and then back to Auto. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Bob, stand by. (Pause) Suit Circuit Relief going Open, then Auto. (Pause) That's done.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, we'll watch it for a minute here and let you know.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Bob. I'm going down the ladder.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Roger, Geno. (Long Pause) [Jack is probably verifying the circuit breakers and performing his other tasks on LMP-4 .]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Yup, still there, Jack. "Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17."

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Good.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Amen there, Gene. Amen. [Cernan - "It had become a little prayer at the start of those EVA's. I just shouted to the world, "God, bless us. Give us a shot at it." I'm beginning to think that there wasn't anything printed or written anywhere on that ladder. And if Jack doesn't recall it, it wasn't there. I think I just decided to say that when we started every EVA. Sort of like blessing the shrimp fleet."] [The only sure way of knowing if the message was on the ladder or strut is to visit the expended Descent Stage at Taurus-Littrow. Gene first "reads" the message at the end of EVA-1 at 124:00:0

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Bob, I'm on the (foot)pad. And it's about 4:30 (on) a Wednesday afternoon, as I step out on to the plains of Taurus-Littrow. Beautiful valley. The first thing I'll do is I'll turn the TGE (Traverse Gravimeter) on, and I'll give you a reading.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay; we're ready.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: And I'm very much interested in my Rover battery (temperature).

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: And, Jack, you're Go for exit and looks like we've got it taken care of.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, and I'm checking the circuit breakers. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: It (the TGE )'s on and (I'm pushing the) Read (button). Bob, it reads 222, 262, 207; 222, 262, 207.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, I copy that, Geno. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (To himself) Okay, get the visor down, Geno. Get the visor down...Holy Smoley. Think it'd be better to leave it up. Beautiful out here today, Bob! We can look to the east for a change - a little bit, anyway.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, copy that, Gene.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Because of) the higher Sun angle. (Pause) Okay, I'll get the LCRU battery changed out.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay. And as you walk by there, if you walk by in the right side of the Rover, how about giving us a SEP temperature readout, please. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: SEP temperature is 103 degrees.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Copy, 103.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: 103, and the mirror is still clean.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Copy that. (Pause) [The SEP temperature was 112 degrees Fahrenheit (44 Celsius) when Gene turned the unit off at 147:18:35.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Well, let's see if I can change this little baby now. Supposed to be simple. (Pause) Bob, we have no use for the old (LCRU) battery, right? [Gene is asking if he can have some fun and see how far he can throw the battery.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: That's affirm. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "During Apollo, the answer to Gene's question was very simple: you weren't going to go back there any time soon. But at a lunar base, any used material will have to be inventoried, catalogued, and stored in some kind of recoverable way because the value of practically any material will, because of transportation costs, be very, very high - at least until the Moon is self-sufficient and is producing it's own stuff. And that won't be for a long time. You're just never going to know when you're going to want to get something and, with a good inventory system

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay. I'm on the porch and the hatch is closed.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (To himself) Oh! Don't bump into that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Are you talking to me or you?

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I'm talking to me. (Long Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, that sounds familiar and looks familiar - the old plains.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: The valley of the Taurus-Littrow.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Want me to get your antenna?

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Yes, let me get that...

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: I'll come over there.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I'll get the TV on. I've already got the battery changed. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Static ends) (Checking that the high-gain antenna is pointed at Earth There's the Earth right in the middle of the antenna (sighting scope). Okay, verify (LCRU) Mode 3; I am in Mode 3; LCRU blankets are open 100 percent, battery covers I'm closing, the battery...Let me close it. Yeah, you can come and get my (PLSS/OPS) antenna .

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Wait a minute. Let me set this down. [TV on. Jack has probably brought the ETB over from the ladder. As per CDR-4, Gene probably left it hanging from the LEC.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Yeah, okay. (Pause) Video Clip ( 3 min 24 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, stay there.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I was just trying to.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay, your antenna's up. Wait a minute. (Garbled) snap the snap. [ Fendell briefly picks up Jack at the gate, then pans clockwise.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Didn't mean to do that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Chuckling) That's all right. I can't get close enough to you. There you are. (Pause) Lean a little more. (Pause) Antenna's up. Let me get the snap.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: And, 17, if you guys are interested, your shadows will be 8 feet long tonight.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: How many meters is that, Bob?

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I'll draw it out...I'll step it out for ya. You can measure it. (Laughter) 163:48:11 Schmitt: Well, I don't know. Should I take my gloves off? I mean my cover gloves.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Why don't you leave them on for a while and see where we're going. See what the boulder field looks like up there (at Station 6).

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Well, I know what it's going to look like.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: No, you don't.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: The point is: my hands will be much better off without them. [The cover gloves add bulk to the hands, lessen flexibility, and hasten fatigue.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Take them off, then. (Long Pause) Okay, battery covers are closed and tight. High-gain is already oriented. Oh, they've even got TV, I guess.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: That's affirm. [Gene can see the TV camera move as Fendell does his pan.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: (Garbled) [Fendell finds Gene leaning across his seat, pushing in the circuit breakers on the instrument panel. Gene is at the bottom of CDR-4 and Jack is taking care of the tasks on LMP-5 .]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: And, Geno, when you push the Rover circuit breakers in, how about giving us a battery temperature reading on the Rover bats.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Tell them what my batteries are reading if I can.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Well, let me see if I can do something else while I'm waiting.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: No, I'm done, Jack. (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: I'll get the old SEP receiver. [Jack goes to the SEP, behind his seat; Fendell follows him.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Well, Bob, battery 1 is 95 degrees and battery 2 is reading zero. So we got a gauge failure. In fact, it's not reading zero; it's off scale low. [Jack reaches back for his cooling control without having to do the double wave.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay, copy that. That's a real cool-down, isn't it? Okay, Jack, if you're going to worry about the SEP, standby and don't do the SEP until after you worry with the ETB, and we'll get to you on that. When you get the ETB to the (CDR) seat, I'll talk to you about it. [Gene goes to the gravimeter, which is on the ground near the LM ladder. Jack goes around the back of the Rover to Gene's seat.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, 102 is the temperature. Video Clip ( 3 min 10 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay; copy that. [The temperature at the end of EVA-2 close-out - at 147:18:35 - was 112ºF. The unit turns itself off when the temperature is over 108ºF, so they will get a little data on the traverse to Station 6 before the unit heats up again.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Bob. Mark.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Mark.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Mark gravimeter; it's flashing. 163:50:04 Parker: Copy that. [Gene is now on CDR-5 .]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, we'll take the big bag. I hope we can keep it on (the gate). (Pause)

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Did you say (garbled under Bob)...

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay. A couple of things on that, Geno. You might try tapping the thing (meaning the bag latch) to see if that loosens the dust. There's also the hook business on the inside of the pallet that you could hook it (the big bag) on. Caution: if you open the pallet, be careful not to knock the clamps off the fender. But you can also reach over the pallet to put the big bag on. [Gene arrives at the Rover carrying both the dustbrush and the big bag. The big bag has the same top cross-section as an SCB but is about twice as long and can be seen in AS17-143- 21924 , taken at about 169:13. Usually, Gene

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, Bob. I brushed it and tapped it (the bag latch) yesterday. I'm not sure we're going to have much luck with them. [Gene is referring to the bag latches on the back of the Rover gate.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Say again there, Gene.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Trying to hang the big bag on the gate) I brushed them and tapped them yesterday.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay; copy that. You might want to put the big bag on the inside of the pallet there, if you can't operate them.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay. [Gene goes out of the TV picture toward the front of the Rover.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, mag Kilo goes on the 500; is that correct?

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: That's affirm. [Fendell pans clockwise to Jack at Gene's seat; he is putting film magazines in the seatpan, taking them from the ETB.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay, I've got Mary and Franny and Nancy (pause) and Donna (pause) and Bobbie and...

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Now standing at Jack's right) Jack, I'm also going to keep this (the dustbrush ) in there (under the seat).

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: ...Karen. [The magazines are marked with letters - MM, FF, and so on. At times through the mission - beginning at 118:15:29 - Jack has used girls names such as Franny for the magazines rather than the standard communications code words like Foxtrot. Bob has followed his lead but Gene won't join in the game until the end of Station 6.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Because it's too hard to get (the dustbrush off the front end). We'll find a place for that in there. [Gene is having trouble getting the brush in and out of the bracket on the top of the LCRU.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: (Not convinced that this is a good thing to do) Well...Okay. [Schmitt - "I may have been thinking that we didn't want any more dust under the seat."]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: It's just too hard to get off the front end. Okay, let's see. "Big bag to gate, dustbrush to (LCRU)..." Let me get that big bag on the inside of the gate if I can. Inside the gate or the pallet, Bob?

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Inside the pallet. My fault there.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: (Showing Cernan his checklist) That says the pallet.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: (Going to the gate) Yeah.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: And if you open the pallet, be careful of the (fender) clamp. Probably, if it's feasible, we suggest you reach across in front of the pallet. Reach across the pallet to do it instead of opening it because of the clamps on the fender.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: It's not feasible. It's not feasible to do that. I got to open it, plus our hook is over center. Let me get something to work on that with. (Pause) You know, Bob, how that pallet locking hook can be out of the little C-shaped release in there? It is.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Oh, boy. Video Clip ( 3 min 12 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I noticed that yesterday. (Pause) 163:53:15 Parker: Jack. When you get done with the ETB, then you might save the grey tape out. We're going to use a little bit of that on the SEP when you get done. (Pause) [Fendell takes a close-up look of Jack working in Gene's seatpan. In the background, Gene swings the geopallet open.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: When are you going to do that?

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: We'll turn the...

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: What am I supposed to do, stand...Well...

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: We'll turn both switches on when you're out at the SEP transmitter.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Well, the tape is in the CDR's seat, and it'll still be there.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: No, we'd like to take the tape from the CDR's seat and use it on the SEP, right now.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: Okay. (Pause) You want me to do it or Gene to do it? [Jack removes the roll of tape and lowers Gene's seat.] 163:54:13 Parker: Why don't you do it since the tape is there. No, let's let Gene do it. Doesn't really matter. Whoever wants to. [Jack takes the ETB to the MESA. Fendell follows him.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: Okay, we'll get it. (Pause) Okay, Bob, the big bag is on the inside of the pallet.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay; we copy that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: I want it...Ooh! The...(Talking to himself) And I know why. (Pause) [Gene goes to Jack's seat; Jack goes from the MESA to the gate. The next task listed on his checklist is a pan taken 30 feet out in front of the ladder.]

A17A1633344.speaker: Cernan
A17A1633344.text: This is the thing that's in the way, Jack. (To himself; discarding a thin, two-foot-long object) Get rid of this thing. We don't need it anyway. (To Bob) Okay, opening and closing of the pallet didn't interfere at all with those fenders.

A17A1633344.speaker: Parker
A17A1633344.text: Okay; copy that.

A17A1633344.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1633344.text: (To Gene) These aren't clamped now. Here's your tape.

A17A1635745.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1635745.text: Okay. Thank you. (Pause) [Fendell pans to Gene, who is mounting sample bags on Jack's camera.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Okay. And, Gene, if you got time there with the camera...when you get done with the camera...how about getting some grey tape and we'll put you to work on SEP for about a minute.

A17A1635745.speaker: Cernan
A17A1635745.text: The SEP receiver?

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: That's affirm. (Pause) And if you get...

A17A1635745.speaker: Cernan
A17A1635745.text: Stand by. Let me finish with SCB-7 here. [Gene reaches into Jack's seat pan for a core-cap dispenser.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Okay. And did you get Jack's camera fixed last night? I didn't hear.

A17A1635745.speaker: Cernan
A17A1635745.text: (Going to the gate with the core cap dispenser) Yeah, we did. (Pause; returning to Jack's seat with the core caps) Okay, there is already one (core-cap dispenser) on the gate. Leave that one there (in Jack's seat pan). Okay, (reading quickly) SCB-7 to gate; 20-bag dispenser on commander's camera. We'll do it when he (Jack) gets back (with the camera); 20 bags on the LMP's camera; core cap dispenser to gate. There's one there (on the gate), there's one under the (LMP) seat. Short can's under the LMP's seat. (Pause, turning to CDR-6 ) Okay, I got to put that cap dispenser on him; I got to give h

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Stand by. I think 8 went in (to the cabin after EVA-2 with SCB-6). Either 4 or 6. No, excuse me; either 5 or 4. [Gene goes to the gate; Jack goes to the cosmic ray experiment, which is hanging beyond the ladder.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Cernan
A17A1635745.text: Okay. We'll put either 4 or 5 on there. Okay. I'll have to wait until he gets back. What do you want? Or let me give you TGE reading and get that out of the way and then I'll work on your SEP. [Gene goes to the TGE at the LM ladder.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Okay; copy that. (Pause)

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Okay; copy that, Gene. Thank you. (Long Pause) [Gene takes the TGE to the Rover and mounts it at the right rear, behind the SEP.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Cernan
A17A1635745.text: Fender wrinkled up in the Sun a little bit last night. RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (10 min 54 sec)

A17A1635745.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1635745.text: Okay, Mark it. The cosmic ray (experiment) is terminated.

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Copy that. Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1635745.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1635745.text: And, Bob, I took two 5-foot stereopairs of the (cosmic ray) configuration. [These are AS17-21381 to 21384. The first two show the "Sun" component of the detector and the other two show the "Shade" component.]

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Copy. And we'll stick it in the ETB and just hang it there.

A17A1635745.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1635745.text: Yep. And in case you're wondering, and so you don't confuse it with a rock, it's in (sample) bag 106.

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Copy that. [Jack goes to the MESA; Gene to the SEP receiver.] 164:00:57 Cernan: Okay. What do you want done to the SEP?

A17A1635745.speaker: Parker
A17A1635745.text: Okay. Take some grey tape over to the receiver, Gene. And with reference to the fact that there is some Velcro missing on the front there which hold the covers down, we'd like to tape the two covers together in the middle there - you know, where the two sides overlap in the middle of the box. Tape those two together. A short piece about an inch long should do it if they are clean. [Fendell examines the LM.]

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640106csm.text: Well, I doubt if the tape will stick because it doesn't (stick) on dust, but I might be able to go over it with one piece to clean it and another piece to tape it. [Schmitt - "You could dust the SEP mirrors, but you really couldn't get the dust out of the cover. So the tape wouldn't stick to the cover to hold it closed."] 164:01:35 Parker: Okay. And the question beyond that: is there Velcro to hold one of those flaps down or not?

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640106csm.text: Okay, so the Velcro is missing from both flaps, I take it.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640106csm.text: Bob, what happened was that the tape (means "adhesive") that held the lower Velcro on there apparently came loose, and it stuck to the upper Velcro.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640106csm.text: Okay. I understand that. In that case, we'd like to take a piece of tape and tape the cover down to keep it closed when it's supposed to be closed. The feeling is that if the cover flaps partly open, you may get specular reflection off the inside of the Mylar down onto the mirrors causing it to heat up during the drive when it's supposed to be closed.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1640106csm.text: Houston, America here. Sorry, but I didn't have my hat on.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640106csm.text: Okay, we'll give it a try. [Fendell finds Gene at the SEP.]

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640106csm.text: Okay; thank you. (Pause) And, Jack, if you're done, you might go rescue EP number 5 from the (LM) footpad, and we'll put it under the LMP's seat.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640106csm.text: Well, there are a lot of other things under there. Okay. I'll rescue it; we'll see where the best place to put it is.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640106csm.text: (At the gate, to Gene) Hey, I got bags on you. I got bags on your camera, Geno.

a17_1640106csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640106csm.text: Okay, we're going to put those two bags on the rear there on our PLSSs? [Jack leaves the gate; Fendell pans up to find Earth.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay. All set for a Flight Plan update here.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640550csm.text: It doesn't matter to us. I just wanted to make sure that we know what you are so we don't let you get away too far (from the Rover) with two uppers and a lower. Two lowers and an upper is certainly better than two uppers and a lower. As long as we know what it is. [The lower drive tubes have a reinforced tip for driving into the ground. An extra upper would be far less useful than an extra lower, because a lower could be used to get a single core sample while an upper can only be used with a lower in getting a double core sample. The core tubes are marked with prominent L's and U's on the tops

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay. It's two lowers and an upper.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640550csm.text: Got that.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Two lowers and an upper.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Man, I'm confused. (To Jack) Okay. When you're ready, I'll configure you.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay, here, let me get this on you first since I got...

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay. [Fendell pans down to find Gene and Jack still at the left side of the Rover. Gene is on CDR-6 and Jack is on LMP-7 .]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: And I'm going to ask you to turn a 180 degrees because you're up on a hill. I'll never be able to do it. [Gene turns to face the Rover; Jack attaches SCB-7 to the left side of his PLSS.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: How's that? I'm down in a hole now.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: That's beautiful. (Pause) Okay, just a minute. Can't get this fixed. (Long Pause) Tallest man on the Moon right now. [Schmitt - "Gene is several inches taller than I am and reaching up to that level was tough in the suit."] [An alternate interpretation is that, with Gene in a hole and Jack on a little rise, Jack is above Gene slightly and is laying claim to the title. Certainly, this would be in character. The TV camera angle makes this a difficult call.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay, that's done.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay?

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Just a second. Let me close the cover. (Pause) Not a very good cover. Okay. [Gene goes to the gate; Jack follows and presents his right side.] Video Clip ( 4 min 01 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 40 Mb MPEG )

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay, Bob, I'm going to put SCB-4 on Jack. (Pause)

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay. That's to be - Okay. It's a Verb 49 to 142, 269, and 359, and that's for the pass where we pull film through there, huh?

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Go ahead.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1640550csm.text: Say again there, Gene. SCB-6? (Gets corrected by somebody in Houston) SCB-4; copy.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: SCB-4 will go on Jack. Okay, Jack, I got to get these PLSS straps, too. Did you get mine?

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Uh...

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: The harness release straps?

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Oh, no. Let's do that. I saw them as you got out, and then I forget about them.

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Yeah. Okay, yours is on over here. Probably a better time to do them, anyway, rather than when we go out. Okay, let me get the bag. I'll get the other one when I configure your other side. (Pause) Okay, you're on. Okay, want to get my PLSS straps? Then I'll be cleaned up, and then I finish your other side. (Pause) [They are behind the gate; Jack is working on the right side of Gene's PLSS.] [Schmitt - "All the equipment was on the back of the Rover, so that's where we stood. And, unfortunately, that meant that we did most of this Geoprep work out of sight. It's too bad we didn't think about th

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1640550csm.text: Yeah, you bet. I don't know what it is yet, but [laughter].

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1640550csm.text: Let me get the other one. (Pause) Warmer out here today. (Pause) Heat treatment on the hands. Okay. [They are thirty-six minutes into the EVA.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay, stay right where you are so I can get this. (Long Pause) [Gene gets the rammer from the gate; Jack presents his left side.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay. Now come over here, and I'll get you a core-cap dispenser, which I left here. (Pause) [They go to Jack's seat; Gene gets the core caps and stows them in a pocket on Jack's SCB.]

a17_1640550csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1640550csm.text: Okay, (reading CDR-6 ) you got SCB-4; you got the cap; you got the rammer; I'll take the hammer. You got the...That's all you need. TGE is on the LRV. Okay, what charge you got there, Jack?

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Okay. 164:11:18 Cernan: And you might want to take a couple...(Long Pause; static, even over Bob) [Jack's pictures of Gene are AS17-140- 21388 to 21391 . They show Gene's RCU, the "red apple" at the end of his purge valve release cable, his right thigh pocket, and his left calf pocket. A detail from 21391 shows the OPS activator on the left side (from our perspective), the label at the lower right for the push-to-talk switch, and the camera mount attachment hardware at left center.]

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: 17, Houston. We think somebody lost their comm. Jack, it's probably Gene going to zero. (Pause)

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: (Static clears) You read us, Bob?

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Roger. Read you now.

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Bob, do you read Gene?

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: (Making a mis-identification) Reading you, Jack. I haven't heard Gene yet.

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Well, Gene's calling you.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: You read me?

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: How do you read me, Bob?

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Okay, read you now.

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Okay, I didn't do anything. I just jiggled my Mode switch here. Okay, (reading CDR-6 again) we got 2 and 3 on the EP's (that is, EP's number 2 and 3), plus one under Jack's seat. LCRU blankets are opened 100 percent; battery covers are closed; dustbrush , I've got; TGE , I've got; mags and polarization filter is taken care of; and I'm ready to traverse to the SEP.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Roger. We understand TV stowed and you're taken care of in the comm. And you might give us a Rover readout either now or when you get to the SEP.

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Okay; we'll see which is convenient. [Gene is now on CDR-7 . Jack has left for the SEP transmitter. He is on LMP-7 .]

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Yeah. (At the) SEP is probably more convenient while you're sitting there waiting for the Nav to warm up or initialize - waiting for us to give you the reading.

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Okay, taking your TV. (Pause) Mode switch is 1.

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Hey, Bob, are you watching LMP?

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Not any more he (meaning Ed Fendell) isn't. I took the TV.

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Okay. (Pause) [Schmitt - "My guess is that I wanted them to record or time my running motion as I was going out to the SEP transmitter."]

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Bob, you still read?

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear. We aren't watching the LMP.

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Okay, I just wondered because I just took the TV. I just want to make sure we got comm here.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Yeah, we're reading you in Mode 1. [At the end of EVA-2 at 147:42:11, Gene turned the LCRU off and lost comm with Houston. The problem was Houston's and, here, Gene is just making sure.]

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: And, for your information, we've both got our cover gloves off.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Copy that. (Pause) [Jack removed his cover gloves at about 163:48:27 and Gene took his off, on-camera, at 164:04:58.]

A17A1641107.speaker: Cernan
A17A1641107.text: Okay, that's in, that's in, that's in. Should have dusted my checklist on the Rover. I can't read down there. [Gene is trying to read a decal affixed to the console. It has a list of Rover start-up procedures.] 164:14:15 Schmitt: Bob, the old tape fix on the SEP (solar panel)'s still working.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Beautiful.

A17A1641107.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1641107.text: Both mirrors (means solar panels) have a little angular displacement, but not more than 5 degrees.

A17A1641107.speaker: Parker
A17A1641107.text: Sounds like that's the least of the SEP's problem, but we have hope. (Long Pause) [During the SEP transmitter deployment at the end of EVA-1, Jack had found that the wire springs that normally hold the two side solar panels open and flat weren't going to do their job. He and Gene then used grey duct tape on the backs of the panels to hold them open. Here, Jack is reporting that, while the side panels aren't lying perfectly flat, the loss in electrical power will be negligible. Jack takes a stereopair of the transmitter, AS17-141- 21510 and 21511. Note the tape along the upper edge with both en

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1641449csm.text: Well, I'm just trying to match my color wheel with Crisium, and nothing matches.

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1641449csm.text: Rog. Seems a few other people have found that, too.

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641449csm.text: (To Gene, who is orienting the Rover for a Navigation initialization) Okay, you're going to be over there, huh? (Pause) (To himself) I'll go over here. (Pause) [Training photo 72-H-1410 shows Jack at the SEP transmitter.]

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641449csm.text: Oh, nothing. That roll indicator isn't worth a ding-dong. (It) says I'm rolled 10 degrees. [Cernan - "It was pretty obvious to me that I wasn't rolled ten degrees, and I just ignored it, I guess."]

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641449csm.text: Okay. (To Bob) Roll zero, pitch is zero; heading is 291; distance, 001; range, 000; amps hours are 90 and 85; volts are 65 (and) 65; Sun shaft device, by the way, is 0.

a17_1641449csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1641449csm.text: Okay. I'll see. I was - I was wondering about that, really.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1641910csm.text: You know, the Crater Dawes has got - starting from the top going down the rim, there's a kind of a light-tan layer, it's a concentric layer that goes all the way around; and then you come into a lighter - it's almost to the white that it looks like on the hills and all round the landing site. And this first layer goes down maybe - let's see, as you look at the total distance in there, about a third of the distance; and then the white layer - concentric layer that goes all the way around, and this is in the western wall I'm looking at now, and it goes down to - to about a half of the distance,

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay, you want the (SEP) receiver on...

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Roger. Both...

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: ...and taped down again, huh?

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Yeah, (garbled).

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Roger. Both the receiver and the recorder on, both switches on and then tape the cover down. 164:19:32 Schmitt: Okay, good luck. (Pause) I don't know if that tape is going to hold. Okay, On and On. (Pause) Okay, it's taped down more or less.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Thank you.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: And then I guess I'm supposed to get on, huh?

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Roger on that.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay, Bob, Nav Reset is now Off and I'm all zeroed up.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. Copy that. And we're ready for you guys to roll.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: (To Bob) Okay, what's the first range and bearing to the Rover sample, past Jones? [A sketch traverse map is shown (identically) on LMP-8 and CDR-8 . As with the prior traverses, Gene and Jack have identical checklist pages. The feature named "Jones" is a cluster of small craters about one kilometer south of the large crater Henry and slightly west. Jack named it for John-Paul Jones, the Scottish-born naval hero of the American Revolution. Unlike other features names which are typed in the checklist maps, this one is written in by hand, although not by Jack.]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay, it will be 185 (on the heading) and 1.5 on the range.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay, 185 and 1.5. 185 and one-and-a-half. Okay. (Pause) [Note that this sample location is not indicated on the checklist map. It is, however, listed in the traverse text on LMP/CDR-9. The location relative to the planned landing spot is 192/1.6 and the 7 degree difference in bearing is a result of Houston's estimate that SEP transmitter is 200 meters east of the planned location. The actual distance is 260 meters.]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Excuse me, Gene.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: No problem. (Pause) [Cernan (laughing as he thinks about it) - "This was probably the first time Jack said "Excuse me" since we got assigned to the crew! Record that for posterity. Obviously, old Twinkletoes, when he jumped on the Rover, probably almost knocked me out (of the Rover). I'm sure that's what happened. But I got even. When I drove on the sides of hills, I always put him on the bottom side. Always! On every hairpin turn, we went around with him on the bottom side."]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Well, shoot. (Pause) I've forgotten how (to get on the Rover).

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Boy, that Challenger looks pretty from here, you know it.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Yep. (Pause) Okay, I'm on.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Did I want a charge? No.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Nope.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: No charge, Jack; no charge.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. Got it. Got it.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. 185 and 1.5 and I'm going to head on about 012. We ought to go right through Jones. (Garbled) Jones.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay, and, Gene, remember the driving fairly slow - or fairly well controlled - the first 300 meters, and a "mark" at the end of the antenna. (Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Watch that, Jack, watch that antenna lead...Uh-oh. (Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Keep going. (Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: (What does it) look like to you?

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay so far; keep going. Okay, let's do that again...

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Yep. But a little different. [Cernan - "We were supposed to drive parallel to the antenna lead and I probably got too close to it and it was easy enough to do a 360 (degree turn and go back) and do it again."]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1641910csm.text: Roger, Ron. Did you tie in some of that ejecta material to the layer at the very bottom of the crater, like an overturned flap or something?

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: I'll pick up that same spot, I can see right where I was. (Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. Give us another mark when you start up on that side.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. We'll give you a hack, Bob. (Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1641910csm.text: The ejecta material is about the - Yeah, that the - Okay, here we come on - Well, it's an odd angle, but I guess it will work. Good. I want to get some of the - 30 and let's see. The first one started at Tacquet. I'm going to whip her back one and get one of - back the other way, because that's kind of a change in - in the color. The color of the area changes right at the Tacquet Rille to - to the brown - browns. This - I forgot my little "gouge," here. It goes north of Malinius [sic], doesn't it?

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Ahh...You're a little...

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Yeah, I'm right on the track. Same tracks exactly.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Well, okay.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: That's exactly...I just came right over. Okay, we're starting Bob. Mark it.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Copy that. (Long Pause)

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: We can't go too far in this heading. We've got a big hole up here.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1641910csm.text: You come up Tacquet, and then you go right near Bessel E, up in - you follow those ridges along into Bessel, there; Bessel E, rather.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: Okay. [This is the large, unnamed feature north of the SEP.]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1641910csm.text: Like a big one. (Pause) Wonder if that's Rudolph? [Gene is referring to a Poppie-sized crater on the northwest rim of the unnamed crater. It is not Rudolph .]

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1641910csm.text: Well, let's see, this is east...Looks awf(ul)...It's a double crater but it's much bigger than I thought Rudolph would be.

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1641910csm.text: No, if you're where you think you are, you're east of Rudolph quite a ways. MP3 Audio Clip ( 14 min 40 sec )

a17_1641910csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1641910csm.text: And you cross just a little...

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Gee, I think you ought to know where we are by now, Bob.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Roger that. [It is a little curious that no one has yet told them that Houston thinks they landed just north of Poppie. Bob will, however, tell them in just a few moments.]

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Maybe that's Lewis and Clark. [Meriwether Lewis and William Clark explored the drainages of the Missouri and Columbia Rivers in the years immediately following the 1803 Louisiana Purchase. The pair of craters named for them is about a kilometer NW of the current Rover position.]

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: After you give me a mark there, I'll talk to you about it.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: I'm sorry, Bob. I guess you didn't hear it. We're passed the end of the antenna and we're headed northeast.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Okay, I...

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: That screw you up?

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Did you give me a mark when you started or a mark when you passed the antenna?

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: I gave you a mark when I started and it took about 20 seconds to get to the end.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Is that good enough or do you want me to go back?

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: No. No. Press on. And, Jack, if you look at your contour map there, we think you are located right now at approximately where the P in SEP is, just below the P in "Poppy". (Note that the map has the crater name mis-spelled.) In which case you're probably driving through that little crater that's just to the northeast there.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Okay. [Houston now has them accurately located. Bob is referring to the contour map on the back of the 1/25000 traverse map labeled "NE Sheet", meaning the northeast of four maps showing the area around the LM. If he is giving them a LM location, it is quite accurate. The "little crater" is the unnamed, shallow feature north of the actual SEP location.]

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: That's probably the one you came upon.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Not very little, though. (Pause) 164:24:50 Schmitt: Okay, Bob. Boy, I wish I could see a little bit better. (Pause) The major boulders still look like the pyroxene gabbro. The surface texture has not changed. There is a granule population, now that I look at it more closely with the shadows. (That is, now that they are driving north, he is noticing the larger granules on the surface because of the shadows they cast.) But I have a feeling that most of those are...They look like they're just very small clods. That should show up in some of the bulk samples we've taken. But, it is remarkable to m

A17A1642335.speaker: Evans
A17A1642335.text: Now, these Haemus Mountains have the same color tones, and what have you, as the - that field from Tacquet to - to Menelaus.

A17A1642335.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1642335.text: When you're a little bit past D-Caldera, you - on to - There's a line between the Sea of Vapors mare? and the Apennine Mountains. That's where you change to f/2.8.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: I think you ought to bear left, don't you?

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Yeah. That's where I'm going here. I just want to get across this...around these boulders.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: There's a crater we're just passing at 207/0.4 about 20 meters in diameter, with the pyroxene gabbro blocks on the rim, a few of them. It's not an exceptionally blocky rim crater, but we are in an area where the block population is up to about 5 percent (coverage of the surface), in contrast to most of the area we traversed yesterday.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: I tell you, going is a little bit rough; there's a population of blocks as Jack said and an awful lot of small craters.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Yeah, I was just going to add that the frequency of craters in the 10-meter size range is quite a bit higher than we were used to yesterday. (Pause) Oops, there's one.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Yep.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Snuck up on you. (Pause) (To Bob) And they all - although not exceptionally blocky rim - they all have a slightly, maybe 2 or 3 or 5 percent more blocks in their walls and on their rim than does the normal terrain.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Roger, Jack. Copy that.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Still no obvious structure within the dark mantling material itself.

A17A1642335.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1642335.text: Okay, Ron. I don't show that on my map.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Bob, you said 185/1.5?

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: That's affirm. [The checklist location of the sample stop is 192/1.6.]

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: What do you want? For the Rover (sample)?

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Yeah, for a sample.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: Oh, they changed it on us. (Pause) Okay. Still seeing the little pit-bottom craters with the glass in them. I've forgotten the acronym already, Bob, I'm sorry. (Pause) [Jack is referring to an exchange at 146:03:30 during the inbound drive from Shorty, when Bob invented the acronym GLPBC for the glass-lined, pit-bottom craters.]

A17A1642335.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1642335.text: Okay. And, as you cross this mare that you - just to the west of D-Caldera, you'll switch - as you get across, and up into the Apennines, you'll switch to f/2.8.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: And you asked me for an LMP frame count a while back and I believe it was 5. That was at the SEP.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: That was after the SEP photos, right?

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: That's affirm. (Pause) Negative; that was before the SEP photos.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Copy that. (Pause) 164:28:43 Schmitt: Okay, Bob, looking up at the North Massif, we see the scattered, strewn field of boulders that generally seem to start, more or less, from a line of large boulders, which might indicate some structure. And those lines are roughly horizontal across the face that we're looking at. The boulder tracks are irregular in shape, obviously downhill, but you'll see in the pictures that they are (pause) curved in places. But they're all - that I see - tend to be aggregates of little craters where the boulder was obviously tumbling and bouncing a little bit. (Pause) W

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: I thought you were close to Henry.

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: Yeah. (Responding to Bob) 188/1.8.

A17A1642335.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1642335.text: And we're just southwest of Henry.

A17A1642335.speaker: Parker
A17A1642335.text: Okay. Copy that. RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 48 sec ) 164:38:03 Schmitt: On the rim. Old Prince Henry the Navigator!

A17A1642335.speaker: Cernan
A17A1642335.text: (To himself) Watch that foot.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1642854csm.text: Ron, you want f/2.8; and then, up here when you get to the Apennine Mountains, the line between the Apennine Mountains and - the mare up there, you want to go to 1/125.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: 188/0.9. [Frame 21533 , is a representative photo showing the North Massif. A labeled version shows the dark boulder and the Station 6 boulder. A high-resolution detail focuses on Station 6.]

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: (The population's) generally about 1 percent between craters. But at the crater rims, it's up to about 5 percent.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1642854csm.text: Okay. Copy that, Jack. And how far down the North Massif...

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: And these craters...

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1642854csm.text: ...is the line of boulders?

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: (Listens to Bob) Oh, there are several of them, Bob. What I'm talking about is about 100-meter-long lines where the boulder trains initiate. And there's one (that) looks like about halfway, maybe two-thirds of the way down in perspective. Another one that's probably about halfway. They're just sort of scattered around on the Massif. (Pause) I think we're getting close to...Well, we couldn't be.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: I've got to move over here a little.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: That must be Jones (Crater).

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: Where are you looking?

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: Off to the right.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: Yeah, our heading that they're sending us down here, it really should put us to west of Jones. So that's about right. (Pause) A lot of static in the background today.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1642854csm.text: Eratosthenes is just - being - picked up.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1642854csm.text: Yeah, I think we are talking to you guys through the LM right now; and how about a speed reading?

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: Okay. We're at 12 clicks and we're full bore.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1642854csm.text: Copy that. (Long Pause)

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: Okay.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1642854csm.text: Okay, Ron. Due to the Lunar Sounder saturating from the SEP, we would like to change the attitude; and, right now, go to that - the Verb 49 maneuver attitude that we called up for 166:36. We'd like you to go that now. Over.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1642854csm.text: Copy that. (Pause)

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: Bob, I wish I could give you more on that structure in there (that is, structure in the North Massif), but I think those lines of boulder sources are about all we can see right now. Talked about the lineaments yesterday and they're not nearly as obvious today in the higher Sun. Looking up Wessex Cleft, even with the Sun in the flat area there, it looks darker than the North Massif side. But again, the Sun angle may be fooling us, but I recall it was darker on the (overhead) photos.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: The old man wrinkled face on the...

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: Sculptured Hills.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1642854csm.text: ...Sculptured Hills, though, is evident as soon as you come out of the Wessex Cleft.

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1642854csm.text: Yeah. And they look like there are boulders up on the side of Sculptured Hills; except that they aren't nearly as big as those on the North Massif. The areas where the boulder source is look like they're made up of boulders no bigger than a meter maybe; whereas, the North Massif boulders are up to several meters. Those boulder sources all seem to be up within a third of the height of the Sculptured Hills, just east of the Wessex Cleft. Here is a boulder track that crossed the slope. See that, Geno?

a17_1642854csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1642854csm.text: Hey, this is interesting. Mag Mike Mike, we're on 172.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: I thought you were close to Henry.

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: Yeah. (Responding to Bob) 188/1.8.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: And we're just southwest of Henry.

A17A1643751.speaker: Parker
A17A1643751.text: Okay. Copy that. RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 48 sec ) 164:38:03 Schmitt: On the rim. Old Prince Henry the Navigator!

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: (To himself) Watch that foot.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: It's called a wheel, I think. (Pause) And Henry looks much like Horatio did. Has boulders on its inner wall (but) not as many. They look light colored: a light-albedo, gabbroic appearance. There may be some right down there, though, that are fine grained; they look a little greyer. [Gene and Jack talk over each other for the next half dozen lines]

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: Jack, there's our target...There's...Either one of...That's one right down there on (garbled) break in slope.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: See the one we've got over has a boulder track. That's the one, that crossed slope.

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: Yeah, if we could get up...

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: Can we get up there?

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: It's awful high. We'll see.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: That's the one. That's Station 6, and that was the...(naming the rock) the turning boulder.

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: Yeah, that's it.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: The one right there. (Pause)

A17A1643751.speaker: Cernan
A17A1643751.text: Station 6: we can probably get up there.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: I think we can; it doesn't look too bad. (To Bob) The break in slope, right now, doesn't show anything obvious, except that's where the boulders start.

A17A1643751.speaker: Parker
A17A1643751.text: Okay, we hope that's fairly obvious.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: And on up the hill you have...(Stops to listen to Bob) But as I was saying, Henry just looks like a somewhat more mantled Horatio. (Laughs, then makes an aside) (This dialog is) getting to be ridiculous. 164:39:28 Cernan: Say, Bob, I'm navigating - headed northwest now - to get around the western rim of Henry.

A17A1643751.speaker: Parker
A17A1643751.text: Okay... [AS17-141- 21551 to 21553 are taken during this westward excursion. They are included in a PDf document that contains AS17-141-21549-59 ( 11 Mb ).]

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: And on that west rim, we've got about 10 percent boulder cover.

A17A1643751.speaker: Parker
A17A1643751.text: Okay. And a reminder, Jack, to keep taking your Rover photos.

A17A1643751.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1643751.text: Yes, sir! And by "boulder", I generally mean "fragment", Bob, in this case. When I say 10 percent, I'm looking at stuff greater than about a centimeter in diameter. (Pause) I'll try to say "fragment" from now on and be more precise. (Pause) Okay. Here's a little area where there's...This is the one part of the rim of Henry I see that has fairly large fragments, or boulders, on them up to 2 or 3 meters. But, again, they all appear to be buried. There are very few - except small ones - sitting out on the surface.

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1643949csm.text: And, you know, the fragment population out here only goes out maybe 200 meters, I expect. [Henry, like Camelot, is about 600 meters across. The blocks extend 200 meters beyond the rim.] 164:40:38 Schmitt: Okay. Now this (particular) concentration of boulders (we are driving past) is because of a 50-meter crater in the rim of Henry. [AS17-141-21554 to 21556 show this ejecta and the next part of the traverse.]

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1643949csm.text: Okay, that sounds like Locke (Crater). [Locke is 100-meter crater on the northwest rim of Henry. At the moment, Gene and Jack are driving by a smaller crater about 200 meters south of Locke and right on the west rim crest of Henry. Jack's size estimate is quite good.]

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1643949csm.text: I think that was one that we...(Hears Bob) 164:40:50 Cernan: Take a picture in here, Jack.

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1643949csm.text: (Responding to Bob) No. Locke, I can see. (To Gene) I'm getting the picture. [Frame 21557 shows Locke beyond the ejecta of the small crater they are passing. It is included in a PDf document that contains AS17-141-21549-59 ( 11 Mb ).]]

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1643949csm.text: Okay, that's not...Locke's right ahead of us.

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1643949csm.text: This is one (of) about 50 meters (diameter) right on the rim crest of Henry, the due-west rim. Now Locke is just ahead of us. It also has boulders in its walls but has relatively few on the rim.

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1643949csm.text: Hey, Ron, we just talked it over down here. The EKG is good and just forget the ZPN for another day. Just go EKG and forget the ZPN. That's compliments of Dr. Z.

a17_1643949csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1643949csm.text: Characteristic of both Henry, Locke, and Horatio is essentially no change in the average frequency of boulders on the rim. The increase comes in the wall. 164:41:34 Cernan: We're at 184/2.3. We're just about between Henry and...

A17A1645119.speaker: Parker
A17A1645119.text: Loud and clear, 17. How do you read?

A17A1645119.speaker: Cernan
A17A1645119.text: Okay. We're parked on a heading of 107. (Jack is laughing) Are you happy with that?

A17A1645119.speaker: Parker
A17A1645119.text: Roger. Sounds great.

A17A1645119.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1645119.text: (Laughing) You parked on a slope, too.

A17A1645119.speaker: Cernan
A17A1645119.text: There's no level...There's no level spot to park, here, though.

A17A1645119.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1645119.text: You want some help getting off? (Laughs) [Because of the slope, neither Gene - who has to get off the Rover on the uphill side - or Jack - who has to get off on the downhill side - is having an easy time dismounting.]

A17A1645119.speaker: Cernan
A17A1645119.text: (Laughing) I've got to go uphill!
