A17A1650430.text: Yes, sir. And there's some little ones over here. 165:27:21 Cernan: Yeah, but then within the blue-gray, we've got all these other fragments. [Someone in Houston notices that the bottom of Jack's SCB seems to be loose.]

A17A1650430.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1650430.text: Well, that's right. It's just several generations of activity; and it looks like the gabbro, though, picked up the fragmental breccia as inclusions. (Pause) Bob, It really looks that way right now. There's a small one here in the... [Journal Contributor Dean Eppler calls attention to a work ( 270k ) by Pulitzer Prize winning Newsday political cartoonist Tom Darcy (1933-2000) which sums up the problem that some journalists had covering the first lunar visit by a professional geologist.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 21 min 43 sec )

A17A1650430.speaker: Parker
A17A1650430.text: Okay, Charlie (Duke) is here mumbling something about it looking just like House Rock. [John Young and Charlie Duke visited House Rock at the rim of North Ray Crater on EVA-3 of Apollo 16. It was the largest lunar boulder sampled by any of the crews. It was literally the size of a good-sized house, being about 12 meters high, 25 meters long and about 20 meters thick. The Station 6 boulder consists of five large fragments of what was once a single boulder about 6x10x18 meters. For comparison, Turning Point Rock is about 6 to 7 meters high and Geophone Rock is 3 meters high.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Charlie (Duke) is here mumbling something about it looking just like House Rock. [John Young and Charlie Duke visited House Rock at the rim of North Ray Crater on EVA-3 of Apollo 16. It was the largest lunar boulder sampled by any of the crews. It was literally the size of a good-sized house, being about 12 meters high, 25 meters long and about 20 meters thick. The Station 6 boulder consists of five large fragments of what was once a single boulder about 6x10x18 meters. For comparison, Turning Point Rock is about 6 to 7 meters high and Geophone Rock is 3 meters high.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: It's very crystalline. I'll tell you, it's not a breccia, not like House Rock. Not to take anything away from House Rock, though.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Hey, Bob, there's a lot of mantling on a very shallow slope of a fracture here on one of the upslope blocks (Fragment 1). I would assume it's just part of the talus picked up as it's rolled down. But if it's worth sampling, you might think about it. (Pause) [Bob waits to get a recommendation from the Backroom but, getting no prompt answer, makes the decision himself.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Gene, if you can get that fairly readily, why don't you...You can perhaps just scoop it up with the bag.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: That's exactly what I can do.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: If you can get up to the rock there. 165:28:45 Cernan: It will be in my flight line stereo, and it's going to be bag 557. And I'll take an "after" and show you where it came from.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Copy that. [Out of sight of the TV camera, Gene gets the sample and takes the "after", which is AS17-140- 21482 . As indicated in a labeled version of the "after", Gene stepped to the northeast corner of fragment 1 , put his left hand on the dust-covered shelf to support himself, and reached out as far as possible toward the center of the dusted area and swept the bag twice from his right to his left, leaving furrows and, at the lefthand end of each furrow, a small mound of dust where he stopped. Later, at about 165:33:38, Gene will take a panorama from higher up the hill which will also

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: This is the easiest part of the rock in the world to work. Man, here's a big white clast. There's one on top about a foot and a half across, and here's one. (It) must be 2 feet across...3 feet. And that's in the blue-gray. (Pause) Feel like a kid playing in a sandbox. (Pause) 165:29:30 Schmitt: (Balancing on his downhill leg) Well, Bob, I think I've done the best I can. I'd say that they're pretty clearly inclusions of blue-gray in the anorthositic gabbro here near the contact. [Jack walks slowly uphill, leaning into it, knees dramatically bent. His SCB is clearly loose. Bob makes a misidentif

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. And Gene, your bag is hanging by one hook there. Be careful, if you can...(Correcting himself) Or, LMP...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I gave you 557, I believe. Didn't I?

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Roger. We have that one. (Pause) And whoever is giving us 557...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay, I'll have Jack fix my bag.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Yup. [While facing more or less north, leaning into the hill, and using the scoop in his left hand as a cane, Jack leans far enough forward that he can grab a fist-sized rock off the ground.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Bob, by accident...I didn't think I could do it, but I got a sample of the inclusion. And it's in bag 539. Video Clip ( 2 min 18 sec 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 23 Mb MPEG )

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Hey, Jack, that's your bag (SCB) that's hanging by one hook. Let me go get it.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Oh, they're talking to me, huh?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah, because I didn't...

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Yup.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I didn't think they could see me. I'm way up on top! (Pause) [While Jack examines the bagged sample, Gene hops into view from behind Fragment 2. Jack seals the sample bag by grasping the ends of the metal sealing strip, flipping the bag over it, and then folding in the ends of the strips.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: And it's blue-gray with light colored...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: (Presenting his SCB) Put these in my bag.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: ...inclusions in it. (To Gene) All right. (To Bob) But the whole thing (Fragment 2) seems to be pretty well altered or metamorphosed...compared to the major rock (Fragment 1) we just sampled...(compared) to the other blue-gray rock. (Pause) This bag (Gene's SCB cover) is terrible. I can't...It won't latch.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Man, there's a dark hole in there where you...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Don't let me...(Pause) Ah! I'm not... [Jack is having a difficult time reaching Gene's SCB. Because of the slope, if Jack is to reach the top of Gene's SCB, they have to be standing on virtually the same hill contour. Gene can stand facing uphill, leaning into the hill, but Jack has to face him and lean sideways into the slope. Jack's right leg is fully extended downhill, and his left leg is bent at the knee.] [Schmitt - "Plus, he's taller than I am. That was always a problem."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Here's another bag to put in there before you go away.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (Taking a full sample bag from Gene) Oh, okay. (Pause, grunting) It won't latch.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Well...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Not at this angle.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Just put the thumb on one side, and I'll...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: It's bent or something. There, that's pretty good. [Jack presents his SCB by turning to face uphill and using the scoop as a cane.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Now let me fix your bag. (Pause) RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 33 sec ) 165:31:41 Parker: And, 17...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Bob, I think that inclusion will give you an example of what...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: That'll stay on. [Whatever adjustments Gene mad to Jack's SCB, he didn't secure it at the bottom.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: ...what the anorthositic gabbro did to the blue-gray breccia. [Gene moves east of the Fragment 2; Jack examines Fragments 4 and 5 while he listens to Bob.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. We copy that. And we're ready for you guys to leave this rock and press on and either get the rake soil and cores near that crater down below the rock just a shade (that is, a short distance), or else go on to some other different variety rocks in the area.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Well, I tell you, going down to that crater is not a problem. Getting back up is. Video Clip ( 3 min 07 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay, well, find a decent area to get the rake soil from and a couple of cores.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Tell you what, Gene, I could go down there and start a rake, and you could come down there.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Yeah, I don't think you ought to try and walk back up, Jack. Let me get a pan from right here where I got this sample; (that is, upslope of Fragment 1).

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I'm going to come over and...I'll go get the rake and get the gnomon.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: 17, it's not that vital to get to that crater. We just need a good place for a rake soil and a double...(correcting himself) a single core.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (Standing in the split, examining Fragment 2 and not facing Gene) Hey, get uphill a little bit, if you can, for the pan, so that you don't...so you see my other pan station.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Where was it?

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: It was over there in that crater, just uphill from the Rover.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I'm going up there. [Jack moves west, going downslope a little and out of the TV picture.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Hey, and, 17, we aren't all that gung-ho about that particular crater, if it's that much of a job to get down to it and back up. We just need a decent place for a rake soil sample and a single core.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. [According to my Merriam-Webster , "gung-ho", meaning "extremely or overly zealous or enthusiastic" came into use by U.S. Marines in about 1942 and was derived from the short version of the Chinese name for the Chinese Industrial Cooperative Society.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Bob, we don't move around from here too much. I tell you, these slopes are something else.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Yeah. We agree with that, from what we see on the television. So use your judgment, and get them where it's the best place

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Well, you might take a look at me walking up. But I don't think I can get to the top. (Pause) [Fendell finds Gene beyond Fragment 2 and, out of sight, Fragment 1.] 165:33:38 Cernan: I just got to get a place I can get a pan from. Right here. Right in this little hole. (Pause) (Gesturing) Okay, now I left the gnomon down there.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I'll have to go get it. (Pause) I think we'll setup right here near the Rover.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I think I'll go and save some water, back on Intermediate. Okay.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Copy that. [Gene switches his cooling and then starts the pan. Jack crosses the TV picture, headed east to get the gnomon. This is the reason he appears in Gene's pan. This pan (assembly by Chris Wells) , which is marked 'north pan' on the Station 6 plan map , consists of frames AS17-140- 21483 to 21509 .] [This superb set of pictures shows Jack going back to the Rover with the gnomon in frames 21496 and 21497 .] [The lightened area around the LM is visible just over the summit of Tracy's Rock in 21495 . A detail from the pan was assembled by Chris Wells.] [In frame 21493 , we see the rake sit

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Oh, and there's Challenger! Holy Smoley! (Pause) You know, Jack, when we finish with Station 8, we will have covered this whole valley from corner to corner!

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: That was the idea. [A portion of Pan Camera frame AS17-2309 shows the South Massif at the upper right and the Sculptured Hills at the lower left. The North Massif is at the bottom right and Henry Crater is the rightmost of the three large craters in a triangular pattern at the foot of the mountain. South is up and Station 6 is on the flank of the North Massif slightly north and east of Henry.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah, but I didn't think we'd ever really quite get to that far corner. Not (Station) 2, but this other one (Station 8). And we're going to make it! [Cernan - "I wish I'd climbed to the top of the mountain to get even a better view. But, even where we were it was a much better panorama than we got from the Scarp. We couldn't see much from the Scarp. Over here, we could see everything: Challenger, the Scarp, the Sculptured Hills, and everything. I do remember this. It was fantastic - like coming over a hill and getting a look into a great big valley somewhere in the middle of Idaho."] [Fendell

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (Having taken another opportunity to examine the boulders) Bob, that blue-gray rock near the contact with the anorthositic gabbro does get some vesicles in it. I think they'll show up in Gene's pictures. (Pause) 165:35:52 Parker: Okay. We have that too, Jack. (Pause) [Schmitt - "This examination of the boulder shows the evolution of my thinking as I was getting new information. The final impression that I had - which was born out by the samples - was of a blue-gray breccia intruded by - or enclosed by, we don't know which - vesicular, tan-gray material which also turned out to be a breccia. No

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: (To Bob) Okay. I just ran out of film at 160. And I'm about two pictures short of the pan, and they (the missing frames)'re upslope. I think I can cover most of that with the 500. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Gene. (Are) you going to go to the Rover and change your mag now?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Well, Jack's going to need some help from me.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Let me know when...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: I'm starting to rake. [Gene moves downhill, going down into the boulder track and then back out. He uses a hopping gait, but with his right foot forward about six to ten inches.] Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (48 sec; 0.6 Mb)

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Let me know when you get to the Rover to change the mags after you get done with that, and I'll tell you what mag to change.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Jack, if you got...

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: But press on and help Jack with those first.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Jack, if you got enough film, I'll just come and help you.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. (Pause) [Gene trips and falls to his hands and knees, apparently without hitting the camera on the ground. He came over a small mound - possibly a crater rim - and, as he came off the mound, caught his trailing left foot, started to tilt sideways over his right foot and lost his balance.] [Cernan - "I had some speed coming down, even though I was coming cross slope. It was so hard to get up there and so easy to come down, so I was moving. I was coming cross slope because, to come straight down, I probably would have gone head over heels. You couldn't come straight down that hill very fas

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (Having seen the fall) (Are you) okay?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yup. (Pause) (Calling to Bob) Remind me to dust my camera, too, will you?

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Don't forget to dust your camera. [Schmitt - "(Laughing) That's a bad habit of mine. When people ask me to remind them to do something, I'll say it right then so I'm not held responsible for remembering."] [Gene shifts position so that his feet are downhill. He then pushes back with his hands to get up on his knees and, as his PLSS rotates past the point of his knees, he rises to his feet.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. We'll keep track of that for you, Gene. [Gene continues on his way, using the same gait at the same speed. Fendell does not follow him and, rather, starts a clockwise pan of the site.] [Schmitt - "By this third EVA we were very confident. We didn't worry about falling. Maybe we should have, but we didn't. What I want to know is how come he didn't get kidded about that fall like I got kidded about the fall at Ballet. That's just as spectacular."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: (To Jack) Okay. Did you get any "before" pictures? 165:37:12 Schmitt: I'm getting them now.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. [AS17-141- 21621 , 21622 , and 21623 are cross-Sun "befores" of the rake site and 21624 is a down-Sun.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (Laughing) 'T ain't easy, McGee. [Schmitt - "This was an expression out of the old 'Fibber McGee and Molly' radio program."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Man, I tell you, these slopes are great. I wouldn't mind being up on top coming down, but...Hey, that boulder track is quite a trench!

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: That thing must be a meter or 2 deep, huh!?

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay; the big rake. Well, I think I'll try...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Wouldn't it be easier to (pull the) rake downhill.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: It would, but the stuff wouldn't stay in. (Laughs) Right? (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Well, I don't know. It's a thought. (Pause) Make sure you get that one by the...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Yeah, I will. (Long Pause) We're not really supposed to be selective about raking.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: No you're not (being selective), you're just covering the area.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: That's why I set up there. (Long Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: A selective sample is better than no sample at all.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Let me put some in there (meaning, in the bag Gene is holding). Okay. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Bag 558.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Copy 558.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Bob, most of them are...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Let me go another couple of swipes.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. There's one(rock) a couple of inches (across). Most of them are an inch or so or smaller. They're angular to subrounded fragments. Some of them look like the inclusions. As a matter of fact, the ones that are broken open look like some of the light-colored inclusions we saw in the big boulder. The others are too dust covered to say anything about.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: A couple of them look fairly coarsely crystalline. (To Gene) Okay. Put these in there. [One of the larger rocks in this rake sample is Sample 76535, a 155 g piece of Troctolite. On page 137 in the Catalog on Apollo 17 Rocks, Volume 4 - North Massif , published in August 1994, Charles Meyer comments that "Troctolite 76535 is without doubt the most interesting sample returned from the Moon. It is a colorful, pristine, coarse-grained, plutonic rock that has had a slow cooling history ... Heroic effort have been made to date troctolite 76535, Most recently, Fremo and Tatsumoto have ... concluded t

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Let me get an "after," such as it is. Oh, we want the...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: They want the soil here.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Soil, that's right. Video Clip ( 3 min 41 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 37 Mb MPEG )

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: That's affirm. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. You want to put that in (Jack's SCB)?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah, I'd better put it in before I...(Pause) Okay. Let's try for the soil. (To Bob) 559's the soil.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Copy that. And, 17, our present plans from the (Backroom) are (that) we'd like to get the single core, the 500 millimeter shots - and, I guess, maybe one could do one, and one could do the other. And then we'd like to press on and do a short Station 7, unless you think you have got a fair variety of rocks here. The feeling is that you have (garbled) significant variety of rocks.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (To Gene) Here. Little more, little more, little more. (Pause) [Fendell's pan crosses the back of the Rover. Neither Jack nor Gene is in sight. They are probably due west of the Rover, hidden by the gate.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay, Bob. I'll get the core and let Jack get the 500's. [Cernan - "(Smiling) I didn't want to let Jack use the hammer because I was afraid he'd hurt himself."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: 559 is the kilogram of soil. I think we've pretty much covered the general variety we've seen here. I think we're seeing most of them in that boulder.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. And so we'd like to go on to Station 7 then - when you get the 500 and the core - in hopes of finding a variation of boulders along the front. (Pause) [There is a discussion in Houston about having Gene do the 500-mm photography because of his longer arms. Jack apparently had had some trouble handling the 500-mm during training.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: (To Bob) Okay. (To Jack) Let me know when you get it. (Pause) 165:41:09 Schmitt: Okay. "After".

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay, why don't you get the 500, and I'll get the core.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: And the LMP's on (frame count) 120. [AS17-141- 21625 , 21626 , and 21627 are Jack's cross-Sun "afters". Note the tongs in 21625.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Copy 120 there. And, Gene, if you want to change, we recommended magazine Foxtrot or Fran (Magazine 146), as the case may be. [Fendell begins a counter-clockwise site pan.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Will try Foxtrot Franny. (To Jack) Don't forget to get (a 500 photo of) that boulder track.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: (Talking through Jack's following remark) And while you're at it, Gene, ...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: This once, I'm going to have to lean against the Rover to do it. [That is, Jack will have to brace himself in order to steady the 500-mm camera to shoot upslope.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: ...you might remember to dust your camera when you're leaning over the seat. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Let me look at your camera. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Oh, man. If this Rover wasn't here, we'd roll downhill.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Hey, Bob. I think we could use an "upper" (drive tube) here if you want to save the lowers.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I think so, too. [The 'lower' core sections have reinforced tips but, at this site, the soil is soft enough that one of the 'upper' sections could be used without fear of damage, thereby conserving the supply of lowers.] [Schmitt - "Obviously, I didn't remember what the core tube count was."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Whichever you want. (To Gene) Do you want your...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: No, I'll get it. Why don't you get your 500, and I'll...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. But do you want a core? Watch the fender. [Gene rounds the front end of the Rover, apparently in a controlled skid.] [Cernan - "I was just sidestepping as I was coming around the Rover, sidestepping to slow down and turn. By this time I was long familiar with operating in the suit, and I appreciated the slope I was on. So I just turned and sort of sidestepped into where I wanted to stop."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: The core's in there, isn't it?

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Well, there's some under my seat if you want to use those.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I'll use those.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Standby, Jack. We have three lowers and two uppers, so we'd just as soon use the extra lower here in the single core. That'll give us two uppers and two lowers left...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: ...for doubles. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: There should be a lower in there, Geno.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah. Bob, any special place you want that? Just out here on the slope?

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: That's affirm... [Fendell finds Jack at Gene's seat, 500 mm camera in hand. The rammer and core caps - among other things - are visible on the left side of his PLSS.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Should have put the gnomon up. Well...

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Just out there on the slope. (Pause) (Talking through Jack's following remark) I guess if you saw a crater you might look at that,...

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: (To Gene) You don't have any film to document, either.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: ...but primarily we're looking at the crater.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: I'll get it. I'll get it, Jack. Don't worry. (To Bob) Okay. (Pause) We have a couple of dents in our wheels. That's better than having a flat tire. (Long pause) [Jack goes east from the Rover; the lens cap is off.] Video Clip ( 3 min 36 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: (To Jack) Did he say "in a crater"? (No answer; pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: I'm not sure what he said. Thinking...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: How do I get this doggone...(Garbled) turn to come off? (Pause) [Fendell pans the TV clockwise. Off-camera, Gene is taking the scoop off of the extension handle so that he can attach the handle to the core.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: You got to unlock it.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah, it is unlocked.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. Now push down and turn.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I got it.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: How am I going to see up there to shoot this thing?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Well, why don't you lean against the rock? Go over there and lean against it. [Cernan - "It was difficult to shoot uphill, because you couldn't lean back very far. So I suggested that Jack lean against the rock."]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Well, I have to do something. I was trying to get so I could lean against the Rover, but that ain't going to work.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: The Rover isn't steady enough for you to lean against.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Well, it's steady enough. There's just no place to lean. [Jack passes in front of the south-looking TV; he is going east. Fendell reverses direction to follow him.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay. And, Jack, and if you'll listen for a minute, I'll tell you some possible 500-millimeter targets the people have in mind. One, the LM, if you can see it from there. Two, Nansen, if you can see it from there. Three, Lara; and four, Shorty. In other words, I guess they're talking about looking along your traverse from yesterday. It would be mostly the back shots, apparently. And then, also, the South Massif, and I don't know what you can get of boulder tracks leading up the North Massif. And most of those will be looking downhill towards the LM, Stations 2, 3, and 4. Over. Nansen, Lara, an

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: I got you, Bob. 165:44:50 Cernan: Yeah, the LM is visible by the way. (Long Pause) [Fendell finds Jack against the west face of the north boulder, leaning his PLSS against it for stability while he aims the 500 uphill to the northwest. His SCB is loose again. Jack's first series of pictures, of the source outcrop for the Station 6 boulder , consists of frames AS17-139- 21186 to 21193 . Comparison with photos taken at the LM allow identification of individual boulders in the source region and, in an enhanced portion of the mini-pan, the upper part of the boulder track.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I got a set of (pause) what looks like the outcrop from which the boulder came. (Long Pause) [Jack adjusts the camera and then takes a few more pictures.] RealAudio Clip ( 7 min 34 sec ) 165:46:10 Schmitt: I'm afraid they're moved a little bit. (Long Pause) [Jack tries to point the camera higher.] 165:46:26 Schmitt: No, I can't; that's it. I got a few pictures looking up the boulder track and then off to the left a little bit; and one off to the right. And I think...I'm not sure how well they overlap; that's just an awful hard shot. [Journal Contributor Syd Buxton has used frames AS17-14

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Okay; good on that. (Pause) And if you're done with that, have you got a frame count - or, you're still taking them, I guess, it looks like.

A17A1652749.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1652749.text: Yeah. (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. My camera is clean. Magazine Foxtrot is on about frame 2, and I cycled through it. And I've got the core all set, and I'm going to go get it. And I didn't hear where you said to put it, Bob.

A17A1652749.speaker: Evans
A17A1652749.text: At about - at about 165:31 or 32 in there, I used mag Mike Mike and took frame 173 and 174 looking north from [garble]. Last one was in the vicinity of Lara Crater.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Anywhere.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Oh, man, you're easy.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: And did you get your camera...

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Anywhere. Not the bottom of a small crater, huh? (Pause)

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Any place. And did you get your camera dusted?

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Yeah. I got it all dusted and the mag's changed.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Good.

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: It's core 48.

A17A1652749.speaker: Parker
A17A1652749.text: Copy that. (Pause) [Fendell pans the TV counter-clockwise, away from Jack who is still shooting pictures west toward Stations 2, 3, and 4.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Okay. I'll even get you a picture of it. (Pause) Oh me, oh my. (Long Pause) [Fendell reaches the counter-clockwise stop without finding Gene. Fendell reverses direction and pans clockwise. He finds Jack, now shooting pictures toward the south.]

A17A1652749.speaker: Cernan
A17A1652749.text: Can you get the LM from there? 165:48:27 Schmitt: Yep. [They are two hours and fifteen minutes into the EVA. AS17-139- 21203 , 21204 , and 21205 are Jack's pictures of the LM. Station 6 is about 3.1 kilometer from the LM, which is about 7 meters tall. The two craters beyond the LM with prominent rim boulder fields may be the east (left) and west (right) components of Trident.] 165:48:30 Cernan: That core went in very easy, Bob. I pushed it in about a quarter of the way. And about another five or six whacks, and it's in all the way. (Long Pause as he takes two pictures of the core tube) Okay. C

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: I don't want to lose that thing (the TGE ), so I guess... Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Okay, 17, when you get back on here, we don't need any charges, and we'll leave the SEP turned off. [Fendell pans the TV clockwise.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1655334.text: America, Houston.

A17A1655334.speaker: Evans
A17A1655334.text: Houston, America. Roger. Loud and clear.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: I'm not sure...Did you turn it off, Gene?

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Yeah, I turned it off. (Pause) I turned it off. Okay. Let me see. We want to move on to (Station) 7 here. (Reading LMP/CDR-11 ) Rake; talus; documented core; you got your stereos; we got two pans; TGE ; camera. (Looking at the traverse map on LMP/CDR-12 ) Okay, we're going to head east and look for Station 7. (Reading LMP/CDR-15 ) block variation; contact change; and get a different sample of rocks. Okay, I sure want to get one or two of those nice ones in the big bag while you're over there.

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Okay... 165:54:29 Schmitt: Open the gate, and I'll bring one. [They have to open the gate to get at the big bag.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: ...Seven(teen)...Okay. And let me know when you get ready to get back on the Rover there, 17. (Pause)

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: (To Jack) Guess what isn't opening again. (Pause) Should, though. It's all set right. [Gene is having trouble opening the gate. The latch is fouled with dust.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: You could put them under Jack's seat if it's easier. (Pause)

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Okay. What do you want done to the SEP while I'm here? Do you want the blanket left open? 165:55:13 Parker: Negative. We'd like the blankets closed and taped down again, if possible, and both switches left off. We won't touch it again until Station 8.

A17A1655334.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1655334.text: Down east of Saenger there, you get into the first ring of Arabia or the second ring of Arabia there.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Oh, the tape's not going to stick anymore, I'm afraid.

A17A1655334.speaker: Evans
A17A1655334.text: Yeah. Hey, you know this is - Let me get this picture. This is the first time I've really been able to see that first ring of Arabia.

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Well, try.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Big bag open?

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Yeah, it's all open. All set. [Jack's sample is 76055, a 18x20x25 cm, 6.4 kg, tan-grey breccia. See post-flight photo S73-15713 .]

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: I need a normal sample bag for one here. It's pretty fragile. [While Jack puts 76055 in the big bag, he is asking Gene for a sample bag to hold another, smaller sample, 76335.] 165:55:37 Cernan: Okay. (Pause) Oh, that doggoned thing's not going to...That tape is full of dust now. (Pause) Okay. Wait a minute, Jack.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Here, let me get this big one (meaning 76055). I'm about ready to drop it. (Pause) It looks like a gabbro.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Here's sample bag 560.

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Copy 560.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: And 560 has an undocumented, except by the pans, very white...(It) looks like a crushed anorthosite. It looks like some of the inclusions in the breccia...(correcting himself) gray, re-crystallized breccia.

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Okay. We copy that. [This is sample 76335, a very friable (breakable), 500 gram anorthosite. By the time the sample got back to earth, the largest piece was 8 x 6.5 x 5 cm. The approximate locations from which Jack collected 76055 and 76335 are shown in Figure 4 from the Apollo 17 Sample Catalog, Part 4 ( 30 Mb PDF ).] [Fendell finds the LM; the lighter-gray surface discoloration caused by the descent engine is obvious and the LM is a black and white dot at it's center. The dot is black on the west; white on the east.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Jack, when you get around, and we close this gate, you might try and hit that top of that SEP down again.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: I will. (Pause)

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Hey, Bob, you're staying keyed an awful long time. We can hear a lot of what's going on back there. (Pause) (To Jack) Wait a minute. Let me get this out of the way. (Pause) Okay. Close it. (Pause) Yeah. That's got it. [Parker has a foot switch so that he can speak to Gene and Jack. Normally, he releases the switch when he is talking with the Flight Director but, here, is leaving the switch depressed.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1655334.text: Okay, Ron, we've got a - a Flight Plan update and a Lunar Sounder PAD, if you want to take it before we get into the visuals here.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Okay, that's tight.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: That's got it. Okay.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Oop, oop, oop. Why'd that come off?

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Well, because it (the gate)'s not locked. It's (garbled) that never was locked. Video Clip ( 3 min 38 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: (Laughing) We lucked out. (Pause) [Fendell finds Jack, who is raising his seat so that he can stow the drive tube. Had the gate swung open, they might have lost some tools. Later in the EVA, during their drive back to the LM from Station 9, that is exactly what will happen. The gate will swing open and they will lose both extension handles along with the rake and scoop. Gene takes a couple of pictures of Jack. These are 22296 and 22297 . Note that Jack's gold visor is up and, therefore, we can see him in the suit. The seismic charge transporter is at the top of the geopallet, directly above th

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Sort of.

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: And, before you get on, remember to close the battery covers if they...

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Jack gets his seat belt out of the way by draping of it over the Rover SCB.]

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Your camera lens looks all right, Geno.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Yeah, I dusted it already.

A17A1655334.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1655334.text: Oh. (Pause) Okay. Cover closed...(Going to the SEP receiver behind his seat) Okay. Do they want it on or off? Leave it off, huh?

A17A1655334.speaker: Parker
A17A1655334.text: Off.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: Leave it off, but try and close that cover as best you can. 165:57:47 Schmitt: Well, I'm afraid the tape has had it.

A17A1655334.speaker: Cernan
A17A1655334.text: I know it.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. Frames - last three frames before 128 were also looking east. Okay, we had an update, huh?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: (Leaning across his seat) You want us to tape it again, Bob? (To Gene) What did you do with the tape?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: If you can grab the tape right off, but don't spend a lot of time on it. [Schmitt - "I think we're both sounding tired after working on this slope. There isn't as much joking as when we first got there. We're quieter."]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: (To Gene) What did you do with that tape?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: Let's worry about it at Station 7, if we're going to worry about it. Press on.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Yeah. Let's forget it now. It's too hard to work on here, and it's not going to take just a minute. It's going to take too much time.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: I'm not sure I can get back on here. [The Rover is rolled about 20 degrees - with Jack's side down.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Well, let me give you a hand.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. T-start time, 166:42:12; T-stop time, 47:10.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: We need any a...We don't need any...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: No. [As noted previously, Jack's gold visor is up. His helmet remains facing the TV camera through all of this, but he turns his head about 60 degrees to look downhill to the south.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Nothing. As a matter of fact...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: I can drive, Jack.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Why don't you drive down and get so you're not...You can get on...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: You can go downhill very easy.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. Let me get the TV; The battery covers are closed.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Let me carry...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Why don't you just go down there.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: ...I'll carry the Rover sampler, just in case. [Jack extracts the sampler, which is stowed vertically next to the control panel.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Got it? Okay. I'll get that out of your way, too.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. I'll head down to that...Actually, I'll sidehill over to those boulders right over there and then see if that's any change (in rock type). [Jack starts downhill; Gene leans over the right-side battery covers.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. You might, if you get another sample, a large sample, you might grab it, and we'll throw it in the footpan here. [Gene wants to get a large rock that they can use in the close-out ceremonies back at the LM. The plan is to split the rock into dozens of pieces for distributions to museums around the world. See 169:43:06.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: And I'll see if I can't find a level spot to...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: I sort of ought to have my scoop, too.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: ...help you get on. No, don't take too much; just take that (LRV Sampler). That's all you need. [Gene goes around the front of the Rover; Jack has only gone a few feet to the southeast.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: How about letting me have your hammer, then?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay; and, 17, can you verify that the gnomon is back in the Rover?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Gnomon is on the Rover. The TGE is on the Rover. [Fendell finds Gene standing a few feet south, examining the Rover. Jack is beyond him, moving diagonally across the slope and toward the southeast.] [Schmitt - "One of the things that bothered me physically was doing a lot of sidehill traversing at Station 6. On going east on the south-facing slope for some distance, the inside ligament on my left leg began to feel fatigued because the right leg was so much down and the left leg was so much up. Most of the stress was on the left leg, and it is the same ligament that I had damaged skiing years b

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: The rake.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: The rake is on the Rover. The scoop's on the Rover. We got the...You put the core under your (seat) pan, right?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Yep, that's right.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. I'm going to power up and see if I can't come down and get you. (Pause) It's fun walking downhill! Boy, that boulder track is impressive. [Gene moves the TV to its stowed position.]

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay; and, 17, when you get moving...

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: (The track is) very symmetrical.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: ...we want to get, and I quote, "a maximum variety of hand samples with a minimum amount of documentation, in a minimum amount of time at Station 7". It's just an attempt to see what kind of variety we can get along the face of the front. Over.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay, Ron, we're all just standing by. That takes care of the Flight Plan updates, and we're just standing by for your visuals. This pass you're to concentrate on the landing site and the D-Caldera, you know?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Roger. (Pause; static) [The remainder of this EVA was reviewed with Gene and Jack, together, in Santa Fe, New Mexico in September 1991.] [Cernan - "I'd like to reminisce with Jack - a little bit - because, for what it's worth, we're sort of authenticating history, nineteen years later. It wasn't until Eric and I sat down in my office and watched the films and listened to our voices that I recalled the steepness of that slope at Tracy's Rock. Because Al Bean painted the picture, I've seen the hill a million times; but, in the years since we were there, I've never fully appreciated that you and

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: Need some help?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: No (garbled).

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1655751csm.text: I shouldn't have left.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1655751csm.text: Ron, we want to concentrate on the small-scale features, and your binoculars may be what you need. We want to look at the dark-halo craters in the site area and examination of D-Caldera with the binocs.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: No, no. I don't need any help. I'll get on. [Cernan - "For Jack to have gotten on that downhill seat, even if he'd jumped up there he probably would have fallen back off. For me, it was much easier to get on the uphill side but it was steep enough that it really did feel like I was going to end up in Jack's seat."] [Schmitt - "It wasn't worth the effort for me to try to get on. By this time, we didn't have any problem with walking some distance."] [Cernan - "The only thing about it is that Jack really did enjoy riding on the downhill side."] [Schmitt - "(Laughing) That might have influenced my

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: (Static clears) I probably ought to turn my water off of Max if that's where it is. It's cold. I don't want to run out today. (Long Pause) Well, the roll indicator says 15 degrees; and the pitch indicator says about 12 (giving a total slope of nearly 20 degrees). I don't know if I believe all that. Bob, you with us?

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: Go ahead. Right. We're with you.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1655751csm.text: Okay. I'm rolling.

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1655751csm.text: Copy that. (Long Pause) Traverse to Station 6 Apollo 17 Journal Geology Station 7

a17_1655751csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1655751csm.text: Hey, Ron, when you come up on the landing site, we would like you to concentrate on Shorty Crater and F Crater and then the other dark-halo craters. As you know, as I told you last night, Shorty ended up with some orange-colored material that looks an awful lot like a Fuma - fumara - a vent anyway - fumarole. And it looks...

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Man, this is still a slope. Jack, I'm going to pull around and in the front of the way you're facing.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: I can go down...There's a crater over here, (garbled). (Pause) Oh, there you are.

A17A1660233.speaker: Evans
A17A1660233.text: Okay. I got to take a look and see which one's Shorty.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: This is much better. How is this?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: That's great.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: We ought to be able to pick up lots of those fragments out in that field out there.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Be right with you.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Okay. (Pause) Bob, I just came downslope reading 193/3.1; just about 100 meters to pick up Jack.

A17A1660233.speaker: Evans
A17A1660233.text: Oh! Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay. Bag 48 Yankee has a sample of about a one-third-meter boulder that was lying in...that's sitting right smack dab in a little crater of it's own.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: Copy that. [48 Yankee contained Apollo samples 76030 through 76037. The largest fragment - 76035 - is a piece of blue-gray breccia. Interestingly, 48 Yankee also contains a 2.5 gram piece of basalt (76037).]

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Oh, Jack!

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: What?

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Oh, you just kicked a snowstorm of dust across here.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: I'm sorry. I just fell, too.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Did you? You all right?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. Want your hammer?

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: I got to drop it (the hammer) in the pan here. Hold on to it, I think. (Pause)

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Couldn't help that one.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. I think, (when) we get (to) some more level spots, I can dust this thing (the battery cover) back there.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Am I really on?

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: You're high. You're (seat belt is) twisted. Go away from you one twist. Okay. (Pause) Is it caught in something? Yeah, it is. You're...Oh, wait a minute...Get up, get up, get up. You've got...You're sitting on...Get up.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: What am I sitting on?

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: You've got to get out. You didn't put this away. Wait a minute. Get up...Out...All the way.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Oh, that thing.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah, this thing.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: That's right. [Neither Jack nor Gene has any idea what "this thing" might have been. A quick review of the dialog hasn't revealed any clues. "It" is probably not the roll of tape, in part because Jack doesn't think the tape roll was big enough to have made him sit high.] [Schmitt - "Why couldn't we have said what it was!"] [Cernan - "You and I knew what was going on, but nobody else could have followed it."]

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: That's where (means "why") you're setting (sic) high.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: I knew I'd forget that. (Pause)

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Okay. Now, let me get this thing out. (Pause) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay. Let's press. Better get (the seatbelt) latched. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: All set?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yep. [The best TV record of an astronaut getting on a Rover is probably that of Charlie Duke at one of the Apollo 16 EVA-2 stations. Fendell recorded Jack mounting the Rover at Stations 3 and 7. The best still is 20453 , which Gene took of Jack at Station 9. Ken Glover has produced a video clip of Jack mounting the Rover onboard the 1/6th-g airplane.] [Cernan - "When you're sitting in the seat, you can't see what's going on in the seat. The other guy is the one whose got to look."] [Schmitt - "It's all by feel."]

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Okay. (Pause) We're rolling, Bob.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: LMP frame (count) is 130.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: You got a lot of static now?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yup. [Cernan - "We were hearing static from the ground. But, as you can hear in the tape, they were reading us loud and clear. We were probably hearing carrier static."]

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Hey, you got a rock on your right of your (garbled).

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah, I got them. (Garbled) (Pause) I got the low-gain (antenna) set.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Hello, Houston. Do you read? 166:05:57 Parker: Roger. We read loud and clear. [Jack's traverse pictures taken during the 500-meter drive to Station 7 are AS17-141- 21637 to 21645 .]

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay; how about that field...Not this block, but (out where) there's sort of a collection of them...

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. Way out there...

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: ...way out there.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: ...about 300 meters or so.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Oh, at least. Yeah. Oh; going into the Sun, I can't see a thing to tell you about Wessex Cleft, that we haven't already said.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: Okay. Station 7 is nominally 208 and 3.3, but it's any group of any significant boulders you want to stop at in reality.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Understand. (Pause) (To Gene) Ohhh, easy.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: You feel like you're on a downslope over there?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. I feel like you're about ready to spin out downhill any minute.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Do you? (Tongue in cheek) I don't feel that at all up here. (Pause)

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Bob, it's hard to give you much (description), looking into the Sun the way we are.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: We must be about 200 meters up the slope, looking at that little valley (Taurus-Littrow) down there, Jack, on the right?

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. I think you're right. The pattern on the slope really doesn't look much different than on the light mantle. Matter of fact, it looks very much like light mantle, except for these large blocks that are in it.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: Okay. Copy that. And you guys may still have your visors up. We can't tell, but you might be better off with them down, if you've forgotten that they're up. 166:07:26 Schmitt: Well...Boy, I can't see. My hands work just as well (as an eye shade) as my visor, as a matter of fact. [During this EVA, Jack frequently has his visor positioned at about eye level. This provides him some shielding from the direct Sun while giving him a view of the ground unobscured by scratches in the visor. At this point in the review, Gene and Jack discussed the possibility that Jack was using one hand to steady hims

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: No, I can't believe mine could be up.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: You've got a crater right in front of you.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. I got it.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay. That looks like a pretty good pile to work on.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. Let's go over in there.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Hey, wait a minute. Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Bob, what heading are you going to want me to park on? Why don't we get in that flat area, Jack, so I can dust the radiators.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yeah.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: We have no constraints, Gene. This is going to be a very short station. Probably not more than 10 or 15 minutes. Just to grab, as I say a maximum variety of hand samples with a minimum amount of documentation and a minimum amount of time.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Okay. We do a pan, and pick up a lot of those small ones, Jack.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Yep.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Rather than trying to chip. (Pause)

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: Okay. We would like to have the...

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: (Garbled)

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: I'd like to see us a little more level.

A17A1660233.speaker: Parker
A17A1660233.text: ...TV camera and its mirrors and stuff dusted there, however. But we won't do anything to the battery.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: I thought you were going to stop back there.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Well...

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: Okay.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: I was going out here around this big one.

A17A1660233.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1660233.text: I'm sorry. I misunderstood you.

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: Yeah. (Pause) See, there's a lot of little ones up in here I want to...

A17A1660233.speaker: Cernan
A17A1660233.text: (To Bob) Okay. Do not do anything to the batteries. Understand.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1660850csm.text: Oh, I hope we got a Pan Camera picture of that - what the - Condorcet [?] or [garble] or something like that, the one I was describing had a little bit of diamond down in it?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Roger.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: I can't figure out where you're going to stop.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Right in here. Right here to give you as much of a level spot as I can. That's about as level a spot as I can find. I'm inside the slope of a crater. Bob, I'm at 200/3.3.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Copy that. (Long Pause)

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: You want me to help you with the dusting, Geno?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: No, I'll get it. Only one guy can do it. (Pause)

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: I just...You take a pan "before", and we'll start picking up some of those samples, and I'll take a pan afterward. (Pause) Well, let's see here. (Pause) See what kind of variety we can get here.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: There is another one of our blue-gray breccias, I think, over there: re-crystallized breccias with some of that crushed anorthosite in it. (Pause) I think right in here. I'm going to take the pan at about...

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: And, Jack, what's your frame count?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1660850csm.text: Ron, Farouk thinks it is on the Pan [Camera].

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. Press on. (Pause) [Figure 178 from the USGS Apollo 17 Professional Paper is a plan map of the Station 7.] 166:10:23 Schmitt: Bob, I'm going to take the pan at 11 feet (focus), so you can see the fragments that we're going to pick up here. Then we can take another one for location work.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Copy that. (Long Pause) [TV on. Jack's near-field pan , which includes almost none of the horizon, consists of frames AS17-141- 21646 to 21664 .] Video Clip ( 3 min 21 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1660850csm.text: You know, in the eastern wall of Picard - I'm looking at it with the binocs now, and you can definitely see the first part of it up there has some vertical ensearpments [sic] - escarpments along the edge of it. And the vertical escarpments are kind of in irregular layers - well, just kind of like you would suspect if you - you eroded out a bunch of lava layers. In other words, they're not continuous, but they're kind of intermingled along, and they go about - oh, a third of the way down from the top of the rim, down to where the talus starts sliding on into the - into the crater.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Should have it, Bob.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: We've got a TV. And, I repeat, we'd like to get some dusting of the (TCU) mirror and the lens of the TV; (dust the) TCU and the TV. [Gene moves the TV so that he can dust the lens.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Let me get you out of the Sun. (Pause) I wouldn't do this for anybody but you, you know that.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. Looks good, Gene. Thank you. (Long Pause)

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1660850csm.text: Good show. We'll tie that - tie that up with what you gave us last time on Picard.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: You know what? I'm getting tired of dusting. (Long Pause) My primary tools: the dustbrush and the hammer. And my head. (Pause) Okay. You ready to start picking (up small rocks)? 166:12:35 Schmitt: Picking.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [Fendell finds Jack WSW of the Rover, bagging a sample. He is leaning forward, but only a little more than he would at a level site.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: And...

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: You notice the temperature difference with that high Sun angle?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Yup.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Roger. You're probably letting in a lot of infrared through without having that gold visor down, too. That's sort of an infrared shield.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Yeah, but mine's been down all the time, Bob.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Except in the shade. [Jack lowers his gold visor, then closes the sample bag by holding it by the two tabs at the top and twirling it three times. He is leaning on his scoop again, handle against his stomach.] 166:13:05 Schmitt: Okay, 540 is the first bag of selected samples.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Copy that. RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (2 min 15 sec) [Gene joins Jack and collects a fist-sized sample with his tongs.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. I'm going to leave you (Gene's SCB) open, but don't let me...

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Let me get...Here, put that one in there. [Gene moves alongside Jack so that they are side-by-side, facing north.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Wait a minute, let's get a bag on it. We're getting too many rocks, and we don't know where they came from. (Pause)

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: I don't think it will fit. Will it?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Well, we'll wrap it a little bit.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Yeah, wait a minute, it will fit. (Pause) Wait a minute. (Long Pause) [Gene presents his SCB; Jack has dropped the scoop.] Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (1 min 03 sec; 0.75 Mb)

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. Bag 541 is partially around another big rock in Gene's collection bag. (Pause) [Once again, Jack retrieves the scoop by stepping on the head so that the handle rotates up to about waist height. With practice, this has become an easy procedure. Gene moves farther west to a large boulder.] Video Clip ( 2 min 15 sec 0.6RealVideo clip or 22 Mb MPEG )

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: Did you get pictures of this thing here?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Yeah; well, not the big rock yet. Not in focus anyway.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: I got to do that. [Gene stops far enough from the boulder that his shadow won't show up in the pictures he is about to take.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: I was just collecting (fragments) in this area. 166:14:34 Cernan: Why don't you keep grabbing a few, and I'm going to...

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: That's what I'm doing. [Gene hops sideways to the north, taking a flightline stereo. These photos are AS17-146-22298 to 22315.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1660850csm.text: It's one of the blue-gray rocks, Bob. And it's got a light-colored fragment that runs the full height of it, about a meter and a half thick. And then it's got the blue-gray rock on the other side. As a matter of fact...(Pause) Let me look at it closely. (Pause) It's a fragment in it all right. [Gene is still taking pictures for the flightline stereo; Fendell pans southward to Jack who is collecting small rock fragments with the scoop.]

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. Copy that, Gene. And remember to document around the corner if you're trying to get some photo-documentation of the boulder. (Pause) [Having bagged the first set of fragments, Jack collects some more. He has the head of the scoop angled 90 degrees to the shaft and is having a much easier time at solo sampling than he'd had at Station 3.] [Cernan - "I notice that we seem much more relaxed during EVA-3. We were confronted with more ambitious things but, even little things like picking up the scoop that we would have commented on earlier in the mission, we were just doing."] [Schmitt - "In

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1660850csm.text: Ron, are there any similarity between the highlands, west of Crisium and those east of Serenitatis?

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1660850csm.text: Okay. Copy that.

a17_1660850csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1660850csm.text: Pin him down. (Long Pause) [Jack moves about ten feet to the south to get some more fragments. In order to collect and bag the samples, he rests the head of the scoop on the ground after he gets a fragment or two, then bends down as far as he can and grabs the shaft about a foot off the ground. This grip makes it relatively easy for him to pour the samples into a bag. Gene's close-ups of the boulder are AS17-146-22316 to 22328. He is using the tongs to make sure that he is the right distance away for good focus. In 22325 , one of the dikelets runs horizontally across the frame about 2/3rds of

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: I wish I could break a sample right off. Here's another one. It is a dikelet! There's three or four of them!

A17A1661610.speaker: Parker
A17A1661610.text: Okay. Copy that, Gene. Very good. [Jack moves a few feet north and collects another fragment. Fendell pans to Gene who is examining the northeast corner of the boulder. The top of the boulder is just a bit above the top of Gene's head. We can see Gene using his tongs to gauge his distance.] Video Clip ( 3 min 18 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Ohhhh, me, oh, my. (Pause) The material in the dike looks...Yeah, it is, it is, it (the blue-gray, dike material)'s not covering it (the light colored host rock). It's between the lighter-colored rock, and it's the blue-gray rock. [Cernan - "I remember this episode very, very vaguely. I didn't describe it very well."] [Schmitt - "You're going through a lot of thought and you're only articulating every once in a while."] [At most stations, Gene has spent the first few minutes cleaning up the Rover while Jack has taken a look at the local geology. Here, the roles are different. While Gene dusted

A17A1661610.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1661610.text: 542 is another bag of goodies.

A17A1661610.speaker: Parker
A17A1661610.text: Copy that. 166:17:09 Schmitt: Gene, let me get rid of this. [Gene is scraping fragments off of the face of the boulder; Jack puts the soil sample in his SCB.]

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Oh, wait a minute. I got...I got...Well, maybe it isn't a dikelet. Maybe it's just a screen covering, a flow covering.

A17A1661610.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1661610.text: No, you got...They're dikes.

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Let me...let me... 166:17:20 Schmitt: (Putting the soil sample in Gene's SCB) They're little veinlets of... [Schmitt - "'Dikelet' was a much better term than 'veinlet'. They're injected magma, melted rock."] [Cernan - "And you didn't teach me that word before we started, either."] [Schmitt - "I think you knew 'dike' before..."] [Cernan - "Yeah; but 'dikelet'...I don't ever remember you telling me to use that word. (Tongue in cheek) Jack used to give me all these words and he'd say, 'Now, when you get up there, Cernan, use these. It will impress the hell out of them.' I had a list of words writ

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Let me get this whole thing in a bag. I got a rock, Bob. It's fractured, primarily around the dike. It's in several pieces, but we're going to put it all in one bag.

A17A1661610.speaker: Evans
A17A1661610.text: I got it in window 2. [Long pause.]

A17A1661610.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1661610.text: (Getting a new sample bag) 543.

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Oh, man, they're going to have to assemble that.

A17A1661610.speaker: Parker
A17A1661610.text: Copy, 543. [Gene and Jack are standing side-by-side, facing west and examining the boulder.]

A17A1661610.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1661610.text: Here.

A17A1661610.speaker: Cernan
A17A1661610.text: Here, I got...I got...Let me get it piece by piece. (Pause)

A17A1663100.text: No, we just do that...

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: I thought we were bypassing SWP.

A17A1663100.speaker: Parker
A17A1663100.text: ...during the mission planning stages. [Jack thinks that both he and Bob are making a sarcastic reference to some pre-flight discussions about SWP, but doesn't remember the context. As Bob has said, the cuff checklist shows a slight course change as they round the southwest rim of SWP.]

A17A1663100.speaker: Cernan
A17A1663100.text: (Waits for Bob to finish) 225 and 3.4. Okay. [Cernan - "I've been reading ahead and I want to warn you that there's another important geologic observation coming up at 166:33:28."]

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: That's pretty close to nominal.

A17A1663100.speaker: Cernan
A17A1663100.text: Yeah. I got my...Man, I tell you, this little navigation map I've got on my cuff checklist ( LMP/CDR-16 ) is unquestionably the greatest thing that I've ever done. [Schmitt - "The other guys may have just had the EVA map with the traverse on it. And you (Gene) said, 'Why don't we put that in the cuff checklist.' It wouldn't surprise me."] [This conjecture is correct. Neither the Apollo 15 nor 16 cuff checklists contained traverse maps.] [Cernan - "I tell you what. It may go back to my days in the Navy when we were doing low-altitude run-ins, and we would take a big sectional map. Your track mi

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: Sure hard to tell where north is on it, though. (Pause) [Schmitt - "Now, as this line indicates, from my geologic experience - to contrast with Gene's Navy experience - you're used to keeping the map oriented one way and translate, in your mind, where north is. I never did it very well, but a lot of people are able to do that."]

A17A1663100.speaker: Evans
A17A1663100.text: It just got dark.

A17A1663100.speaker: Cernan
A17A1663100.text: Trying my best to keep you out of those slopes.

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: That's all right. I'm learning to tolerate it. (Pause) Okay, Bob. We're pretty close now to...No, we're not. We're still about 100 meters, I think, from where the break in slope is with the plains. But we're away from the block population except for scattered...(except for) two great big blocks out ahead of us, this side of the SWP Crater. But the average population is down to the 1 percent or less, again. (That is, one percent of the surface is covered by rocks ("blocks") bigger than about one centimeter.) That average population really never changed up in here. Just the big blocks were aroun

A17A1663100.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1663100.text: Ron, I think if you put an order of priority on some activity here, as far as the geology goes, you might consider sketching out on Shorty - with just a rough handle on where you thought you saw some of the coloring differentiation up on the northern side of Shorty - and also give some thought on F Crater, if you will. I know you didn't get a chance to look at it because - If we can tie up the - what you see from orbit on Shorty to what we know we've got from the ground truth, we might really have something here, as far as matching up on some of these other craters.

A17A1663100.speaker: Parker
A17A1663100.text: (Lost under the Public Affairs Commentator)

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: ...half-meter to one-third-meter, glass-lined, pit-bottom craters. (Pause) Look at the size of those things (the big blocks)! 166:33:28 Cernan: Boy, aren't they big mamas...mamoos. [Jacks traverse photos are AS17-142- 21671 to 21691 . Frame 21674 is a photo of the "big mamoos". Mamoos is slang for breasts.]

A17A1663100.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1663100.text: (Laughs) And it looks like they're probably the same thing that we sampled. They have the inclusions in them, white inclusions. They look like a mixture of the gray of the re-crystallized breccia, and the tan-gray of the anorthositic gabbro. (Pause) That must...Hey, look! There's Van Serg. Blocky-rimmed crater. That's the other side of Cochise there. See it?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1663404csm.text: Guess I can change the DAP here and get that out of the way. [Long pause.]

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah. Way over there.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah! Cochise is certainly a shallow crater, although we knew that. It doesn't have any...It only has one place I can see that has any blocks on the inner wall of Cochise. Otherwise, it has a surface much like what we're driving on - for walls and for the floor. One place on the south-southeast wall, there is a concentration of blocks much like we saw in Henry or in Horatio. But the rest of the crater seems to be pretty well mantled. (Pause) Van Serg is a very blocky rim crater, big blocks up on the rim.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Do you have a lot of static, Jack, or is it just me?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: No, I think it's just you. People are always giving you static. (Pause)

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Bob, if you are still reading me, I'm looking at the Sculptured Hills, and I still have that (impression of an) old man, wrinkled-face appearance, even up close at this Sun angle. And those wrinkles go from, generally, upslope at the west to downslope at the east.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1663404csm.text: Well, let's see, just kind of fouled that one up. Really wanted 142, narrow dead band, don't you, at 142, 269, and 0 - and 359? Thought we were already in that attitude.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: Hey, are you...No, you're right at the edge of Cochise. Aren't you?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Where? Right here?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah. Aren't you?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: No, we're not that close. Uh-uh. Cochise is up at...See that rim where those blocks are?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: No, that's a small crater.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Oh, I'll bet you that's Cochise up there. We've got to go quite a ways yet to get to...

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: How about a range and bearing there, guys?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: This sideslope driving is really a tough...

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: How about a range and bearing?

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Okay. It's 210/3.4.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: Copy that. 210/3.4. And you should be somewhat north of Cochise there, as per planning, although you may be cutting south to try (to avoid) going directly up-Sun.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: I guess that's some other...

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: That's just a depression. I think Cochise is over that rim.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: That's just a depression. Yeah, yeah. (Pause) Those are getting warm. (Pause) [Jack is probably saying that his hands are getting warm; either that or he has noticed the battery temperatures. However, only the temperature gauge for battery 1 is working - the other having failed during the rest period. In addition, the battery 1 temperature at the next stop will be 115ºF. Prior temperatures on this EVA were 95ºF at the start, 100ºF when they left the LM, and 108ºF at the start of Station 6. The temperature at the end of EVA-2 had been 114ºF degrees.] [Cernan - "I've got

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Boy, I tell you that. Every bump you go over on a sideslope is just accentuated. (Pause)

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah, we don't think you're anywhere near Cochise.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah. I agree.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah. I think it's over that rim up there.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: That's just a big, shallow depression. (Pause) [They are roughly 300 to 400 meters north of Cochise.]

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: All I'm doing is flying the 3.4-kilometer arc right now. [Cernan - "We do that a lot when you're flying an approach. I don't know why I was doing that. Maybe it was the Sun angle or the slope. It wasn't the direct route to where we were going; but, by staying at 3.4 from the LM, we were going to get there."]

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: Say again there, Gene.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: There's another one of those deep craters that doesn't have a blocky rim.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1663404csm.text: Copy.

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
