a17_1663404csm.text: That's one of the more striking characteristics of the mantle are these craters that look, as far as the diameter-to-depth ratio is concerned, like they ought to be fairly young. But there's no blocks on the rim, and they seem to have this mantled appearance, just like some of the large craters. (Pause)

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1663404csm.text: As I look up Wessex Cleft from just about abeam of it...(Turning to avoid an obstacle) Let me get over here...It still shows me an albedo change and a surface wrinkle-texture change. [Gene is driving generally southeast as he drives his 3.4-km arc as he approaches SWP. The Cleft is north, to his left; however, as he maneuvers to avoid craters and rocks, occasionally he gets a look in that direction.]

a17_1663404csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1663404csm.text: Yeah, I think so. You've got it at the same Sun angle more or less, on part of it there.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay, Ron. We're about 30 seconds from T - from Lunar Sounder Standby time.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: See that...Those two up there would be reasonably well up the slope. (Pause)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Bob, no parking constraints on the battery?

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: Roger. No parking constraints. We'll park at 045, Gene. Or wherever you like, really.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: I have to park about 045 because I've got to be pointing uphill so we can get out.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay. Any place you want to. 045 is fine.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Jack, I'm going to park...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1664637csm.text: 5 seconds.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: How about just the rim of that little crater there?

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1664637csm.text: Mark.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Well, this is so level right here, Jack, I'm going to just park it...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: Well, I was just thinking on top of that crater is closer to the...That's level, too, on the rim. And it'll give them a good view of the sampling area. (Pause) I think we can...If we work on those blocks there, we're in pretty good shape. (Pause)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1664637csm.text: Got it.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: Bob, we're directly downhill, and that is (to say, directly downhill) from the highest point that I could see up on this first Sculptured Hill. (Pause)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Bob, I'm parked at (a heading of) 026; bearing is 226; distance, 6.6; range, 4.0; amp-hours, 85 and 80; battery is 1...I think it's 115; and the motors are all off-scale low.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Not really, but...Okay...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: And here, we would like...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: ...0 (and) 230 on the forward; and off-scale low (on the left rear); 220 on the right rear.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay. There's your 1 minute, Ron.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay. Recorder is going Off, not to Heaters.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay. We copy that. We'd like to get the usual dusting here. (Pause) Up front.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Yeah. And I'm fairly level.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: Not really. (Laughing)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: I'm not, huh?

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: I just about rolled downhill again. [Schmitt - "Your ability to sense a slope in one-sixth g is not as great as it would be in one g. The extreme, of course, being zero g where you wouldn't sense a slope at all."] [On all of the Rover missions, the crews drove up slopes which seemed much steeper once they got off the Rover and tried to stand.]

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Oh, man. (Laughs) I am pointing uphill, aren't I?

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1664637csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Well, at least we don't have a sideslope.

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: And, 17, we'd like...

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: (To Bob) Battery covers stay closed?

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: Battery covers stay closed. But we do want the LCRU, and the TV camera, and the TCU (Television Control Unit) dusted. (Pause)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1664637csm.text: Okay. (Pause)

a17_1664637csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1664637csm.text: And, 17, we'd like the SEP blankets opened and dusted one more time.

A17A1664946.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1664946.text: Bob, the first block I looked at here looks like subfloor gabbro.

A17A1664946.speaker: Evans
A17A1664946.text: On TL-50. And, at the right-hand side - if you're looking at the thing from the bottom, the righthand side is 0 - go up 60 degrees. You're 60 degrees up from the horizontal and 30 degrees down from the vertical. It'll be something about like that.

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: Okay. We copy that. (Long Pause) [TV on.] Video Clip ( 3 min 33 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG )

A17A1664946.speaker: Cernan
A17A1664946.text: You even sound better. (Pause) Battery covers are awful dirty, but I will not dust them as long as you're happy.

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: Yeah. I don't think dusting the battery covers gives us any cooler batteries.

A17A1664946.speaker: Cernan
A17A1664946.text: Well, I know; but it keeps the batteries from getting dust in them. I've had pretty good luck with them. They've been pretty clean.

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: Roger on that. (Long Pause) [ Fendell pans counter-clockwise.] 166:51:10 Cernan: You are dusted; and you're shiny bright. All over. RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (1 min 06 sec)

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) We thank you. Ed (Fendell) thanks you.

A17A1664946.speaker: Cernan
A17A1664946.text: And we all thank you. Listen, if Ed thanks me, that's enough. (Pause) A man couldn't ask for any more than that. (Pause) [While Fendell is panning counter-clockwise through NE, Jack runs rapidly across the picture, going cross slope to the southeast. He is taking 3-4 foot strides.] [Cernan - "Jack is really covering some territory. The fact that the camera is panning in the opposite direction makes it look faster, but he's really moving across that slope."]

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: I think your LMP just ran away.

A17A1664946.speaker: Cernan
A17A1664946.text: Okay, I've got my thing...(Hearing Bob) Where'd he go? (Calling) Jack?

A17A1664946.speaker: Cernan
A17A1664946.text: Oh, there you are. I thought maybe you fell in that crater I'm looking at. (To Bob) Okay. I'm going to give you a TGE reading.

A17A1664946.speaker: Parker
A17A1664946.text: Roger. Give us a mark. 166:52:00 Cernan: Our fender's beginning to fade and, uh-oh, the clip came off (the replacement fender but not the Rover) on the inside; that's what's wrong. We'll have to fix that before we start. The outside one's holding, but the inside one's not.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1665157csm.text: Ron, I guess one of the things that at least goes through Stu's and my mind on that Shorty Crater - and I think you dispelled it when you say it goes out like in a 60-degree angular cone away from it. -_ But the question we'd really like to be thinking about - Is that a concentric coloring around there, like it might be just a layering from a flap ov - you know, a turned-over flap or something like that, or whether it just seems to be some sort of a - I don't want to say flow, but something that would give it direction that one - the one 60-degree direction like that.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Bob, all the blocks bigger than 20 centimeters that I've looked at up here are subfloor gabbro in appearance.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: I've looked at about five. (Pause) [Fendell reaches the TV's counter-clockwise stop, and then reverses direction.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Did we get a mark there on the gravimeter, Gene? [Gene had not given a mark, having been distracted by the fender clip.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Thirty seconds ago, Bob.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Roger. I copied it. Just wanted to check. (Pause)

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay, Jack. You find anything up there?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Gene, I'm going to go up and look at this one rock. Why don't you set up and sample any one of these other big ones. They're all the same. Like the one near the Rover. And I'll go up and try to get this big one down there.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay. We're - we're ending up looking at future passes, not today probably, but for the future and see if we can fit in one or two more observations to you here, where we can set up the back room like we had in all the - if you'll go along with that, and if we can fit it in, would you like to do that?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, okay.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: It's the only one left to look at, but right now we're dealing with subfloor material, I think.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: What about some of these little fragments that seem to be sitting more on the surface?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Yeah, we're supposed to rake here. We'll get those with the rake. [Fendell finds Gene north of the Rover at an appreciable distance. Jack is beyond him, hopping upslope and approximately three times farther away.] [Schmitt - "With that slope, the kangaroo hop was the only way to move."] [Cernan - "You couldn't really go one foot in front of the other uphill, because you can't get your foot high to take that step. So you hop."] [Schmitt - "I don't recall anybody ever walking up stairs in a pressurized suit."] [During the Apollo 16 EVA deployment at 121:22:45 , shortly after the loss of the heat

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: That one up there, by the way, is sitting on the surface. These others are submerged.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Yeah. That's why I want to look at it.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: You don't have a hammer, but if you need me, I'll come up there because I think that may be worthwhile. Video Clip ( 3 min 56 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 39 Mb MPEG )

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: I'll roll it down to you. 166:53:35 Cernan: Yeah. Thanks a lot. (Long Pause) [Gene makes his way cross slope to a boulder due north of the Rover. This is the sample 78135 location as indicated in the Station 8 plan map . Jack is climbing farther uphill to another rock, which is the sample 78220 location. Fendell starts to follow Gene, doesn't find him, and goes back to Jack. Gene's cross-Sun stereo pictures of the rock near the Rover are AS17-146- 22365 and 22366 . Ulli Lotzmann has created a stereo-image from the pair.] [Frame 22367 is a "locator" to the Rover. This excellent picture shows th

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: A reminder, 17. We'd like to have you leaving here in three-zero minutes to make up some of the (extra) time we spent at Stations 6 and 7. [Fendell finds Jack leaning over the upslope boulder. The plan map of Station 8, extracted from the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report, indicates that the boulder is approximately 53 meters ENE of the Rover. The TV record suggests that the boulder is directly uphill from the Rover. According to the mission report, Jack's heart rate peaks at about 167:05 at 122 beats per minute. Gene's peaks at about 167:10 at about 122 beats. These times correspond, rough

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: And we'd also remind you that we'd like a rake soil sample here, too. That may be the only way we try and pick up some stuff other than subfloor, if that, indeed, has come down from the top of the Sculptured Hills. 166:54:20 Schmitt: Okay, Bob. This rock is a big chunk of shattered, but still visible, bluish-gray anorthosite. It's glass-coated, and it actually looks like it's vesicular. I'm going to roll it downhill so we can work on it. Well, I'll document it first. (Pause) [Schmitt - "Good idea, Jack."] [Jack has taken cross-Sun photos of the boulder and is now taking a down-Sun from the rig

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1665157csm.text: I think Family Mountain is the bigger of the two mounds to the west of the landing site, isn't it?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Did you copy that?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Roger. I copy that. We'll be watching it coming.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay. But the point is, as Gene said, it's the only rock - (the only) big one anyway - in the area that I see that's perched on the surface as if it might have rolled here.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay. Copy that, Jack. (Pause)

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: But I don't see a (boulder) track. [Fendell zooms in on Jack. The rock is perhaps one third of a meter high and two-thirds of a meter across. From later evidence, it is also about two-thirds of a meter long in the direction away from the camera. It is also broader on the bottom than the top.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Man, this one here is tough as a...

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, we can get some small ones.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Yeah, that I'm going to do. I tell you, this one is so...

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay, H 2 Tank 2 Fan is On now; Tank 3 Fan is On.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: I thought you might be able to break it up.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, there's no...there's no corners on it. (Long Pause) [ Jack moves a few steps uphill. He turns his camera toward the Rover, takes a "locator", then moves to the upslope side of the rock. The "locator" is 21702 ; and 21703 is another down-Sun.] RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (0 min 40 sec)

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: (To Gene) Ready for this?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: We're ready. 166:56:28 Cernan: Bob, (bag) 563 is the sample.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Copy, 563. [Frame 22368 is a cross-Sun "after" of this sample.] [The samples from this rock are described in the Lunar Sample compendium for sample 78235 .]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Over here to the (garbled under Jack). Movie Clip by Peter Dayton (55 sec; 0.7 Mb)

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Are you ready? Are you ready for this?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: I'm not sure I am, but go ahead. (Pause) [Jack flips the rock over with his right foot. It starts to roll toward the Rover, but veers toward the right. Jack follows and kicks it again to keep it going. After a short while, it lands in a shallow depression and stops.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: (To the rock) Go! Roll! Look, I would roll on this slope, why don't you?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1665157csm.text: Ron, I just might draw your attention to the Flight Plan at 167:20, in that area where the Lunar Sounder finishes up, and it says that there will be no SIM bay or PCM data recorded until 169:03 and then you have to Configure the DSE there. Just want to draw your attention to that.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Five-sixths gravity that's missing. (Pause)

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Hey, I'll bet you they would like, if I didn't step on it, a sample out of the bottom of that thing. (Pause) Yup. (Pause) [Jack climbs back up to the place where he'd found the boulder, intending to sample the soil which it had been covering. Gene comes into view briefly, going away from the Rover and hopping uphill.] Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: These others all look...You're right, Jack, they look like what we've been sampling (that is, the subfloor gabbro). (Pause) And they're all pretty well mantled except the ones you got up there. There's one more piece I see on the side of that crater that may not be.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1665157csm.text: Hey, when you all drew that 60-degree angle, were you making that 63 degrees up from - not 60 - 60 degrees up from line 63?

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Bag 545 will be soil from under that anorthosite boulder. (Pause) Bob, the only thing that bothers me about that boulder being subfloor - I mean Sculptured Hills - is that it's glass-coated.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1665157csm.text: Copy that. [Gene reaches the rolled boulder. Jack is still sampling soil at the original boulder site, this time holding the sample bag low and at arm's length. He is holding the scoop nearer the handle than the head.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: It may have been thrown in here by an impact. (Pause; turning) Oh, you're here! [Jack goes down to Gene.]

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, let's sample it, and then roll it down.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, okay. I never would have moved it if I thought you were coming up.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: Well, I wasn't coming up; but I looked at some of those others, and there's only one more...

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Okay. Well, I got it documented up in place. Let's...That's not the...I think that's the side that was down. Let me roll it over... 166:58:40 Cernan: (Placing the gnomon) Well, let me get a piece of that side since it was underneath. Then we'll roll it over and get a piece of the other side.

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: Good thinking. (Pause) Ah...Okay, yeah. Let's do it (take documentation photos) again. Except I got dust all over it (meaning the rock).

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1665157csm.text: (Left of the rock) Well...

a17_1665157csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1665157csm.text: (Right of the rock) The albedo...The down-Sun picture's not going to mean much. Let me get this (soil) sample in your bag. (Pause; going to Gene) I think we ought to change your bag because the stuff's going to start flying out.

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1670203csm.text: Ron, we're going to lose you shortly, and all the systems look Go here. I've got a bet with EECOM that you'll get everything in the Flight Plan. You won't miss anything for me.

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1670203csm.text: (Turning to look) Okay, I see that one.

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1670203csm.text: That's a good one. I'll go get it with my tongs. That's a good one. That one I worked too hard to get. (Pause) [Gene goes about 20 meters to the right of the boulder, using a skipping gait as he goes slightly downhill.] [Cernan - "I was braking as I was going downhill and then I hopped on two feet coming back up. You can see the degree of that slope. It was a lot of work; I wasn't making much progress." Frame 22379 from the pan Gene will take at 167:07:20 shows the footprints Gene's makes during the little excursion, skipping out on the left and hopping back on the right.] 167:02:22 Cernan: He

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1670203csm.text: Hey, Houston. This is about a 50-50 mixture of what looks like maskelynite or at least blue-gray plagioclase, and a very, let's say, light yellow-tan mineral, probably orthopyroxene. It's fairly coarsely crystalline.

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1670203csm.text: Yeah. And the other one's not even circled; it's just north of the - the one in the bottom, and that's the one that - impact-type, because it's got ray - ray material, but it's a fresh impact bringing up bluish - bluish-type material.

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1670203csm.text: Copy that. [Cernan - (Tongue firmly in cheek) "I had that description written in my checklist, too. (General laughter) And, when I had to go pick up the chip of that boulder, Jack immediately picked up the cue and described it himself. Jack, this was going to be my big moment! You were going to let me do the whole thing, but you couldn't stand it."]

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1670203csm.text: Okay. When you guys get done with that rock, we'd like to get to the rake sample, please. And that's probably just as well done by the Rover as anyplace else. We don't seem to see anything worthwhile here doing besides that. [From his hands and knees position, Jack gets a sample bag and hands it to Gene.]

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1670203csm.text: (Referring to the fragment) You got it?

a17_1670203csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1670203csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Jack pushes back off of the rock but can't get his PLSS back far enough to rise. On the third try, he rocks his PLSS back far enough that he starts to tip over backwards. Once the PLSS is over his feet, he rises and hops back under the PLSS to catch himself.] 167:03:29 Cernan: Okay. That went in the same bag, Bob, as the rest of the chips from the bottom. All the chips from the bottom are in 464.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Did you get anything out of that little crater?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: (Going into a meter-deep crater just north of the rake-sample site) No. But I'm going to right now.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Okay.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Why don't you get your "after" picture (of the rake site) over there and go down and get that trench. I'll come down...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: You don't want a bag? Okay.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I can bag it. I can do it myself here. 167:14:37 Schmitt: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jack goes SE of the rake site to take a flightline series of photos. He hops north after each picture to get a stereo sequence. These photos are AS17-142- 21712 to 21715 .] [Frames 21713 and 21714 show Gene sampling in the crater with his tongs.] [Frame 21716 shows Gene examining his sample.] 167:15:04 Cernan: Boy, almost pure white and very friable. Oh, boy, is it. Pure white! Right out of a small little pit crater on the side of this crater I just walked in, Houston. And it's pure white, very friable. I got about,

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (On his way to the Rover) Bob, the walls of the big craters around here - that is, the ones that are, say, 15 meters in diameter - tend to be a little bit lighter albedo than ones down in the mantled area. (Pause) I'm afraid those pictures on that rake may be through a dust-colored lens. [Having hopped out of the crater, Gene gets the gnomon.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Well, they were also in my documented sample here, too. (Long Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: (Hopping toward the Rover, almost tripping) Okay. Where do you want this trench? On the side of this crater?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Well...

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I'll drop my gnomon...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: ...I don't know. I was just thinking about that. I think we ought to get out in the inter crater area to see if there's any stratigraphy to whatever the talus is. 167:16:54 Cernan: Okay, Jack. I'm going to leave the gnomon right here...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I'll get it.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: And, while you're digging that trench, we've got the pan to get, but I want to fix this fender. [Fendell finds Jack leaving Gene's seat, headed for the gate.] [Schmitt - "The level of emotion seems to have dropped off a little bit. We'd been walking up and down that hill for quite a while."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I guess the pan's mine, isn't it, this one?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Yeah, it is. And I want to fix the fender before...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Okay.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: ...before we leave. (Garbled)...

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Okay. We agree with that, and you might get us...

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: ...one, and I'll tighten...

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: ...you might get us the gravimeter reading there, Gene, while you're at it. And if you have time, you might drop the gravimeter on the ground, and we'll get a reading with it on the ground as well. Video Clip ( 2 min 50 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPEG )

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Holy Smoley! [Jack is probably taking "before" pictures of the trench site. Frames 21717 and 21718 are the cross-Sun pictures.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: The gravimeter is coming up.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Copy that. [Fendell reaches the counter-clockwise TV stop and reverses pan direction.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: You want it dropped on the ground, huh?

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Gently. 167:17:49 Cernan: Gently. I can't find a general level spot, but I'll level it. If it takes pictures...(correcting himself), or, if it does it's thing on the Rover (which isn't very level), it'll do its thing here. [Frame 21719 is Jack's down-Sun "before" of the trench site, showing Gene in the background taking the TGE off the Rover.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Yeah, this is just to get a check...

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Okay. Mark. (Garbled)

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: It's fender-fixing time; it's camera-taking-off time. (Pause) And I think I'll zap myself with a little cool water. [Cernan - "The reason the camera comes off is that I've got to get close to the fender. The camera keeps you about a foot away from anything. Plus you bang up the lens."] [Schmitt - "There's something I don't think I mentioned back at Station 7. We were talking about manipulating things more easily. When I was getting samples into a bag, I had mastered how to do that without the camera interfering; where, on the first and second EVAs - like Station 3 - I hadn't figured it out."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: And how's the trench going, Jack?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Oh, down. (Pause) [Fendell zooms in on the rock at the rake site.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Oh, man, I tell you. When you call for cold water, does it come in nicely. Whew! (Pause) I'm really happy with this fender, really happy with it. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Bob, I have gotten a wall now, in one place, that's standing about 25 centimeters high. And it shows no apparent change in the texture of the soil to that depth; except possibly at the lower 5 centimeters, there's some zones that might be slightly more granular. Particle size may be up a little bit. [Jack's speech pattern has slowed noticeably. He spends time searching for words.] [Schmitt - "Part of the reason is that I'm tired. It also happens when I'm thinking and trying to talk simultaneously - which I never did very well."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Okay. I copy that. Probably just three samples will be sufficient, then.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I think so. Maybe four. [Schmitt - "It was a judgment call based on how deep the trench was. You'd take one at the bottom, one is the middle, and a skim off the top."] Video Clip ( 3 min 10 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Be there in a minute, Jack.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Oh, that's all right. I can probably get started. (Pause) [Jack's heart rate is down to about 90 beats per minute. Gene's is only down to about 110.] RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (2 min 21 sec)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Ohhhh, boy!

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Need some help?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Nope. (Pause) Boy, we're sure giving this suspension system a workout. Whew! I can even see it. (Long Pause) [Cernan - "I was leaning over the fender, putting pressure on the Rover; and I think I was bouncing it up and down. I think that each wheel had a V-type torsion bar (see 20453 ) because the Rover had been folded up for storage in the LM. We didn't have shock absorbers because we would have had dust problems."] [Schmitt - "The Rover was parked with the rear end downhill, so you were more or less able to stand there looking at it."] [Fendell finds Jack southeast of the Rover, trying to an

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Well, everything's getting awful dusty.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Boy, everything is stiff. Everything is just full of dust. There's got to be a point where the dust just overtakes you, and everything mechanical quits moving. [Schmitt - "Anyone planning to work on the Moon or Mars ought to have Gene's statement engraved on their forehead and on the inside of their glasses."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Still struggling) Like scoops. (Pause) 167:21:22 Cernan: I'm not sure whether Detroit would like the fender, but it will sure buy the fix. Okay, it's fixed.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: And I'm happy; I like it.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Roger. We copy that. And copy it again. [Jack gives up on the scoop head and sets it at angle of about 20 degrees from vertical.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: And we'd like to have you guys moving in about 3 minutes.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: And again on the (garbled). (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Responding to Bob's "3 minutes") Good luck!

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: You need any help (garbled) bag those samples, huh?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Yes, sir. I think I do. I can't adjust my scoop to my self-bagging method. [Schmitt - "This confirms what I thought back when we were going through Station 7 - that the 90 degree angle was something I'd worked out in order to bag samples more easily when I was working alone. I'd hoped to do that here while Gene was doing something else; but, now, Gene's come over and we'll go back to two-man sampling routine."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: (Going to Jack) Let me get back on some lighter cooling here, too, to save some water. Okay, now.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Okay; the bottom 10 centimeters...

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Let me get your bags...I left my camera off when I...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: ...of a... [Gene gets one of Jack's sample bags.] 167:22:12 Schmitt: Well, shoot! I didn't take a picture of the trench after I dug it. Let me take one shot. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: What's this? The bottom?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Backing up to take pictures) That's the bottom. [Jack's pictures of the trench are AS17-142- 21720 , 21721 , 21722 , and 21723 .]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Okay. The bottom is in 548. It's very cloddy. Looks very much like the surface we're standing on except it clods up quite a bit more. Can you tell anything from the trench itself?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I told them...I talked to them a little bit about it.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Okay.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: It looked a little coarser-grained, but that's all. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: It sure holds a nice wall, though.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Yep.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: That's the kind of wall I expect those core tubes held. Video Clip ( 3 min 10 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 31 Mb MPEG )

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: You got another one (bag)? Okay. Skim of the upper...We'll see how well I do. (It's a) skim sample of the upper half centimeter. Maybe a centimeter deep. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Pouring) Okay. Can you hold that?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I'm going to put it in your bag.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Presenting his SCB) Is it going to fit in there?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Well, there's no choice, right now. Let me...Yeah, these little ones will fit in there. (Pause) Stand by. I want to put this one in there, too. That's in bag 549.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: (Sealing the bag and putting it in Jack's SCB) Okay. Try again. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Okay, the upper...Below that skim: the next 5 centimeters. (Pause) [Schmitt - "After I got the skim, I just stuck the scoop part way in the wall and scraped upward to get the next 5 centimeters."]

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Put it (the bag) down, Geno.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Well, just put it (the scoop) over it (the bag).

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Well, I can't turn it (the scoop). (Pause) [Gene has been holding the sample bag at about chest height, thereby forcing Jack to fully extend his arm and raise it over his head to pour.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Scraping a deeper section of the trench wall) And the next 10 centimeters down...(Pause) (To Gene) Can you get this one too?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Yep. (Pause) [Gene gets another sample bag and holds it at about the same height; Jack solves the pouring problem by rotating the scoop.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Now, I got to get your bag (SCB).

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: (Presenting his SCB) Okay. That was the next 10 centimeters; and, then, the first sample, of course, was the 10 centimeters below that.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Roger. Copy that.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: And that last bag was 551.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Okay. Copy that. We're ready for you guys to move out.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Okay. 167:25:15 Cernan: You didn't get a pan here. While I clean up the Rover, you can get your "after" of the trench in the pan.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I will.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I'll get the TGE and clean up the Rover.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: That's affirm. We agree with that. [They both turn to look at the trench.]

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: What's the key that keeps...I keep getting keyed.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: It sounds like Bob's stepping on his foot mike.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Yeah, he's so excited...

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Okay...

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: ...he can't stand it.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: You done with the gnomon?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Yup. [Jack has taken two final "afters" of the trench. These are 21724 and 21725 .]

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Okay.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I'll get the pan.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: (Getting the gnomon and heading for the gate) You get your pan, and I'll get the TGE and clean up.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: You took a pan up the hill there?

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Yeah; I took it way up there, somewhere. 167:25:47 Schmitt: Okay. I'll take it right here, then. (Pause) Uh, oh.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: What?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Samples came out.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: A sample came out?

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: I'll pick it up.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Yeah, your top came open. It's awful full, Jack. If you can't get it, I'll get it with the tongs. [The top of Jack's SCB is flapping open. Two sample bags have fallen out.] 167:26:06 Schmitt: Go ahead and go to work, and I'll get the pan first. I lost two of them, I guess.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Yeah, those are the last two I put in there. Your bag is so full they won't stay. Let me give them a reading here. Hey, Bob, can I move it on the Rover and then give you a reading? Video Clip ( 3 min 41 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG )

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Yes. As long as you're careful not to hit the button while you're doing it. 167:26:25 Cernan: Yeah, I can. I'll do it. (Responding to Bob) I won't hit the button. Just easier to do it that way. I don't know why I asked you; I know I can. (Pause) [ Jack's Station 8 Pan photos are AS17-142- 21726 to 21745 .] [This is an excellent pan.] [Frame 21727 shows the Rover tracks made as they approached this stop and, as well, Cochise Crater just above the center of the image.] [Frame 21728 shows more of the Rover tracks and, in the distance, the light-colored, sunlit face of the Scarp.] [Frames 21729 ,

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: Even this thing ( TGE ) doesn't want to go on; it's so dusty. Okay. It's on and it's locked, and here's your reading. 670, 117, 301; that's 670, 117, 301.

A17A1671427.speaker: Parker
A17A1671427.text: Okay. We copy that. [Schmitt - (To Gene) "I don't know if you were aware of it or not, but one of the most successful experiments that we conducted was the portable gravimeter. They got great readings all across the valley; and the interpretation is great about the depth of the basalt fill in the valley - about two kilometers deep."] [Cernan - "I'm glad; and I do think I remember that. But it was always a pain number one in the butt."] [Schmitt - "And what it tells you is that the valley used to be almost five kilometers deep before it filled up. The eruption of mare basalt started very soon a

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I've got to dust that thing (the TGE ) the next time around. Jack, we've got to do some bag (SCB) changing here.

A17A1671427.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1671427.text: Yup.

A17A1671427.speaker: Cernan
A17A1671427.text: I'll get those things with my tongs. You can't get them. You'd have to bend over. Every time you jump around, you come close to losing something. (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 7 min 47 sec ) RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde (3 min 04 sec)

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Arriving with the tongs and picking up the first sample bag) I'll just take them back there. Put them under the seat.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. (Pause) You want me to take that one?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Now getting the second sample bag) No, I got it.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. (Pause) [They head toward the Rover.] [Cernan - "Coming down those shallow slopes is poetry in motion. That's productive use of your time. If you could do something like helicopter skiing - have somebody drop you off at the top and pick you up at the bottom - you could really cover a lot of territory."] [Schmitt - "In that Essex study, my proposal for the Mars part of it was that you have a Rover that you can run either manually or automated. So if the pair were out working, you could have somebody else, say back at the base or the lander, remotely move it to where you want it. And then,

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Damn.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: You got another one dropped there, Gene. Jack got it.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Another one?

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Jack's getting it.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay. (Pause) [Jack gets the fallen sample with the scoop and carries it back to the Rover as in an egg-and-spoon race.]

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Jack, we've got to make a place in here for that full bag. Let me put the small can over there, and core tube over there.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: (Holding the sample, still in the scoop, up to the TV) Have a sample. 167:28:27 Cernan: Okay. Let me take your bag off first.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. Well, you might as well fill it as full as you can.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yeah, I am. (Marveling at the weight of Jack's SCB as he starts to take it off) Holy Smoley! (Laughing) Turn to the left. (Pause) Okay. It's off. Let me fill it. (Pause) [Gene is at Jack's seat with the SCB. Jack goes to the gate.]

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Your bag isn't in much better shape.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Roger. We'd like to have you check the Commander's bag. You might put them both under the seat there.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Well, we're running out of bags, aren't we?

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. We've got one bag left...we should have there. It was on the gate, right?

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay...

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yeah. We had put it (the SCB which had been on the gate) under the seat. Okay, bag number 4 (which Jack has been wearing) is absolutely full. (Pause) and it's under Jack's seat.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I suggest that you take the other bag that's on the gate there, and put that on either you or Jack. And also, the Commander's bag is pretty full also, we suspect. [Gene has removed an empty SCB, from under Jack's seat.]

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Why don't you put it on me? Mine gets full faster, somehow. [The reason, of course, is that Jack is doing most of the sampling while Gene holds the sample bags and then puts them in Jack's SCB.] Video Clip ( 2 min 21 sec 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 23 Mb MPEG )

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: You might check Gene's bag anyway.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Stay there, stay there. I'm trying to get the bottom hook.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Oh, I'm sorry. (To Bob) I checked it. He's got about six samples to go.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. And...

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: And I just want to be sure that it's locked down. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay. Well, turn to the left so I can get this other hook. (Pause) Okay. It's not coming out; I guarantee you that. Now...

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. And SCB-5 is one for the LMP if you want to take it off the gate.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: ...(garbled) check yours one more time. And that's locked.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: We got it.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Turning so that Jack can check his SCB) SCB-5 is on the LMP.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: There is nothing on the gate. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Well, I think that (Gene's SCB top)'ll stay down, but it's not very good...

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I've got one more loose sample I'm going to throw in the big bag back there. You happy (with the SCB)?

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: (Referring to the loose sample) A local one, you mean?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yeah.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Well...

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Well, let me leave it under your seat.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: No, let's...Can I put a bag around it?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: No, it's got a bag around it. It's all bagged. It's right there.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: (Garbled) 167:31:00 Parker: (Seeing Jack standing idle) Okay. Jack, while Gene's doing that, why don't you read the SEP temperature, or somebody read the SEP temperature anyway, and close the blankets.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I'll do that. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay, Bob. Let's see, you got your (gravimeter) readings...

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Copy. 120.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Those blankets just aren't staying closed. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I guess we're ready to head on out. Do you agree?

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. And, Gene, when you go to change the LCRU, we'd like you to turn it to Off. O-F-F, on the Power switch, the Internal Power, External switch. And we'll be reading you through the LM. It will give you a chance to cool down the LCRU on the way home to Station 9.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: All right.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: And, Houston, what's the temperature limit on the DSEA (the SEP Data Storage and Electronics Assembly)?

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Stand by, Jack. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "I think that I was getting so that I didn't quite trust Houston. They kept having us fool around with the SEP and my feeling was that it was probably gone. So I'm trying to prod them a little bit, having just told them that it was 120 (degrees) and my memory, at the time, was probably that that was way outside the limits. Literally, the science room was leading us down the garden path on the SEP, because all this SEP stuff we were doing was wasting time. It had quit working when? Sometime in the first EVA, didn't it? As with the (long-period) gravimeter

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Do you read us, Bob, through the LM?

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Roger. We read you through the LM. Do you read us through the LM?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yeah. Not as well, but we're reading you.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. And the temperature limit, Jack, is 160. We'll just leave it as is until we get back to the LM. [This may be a temperature at which physical damage may occur to some of the SEP components. Bob doesn't mention the 108 degree shut off until 167:59:07, when they get to Station 9.]

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I was going to say, we could take it out and put it under the seat or something, but that sounds all right.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay. An EMU status check. I'm at 3.88 (psi suit pressure), and I got 48 percent (oxygen), no (warning) flags, and I'm Intermediate cooling .

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Copy that.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: And the LMP is at 47 percent, no flags, 3.86. Hey, Gene?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yeah.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Well...Bob, I guess...Remind us to change the LRV Sampler (the "Dixie cup" sampler) at the next station. It's almost out of bags.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Well, let's do it next time around.

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: Okay. When you get on, Jack, you can give me a frame count as you start moving. 167:33:28 Schmitt: Yep. (Pause) (To Gene, who has fallen) Hang on. Need some help?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Nonchalant) Nope.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Go downhill. Get your feet downhill.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Yep. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Let me help you.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Laughs)

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Watch it, there's a crater right behind you.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: I got it. I got it. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Here. Here. Grab my hand.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Okay, now, just push up on my head. [By pushing back on the front of Gene's helmet, Jack can get him rotating back over his knees.]

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Okay. I'm not going to do it too hard. Going backwards.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: It's all right; just push up. Okay. Okay.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: (Chuckling) Boy, are you...(Chuckling) You('ve) got your pockets completely filled with dirt.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: Well, extra sample.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Do we throw those pockets away this time around?

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Laughing) Extra sample. (Pause)

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Are you a mess!

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Laughs) Well, that one was coming for a long time!

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: My hands are already tired from dusting you.

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: That one was coming. I keep trying to blow the dust off my camera, which is very frustrating.

A17A1672735.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1672735.text: Very ineffective, too. (Pause) [Cernan - "At least I fell off-camera."]

A17A1672735.speaker: Cernan
A17A1672735.text: (Preparing to mount the Rover again) Okay. Do we try that trick again? (Long Pause) You know that happened on an upslope getting on the Rover. Okay. I'm all locked in. Let me know when you are. How come we haven't deployed any charges? I guess the last one...I remember when that one is. Okay. MP3 Audio Clip ( 17 min 44 sec )

A17A1672735.speaker: Parker
A17A1672735.text: We'll deploy one at Station 10.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Okay. (Consulting checklist page LMP/CDR-20 ) We're heading to Station 9 pointed about 267. Okay, and they're reading us through the LM, so I won't worry about the low-gain. We're powering up. The switch is on. Okay, I'm going to make a turn to the right.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. And the updated (Rover) headings, since you're at the north end of Station 8, will be something like about 240.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Okay, Bob. 240. [The heading of 267 indicated on the checklist for the drive to Station 9 would have been valid had they done Station 8 at the south end of the planned area. Because they are at the northern end, their average heading will be more to the south.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Bob, I think your rake sample here at the Sculptured Hills is going to have to tell the tale combined with the observation that most of the blocks we saw were, like (the one) Gene sampled, looked like subfloor gabbro. It's conceivable that the Sculptured Hills could be the same kind of material. I think it's fairly clear that the boulder population does not resemble the Massif (boulder) population at all.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) 167:36:44 Schmitt: (Laughs)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: You been riding on this downslope all the time!?!

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (Laughing) Yes, but...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: And you hadn't said anything, huh?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Scary, isn't it?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: (Laughing) Man, I'm glad I'm driving! [Cernan - "The 240 heading - southwest - put me on the downslope side of the Rover. And what I'm saying here is that I'm never going to put myself on the downslope again."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. And, Jack...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: (Still laughing)

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: ...when you're not holding on with two hands, we'd like the frame count from you.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Wait a minute. Yeah. (To Gene) Is that Van Serg over there? [Van Serg is WSW of Station 8, beyond the southern rim of Cochise but short of Shakespeare.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Ahhhh...

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Should have a bearing (at Station 9) of 234...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: I think it's...

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: ...and a range of 2.1.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: I don't know...No...It's...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: (To Bob) Okay. (Pause) (To Jack) We got to get around SWP (means "Bowen") here and then ... Well, that's...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: ...and then head on more westerly.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: LMP frame is at 80.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Copy 80.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: SWP...(correcting himself) or Bowen, I mean. Bowen, I guess that is.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well...(Pause) That's SWP over there. Bowen is out here ahead of us.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yeah. (Pause) Guess he said...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Bowen isn't much of a crater on the map. [During the initial stages of the drive, they are headed more or less southwest, toward the South Massif and Bear Mountain. Jack's traverse photos are AS17-142- 21746 to 21751 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: ...225? What did you say, Bob? 225 what?

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Heading ought to be about 240; 240 for a heading for there. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Did you hear him? I didn't hear him.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: 240. Are you not reading him?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: But what did he say for bearing and range? That's what I'm interested in.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: (Enunciating the digits slowly) 234...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: 240. State bearing and range, Bob.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Okay. I got that. (Long Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. And we think you're even farther north than I was saying. Maybe it's about 215 would be your heading for there.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Okay, Bob. I'll find it. 234/2.1.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. [Cernan - "Because of the slope and the craters, we made some wide turns and I just wanted to know where we wanted to go, not how to get there."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: And all the big blocks still look like subfloor from the Rover. But "big blocks" in here are only about a third of a meter in diameter. And they're subrounded to subangular. Okay. We're out on the plains again now, just off the break in slope (coming down off the Sculptured Hills) (Long Pause) 167:39:41 Cernan: That stuff sure looks like outcrop down in the East Massif on the lower slopes, where the high albedo is. Doesn't it? See it over there? [The East Massif summit is SSE of their present position. As mentioned previously, this outcrop area is visible in AS17-146- 22367 , a photo taken fro

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah. Yeah; it does. (Pause) It was one of my guidelines for the geophone deployment...(correcting himself) (I mean) "guide points". (Pause) [Schmitt - "When I was laying out the east geophone line, I had picked out a point on the horizon to walk towards."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: There's some more of that blue-gray rock there on the east end of the South Massif, down low.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yep. [They are headed southwest again. Jack's traverse photos covering the drive from here to the rim of Cochise are AS17-142- 21755 to 21764 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: It looks like it might have been a slump block or something.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yep. You can see it's blue-gray because of it's contrast with the light mantle.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yep. It might be a slump block, or something like that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Jack, I'm going to go to the left. [Cernan - "Note the change in course."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: You going to go through...(Laughs)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Need 234...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (Garbled).

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: No, No. I'm going over here. This is closer. It's a shorter cut.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: That's probably Bowen there, don't you think?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: I think...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Ahhh, well (not sure)...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Well, see, we never got too far...

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: How about a range and bearing, guys.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (Garbled) aren't very far from SWP.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Maybe we got too far east. (Responding to Bob) Okay. It's 228/3.4. And we're moving along at 10 to 12 clicks. That's all it'll hack.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Copy that. (Pause) How about an amps reading? We haven't had one of those for a couple of (garbled). 167:41:11 Schmitt: Starting to rain again. [The replacement fender has started to fail, flapping around and allowing the rear wheel to shower them with dust.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Got a crater ahead of you.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Oooh, boy.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Down-Sun isn't much easier than up-Sun.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: It's just easier on the eyes. (Chuckles) You just can't see any more, that's all. (Pause) You don't have that static, huh? [At Houston's request, they turned the LCRU off at 167:31:36 and are transmitting directly from their OPS antennas to the LM.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Nope. (Pause) Hope you've still got an (OPS) antenna; I haven't looked recently.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Well, there's no holes in the high-gain. [A hole in the high-gain antenna would indicate that Gene had caught his OPS antenna in it and, possibly, broken it off. Gene doesn't remember having such troubles in training.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Might have hit it on a rock (when you fell at Station 8).

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: (Reacting to a rock or crater in their path) Oh, boy!

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Okay. We're back into the mantle area (and the) population of fragments is still one percent or so. The crater out off to our left, which is at 227 and three point ...What is that? Three point what? Three?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: It is a fairly good-sized depression, but it's completely mantled. There's no blocks showing in the wall at all. (Pause) How do you read, Bob?

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Loud and clear. We're listening. [Note that, despite Jack's earlier complaints about needless acknowledgments from Houston, here he wants to make sure that they are being heard.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Now, there's a crater in the wall of that depression or the small one near it. And it has one big block in the side, as if it penetrated the mantle and exposed some of the wall of the depression. Just about a 30-meter crater. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Valley of Taurus-Littrow is not planar!

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: No, it isn't. (Pause) I'm glad we changed it to a "subfloor" instead of the "plains" unit. (Gene laughs) [Schmitt - "I think that, at some point in the deep, dark past, the geologists at Flagstaff may have called the valley fill the 'plains unit'. You referred to these things as they appeared in the (overhead) photographs - the floor, the plains of the valley. They may have called it the plains unit at one time and then, because we're talking about the rocks - what's underneath that floor - decided to refer to it as the subfloor basalt."] [The decision to call the bedrock "subfloor" seems to h

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Okay. We're in the inner wall of the depression here, and the rocks still look like subfloor gabbro. Boy, there's certainly not much variety. (Pause) In general, there are few exotics ... 167:43:34 Cernan: Ooh, now that's got to be Cochise.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Ah, look at Cochise.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: That's Cochise!

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. We think you're coming up on Cochise.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Get yourself a couple pictures while you're looking right at it.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Could you swing right. Swing right. [Frame 21765 shows the approach to the rim of Cochise.] [Frames 21766 , 21767 , and 21768 show the interior of the crater.] 167:43:44 Cernan: Bob, we are on the northeastern rim of Cochise. I'm going to work my way around the other side.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: And Bob...

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. Copy that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: ...looking at the western wall of Cochise, I can see a contact within the subfloor between albedo units, one of which is a light tan-gray and the other is a light blue-gray. (It) may reflect the two kinds of subfloor gabbro we've already sampled. Vesicular and non-vesicular. And that contact looked like it was dipping...(The) apparent dip in the wall was to the north. In the west wall dipping to the north about 20 degrees. [The contact is visible in 21780 , dipping down to the right, just above the TV camera and intersecting the right-front corner of the TV camera mirror. The picture was taken

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) Which one's on top? Can you tell?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah. The blue-gray's on top. I'm sorry.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Thank you. And you got a bearing and range there at the rim of Cochise?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: I took a picture of it and... 167:44:56 Cernan: (Answering Bob ) Okay. We're at 228/3.0, and we're headed south and not quite on the east rim.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: All right. [AS17-142- 21769 to 21777 are taken as they skirt the rim of Cochise, headed south at first and then southwest.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: I'll give you a hack at the east rim. [That is, when they are east of the center of the crater.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Bob, I got a picture of that contact, so...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: (To Bob) I took some pictures right into Cochise, too, when we were coming up. [AS17-146- 22404 to 22408 are Gene's pictures from the east rim of Cochise.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Good. It'll show on yours, too, probably. I hope. (Pause) Okay. We're sort of on the inner...(Garbled)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Mark. 230/2.9. We're on the east rim.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Copy that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well, we're sort of inside the east rim a little bit.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Well, don't get too far inside.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: We're halfway between the rim and where the blocky wall starts.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: All right. Copy that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Did you get that, Bob?

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Yeah. We got that. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Cochise is much like Horatio - actually, more like Camelot, although not as blocky in the walls, in general - in that it has blocky walls but a mantled rim. (Pause) Again, all the blocks I see in here - big ones and blocks down to about 20 centimeters - are subangular, in general, and appear to have the appearance of the subfloor gabbro; although most of the smaller rocks do not appear to be highly vesicular.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: All right. We're copying that all. (Long Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: We're at 232 and 2.7.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Watch it. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: You know what happened there?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: What? 167:47:32 Cernan: I was just about to take a picture, and the minute you take your eye off anything... [Gene's picture is 22409 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeh. (Pause) I got another view of that contact, and let's put that on the northwest wall of Cochise and dipping to the southeast. (Is ) that right?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: South and east is to our left.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: No, no, no, no, no. Put it on the northwest wall dipping to the northeast. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yeah, that's right. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: See that, Geno, can you see that over there?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Oh, yeah! I can see it now between the gray and blue-gray?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Oh, yeah! Yes, I sure do.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Can you swing in there, and let me get another shot of it? 167:48:25 Cernan: You betcha. (Pause; Jack laughs) Now, there's a good view right here. [Jack's photos into Cochise from this location are AS17-142- 21778 to 21782 . Gene's are AS17-146- 22410 to 22412 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Okay now, I need to have you go left. (Pause) 167:48:40 Cernan: Okay. I got two of them in there, too.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Great. 167:48:43 Cernan: Look at that rock right in front of us. It looks like a contact between a blue and a gray.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Oh, yeah, there it is. Yeah, you're right.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: We can't get down to it, but take a picture.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well, I think we've done...I think we've got that (contact) relationship. I think we got it at Station 1, as a matter of fact. [Cernan - (Tongue still firmly in cheek) "At 48:50, where Jack says 'I think we've got that relationship', I don't want anyone to misinterpret the fact that we've been on the Moon three days. (Laughing) 'We can't get down to it, but at least we can take a picture.' "] [Schmitt - "It'd be a little hard to have a relationship in those suits, anyway."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: But that's a big beautiful boulder on the...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah, that's...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: ...inner rim...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: ...that's quite a block.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: ...inner south rim of Cochise.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Oooh...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: It's a single block. [This is the block in 21777 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: That's how you bend your tires. [Schmitt - "Gene was still talking about the rock in Cochise, and I was talking about a rock he hit."] [Cernan - "We're moving pretty rapidly through this area. If you're going ten kilometers (per hour) and you hit a football (sized rock), you feel it. We put some dents into those wire-wheel tires."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Well, that's what it (the wire wheel)'s for. (Pause) Boy, that's a nice...Oh, man, would that be (garbled)...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well, now, that might be glass covered. That might be a glass coating; the way it sort of hangs on the outside there. Hard to say.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: We're at 234 - can't see it - 2.5. 167:49:23 Schmitt: Starting to sling dust. I wonder if we've lost our fender.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. Copy that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: No, they're on there tight. (Garbled) warp. [Gene seems to be speculating that the fender has warped. He had tightened the inside clamp at Station 8 and, once he and Jack reach Station 9, they will take another look. At 167:56:11, they find that the fender has, indeed, warped. Gene brought the fender back to Earth. It is currently on display at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum in Washington. The rear portion of the fender - the last two or three inches that would have borne the brunt of the rooster tail - appears to be badly worn.] [Schmitt - "And if there is dust between the cl

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: You think that's Van Serg? Right over there.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Well, let's see...(Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: There it is. Betcha you.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yeah. I think you're right, because that's just about the right place. Let's see, 234 and 2.1 is where I want to go, and I'm at 230/2.5.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Okay, our...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Pretty close. [Jack's photos taken during the drive from Cochise to Van Serg are AS17-142- 21783 to 21788 .]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Our block population in here now - on the south rim of Cochise and out ahead of us - looks like it's up to 5 percent. (Pause) And it all looks like light, tan subfloor gabbro...or tan-gray. You don't see much blue-gray; not out on here. (Pause) There's a recent hit, (a fresh crater).

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: This Rover is getting tested for what it was built for now.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeh. (Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: I tell you it handles just the way as advertised, maybe even better.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. We think you guys are getting to the point we ought to swing a little bit west to make that 234/2.1.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yeah, I am, Bob.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: I think we've got it. Tally-ho... ["Tally-ho"is a call made during a hunt when the fox is first seen.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Bob, that's my fix. I'm just navigating to it.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: I know where. I'll get there.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Roger. [Cernan - "I was getting irritated with Bob for telling me how to get where I'm going. There was a touch of it a page or two ago and you're seeing it again here. What Bob doesn't see is that you don't just go from here to there. I might have to go around something, and I can see why I'm saying 'Damn it, I'm too good of a pilot not to know where I'm going! Don't tell me; just tell me where I need be and I'll be there.' Jack used to get irritated at Bob, and this is the first sign of my irritation."] [Throughout these transcripts, Gene has shown great restraint in the face of provocation

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: We have a Tally-ho on Shorty...I mean of Van Serg. (Bob chuckles) How about through there, Geno?

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Thanks.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Let's not pre-judge the crater too much.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: You want 234/2.1. Okay.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: And remember we talked about parking on the southeast rim.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: It wanders like...Our wander-factor in here has got to be 50 percent.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: Copy that. [Cernan - "We had been moving at 10 or 12 clicks for a while but we're not moving that fast here. We're picking our way through here, probably at low speed, but as fast as we can get through the block field. With a wander factor of 50 percent, I've got to drive 15 meters to go forward 10."]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Bob, you're being cut out. I can't tell what you're saying. (To Gene) Isn't that where we want to go, over there?

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well...Look, (garbled) way to get...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: ...(garbled) found the crater.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: No, we didn't. It's there on the right.

A17A1673530.speaker: Parker
A17A1673530.text: ...It doesn't make much difference, 17. If you see Van Serg, that's what we want.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well, you're...

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Let me wander over that way. That's where I want to get, but I couldn't go there because of that...(Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: There's a different looking rock there. 167:51:54 Parker: And remember, we're talking about parking on the southeast rim. (Pause) [Frame 21789 shows the Van Serg ejecta and 21790 shows the rim.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (To Gene) Yeah, I think you're going to have to bear right.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Yep. That's why I...I've got to get through this (boulder) field, though.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Yeah, I know. (Laughs; Pause) Okay, Bob. We're still primarily in an extreme block field here now. It's up to a 20 percent cover, and...(20 percent cover) of fragments, mostly the subfloor. Some of it looks quite highly shattered. I just saw one piece that looked like a white anorthositic rock.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: How's this look to you? We can go farther up there, I guess. Let me go farther up.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Get a little farther on the southeast. A little higher...

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: Well, okay, if you can get up.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (Garbled) to overdo it.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Well...(Pause)

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: There is some grayish rocks that are...Oops! High centered. [Gene has scraped the bottom of the Rover on a rock.]

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Right, coming up here. I turn to the right and park right here.

A17A1673530.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1673530.text: (Returning to his description of the grayish rocks)...that have somewhat of a swirl texture.

A17A1673530.speaker: Cernan
A17A1673530.text: Okay, Bob, we're at 230/2.2.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1675309csm.text: Hello, Houston; America. It looks like we're with you again.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675309csm.text: Yep. What did I say? 230? I meant...Yeah, bearing is 230/2.2, and I'm parked on a heading of 320, which gives you a better view.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: Oh, boy. This (seatbelt) is getting harder and harder (to release). (Long Pause)

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: Well, what's wrong with it, now. I might have got it twisted.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675309csm.text: Here, let me look at it.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: Got it hooked, but not so I can get it undone. 167:54:14 Cernan: Here, let me look at it. I'd say "stay put", but I don't think you have any choice. That fender just curled under, that's where we're getting the dust. (Pause) Starting to warp. Look at those other fenders, talk about warping. [Cernan - "I'm out of my seat and I'm walking behind the Rover to see if I can't help Jack with his twisted seatbelt. And, while I'm there, I see the fender curled under. That's where we're getting our dust. And, maybe the other fenders were getting hot and twisted in the Sun."] [Schmitt - (To Gene) "Isn't

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: Did I get it (the seatbelt) twisted or something?

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675309csm.text: Yeah, you did twist it when you put it on. Okay, scrunch down.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675309csm.text: Okay. (Pause) You had one twist in it.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: Boy, that makes a difference (by shortening the belt).

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675309csm.text: Sure does. Here. (Pause) Your footpan's down, too. [Gene has rotated Jack's footrest out of the way.]

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675309csm.text: I'll get it. (Pause) It's lost it's stiffness in there. Okay, I guess nominal plan for Shorty, huh? Or Van Serg.

a17_1675309csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1675309csm.text: Ron, we're Go for retraction on HF Antenna 2, HF Antenna 2. You're Go for retraction.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Van Serg looks like a blocky-rim, fresh impact crater right now.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay. We copy that. How about scuffing your feet and seeing if it looks orange underneath?

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Slight differences...(Stops to listen to Bob) Don't worry.

A17A1675510.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1675510.text: Hold on that, Ron. Hold. We've lost data here 2 second. Please hold.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: And, Gene, before you go away, we'd like the rest of the Rover readouts, like batteries. And how about a SEP temp readout before one of you guys leaves there?

A17A1675510.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1675510.text: Ron, will you verify you hadn't started to retract them yet?

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
