A17A1675510.text: Can you get that (SEP) on that side, Jack.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: I will.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: (To Bob) Should have TV.

A17A1675510.speaker: Evans
A17A1675510.text: Yes, verified. I did not touch anything.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Rog. We have it, and I'm sure that Ed ( Fendell ) would like a good dusting job up front. [TV on. Jack is at the SEP ; Gene is leaning over the instrument panel from beside his seat.] Video Clip ( 3 min 50 sec 1.0 Mb RealVideo or 38 Mb MPEG )

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Well, there's so much...

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: I'll dust it if you can't read it.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: ...dust.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: I'll get it.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: I've got it.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: I'll get it.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: (I've) wiped the dust off (the SEP) just over the gauge. It's about 125 on the SEP.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay. Copy that. 167:56:11 Schmitt: Boy, everything is really bad now. The (replacement) fender warped.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Yeah, the fender dug under. See if you can straighten it out. [Fendell pans counter-clockwise, past Jack who may be trying to put some fore-aft creases in the fender to prevent the back end from folding under.]

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay, and leave the covers...

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Okay. Amp hours, 82 and 80. Battery, 122 and off-scale low. Forwards are 210, 240; Rears are 225 and 220.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay. We copy that. 167:56:43 Cernan: That's just a sample of the kind of dust we would have got, Jack, if we hadn't of had that fender yesterday. Fender's almost worn out. [When the replacement fender was installed, the map sheets were quite stiff; they no longer are. Gene brought the replacement fender back to Earth and it is on display at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. Ken Glover has provided a photograph of the underside of the fender , with the aft portion at the left. Glover writes: "From memory, I would describe the abrasion as being along the longitudinal axis, and cl

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Can you get a (lens) dustbrush, and let's check our cameras.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Stay where you are, and I'll give you a zap-a-reen-o, wherever you are. (Pause)

A17A1675510.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1675510.text: Okay Ron. Let's try HF Antenna 2, Retract now, please.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Okay. (Pause) Got it?

A17A1675510.speaker: Evans
A17A1675510.text: Okay.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Yup.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Okay, how many bags do I have.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: I don't know, but I've got a lot of dusting to do here.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Do you have a lot of bags?

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Yeah. I must have...I've got four of them is all.

A17A1675510.speaker: Evans
A17A1675510.text: There we go. Let's see. Give you a countdown on it. Okay, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1...

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: I'd better change my bag (that is, get a new pack of sample bags to hang on his camera).

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Can't even read the Rover. 167:57:33 Schmitt: Yeah. I have an empty bag (SCB) on me now, right? Collection bag?

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Empty. (Pause)

A17A1675510.speaker: Evans
A17A1675510.text: Mark it. Barber pole.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay, 17...

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Don't know how much time do we have here?

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay, 17. We're looking at a nominal Station 9 here. You've got about 25 minutes remaining. [Fendell pans past Gene, who has the large dustbrush in hand, headed for the LCRU.]

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: No such thing as a nominal station any more.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: This may be the first and only one of the traverse.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: The geology won't let it be nominal. Okay, I've got some new (sample) bags, Bob.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay. We copy that, Jack.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: And I guess I'm pretty good on film.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay. And you're going to get a radial sample here...

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Well, maybe I'm not.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: ...and so you might check your Rover sample(r) (the LRV Sampler ) bag supply. [Fendell reaches the counter-clockwise stop and reverses direction. The cuff checklist pages pertaining to Van Serg are LMP/CDR-21 , LMP/CDR-22 , and LMP/CDR-23 . Figure 6-123 from the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report is a plan map showing the position of the Rover relative to the rim.]

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: That's right. I want to take that.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: And you might give me frame count or check it to make sure you're okay.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: I just did, and it's 123.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Okay, good enough.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: (Calling to Houston) How do you want the SEP blankets?

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Leave them closed, please, Gene...

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Open, I think.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: ...as closed as they'll get.

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Closed. (Pause)

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: We been riding with this thing off?

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: What?

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: SEP?

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: Yeah, it should be off.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Yeah, it is. Doesn't seem like it'd get much data that way. Even if it's hot.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: Yes, but it's automatic...

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: I guess they're worried about getting it so hot it...

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: It shuts itself off when it gets above 108, so it's no good anyway.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: Are you kidding? Oh, boy.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: We've been hoping all day. It's been off all day, since Station 6. We've been hoping that it would cool down so that we could get some more data, but it's not, obviously.

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: It's not going to make it, Bob.

A17A1675510.speaker: Parker
A17A1675510.text: That's obvious by now. Video Clip ( 3 min 13 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

A17A1675510.speaker: Cernan
A17A1675510.text: That's a shame!

A17A1675510.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1675510.text: (Changing subjects) This is starting to look like a (U.S.) Geological Survey expedition. The vehicles are all covered with dust. (Long Pause) [Fendell examines a small, blocky-rimmed crater near the Rover.]

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675956csm.text: Oh, look what's in there. (Long Pause) I don't think I can read that unless I dust it with a lens brush . (Pause)

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675956csm.text: Okay, can I get by you here? (Does) my bag (that is, his SCB) look all right to you?

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675956csm.text: Okay. [Fendell finds Jack at the gate; Gene at his own seat.]

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675956csm.text: Okay. What are we going to do here? (Consulting checklist) We're going to go up there and sample on the rim; look at the walls and the floor, and miscellaneous, and...

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1675956csm.text: Well, we are on the rim (garbled).

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675956csm.text: ...then you're going to take 500 millimeters when you get back to the Rover while I do a radial sample.

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1675956csm.text: Okay, Ron, if you'll give us a hack, we're - you're Go for HF Antenna 1, Retract.

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675956csm.text: But the first thing we do is go up to the crater. Bob, I think the mantle objective here really is immaterial, because the blocky ejecta around the crater covers...Oh, boy...

a17_1675956csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1675956csm.text: (Stepping back from the Rover to look around) Well, it looks like it extends several hundred meters out from the rim. Say a couple of hundred meters.

a17_1680423csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1680423csm.text: Ron, we can see stall current now. Can you give Antenna 1, Off?

a17_1680423csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680423csm.text: (Arriving at the rim) Holy Smoley! [Cernan - "This is recall to me. This I've seen before. We're just over the rim of the crater."] [Schmitt - "You can remember walking up and, the first time you look in the crater, there's a lot more crater there than you think there is. I remember Van Serg pretty well."] [Gene and Jack will both take pans of the interior of the crater. Jack's first Station 9 pan consists of frames AS17-142- 21798 to 21824 and will be taken at 168:20:21. Frame 21802 shows the mound at the bottom of the crater.] 168:04:31 Schmitt: ...intensely shattered in that area, as (are)

a17_1680423csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1680423csm.text: Ready for Pan Camera Mode to Standby?

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1680744csm.text: Okay, Ron, Pan Camera to Standby.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Here's a whole big...We ought to take that just as is. (Pause) Well, put a bag around one end if we can. Here, the other end is smaller.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1680744csm.text: Okay, Pan Camera. [Garble] standby. Errr - Power is coming on. Barber pole. Gray. [Long pause.]

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: Yeah (garbled)...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Let me hold this end. Let me hold it, and you put the bag on. (Pause) That's breccia, too. That's...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: Well, it's...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Well, see that? See the white fragments in there?

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: Yeah. It certainly...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: It's got a lot of very small...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: It looks like this big one over here. (To Bob) You know, it might be that these might be pieces of the projectile. I don't know. 'Cause it doesn't look like...It's not subfloor. (Pause) (To Gene) Okay. Pin it down. (Pause) [Schmitt - "It's a big rock - too big for a bag. The bag's on one end and I'm trying to get it down in the bottom of his SCB so that the bag stays attached."] [Cernan - "We did that a number of times, to protect or identify a rock."]

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Well, that's wrapped in...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: If you put it end down, it may stay in the bag.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: I doubt it.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: What's the number?

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: It's 480, and it's a relatively tabular shape, and it's about...

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: (Presenting his SCB) And it's going to ....

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: ...10 inches long.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: And it's highly friable. It breaks apart.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1680744csm.text: Ron, you can turn HF Antenna 2, Retract, switch to the Off position.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Oh, not so much.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: In small chips. Well, you did it with your hands there. I call that "being friable", compared to what we've seen anyway. Video Clip ( 3 min 04 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPEG )

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1680744csm.text: Okay. Thank you. Sorry.

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1680744csm.text: Okay, and let me get an "after" or two. [AS17-146- 22415 and 22416 are Gene's "afters". He moved in and to his right between the frames.]

a17_1680744csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1680744csm.text: Let me get a soil right over here. (Pause; having difficulty with the scoop head again) Okay. The soil next to the boulder, down to about 3 centimeters, is in bag 569.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1681123csm.text: Ok - okay, Ron. You got your steno-maphic [sic] tools out up there? Because we got a Flight Plan update for tomorrow - the trim burn or the bagel burn, I guess.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Boy, I'll tell you, I don't...(Pause) (To Bob) There's more dust on these rocks. It's harder to see a fresh surface. They're not as clean. (Pause) [Jack moves farther beyond the rim crest and goes out of sight.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: That's subfloor.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Lookit. And even the floor of the crater is mantled down there.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: You know, that seems...Yeah. That seems like a...what you got? A piece of glass?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah, I think it is glass. At least it's glass covered. Just glass covered. Houston, I've got an undocumented sample. It's about 2 meters west of where we just sampled. It's a glass-covered, oh, baseball-size rock in 571. Video Clip ( 1 min 18 sec 0.3 Mb RealVideo or 13 Mb MPEG )

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1681123csm.text: Copy that. (Pause) [Jack moves southwest, parallel to the rim, his head and shoulders coming into view.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay. At - Okay, I've got volume 3 now.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: A lot of these blocks up here, Houston - particularly the more fractured ones, but even some that aren't - are a gray-matrix, fragment (means 'clast') breccia. And it looks like, really, the fragments are quite fine. On the rim anyway, we haven't seen any large fragments. The largest I've seen is about 2 centimeters. But down in the (central) mound you can see some fragments that are probably half a meter in diameter. [Schmitt - "For clarification, in this paragraph my use of the word 'fragment' is confusing. I had started to use 'fragment' when I should have been using 'clast'. A 'fragment' i

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: (Having joined Jack) Jack, are you going around that rim of the crater up there?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: I was just looking at rocks.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Well, okay.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay, the first one is at 180:20. Add "P00," and below it, add "Verb 49 maueuver to P52/trim attitude."

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: We...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: I want to get a pan before I leave back there.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Oh, yeah. We need to see if we can get some of the subfloor. I'm not sure I understand what's happened here, yet. This should have brought up subfloor according to the theory, and it hasn't. [Because they are well out on the valley floor and shouldn't be standing on more than a few meters of regolith and/or mantling, an impact the size of Van Serg should have brought up subfloor gabbro.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: That looks like some of the...Look at some of the breccias, the blue breccias with the big old slabby white...(Look at) the fracture face with the white inclusions. [Schmitt - "What Gene's referring to, here, is that this stuff looked a little bit like the blue breccias up on the North Massif (at Stations 6 and 7) because, in appearance, it was dark, bluish-gray with the white clasts. As it turns out - and I don't remember if we came to the conclusion before we left (the Moon) or not - these were those regolith breccias."] Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Down there.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah, down in the floor itself.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah, it has that appearance all right. Hey, Gene...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Do you see that rock...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: (Garbled)

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: ...that rock that's fractured in sort of a pyramid shape down there? Out here on the right? The right end of the floor down there. That big one?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: It's sort of pointing west...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: ...(Correcting himself) Pointing east. That's a unique fracture, isn't it?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1681123csm.text: Roger, 17...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: And there's another one that's fractured almost in a...(Stops to listen to Bob)

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1681123csm.text: ...And we'd like to be moving from here in about 10 minutes, so we probably better be trending back toward the Rover, unless you're seeing something really great out there.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay, we're going to give you the High Gain angle numbers and the Verb 49 maneuver numbers tomorrow morning. They'll probably change on latest updates, so we won't give anything for the - You can just put three blanks for the roll, pitch, and yaw there with that Verb 49 maneuver. Okay, if you go down the page...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Well...Hey, Bob, we ought to find out whether or not...(We) ought to find out what the rock is here, if you've got a little time.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Jack, let me to put this in your bag and start...I'm sorry.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1681123csm.text: Rog. You got 10 minutes. I'm just telling you to start thinking about getting back.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah. We're always thinking that way. [Jack finally presents his SCB to receive Gene's glass sample.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay, Bob. One thing I noticed we do uncover. There's a lot of, oh, 2-, 3-, 4-millimeter-size fragments of glass we're kicking up all over the place.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Little glass balls.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: (Moving southeast along the rim crest) Hey, Gene?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Almost like Pele's (Tears)... [Pele's Tears are small drops of volcanic glass, a reference to the Hawaiian volcano goddess and to geology field trips Gene took to the island of Hawaii - also known as the Big Island - during training for both Apollo 14 and Apollo 17.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Gene?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Can you come over here? I think there's some subfloor here. We ought to...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: We ought to try to document it. But I tell you, most of the rocks are the fine-fragment breccias.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Let me see if I can't get one of those little...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: There's some glass. Hey...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: (Stopping about 4 meters northwest of Jack) You see, if they're like Pele's...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: ...Eyeballs or whatever they are.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: I think we can get some over here. If you're careful coming over here, we can get glass that looks like it may have crystallized (that is, solidified) in place here.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: (Joining Jack) Okay. I'm talking about those little balls, too.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: See that...Whoo, take it easy...Take it easy.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Where are you? Right there?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: (Pointing with the scoop) Yeah, but put your gnomon right over here, and we can get (indicating) that for glass and that for subfloor.

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay. Let me... 168:15:11 Schmitt: But I'm not sure that is. It may be breccia. Everything is covered with dust here, and it's hard to tell the types. Most of the rocks we're seeing are breccias. (Pause) Make sure that glass is in your stereo. (Long Pause) [Jack takes down-Sun picture AS17-142- 21795 ; Gene gets cross-Sun stereopair AS17-146- 22419 and 22420 .]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1681123csm.text: (Finished with his stereo pictures) Okay. 168:15:45 Schmitt: Be careful with it. (Pause) [Jack turns toward the Rover to take "locator" photos AS17-142- 21796 and 21797 ; Gene moves in with the tongs to collect the sample.]

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay, after "IR Cover, Close," we'll put "turn the UV, Off; the IR, Off"; and then enable all jets before the fuel cell purge, huh?

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: Oh, shoot! (Long Pause) 168:16:04 Cernan: I don't have any bags so...

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1681123csm.text: Okay. At 180:58, where it says "Configure DSE," change "High Bit Rate" - cross it out, and make it "Low Bit Rate."

a17_1681123csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1681123csm.text: (To Bob) Okay, the glass looks like a glass agglutinate. (Pause) [Jack takes the glass sample, but drops it.] [Gene has used the last of the sample bags in the bag holder attached to his camera. We can see the empty holderstill attached to his camera until about 168:19:06.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 23 sec )

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: Oh, no!

A17A1681612.speaker: Cernan
A17A1681612.text: It break?

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: (Relieved that it didn't break) Good. I think that will survive going back (to Earth) now. (Pause) [Gene retrieves the sample with the tongs and Jack takes it again.]

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: Okay. It's a frothy glass agglutinate; it's going to be in bag 481.

A17A1681612.speaker: Parker
A17A1681612.text: Copy that. Video Clip ( 3 min 27 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 34 Mb MPEG )

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: And it looks almost like a cowpie-type of bomb, Bob, if you'll pardon the expression.

A17A1681612.speaker: Parker
A17A1681612.text: I will. I don't know about anybody else.

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: Although it's not flattened. It's an aggregate of glass in...Or, it's a pile of about four fragments, much like the one we're sampling. (Pause)

A17A1681612.speaker: Cernan
A17A1681612.text: Jack, we want to get a good scoop sample here. Maybe can we get some of those little fine pieces of glass around.

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: And it (the agglutinate) looks like it's in place from the day it was born.

A17A1681612.speaker: Parker
A17A1681612.text: Copy that. [Fendell de-zooms and it's hard to see any detail of what they are doing.]

A17A1681612.speaker: Cernan
A17A1681612.text: Oh, God, ding dumb! (Pause)

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: I'm having a hard time with this one.

A17A1681612.speaker: Cernan
A17A1681612.text: (I'll get) a piece of that rock right behind it. (Pause) (Garbled) (Pause)

A17A1681612.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1681612.text: Okay. And you might as well scratch out those words where it says "Eat period" on that line, and down at 181:23, add "P41 - P41."

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1681612.text: Want a bag? (Pause) [Fendell zooms in again. Gene gets a sample bag from Jack's supply.]

A17A1681612.speaker: Cernan
A17A1681612.text: Yup. Let me turn around. (Pause)

A17A1681612.speaker: Schmitt

This exercise may be an indication of me getting tired and getting a little bit careless in the way I retrieved that scoop because, if

a17_1682617csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1682617csm.text: You know, I look at that D-Caldera from a distance - I can still see it in the binocs - and I keep trying to look for some hint of a topographic expression, a topographic rise surrounding the caldera. There's no rise around the rims - or anything.

a17_1682617csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1682617csm.text: Okay. 85 is the mag count on the 500.

a17_1682617csm.text: I think that's a smart move, Bob. I don't think the radial sample's going to tell you much here.

a17_1683106csm.text: Okay.

a17_1683106csm.text: Yup. (Pause) 485!

a17_1683106csm.text: 485. Okay. What did I say (for the prior sample) 483, 484? Okay. (Pause)

In trying to be objective about what we've seen here at this station, I thought he might have taken hold of the apparent fatigue a little bit sooner."]

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan

a17_1683106csm.text: Copy that.

a17_1683106csm.text: (Presenting his SCB) Bob, a possibility here is that this upper 6 inches of gray material, in here, is the latest mantling in the area and the light-colored debris may be what's left over from the (Van Serg) impact. Video Clip ( 4 min 21 sec 1.1 Mb RealVideo or 43 Mb MPEG )

a17_1683106csm.text: Okay, I need a magazine too, Bob. I don't have any film at all.

a17_1683106csm.text: Roger. That'll be Bravo (Apollo magazine 134, which Gene used during the first EVA) if you change yours here, or you could change it at Station 10.

a17_1683106csm.text: For the ejecta pattern of Eratosthenes, you can just see it looking back into the Sun now, and the terminator is right - right in the middle of Eratosthenes now. And you can sure see the classic impact ejecta pattern around it. It goes out for - you know, almost two crater diameters as we can see the topographic expression. You can see the scalloping or scouring as it's gone back across there, due to the shadows that are created in the low Sun angle.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1683106csm.text: I'll change it here. It's just as easy while we're in there; (that is, while they have Gene's seat raised to get a magazine for Jack).

a17_1683106csm.text: Okay.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1683106csm.text: (To Gene) Okay. You want Bravo, huh?

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1683106csm.text: Bravo. And I'll get the DSEA. (Pause) Bravo was outside there; I saw it.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Schmitt

a17_1683106csm.text: Let me get this...Hold it long enough for me to get this ( dark slide ). Then I can get rid of this all at one time.

a17_1683106csm.text: Okay.

a17_1683106csm.text: (The dark slide falls out) Oh!

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1683106csm.text: I got Bravo. 168:34:04 Schmitt: Okay. I got that one.

a17_1683106csm.text: Ron, at your convenience, we would like H 2 Tanks 1, 2, and 3 Fans, Off. H 2 Tanks 1, 2, and 3 Fans to Off.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1683106csm.text: (To Bob) We lost the dark slide out of Bravo, and it's in the dirt. I'm not going to pick it up.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1683106csm.text: All right. Copy that. There's no point in putting it back in. It probably wouldn't go in anyway.

a17_1683106csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1683106csm.text: No, not dirty. Okay. I'm changed. (Going to the gate) And I don't know what the mag count is, but let me get the DSEA. If this thing is true to form, I'm going to have to get in there...I got to...(Surprised) The bow is tripped! a17_1683106csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1683106csm.text: Okay. I'm going to turn off all the H 2 Fans. There's 3, 2, and 1, are all Off.

A bird-in-th

A17A1683550.text: It's all right. If we get a single, we get a single out of it.

A17A1683550.text: Okay, Ron, FAO's data says that on magazine Yankee Yankee, we have 20 unscheduled frames that you can use prior to the scheduled photography. After the scheduled photography, anything that's left will also be yours.

A17A1683550.text: (Going around the front of the Rover to his seat) Oh, you're doing it, huh?

A17A1683550.text: I've got it started.

A17A1683550.text: Well, you're not even...Okay. Not even going to debate the issue?

A17A1683550.text: (Cheerfully) Nope. It takes too much time debating it.

A17A1683550.text: Well, let's see how much time it takes. I hope you're right. [Schmitt - "I think this exchange is another symptom of my being tired."] [Cernan - " It was a symptom of being tired. My willingness to do the core had nothing to do with my geologic expectations. I was just saying, 'Whatever we're going to do, let's just get on with it'."] [Schmitt - "Had I really been thinking, (I would have realized that) those rocks are so soft you'd go through them (with the core) anyway."]

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay. And...

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay, and we need a "lower" out of my bag.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Let me get the core.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Watch it. You're in a crater almost.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: A "lower" out of my bag is all we need.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Yeah I want to get (garbled) for you. [Jack gets a core tube out of Gene's SCB. Gene is holding an upper section.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay. We have to have you guys moving in 10 minutes. And we'd like to also deploy EP number 5 here.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay. I'll start on the (garbled under Jack).

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: ...(Garbled) the lower? (Pause) This is a lower, right?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Yup.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: You got an upper? [They connect the core tube sections.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Yeah. (Pause) Why don't you get (seismic package number) 5 out, and I'll start on the core.

A17A1683550.speaker: Evans
A17A1683550.text: [Laughter] Oh, that is a good thought. No, it's just that every once in awhile at these terminators, you know, you - you have some real good shots, and we just can't schedule them, you know, all the time, because sometimes you can't do it. But you take one or two shots of each terminator when it comes by, you get some real good pictures.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: I'll get that. And I'll put that right there.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: (Holding the core in front of the TV lens, fitting them together) Okay. The lower is 50; the upper is 37.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Copy. 50 and 37.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Is that "5", Jack?

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Yup.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Why don't you put it up...Well...You put the gnomon away. Put it fairly near that trench. At least there is some documentation there.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Yup. [Gene goes around the front of the Rover; Fendell follows him.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: I'll try to have the pan going while you're doing it. Okay, Houston...(To Gene) Which way you going to drive out of here?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: I'm driving out of here...

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Left or right? [Jack wants to put the explosives package somewhere where it won't get in Gene's way as they leave.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: I've got to go right. I got to go right.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Okay. (Pause) Pin 1 is pulled and safe. Pin 2 is pulled (and) safe. Pin 3 is pulled and safe. (Pause) [Fendell finds Gene hammering the drive tube, north of the Rover.] RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde ( 2 min 55 sec )

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay, Jack. And we'll document it back to the Rover, I guess is the best way. That doesn't look too hard, Gene. [Just as Bob says this, the tube penetration comes to a halt.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Until just now. [After two more hammer blows, Gene seems to break through whatever was blocking progress and the core begins penetrating again.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Try to...Oops, looks like you proved me wrong!

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: The first core was easy; the second one a little tougher; and then it got tough down at the end. [Gene stows the hammer in his shin pocket .] 168:39:47 Schmitt: Stay there, I'm getting a picture of you. Okay? 168:39:49 Cernan: Okay. [Frames AS17-143- 21836 to 21858 are Jack's second Station 9 pan taken near the Rover.] [Frames 21836 and 21837 show Gene hammering the core.] [Frame 21838 shows the seismic charge.] [David Harland has assembled frames 21836 to 21841 , which show Gene collectiing the core.] [Frame 21857 shows Gene with the core at the back of the Rover. A detail gives good views of

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: I got it.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: You got it from here?

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Yeah.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Gene pulls the core out of the ground with his left hand. It takes about 12 seconds. Gene then rotates the core so that it is parallel to the ground and examines the outside from the top down toward the bit. As he finishes the examination, he lightly touches his forefinger to the soil exposed at the tip.] Video Clip ( 3 min 13 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG )

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: (It's) full, but it wants to slide out. It's full. No rocks in it. It looks like just the same stuff we've been traveling through. [Gene goes to the Rover, using his forefinger as a core plug.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Evans
A17A1683550.text: [Humming]

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay, Jack. I think you better help Gene with recovering that core there where he thinks it's going to fall out.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: You know, I think you're right. And if you'll just wait until I finish the pan, that's exactly what I'm going to do.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay. I didn't know what you were doing.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Bob, it's capped.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Got you. Okay. (Pause) [That is, Gene has capped the bit end of the lower section.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: (To Jack) Just hold the (extension) handle. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Okay?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: I can take this one off. (Pause) It's very loose soil, Jack. And it's...Just any little movement and you'll lose some of it. Let me cap that end. Don't move it. [Fendell finds them at the gate.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Uh-oh, you almost knocked some out. Get your...you know where your thing (the rammer) is?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Yeah, but I need you...The cap's on you. The last one's gone off the Rover.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: That's all right. I'll stay here. Go put your top in. I won't move it. (Long Pause) [Gene goes to Jack's seat with the lower section. He gets a cap and screws it on, then puts the section under the seat. Jack turns to present the left side of his PLSS. Gene gets a cap for the upper section that Jack has been holding.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Any little movement and that stuff starts...

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Yep. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay. (Pause) Turn around. I'll get the rammer (off the back of Jack's PLSS).

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Okay.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Oh, man! Even these pins are getting stiff. (Pause) [Gene is talking about the pins that hold the extension handle to the upper section. This is the extension handle which is normally attached to the rake. Gene gets the rammer and goes to Jack's seat; Jack goes to the gate.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Okay, Bob. The top rammed down, oh, almost half way without any effort. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Copy that.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: The scoop's back on (the extension handle). (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: The bottom rammed down about an inch.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Okay, Robert. Let's see...

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Turn around and I'll get this.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: What was the last thing - let's see - we had to do?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: A couple of football-size rocks.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: You got the D. S. E. A.?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: I got it.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: I got the charge. You got the double core.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: I got the double core.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: And I got one sample of a radial sample. [Jack giggles at the thought.]

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: That's a unique one. Video Clip ( 3 min 18 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPEG )

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: (Laughing) (And the sample is) in my pocket.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: And have we got the gravimeter back on the Rover?

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Yes; it's on.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: And we want to get a large block. Why don't we...

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay, and there's a...

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: No, let's get a couple of them. I've got one.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: ...(garbled) here for a SESC from the shallow trench. We'd also like to have you moving in 4 minutes. That's with wheels rolling in 4 minutes.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: SESC, huh?

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Roger; but we have to have the wheels rolling...

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: I don't know if we can do that. We can try it.

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: We want the wheels rolling in 4 minutes, so I don't think it's practical at this time.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Bob, we cannot get an SESC in 4 minutes...

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: Okay. Copy that...

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: ...and roll...

A17A1683550.speaker: Parker
A17A1683550.text: ...Copy that.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: ...at the same time. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Now, I've got to push this latch on the gate...(correcting himself) on the pallet to get it locked.

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Need some help?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Push the pallet while I trip the latch, will you? Because I got to trip the latch. There's so much dust in that core. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Get it?

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: No. No. Wait a minute. Open it up. (Pause)

A17A1683550.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1683550.text: Wait a minute. Okay.

A17A1683550.speaker: Cernan
A17A1683550.text: Now...Now that's where...Now let me trip it. (Pause) Okay. Try it. (Pause) Locked?

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1684451csm.text: Okay, magazine Yankee Yankee is in the Nikon - finally.

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1684451csm.text: Should be locked now. RealVideo Clip by Mick Hyde ( 1 min 00 sec )

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1684451csm.text: That got it. That got it. (Pause) Okay.

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1684451csm.text: Got a big rock there, too?

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1684451csm.text: Well, you know, the thing that amazes me is that there's no subfloor around here.

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1684451csm.text: I got one here. (Pause) Okay. I'm about ready to clean up the Rover here. (Pause) [Fendell is looking in the direction of the marker flag on the Explosives Package. It is orange. When Fendell first pointed the TV at the horizon beyond it, he was at minimum zoom and the flag was just a few picture elements across and, therefore, just a faint blur of color. After a while, someone noticed the patch of color and Fendell zooms in to see what it is. Because it is actually in the very near field, rather than in the far field, zooming only blurred it more.]

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1684451csm.text: Okay, 17. What's out there in the distance on a hillside in the field-of-view of the camera? The camera is pointing at it. (Pause) Oh, I'll bet that's the Italian (flag)...

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1684451csm.text: We've got to get a distance. Which hill? Let me see where you're...

a17_1684451csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1684451csm.text: ...that's the flag, I bet. On the charge. [There are prior references to the "Italian Flag" at 147:01:36 during the drive back to the LM at the end of the second EVA. The flag is shown here in AS17-143- 21837 . The actual color is international orange.] [Schmitt - "I think that it was Bob who told me that they really didn't have any idea - when he started to call us - of what that was. None! And I don't think I've ever seen this sequence in a NASA tape."] [Cernan - "I have never seen this picture until just now. Never. Never!"]

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: I wonder where we stand on time.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: (Looking at his watch) Well, we've been out about 5 hours and 20 minutes or so.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Where are we headed, now that we are moving?

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: That's affirm...

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Well, I'm trying to get out of the block field here, then I'll head back to the southwest. (Pause) [Cuff checklist page LMP/CDR-24 shows the planned traverse to Station 10. For completeness, pages LMP/CDR-25 , LMP/CDR-26 , LMP/CDR-27 , LMP/CDR-28 , and CDR-29 cover the planned drive to Station 10, the planned activities at that station, and the drive back to the LM.]

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: We going to Sherlock (Station 10) at all, Bob?

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: No, we're going straight home...

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: (To Gene) That must be Gatsby (Crater) over there. [AS17-143-21860 to 21863 cover the next portion of the traverse.]

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: ...you can follow the (garbled, but means the Nav system) home. (Pause) And a reminder, Jack. We can get lots of photos. We've got lots of film left right now.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Okay.

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: And, 17. Gene, I guess you're the one that took the SEP out. Do you remember the reading of the SEP temperature when you broke it down?

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Didn't even look, Bob.

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: It was 125 when we started the station.

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: Roger. Copy that. (Pause)

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: That's Gatsby there, I guess, huh?

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Yeah.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: It's not unlike Van Serg, though. 168:50:15 Schmitt: Hey, you know that looks like the mantling...Hopefully, we can get a...Watch your rock. There you go. (Hopefully), we can get a shot looking back to the northwest...

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Yeah, I'll get that when I... 168:50:33 Schmitt: ...into Gatsby, because it looks like the mantle streams over the side from the southwest. Can you swing to your right and get up a little closer to the rim, there? [AS17-143- 21864 shows Gatsby from the east. Frame 21865 is taken after Gene turns to give them a better view into the crater.]

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Hey, there is a couple fragments in spots...

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Look at that. See that?

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Yeah.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: See that structure. See how the...

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Yeah.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: ...see how the mantle streams over...

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Yeah; from the northwest. Can you get that?

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Yeah.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: And from the southwest.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Got it? 168:51:03 Schmitt: Yeah. Go ahead. Keep going. (Pause) Good shape. Got it.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: We're 236/2.1. (Pause) [AS17-143- 21866 and 21867 are additional pictures of Gatsby. AS17-143- 21868 to 21870 are taken as they drive south around Gatsby and then drive toward Sherlock.]

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Bob, what I'm looking at is the northwest portion of Gatsby, where there's a very, very concentrated block field on the inner wall; (that is, we can see blocks) except where there are, on the southwest, three streams and, on the northwest and north, a continuous stream - if you will - or radial band of mantle that appears to be burying that field (or) overlying and mantling the field. We got some pretty good pictures of it, I think.

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: Okay. Copy that.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Bob, I'm more and more convinced there's a mantle. (Pause) One possibility, I guess, is that, if it's a pyroclastic mantle, that in the lunar vacuum environment and with whatever volatiles we're dealing with, the stuff becomes extremely fine upon vesiculation. We may have been on it all the time and not known it...(that is), as far as recognizing it.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: See, as soon as we come through this draw, how smooth or free of any debris or boulders it is on the other side of the upslope.

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Yeah. (Pause) Watch it.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Yup. (Pause) Bob, do we have an extra EP (Explosive Package)?

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: No. We have two of them behind you. We're going to deploy one. I'll give you a reading soon on that.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: Okay. Well, one I deploy at the end, I know, (near the place where he will park the Rover at the end of the EVA). I thought we had an extra one here somewhere.

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: Okay. Yeah, that's the one we were planning on deploying all along, and it's there. We'll be deploying at a range of 0.1, which is just before you get to the SEP.

A17A1684856.speaker: Cernan
A17A1684856.text: (Responding to Bob) Okay. (To Jack) I guess Sherlock's going to be right over the top over here. I saw it when we were on that other ridge. (Pause) Hey, you know, there's a lot of bad landing places around here. That low Sun angle, I think, shows most of them up. (Pause)

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: Bob, I...

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: And, Geno, we were looking...

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: ...I don't under...

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: ...at the map here...

A17A1684856.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1684856.text: ...I don't unders(tand)...

A17A1684856.speaker: Parker
A17A1684856.text: ...and if you keep going straight to the LM, you're probably going to run into this crater area around San Luis Rey. You probably ought to head somewhat south of directly back to the LM, so we can at least tip the western edge of Sherlock and then pick it up and go from there back to the SEP. It looks like it might be rather rough there in that dotted-lined area, if you can look at the backside of your map, Jack. [Bob is referring to the contour map on the back of the traverse map.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1685427csm.text: Hey, Houston; America.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Bob, I've already been doing it. I'm at 244/1.7.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: Copy that. Thank you.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Already been doing that.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: Okay.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: And, Bob, about 200 meters back, we crossed back into our standard mantle surface of about one percent fragment cover...

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: Okay 200 meters back, you (garbled). Okay. Copy that.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: ...(when we came) out of the block field, which...(Stops to listen; pause) (To Gene) I can see the LM. 168:55:55 Cernan: Yeah, I can see the LM. And there's Sherlock, where those blocks are. [AS17-143-21871 to 21873 may be taken at about this time.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Yeah, that's the block field, the Sherlock block field; that's right. That is a block field.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Some big ones there.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) Old Station 10. I might even call it "10 Alpha" in honor of the Apollo Program Office. The...

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: "10 Bravo", Apollo.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: ...Apollo Spacecraft Program Office.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: (Hearing Bob) Oh, that's right! "10 Bravo". I knew I'd never get that straight! [Schmitt - "I think I was using 'alpha' or 'A' for 'Apollo', and Bob was using 'Bravo' in the sense of 'job well done'. It's possible that I had something going with those guys. It's possible, but I just don't remember."]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: Do those blocks look like gabbros to you guys?

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: How fast do you think we're going, Jack, without looking?

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: I think we're going about 18 clicks.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Hey, you're just about right. (Pause) Seems like the first time we've been able to go downhill. (Laughs) Not really. (Pause) [Schmitt - (Laughing very loudly) "That I remember!!"] [Cernan - (Laughing) "The fastest we went was coming off of the Scarp and, for a short period of time, we did hit 17 clicks (kilometers per hour). But, here, I think we set this one up."] [Schmitt - "Sometimes in my talk, I say that, in normal terrain you can push the Rover up to 10 to 12 clicks. But that, one time going downhill, we had it up to 18 kilometers per hour and regretted it. And we were bouncing."] [Cerna

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Oh, yeah. [AS17-143-21874 to 21882 are Jack's pictures of their approach to the big block near Sherlock Crater.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: And I'll try to get a reading on what it is.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Some pictures of it as we come up to it.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Yep. 168:57:04 Cernan: Boy that's a big one. (Pause) 168:57:10 Schmitt: Watch it!

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: (Garbled) (Pause) [I have marked a likely candidate for this boulder on a high-resolution scan ( 1.5 Mb ) made from a print of AS17-2309. The candidate boulder is marked '168:57:10'. The distances from the photo stop made on the east rim of Gatsby at 168:51:03 and from the sample stop just north of Sherlock at 168:59:46 are consistent with the travel times. See, also, Figure 7e ( 0.8 Mb ) in the Professional Paper.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Looks like our old friend, the subfloor...

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: The subfloor.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: ...isn't it?

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Yup. 168:57:23 Schmitt: Yep. Vesicular subfloor. Vesicles are about a centimeter maximum size. They look like they're fairly evenly sorted. And the rock itself seemed to be massive. [Schmitt - " 'Evenly sorted' is an oxymoron. 'Sorted' implies that there's a non-random organization. 'Evenly sorted' means it's random. It's not very good jargon. It's used; but it's not very good jargon. And by 'massive', I mean that there is no other organization - the material within the vesicles didn't seem to have phenocrysts or alignments or anything like that."]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: 250/1.4. [Unlike the LM, Geophone Rock, Turning Point Rock, and Tracy's Rock, this boulder is not readily apparent in the high-resolution pan camera image of the landing site taken from the Command Module.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Okay, we're back into about a five percent rock cover as we cross the edge of the Sherlock block field. 168:57:52 Cernan: That's Sherlock over that rim over there. [AS17-143-21883 to 21885 are the next in Jack's sequence of traverse photos. 21883 may show the Sherlock rim.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Yeah. Yeah. (Pause) Once again, all these subfloor blocks look as if they're buried. Not mantled, necessarily, except maybe that one. That... Can you swing right, just a tad? 168:58:08 Cernan: That one's got the mantle blowing up on it, in it...

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1685427csm.text: Well, let's see, probably about time to P20 here. Plus-X forward, SIM bay attitude; 2 Enter Enter, plus 5 Enter. X, okay, Proceed. Noun 78 - Well, that's already loaded. 52.25; plus X is 180; okay? Except we're going to do - half a degree deadband, 2 Enter - 2½ degree deadband, I mean. Plus 2.50. [Garble] number 50 is the Moon. And right now, we'd like to orbrate around the Moon. [Garble] - 2 [garble]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: ...in it's fractures and everything.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: That's the best example of that, I think.

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Take a picture of that?

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1685427csm.text: I got it. I got it. Watch....

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Got it; got it. [AS17-143- 21886 is Jack's photo of the large block on the Sherlock rim.]

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1685427csm.text: Okay. Now, do those blocks look like the same subfloor gabbro?

a17_1685427csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1685427csm.text: Yeah, that's just got the mantle... MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 30 sec )

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Watch it! (Garbled) another one.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (Answering Bob's question) Yes. Everything in here, so far, is the tan-gray subfloor gabbro that I've seen. I haven't...Oh, there's one over there that's the blue-gray. But blue-gray is not abundant.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Okay. Copy that. (Pause) And, 17, as you're getting closer, we're going to want an LRV sample at 1.1 (km) on the range.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Okay.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: What are we now? 1.2?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (To Bob) Okay. We'll try to get block and soil.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: That'd be good. [AS17-143-21887 to 21890 are taken during the approach to the next Rover sample stop. Note the distinctive rock above the TV camera in 21890 and compare with Gene's photo AS17-134- 20455 .]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: There's a fresh little pit. (Pause) Bob, I am continually impressed by the lack of exotic fragments in here. [Schmitt - "Two or three kilometers away on either side, we're surrounded by highlands - high mountains with entirely different kinds of rocks. Yet I don't think we ever recognized any fragments of the breccias from the mountains. You would have thought that some would have been thrown in there in 3.8 billion years; but we just didn't see any. The interpretation, now, is that, at about 3.5 (billion years ago), there was a mantling of the dark pyroclastics with a little bit of orange soi

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Okay, Jack. How about picking out a place...

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (Garbled) Okay. If you head into that little...Well, that's a crater there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Let me get around it. We can go a little bit further.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah. Maybe...

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: I'll go up on that flat area up there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah, yeah. (Pause) There are a lots of little fragments over there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: "Flat area"; ha, ha. (Pause) (I can stop) any time. 168:59:46 Schmitt: Okay. Now swing a shallow turn. (Pause) Whoa. Well, I don't ...

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Can you get any of those? [Jack's photos taken during the final approach to the sample site are AS17-143-21891 to 21893.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Unfortunately, I can't see them (now, because they're in) the shadow (of the Rover).

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: How about that one right in front of you, in front of the television camera shadow. See that little one up there? Right there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: With the...It's a little big, I think.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Upper right...No, upper right. Straight up the line.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Oh, okay. Yeah. If you can get over there, I can get it.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: I can get there. (Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Oh, I guess I had the wrong...I guess I wasn't looking at the right one. The (Rover) shadow is making it impossible to see down there. Now, see what you can get. [During our review, Jack noted that, at this point, his voice quality changed dramatically as he looks down to see what he's doing, getting his chin as far down on his neck as possible.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Bob, we're at 253/1.1.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: You're going to have to...If we do another sample, you're going to have to swing right so I can see. I can't see this way.

A17A1685822.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1685822.text: Hey, Ron, do you have your volume 3 handy?

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Yeah. (Pause) [That is, Jack wants Gene to turn toward the north so that there is no Rover shadow on Jack's side of the vehicle.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: And 53 Yankee.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that. Is that soil or rock?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: That's soil. I can't see to get a rock.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Okay.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Go forward just a little bit, Gene.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Okay.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Except you're going to get yourself in a box here.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: No, that's all right.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Whoa. (Pause) A little more, sorry. (Pause) (Head-down voice quality) Little more. Okay.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Get it?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: I will. (Pause) Got it.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: I can't see the LM anymore.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (Normal voice) Okay. The rock fragment... 169:01:36 Cernan: That's 54 Yankee. (Long Pause) [They both take documentation photos. Jack's is AS17-143- 21894 and Gene's is AS17-134- 20455 .]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Awgh! Okay. You got a rock right in front of you, don't you?

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: I see it. (Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Rolled over (the rock). Good old Rover. [Cernan - "I think I was probably going pretty slow. As long as you don't hit those things hard and fast, you're okay. So I just went over it with the wheel."]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: LMP frame for that sample (pause) looks like about six-zero.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Six-zero! Have I taken sixty pictures (since leaving Van Serg)? (Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Boy, these rock fields are something else again. [AS17-143- 21895 to 21905 are Jack's photos taken during the next few minutes.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah, 60. Looks like some of our gray variety of subfloor up here, around the rim of that little crater. You know, I'm starting to think that maybe the gray, relatively-nonvesicular subfloor may be (the) deeper fraction, based on what we saw...Well, actually, though...Let's see, that could have been overturned. I don't know. (I'll) take that back. There just isn't much of it around here, although we saw a lot of it in the wall of Cochise.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Roger. We got that. [Schmitt - "Obviously, I was just running something through my mind out loud and (when) it didn't make sense to me, I decided to forget about it."]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: What do you think this is, San Luis Rey? We're at 252/0.9.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: I wouldn't doubt it at all.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: I'll bet that's San Luis Rey. 169:03:36 Cernan: We're on the east side of it...Mariner and San Luis Rey. (Pause) They're shallow (and) filled with rocks. [As shown in AS17-143- 21906 , Gene takes a turn to the south, probably to get around a crater. Frames 21907 and 21908 are subsequent traverse photos.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: As close as we can tell, you're at one or the other of them.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Boy, I tell you they're a lot...(To Bob) Okay. We're at 250/0.9.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Mariner should look pretty fresh. (Long Pause) Boy, I certainly don't see much variety other than the gray and the tan subfloor varieties. There's old Challenger. 169:04:29 Cernan: There she is. Pretty as a picture. (Pause) [Schmitt - "I have an image of what the Challenger looked like coming back from Station 5 on the second EVA, but not from here."] [Cernan - "Me, either."] [They both take pictures. Jack's is AS17-143- 21909 . The LM is just to the left of center, as indicated in a labeled version . Gene's photo is AS17-134- 20456 . The LM is just under the angle of the high-gain.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1685822.text: Ron, we're going to lose you in about 1 minute, and you're looking great. No problems at all.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Boy, I tell you, there's no getting out of this stuff (the boulder fields). You go from one to the other.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Okay, 17...

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: I don't know whether I said it or not...

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Gene, at a range of 0.1. We're going to deploy the quarter-pound charge, and that'll be Jack's getting off to deploy it like we talked about last night. [Bob's reference to "last night" may be an indication of how tired he is, as well. I haven't been able to find a discussion of this EP deployment during the closing stages of EVA-2 or during the subsequent discussions in the cabin. More likely, Bob is referring to the EVA-3 pre-brief conducted while Gene and Jack were eating breakfast. It is now about 10:30 in the evening in Houston and, like everyone else, Bob has had three long days.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Evans
A17A1685822.text: [Laughter] Okay.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Okay. (Pause) That's EP-2, Jack.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: EP-2; right. (Pause) Bob, we're moving in and out of areas of, say, 1 percent to 5 -to-10 percent blockiness. And where it gets blocky, not only is it more blocky, but we seem to have more of the medium-sized craters in the range of 20- to 50-meter-diameter craters. (To Gene) That may be Mariner right there. (Pause) [AS17-143- 21910 seems to be Jack's only traverse photo taken between the spot where they saw the LM and the fractured boulder at San Luis Rey mentioned at 169:07:24.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: How do you read, Bob?

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Loud and clear. Loud and clear.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (To Bob) Hey...Van Serg, let me mention again, was an unusual experience in the plains geology here. (To Gene) That must be part of San Luis Rey or Mariner, one of them.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Yeah That's pretty deep. Pretty deep.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah, it is.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: It's really big.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yep. (To Bob) We're at 252 and 0.6.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: The crater on our left - that is, south of us - is a large crater. It's somewhat deeper than (other) craters of the same size (diameter) that we've seen. And it, too, though, has large blocks mainly in the walls, although there are blocks up here in the rim, occasionally up to 3 meters (in size). (Pause) Look at that string of blocks over there; that may be it (that is, San Luis Rey).

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Yeah.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: That's an edge of a crater, I guess.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Want a picture of that? 169:07:24 Schmitt: Got it. (Pause) [AS17-143- 21911 may show the fractured rock at San Luis Rey. Frames 21912 and 21913 are taken during the remainder of the drive up to the point where Jack gets off west of the SEP transmitter array to deploy a seismic charge.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Look at the way that thing's fractured. Yeah, this is the San Luis Rey complex, because see how elongated it is?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah. Yeah. [Cuff checklist page LMP/CDR-28 shows a sketch of the complex. Compare with a detail from Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report Figure 6-3.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Fact is, we're going to cut right through the western half here. (Pause) We're at 244/0.4.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Bob, I may have said early on - up there at Van Serg - that I saw subfloor, but we never did sample any that I know of. And the dust was thick enough that I'm just not sure. The breccias were the most obvious thing there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Okay. Most interesting.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: It might have been a window in the plains here, of some kind. But it's strange to see it there, with so much subfloor all around it that we saw. (Long Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: And, Jack, you're going to get a feedwater tone pretty soon.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Got it. (Pause as he switches to the Aux supply) Okay, I should be in Aux(illary) now.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: There she (Challenger) is.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: And as soon as we get to the 0.1 (range), let's stop and deploy the charge.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: All right. (Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Okay. And then, I guess...(Pause)

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Then we'll head back to the LM.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: I don't go to the...

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Unless you want to go to the ALSEP.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (Chuckles) I think I'm going to. When do I go to the...Oh, you go to SEP. That's right. [After they unload the Rover at the LM, Gene will drive the Rover out to its final parking place near the SEP transmitter, a spot far enough east of the spacecraft that the TV audience on Earth can watch the launch. This final parking place is called the VIP site, recalling the close-in viewing stands at the Cape reserved for Very Important Persons.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Yeah, I go to SEP when I...Take the Rover around here.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: We're going to let you play the Return-to-the-ALSEP game there, Jack. We've got a few things for you to do out there, when the time comes.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (To Bob) Okay. (To Gene) (Has the indicator cycled to) 0.1? No.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: We're almost to SEP. We're about...

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Rog. It'll be just short of SEP.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: ...50 meters from SEP (transmitter).

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Is it short of the antenna?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Well...

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: ...We'd like to have this...

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: ...You see, we can get to the end of the antenna...

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: No, no. Let's have it east of the antenna. If we are there, let's deploy it right where you are.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Okay. We're about 30 meters east of the antenna. How's that?

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: That sounds great.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: Okay. And we're measuring 221 and 0.2; 221 and 0.2.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Copy that. (Pause) [The range reading of 0.2 indicates that the Rover navigation system thinks they are 150 to 250 meters from the SEP transmitter, an error of about 100 to 200 meters, depending on whether or not the indicator is about to click down to 0.1. This close to the SEP, the difference between the bearing readout of 221 degrees - about SW - at the true bearing of about 270 is almost meaningless. Further information of the cumulative range error becomes available when Gene gets back to the LM at 169:18:00.] [Cernan - "It worked great. They knew where we were, even when we didn't."]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: There's a rock (that) I stood up down there, and I want to get...

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: And it's EP number 2 that we're after, Jack, in case you didn't follow us.

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: ...It's the only dense (that is, fine grained) rock (I've seen)...(Stops to listen to Bob) Okay. [Schmitt - "I'd probably noticed this rock during the first EVA when we were laying out the SEP. It was non-vesicular and fine grained, which was what attracted my eye."] [This rock is sample 70215 , an 8.11 kilogram piece of fine-grained basalt. It is the biggest rock that they brought back. Jack will collect it at 169:15:01 .]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: (To Gene) Hey, our gate's open.

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: It's open!?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Yeah. (Pause) But it looks like everything's here. [What Jack doesn't realize is that the rake, the scoop, and both of the extension handles have fallen off the Rover, somewhere between here and Station 9.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Cernan
A17A1685822.text: How about the big bag?

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: Big bag's there.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: Is that the gate or the pallet? [The geopallet is attached to the Rover chassis behind the seats. There is a latch behind Gene's seat and, behind Jack's seat, the pallet is attached to the geopost. If the latch on Gene's side was unlocked, then the pallet could pivot. The "gate", in turn, is attached to the pallet and is also hinged behind Jack's seat. The gate latch has been giving them trouble throughout the EVA and it seems most likely that it is the gate that is swinging open.]

A17A1685822.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1685822.text: It wouldn't dare run away.

A17A1685822.speaker: Parker
A17A1685822.text: The gate or the pallet?

The actual bearing is about 080 and the range is about 150 meters. Because the distance from the LM to the SEP is short, the bearing error is meaningless. The range reading of 0.1 means that the navigation system thinks the range is between 0.05 and 0.15 km, an indication of a relatively small error.]

A17A1693637.text: Houston, before we close out our EVA, we understand that there are young people in Houston today who have been effectively touring our country, young people from countries all over the world, respectively, touring our country. They had the opportunity to watch the launch of Apollo 17; (and) hopefully had an opportunity to meet some of our young people in our country. And we'd like to say first of all, welcome, and we hope you enjoyed your stay. Second of all, I think probably one of the most significant things we can think about when we think about Apollo is that it has opened for us - "for us

A17A1693637.speaker: Cernan
A17A1693637.text: It's a rock composed of many fragments, of many sizes, and many shapes, probably from all parts of the Moon, perhaps billions of years old. But fragments of all sizes and shapes - and even colors - that have grown together to become a cohesive rock, outlasting the nature of space, sort of living together in a very coherent, very peaceful manner. When we return this rock or some of the others like it to Houston, we'd like to share a piece of this rock with so many of the countries throughout the world. We hope that this will be a symbol of what our feelings are, what the feelings of the Apollo

A17A1693637.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1693637.text: (Taking the rock as Gene hands it to him) A portion of a rock will be sent to a representative agency or museum in each of the countries represented by the young people in Houston today, and we hope that they - that rock and the students themselves - will carry with them our good wishes, not only for the new year coming up but also for themselves, their countries, and all mankind in the future. A17A1693637.text: In the big bag.

A17A1693637.text: (Taking the rock and returning to the Rover) And now - let me bring this (TV) camera around - to commemorate not just Apollo 17's visit to the Valley of Taurus-Littrow but as an everlasting commemoration of what the real meaning of Apollo is to the world, we'd like to uncover a plaque that has been on the leg of our spacecraft that we have climbed down many times over the last 3 days. [Gene has swung the TV around to point at the LM ladder. He is now at the ladder himself and removes a cover off the plaque. He tries to hang the cover on a ladder rung but gives up and drops it to the ground. Ja

A17A1693637.speaker: Cernan
A17A1693637.text: And I'll read what that plaque says to you. First of all, it has a picture of the world. Two pictures. One of the North America and one of South America. The other covers the other half of the world including Africa, Asia, Europe, Australia, covers the North Pole and the South Pole. In between these two hemispheres, we have a pictorial view of the Moon, a pictorial view of where all the Apollo landings have been made; so that when this plaque is seen again by others who come, they will know where it all started. The words are, "Here man completed his first exploration of the Moon, December 197

A17A1693637.speaker: Parker
A17A1693637.text: Roger, Gene. We in Houston copy that and echo your sentiments. Dr. (James) Fletcher (the NASA Administrator) is here beside me. He'd like to say a word to the two of you. [Gene and Jack start for the Rover but stop again and move to stand in front of the camera as they listen to Fletcher.]

A17A1693637.speaker: Fletcher
A17A1693637.text: Gene and Jack, I've been in close touch with the White House, and the President has been following very closely your absolutely fascinating work up there. He'd like to wish you Godspeed as you return to Earth, and I'd like to personally second that. Congratulations. We'll see you in a few days. Over.

A17A1693637.speaker: Cernan
A17A1693637.text: Thank you, Dr. Fletcher. We appreciate your comments, and we certainly appreciate those of the President. And whether it be civilian or military, I think Jack and I would both like to give our salute to America. [Gene salutes as he stands facing the TV.]

A17A1693637.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1693637.text: And, Dr. Fletcher, if I may, I'd like to remind everybody, I'm sure, of something they're aware, but this valley of history has seen mankind complete its first evolutionary steps into the universe: leaving the planet Earth and going forward into the universe. I think no more significant contribution has Apollo made to history. It's not often that you can foretell history, but I think we can in this case. And I think everybody ought to feel very proud of that fact. (Pause) Thank you very much.

A17A1693637.speaker: Parker
