a17_1695012csm.text: You did the javelin!

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1695012csm.text: That was unkind.

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1695012csm.text: Roger, Gene. And we...

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1695012csm.text: I didn't throw it as far as I could have. I just...

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1695012csm.text: ...we timed the parabola for that, and we have one excellent measurement of "g" on the Moon now.

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1695012csm.text: Yeah, I didn't get you a pendulum, but I don't know where I would, Bob. Okay. I'm going to have to take you out to the VIP site!

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1695012csm.text: Okay. We're ready for that, and we'll...

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1695012csm.text: If you concur?

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1695012csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [In Houston, Experiments suggests to Flight Director Gerry Griffin that, as a result of Gene's treatment of the gravimeter, "that calls for another bias reading." Griffin replies, "You'll have to get it yourself."]

a17_1695012csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1695012csm.text: (Looking at his checklist) Well, let me make sure I got everything. Okay. (Pause) Remember, we... [TV off. Gene is on CDR-31 .]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Roger. Read you through the LM. You guys both read me through the LM?

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: That's affirm.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Okay. The first thing I want to do...Tell John (Young) I'm going to do it exactly like he wants. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) The (LMP) camera is under the seat, I hope. Let me look. (Pause) Yeah, camera's there. (Pause) [Cernan - "John Young drove his Rover out there to do the same thing - to get a picture of lift-off. And John may have told me something about positioning the Rover."] [Schmitt - "You know what I think it may have been? I was thinking about it a moment ago. (AS17-143- 21932 shows that) you positioned it at an angle to the line between the VIP site and the LM so that the TV camera had

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Jack, did you do something with the dustbrush ?

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: No.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: It was under the seat, right?

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: It was, yeah.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Yeah. I want to make sure it is because I'll need it out there.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: No, wait a minute. I don't know that it's there now.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Well, I want to make sure that I can get...that I've got something to dust with (so the Rover won't overheat). [They no longer have a right-rear fender and, even in the short drive out to the VIP site, it will get covered with dust. If the Rover electrical system is to survive for very long, Gene will have to give it a thorough dusting.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Evans
A17A1695308.text: Okay, Houston. This is America. Once we get the antenna set right, it is easy to lock up.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. (Joking, very dryly) And, Jack, as you go out to the ALSEP, let me cue in on your next 3 hours worth of work out there, repairing the ALSEP. All right? Over.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Oh, okay. Go ahead. I'm here.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Number one, we want to retrieve the UHT. And I quote, "tap sharply" - that's "sharply" - on the (LSG) gimbal, which is the center section there, the little square metal piece in the middle...tap sharply on the gimbal with the UHT, and then reverify the level on the LSG. We'll check response here in Mission Control after you've done that.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: (Incredulous) You mean tap on the thing (the bar) that swings!?!

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: That's what they say.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: You always wanted to do that, didn't you?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Yeah, that's right. (Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Well, let me see if I can have a clean UHT to do that.

A17A1695308.speaker: Evans
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Tank 1 H 2 , Fans 1, are On.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Okay, Bob. Everything (that is, the Nav system) is zeroed.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. And I'll be talking to Jack here, Gene, for a while. You can interrupt with your comments talking over me, and I'll try and copy them.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: One comment. I got a (warning) flag on the other battery (at) 139 degrees.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. We copy that. [When Gene arrived back at the LM at 169:18:27, the Battery 1 temperature reading was 132 degrees. It is now 139 degrees, hot enough to have tripped a warning flag on the top of the console.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: How much is "sharply"?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Sharply is sharply. It's probably not heavily, but sharply. Fairly light, but sharply.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: On the edge?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: No. You can see that little square metal piece in the middle there?

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: On the edge?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: You see that little square metal piece on there? You can just sort of rap on that...

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Oh, yeah. Okay. Here goes. (Pause) I did it.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. And then it says...

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: You want me to do it again?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Stand by. (Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: That was sort of a moderate "hard tap".

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Go ahead, and hit it harder.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: It is level.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Hit it harder, please.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Okay. (Pause) (Is that) okay? I can hit it harder yet.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. We've observed something there. Stand by. (Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Bob, you might be getting TV the way the antenna's oriented right now. [Cernan - "As I remember, I went around behind the VIP site and drove up to the spot. So the antenna was probably looking pretty close to the Earth."]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Jack, go ahead. We'll do some more stuff here. In the meanwhile, while they're thinking about what's wrong with it...Did you just tap it again? 169:56:44 Schmitt: No, I didn't touch it. I'm over at the Central Station now.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. They're looking at it. All right. Now, we want to take some photographs at the Central Station and a few selected photographs of the ALSEP. Number one, we want a "7-foot cross-Sun" to the south of the ALSEP Central Station and then a 7-foot down-Sun of the Central Station. Over. [That is, Houston wants photographs taken while he's standing 7 feet north of the Central Station, and then another from the east, with the Sun at his back.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: A 7-foot cross-Sun to the south.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: That's what it says.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: And then a down-Sun.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Roger. A 7-foot down-Sun.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: You might tell me what they're trying to get with it. I might be able to help them.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. I presume that what this means is looking to the south. It was cross-Sun originally. I suspect that's what happened here, the way it was written up. So it's a 7-foot looking at all the switches to make sure you guys turned them the right way, I suppose. And then a 7-foot looking down-Sun, so that would be facing west, that side of it. 169:57:49 Schmitt: Okay. I got it. What else? [AS17-134- 20489 is a cross-Sun to the south, showing top half of the Central Station and, beyond it, Geophone Rock. Frame 20490 shows the lower part of the north face where the switches are located. Frame 20491

A17A1695308.speaker: Evans
A17A1695308.text: Hey, that's mighty fine, by gosh.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Now, there's a problem with the Central Station in which they think the south end is buried more deeply in the dirt than they had intended. And the Central Station is, at the present time, getting very warm on the back side, on the south side there. They believe you probably buried it in the ground when you were trying to tilt it to the proper alignment. They're requesting that, when you're at the ALSEP, you remove any soil buildup or debris with a convenient tool. They don't want you to touch it because it's fairly warm. But if you have a UHT or something to move it...Do you have a UHT

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. You know the...

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: It is piled up there. That's a good call.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Yes. Okay. They'd like that (dirt) brushed away. (Pause) And you can give me a call...

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Fortunately, I brought my handy-dandy Rover sampler out.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. You can brush that (dirt) aside, and give me a call when you think that's cleared up the way it ought to be. That's probably one of those things we didn't think about when we decided to tilt the Central Station.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Well, you couldn't anticipate the soil, Bob. (Pause) It's very soft.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Bob, we are at VIP.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. And Ed Fendell is hard on my back to remind you that it's better to be too far away than too close. [Because of the great distance between the Earth and Moon and other factors, Fendell will have to command the TV camera to start panning upward about 2 seconds before the actual launch. That way, the camera will actually start tilting up at the right time. The farther from the LM that Gene parks the Rover, the smaller the fraction of the TV frame that the LM will fill; and any mistakes Fendell makes in the panning speed won't matter quite so much. From the time that Fendell pushes the butt

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: (Agreeably) All right! I thought I was, but I think I may move just a little bit. There's a little rise here I can give you. (Pause) I think I'll give it to you.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Mpeg Clip (0 min 20 sec) [Gene has climbed on the Rover and, as he drives a short way to the "little rise", we get a few seconds of video from the moving Rover. Dave Scott attempted to provide video during his drive from Station 9 to Hadley Rille, starting at about 165:16:09 ; but that attempt yielded only a few, very brief views of the right-front wheel and the lunar surface passing by underneath. Transmission to Earth requires that the high-gain antenna be pointed almost exactly and, here, we get a bit of video by luck. The LM can be seen at the left side of the image.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: By the way, Bob, the soil gets more cohesive with depth. I hadn't really noticed that before.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. We copy that. Duly noted.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: It's quite a bit more cohesive at...(It) feels about the same down to 3 centimeters out here; and then the cohesiveness goes up so (much that) it's difficult to scrape with the Rover sampler.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Copy that, Jack. (Long Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: (To Houston) Well, I think you can see almost everything from here.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay, Geno. And, Jack, let me know when you get done scraping that soil away.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: I will. (Long Pause) [AS17-143- 21932 shows the final Rover parking configuration.] [Cernan - "I sit here (looking at the picture) and swear that I parked the Rover with the wheels straight. That's the final parking? Well, we're behind the LM and it's about the right distance."] [Schmitt - "Why doesn't it have a fender?"] [Cernan - "I took it off. Both of them. I took them both home."] [At some point before he goes back to the LM, Gene will remove the replacement fender - which is now at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum in Washington. He will also remove the rear section of the

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: And now comes the hardest (high-gain antenna) alignment of them all! But I'll get it. (Long Pause) Somewhere about there. See if I can't tweak it up for you. [Gene has parked the Rover pointed a little bit south of west, necessarily in the general direction of the LM so that the TV can be used to watch the launch. Because Earth is in the southwestern sky, the bore sight on the high-gain antenna is over the batteries and Gene is having to lean in to do the alignment. The normal Rover heading at one of the geology stops was 045 (northeast). With that heading, the high-gain was pointed back over

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Bob, the east-west level bubble (on the Central Station) is not quite level (that is, it is not quite centered). The north-south is. Do you want me to tweak that up?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Yeah, you might tweak that up. We are getting a good signal, but go ahead and tweak it up just a little bit. (Pause) And, Gene, what are you doing these days?

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: I'm getting the high-gain set up for you.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Now you know why we didn't make you park it in that orientation all the time, don't you? Video Clip ( 3 min 13 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Boy, I'll tell you. It was a piece of cake up until now. (Pause) There, I got you. (Pause) [TV on]

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Bob, you're looking right down the center of my eyepiece. [That is, Earth is centered in the scope.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay, I don't think...

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: You should have TV.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Yeah, we're getting TV there, Geno.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: You getting it?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: We've got TV.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Well, let me take a look, and clean things up.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. I guess you can dust and dust and dust some more for a while.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Let me get this dusting problem out of the way before I do anything else.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Roger. [Gene moves the TV to clean the lens; he points it at the South Massif. He is on CDR-32 .]

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: You can look at your vantage point, and if you don't like it, let me know.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. I'll tell Captain Video (Ed Fendell). (Pause) [Fendell pans counter-clockwise to the stop and then reverses direction. Captain Video was also the name of a character in a children's TV program of the early 1950's.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Bob?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Go.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: How close can soil be to this back plate of the ALSEP?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Stand by. I'll check.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: It's about 30 centimeters away, most of the places now.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. That sounds good. We'd like you to return to the surface gravimeter, Jack. What you did had some effect, but not a lasting effect. And we'd like you to "rap even more sharply", more strongly, on the gimbal another three times. And we're again watching it, and we'll let you know what to do. (Pause) And I might tell you that this has all been done recently - this afternoon - up at Bendix on the "qual(ification)" unit, and it survived it and so we aren't in any real danger, apparently, of destroying it.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Three times, huh?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Rog. Or up to three times. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - "Bendix built a production unit (of the gravimeter) that they put through thermal/vibration qualification tests. The qual unit was presumably identical to the flight unit."] [Cernan - "They generally had a flight unit, a backup unit, and a qual unit (of most pieces of equipment)."] [Schmitt - "My guess is that they didn't build a backup gravimeter."] [Fendell has the TV pointed at the LM. In the background, (West) Family Mountain is to the left of the LM, (Old) Family Mountain is to the right, and the North Massif is on the right edge of the f

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Bob, don't let me forget to bring a dustbrush back (to the LM) when I come. I'm going through my checklist...

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. I'll mark that down and remind you. And, Jack, you'll be glad to know that the temperature of the back plate there (on the Central Station) has already dropped twenty degrees - two-zero (20) degrees.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Oh, beautiful! Bob, I don't think that (Central Station) bubble is working.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Oh.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: How's your signal now?

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Stand by. I'll check. But why don't you go to the surface gravimeter? (Pause) 170:06:10 Cernan: Bob, how's your TV lens? I don't have a lens brush . It looks good from here. I don't want to use this ( big dustbrush ) unless you think so.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Stand by.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: (Singing) "Knock three times." [The first line of this popular song is "Knock three times on the ceiling if you want me."] [Journal Contributor Brian Lawrence notes that "'Knock Three Times', by, Dawn, was Number 1 in both the U.K. and U.S. in May 1971."]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Roger,...

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Are you satisfied...

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: ...Get out of the way please, Jack (means Gene); and we'll take a look against some bright soil.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: What?

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: No, that's me he's talking to. (Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. It looks pretty good, Geno. Go ahead.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: I don't have one of the lens brushes .

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Yeah, go ahead. It looks pretty good to us.

A17A1695308.speaker: Cernan
A17A1695308.text: Okay.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Okay, Bob. Here come the raps. Knock three times. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) [Fendell looks at Geophone Rock and then at the U.S. flag.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay, Jack. It's really fighting us pretty hard. We'd like you to put the UHT in the socket, and rock it very firmly. Don't pick it up, but rock it very firmly from side to side in all four directions. Move the UHT about 6 inches in each direction while you're doing it.

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay, I rocked it. It (the gimbal)'s swinging.

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Is it reading...

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: And the level bubble is (pause) centered. (Long Pause)

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. We understand it's in good configuration again as far as alignment and leveling is concerned, Jack. Let's go on and take some more ALSEP photos, and let them think about it for a minute. Video Clip ( 3 min 13 sec 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1695308.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1695308.text: Okay. What do you want? [Fendell pulls back on the zoom.]

A17A1695308.speaker: Parker
A17A1695308.text: Okay. Next, what we want is some heat flow (photos)...(Pause) Okay. We just got late word. They'd like to do it one more time, and then call it quits. (Pause)

A17A1701113.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1701113.text: Okay. You got the standard documentation.

A17A1701113.speaker: Parker
A17A1701113.text: Okay. Go ahead. They can't complain about that, certainly. [AS17-134- 20495 to 20497 are Jack's photos of the east heat flow hole.] [Frames 20495 and 20496 are a stereopair from the north, with a step taken to the left between frames.] [Frame 20497 is a down-Sun.] Video Clip ( 3 min 30 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1701113.speaker: Parker
A17A1701113.text: Okay. We'd like a 3-foot shot of the lunar mass spectrometer (LMS), including the orifice where the breakshield was. And, Geno, we are observing some degradation and would like to have the high-gain... [In the Preliminary Science Report , the spectrometer is called the LACE or Lunar Atmospheric Composition Experiment. "Breakshield" is a reference to a dust shield which covers the entrance port and which will be moved back only after lift-off and the detonation of the seismic packages.]

A17A1701113.speaker: Parker
A17A1701113.text: Yes, Jack; 3-foot cross-Sun. And, Gene; this is Houston. We'd like to get the high-gain re-oriented a little bit. We're observing some degradation in the picture.

A17A1701113.speaker: Cernan
A17A1701113.text: I'll tweak it. (Long Pause) [AS17-134- 20498 and 20499 are Jack's cross-Sun and down-Sun pictures of the Lunar Mass Spectrometer, respectively.]

A17A1701113.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1701113.text: (To Bob) Okay. Got it. Now what? (No answer; pause) LMS is complete.

A17A1701113.speaker: Parker
A17A1701113.text: Okay. Copy that. Now we want to go over (to) the neutron flux, Jack.

A17A1701113.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1701113.text: Okay. (Long Pause) How's the gravimeter doing?

A17A1701113.speaker: Parker
A17A1701113.text: We're looking at it, Jack. I'm not sure. (Long Pause) [Fendell has been panning clockwise and reaches the rear of the Rover. Part of Jack's seat is visible and there is no camera or lens in evidence. However, even if Gene has put the camera in place by now, he remembers putting it between the seats, and that part of the Rover is hidden behind the console. Before going to remove the neutron flux probe from the deep core hole, Jack takes three more ALSEP documentation photos. AS17-134- 20500 shows the LEAM and, beyond it, the Central Station, the RTG, and the trash pile. 20501 is an up-Sun of th

a17_1701304csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1701304csm.text: Ron, sorry to interrupt you eating, but could you take the H 2 Tank 2 and 3 Fans to On? We're trying to get the pressures up prior to sleep.

a17_1701304csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1701304csm.text: Okay. 2 and 3 are On.

a17_1701304csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1701304csm.text: Hey, Bob. The panel you want covered...(To himself) Yeah, that's the panel. Okay. (To Bob) You want the panel with the On/Off switch and the signal strength switch and so forth covered, don't you? [Fendell pans counter-clockwise. Gene is referring to the line on CDR-32 which says "Cover LCRU C/D panel with 65% blanket".
