A17A1702454.text: Looked like it was going a million miles, but it really didn't.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Didn't it? [Because of the Rover's location east of the LM, none of the following close-out activities are visible.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, here, this is an ETB.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Let me make sure that that's all cinched up.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. And then start on up. We got to get going here.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Yeah. Unfortunately, their little plan didn't count for the fact that it's hard to pack the ETB with the film magazines in it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: And I'll try and get the big bag here cinched up.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: That is a major task.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Yes, that's going to be...Oh, is it heavy. Is it heavy. Something in that core tube you put in there?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Don't tell anybody, though, because they'll get mad at me. [Schmitt - "I grabbed one of the unused core tubes, grabbed hold of the strut, and leaned on it underneath the LM, just behind the strut, and pushed it in as far as I could. And I think it went in about two-thirds of the way, and then I capped it."]

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Oh, man, is that (big bag) heavy. Holy smoley. Oh! (Pause; static)

A17A1702454.speaker: Evans
A17A1702454.text: Okay, going to Block. And you say you have got a TEI PAD, huh?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: (Garbled) 252 has about three-quarters of a core - hand pushed (into the ground) - (taken about) half a meter inside the plus-Y (north) footpad.

A17A1702454.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1702454.text: ...36076; plus 0.56, plus 0.80; 196:58:46.51; Noun 81s: plus 2785.7, minus 0957.1, minus 0174.6; roll of 179, pitch is 085, yaw, 343. Rest of the PAD is not applicable. Sirius and Rigel are the set stars, but we got a little difference on the hour line. Tonight's hour line is 136:16:00.34; four jets, 12 seconds. I've got three comments. First comment...

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Okay; copy that.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, Jack, how's that ETB coming so you can get going?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Fine.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, I've got to...

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I've got to put it on the strap, though.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: I can get that. This is all cinched up. I think it'll hold. Why don't you start on up? Then I'll start dusting you.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Very good.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Anything fall out?

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Nope.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Oh...

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Let me dust you. Set that down, and I'll hand it all to you.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay, you'll have to hand stuff...

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Okay; and, 17, a reminder. We need you inside in 10 minutes.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, Bob. (To Jack) I'll get your front real quick. (Long Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Evans
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Go.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I'll do a lot of jumping up here in a minute.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Your back is clean.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I'll get the legs as best I can.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Why don't you get me here before you do that?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay. And while I'm doing that, will you take this...

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: (Garbled)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I'll get it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Boy, you got dirty today. I think we're just going to have to live with it. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Get my top. I can kick a lot of that stuff off my legs. (Pause) How do I look in back?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Terrible. (Long Pause) Okay, turn. Oh, man. (Pause) You're going to have to...Your legs are really filthy. Not much I can do about it. Video Clip ( 3 min 36 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, I'll get them off. Why don't you start back...

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Just kick them against each other when you go up.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Start on up.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: You might shake the bags.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: And don't forget your PLSS an...

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: (Responding to Bob) No.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Do what?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: PLSS antennas .

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Although it doesn't make much difference anymore.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: That's to get them out of the way. The big bag didn't stay closed very long.

A17A1702454.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1702454.text: That's a good readback, Ron. Okay, it's all yours on the Flight Plan, and - Ron, we might point out that, if you get going into the presleep checklist here, in the VHF comm configuration. Get that done, then there's a break - you'll lose comm and you'll have a 15 - 20-minute break, you can jump into your eat and then go right to bed.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I don't know how we're going to get that in.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Well, I can hand it to you.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: It never had a very good closure on it... 170:34:12 Cernan: That Velcro won't hold.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: ...but it can be closed.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: I had it over the top. The latch was closed, but...

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Oh, it won't hold with all that weight in there. Okay, I got your antenna.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, let me get a high...Got to close this. You don't want that in your way.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I can't close it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Oh. (Chuckles) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: You might try. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Get all your flaps? (Pause) Okay, hold your head down. (Pause) No.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Won't go, huh?

A17A1702454.speaker: Evans
A17A1702454.text: [Garble] on panel 9. Okay, it's Receive. And, we're in Duplex Alpha. And Squelch B is - Whooh! About 5, that cuts out the noise. I don't know if I'd ever hear them or not, but, anyhow, it cuts out the noise. Okay, let's see - Bat C is about 36.7. Pyro A: barely below the line, but we'll say 37.0, and pyro B is 37.0. Okay, looks like it's in good shape.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: No. Will that bother you getting in? [Gene has been unable to get Jack's antenna tied down. Here, they are deciding to leave it up.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I can probably make it. 170:35:05 Cernan: Okay, head on up. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: (Missing the rung) Oops. Try that again. Okay, why don't you hand me the neutron flux, and I'll put it...

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, neutron flux.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: ...on the platform. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Why don't you start in, and I'll get some of these bags (the full SCBs) out of the way.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Well, I just...(Pause) You don't want to hand them to me up here?

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: And, Jack, for your thoughts, we've agreed that you can delete the tracking light. We'd like to get you guys in as soon as possible. Seven minutes now. And we'll delete the tracking light test. [Jack is on cuff checklist page LMP-32 . Gene is on CDR-34 .] [Cernan - "Jack was supposed to turn the tracking light on so that I could see if it was blinking. Ron needed to track us visually. Bob was getting quite worried about us getting in, because I remember that I told him, 'Don't worry, we're doing it.' Jack and I felt like we had our act together. We weren't pushing against oxygen starvation or

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: LM Crew
A17A1702454.text: (Garbled) (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay, that's all I can handle up here. One more and I can put it up here.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Watch the cover on this one. (Pause) Got it?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Got it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Stand it up, because the cover won't hack it. (Long Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. Soon as you get on in, I'll come up to the porch. (Long Pause) Video Clip ( 2 min 55 sec 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Where's that EVA pallet that's always in my way?

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: I think we aren't going to have one of those (an EVA) tomorrow, Jack, so we did away with that. (Pause) We hope we're not going to have one of those tomorrow.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Bob, we're maximizing our efforts, so just bear with us. Jack's going to be in about 30 seconds, and I'm on the ladder hauling some stuff up now. (Light static starts) [Gene is on CDR-35 .]

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Roger. "Don't panic."

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Well, we're not. I just don't want you to.

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: I never panic there, guys. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: (In the cabin by now) Got some stuff for me?

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Yes, sir. (Pause) This is not the time to rush. It's the time to do it nice and slow and right.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Oh, we're all right.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay. (Pause) You're not going to like this (big bag), but I'm going to give you this one first because I've got it in my hand.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Either one. (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Oh, hang in there...I've got it! Oh, that's a heavy bag.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: That is heavy, babe. Let me tell you, that's heavy. (Pause) [Schmitt - "I wouldn't be surprised if we had almost a hundred pounds in that big bag. I think that all the big rocks were in there. But it's strange, that's still not a lot of weight. We must have been feeling the mass more than the weight."] [The actual weight of the big bag, as reported at 171:36:39, is 71 terrestrial pounds or 12 lunar pounds. This is slightly more than half the 137 pounds of samples they collected during this EVA.] [Cernan - "Relatively, I guess it was heavy. We didn't pick up a hundred pounds of stuff very often

A17A1702454.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1702454.text: That's affirm, Ron. That closes it all out and you can just precede [sic] through your checklist and we'll stand by, if you want any calls. We'll see you tomorrow. And, the Doctor's just...

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay; next.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Can you reach that one? If not, I'll shove it in further.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I got it. (Pause) Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: One more coming at you.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Tilting up right now.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Go ahead. (Long Pause) [Fendell is looking at Earth.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay, next.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, tilting up at you.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Got it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay? (Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay, next. Okay, Bob, we've got...

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Oh, here... 170:39:55 Schmitt: Big bag, three SRCs (means "SCBs") and a neutron flux. Video Clip ( 3 min 36 sec 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 36 Mb MPEG Clip )

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Okay, and we gather an ETB coming up with two cameras in it. [The ETB is hanging near the ground from the lanyard. Gene is pulling it up by hand.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: ETB's next. (Pause) (To Gene) Got an ETB? Yeah. (Pause) ETB has two cameras.

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Okay. And as you guys say farewell to the Moon, we're looking up to the Earth (with the Rover TV camera) down here where you guys are returning pretty soon.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: (To Jack) Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: You're going to have to push that.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, let me get it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: That's all right. I'll wait until you're ready.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay? Can you make it?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Yeah, I've got it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, let me get that other thing (garbled). (Pause) [Fendell points the TV at the LM.] 170:41:00 Cernan: Bob, this is Gene, and I'm on the surface; and, as I take man's last step from the surface, back home for some time to come - but we believe not too long into the future - I'd like to just (say) what I believe history will record. That America's challenge of today has forged man's destiny of tomorrow. And, as we leave the Moon at Taurus- Littrow, we leave as we came and, God willing, as we shall return, with peace and hope for all mankind. "Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17."

A17A1702454.speaker: Parker
A17A1702454.text: Roger, Geno. Thank you very much. (Pause) [Journal Contributor Rob Bourke had an opportunity to interview Gene during a visit to the Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, California, in September 2000. He writes that his opening question concerned Gene's final words on the surface ""Was it on purpose or pure chance that the words, 'America' and 'Challenge' also happened to be the call sign names of his two spacecraft on that flight? (That is, Command Module 'America' and Lunar Module 'Challenger'.) It was a great opener. He responded with a genuine smile and said that no one had asked about tha

A17A1702454.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1702454.text: Okay, let me look at FAO here. He's - he'll give me the word.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Bob, I am up on the ladder and I'm going to be going through the hatch. (Long Pause)

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Gene, I've got to get out of your way.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Yup. (Long Pause; static) [Here, Jack is closing the hatch so that he can get behind it and give Gene room to get in the cabin.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, let me...(Pause) Okay, babe, here I come.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Come on in.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Hatch look good to you?

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Well, it's dirty.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Keep her down. Buttons. (Pause) Come towards me a little. There you go. (Pause) Okay, you've got it.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Okay, I'm inside the hatch.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay. [Fendell points the TV at the ground again, possibly for thermal reasons.]

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Let me look at that hatch once more.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Okay.

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: That's the last time we want to have to open that.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: Caught in the same way again (on the DSKY).

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Yep. Let me just...I can see down there.

A17A1702454.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1702454.text: I can see (the hatch seal)...

A17A1702454.speaker: Cernan
A17A1702454.text: Does it look good to you?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Then we've got to turn our H2O off. Oh, we've got to turn our...Let's turn our water off first, before you lock it (meaning the hatch).

A17A1704450.speaker: Evans
A17A1704450.text: I'm wearing the comm carrier now. But it itches if you sl - if you leave it on all night, you know?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Well, it's locked now. Can you get your own water? If not, I'll get it.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: I doubt it. Haven't been able to before.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, I'll get it. [Schmitt - "I don't remember exactly where the shutoff was, but I just never could reach it. Maybe not even in training. With his longer arms, Gene could handle it. I was probably standing facing the rear - which would have made it easy for him to get to the shutoff. Or, maybe I was facing inboard helping him with the door. It would have been a whole lot easier with more room in the LM; of course, (laughing) the suit probably would have expanded to fill it. Parkinson's Law applied to lunar modules."] [ Parkinson's Law - : " Work expands so as to fill the time available for i

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Have you got yours?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Let me see. (Pause) Mine's off. No, wait a minute. (Pause) Mine's off. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Evans
A17A1704450.text: Okay; get the onboard readouts, recycle the fans; we'll save the potable water - Waste Management Overboard Drain - okay, that's Off; Waste Stowage Vent valves are closed. Battery Vent, by the way, is in Vent. How about a battery readout? [Garble] Alpha is 1. - Okay, Optics are Zero [garble] Optics is [garble]. Optics are stowed. Cabin Pressure Regs, two...

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: No, I can't get it.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. I'll get it for you. Not now. Before you move any more, let me get over here out of the way.

A17A1704450.speaker: Parker
A17A1704450.text: Okay. And pay attention here, 17, when you come on, we'd like you to leave Press Reg A which is the one that's been Off...We'd like to leave that closed.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: (To Jack) Turn around.

A17A1704450.speaker: Parker
A17A1704450.text: Just use Press Reg B (garbled).

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, Bob.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Get it, Geno?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Turn some more, I can almost reach it. Another...

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay. (Pause) [The three PLSS water controls - the feedwater diverter valve and the primary and auxiliary On/Off levers - are located on the lower right front corner, with the diverter valve being at the corner and the other two being inboard from it on the front edge. The levers have dramatically different shapes so that they can be easily distinguished by feel.]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. Your Aux water is Off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, Bob...

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: No, no. The Prim(ary) water.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: (Garbled).

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Standby. (Pause) Your Prim water's Off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Is your Prim Off?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Yep. It's Off. Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Reading) PLSS Prim water closed. Forward hatch Closed and Locked. Okay, I've got to get the upper (dump) valve, Jack. Move in.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay. (Pause) How's that?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Oh, that ought to do it. (Pause) It's Auto and I've got the lock on it. (Pause) Okay. Now, Bob, say again which Reg A you want left.

A17A1704450.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1704450.text: Hey, Ron, we didn't - we didn't copy your battery manifold - or battery manifold readout.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Reg A left closed, I got it.

A17A1704450.speaker: Parker
A17A1704450.text: That's affirm, Jack.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Go ahead.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, dump valves are both Auto...Cabin Repress, Auto.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Cabin Repress, Auto .

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, and I've got plenty of (PLSS) oxygen so we're in good shape for an Auto Repress.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Cabin Repress breaker Closed on 16.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay, Cabin Repress, Closed.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Come on, baby, there it comes. Half a psi. Okay, it is increasing. (Repress becomes audible) You can go to Cabin on the regulator .

A17A1704450.speaker: Evans
A17A1704450.text: Cabin Repress valve - I haven't kicked them off. I think one of them was closed. Okay. Tunnel Vent valve should still be off. Okay, it's Off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Reg B.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Yeah, just the one regulator your using. (Pause) 1.5 (psi).

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Reg B is in Cabin.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, she's coming up. There's 2.0. Your next move will be to get your PLSS O2, Off. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: 2.5 (psi). Okay, get your PLSS O2, Off. (Pause) Mine's Off. Get it? We'll be soft-suited shortly. (Pause) Just get around. I'll get it for you.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: I think that I've got it. (Pause) There I got it. [The oxygen control is on the chest-mounted RCU .]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. "Verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6 to 5.0." We'll watch it here.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: I'm watching. (Pause) Five (psi). 170:48:xx Cernan: Okay. 5.0. 170:48:xx Schmitt: 5.0. 170:48:xx Cernan: Boy, it got hot in here, didn't it? Okay, purge valve to Depress; verify your circuit breakers. 170:48:xx Schmitt: Say again, that last one. [Schmitt - "When Gene gets business-like, he sometimes talks too fast."]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: You don't need your (garbled) Depress (garbled) but you don't need it.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Oh, yeah. No. [They are now at the top of the right-hand column of Surface 7-1 . According to plan, they should be at 169:40 minutes into the mission and are, therefore, still about an hour behind, as they were at the start of the EVA. The planned start of the rest period is at 174:39 and they will actually start it at about 175:20, having gained back about a half hour. Because their workload between wake-up and launch is fairly light, they are in very good shape.]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Verify your circuit breakers...White Dots out plus EVA decals.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: No White Dots (in). (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, I'm squared away there. (Pause) (Are you) squared away?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Standby.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Looks good.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Stay at (circuit breaker panel) 16 now, ECS Suit Fan 2, Closed?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Suit Fan 2's Closed.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Suit Fan Delta-P, Closed.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Closed.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Caution lights are on, that's good. Until the Sep(arator)...Wait, ECS Caution...They'll go out when it (the Separator) winds up. Doff gloves, stow on comm panel. Oh, oh! Sweet music to my ears. [Schmitt - "This sounds like Gene's hands were bothering him. Whatever he might have said later, he was happy to get those gloves off."]

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Going to have to put them on again, in a few minutes.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: I know. It's still sweet music.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Come on, now. [Once they get hooked up to the LM ECS and get their PLSSs off, they will put their gloves back on so that they can depressurize the cabin, open the hatch, and jettison the PLSSs and other unneeded gear.] 170:49:34 Cernan: I have never seen so much dirt and dust in my whole life. Ever. (Pause) Ron's not going to be able to see through either one of these helmet visors. (Laughs) Yes, he will. [Schmitt - "There was dust on everything we wore. Gene succeeded in falling and I did too - several times. The helmets had a lot of dust on them, and I suspect we got them pretty badly scratc

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: But they sure do get scratched, if you're not careful. (Pause) Okay. (Long Pause) I think it's harder getting them (the gloves) off, these days, than it is getting them on. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Ah, I did it! Patience. Maximum effort. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: There's one. (Long Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay, (my) gloves are off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: My gloves are off. We're right there (on the cue card). (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay, "verify safety on the dump valve ". I'll do that. (Pause) Okay, I verify that, there. (Garbled).

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: We want to take a double look at something down there.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: (Garbled). It's locked. [They have been using the overhead valve and what may be happening here is that Jack first checked the safety on the overhead valve and is now verifying the safety on the hatch valve.] [Training photo KSC-72PC-540 shows the overhead valve at the upper right.]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Uh-huh. (Pause) Happy?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yep. Okay, Descent H2O valve, Open.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, "Descent H2O valve, Open."

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: That's Open.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: "Remove purge valves, stow in purse ." (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, "disconnect OPS hose." (Long Pause) Oh boy! That lock/lock is just tight on there, Jack.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: It is. (Pause) Got it.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Your's Off?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yeh.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. "Connect LM hoses, red to red, and blue to blue." We've got to do that this time, because we've got to dump the PLSSs. Okay?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay. Let me turn around here.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Let me get out of your way.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: I'll get back in here.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, I'm out of the way now.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: How would you like to get off the PLSS water and get some spacecraft water, too? 170:53:02 Cernan: Oh, that's the next thing. Suit Isol(ation Valve) to Suit Flow, On; and then we'll put PLSS pump and fan Off. Then we'll disconnect the PLSS water and connect spacecraft water. (Pause) [The switches for the PLSS pumps and fans are on the chest-mounted RCUs. Note that, after the second EVA Gene and Jack commented about something being hot. One possibility is that the hot object was an RCU . If so, it is notable that there is no comment about heat here.] [Schmitt - "Driving back from Station 5, the

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: You might unhook that stuff up there so you can get to your hoses.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: I can't reach it though.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Oh, okay. I can get it, I think.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: I can get it. (Pause) Okay, I got them. (Pause) Okay, we want red to red and blue to blue. (Pause) We got to verify these, too, because...

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yep. [They want to make sure that they have the hoses hooked up properly before they depressurize the cabin for the jettison.]

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Bob, you still with us?

A17A1704450.speaker: Parker
A17A1704450.text: You bet, I wouldn't leave for the world.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay, I'm hooked up and locked.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: You want to verify? And I'll do it for you, if you want.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, see if you can't find this one. See it?

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yeah.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Here, verify the red one. Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: In and locked.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Got the red one, locked. (Pause)

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. Let me take a look at yours. (Pause) Locked. (Pause) Locked.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Locked.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, now...

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Ready for Suit Flow?

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Yes, sir; Suit Flow on both of them.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Okay.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Oh man, it feels great!

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yes, sir.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: PLSS pump Off and PLSS fan Off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: PLSS fan's Off; pump's Off.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay. Disconnect PLSS water from PGA. Connect the LM water. Boy, I never thought air could feel so cool.

A17A1704450.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1704450.text: Yeah.

A17A1704450.speaker: Cernan
A17A1704450.text: Okay, the PLSS water is disconnected. I think that's mine. Yeah, that's mine. Spacecraft water. (Pause) Okay. Mine's connected. (Pause)

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1705507csm.text: Hey, Ron. We hear an intervalometer going off every 20 seconds...

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1705507csm.text: [Laughter] No; I can't figure out what that is.

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1705507csm.text: How about pushing on that (spacecraft water hose to seat it in the connector)?

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1705507csm.text: Yeah, but I want to see it first. (Pause)

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1705507csm.text: Rog. I'm sure. Well, we're going to get a recording of it. I mean, we - I am going to listen to the recording when I get a chance and I'll show it to you. Because it's been the last 2 days, every 20 seconds, big as life.

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1705507csm.text: Watch your helmet. You're going to scratch it.

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1705507csm.text: You don't have your visor down. Neither do I.

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1705507csm.text: Okay, connect...Okay, PLSS mode O. Bob, we're both going off the air. We'll get on LM comm.

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Parker
a17_1705507csm.text: Okay. We'll be waiting for you. We're here. [They are about to start the steps on Surface 7-2 .]

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1705507csm.text: How about some cooling? [Schmitt - "Between here and about 171:01, it sounds like there was some recovery in my voice from the let down of getting back in and struggling to get the LM configured and pressurized and stuff like that. By 171:01, I sound much more businesslike."]

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1705507csm.text: Okay, zap me with it, and go "O", and then put your audio breaker, Open; and connect the LM comm. Then an audio breaker Closed. Okay? (Long Pause)

a17_1705507csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1705507csm.text: [Laughter] Okay. Thank you much. We'll see you all in the morning then.

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: Okay, Bob. I never stopped doing what I wanted to do anyway even though a Marine was talking. (Pause) [Schmitt - "Apparently, the MCC-H Conference was just a 60 minute pad they built into the flight plan in case we had to talk about lift-off or a LM problem of something like that."]

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Okay. CDR's OPS 6100 (psi); LMP, 6500. [Comm Break. They are performing the OPS checkout near the middle of the right-hand column of Surface 7-2 .] 171:09:33 Schmitt: Okay, Houston this is the LMP. LMP's OPS is regulating at 4.25.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay, I copy that. [They are checking the OPSs to see if they produce a proper regulated pressure. Each contains oxygen bottles pressurized at greater than 6000 psi and that pressure needs to be regulated down to the 3.8 psi that the suit is designed to handle. Jack's OPS is regulating at a pressure that is slightly higher than normal. Previously, Gene described plans for using the OPSs in case he and Jack were unable to dock with the Command Module and had to make a suited EVA transfer. If one or both of the OPSs fails this check of the regulators, they will keep one or both of the PLSSs rath

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: And the CDR's is 3.9.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay that.

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: That might be ...I started...Let me bleed it off and let me see what it regulates at next time. I didn't have my hose locked, Bob, and it came off the first try. (Pause) [Schmitt - "To check the regulator, you had to have the hose blocked off and I was saying that I may not have done that. As I recall, there was a place you locked the hose in to seal it off; and then you opened the valve to see how it regulated into the hose. I interpret what I said here to mean that the hose wasn't locked down and that there was some flow out. But that would have given a lower regulated pressure; so, I don't

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: Bob, we'll take another OPS check later on when we stow them. We're pressing on. (Pause) [Cernan - "Obviously, it didn't concern us. If it was regulating at 4.25 it would have made your suit harder, but it still would have been okay. If it had been regulating at 2.0, it would have been something different."]

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Jack, they're saying we better do that (second check) before you throw out the PLSSs because we have to verify a good one before you dump the PLSSs.

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: Okay, we'll do that. [Long Comm Break]

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Okay, Houston, we rechecked the LMP's OPS and it's regulating at 4.25, again.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Is that a steady 4.25, Jack?

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Yeah, it's done that twice now. (Pause)

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay, and it's steady once you do a check, right?

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Right. It's open now. We've been watching it for about a minute, now.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay, we'll go with it then, Jack.

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Okay. [Comm Break. Houston has decided that Jack's OPS is acceptable as is. Once they get the OPSs stowed and get the PLSSs positioned for the jettison, they will weigh the sample containers, just in case they have hauled in too many rocks and have to jettison some of the rocks along with the PLSSs. They are moving to the tasks on Surface 7-3 .]

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: Okay, Bob, we're going to start the (sample) weighing process here...

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay we're ready to copy...

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: ...It might take a couple minutes to get things squared away.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay give us a call. We're ready to copy the weights.

A17A1710709.speaker: Cernan
A17A1710709.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Bob, sample (bag) 15 Echo has a bunch of dust that gradually accumulated in my (shin) pocket.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: No fair, Jack! You can't go collecting samples after the EVA's over! [Comm Break]

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Say Bob, right now I can't find the sample containment bag number 5. Number 5 collection bag will be in (containment) bag 3.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay, we note that. Thank you. Very good. (Long Pause) [ Sample Containment Bags were flown on the J missions to help reduce the amount of dust in the cabin. The Sample Collection Bags were put inside the Containment Bags . Photos of containment bags in the National Air & Space collection courtesy Allan Needell.]

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: Okay, and we're going to cross out "3" on the bag, and put a "5" on it.

A17A1710709.speaker: Parker
A17A1710709.text: Okay, or I think we could keep track of it otherwise; but that's fine.

A17A1710709.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1710709.text: That's for our reference too. [Very Long Comm Break. During this break, they are weighing the sample containers.] [Cernan - "Each pound mattered. I'm not saying that we would have thrown out a pound of rock. There were margins. But, weight translated into less Delta-V(elocity) and into fuel."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: And Danny's not out there to hand us in the lightweight PLSSs! [This is another reference to the mock-up PLSSs used during training and to suit engineer Danny Schaiewitz.] [Schmitt - "The PLSSs were handed in for egress training and we may not have had PLSSs in the cabin, just to protect the equipment."] Video Clip (1 min 08 sec 4.3 Mb mp4 ) PLSS jettison sequence filmed by Ed von Renouard , Video Technician at the Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station during Apollo. On a few occasions, he filmed his video console monitor using his personal Super-8 camera handheld. Digitized by Colin Mackellar, w

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay. Here goes the old...Whose PLSS is this now?

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Well, look at it, if you want a memory.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: That must be yours; it's red. No, that's mine...No, it's yours. Here goes the old Commander's PLSS.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay, baby thanks for doing a good job. And that was a backup PLSS too. [Cernan - "The PLSSs were all the same but, for some reason, the decision was made quite late on to use my backup. I don't know what happened to the primary."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Well, that wasn't very good.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: It walked down the ladder.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: It went down as gracefully as you did. [Schmitt - "I was leaning over the hatch and pushing the PLSS out with my hands. Gene was probably watching out the window. I don't think I could see down the ladder and just saw it bounce a little bit."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Look at that. Okay, what's next?

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Well, I can give you some of these. (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Here hold...Okay.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Everything is in here.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay. That's the first thing.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (Garbled)...(Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Beautiful gloves.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Well, Houston, I think we ought to probably just mention, anyway. We are jettisoning two sets of EVA gloves. I think that's worth mentioning. Because they did their job!

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Just like everything else did its job. Let me jettison mine.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay. (Pause) [As indicated by a discussion at 174:52:48, they are both wearing their used EV gloves and have just jettisoned their unused gloves. The checklist does not call for any glove jettison. It does, however, call for boot jettison, which they seem not to have done.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Ooops, we didn't get them clear. (Laughs)

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: Okay, we copy two sets of EVA gloves to the surface for the last time.

A17A1715320.speaker: LM Crew
A17A1715320.text: (Garbled)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: They're very reluctant. (Laughs) What else have you got there?

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: ISS?

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (Garbled) together.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: The other ISS. (Pause) [The only reference we have been able to find to an ISS - other than Inertial Sensor System, which doesn't make sense in this context - is on page 7-3 in the surface checklist where the crew is instructed to "Remove ISS, Wrap & Tie the Following: Lunar Boots (4), RCUs (2), Armrest (1), Yo-Yo's (2)" and then on page 7-4 where they jettison the ISS along with the PLSSs. Gene and Jack think ISS may be Interim Stowage Shelf, perhaps a part of the Interim Stowage Assembly.] [Note that neither of the yo-yos was actually discarded. Gene's was sold at auction in early 2006 for U

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Nope, one more.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: That it?

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Got one more thing.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: PLSS.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: No wait.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Oh, is there something (garbled)?

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Watch it.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (Garbled) this, I'll get it. (Long Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay, let's get this out.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay, the old LMP's PLSS.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (Garbled) that OPS stays where it is.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, get it down there and then put your foot against it and it'll probably go. (Pause) The only geologist's PLSS on the Moon. (Pause) (To Gene, who is kicking the PLSS out the hatch) Good boy. Have fun PLSS. Ooh. (Pause) [Cernan - "I remember that one of the PLSSs sort of got hung up on the porch and I had to get way out with my leg to get it unstuck. You didn't have room to throw them out; you just had room to push them out."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: That'll stay there. Okay, we got everything else?

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay... [AS17-145- 22196 , 22199 , and 22211 show the jettisoned PLSSs. These photographs will be taken after Gene and Jack get out of their suits.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Hatch seal clear.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Pretty good.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Pretty good from here.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Too bad we don't have a broom (to sweep the dust out).

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Is that everything else? Nothing else here to go. Nothing behind you. Nothing here. (Pause) Okay! (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Hatch going closed. (Pause) Get to do this again tomorrow. [They will do a very brief trash jettison in the morning.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: I know it. Okay, forward hatch closed. Let me see if I can't lock it. (Long Pause) Okay, it's locked. (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay, "Cabin Repress, Dump valve , both Auto, verify."

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: They all are auto and locked.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: "Cabin Repress, Auto. Verify."

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Verified.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: "On 16, Cabin Repress, Closed."

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Repress going Closed.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: "Master Alarm and Cabin Warning Light (should come) on." There it is. (Pause) Cabin's coming up. (Pause) Okay, it's increasing and you go to Cabin on that one reg .

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Reg Bravo. Cabin.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Okay, cabin's coming. It's about 5 (psi). Okay, (warning) lights are off. Repress stopped. Cabin pressure stable. (Pause) Okay, Houston, Challenger; we're going to take off our gloves. (No answer; pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Hello, Houston. How does it look?

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: Roger. You look stable, and...Stand by. (Pause) Okay, you're Go to unsuit there, guys. (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Speaking of suits. These things perform super! (Long Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay, and we can get our helmets off.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: If I can ever get unsuited. (Pause) (Garbled; laughs) That's my hand. Let me try the other one.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Oh, let me get it for you. I'm free here. No sense...Yeah, but I'm...(Both laugh) There. Okay.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: The right one went easy last night. I think they're all really getting (dusty)...

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Oh, and the helmet is off, and I'm stowing it in the BRA! (Pause) Well, there's no changing our minds now (about a fourth EVA), the PLSSs are going to be hard to retrieve. (Pause) But you could if you had to, though. [Both Gene and Jack have the impression that the BRA was hung in the back of the cabin. Charlie Duke joins the conversation.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Duke
A17A1715320.text: Challenger, Houston. From the old backup crew that followed you every step of the way, super job on EVA you guys.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (Thinking he's talking to John Young) Thank you, John. Appreciate the words, Jose. But we also appreciate your helping us get it this far.

A17A1715320.speaker: Duke
A17A1715320.text: (Retaliating) Roger, Neil.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Hey, you know, and all those things you tell people...(Hearing Charlie's "Neil") Was that Charlie!? I haven't heard your voice since down...You know all those good things you tell us about dust and all those other things: you know, you believe them all just like everybody else does, but you've just got to come out here and experience it for yourself to really be a believer.

A17A1715320.speaker: Duke
A17A1715320.text: Yeah, well I take it back about it all looks the same. [Schmitt - "Charlie thought that all parts of the Moon looked just like all other parts of the Moon. And I think the TV of Taurus-Littrow changed his mind. He and John were in a pretty desolate, unscenic place at the Descartes site."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Hey, it really doesn't, Charlie; but all those physical things you get handicapped with...There's a lot of easy things as far as one-sixth g, but all those other things (you've got to experience). You know there's nothing like doing it to be a believer.

A17A1715320.speaker: Duke
A17A1715320.text: Well, you guys did it great.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Charlie, it may all look the same, but Taurus-Littrow, mark my words, has some variety.

A17A1715320.speaker: Duke
A17A1715320.text: Yeah, we could tell that, Jack. Great job.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Thank you, Charlie; and thank you for all the help.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Hey, Charlie, remember a long time ago when I said something about being down among them. I didn't know what it was until we got here. [Cernan - "Charlie was CapCom on Apollo 10. When Tom Stafford and I went down in the Lunar Module over the top of the Apollo 11 landing site, I said 'Boy, we are down among 'em,' meaning that it seemed like we were going right down over the mountain tops."] [Journal Contributor Brian Lawrence believes the exact quote is "We is down among 'em, Charlie."]

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: Challenger, we have a good word from the old program manager...

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (To Jack) Where are we (in the checklist)?

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: ...even though you guys were pretty piggy there in bringing rocks back, we're going to let you keep them all. You only busted the red line (that is, are overweight) by 40 pounds.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Okay. He's a pretty good guy any way. [Deke Slayton joins the conversation.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Slayton
A17A1715320.text: That assumes your good buddy upstairs gets a good plane change tomorrow. [If the plane change leaves Evans in less than an optimal orbit for rendezvous, they might have to discard some of the samples.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Oh, he will; and I'll tell you, Gene and I both have lost 20 pounds apiece on this mission.

A17A1715320.speaker: Slayton
A17A1715320.text: We can believe that.

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: (To Jack) Verify safeties (on the dump valve locks). Hey, we're on VOX anyway. Let's go to ICS/PTT.

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: It's safer that way. [In a moment, they will switch from voice-activated comm to Push-to-Talk. The safeties were pins with wires on them so that they wouldn't drop off and get lost.]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Yeah, specially when you don't know you're talking. (Pause) Okay, we came to the end of the EVA-3 prep and post card.

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: Roger. We're following you to the surface checklist. [They are now starting Surface 7-5 .]

A17A1715320.speaker: Cernan
A17A1715320.text: Hey, Jack and I are going to frame this page 2-3 , cut it down the middle and each take half. (Pause)

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: I'm going to take the front half. Gene will take the back half. (Long Pause) [Page 2-3 in the LM Lunar Surface Checklist lists procedures for a One-Man EVA. The reverse side - page 2-4 - is a procedure to follow in the event of a LM repress failure.] [Schmitt - "We probably never decided who would go out (for a one-man EVA). The back half of the page is something immaterial to the one-man EVA, and this remark suggests that we had had some discussion about who was going to be the one man."] [Cernan - "It wasn't discussed in that much detail but, if we only had one PLSS, I suppose that - politic

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: Okay, Roberto, we're going to manage the old batteries.

A17A1715320.speaker: Parker
A17A1715320.text: Okay, and Challenger we're ready to manage the old batteries.

A17A1715320.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1715320.text: The old ED batteries are 37.2. A and B. (Pause) (To Gene) I was just going to say I wish we had a broom. [Comm Break.] [The following is a discussion about the use of batteries versus fuel cells in the LM design.] [Schmitt - "The early plan, the first design reference mission that Grumman put together, was a fuel-cell vehicle. And what killed the fuel cells were the fuel-cell problems that Gemini ran into. And that scared the managers, so they went to batteries. It's unfortunate, because the Apollo fuel cell was a different fuel cell"] [Cernan - "We also had a Block II development of solar pan

A17A1724657.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1724657.text: Challenger, Houston. 172:xx:xx Schmitt: Go ahead. 172:xx:xx Mattingly: Hey, how about if we hit a Pro(ceed) on the DSKY and get it into P00 and back into Standby? We're worrying about the clock registers overflowing. And we'd like to get that done before 172:50, or somewhere in that neighborhood. 172:xx:xx Schmitt: Okay; stand by. (Pause) Is that what you wanted? 172:xx:xx Mattingly: Oh, we can't watch it, Jack. If you just tell us that you've got it into P00 and back into P06. 172:xx:xx Schmitt: That's what happened. (Pause) I thought you watched it the other night. 172:xx:xx Mattingly: No, w

A17A1724657.speaker: Cernan
A17A1724657.text: Hello, Ken. How do you read Challenger CDR?

A17A1724657.speaker: Cernan
A17A1724657.text: Okay. [Very Long Comm Break.] [Gene is now out of his suit and they are probably working on Jack's, now.]

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Oh well, yeah. Yeah, that's right. And, now as I think back, I guess that's the main difference between the tan rocks at Station 2 and Station 6; because the ones at 6 appear to have an igneous texture or at least a very crystalline texture and inclusion-like masses of other rocks. Whereas, the ones at Station 2, they seem to be fragment breccias, as I recall.

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: That's right.

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Although they may have been recrystallized or metamorphosed, they were clearly breccias at Station 2. I just forgot about that.

A17A1734201.speaker: Parker
A17A1734201.text: Okay, copy that.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay, and "can you amplify your description going out to Station 6? In particular were there blue-gray and tan-gray bands on the North Massif?" (Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Rather than bands, there were lines that appeared to be the upper terminus of the source of the boulders that were strewn below that line. And those lines tended to be either...(to) show a blue-gray source or a tan-gray source, if you will. (Garbled for a few seconds) Oh, those (garbled) bags.

A17A1734201.speaker: Parker
A17A1734201.text: Challenger, if you think you're talking to us, you're breaking up badly.

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: I just thought you might be interested; we just had a little spurt of dust come up by the window.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Was there a sleigh with it? (Long Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Wise guy. (Pause) [The date is December 14. It is about 2:37 a.m. in Houston. Mattingly is wondering if they've had an early visit from Santa Claus.]

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay. Did you see very much of dust, or was it just one little shot?

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: One little shot, it was actually just particles. Something we threw out must have popped.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: (Returning to the geology questions) Okay. "Do you have any preliminary stratigraphic sequence for the plains?"

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: For the plains, huh? (Pause) Well, my guess would be that the Van Serg breccias were the oldest rocks. The subfloor gabbro's the next oldest; and the mantling material's the youngest. But the only good clear relationship was mantle on top of the subfloor gabbros. We really don't have a good relationship of the (Van Serg) breccias and I guess I lean towards thinking that Van Serg was a window in the subfloor rather than being a bed of some kind on top of the subfloor.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay, and "do you have an opinion on what underlies the Sculptured Hills?"

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Well, I think, we said...The rake sample is probably going to have to tell the tale there. My guess is - from the boulders of subfloor around up there that are of gabbro - that maybe the Sculptured Hills are a version of the subfloor rocks. I don't think that the orthopyroxene anorthosite rock was necessarily indigenous to the Sculptured Hills. It was glass-coated and permeated by glass, so I suspect it may have been thrown there by an impact somewhere else. [Schmitt - "The Sculptured Hills are almost certainly a variety of the ejecta blanket of the Orientale Basin. Why they have a different s

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: All right sir, we've got one last thing for you to clean up. Back on page 7-6 of your checklist, it looks like we may have skipped some steps on the (Cabin) Gas Return Valve, and (we'd) like to make sure that you get that to Auto and the (Suit) Gas Diverter (Valve) pushed to Cabin before you stow the oxygen hoses. (Long Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Okay, Ken, we got Cabin Gas Return (Valve) , Auto.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay, understand Auto and you got the Select to Cabin?

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Yeah, Gas Diverter's pushed to Cabin and we're drying the PGAs (the suits) out.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: All right, sir. (Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: And I guess if you could go in...My feeling is if you go to the bottom of every one of those large craters like Camelot, and you'd examine some of these fragments on the walls and down into the bottom, I just get a feeling you'd find this blue-gray breccia down there.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: All right, sir.

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: I mean in all the big craters like Camelot.

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: I think maybe that's true; however, we do not see isolated fragments of it very often, if at all, out here on the plains themselves, away from the craters. So if the blue-gray breccia - (correcting himself) the Van Serg breccia - does underlie the subfloor, it's far enough down (below the surface) that the craters we have apparently have not penetrated and brought up much of that kind of material. (Pause) Well, that's it.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay guys, it's time to press on and finish up chow time and I've got your stowage summaries whenever you're ready for that, to get started on.

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: Okay, Ken let us finish eating, then we'll go back to work.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay, give me a call when you're ready. (Long Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: (Inadvertent key) I'll help you (garbled). [Long Comm Break]

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Okay. Ken I'd like to go ahead and hear your recommendations on stowage and I'll write it down.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: All right, sir. On (Surface Checklist) page 2-2, I've got some numbers to fill in at the bottom under the collection bag stowage. (Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Okay, I've got it.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Okay, number 1 with the aft of the engine cover is bag 8. And then the second line, it's bag 7. The third line it's bag 6 left-hand and 5 right-hand. And the last line is bag 2 and 4. And you can disregard the max. weights. [The planned maximum weights were 40 pounds aft of the engine cover; 40 pounds in the LHMS (Left-hand Mid-Section) which is a stowage area just aft of the area where Gene's PLSS had been stowed and, now, the rock boxes are fastened to the wall; 40 pounds each in the LHSSC and RHSSC (left-hand and right-hand-side stowage compartments) which are below the side instrument pane

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Okay, just so we got it straight: aft engine cover, bag 8; left hand side, bag 7. Left hand plus the right-hand side: number 6 left-hand and 5 right. And the ISA (Interim Stowage Assembly) bags 2 and 4.

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: That's affirmative. (Pause)

A17A1734201.speaker: Cernan
A17A1734201.text: Okay. [Long Comm Break]

A17A1734201.speaker: Mattingly
A17A1734201.text: Hey, Jack, the people down here watching things noticed that your Suit Isol(ation) Valve is still in Disconnect. If you're trying to dry the suit out, you might check that. It's your option what you want to do with it.

A17A1734201.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1734201.text: I'm glad somebody is watching things! Thank you. [Schmitt - "Ken was being very diplomatic."] [Very Long Comm Break]

a17_1794112.text: This is Apollo Control; 179 hours, 41 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. About a minute until we have lock-on with the Command Module America on 47th revolution around the Moon. Shortly after we have good solid lockup, the Spacecraft Communicator Ken Mattingly will call Ron Evans on air/ground 2 circuit for a wakeup. We'll bring that up at that time. Meanwhile the crew in the Lunar Module Challenger is still asleep at this time, with some 3 hours remaining until they're awakened. Standing by for word that we've locked onto the Command Module downlink. We've had acquisition. We'll bring up air/ground

a17_1794502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1794502csm.text: Good morning, America. Rise and shine.

a17_1794502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1794502csm.text: Hello, America, this is Houston. Over. [Long pause.]

a17_1794502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1794502csm.text: Hey, Houston, this is the Command Module Pilot on the United States spaceship America. I'll be ready to go to work as soon as I can get untangled.

a17_1794502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1794502csm.text: Okay. We got plenty of that for you.

a17_1794502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1794502csm.text: [Laughter.] Okay. I think I woke up just about the time - just before you called, for some reason.

a17_1794910csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1794910csm.text: Well, Houston, at least it's daylight today. Yesterday you got me up in the middle of the night.

a17_1794910csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1794910csm.text: Oh, this is a gentleman's day.

a17_1794910csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1794910csm.text: Of course, I guess it's really a 2-hour day when you go around the Moon, isn't it?

a17_1794910csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1794910csm.text: You don't get so tired that way.

a17_1794910csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1794910csm.text: Okay. S-Band Mode is to Voice, Squelch is - says "Off"; I'm want to leave it Enabled. Crew report, I'll get in a minute and wind your watch.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Houston, America. If you happen to have a summary report of EVA-3, I'd sure like to hear it.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. We'll do that. Let me give you a - a quick rundown on review of what we're going to do this morning. We've got the extra RCS trim burn that's going to be coming in, and I've got a PAD for that guy. And I have about 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 one-liners to go into your Flight Plan to - to bring it up to date. The general plan is to do a minus-X RCS on the trim maneuver, in order to avoid impinging on the SIM bay. That burn will be about 30 seconds worth. And that's going to give you about 9 foot per second Delta-V. The maneuvers have all been checked out, and it's a reasonable time line. A

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Ah ha! Okay. That sounds like good.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: So, when you're ready to copy some of those things, that's - Might be a good thing to get started on. Go ahead and finish squaring away your cockpit. And, while they're putting together an official summary, I can tell you my unofficial summary of EVA-3 is that that sure is super. You've got to watch those tapes when you get down. That's really a - that's really a spectacular place, as you can probably see. And they found a lot of mighty...

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Oh, that's really [garble].

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: [Laughter.] I can - yep, I'll bet. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: What you ought to do is, when he gets aboard, you ought to tell him that you saw a bunch of vertical dikelets over on the north side of the massif. Tell him they were very dark, very small.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Vertical dikelets?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Yeah, I think that's a word he coined on the way down there.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Dikelets? Oh, okay [laughter].

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Hey, I got a Update Book here. I guess it'll be good for a trim burn - trim [garble].

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. In general, let me tell you also that your RCS is 4.7 above the Flight Plan. And, just as a summary, unless you want to plot them, I'ii just tell you that the oxygen and the hydrogen are doing good things. And you've got plenty of it. And I'm ready to give you a - The first PAD will be a trim RCS burn and the second one will be the plane change burn. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. No, that's good on the hydrogen and oxygen. And, I'm ready to copy the trim P30 PAD.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. I'll give you the trim. RCS/G&N; 37416; GET 181:34:01.22; plus 0009.2, all zips, and all zips; roll 180, 179, 316; 0067.3, plus 0062.4; 0009.2, 0:30, 0009.2; 13, 292.3, 29.9. And at Sirius and Rigel, 118, 159, 349. This will be four jets, minus-X on the RCS. And, I'd like to just add a comment here about the attitude. This attitude is one that's computed after you've gone to the plane-change REFSMMAT. And when you call P41, you'll be getting a different set of attitudes computed out of it because of the P41 computing a plus-X burn. But, when you're in attitude and P41's called, and you g

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. The first one is at 180 hours and 20 minutes. [Pause.] And...

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Yey. You wanna do that because we're going to the pictures anyhow.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Oh, okay. This really is a posigrade burn is what you're saying. And I really won't be able to trim it?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: I'm not sure I understood your comment there.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Well, in other words, we're not - we're not changing Noun 81. You know, like we do on the - the Sep maneuver.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Oh. That's - that's correct. You're - you're gonna - you're gonna see the numbers go to zero during the burn.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Real good. We just won't - [Verb] 50 [Noun] 18 won't be the right attitude. We'll use the Verb 29 maneuver and use that attitude.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: That's correct. And then when you get there, that should put it all in - in the X-axis.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Mighty fine.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Now I'm ready for the readback.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Ah, let me read it back. Okay, it'll be G&N/RCS for the Trim burn. Weight is 37416; T IG is 181:34:01.22. I'm not sure on the seconds, is that correct.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: That's correct.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Noun 81 plus 9.2 in X, 0, 0, roll, 180; pitch, 179, yaw, 316; H A will be 67.3; Perigee, 62.4; Delta-V total is - be 9.2; burn time is 30 seconds; Delta-V C is 9.2.
