a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. And that pitch align is 159. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Pitch align, 159.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. The next one will be the plane change, and I'll have that ready in just a second. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. I'm in the Flight Plan with that one.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Stand by just a second. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. LOPC SPS/G&N; [pause] 37416; plus 0.38, plus 0.92; 182:33:53.00; minus 0017.9, minus 0365.5, minus 0006.9; roll, 0; pitch, 0; yaw, 315; 0062.7, plus 0062.6; 0366.0, 0:20, 0353.8; 22, 148.9, 19.5; Sirius and Rigel and the roll, pitch, and yaw aligns are the same: 118, 159, 349. This will be four jets and 12 seconds. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. LOPC, SPS/G&N, 37416; plus 0.38, plus 0.92; T IG 182:33:53.00; Noun 81 is minus 17.9, a minus 365.5, and a minus 6.9; roll, 0; pitch, 0; yaw, 315; H A , 62.7, perigee, 62.6 - That's pretty circular - Delta-V total is 366.0, burn time is 20 seconds, Delta-V C , 353.8; sextant star 22, shaft 148.9 and 19.5; Sirius and Rigel, 118, 159, 349; four jets, 12 seconds.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. It's a good readback. And I've got a couple of Flight Plan things to give you when you're ready for that. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. I'm with you.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, I've got it.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. We owe you an attitude there and the attitude will be 179, 222, 359. The High Gain: pitch, minus 39; yaw, 145. Why don't you read them back individually as we go along?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Roll, 179; pitch, 222; yaw, 359. High Gain will be minus 39 and 145.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. And that's the - that's at 180:20. That's with the Verb 49 there. The next one is at...

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Ah, yes. That's right.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, at 181:35, we'll have a Verb 49 to gimbal lock avoidance; roll 081, 181, and 317. High Gain will be a pitch of minus 19, and yaw, 227; Auto and Narrow for AOS.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Now at 181:43, you can just skip that High Gain call out. At 181:45, we want to add a Verb 49 maneuver to the LOPC burn attitude. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. At 181:45, Verb 49 to LOPC burn attitude.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Now on the next page, we go over to 182:15. And, I want to add a PU Valve to Decrease. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: 182:15. [Pause.] PU Valve to Decrease.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: All right, sir. And I have two more to give you, but before we do that, how about let's terminate the jet monitor by calling P30 - P20, and a Verb 21 Noun 26 to all zips, and then we can uplink while we're finishing. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. You have Accept. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. And you got the monitor terminated?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Yes. It's terminated. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: I guess it went to P30 faster than it showed up down there or went into P30 not through it. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, why don't you put the Pan Camera to Standby and the Power, On, while we're about it and we can let them look at that stuff while we're getting the rest of our Flight Plan updates? [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Pan Camera's Standby, Power is On.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, thank you.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: All right. Let's go back to our updates and the next one should come at 182:44. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. At 182:44, I want to delete the "Mapping Camera, Extend." [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Delete the "Mapping Camera, Extend." Wait a minute. I scratched out the opening the cover. We got to do that.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Yeah. Okay.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Then the next thing we want to do is at 182:48, just a half inch down. I have a new attitude for you. Where it says 097, 068, 019, it's now going to be 096, 097, and 352; and the orb-Rate attitude is still all zeros. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. The attitude after the P20 option 5 plus-X forward will be 096, 097 and 352 and orb Rate is 0.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, that last angle was 352. I'm not sure we got that right.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. 352 for Yaw. That's correct.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: All right, sir. And while we're about it, why don't you take the Pan Camera Power back Off? [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Pan cam - pan ca - Pan Camera Power is Off! [Laughter].

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, and as long as we're talking about Pan Cameras, let's go to 183:45. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, and after the Pan Camera block, want to add "V Over H Override to High Altitude." [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. After "Pan Camera, Standby, Stereo, and Power," put "V Over H to High Altitude."

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: That's affirmative. And the last update is on the next page - 184:27. And it says "Mapping Camera, Retract" and since we didn't extend it you don't have to retract it.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Sounds logical. Okay, Mapping Camera, delete the "Mapping Camera, Retract."

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: All right, sir. And let's see what else we have here - how about running your paw over most of your biomed sensors? It looks like you've got some noise on there. And avoid changing them. Why don't you just kind of rub on each one and see if we can get it to come in a good signal? [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. I'll do that. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. You're making progress there.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Hey, it's working, huh? [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Hey, there's old Hadley Rille out there. That's a pretty deep little trough. Hey, you really didn't get a perspective of that thing, at least I didn't from some of the pictures. Not until you had a chance to get up here and take a look at some of the other things. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, I'll - I'll tell you when we get through...

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, that's the last of the Flight Plan things, huh?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Yes, sir; that was the last of the Flight Plans, and I still need a morning report from you and things like that; and I'll keep an eye on the clock down here and try to help you stay on the time line. The one thing that I see that may have to change is - I gave you a Delta-V C for the RCS burn that wasn't very useful, and we have to set it up to count in the other direction. There's a couple of things you do - like set it to 100.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: [Laughter.] Yes. Yeah, okay.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: It's just a backup monitor anyhow and so it's - setting it to 100 is probably the safest thing to do.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Yeah, that's right. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. Let me see if I've got time to put some hot water in my eggs.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, Ron, the computer is yours when - whenever you want to go to Block. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Sleep last night was probably about 6 hours - kind of intermittent - but it seemed to me like when I was sleeping I was sleeping pretty good. For some reason, I woke up a couple or 3 hours after I went to sleep and I got to sleep about an hour late. Oh, and I was just itching like a son of a gun.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: What's that? The sensors?

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: The only thing I can think of is that - No, my arms, you know, my forearms.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Oh, I see.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: From the wrist back to the elbow.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: The only thing I can think of is maybe the old Beta cloth itch, you know. Then I looked around and there was nothing there. You know, no hives or anything like that. So I got out some of that [garble] cream and put that on and it stopped it. Went back to sleep.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay. And it's coming up on time to start our - our first Verb 49 maneuver which can be running and I'll watch the angles while you put a little hot water in your food there if you want to. [Long pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, we've got to target load, I guess, in desired orientation. [Garble] okay, [garble]. [Pause.] Verb 49 Enter, Verb 25, Plus 179.00 Enter, plus pitch 22 - 222.00 Enter, yaw 359, plus 359.00 Enter. Okay, we're still saying 0.2 of a degree per second; Proceed to [garble] keys - Proceed.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: Okay, and the High Gain to Auto, please. [Pause.]

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: High Gain's in Auto and we'll set that at minus 39, yaw 145, just in case it breaks lock.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1795502csm.text: Hey, Ken, I'm going to be off my headset here while I change back to my comm carrier.

a17_1795502csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1795502csm.text: All right, sir.

a17_1802516csm.text: I got bacon bits. Those are easy to fix. [Long pause.]

a17_1802516csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802516csm.text: I had three jugs of water.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. We're going Att 1/Rate 2. Yes. [Pause.] Oh. Star number 11 - Aldebaran.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: You lucked out.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Yeah. That's a good one. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: It's a little ways off. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. Proceed, it was Aldebaran. [Garble] Dnoces. To Dnoces. [Long pause.] 6. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.text: Dnoces is hard to recognize through the telescope. Must be it. [Pause.] Yep, that was it. [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: How about that? [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. Need for some torquing angles. Plus 173 [pause] 5.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, got those.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, we'll torque at 30:10.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: 52 - 52 Enter. We want to do an Option 1 to the LOPC orientation. Okay? Let's see, 622, 180 - that's a pretty neat - isn't that where I'm supposed - and 8179316. Outstanding! Okay, it's dark out there, and I think I could find a star if I had to.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, I copied the angles for you if you need them.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: [Garble.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. It scares me everytime that light comes on. Ah ha! It went away. [Garble]. [Pause.] What the coarse align error is. [Long pause.] [Garble.] [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.text: Just barely in the sextant field of view.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: I don't know. That wasn't a very good mark. [Long pause.] Let's try that again. [Long pause.] Okay, let's try Dnoces again. Pretty logical since we're in this attitude. But we didn't gauge our...

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. And the angles I copied last time were 217 on the shaft and 33 on the trunnion. [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: [Garbled under Mattingly.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: That's close. [Pause.] Just in the sextant again. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Looks like 217 and 33's going to be it once you get it in there. [Long pause.] I'll settle for that. There's the old coarse align error. I'll let you copy those down there. I don't want them up here.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: And you can torque any time.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: And let's see - Okay; we'll torque at 34:30.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, that's a good number. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Ah ha! Knows exactly where it is. Okay.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Isn't that amazing?

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: And it shows we even know how to calculate the burn attitude.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Yeah. That's good. [Garble.] [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. We're CMC, Rate 2. [Pause.] Here. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, Count. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: And, Ron, I just noticed that in all our scribbling, I missed the line that said "Configure for the dump" on the previous column about 23. I don't know if you saw it in there or not. [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: I missed it. [Pause.] I'll sure get it. [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: And when it's convenient for you, I've got...

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: ...couple of hydrogen tank fans to change and the - the good docs would like to hear how you're eating and pushing pills.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: [Laughter] Okay. Took a Seconal last night, and I'm by the H 2 fans.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay. And that's Hydrogen tank 3: Fans, Off, and Hydrogen tank 1: Fans, On.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, number 3 went from Auto to Off, tank 1 is going from Off to On.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Very good. [Pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Okay, let's see, I got that done - at 40. Next thing we got coming up, huh? Okay, I'll go down there and get some of this stuff configured. Oh, I ate just about everything yesterday, and then some other things on there, and a bunch of extra stuff too, so when I get a chance, I'll call that down. Okay?

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1802720csm.text: Sounds fine.

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: Getting ready for this urine dump. [Long pause.]

a17_1802720csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1802720csm.text: [Garble.]

a17_1804627csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1804627csm.text: And, Ron, we're coming up on dump time and don't forget, we want to close the covers, and that kind of good stuff before we start the dump.

a17_1804627csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804627csm.text: Okay. UV cover is clo [pause] - Let's see - UV is Off. IR is Off. [Pause.] That's. [Long pause.]

a17_1804627csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804627csm.text: That's. Yeah, I start on old fuel cell purge here. Do this O 2 fuel cell purge. [Pause.] Okay. [Long pause.] Now let's see, the waste...

a17_1804627csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804627csm.text: Mark it. The old waste water dump is on.

a17_1804627csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804627csm.text: Drain Valve is Dump; Battery Vent is Closed.

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1804951csm.text: Okay, Ron, the EECOMs have calculated about 12 minutes to go on your dump, and it wouldn't hurt to set your kitchen clock or whatever you do to help remind yourself because that'll be after LOS. And we've taken a look at all of the systems and everything looks pretty good there and Retro would like to remind you that the weight has changed on your trim PAD and that has some implications to the way that it computes the burn arcs if you want to be superprecise. And looks like everything is Go for a trim.

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804951csm.text: Okay; sounds good: I'll set my little ding-ding here for about 10 minutes.

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1804951csm.text: Why don't you try about 9? Charlie swears it's no more than that.

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804951csm.text: Ah, okay. [Pause.] I believe Charlie. [Long pause.]

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1804951csm.text: Want me to configure the DSE, or are you going to set it up for me?

a17_1804951csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1804951csm.text: Why don't you do that one?

a17_1805432csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1805432csm.text: And, Ron, we've got about a minute and a half to LOS and I never did give you a summary of the EVA. Just a few quick particulars were that they got 7 plus 15 out of EVA-3. Got almost everything done. They had to delete station 10 in order to make up time, but that's made up for by the fact that they found some more interesting things at other stops. And there was - I mentioned the dikelets, and there's some indication that they may have seen a dike or something of that nature over on the North Massif. And Jack went out and applied all his - his physical skills to the lunar surface gravimeter a

a17_1805432csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1805432csm.text: This is Apollo Control. We've had Loss of Signal from the spacecraft America, going behind the Moon, nearing the end of revolution number 47. Now a Ground Elapsed Time of 180 hours, 56 minutes. 2 hours, 48 minutes remaining until Cernan and Schmitt aboard the Lunar Module Challenger are awakened at Taurus-Littrow. And approximately 48 minutes until America comes around again, coming up on two maneuvers. Spacecraft communicator Ken Mattingly read up the PADs or the data needed by the Command Module Pilot for performing these maneuvers. The first is a trim maneuver to tune up the Command Module

a17_1813955csm.text: This is Apollo Control at 181 hours, 39 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Some 37 seconds now until the spacecraft America comes from behind the Moon on revolution 48. One of the first items of business on this pass will be a report by the Command Module Pilot Ron Evans on the trim maneuver which he will have completed just prior to acquisition on this rev. 2 hours and 4 minutes remaining of the Challenger crew sleep period. Waiting now for word from Network that the...
We've had acquisition now. We'll stand by for the initial calls.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yes, sir. We certainly do and they worked real hard to get the - these experiments and the equipment all squared away. I was following along with them pretty well and I had lot of confidence.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Ah ha! Looks like we're getting you already. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Hello there. How's it going?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Just now calling the Verb 82. It's 67.4 by 62.8 [nautical miles, 124.8 by 116.3 km]. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Let me give you a little burn report here...

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: All right.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: ...[garble] reading on the burns, so you can get that off the recorder.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Ah, let's see. Okay. With 30 seconds of burn time, by my stopwatch there, I ended up with a plus - no, let's see - with a minus - minus 0.5 X. I think 0 in Y and a plus 0.5 in Z. Okay_ so I tweaked out the plus X and rolled right 90 degrees and burned a 0.6 in a plus-Y. Okay. With final trim of - on the Noun 85s of 0 plus 0.1 and a minus 0.1. Delta-V C was a minus 110.4 but we had that about a minus, a plus 110.4. But there's no bias check at a plus 0.9 - on the bias.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, the Noun 20 values - Noun 20 values - after the 90-degree roll there and for the final trim were 270, 179, 317.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Sounds like you're way ahead of the game.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah. Worked real fine.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Have you had a chance to get anything to eat yet? [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah, I ate some scrambled eggs and I'm nibbling on the bacon bars: and I had a - some orange juice.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, I wasn't trying to fish for a report. I was just trying to find out it you were still eating or how things were going.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: [Laughter.] I'm a little - I'm still eating a little bit. But we're in good shape.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. You get a - you get a medal for not overdumping the waste water tank. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah. It's amazing.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: The old 9-minute mark was right on. I set it at 8 minutes, just to be sure, and 1 minute later it was 10 percent. Tell Charlie he figured right there.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, we won't be able to talk to Dumis again.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: [Laughter.] That's right. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. And I don't remember if I explained...

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: I didn't bother with the sextant star check.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah. Okay. And I don't know if you've got an explanation on why your angles changed for the P20 business after the burn, but, this - this plane change burn is going to have a little orbit shaping in it as well as the previous one. So that it - it is going to have some components that are both radial and tangential. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Ah ha. Okay.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: So that meant that your REFSMMAT wasn't quite the REFSMMAT that you were anticipating earlier. And that explains the - why those angles had to change on you and also explains some of those odd-ball components.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Okay. I was wondering about that but - I'll tell you, those guys in the Trench down there know so much more about what's going on when they calculate that stuff than I do that I'll - I'll - I'll believe them. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Hey, Ron, are you - are you in a place where you can spare a minute or two? Is it convenient?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Sure.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Got somebody that would like to talk to you for just a minute.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Oh, yeah?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: NASA
a17_1813955csm.text: Ron, this is Jim Fletcher. How are you?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yes, Dr. Fletcher. Mighty fine, sir.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: NASA
a17_1813955csm.text: We had hoped to catch you last night but you were behind the Moon when the ceremony was going on. Did you catch any of it at all?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, I - I got the briefing, or the report from it from the CapCom, but it sounds like it was a mighty fine ceremony and something that this nation can really be proud of.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: NASA
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, Ron, there's one thing that the President wanted to make sure that you got. And I had hoped to do it last night. We've been in very close touch with the White House and the President has been following closely what - what's going on up there and, of course, it's absolutely fascinating to us down here. But he wanted to be sure that you understood that he'd like to wish you Godspeed as you return to Earth. And I must say I'd like to add that and also add that, from everything I heard, this is a spectacular success. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, thank you very much, there, Dr. Fletcher, and please convey my thanks to Mr. President. I appreciate that very much, and I - I also appreciate the opportunity to be able to do something for my country and I - hopefully, this is the one thing that I will be able to do. And I certainly appreciate it. Just the thoughts, themselves, really.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: NASA
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, very good, Ron. I'd just like to say that I've never - I've never had any idea whatsoever that things would go so well in the scientific part of the - of the orbital science. It's - it's almost unbelievable when I talk to the guys in the backroom, and I just wanted to make sure that you knew that I knew it.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: NASA
a17_1813955csm.text: Well, very good. Thanks kindly.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yes, sir. Dr. Fletcher; appreciate it.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: And, Ron, how about the High Gain? [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. Let me reset it here I guess. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1813955csm.text: 181:50:14 - That was NASA Administrator Dr. James C. Fletcher.
That was NASA Administrator Dr. James C. Fletcher.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. I'm in Reacq and Narrow now.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1813955csm.text: 181:50:40 - He was passing along a similar message to the one that he spoke to the crew in Challenger on yesterday while Evans was apparently behind the Moon, or at least out of contact on that particular circuit.

He was passing along a similar message to the one that he spoke to the crew in Challenger on yesterday while Evans was apparently behind the Moon, or at least out of contact on that particular circuit.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: And how about Auto on the High Gain when you get a chance?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, I'm right there, so we've got her.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, and let's see we've got a few minutes. I had - I had two more magazine changes to go in the Flight Plan if it's convenient to give them to you now.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Ah, let me get started on the other Verb 49 here, okay?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, just fine.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Lights. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: 315. Plus Enter - plus [pause] and one more Proceed. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, we're on our way. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, Ron, just for your information, about 291 looks like the maximum yaw you ought to see on this. And we'll keep an eye on it for you.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: 203. [Pause.] [Garble] [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, why don't we take some of those Flight Plan changes here? [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay. And these are real simple ones on page 283. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: 283. You're really looking ahead. [Pause.] Okay.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, at 187:45, you've got a magazine Bravo Bravo called out and we'd like to make that Delta Delta. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Delta Delta it is.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, and a couple of lines below that you have a magazine November November, we want to change to Kilo Kilo.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Kilo it is.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, that was kind of painless, wasn't it?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah, that was.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: And that's all I've got. We want to remember to get the PU Valve to Decrease. [Pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Yeah, I could do that now, I guess, couldn't I?

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay.

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Okay, we're setting on the minus 200-Decrease. [Long pause.]

a17_1813955csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1813955csm.text: Got a time here and let me bring you up to date on the [pause] lookout.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay. Ready to go on the food?

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Yes, sir.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Looks like we're going to miss it.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay. Day 8: sausage, grits, fruit cocktail, orange beverage, coffee, and tea, and a vitamin. [Pause.] Next box: ham - couldn't find my cheese 'til last night so I didn't have it, one rye bread, can of peaches or sack of peaches, cereal bar, orange drink, coffee, graham cracker cubes, apricot cubes, jelly candy, sugar cookies. Supper - had hamburger and catsup, [pause] vanilla pudding, grape drink; [pause] I guess that was it. [Pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: All right, sir. [Pause.] We've got about 34 minutes or so until the burn. I've got a news summary I can read if you'd like to have that or if you'd like to put it off 'til later I can do that too.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: ...we're off in roll by a degree from where he calculated it. [Pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Ah, got the wrong pitch. Acts just like the simulator, you can't tell, I thought when you got in the spacecraft that if you're 180 [garble] it's supposed to flop back and forth, but it doesn't do it. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: No, why don't you go ahead?

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: I'll just read it and if I start to bother you, why just holler at me and I'll stop.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: This is put together by a - a Mr. Jim Korkowsky and it looks like he's done a pretty nice job of summarizing the news, so I'm going to read it cold. And he's given us a summary of the late news. And the weather couldn't be worse in Houston. It had to be better on the Moon or in orbit around it. This morning more cold and drizzle blanketed the Houston metropolitan area. Yesterday morning it was 32 degrees. This morning a little warmer but a lot wetter, and it's getting colder on Friday. On the national-international scene: Peace talks in Paris between Dr. Henry Kissinger and Le Duc Tho have end

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: On the regional and local scene: the Houston City council has vetoed a plan to build a new commuter airstrip in southwest Houston for the STOL aircraft. Residents of the area have been protesting. The community of Tomball, north of Houston, is looking for a new police force. The police chief and seven officers walked off the Job Tuesday, after the City Council refused the officers a pay raise. In Harris County, the State Highway Patrol snd reserve police have been called in to maintain police protection. That's maintain protection in Tomball. The project to expend the - expand the Armand Bayou

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: That's a good summary; appreciate it. Little bit of everything in there.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Yeah, it looks like Mr. Korkowsky reads a lot of newspapers there.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: [Laughter.] He sure did. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay, Ron. We're picking up some thermal problems on the Pan Camera. Would you manually roll left to 30 degrees and we'll hold it until we've passed - you know the terminator - or cross the terminator.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: And, Ron: that terminator crossing comes fairly close to the burn, so you might think about, if it looks agreeable to you, just go ahead and we'll use that as the burn attitude. You'll have to get a new P40 trim to take care of the gimbal offsets. So you may see a slight Pitch and Yaw attitude change.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay; that's no problem. I'll just roll left and then use a P41 trim. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: [Cough] [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: I hit Accel Command to make that 90-degree roll there, the other day, or just a while ago. And, if you hit the stick a little too hard, you really ramp it up to a little better than a - a degree a second. You can really get a sensation of roll, especially when you can see the Moon. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: How's that? Pretty good attitude?

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Looks like we're going to have to go a little further to give us 5 or 10 more?

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay, I didn't let go of the stick, just - okay.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Ah, you're learning our tricks, aren't you?

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: [Laughter.] [Pause.] Used a teacup of gas there.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay, now - now, you're in good shape.

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1815814csm.text: Okay, we'll stop it right there, then. About 35 degrees or so. [Long pause.]

a17_1815814csm.speaker: Unknown speaker
a17_1815814csm.text: Anything to make you happy.

a17_1821022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1821022csm.text: Okay. I just made a Delta-V check a while ago and it was minus 22.2. Bias check was a mi - let's see, went from 100 to 100.9 in a minute and 40.

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay.

[Long pause.] 353.8 for the Delta-V C . [Pause.] Okay; SIM bay I checked it a while ago, BMAGs are Rate 2, Auto RCS Selects are okay. [Long pause.] Okay. [Garble] 7416, that's pretty good. Okay, plus 0.38 and a plus 0.92. That's all right. [Pause.] Okay, Verb... [Pause.] Load my own, I guess, it looks like, don't I?

a17_1821022csm.text: Yes, sir. When I gave you the uplink, they had to put in the - the trim burn.

a17_1821022csm.text: Yeah, that's right. Plus 182 Enter. Plus [pause] 182:33:53 ...

a17_1821022csm.text: Looks good.

a17_1821022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1821022csm.text: ...[Garble]. It's all right. 25, Enter. Okay; Noun 81s, 15.9, minus 17. Okay; Y is a minus 365.5. Z - 9 - minus 9 Enter. Okay; 17.9, 365.5, minus 6.9, Proceed.

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay, we can give you another one here if you'd like that.

a17_1821022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1821022csm.text: I don't see any reason - Oh really, I'll do it just for the heck of it.

a17_1821022csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1821022csm.text: Okay, ah...

a17_1821022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1821022csm.text: Got time here - let's see, 19 minutes...

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay...

a17_1821022csm.text: [Garble] down here and I'll just let you read them to me as I get [garble]...

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay. Plus - What did you say it was?

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay.

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay, [pause] we scratched out the part, so we're going to turn the tape recorder on, right?

a17_1821022csm.text: Okay.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Hey, refresh my memory on the mission rules there, Ken, could you? If it doesn't start on bank A, do we start on bank B? [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: Stand by. We're - we're making sure we'll tell you the right thing, here.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay, Ron. The rule says, "If no start on A, try B."

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. That's what I thought. [Pause.] [Humming] [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Plenty of battery juice here. Let's go to A, On - and B, is On and coming up. Okay, fuel cell 3, pressure is all right in 2-A; and 2-B is okay. And Helium Valves are in Auto, we're in Decrease; and the Oxidizer Flow Valve PUGS Mode is Primary. Primary, Decrease, and Normal. Okay. That's a lot of work. I'd like to get strapped in a little bit here. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. Bus tie - I forgot the crazy tape recorder. [Pause.] Command Reset - here we go. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. Helium valves, I did that. Servo Power 1. Okay - number 2, back to AC.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Mark. Directs are Off. BMAGs are uncaged. Okay, no hardovers. Go to SCS. Hand Controller number 2 is Armed. Okay. pitch 1, got it; yaw 1, ah, we got it. Okay. Trim is about set there; okay. Yaw's 0.9; pitch is about [pause] kazink, kazink, kazink, kazink. Okay; we have the trim. Okay. Give it back to the computer. Returns to zero. THC clockwise; no MTVC. Okay; pitch 2; got it; yaw 2, got it. Ah ha! We have the trim plus point - about - and plus, plus, minus. Okay; give it back to the computer. No MTVC.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; 3 minutes to go. THC. Okay. On the AC. Directs are On. Cage the old BMAGs. Key Release. Proceed for the final trim. Got a 618. D-18 says we're there. Okay; we'll Enter that. 204. Do you want a gimbal test option? Yes. Plus 2, minus 2, 0, plus 2, minus 2, 0. 3004. Okay; we have the trim with 3 minutes to go. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; Limit Cycle's back Off. [Garble] burn, we'll go Rate to High [Cough]. [Pause.] DET looks good; we've got a 20-second burn. Shutdown on 21 seconds. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. Delta-V in Standby. Have CMC, GDC, Rate Command; Limit Cycle, Off; Deadband, Min; Rate to High; Trans Control Power's Off. Directs are both Off; CMC, Auto. Okay. There we go; missed one. Att 1/Rate 2 on the old BMAGs. Rate Command; all four Gimbal Motors are On. We're CSM on the CG. [Garble] Logic, [garble] Roll, Roll; Alpha; S-IVB. pitch is Auto; DET is working; Armed, Armed.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; at 16, Auto RCS Selects, On; circuit breakers are still good [humming]. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. I'm waiting for 30 seconds [garble] the Normal Trans Control Power and the Delta-V Thrust A switch. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: EMS G; EMS to Normal; Trans Control Power is On; and Delta-V Thrust A is On. Okay; four jets, 12 seconds. [Humming] [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; we have ullage. Okay; 699, Proceed.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: 3 - oh - okay! Woohoo! There we go! We got ignition about 87. Okay; number 2 is coming On; we're up to 90 on the Delta-V C . Wait a minute! Okay; 913. Looking good. Okay; Roll Error is Off. That's all right; we're done. 3, 1...

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Shutdown - automatic! Okay; minus 9.5 on the EMS. Okay; 366.8. Let's Proceed to stop the Rates here. 6.8. Okay; man, look at those [Noun] 85s! I'm a little bit off, but that's good.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; pitch 2; got it; yaw 2; got it; and number 1, got it; number 1, got it. Okay; Servo Thrust is Off. Well, let's see. Forgotten what it feels like. Ha: That's pretty neat. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; that was okay. Somehow we got a 0.3 in there. That's in X anyhow. Y is zero; that's what I want. Z is all right, so we'll just leave it that way. I'll Proceed with the changes again. That just changed. Okay; 00 Enter. [Pause.] Okay; Verb 6 Noun 20 Enter. Okay; I presume you're reading the DSKY there, or haven't you been, Houston?

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: Yes, sir. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Three. [Pause.] The time as near as I could tell was pretty good. What, V GX - What did I say - 366.8, I think. Delta-V C is a minus 9.5; tail off is 11 or something. 12.2. [Pause.] Okay; let's get some more switches off. Trans Control Power - okay - Locked, Locked.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Trans Control Powers are Off; Directs are Offf; Direct Ullage circuit breakers are Open; Pitch 1, yaw 1 are Open. Okay. EMS Function is Off. Mode is Stand [pause] Rate 2. Okay. We'll come and get the bus ties. [Long pause.] [Humming] [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Hey, that was a neat burn [garble]. [Cough].

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: Feels more like an airplane, that way, doesn't it?

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Yeah. Yeah. It was kind of like an afterburner that time. Okay. A Bat Bus AC is Off; BC is Off. [Pause.] Not too bad. Okay; we're on Main A. Must be [pause] little oxidizer, yes. [Pause.] 0.6. Fuel is 28.4 [garble] and balance is minus - Now, let's see - about 460, I guess. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Thing going in the right direction?

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: We don't think the PUGS really ever stabilized.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Nah, I don't think it did, either. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay; AC Roll switches are Off, now. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: And, Ron, we're ready to give you some new stuff in the computer whenever you're - pass by and give us Accept.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. You have Accept. While you're doing that, I'll do the post-SPS SIM prep cue card.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: All righty. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: And I'd really forgotten how that thing kicks you in the seat of the pants. I guess I must have been floating off the seat a little bit more this time than I was on the - the rest of the burns. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. Pan Camera Power is Off; and the old Logic Power should go to Deploy/Retract. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay, down is A, down is B. Deploy/Retract. [Coughs] Got - to inhibit all jets. Okay, we'll inhibit the - I'll except the roll, right now.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: On - okay [garble]. [Pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: I'll just inhibit the Roll 1, Delta 1, and then I can start the - Yeah, here's the DAP now. You through with the computer?

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. We're through. It's your computer.

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: And [pause] [garble] two are On, Off now. [Pause.] Camera Laser Altimeter, Open. [Pause.] Barber pole in the gray. [Long pause, Cough] 20 Enter. [Pause.] 22 Enter, 5 Enter, plus-X SIM bay att. [Long pause.] 2.25 [pause] 2 Enter. We are going to use a 2½-degree deadband this time. [Long pause.] Fifty is around the Moon. Okay. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: 276 plus 2. That was... [laughter]. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: Different attitudes. [Long pause.]

a17_1822535csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1822535csm.text: I think I'll make a cup of coffee.

a17_1824741csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1824741csm.text: Ron, I've got your Pan Camera photo PADs when you're ready. [Pause.]

a17_1824741csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1824741csm.text: Okay. I just happen to be ready to copy.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Ken, I'm just now remembering one of your comments from 16 that we didn't get done on this extra comm carrier cloth - there's cloth here, you know.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Uh huh.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Don't need any extra electronics, but we sure could use another cloth hat [laughter].

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Oh, you can wash it off. You probably do that inadvertently.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: [Laughter.] I already have. I didn't wash it with the right thing though.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: [Laughter.] I - I was wondering if you would own up to that. Hey...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: [Laughter.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: ...the good Doctor over here says that your - your traces are flat lines. Thought you ought to be aware of that.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Oh, they are?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Do you feel okay?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Well, let me... They're kind of itching it - They're kind of itch - Yeah, I'm okay. But they're kind of itching anyhow. I feel like I ought to change them so...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Okay. That would really make him happy. [Pause.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: No wonder they're flat lines - It's unplugged.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Okay.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Said something sooner [laughter].

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: All righty. We're about 4 minutes from LOS and...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: I can turn that [garble] off.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: ...and all systems have been looked at, and they're all looking okay. So, guess we'll see you on tother [sic] side.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Okay. How's my stuff, now that I got plugged in?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: We don't see anything, yet.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Didn't, huh? [Long pause.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Well, I needed to change them anyhow so...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Okay.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: I'll try to...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Looks like you hit something there when you did that. [Long pause.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: I was just shaking my coffee. [Pause.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: I tell you, it sure put life in the signal.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: It did?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: How are those binoculars working out?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Hey, they're working real good. I find I have a bit of a problem holding them still, though.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Yeah, they're about the max magnification, I think, that you can hand hold. Have you tried looking...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Yeah.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Yeah. And they just don't quite look as - let enough light through, I don't think, in Earthshine. In other words, you can see better with the naked eye, but they don't - they don't let enough light through the binocs to enhance your image capability at all.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: Okay. I was curious because I noticed in the - in the dark shadows in the daylight side, that they did bring out things that you couldn't see with the naked eye. I guess that's contrast that does that.

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: Yeah, I noticed that too. Yeah, you can look down in the shadow of a - of a crater, where you got the Sun down there, but if you have more backlighting or something. You know, but you can - you can see that pretty good with the naked eye, anyhow. Earthshine, now, about all I can get out of the Earthshine, really, are differences in albedo. And you can get some - textural - Well, not so much textural differences, but terrain bumps and humps, and flow fronts, and - see craters, you know?

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mattingly
a17_1825014csm.text: I wish I was there with you. [Pause.]

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1825014csm.text: I tell you, I had no idea how interesting and how much fun it would be. [Pause.] After the first day, and I finally got over the - I guess you could - I don't know. You'd call it the effects of adapting to zero g or something. But you're just a little bit woozy. You really don't feel like doing a heck of a lot that first day up. So, it's good that the first day is kind of...

a17_1825014csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1825014csm.text: 182:56:08 - This is Apollo Control. The Command Module America passing behind the Moon on the end of the 48th lunar orbit. 48 minutes until the crew of Challenger is awakened at Taurus-Littrow. During the just-completed front side pass the Command Module Pilot Ron Evans completed the lunar orbit plain change maneuver which went nominally on time with velocity change of 366 feet per second [112 m/s] using the Service Propulsion System engine. Just prior to that, before he appeared on the front side of the Moon, a small trim maneuver was performed using the forward firing Reaction Control System

This is Apollo Control. The Command Module America passing behind the Moon on the end of the 48th lunar orbit. 48 minutes until the crew of Challenger is awakened at Taurus-Littrow. During the just-completed front side pass the Command Module Pilot Ron Evans completed the lunar orbit plain change maneuver which went nominally on time with velocity change of 366 feet per second [112 m/s] using the Service Propulsion System engine. Just prior to that, before he appeared on the front side of the Moon, a small trim maneuver was performed using the forward firing Reaction Control System thrusters.

A17A1832959.speaker: LM Crew
A17A1832959.text: (Sung with occasionally successful harmony) Good morning to you; Good morning to you; Good morning, Dear Gordy, Good morning to you. (Long Pause) [Schmitt - (Laughing) "You're being overly generous. I didn't hear any successful harmony."] [My Beautiful Australian Bride, Dianne Jones, a woman of good musical judgment, agrees with Jack. I am outvoted. There was no successful harmony.] [Cernan - "Can you imagine (the scene) down in the MOCR. They're quietly sitting there watching the systems and figuring out what their going to do next and off the open carrier comes this noise."] 183:xx:xx Fuller

a17_1833200.speaker: Evans
a17_1833200.text: Sure have a lot of different albedo textures on the thing. What makes it look like a - I sure want to see that low Sun, see if that's a topographic rise over Tsiolkovsky or not, and I - looks to me like there's just a - it's just an albedo. It has dark albedo streaks in there. Maybe they are shadows, but I don't think so. Can't see - interpret. You have flow from a so-called landslide. Looks like in a spot or two there, it's rocky. It doesn't come out and roll over. It just comes out and slopes down at maybe a 45-degree angle.

a17_1833200.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1833200.text: This is Apollo Control at 183 hours, 32 minutes. We're about 14 minutes away from the scheduled wakeup time for Apollo 17 - the Lunar Module crew. However they beat us to the punch this morning and we just got a rousing rendition of "Good Morning To You" sung by the crew of Gene Cernan and Jack Schmitt on the lunar surface. The Surgeon reports that the two crewmen appear to have gotten a good night's sleep - 6 to 7 hours, and we'll pick up with the taped replay of that Good Morning rendition from the crew and then follow it live.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1834022csm.text: is that - jets are enabled, that C-1 and C-2 for roll, Off. Pitch and yaw are off. [Pause.] And, Houston, ready for Pan Camera to Standby and Stereo to Power and all those good things whenever you are.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, Gordy. It's already in the jett bag, thank you. (Pause) [Cernan - "Obviously, I did not leave the LMP's camera on the Rover pointed at the zenith. But I swear I put something there. It's possible it could have been the 500 lens, because we didn't bring it back and I mentioned it was under the seat. I know that I did something with a camera. Now, it could have been a lens. And I stuck it between the seats, sort of wedged it in somewhere, and pointed the lens toward the zenith."] [Schmitt - "Houston wanted us to jettison the camera because they didn't want us to take pictures of Ron Evans'

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1834022csm.text: And, Gordy, you might make some notes that before I put it in there (in the ETB at about 174:31:44), I took a black-and-white window pan with mag Nancy (Apollo magazine 143).

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, Jack. Roger.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Gordo, on Reg A, you interpret that is just a small leak by the reg? That it would be usable, if you had to.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: That's affirmative, Geno. It's a small, slow leak and it is usable if needed. [That is, if Reg B doesn't work, they'll be able to use Reg A for repressurization following the final hatch opening.]

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, thank you. In summing up so far, I think that's all the system anomalies we got, isn't it?

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1834022csm.text: You may be interested. We just woke up the Challenger, or maybe they woke us up, I guess. They gave us a song here from - from there first, and they're all fine and they're in their Surface Checklist - getting ready for ascent.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: That's all I can think of at the moment. I do have revised times for the rest of the Lunar Surface Checklist which, at a convenient time, I can give to you, so that you'll have a how-goes-it as you go on down the line here.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Why don't you give them to us now, Gordy?

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, turn to page 7-9 . (Long Pause)

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Go ahead.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, (on page) 7-9, LGC/IMU Power-up, change that time from 183:04 to 184:10. The eat period time is now 184:20.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Turn the page (to 7-10 ), and the "183:59" above "Park Rendezvous Radar" is now 185:05.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Next page ( 7-11 ), "don suits" at 185:15. (Pause)

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Go to the next page ( 7-12 ). "Prep for equipment jettison" is 185:50; and, the same page, "helmet/glove donning" is 185:58.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Next page ( 7-13 ), "pressure integrity check", 186:04. "Cabin depress" is 186:08; and "hatch opening" is 186:12.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Next page, 7-14 , "cabin repress" is 186:15. "Cabin cleanup for launch" is 186:20.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1834022csm.text: Must not be because I don't know for sure what you mean (chuckle).

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: And on the following page ( 7-15 ), we're going to delete the P22 but we'd like you to do all the procedures except those from "Verb 95 Enter," through "P00 Enter," inclusive...(That is), the center section of procedures. So you'll still be closing the rendezvous radar breakers, going to LGC, and parking the antenna and copying PADs. Over.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, we're going to delete everything from Verb 95 through P00 on P22. That's the center of the page.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: That's affirmative and then the next page, "cabin prep for ascent" is 186:45, and instead of 39 minutes we're going to have you do that in 3 minutes. And you should have a little more time than that, since you got up early. That puts you right back with timeline, at lift-off minus 1 hour and 15, at 186:48. Over.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, top at 7-15 where we pick up what was going to be the beginning of the P22? Have you got a time up there?

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: I guess we'll just have to work that in with the cabin cleanup time. We had deleted that whole time block but you do have to catch those procedures.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1834022csm.text: Roger.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, and then the times on the top of 7-10 , for P22, are not applicable, and I guess you can give us an update for our P57 lift-off time.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: That's affirmative. We might...There's a couple more changes coming at me here but let me make sure I got them straight and I'll call you later. Go ahead with whatever you were doing.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1834022csm.text: (Coughs) Gordy, if I get ready for the "LGC/IMU power-up", I'll give you a call even though it comes earlier; but I'd like to get that started, as soon as we're ready to start it.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1834022csm.text: Yeah. You know, but it would have to be a relatively thin crust.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay. We concur with that. (Pause) 183:46:52 Schmitt: Hey, Gordy, as far as the food, medication, and sleep goes...(We took) no medication. Gene had 5 hours of good sleep, I had probably around my usual 6, in spite of my poetic inclinations. [Schmitt - "Our rest period was normally eight hours, and we were usually a little late getting started."] [Cernan - "We'd sit around and talk and Jack'd stick his finger in the rock bag."]

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1834022csm.text: And the food...We continue to do well, I believe. We've eaten a wet pack apiece last night. We got one this morning. We've eaten our scrambled eggs and sausage yesterday, and we've run out of juices and tea. And which is somewhat of an inconvenience I might say. And if you've got any specific questions, I can fill you in on it; but, I think, foodwise we've done pretty well. [Schmitt - "The wet packs were the original form of the Army's irradiated Meal-Ready-To-Eat."] [Cernan - "They were cold, not warm."] [Schmitt - "We had four kinds, as I recall: peanut butter, a hamburger, wieners..."] [Cer

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Can you give us a feel on the fluid intake?

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1834022csm.text: Well, that's what I was trying to do when I said we'd drunk all the juices and tea. Plus, Gene, in particular, takes water from the hose.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, Jack, fine. Sounds good. [Very Long Comm Break. They've already had breakfast, a bit out of sequence, and will now power-up the inertial platform and other elements of the navigation system. During this LM Comm Break, Houston has AOS with Evans, who is on his 49th orbit.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 16 min 21 sec )

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1834022csm.text: Okay, 30 seconds to T-start time.

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1834022csm.text: This is Apollo Control at 183 hours, 49 minutes. Gene Cernan and Jack Schmitt aboard Challenger on the lunar surface after having gotten up about 15 minutes early. Now having breakfast. They're a bit behind in the timeline but we expect to have them caught up by the time they are about 1½ hour prior to lunar lift-off, which is when we begin the really busy period of lift-off preparations, and everything appears to be going along very smoothly at this time. The crew's early arising caught us a little unprepared here in Mission Control. We had our own wake up tune to play up to them this

a17_1834022csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1834022csm.text: And after giving us a few minutes to catch our bearings, we hit them with the theme from 2001 A Space Odyssey. Since then things have been going along pretty much normally. The poetic offering was from Jack Schmitt. He said it was for all the kids back home. It was his version of the Night Before Christmas. We have reacquired Ron Evans aboard the Command Module America and everything is progressing very smoothly aboard that vehicle. We're on separate communication circuits at the present time and will be, up until the revolution prior to LM lift-off at which time we'll switch back to a single

a17_1834900.speaker: Evans
a17_1834900.text: Okay. This jett bag is so full of junk, I don't know if I can get it through the tnnnel.

a17_1834900.speaker: Evans
a17_1834900.text: Okay. Stow the old rope in the right-hand temporary - right hand, okay. That's fine. Did that. Decon bag straps from top of A-2 and hang on L-3. Okay, that's the way it's been for a long time. Remove two jett bags, vacuum bag, and the vacuum cable from A-2. Okay, the cables are already in the bag. Yeah. Empty jett bag, the vacuum bag, and the cable in left-hand temporary stowage - put them in last night. Ah, yes, that's in there. Okay, let's see. Stow the empty jett - Oh, I did that, okay. Replace remaining jett bag on A-2, and load with following. Okay, A-9 is empty, so I got that. Fecal bags

a17_1834900.speaker: Evans
a17_1834900.text: Extra ones. Okay, that's all four of them. There, forgot to take that one off.

a17_1835447csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1835447csm.text: Oops. Just about threw away my PRD [Chuckle.]. That, wouldn't we?

A17A1835732.speaker: Cernan
A17A1835732.text: Okay, Gordy, it's PGNS (Primary Guidance and Navigation System) power up time.

A17A1835732.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1835732.text: Okay, Geno. And I've got a couple more items to completely clean up the checklist whenever you can get to that.

A17A1835732.speaker: Cernan
A17A1835732.text: I'll let Jack give you a call. I'm going to start on the PGNS, if you're ready. (No answer; Long pause) Gordy, you ready for the PGNS?

A17A1835732.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1835732.text: That's affirmative, finally got you a Go to start it as per checklist. [They are about 54 minutes behind schedule and will catch up easily.]

A17A1835732.speaker: Cernan
A17A1835732.text: Okay there's the Pro; I did get the Restart. (Pause) I got the No Att, the DAP, Gimbal Lock light, and a Program Alarm light's on.

a17_1835931csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1835931csm.text: Okay. Get all of that old food down in there.

a17_1835931csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1835931csm.text: Mark it. The gimbal operate breaker is Closed.

a17_1835931csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1835931csm.text: That's the IMU Operate breaker. And I'll stand by for 90 seconds (until the corresponding lights go out).

a17_1835931csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1835931csm.text: And we're ready for a Power Amp, Primary; and High Bit Rate. (Pause)

a17_1835931csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1835931csm.text: Okay. You got it. [Long Comm Break]

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1840511csm.text: [Coughs]

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay, Gordy, P57 lift-off time 188:01:43.85.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: That's affirmative. And then we'd like you to delete all the steps below that lift-off time, from the A/T-3 data star info box through the Verb 32 after "for the remaining data stars" and after last star. In other words, just delete all between the box and up to circuit breaker AOT Lamp, Open. And, of course, there'll be no P22 time, over.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. Delete all the data star information between the start of that box and, "after last star, Verb 34 Enter, 00 Enter."

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: That's correct and then turn to page 7-15 . We're changing...Looking here a little closer, we find that radars are already in good position, so you can delete all procedures on page 7-15, except "Copy Ascent PADs, CSI PAD, and LM DAP weight." (Pause)

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1840511csm.text: Mark, T-st - T-stop.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1840511csm.text: Mark it. Stop. Okay? Hey, while I'm thinking about it, I started the - the Mapping Camera and Laser Altimeter about 3 minutes early there - on the back side.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Schmitt
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. We've deleted everything but the last three lines on that page.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. On page 7-12 , back up a couple pages. In the lower right corner there, in the blank space, you might jot down 185:58, VHF check with Command Module. And that'll be according to the procedures on 7-15 in the box. You might just parenthesis 7-15 to remind you where the procedure is. But the comm check will come during that time when you're prepping for equipment jettison, or right around there. (Pause)

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. We got that.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. That's all we got for you, and we have the E-MOD dump okay.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. [Comm Break]

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1840511csm.text: (Now on 7-10 ) Gordy, we're on P00 in Data and we're standing by for your up-link, and how long does that AOT Heater breaker have to be open? I pushed it in at 184:08.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. I'll get an answer for that, and I think we'll be coming with the up-link here shortly. (Long Pause)

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: Gene, no time constraint on that AOT breaker; except, if it (the telescope sight)'s foggy, it hasn't been in long enough.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Overmyer
a17_1840511csm.text: Roger.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1840511csm.text: (Laughing) Thank you, Gordy. (Long Pause)

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1840511csm.text: Challenger. Here comes your up-link.

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Cernan
a17_1840511csm.text: Okay. [Comm Break. They are getting state vector information from Houston.]

a17_1840511csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1840511csm.text: On. Starting - Yeah, [garble]. It's just the starting torque on this crazy motor, I guess. Well, it works. I'm glad I tried that out. I'd hate to have that thing while we're - Oh, I know what to expect now. Now, if this thing will fit down here between F-2 and the MDC like it's supposed...

a17_1841757csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1841757csm.text: [Clipped] our time here? Let's see, 17. We're just barely - barely making headway, here [clipped]. Okay to that. Close out curtain and stow in the right-hand temporary stowage bag. Okay. Good idea and then we can get in there and put them old rockboxes in those holes.

a17_1841757csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1841757csm.text: Oh, okay. Let's see. Do you have a zodiacal light photo PAD yet?

a17_1841757csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1841757csm.text: [Humming] Have a sugar-cookie cube for a little energy. [Clipped] R-12's [garble].

a17_1841757csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1841757csm.text: Off. Barber pole. [Clipped] ER's going Off. Transponder is going to Heater. Okay, Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover - Closed - Barber pole. Gray. Okay. Those all three are closed, in, Tank 3 Isolation Valves. Okay, we can go to P00 and turn on A-1 and 2. A-1 - down - up - down. Okay. A-2. We got coupled attitude.

a17_1841757csm.speaker: Mission Control
a17_1841757csm.text: This is Apollo Control with 184 hours, 32 minutes. Jack Schmitt and Gene Cernan aboard Challenger on the lunar surface at the present time, are going through the platform alignment, getting their guidance and navigation equipment ready for lunar lift-off. They will also shortly begin donning their pressure suits. And they appear to be running about 30 minutes behind the timeline. However, we expect they will have adequate opportunity to make up the lost time prior to a lunar lift-off. And, we're looking for lift-off to occur pretty much on time at 188 hours, 1 minute, 44 seconds Ground Elapsed

a17_1843038csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1843038csm.text: [Humming] How did that plane change - the tracking work out on that plane-change burn? Is that okay?

a17_1843713csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1843713csm.text: [Whistling] And, Bob, you give me a clue when getting ready to do that Verb 49?

a17_1844303csm.speaker: Evans
a17_1844303csm.text: Okay. Nikon, 55-millimeter [garble] 2, infinity. Mag Yankee Yankee - gives frame - let's see - [garble] lights and tape the old floodlights. Okay.

A17A1851721.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1851721.text: We're copying your ticker (that is, his heart beat) loud and clear. Also your voice.

A17A1851721.speaker: Cernan
A17A1851721.text: Gordy, Gene. I'm going off the air.

A17A1851721.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1851721.text: Okay, Geno. [Very Long Comm Break while they get Gene suited. Once they get done, they will report their PRD (Personal Radiation Dosimeter) readings. This activity is near the top of the right-hand column of Surface 7-12 and was scheduled for 184:59. They are now only about 32 minutes behind schedule.]

A17A1851721.speaker: Evans
A17A1851721.text: Okay. Start the old Auto Pitch rate. I guess we did that. Auto RCS Select. Jets back On. Let's see. Where are we now? [Garble] P20, option 5, landmark track. [Garble].

A17A1851721.speaker: Evans
A17A1851721.text: Zero Enter. [Garble]. Two Zeros Entered. [Garble] Entered. [Garble]. Couple more. Okay. Proceed to [garble].

A17A1851721.text: Noun 79 [garble] 0.5, okay. Verb - [garble] Enter. Proceed. Seven? That's pretty close. Okay. [Garble]. The old High Gain. [Garble].

A17A1851721.speaker: Evans
A17A1851721.text: That's a minus 2. [Garble] at 330. Reacq and Narrow for AOS. [Garble]. Okay. Landmark track. Guess we'd better do that. [Humming]

A17A1851721.speaker: Evans
A17A1851721.text: [Garble] is over there. No Go. [Garble] well on that.

A17A1851721.text: Plus Enter Zero all the [garble] be below the lunar surface.
