A17A1851721.text: Oh, the old check valve, and that buster's kind of tight. Lots of pressure. [Garble].

A17A1851721.speaker: Cernan
A17A1851721.text: Okay, Gordo. This is CDR. You ought to have me all back up on the comm and biomed now. (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay; it's 4.5. Stand by for the decay. (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Oh, man, I got to go get that Water Sep(arator) Select.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Pull the 2, huh? [They are on page 7-13 of the Surface Checklist. The instruction to switch to Water Separator 2 is a late addition.]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Oh, boy.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Want me to get it?

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: No. I got longer arms, I guess.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: I can reach back in there.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. If you can get back there.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: I think. (Pause) Now, they want it?

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Yeah, now. Pull the 2.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay. Pull the 2. Okay.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Happy with the suit circuit?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: And, yeah, we got a decay in the suit loop.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay; verify suit circuit lock's up. I'm dumping all the way.

A17A1860130.speaker: Overmyer
A17A1860130.text: Mark. T-2.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay. (Long Pause) (Suit) circuit's 4.2. (Long Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay, you're at 0.7 in the cabin and 4.1 in the suits. (Long Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: About 4.0, and the cabin is 0.3. (Long Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay; let me see if I can jar it (the hatch).

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay; I guess we're Go for EVA-4.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Five, isn't it?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Five this time? [EVA-4 was the PLSS jettison prior to the last rest period.]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Oh, man, I got it open. If I could bleed that pressure. Oh, boy! Let me hold it here for a minute. (Breathing heavily, but chuckling) There's a lot of psi on that hatch. (Pause) Okay; that'll hack it. Let me go to Auto here. [Cernan - "You get the pressure in the cabin low enough that you can get the hatch open; but there's still a tremendous force on it and I had to hold it open to get it all the way down."]

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Save our (surface) checklist (from blowing out the hatch). (Pause) Make it...Oops, that's closed.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: That's Auto, and the lock/lock is on. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Hatch is open all the way. Where are we?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Why is that still waving in the breeze? Don't understand that.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: There's a solar wind in here. We're on (page) 7-dash-something here. [They are still on Surface 7-13 .]

A17A1860130.speaker: Evans
A17A1860130.text: High Gain to Auto.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Not still venting, are we? Houston, how's our cabin configuration? Seem's to still be a little breeze going out the hatch.

A17A1860130.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1860130.text: All the numbers look good here, Jack. [Schmitt - "There were all kinds of nooks and crannies in the LM, now. Not just the ordinary nooks and crannies, but we had bags that had gotten pressurized and, so, everything was venting. It didn't happen instantaneously. I don't remember thinking about that at the time, but that's probably what it was. There were just lots of sources of oxygen."]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay, hold that (hatch), Jack.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay. (Pause) Partially open; that's good. (Garbled) "Forward hatch...jettison the jett bag !"

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. Ready?

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Here goes Santa Claus...

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Here you go, Santa Claus.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: ...Santa Claus' bag.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Another bag of goodies. (Pause) Give it the old... There you go.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: 3-point kick (a reference to a 'field goal' in American football).

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Nice. Beautifully done! [Cernan - "A lot of things we would just set down in front of the hatch and - pop - just kick them out. It was easy enough to do that. Kick them far enough to clear the porch."]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Just where we wanted it. All clear of the Ascent Stage. (Pause) Need the...

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay; clear. (Pause) Good boy! Now, for your next act. Watch it. (Pause) No.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: No. No. Never mind.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Don't even think about it. [We have no idea what is going on here. One possibility is that Gene has started to turn around, pretending that he is going to get out for an EVA or to get the clean gloves.]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: (Laughing) Okay. (Laughs)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: (Laughing) Okay?

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: (Reading) " Jettison bag . All items are clear of Ascent Stage." Ready to close hatch?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Looks like it.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Short EVA-5.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: (To Houston, joking) Are we Stay NoStay for hatch closure?

A17A1860130.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1860130.text: You have a Go for closing the hatch.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: (Laughing) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. The hatch is closed. Boy, is it easy to get around in here without a PLSS on. [They now turn to Surface 7-14 .]

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay; your Dump Valve verified in Auto?

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Yes, sir, and locked.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay. (Pause) Cabin Repress (valve) . Okay.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. Verify it's Auto?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: It's Auto.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay; on (circuit breaker panel) 16, Cabin Repress, Closed?

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay; Cabin Repress going Closed.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: And the hatch looked clear when I sealed it. Clear when I closed the hatch.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Okay. Closed.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: There's the Master Alarm. (Pause) And the cabin is coming up. (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Lots of O2.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: (Sound of repress begins) Okay; cabin is increasing, and you can go to Cabin on Pressure Reg B (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: It's in Cabin.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. Cabin warning light will go off here shortly. (Pause) And my suit's coming down.

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Mine, also. (Pause) Okay. We're just about to go through 50 percent, Descent O2 (remaining). (Pause) We're there. (Pause) Okay. Cabin's almost at regulating pressure.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: And Cabin light's still on. Next thing we'll do when it stabilizes, we'll doff our gloves, doff our helmets...

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Locked up.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. You can doff your gloves. (Pause)

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Let me watch that pressure a minute. (Pause) Well, it looks like it's stable at five. Okay. (Pause) How's the cabin look, Houston? Looks good here.

A17A1860130.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1860130.text: Okay; it looks good here. [Public Affairs reports a 60 second EVA from hatch open to hatch close. By the normal definition of 3.5 psi to 3.5 psi, this was a six-minute EVA.]

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Okay. (Lost under the PAO commentator).

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: I hope so. Physics says it should have been.

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: There's an experiment. (Pause) Not really, since we do that with our PLSS and everything else. (Pause) Okay. Take your helmet off. (Pause) Boy, that was painless enough. (Pause) Jack, I'd wrap that thing around it like (garbled).

A17A1860130.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1860130.text: Wait a minute. (Garbled) take our helmets (garbled).

A17A1860130.speaker: Cernan
A17A1860130.text: Not yet. We (garbled) obviously. Stow them on the engine cover. Okay. [Comm Break. After doffing the helmets and gloves, they will stow the LEVAs and EVA gloves and, in general, get things out of the way in preparation for launch.]

A17A1860130.speaker: Evans
A17A1860130.text: Yes, I think I got a - yes. I got a 405 alarm and I don't think it will take a mark. Wnen you have that 405 alarm. But, anyhow, I took two marks on it.

A17A1864700.text: Okay, Gordy, here's your readback. Direct rendezvous is 188:01:35.93; 55408, 00320, minus 0005, plus 37430 minus 72507, 58669, 56907, 00320, 05359; 188:55:5700; 10900; 629; 622. Remark: one rev late Tig is 190:00:18. Over.

A17A1864700.text: Okay, that was a good readback. Now I have a Co-elliptic Ascent PAD. Tig is 188:04:14.00; 55390, 00380, minus 0005; plus 37430; minus 72507; 58630; 56907; 00380. Rest of the PAD down to LM weight is NA. (NA = not applicable) Your LM weight is 10900, and the HA and HP are NA. Over. (Pause)

A17A1864700.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1864700.text: Okay, Gordy, co-elliptic readback: 188:04:14.00; 55390, 00380, minus 0005; plus 37430; minus 72507; 58630; 56907; 00380; rest of PAD is NA except for LM weight, 10900. Over. [Schmitt - "These were all contingency PADs and there was only a limited amount of information that could be stored in the computer."]

A17A1864700.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1864700.text: Okay, that's a good readback. Turn to page 10 (of the LM Data Book); I have the CSI PAD, co-elliptic.

A17A1864700.speaker: Cernan
A17A1864700.text: And, Gordy, I'm starting to pick up the breakers on panel 11.

A17A1864700.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1864700.text: Okay, Geno. (Pause) [The circuit breaker configuration is shown of Surface 8-2. Gene has probably verified the switches listed on 8-1.]

A17A1864700.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1864700.text: Okay. Tig is 189:01:53.81. Tig at TPI is 190:55:00.00. Noun 81 is 0539; and Delta-VY is a plus all balls (that is, all zeros). 373; 05419, 06550; plus 0539; plus all balls; and plus 0012.

A17A1864700.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1864700.text: Okay. CSI PAD: 189:01:53.81; 190:55 all zeros; plus 0539; plus all zeros; 05419; 06550; plus 0539; plus all zeros; plus 0012. Over.

A17A1864700.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1864700.text: Okay. That's a good readback. That's all I have for you.

A17A1864700.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1864700.text: Okay. [Comm Break. During this break, Houston has LOS with Evans on his 50th orbit. Gene finishes his circuit breaker check on Surface 8-2 and Jack does his on Surface 8-3.]

a17_1865343.speaker: Cernan
a17_1865343.text: Okay, Gordo, we're on the top of (page) 8-4.

a17_1865343.speaker: Fullerton
a17_1865343.text: Roger, Geno. [Comm Break. They have just finished a check of their circuit breaker configuration. And are about to perform a radar "self" test.]

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: And, Challenger, it's your computer now.

A17A1871623.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1871623.text: Thank you. [Long Comm Break. Next, they will recheck the platform alignment as per the procedures on 8-7 and 8-8.]

A17A1871623.speaker: Cernan
A17A1871623.text: Gordo, did you ever get any word on the Rover batteries?

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: No. I sure haven't. I haven't heard on that one.

A17A1871623.speaker: Cernan
A17A1871623.text: It's not important. I just wondered whether those things were going to be working back there (to give TV of lift-off).

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: Okay. We've got no reason to believe they won't. When you get down to parking the rendezvous radar antenna after this P57 (platform alignment program), give me a call. We're going to change the parking position.

A17A1871623.speaker: Cernan
A17A1871623.text: Okay. (Pause) Why don't you just give me the numbers now?

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: Okay. Do as the checklist shows (bottom left on 8-8), except do a Verb 41 Noun 72 to 0 and 30 degrees. Go to Slew, and then delete the "manual slew for 3 seconds." They want to leave it there for temperature purposes. This will be a cooler position for it during ascent.

A17A1871623.speaker: Cernan
A17A1871623.text: And the first 01...(correcting himself) first (Noun) 04 was 0.01.

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: Roger. We got that. [This is a gravity check of the platform alignment, as indicted at the top of Surface 8-8.] [Comm Break. TV on. Fendell plays with tracking he will use to follow the launch.] RealVideo Clip by Ken Glover (2 min 26 sec)

A17A1871623.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1871623.text: Challenger, Houston. We've got you on television now. We have a good picture. RealVideo Clip (4 min 24 sec)

A17A1871623.speaker: Cernan
A17A1871623.text: Glad to see old Rover's still working. [Comm Break] RealVideo Clip (4 min 24 sec)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Houston; coming up on 10 minutes. And we're ready to pressurize the APS (Ascent Propulsion System).

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Okay; you're Go to pressurize the APS (Ascent Propulsion System). [In the following procedures, they are firing small explosive charges which open the valves on the helium tanks which, then, provide pressure to the propellant tanks. Readers may want to note the Emergency Launch procedures listed in the box at the right side of Surface 8-16. If the crew had found a leak in the either of the tanks in the Ascent Stage, they could have launched almost immediately to take advantage of as much of the propellant as possible.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. The Master Arm is coming On. I've got two good lights. (Pause) Tank 1 is selected. Okay, Ascent Helium Press(urize) Tank 1, Fire. Ready; 3, 2, 1. Mark it. We got a squib fired, Houston. [That is, they could feel the vibrations caused by detonation of the charge.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger. (Long Pause) Challenger, you're Go for Tank 2.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, understand; Go for Tank 2. (To Jack) Ready? Okay. 3, 2, 1. Mark it. Tank 2. We got the squib. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Challenger. Both tanks look good.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (To Jack) Wonder why they didn't balance off? [Schmitt - "On our gauges, the pressures for the two tanks were different, and they should have been the same. Down below (187:54:07), Gordo will tell us that they think there's a transducer problem."]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Master Arm is coming Off, and the lights are out. (Pause) Okay, Jack. System A, Ascent Feed 2, Open. (Pause) Okay, monitor your...Okay. System A Main SOV (Shut Off Valve) Closed. [For the first part of the ascent, they will use Ascent Fuel for the RCS (Reaction Control System, the small steering jets) and save the RCS Fuel supply for final maneuvers - hence the closure of the shut-off valves. See Gene's comment at 187:56:26.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (To Jack) How does it look to you? Okay; B Ascent Feed 2, Open. (Pause) I can feel them (the valve charges) in the floor when they go. Okay; and B Main SOV, Closed. Check your manifold pressures. Are you happy? (Pause) Okay, Houston. We got Ascent Feed. [They are now at the bottom of Surface 8-16 and are waiting for permission to launch. Details of the launch are given in the LM Timeline Book, which is not reproduced here. See Surface 8-17.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger. And America, can you read Houston? Over.

A17A1875101.speaker: Evans
A17A1875101.text: America. Roger. Loud and clear.

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Ron. You're loud and clear. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. We're standing by for 5 (minutes to lift-off). (Pause) Houston, Challenger is Go for lift-off. We're at 7:54 (prior to lift-off) and counting. RealVideo Clip (3 min 07 sec)

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger, Challenger. You're Go for lift-off.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Roger. Understand. Challenger is Go for lift-off. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Challenger, Houston. We think the transducer in tank 2 has shifted. We want you to monitor tank 1 for APS helium (pressure). Over.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Roger. We were looking at that, and we'll monitor 1.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (To Jack, who is back on VOX) What of this do you want?

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I need the big one there, with the cards in it. (Long Pause) [This card contains the final checklist items.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Here you go.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Thank you.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: That's all right. (Pause) Okay. (Long Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Let's go over the APS burn card.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. My Display/Engine Override Logic breaker is In; circuit breakers Stab(ilization)/Control all Closed on panel 11, except AEA and DECA Power.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Stab/Control breakers are all Closed, except AEA and DECA Power.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Logic breaker's In.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Logic breaker's In.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: And all of mine are Closed except Descent Engine Override. Logic's In.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Rate Scale, 25 Degrees per Second.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Attitude/Translation, 4 Jets.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: 4 Jets.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Balance Couple, On.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: On.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Dead Band, Min.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Dead Band in Min.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Abort/Abort Stage, Reset.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Abort/Abort Stage are Reset.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Attitude Control, three, to Mode Control.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Attitude Control, three, on Mode Control.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. And you're going to be in Auto and Att Hold.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: PGNS is Auto, and AGS is Att Hold.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Stop pushbuttons are reset, and...

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Reset here.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: ...And you're in Jets.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: And I'm in Jets.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, let's take a swing around the systems.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I just did. Everything looks good. The propellant pressure is holding up. We're tied to the Ascent tanks on the RCS (Reaction Control System). [Cernan - "We had two sources of propellant for the RCS systems. One was their own tanks and, for the other, we could crossfeed and utilize ascent propellant. We did that during the ascent phase to save the RCS fuel for rendezvous. We had a margin in the ascent tanks to cover that."]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay; 5 minutes and my...

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: That EC...

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Rendezvous Radar breaker is Closed. (Pause) And let's go to the Timeline Book.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Got it. RealVideo Clip (3 min 47 sec)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Make sure of everything in here. (Long Pause) Okay. At 2 minutes, I'll get the Master Arm. We already are Vox. You'll get 400 plus 1. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. And I'll get the (16 mm sequence) camera and...

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (Sounding very relaxed) Okay. At 10 seconds I'll hit the Abort Stage, followed by the Engine Arm to Ascent. (Pause) You get the Pro(ceed). I'll backup the start. If we don't get a start, I'll go Guidance Control to AGS. I'll wipe out the thrusters. I'll go AGS Auto. And if we don't get a start, we'll back off. (Pause) Okay?

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. (Pause) [Cernan - "In listening to this, it's obvious that we were pretty confident. I know how prepared we were and I'm still impressed. I'd have to go back and study and learn this all over again. It sounds to me like we knew exactly what we were going to do in the event of a no-light. You get to a point where you hope it never happens but you almost dare something to fail. Because you know that, if it does, you're prepared to handle it. I don't specifically remember why I was going to wipe out the thrusters (by rotating the control through all thruster positions), but I think we had t

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Houston, we have an awful lot of noise coming up (the comm circuit).

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Challenger. I understand.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I think we can read you, Gordy. You sound pretty good now.

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: That's VHF noise, Jack. (Pause) (Go to) VHF B. (Pause) [They are hearing the Command Module. Because Evans is in a 60 mile orbit, he 'rises' over the LM horizon about 6 minutes prior to passing overhead. They will launch prior to his overhead pass.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. I can cut it out with a high squelch (setting) on Bravo.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Houston. Challenger's at 2 minutes and 50 seconds (prior to launch).

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger, Challenger...

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: We're Go for PGNS...

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Everything looks great down here.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: ...direct (ascent). (Responding to Fullerton) Okay. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I'm not going to be able to squelch him (Evans) out any more.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Turn the volume down a little bit. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (Responding to Evans, who is talking to them directly) Reading you loud and clear, America. This is Challenger. We're coming up on 02:10 from lift-off.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: (To Evans) We'll be with you shortly. Okay, Jack. Double-check your Logic Power breaker.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Checked.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, Master Arm is On. I've got two good lights. [These lights indicate that the explosive bolts which they will fire to separate the Ascent Stage from the Descent Stage are ready to fire.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. I've got 400 plus 1 in.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: My watch is reset (as a backup to the event timer.) (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. You got 367. You want to pick up the (16 mm sequence) camera just before I hit Abort Stage. (Long Pause) RealVideo Clip (3 min 29 sec)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: One minute coming up, Gene.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Take your final look at the valley of Taurus-Littrow, except from orbit. (Pause) Okay, one minute, Houston. We're 50 seconds now, and we're Go.

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger. You're looking good here.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I'll get that (camera) at 30.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Camera's not going to run without me holding it.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Average G , 20 seconds. [Cernan - "This was a routine in the PGNS to start recording data from the accelerometers."]

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Ah, shoot!

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Now, let's get off. Forget the camera. (Garbled)... MPEG Clip by Kipp Teague (30 sec; 3.9 Mb)

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Ten seconds.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: ...10 seconds.

A17A1875101.speaker: LM Crew
A17A1875101.text: Abort Stage. 188:01:30 Cernan: ...pushed. Engine Arm is Ascent. [The accompanying video clip of the Apollo 17 LM launch (1.8 Mb) starts 3 seconds before ignition and then follows the LM for the first 13 seconds of the ascent.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. I'm going to get the Pro. (Pause) 99 Proceeded 3, 2, 1...

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Ignition. [Schmitt - "As I recall, at the moment of ignition, all we had was static - loud static. And I was looking to see what happened, to see if I'd lost lock."] [Cernan - "Jack spent half of the lift-off trying to get comm back."] [Schmitt - "And I remember somebody telling me that what had happened was that they had a site handover scheduled right at lift-off! And nobody caught it."] [Jack's memory is not quite accurate, although the problem was, in part, due to procedures on the ground. The following has been extracted from the Apollo 17 Mission 5-Day Report: "On lunar module ascent, tw

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: We're on our way, Houston!

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Rates are good. AGS saw it (that is, the ignition). (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: LM Crew
A17A1875101.text: Pitchover!

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger. You have good thrust. (Pause) [After launch, Fendell successfully tracks the LM for 26 seconds. He finds it again, very briefly, at 45 seconds and, a minute later, points the TV back at the Descent Stage. The flag is still standing, as is the SEP pallet Gene had leaned against the north landing strut. Note that the flag is pointing north. As can be seen in Jack's post-EVA-3 photo AS17-143- 21948 , the flag was pointing east. Clearly, what has happened is that the ascent engine exhaust exerted sufficient force on the flag so that, like a weathervane, it swung around to point directly awa

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay, 30 seconds; 308 is your number.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay, coming through 1500 feet.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: And H-dot looks good.

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger. We've lost data right now, but we'd like Aft Omni. Aft Omni, please.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Okay; coming up on 40 seconds. And we're Go. Coming right over the top of Camelot. (Pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Awful lot of static, Jack. We break lock?

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Yeah.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: Why don't you get it on an Omni, or something?

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Yeah, I got it. It's on the Omni.

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: See if you can get comm back.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Hello, Houston. How do you read?

A17A1875101.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1875101.text: Roger, Challenger. You're loud and clear, and both systems look good. You're right on the line.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: Okay. Should be about 145 and minus 47. [These are pointing angles for the high-gain antenna.]

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: See if we can get comm.

A17A1875101.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1875101.text: I will. (Long pause)

A17A1875101.speaker: Cernan
A17A1875101.text: 01:30, Houston. We're in the blind, and we're Go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Challenger, Houston. Aft Omni, please. Would you relay, America? (Pause)

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Houston. Three minutes, and Challenger is Go. We're through 25K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: (To Evans) I tried it...I tried it, Ron, and it doesn't hold.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Try Aft Omni again, Jack.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: It doesn't help.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: America, Houston. Tell Challenger...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: All my comm breakers are in.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Try Aft Omni again.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: ...that they're right on the money on trajectory; both systems are Go. Over.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Houston. In the blind, Challenger's Go; coming up on 03:25 and at 30K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, there's Aft. How do you read, Houston?

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: America, would you relay to Challenger to go Aft Omni?

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: (To Evans) We are Aft Omni. How do you read?

A17A1880426.speaker: Evans
A17A1880426.text: (To Houston) Okay, they are in Aft Omni right now.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Okay, America, tell Challenger...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: And we're reading Houston.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: ...we're reading them 5 by. (Pause)

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay. We're reading you, Houston.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Jack...

A17A1880426.speaker: Evans
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Challenger, America....

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: (Garbled)

A17A1880426.speaker: Evans
A17A1880426.text: ...Yeah, you got them.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: ...we need a 623 plus 10,000. Jack, give us a 623 plus 10,000. [This is an AGS update in case the PGNS fails and they have to use it.]

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, 4 minutes. Challenger's Go. We're through 37K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger, Challenger. You're looking good here.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, that (623)'s in.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Noun 37 says we got about a 07:16 burn, Jack.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, at 04:30, I'll be about 282 coming through 41K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, 04:30. 282 is great; 41K is great, 73 is good; AGS and PGNS are right together.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Houston. Challenger is Go. We're now through 43.5 (thousand feet).

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Challenger, Houston. We'd like to terminate Ascent Feed now. [Cernan - "As I remember, the time to get fuel out of the ascent tanks (for the RCS) was when we had a g-force because, once we were in zero-g, we could not have gotten any even if there was some left. Now they've decided that we've taken enough of the ascent fuel for the RCS. They don't want to get the ascent fuel any lower because they want it for the ascent engine, itself. So, the RCS is now going on it's own tanks - which are full at this point, and that's important. Well, they're not full, because we didn't cross feed on the des

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Main SOV (Shut-Off Valve) is going On.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: And the reason is the mixture ratio problem....

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Ascent Feed, Closed.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: ...That's just to be conservative and safe. Over.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Understand. And we're going 5 (minutes), and we're now out of 48K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, the (sequence) camera's stopped.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, burn time's going to be about 18 or 19. 07:18 or 07:19, Jack.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay. [I asked Gene and Jack if, like Conrad and Bean, they experienced a significant amount of LM 'wobble' RCS firing during the trip up from the surface. Neither remembered anything notable.]

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay. The AGS has us just about in plane.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: PGNS and AGS are looking good.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: A little bit north.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Houston, 05:40. Challenger's coming through 52K. And PGNS says 126 on the H-dot. We're Go. [They are gaining altitude at the rate of 126 feet per second.]

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: AGS likes the plane.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger, Challenger. Your trajectory is right on the money. Both systems are Go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Get a good shutoff time now.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, it'll be 20...7:20 (into the burn) on the shutoff.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, we've already terminated Ascent Feed. You got 1300 (feet per second horizontal velocity) to go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay. Let's double-check everything now.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: You got that; you want...

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Next move is at 200 feet (per second).

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Engine Arm, Off with 200 to go. AGS and PGNS are right together.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: We got about another minute to go, Houston. And we're coming up on 57K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger. And we agree with the...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: 900 to go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: (Garbled) out nicely. Okay, H-dot is rounding right out to the target.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: 700 to go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Coming up...

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Okay, normal shutdown and normal trim procedures.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Mark it.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Roger. Normal shutdown, normal trim. Give me a hack at 200 (fps horizontal velocity to go), Jack.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, it's 500 now...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Mark it, and the ascent feeds are already terminated.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay. Very good.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Seven minutes, Houston. And we're passing 59K.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: 300; stand by. 200 to go.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Mark it.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Engine Arm is Off.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, stand by for shutdown; 80, 50...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Shutdown!

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Auto Shutdown...

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Auto Shutdown.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: ...Houston, Auto shutdown!

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger. [Cernan - "As I remember, my intent was to let the PGNS shut it down and, if it didn't within a second afterwards, I was going to. I think I shut it down anyway. I wasn't going to let it send us into orbit around the Sun. But I was less concerned about the shutdown than the start. I was told that, at lift-off, I beat the PGNS start by some micro-cosmo of a second."]

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, no trim, Houston; no trim.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger. We're reading the DSKY.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: We're showing a 50 (mile) by 9.1 (mile elliptical orbit).

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Roger. (Pause) And MSFN confirms that orbit (with tracking from Earth).

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay. AGS got a little bit of out-of-plane. Dispersion was 0900.

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Engine Stop is Reset. Get in the attitude for the tweak. Okay. [That is, Gene is positioning the LM for a slight correction burn (or, "tweak"), using the RCS.]

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Okay, AGS says it's 9.1. [This is the low point of the orbit they have just entered.]

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Challenger, Houston. There will be a tweak. Stand by for it.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: 48 (mile high point) by 9.1; 49 by 9.1. (Long Pause)

A17A1880426.speaker: Cernan
A17A1880426.text: Okay, that's our attitude. We're in attitude for the tweak.

A17A1880426.speaker: Fullerton
A17A1880426.text: Okay, Challenger. Here is your tweak. Ignition is at 12 plus 12; VX is a minus 4.0 (feet per second); Y, minus 9.0; and Z, plus 1.0. That's at 12:12; minus 4; minus 9; and plus 1.

A17A1880426.speaker: Schmitt
A17A1880426.text: Roger. That's at 12:12; minus 4; minus 9; and plus 1. 188:10:40 Fullerton Roger, that's a good readback. [Cernan - "That was exciting! I hadn't gone through that for a long time. Eric and I did the descent alone and I sort of re-lived it all. But it's more fun to re-live the ascent with Jack."] Post-EVA-3 Activities Apollo 17 Journal Return to Earth
